findings.claim: Plain filter layers (`l.kind === "filter"` with `!ownPx(l)`) keep an empty `l.px` allocated at the canvas size when the filter layer was created, and none of the five whole-document geometry operations (`turnDocumentNow`, `straightenDocumentNow`, `cropCanvasNow`, `resizeImageNow`, `extendCanvasNow`) updates `l.px` to `nw × nh`. Mask creation (`maskFromSelection`, `fillLayerMask`, `maskFromLayer`) sizes `l.maskPx` from `layer.px.width × layer.px.height`, producing wrong-resolution masks (downsampled on upscale/extend, oversized after crop, transposed after 90° turn), skipping mask shift/resize in `extendCanvasNow` (wrong pixels on screen, in exports, and in paid runs), breaking `stackPlan` (forcing synchronous full-document flatten on 15k images and refusing exports/runs above 268 MP), and uploading a stale empty PNG when `extendCanvasNow` sets `l.dirty = true`.
findings.scenario: 1. Open a 500 × 500 image and add a Curves filter layer (`l.px` is 500 × 500). Resize or upscale the image to 4000 × 4000 (`resizeImageNow` sets `l.w = 4000, l.h = 4000` while `l.px` stays 500 × 500), select a crisp subject, and click 'Mask from selection' on the Curves layer: `l.maskPx` is created at 500 × 500 (8× too coarse in each axis), blurring the filter mask on screen, in exports, and in paid runs. 2. Or open a 2000 × 2000 image, add a Curves filter layer (`l.px` is 2000 × 2000), crop to 800 × 800, add a mask ('Mask from selection'), hide the Curves layer, and extend the canvas by 200 px on the left: `l.maskPx` is 2000 × 2000 (`!== W` of 800), so `extendCanvasNow` skips `l.maskPx.resized(nw, nh, { x: left, y: top })` and stretches the unshifted mask across the 1000 × 800 canvas, while `l.dirty = true` makes `syncLayersOnce` PNG-encode and upload the stale 2000 × 2000 empty `l.px`. On a >268 MP tile document, cropping/turning and adding a mask to a filter layer also causes `stackPlan` (`fm.width !== this.width`) to return `null`, throwing on flatten/export/run.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:324` creates plain filter layers with `px: this.pixels.Layer.empty(this.width, this.height)`. Mask creation reads `layer.px.width` / `layer.px.height` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:160` (`const m = this.pixels.Mask.empty(layer.px.width, layer.px.height);`), `228` (`fillLayerMask`), and `266` (`maskFromLayer`). None of the geometry ops replaces `l.px` when `!ownPx(l)`: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:678,686-687` (`turned.set(l, { px: (l.kind !== "filter" || ownPx(l)) && l.px ? l.px.turned(op) : null, ... }); ... l.w = nw; l.h = nh; if (t.px) l.px = t.px;`), `980,1052-1056` (`straightenDocumentNow`), `1387-1391` (`cropCanvasNow`: `if (ownPx(l) && l.px) { l.px = l.px.resized(nw, nh, { x: -left, y: -top }); l.dirty = true; }`), `1454-1472` (`resizeImageNow`), and `1646-1649,1658` (`extendCanvasNow`: `if (l.maskPx && l.maskPx.width === W && l.maskPx.height === H) { l.maskPx = l.maskPx.resized(nw, nh, { x: left, y: top }); ... } if (ownPx(l) && l.px && l.px.width === W && l.px.height === H) l.px = l.px.resized(nw, nh, { x: left, y: top }); ... l.dirty = true;`). `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:178` rejects `stackPlan` when `fm && (fm.width !== this.width || fm.height !== this.height)`, and `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:906` uploads any layer with `l.dirty && l.px`.
findings.fix: In `turnDocumentNow`, `straightenDocumentNow`, `cropCanvasNow`, `resizeImageNow`, and `extendCanvasNow`, replace `l.px = this.pixels.Layer.empty(nw, nh)` on plain filter layers (`l.kind === "filter" && !ownPx(l)`); in `extendCanvasNow`, resize any existing `l.maskPx` onto `(nw, nh)` (scaling from `W × H` if its resolution differed) and do not set `l.dirty = true` when `l.kind === "filter" && !ownPx(l)`.
findings.why: Verified at f45a86cc: addFilterLayer (inpaint_ed_filters.js:324) and setValue (inpaint_ed_persist.js:208) allocate plain filter layers (!ownPx(l)) with px: Layer.empty(W0, H0), and none of the five whole-document geometry operations (turnDocumentNow:678,686-687, straightenDocumentNow:980-983,1052, cropCanvasNow:1387-1391, resizeImageNow:1454-1472, extendCanvasNow:1646-1649) updates l.px when !ownPx(l). All three mask-creation paths (maskFromSelection:160, fillLayerMask:228, maskFromLayer:266 in inpaint_ed_masks.js) size MaskPixels from layer.px.width x layer.px.height instead of this.width x this.height. After any aspect-changing 90-deg turn or crop before masking a filter layer, drawTilesInto on screen uses independent fx and fy so the mask looks right on screen, whereas stackPlan (inpaint_ed_stack.js:178) rejects fm.width !== this.width and flattenToCanvas (inpaint_ed_filters.js:1531,1570) uses a single scalar ms = layer.maskPx.width / this.width on both X and Y, silently squashing the mask in JPEG/WebP/PNG exports and paid-run crops; upscaling/resizing permanently downsamples new filter masks by the old size; and extendCanvasNow:1648,1658 skips shifting stale-sized masks while uploading the stale empty l.px.

findings.claim: All three depth routes (`computeDepthMap`, `depthFromPoints`, and `depthFromLayer`) store a live `Float32Array` on `map.meta.raw`, and `mapToJSON` serializes `map.meta` verbatim via `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(map.meta))`, turning millions of floats into a `{"0":...,"1":...}` JSON object on every `getValue()`. After *Depth from layer* (`WORK_MAX = 4096`), `document.json` exceeds `.scumble`'s 64 MiB header cap so saving the document is refused outright, and on a 4096x4096 square image (or two 15k tabs) `JSON.stringify(this.bundle())` exceeds V8's 512 MB string / IPC limit, silently halting `autosave.json` for all open tabs or OOM-crashing the renderer — while the serialized `meta.raw` is unusable after reload anyway.
findings.scenario: Open a 15000x10000 (or 4096x4096) image, import or paint a height/depth layer, and run Image > Depth > Depth from Layer (or `depth_map` with `from_layer`). `depthFromLayer` sets `meta.raw` to an 11.18M-float (3:2, 4096x2731) or 16.78M-float (1:1, 4096x4096) `Float32Array`. 1.5 s after every subsequent edit, `host.saveAll()` -> `bundle()` -> `ed.getValue()` -> `mapToJSON` expands `meta.raw` into ~326–480 MB of JSON text on the main thread, freezing the window for seconds; on the 4096x4096 tab (or two 3:2 tabs), escaping `state` inside `JSON.stringify(this.bundle())` exceeds V8's max string length and throws inside `saveAll()`'s `try/catch`, silently stopping session autosaves for every open tab (or hitting the ~512 MiB IPC OOM cliff). When the user then tries File > Save (`Ctrl+S`), `docfile.js` refuses the save because `scumble/document.json` exceeds `MAX_HEADER` (64 MiB). Even on the smaller Depth Anything route (~403k floats, ~11 MB JSON per edit and in MCP `get_state`), reloading turns `meta.raw` into a plain `{ "0": ... }` object that `setDepthDetail` immediately rejects.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:25` sets `const WORK_MAX = 4096;`; `:175` (`computeDepthMap`), `:251` (`depthFromPoints`), and `:534` / `:568` (`depthFromLayer`: `const meta = { fp, source: "layer", layerId: layer.id, lo: 0, hi: 1, detail: 0.5, raw, rw: dw, rh: dh };`) put a `Float32Array` in `meta.raw`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:114` (`makeMap`) and `:290` (`deriveMap`) shallow-copy `meta`, and `:358` (`mapToJSON`) executes `meta: map.meta ? JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(map.meta)) : {},`. Callers: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:97-102` (`getValue`), `renderer/editor/host_queue.js:527-528,537` (`state = ed.getValue(); ed._stateKey = hashString(state);` then `try { window.scumble.state.save(JSON.stringify(this.bundle())).catch(() => {}); } catch (err) { console.warn("autosave", err); }`), `renderer/editor/host_queue.js:563` (`referencedFileKeys` parses `ed.getValue()` and walks every key of `meta.raw`), `renderer/commands_depth.js:170` (`get_state`), and `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:240` (`saveDocument`) -> `electron/main/docfile.js:53,448` (`const MAX_HEADER = 64 * 1024 * 1024;` ... `if (headerBuf.length > MAX_HEADER) throw failure("refused", ...)`). On reload, `inpaint_maps.js:415` (`mapFromJSON`) copies `json.meta` as a plain Object, which `inpaint_ed_depth.js:1032` (`if (!meta || !(meta.raw instanceof Float32Array)) return;`) cannot use.
findings.fix: Keep session-only typed arrays off serialized `map.meta` (e.g. store `raw`, `rw`, `rh` in a non-serialized property or `WeakMap` on the map / editor, or strip typed arrays and `raw`/`rw`/`rh` in `mapToJSON` before `JSON.stringify`).
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:358`, `mapToJSON(map)` serializes `map.meta` verbatim via `meta: map.meta ? JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(map.meta)) : {}`. Because `Float32Array` is an integer-indexed exotic object rather than an `Array`, `JSON.stringify` expands every element into `"0":<val>,"1":<val>,...` — allocating a huge JSON string, parsing it into a multi-million-property plain `Object`, and immediately stringifying it a second time inside `PersistPart.getValue()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:42,96-104`). All three depth-creation paths store a live, non-detached `Float32Array` on `meta.raw` (`editorPool().run("depth_guide", ...)` only transfers `[guide.image.buffer]`): `computeDepthMap` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:151-160,175`, ~406k floats on `standard`, or `wf * hf` = 2.52M–2.98M+ floats on `finest` 3x3 via `host_helpers.js:656-678` and `inpaint_edges.js:206-219`), `depthFromPoints` (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:241-243,251`, up to 768x768 = 590k floats), and `depthFromLayer` (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:514,534,555,568`, reachable from the sidebar `From layer...` button at `:715-718,749-752` -> `openDepthFromLayerMenu` `:592-614` and MCP `depth_from_layer` at `renderer/commands_depth.js:148-168`), which sizes `rawDepth` at `workSize(W, H, WORK_MAX)` with `WORK_MAX = 4096` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_depth.js:7,70-75`). Neither `makeMap` (`inpaint_maps.js:114`) nor `deriveMap` (`:290`, used by `setMapMeta` `:932` and `editDepth` `:1032`) strips `meta.raw`.

No guard prevents this payload from hitting both `.scumble` saves and session autosaves, and `meta.raw` serves almost no purpose (note two minor citation corrections to the candidate report: `WORK_MAX` is in `inpaint_depth.js:7` rather than `inpaint_ed_depth.js:25`, `MAX_HEADER` is at `electron/main/docfile.js:197` rather than `:53`, and `setDepthDetail` in `renderer/editor/host_state.js:92-97` only saves the setting string — in fact nothing in the editor reads `meta.raw` at all except MCP `sample_depth` at `renderer/commands_depth.js:103-106`, and legacy `state.depth` in `inpaint_ed_persist.js:80-95,355` deliberately omitted `raw`). Exact byte math confirms both hard limits are exceeded: (1) On `depthFromLayer` for a 3:2 image >= 4096 px (`4096 x 2731` = `11,186,176` floats), key+punctuation overhead alone (`"0":`..`"11186175":,`) is `123,123,003` bytes (~117.4 MiB), so even an all-black/white mask (`0`/`1` values) is `134.3 MB`, and a normal greyscale layer (`Math.fround(k / 255)` promoted to IEEE-754 float64 `Number` in V8 `JSON.stringify`, ~18.5 chars/float) makes `ed.getValue()` ~330 MB (~315 MiB). Even an ordinary `1920 x 1280` (2.46 MP) greyscale layer (~70 MB) or a `3840 x 2160` / `6000 x 4000` `Compute depth map` with `Detail: Finest (3x3)` (~70.6–82.4 MB) exceeds `MAX_HEADER = 64 * 1024 * 1024` (`67,108,864` bytes) in `electron/main/docfile.js:197,447-448` (via `host_documents.js:240,246` -> `electron/main/documents.js:171,205-208`), refusing `Ctrl+S` / `File > Save` outright, with no UI button in `renderDepthRow` (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:739-850`) to delete `maps.depth`. (2) On a `4096 x 4096` square image (`16,777,216` floats, `190.2 MB` keys+punctuation + ~310.4 MB float text = ~500.6M chars in `ed.getValue()`), or two 3:2 tabs (or one open + one in `host.closed` via `rememberClosed` at `host_documents.js:338-346`), `JSON.stringify(this.bundle())` in `host_queue.js:537` escapes all `2 * 16,777,216 = 33.55M` key quotes (`"` -> `\"`), pushing the bundle string to ~534M–555M+ chars against V8's `String::kMaxLength` (`536,870,888` chars on 64-bit V8) and Electron's ~512 MiB renderer->main IPC OOM cliff (`electron/preload.js:86`). Worse, if `JSON.stringify(this.bundle())` stays just under 536.87M chars and crosses IPC, `electron/main/autosave.js:105,149` runs `JSON.stringify({ state, time })` a third time (`\"` -> `\\\"`, adding another `+67.1M` chars -> ~601M chars > `536,870,888`), throwing `RangeError: Invalid string length` in main. Both renderer throws (`catch (err) { console.warn("autosave", err); }`) and main IPC rejections (`.catch(() => {})`) are swallowed at `host_queue.js:537`, silently halting `autosave.json` for every open tab, while `saveBeforeRestart` (`renderer/shell.js:1019,1027,1042`) throws uncaught on quit/restart. `referencedFileKeys` (`host_queue.js:560,563`), `documents.write` (`documents.js:181-182`), and MCP `get_state` (`commands_depth.js:170`) also parse and walk all millions of keys, and `mapFromJSON` (`inpaint_maps.js:413`) retains the useless `{ "0": ... }` object in memory on reload.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including the 0.1.56/0.1.57 `mapsUnstored`/`storeMaps` entries), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`, where `P16` only noted normal 1 MB triple-escaped `autosave.json` files without depth maps). This defect is not recorded in any known list.

Severity is `must`: normal use of `Depth > From layer...` (or `Finest` 3x3 depth on 4K+/24MP photos) blocks `.scumble` document saves completely with no UI way to clear the map, and on a 4096x4096 image or multi-tab session silently breaks `autosave.json` (and `saveBeforeRestart` on quit, or OOM-kills the renderer at the ~512 MiB IPC cliff), causing silent loss of unsaved work across all open tabs.

findings.claim: The 0.1.57 fix for large-picture layer splits (`splitSendSize`) scales inputs above 4096^2 down before `splitSizeRefusal` and bills the paid Seedream split API, but `readyRow` still bakes every returned layer onto an unchecked full-size `<canvas>` (`canvasOf(img, row.w, row.h)`) and PNG-encodes that full-size canvas on the window. Above Chromium's 268.4 MP canvas limit, `c.toBlob` resolves null after the paid call has already completed, crashing `canvasBytes(c)` and discarding all paid layers; on a 15000 x 10000 (150 MP) document, it synchronously allocates and single-thread PNG-encodes 600 MB canvases per full-frame layer (up to 17 x 600 MB = 10.2 GB on WaveSpeed/Oxen/OpenRouter) without zeroing `c` on the tile backend, while `sourceBytes` still calls `editor.layerPixels(job.layer)` (`toCanvas()`) when splitting a layer.
findings.scenario: 1) On a 20000 x 15000 (300 MP) tiled document, run Split into layers on ModelArk, WaveSpeed, Oxen, or OpenRouter: `splitJob` scales `send` to 4732 x 3549, passes `splitSizeRefusal`, samples the composite via `sampleRegionSettled`, and bills `providerEdit`. When the ~2K layers return, `planLanding` sets `row.w = 20000, row.h = 15000`; `readyRow` calls `canvasOf(img, 20000, 15000)` and `deps.canvasBytes(c)`, where `c.toBlob` returns `null`, `null.arrayBuffer()` throws TypeError, `runJob` catches at line 468 ('Nothing was added'), `dropLayerParts` deletes the parts in `finally`, and the paid run is lost. 2) On a 15000 x 10000 tiled document on WaveSpeed/Oxen/OpenRouter (`full: true`), all up to 17 returned ~2K layers have `row.w = 15000, row.h = 10000`, allocating up to 17 unzeroed 600 MB `<canvas>` elements on the main thread and running 17 x 150 MP Blink `toBlob` PNG encodes instead of keeping the native ~2K layer pixels at `w: row.w, h: row.h`.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/splitlayers.js:193-195 `const send = splitSendSize(rect.w, rect.h); const no = splitSizeRefusal(send.w, send.h, model);` lets >268 MP documents through to `providerEdit` at line 438. In `readyRow` / `canvasOf` (renderer/editor/splitlayers.js:249-268): `const c = canvasOf(img, row.w, row.h); return { px: editor.pixels.Layer.fromCanvas(c), png: await deps.canvasBytes(c) };` creates a raw `row.w x row.h` `<canvas>` with no `canvasFits` check and never resets `c.width = c.height = 0` when `editor.tileMode` is true. `deps.canvasBytes` is renderer/editor/stitch.js:741-744 `const blob = ... await new Promise((resolve) => canvas.toBlob(resolve, "image/png")); return new Uint8Array(await blob.arrayBuffer());`, which throws when `blob` is `null` above 268.4 MP, caught at splitlayers.js:467-471 (`dropLayerParts(res)`). On `full: true` providers (splitlayers.js:58-61, 158), every layer gets `w: rect.w, h: rect.h`. Also at splitlayers.js:242, splitting a layer calls `x.drawImage(editor.layerPixels(job.layer), 0, 0, w, h)` which materialises a full-layer `<canvas>` on the window.
findings.fix: Keep each returned split layer at its native decoded resolution (`editor.pixels.Layer.fromImage(img)` and `png = row.entry.mime === 'image/png' ? bytes : await deps.canvasBytes(canvasOf(img, iw, ih))`) while placing the layer in the document at `x: row.x, y: row.y, w: row.w, h: row.h` (matching how `InpaintEditor` stretches `layer.px` to `layer.w x layer.h` during `resizeImage`). In `sourceBytes` for `job.layer` when `scaled && editor.tileMode`, sample from the layer's tile pyramid (`sampleRegionSettled` or `drawLayer` at scale) instead of `editor.layerPixels(job.layer)`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc. Every code path and failure mechanism holds (noting two tiny prose details: `splitSendSize` shipped in 0.1.56 rather than 0.1.57 per `CHANGELOG.md:94`, `splitSendSize(20000, 15000)` floors to `4729 × 3547` rather than `4732 × 3549`, and `deps.providerEdit` is at `splitlayers.js:432`).

1. **Post-billing crash and permanent loss of the paid split above 268.4 MP:** Scumble's default tile backend (`inpaint_ed_open.js:84-97`) supports `this.huge` documents above `CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS = 268,435,456` (`inpaint_sizelimit.js:6`) up to `1,073,741,824` px (`65,535` px per side). Both entry points — *Image › Split into Layers...* (`renderer/splitdialog.js:26, 98`) and MCP `split_layers` (`renderer/commands_runs.js:233-253` -> `host_generate.js:351-353`) — call `runSplitLayers` -> `runJob` (`renderer/editor/splitlayers.js:400-473`) with no `editor.huge` or `canvasFits` guard. In `splitJob` (`splitlayers.js:189-195`), a `20000 × 15000` (300 MP) document sets `rect = { x: 0, y: 0, w: 20000, h: 15000 }` and checks `splitSizeRefusal` only on `send = splitSendSize(20000, 15000)` (`4729 × 3547`, 16.77 MP), which passes. In `sourceBytes` (`splitlayers.js:218-235`), when splitting the visible picture (`!job.layer`), `scaled` is `true`, so it bypasses `flattenToCanvas` (which would have thrown on `this.huge` at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:564`) and samples from tile mips via `editor.sampleRegionSettled` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:892-903`) into a `4729 × 3547` canvas. `runJob` (`splitlayers.js:432`) then sends the request via `deps.providerEdit` (`electron/main/providers/index.js:314`), passing `ark._layerSizeRefusal` (`layersplit.js:45`) and **billing the user's ModelArk, WaveSpeedAI, Oxen.ai, or OpenRouter account**.

When the ~2K layers return, `prepare` (`splitlayers.js:281`) calls `planLanding(entries, job.rect, bw, bh, taken)` (`splitlayers.js:128-144`). Because `entries[0]` is always the base (`entry.base === true`), `rows[0]` unconditionally gets `w: 20000, h: 15000` on **every** provider (including ModelArk, where non-base layers have `bounding_box`; on WaveSpeed/Oxen/OpenRouter, `layersplit.js:127` / `openrouter.js:579` set `full: true` for unboxed layers and `fitFull` at `splitlayers.js:301, 322-328` also assigns `w: 20000, h: 15000` to every layer matching the base's aspect ratio). At `i = 0`, `prepare` (`splitlayers.js:305`, outside the `res.tolerant` catch at `287-298`) awaits `readyRow` (`splitlayers.js:249-257`). Because `iw !== row.w`, `readyRow` calls `canvasOf(img, 20000, 15000)` (`splitlayers.js:255, 259-268`), which uses raw `document.createElement("canvas")` without `makeCanvas`/`canvasFits`. Above 268.4 MP, Chromium leaves `c` unbacked: `TileLayerPixels.fromCanvas(c)` (`inpaint_tiles.js:825, 2619-2633`) reads all-zero `ImageData`, and `deps.canvasBytes(c)` (`renderer/editor/stitch.js:741-744`) awaits `c.toBlob(resolve, "image/png")`, which resolves `blob = null` and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'arrayBuffer')`. `runJob` catches at `splitlayers.js:467-468` (`"Nothing was added."`), and `finally` (`splitlayers.js:469-471`) calls `dropLayerParts(res.layersToken)` (`providers/index.js:451`). Since the window did not reload (`pageWentAway === false` at `providers/index.js:344`), no `.split` recovery file exists on disk, and all paid layers are permanently lost.

2. **15k (150 MP) memory/CPU bloat, OOM risk, and `sourceBytes` on a layer:** On a `15000 × 10000` tiled document (`editor.tileMode === true`), `readyRow` (`splitlayers.js:255-256`) allocates a 600 MB GPU-backed `<canvas>` per full-frame layer (up to 17 × 600 MB = 10.2 GB at the default `count: 16` + base on WaveSpeed/Oxen/OpenRouter, and up to 32/99 when asked), forces a synchronous 600 MB GPU-to-CPU `getImageData` readback in `TileLayerPixels._readCanvas`, runs Blink's single-threaded `c.toBlob` PNG encode on 150 MP per layer instead of worker `encodeTilePixels`, and never zeroes `c.width = c.height = 0` on the tile backend. Worse, because Chromium's renderer typed-array ceiling is ~15.5 GB (~18 full 15k layers, `inpaint_arena.js:38-52`), baking many full-frame ~2K layers to 15k tiles can throw `PixelMemoryError` mid-loop in `prepare` after the paid API call has already completed, likewise discarding the paid run via `dropLayerParts`. Additionally, in `sourceBytes` (`splitlayers.js:242`), splitting a layer (`job.layer`) calls `editor.layerPixels(job.layer)` (`inpaint_ed_view.js:371` -> `layer.px.toCanvas()` at `inpaint_tiles.js:2129`), materializing an unzeroed full-layer CPU canvas on the window at 15k (and throwing `checkCanvas` before send above 268.4 MP). Note for the fix: `splitlayers.js:10-12` and `tools/ark_test.py:342, 896-897` currently assert `l.px.width === l.w` at `1200 × 800`, so if native ~2K resolution is kept on large/scaled-up splits (or above a pixel/arena budget), either gate `ark_test.py` and the header rule should be updated intentionally or baking should only happen when `row` is small.

3. **Not known & severity `must`:** Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, both 2026-11-07 `verified.json` files, `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`. In `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` (`host-gen/split-refuses-large-pictures`), large documents (>36 MP) were previously refused *before* any API call; the 0.1.56 fix (`splitSendSize` + `sampleRegionSettled`) opened the send gate for >268.4 MP and 15k documents while leaving `readyRow` unguarded, turning a pre-send refusal into a post-billing crash that loses paid API runs. Under the severity rubric, losing money / discarding a paid API result is `must`.

findings.claim: cropCanvasNow, resizeImageNow (including whole-image upscale), and extendCanvasNow (for a hidden Deep paint layer) replace a Deep paint layer's l.px at the new canvas dimensions and set l.dirty = true, but keep l.ref pointing at the old PNG and finish with notifyChanged() without calling syncLayers() or scheduleAutosave(). Autosave then writes the new document width/height alongside the old-sized l.ref, so an unclean exit before the next pixel edit or manual save either loses all paint on the Deep paint layer or stretches the uncropped/unextended PNG across the new canvas.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a 6000 x 6000 image (36 MP, >= pngStreamFrom = 32 MP; or any smaller image for the stretch case), compute surface maps, add a Deep paint layer, paint strokes on it, and wait ~1 s so scheduleAutosave's syncLayers() uploads the 6000 x 6000 paint PNG into l.ref.
2. Crop the canvas to 4000 x 4000 (or resize/upscale the image, or hide the Deep paint layer and extend the canvas), then wait 1.5 s for host.changed's debounced saveAll() to write autosave.json without making further pixel edits.
3. Kill or crash the app (before clean-quit flush) and relaunch so setValue() restores the autosave.
4. At >= 32 MP on tiles, pixelsOffThread decodes the old 6000 x 6000 PNG at its native size, setValue throws at pixels.width !== this.width, catches, logs a warning, and replaces the Deep paint layer with Layer.empty(4000, 4000), losing all paint; below 32 MP (or on the canvas backend), Layer.fromImage(limg, 4000, 4000) silently squashes the uncropped 6000 x 6000 paint into the 4000 x 4000 canvas.

findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js`, `cropCanvasNow` (:1391) replaces a Deep paint layer's `l.px` via `l.px.resized(nw, nh, { x: -left, y: -top })` and sets `l.dirty = true`, leaving `l.ref` pointing to the pre-crop PNG, and finishes at :1405-1406 with `this.followGeometry(...)` and `this.notifyChanged()` without calling `this.syncLayers()` or `this.scheduleAutosave()`. `resizeImageNow` (:1472, :1492 — including whole-picture upscale via `resizeImage(nw, nh, { base })`) and `extendCanvasNow` (:1642, :1649, :1658, :1681 — for a hidden Deep paint layer kept out of `flat`, as well as filter `maskPx` at :1390/:1470/:1648 and hidden full-canvas `paint` layers at :1652) do the exact same thing. By contrast, `turnDocumentNow` (:738-740) and `straightenDocumentNow` (:1092) explicitly run `this.syncLayers().catch(...)` with the comment that otherwise a crash before the next edit would restore the old layer files into the new geometry.

Tracing persistence and restore: `notifyChanged()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1347-1351`) calls `host.changed(this)` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:503-506`), which debounces `saveAll()` by 1500 ms (:534-538) and writes `ed.getValue()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:42-61`) into `autosave.json` with the new `width: nw, height: nh` alongside the old `ref: l.ref` (or `ref: null` if the user cropped before the initial 15 s `scheduleAutosave()` timer at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:297-304` had fired — note the candidate's scenario says ~1 s, whereas `scheduleAutosave` is actually 15000 ms, so once `l.ref` is uploaded after 15 s or a prior save/run, no timer is pending at all after the crop). Because non-pixel actions (filter sliders, prompt edits, selections, visibility) never call `scheduleAutosave()`, `l.ref` remains stale indefinitely until the next pixel/mask edit, `Generate` (`serializeForPrompt` at `inpaint_ed_persist.js:411`), `.scumble` save, or clean quit.

If the app crashes or is killed in that window and relaunches into `setValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:190-208`): (1) on tiles when the old PNG has `>= pngStreamFrom` pixels (`32 * 1024 * 1024` = 33,554,432 px at `inpaint_canvas.js:761`, e.g. 6000x6000 = 36 MP, decoded at native size by `pixelsOffThread` -> `hugePngSize` -> `pixelsFromPngStream` in `inpaint_load.js:291-302, 410-415`), line 200 throws on `pixels.width !== this.width || pixels.height !== this.height`, lines 201-206 catch, record `missing` (warning banner), and line 208 replaces the layer with `Layer.empty(nw, nh)`, losing all Deep paint strokes (for both crop/extend and resize/upscale >= 33.55 MP); (2) below `pngStreamFrom` or on the canvas backend, `pixelsOffThread` returns null and line 198 runs `this.pixels.Layer.fromImage(limg, this.width, this.height)` (`inpaint_pixels.js:172-176`, `inpaint_tiles.js:834-841`), which draws the old `W x H` PNG stretched across `nw x nh` and passes line 200 with no warning, silently squashing/shifting the uncropped or unextended paint on crop/extend (while `ref: null` silently restores empty at :208).

findings.claim: When a plain Deep paint layer (opacity 100%, normal blend, no layer mask or clip) has a feathered depth, luma, or colour limit (`params.limit`) over transparent or semi-transparent pixels, `limitStage` interpolates straight RGBA channels linearly (`mix(i, c, w)`). Because `applySurface` composites paint `over` transparent input (`c.a > i.a`) without setting `def.over`, `mix((0,0,0,0), (t, 1), w)` multiplies straight RGB by `w` as well as setting alpha to `w`, turning feathered limit edges dark/black on screen, in exports, and in banded run composites.
findings.scenario:
1. Open or create a picture with a transparent region (e.g. `B = (0, 0, 0, 0)` after erasing/cutting out on a transparent base or PNG), compute surface maps, and add a Deep paint layer (`opacity = 1`, `blend = "normal"`, no mask).
2. Paint bright colour onto the Deep paint layer across the transparent area (`applySurface` outputs `c = (tR, tG, tB, 255)` via straight-alpha `over`).
3. Add a `params.limit` (e.g. a depth or colour limit with feathering so `w = 0.5` across part of the stroke).
4. At `w = 0.5`, `limitStage` outputs straight RGBA `(0.5 * tR, 0.5 * tG, 0.5 * tB, 128)` instead of `(tR, tG, tB, 128)`, producing a dark halo (effective premultiplied intensity `0.25 * t` instead of `0.5 * t`) in both the viewport and exported PNG/TIFF files; nudging layer opacity from 100% to 99% flips `plain` to `false` (`limitOver = true`) and makes the halo suddenly jump back to the right brightness.
findings.evidence: In 0.1.57, `applySurface` and `SURFACE_GLSL` (renderer/editor/inpaint_surfacefx.js:149-155, 189-191) were updated so paint is composited `over` transparent input (`float ao = c.a + (1.0 - c.a) * p.a; vec3 v = clamp((b * c.a * (1.0 - p.a) + t * p.a) / ao, 0.0, 1.0); return vec4(s_toSrgb(v), ao);`), making `surface` the only filter without `over: true` (renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:1388-1397) that raises alpha (`c.a > i.a`). In `applyFilterLayer` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:598, 882, 1487) and `bandFilter` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:357-368), `this.isFillLayer(layer)` is `false`, so `plain` is `true` and `info.limitOver = !plain` is `false`. `limitStage` (renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:69) sets `const over = !!(def && def.over) || !!info.limitOver;` (`false`), so `LIMIT_SHADER` (:41) executes `mix(i, c, w)` and `limitStageCPU` (:186-189) computes `iR + (cR - iR) * w` and `iA + (cA - iA) * w` in straight RGBA.
findings.fix: In `LIMIT_SHADER` (renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:41) and `limitStageCPU` (:186-190), interpolate premultiplied RGBA when `u_over == 0`: `float ao = mix(i.a, c.a, w); vec3 rgb = ao > 1e-6 ? mix(i.rgb * i.a, c.rgb * c.a, w) / ao : vec3(0.0); return vec4(rgb, ao);`. When `i.a == c.a` this is identical to `mix(i, c, w)`, and when `i.a < c.a` it equals `applySurface` at effective paint alpha `w * p.a`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc`. Every line number and mathematical claim in the finding holds across both the WebGL2 and CPU paths and across both Canvas 2D screen/flatten rendering and the tiles banded export/run program.

**Reachability and guards checked:**
1. Transparent or semi-transparent pixels below a Deep paint layer are fully reachable: `computeSurfaceMaps` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:452, 455`) composites over `#808080` so surface maps compute cleanly on transparent PNGs/cutouts, or the user can erase/cut out on the base or layers below after computing maps.
2. `params.limit` (Depth, Luminosity, Colour) is explicitly exposed on Deep paint (`filter: "surface"`) layers in the layer panel (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:219, 248-256`, since `isFillLayer` is `false`) and in MCP (`renderer/commands_edit.js:81, 128-156`). All three limit sources produce smooth intermediate feather weights `0 < w < 1` across transparent or semi-transparent regions (`renderer/editor/inpaint_weights.js:192-222`: `depth` samples `maps.depth` independently of `i.a`; `color` evaluates `exp(-dd / (2 * s^2))` on `i.rgb`; `luma` feathers near 0 on `(0,0,0,0)` or across any semi-transparent `0 < i.a < 1` cutout edge).

**Exact straight- vs premultiplied-alpha trace:**
- All filter textures and `GLSurface` framebuffers store straight RGBA8 (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:500, 523, 681, 709`: WebGL2 context `premultipliedAlpha: false`, `UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL = false`).
- In `applySurface` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_surfacefx.js:145-154`) and `SURFACE_GLSL` (`:187-189`), painted pixels (`p.a > 0`) are composited `over` the backdrop `i` in straight alpha: `ao = i.a + (1 - i.a) * p.a` and `v = clamp((b * i.a * (1 - p.a) + t * p.a) / ao, 0, 1)`. Over transparent input `i = (0, 0, 0, 0)` with opaque paint `p.a = 1` (shaded sRGB colour `T`), `applySurface` outputs straight RGBA `c = (T, 1.0)`.
- `FILTERS.surface` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:1386-1395`) sets `ownPixels: true` without `over: true` (only `fill` at `:1359` and `gradient` at `:1378` set `over: true`). Therefore, for a default Deep paint layer (`opacity = 1`, `blend = "normal"`, no mask, no clip), `isFillLayer(layer)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:598`) is `false`, making `plain = true` in both `applyFilterLayer` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:1487`, note `preview` at `:1481` is also `false` whenever `this.viewPass` is set on screen) and `holdStackNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:258-259`). Both `filteredCanvas` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:882`) and `bandFilter` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:368`) set `info.limitOver = !plain = false`.
- `applyFilter` (`inpaint_filters.js:1482`) invokes `limitStage` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:55`), where line `69` computes `const over = !!(def && def.over) || !!info.limitOver;` -> `false` (`u_over = 0`).
- `LIMIT_SHADER` (`inpaint_limit.js:41`) then evaluates `mix(i, c, w)` component-wise in straight RGBA, and `limitStageCPU` (`:186-189`) likewise computes `iR + (cR - iR) * w` and `iA + (cA - iA) * w`. For `i = (0, 0, 0, 0)`, `c = (T, 1.0)`, and `w = 0.5`, this outputs straight RGBA `(0.5 * T, 0.5)` instead of `(T, 0.5)`.
- Downstream, on the screen/canvas path, `surfaceToCanvas` / `drawSurfaceTo` (`inpaint_filters_gl.js:615-636`) blits to `g.canvas` (`premultipliedAlpha: false`) and draws onto `ctx` after `if (plain) ctx.clearRect(...)` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:1593-1594`, `:1608`), so Canvas 2D premultiplies `(0.5 * T)` by alpha `0.5` to effective intensity `0.25 * T`. On the tiles program path (`programFinish` at `inpaint_ed_stack.js:470, 484`), `readSurfaceBytes` reads straight RGBA `(0.5 * T, 128)` directly into the exported PNG/TIFF or `readBoxBytes` buffer. Nudging layer opacity from 100% to 99% flips `plain` to `false` (`over = true`), switching line `41` to `vec4(c.rgb, c.a * w) = (T, 0.5)` and jumping the feathered edge back to full brightness `~0.495 * T`.

**Known-issues check:**
Not in `docs/BUGS.md`, `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, or `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`. In the 2026-11-14 0.1.56 release review (`docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md:530-531`, `docs/BUGS.md:100-101`), `applySurface` / `SURFACE_GLSL` were updated to composite `over` transparent backdrops in straight alpha, and `filters/band-filter-limit-not-over` (`review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:22-36`) fixed `bandFilter` missing `info.limitOver = !plain` for non-plain layers; this finding exposes an unaddressed interaction left by that 2026-11-14 `applySurface` change when `plain` is `true` (`surface` became the sole filter without `def.over` that raises `c.a > i.a`, while `limitStage`'s `u_over == 0` branch still assumes `i.a == c.a` or straight-channel lerp).

**Severity calibration (`should` vs `must`):**
Calibrated as `should` (matching the `filters/blur-backing-raises-alpha` precedent in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:280, 291`, in contrast to `filters/band-filter-limit-not-over` at `:24, 35`): the dark halo is immediately visible on screen (screen and export do not silently diverge), the Deep paint layer is non-destructive (`layer.px` retains the uncorrupted straight-RGBA paint with no data loss), it only affects feathered `params.limit` edges over transparent/semi-transparent pixels on a plain Deep paint layer, and users have a direct workaround (layer mask or 99% opacity).

findings.claim: On tile-backed 15k (15000 x 10000) documents, Deep paint bypasses worker mip-chain scheduling in both screen passes and settled sampled passes: `ownPixelsFor` drops `screen` / `display` from `vp` before calling `drawTilesInto`, and `passStores` omits `layer.px` for `ownPixels` filter layers. As a result, any zoomed-out draw or `sampleRegionSettled` call after a whole-layer change builds up to 2,360 mip chains synchronously on the main window thread (~500 ms frame stall) and permanently retains ~200 MB of mip buffers on the tiles.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a 15000 x 10000 document on tiles with surface maps, add a Deep paint layer, and fill a large selection (or crop, rotate, undo, or open a saved `.scumble` with full-canvas Deep paint) while viewing at fit zoom (`scale < 0.5`, mip level 3-4), or save/run Magic Wand while zoomed to 1:1.
2. On the next screen frame at fit zoom, `drawViewComposite` sets `this.viewPass.screen = true`, so the base and pixel layers offload missing mips to `ChainScheduler` after 16 tiles; however, `ownPixelsFor` creates `{ x: x0, y: y0, w: w / sx, h: h / sy, sx, sy }` without `screen` or `display`, forcing `layer.px.regionCanvas(..., level, false)` to run `plainChain` / `edgeChain` synchronously on the main thread for every painted tile (~500 ms stall).
3. At 1:1 zoom (where no mips exist on `layer.px`), `sampleRegionSettled` (Ctrl+S thumbnail, Magic Wand coarse flood, plugin settled flatten) calls `primePass` -> `passStores`, which skips `layer.px` because `layer.kind === "filter"`; `sampleRegion` then builds and permanently attaches 87 KB `t.mips` chains on the main thread (~200 MB across 2,360 tiles) instead of streaming transient single-level cells from the mips worker.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:794-797 in `ownPixelsFor`: `if (isTilePixels(layer.px)) { const vp = { x: x0, y: y0, w: w / sx, h: h / sy, sx, sy }; ctx.setTransform(sx, 0, 0, sy, -x0 * sx, -y0 * sy); this.drawTilesInto(ctx, layer.px, 0, 0, W, H, vp);` — contrast `applyFilterLayer`'s mask path in the same file (:1540, :1562), which preserves `screen`/`display` via `const mvp = { ...(fvp || vp), sx, sy };`. In `drawTilesInto` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_chrome.js:113-114), `const display = !!(vp.screen || vp.display); const rc = px.regionCanvas(..., level, display);` therefore passes `display = false`, which in `_levelBytes` (renderer/editor/inpaint_tiles.js:1088-1098) skips `ChainScheduler.request` and calls `edgeChain` / `plainChain` (:129-157) synchronously on the main thread. Second, in `passStores` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:844-850): `if (layer.kind === "filter") { if (!controlOnly && !skip) { add(this.liveMask(layer), 0, 0, this.width, this.height); drawn.add(layer); } continue; }` omits `if (this.hasOwnPixels(layer) && !this.liveStrokeOn(layer)) add(layer.px, 0, 0, this.width, this.height);`. Note also that `dropStaleViewCaches` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_draw.js:225) only clears `_fcacheView` / `_fcacheSample` for `i = from + 1` (strictly above `from`), and `filterKey` (inpaint_ed_filters.js:712-716) omits `layer.px.chainEpoch`.
findings.fix: 1) Propagate `screen` and `display` from `this.viewPass` into `ownPixelsFor`'s `vp` (`const curVp = this.viewPass; const vp = { ...(curVp ? { screen: curVp.screen, display: curVp.display } : null), x: x0, y: y0, w: w / sx, h: h / sy, sx, sy };`). 2) Include `layer.px.chainEpoch || 0` in `filterKey` when `(vp?.screen || vp?.display)` and `ownPixels` (or clear `l._fcacheView` / `l._fcacheSample` starting at `i = from` when `this.hasOwnPixels(this.layers[from])` in `dropStaleViewCaches`) so coarse mips do not stay cached after worker chains land. 3) In `passStores` (inpaint_ed_stack.js:846), also call `if (this.hasOwnPixels(layer) && !this.liveStrokeOn(layer)) add(layer.px, 0, 0, this.width, this.height);`.
findings.why:
Both call paths hold at f45a86cc. First, during any zoomed-out screen draw (`scale < 0.5`, `tileLevel >= 1`) with a visible Deep paint layer (`layer.kind === "filter"`, `FILTERS.surface.ownPixels === true`), `glCompositeUsable` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_display.js:279`) returns `false`, so `drawViewComposite` (`:413-415`) sets `this.viewPass = { x: region.x, y: region.y, w: region.w, h: region.h, sx, sy, screen: true }` and runs `drawComposite` -> `drawLayersInto` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:81`) -> `applyFilterLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1509-1511`). `applyFilterLayer` keeps `screen: true` on `this.viewPass` (`fvp` at `:1504`), and its own filter-mask tile path at `:1540, :1562` preserves `screen`/`display` via `const mvp = { ...(fvp || vp), sx, sy };`. However, `filteredCanvas` (`:869-884`) -> `applyFilter("surface", ...)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_surfacefx.js:124, 207`) invokes `info.own` -> `ownPixelsFor` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:775-808`), which at `:795-797` constructs `const vp = { x: x0, y: y0, w: w / sx, h: h / sy, sx, sy };` without `screen` or `display` and calls `this.drawTilesInto(ctx, layer.px, 0, 0, W, H, vp)`. In `drawTilesInto` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_chrome.js:113-114`), `display` evaluates to `false`, so `layer.px.regionCanvas(..., level, false)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_tiles.js:2333, 2399`) writes into `SAMPLE_REGION` and calls `_levelBytes(tx, ty, level, false)` (`:1067-1099`), bypassing the `if (display)` `ChainScheduler` budget (`CHAIN_SYNC_BUDGET = 16` at `:208`, `:1088-1097`) and running `edgeChain` / `plainChain` (`:129-157`) synchronously on the main thread for every allocated tile in view (up to 59 x 40 = 2,360 tiles on a 15000 x 10000 canvas, ~420-510 ms main-thread stall per `:902-903` and `tools/perf_test.py:294`). The cache-invalidation corollary in the finding also holds: when worker chains land on `l.px`, `watchChains` -> `staleViewCachesAbove` -> `dropStaleViewCaches` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_draw.js:160-166, 217-233`) only clears `_fcacheView` / `_fcacheSample` for `i = from + 1` (strictly above `from`), and `filterKey` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:712-716`) checks `layer.px.version` without `layer.px.chainEpoch`, so fixing `ownPixelsFor` requires invalidating `from` as well when `this.hasOwnPixels(this.layers[from])`.

Second, in settled sampled passes (`sampleRegionSettled` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:892-903`, called by `documentThumbnail` on Ctrl+S at `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:58, 242`, Magic Wand / Bucket coarse flood at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1107`, and `Document.flatten({ maxSize, settled: true })` at `renderer/plugins.js:113`), `primePass` (`:877`) calls `passStores` (`:812-865`). At `inpaint_ed_stack.js:844-850`, `if (layer.kind === "filter")` adds only `this.liveMask(layer)` and `continue`s without adding `layer.px` when `this.hasOwnPixels(layer)`. Whenever `layer.px` lacks up-to-date `t.mips` (e.g. while working at 1:1 zoom, or right after a whole-layer fill, crop, turn, undo, or open), `primeRegion` (`inpaint_tiles.js:916`) never primes transient single-level cells from the mips worker, and `sampleRegion` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:76-78`) then runs with `display: false`, building and permanently retaining 87,296-byte `t.mips` buffers on the main thread (~206 MB across 2,360 tiles, plus ~25.7 MB `e.data` across 98 edge tiles) instead of releasing single-level worker cells in `finally` (`:901`). `tools/perf_test.py --filter=surface` missed both paths because setup (`:174-189`) draws at fit before timing starts and the whole-change / `panel_flatten_settled` block (`:281-282, 405`) hides `fxLayer`.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including the 0.1.56 Deep paint review entry at `:96-105`, the `cropFilterInput` pan entry at `:111`, and K12's `belowStats` relight entry at `:134`), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md` (`:344-350`, which notes only steady-state `getImageData` + upload cost), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the three `verified.json` files; this defect is not known. Severity is `should`: no pixels or user data are lost, but normal workflows on 15k tiled documents hit ~500 ms main-thread freezes and ~200 MB of permanently retained mip buffers, matching the `should` calibration of comparable 15k main-thread stall and memory-retention bugs in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`.

findings.claim: When a Deep paint layer is active and the toolbar's `Sample` selector is set to `"layer"`, `sampleRegion`, `sampleCanvas`, `floodStack`, and `passStores` all reject `l.kind === "filter"` without checking `this.hasOwnPixels(l)` and silently fall through to compositing the entire visible image. In Eyedropper this also bypasses `surfaceAlbedo` (which `pickColor` disables when `sample === "layer"`), picking shaded composite colours even over unpainted areas, while Bucket and Magic Wand flood the shaded composite instead of the Deep paint layer's own paint.
findings.scenario:
1. Add a Deep paint layer, paint a flat `#c03020` shape on part of it, and switch the options bar `Sample` dropdown from `image` to `layer`.
2. With Eyedropper (or Alt+click with the brush), click an unpainted area of the Deep paint layer: instead of reporting `"Transparent here, nothing to pick."` (as on a paint layer), `pickColor` skips `surfaceAlbedo` because `sample === "layer"` and `sampleRegion("layer")` falls through to `drawComposite`, picking the raw shaded base colour (which turns double-shaded if painted onto the Deep paint layer). Clicking the `#c03020` paint likewise picks the lit/reflected composite pixel instead of `#c03020`.
3. With Bucket or Magic Wand and `Sample: layer`, click inside or outside the painted `#c03020` patch: `floodStack("layer")` and `sampleRegion("layer")` fall through to the full composite stack, so the flood stops on photo shadows/highlights below instead of flooding the Deep paint layer's own pixels.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_chrome.js:299-301 exposes `Sample: ["image", "layer"]` for `bucket eyedropper wand`. In `pickColor` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shape.js:283-286): `const surface = sample !== "layer" && this.hasOwnPixels(layer) && this.hasSurfaceMaps() ? layer : null; const d = this.sampleRegion(surface ? "image" : sample, [x0, y0, x1, y1], 1, ...)` — turning off `surfaceAlbedo` when `sample === "layer"`. Severity `should` holds: users working on a Deep paint layer hit broken layer-only colour picking, flood filling, and wand selection in normal workflows, though no persisted data or paid run output is silently corrupted.

findings.claim: A live Wrap link (`l.wrap`) tags its creation geometry with `this.geometryToken()` (`this.geometrySeq`), which increments monotonically on every whole-document geometry operation and is never restored on undo. Undoing a crop, turn, resize, or straighten restores `l.wrap` from the snapshot and calls `notifyChanged()` -> `syncWraps()`, which sees `w.geo !== this.geometryToken()` and immediately clears `l.wrap = null`; conversely, if `maps.normals` is absent during a geometry op, `syncWraps()` skips pruning `l.wrap`, allowing `getValue()` / `wrapLink()` to persist pre-geometry `x, y, w, h, box` coordinates without `geo`.
findings.scenario:
1. Wrap a decal layer `D` onto a surface (`wrapLayer` sets `WL.wrap.geo = 0`, hides `D`, and selects Transform).
2. Crop or rotate the canvas (`geometrySeq` becomes `1`), then immediately press Ctrl+Z to undo the crop/rotate.
3. `applySnapshot` restores the pre-crop canvas, surface maps, `D`, and `WL.wrap` (`geo: 0`), then calls `notifyChanged()` -> `syncWraps()`. Because `this.geometryToken()` is still `1 !== 0`, `syncWraps` sets `WL.wrap = null`, silently severing the live wrap link so dragging `D` no longer moves the wrap.
4. Conversely, if `maps.normals` was cleared before cropping and saving `.scumble`, `syncWraps` returns early at `!this.maps.normals`, `getValue()` writes the uncropped `WL.wrap`, `wrapLink` strips `geo` on reopen, and recomputing normals + moving any layer causes `putWrap` to clear the wrong pre-crop `w.box` without an undo step.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:493 sets `out.wrap = { ..., geo: this.geometryToken() };` where `geometryToken()` returns `this.geometrySeq` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:853-855). `turnDocumentNow` (:704), `followGeometry` (:873), and `straightenDocumentNow` (:1059) in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js bump `this.geometrySeq++`, while `restoreGeometry` (:851-860) restores `this.docXf` without restoring `geometrySeq`. On undo of a `turn` or `canvas` step, `applySnapshot` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:737, 780) calls `this.notifyChanged()` -> `this.syncWraps()` (renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1348), hitting `if (w.geo !== this.geometryToken()) { l.wrap = null; continue; }` (inpaint_ed_filters.js:517). Meanwhile line 507 (`if (this._syncingWraps || !this.layers || !this.maps || !this.maps.normals) return false;`) skips pruning when `normals` is absent, and `getValue` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:60) writes `l.wrap` while `wrapLink` (:20-26) drops `geo`.
findings.fix: Clear `l.wrap = null` explicitly inside `turnDocumentNow`, `straightenDocumentNow`, `cropCanvasNow`, `resizeImageNow`, and `extendCanvasNow` (so stale links never survive onto `getValue()` even without `maps.normals`), and compare `w.geo` against `this.docXf.join(",")` (which `restoreGeometry` restores on undo) instead of monotonic `this.geometrySeq`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc. When `wrapLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:422-451`) creates a live wrap layer, `putWrap` (`:475-498`) writes `out.wrap = { source: src.id, ..., stamp, geo: this.geometryToken() }` (`:493`), where `geometryToken()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:853-855`) returns `this.geometrySeq` (initialised to `0` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:255`). Every whole-document geometry operation takes its `canvas` undo snapshot (`snapshotLayer` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:176-177`, which preserves `c.wrap` pointing at `{ ..., geo: 0 }`) before bumping `this.geometrySeq++` (`turnDocumentNow` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:660, 704`; `straightenDocumentNow` at `:969, 1059`; `cropCanvasNow` at `:1381, 1405`, `resizeImageNow` at `:1436, 1491`, and `extendCanvasNow` at `:1581, 1674` via `followGeometry` at `:873`), and ends with `this.notifyChanged()` -> `this.syncWraps()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1348`). In `syncWraps` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:517`), `if (w.geo !== this.geometryToken()) { l.wrap = null; continue; }` nulls `l.wrap` on the live layer while the snapshot's copy retains `{ ..., geo: 0 }`.

When the user presses Ctrl+Z (or restores a `turn` snapshot via `restoreTurn`), `applySnapshot` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:687, 737` for `turn`; `:749, 757, 780` for `canvas`) calls `this.restoreGeometry(snap)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:851-860`), which restores `this.docXf = snap.xf.slice()` (`:855`) and maps `this.maps` back to the pre-op geometry via `mapExtras(D, "undo")` without restoring `this.geometrySeq`, installs the snapshot's layer copies (with `w.geo === 0`), and calls `this.notifyChanged()` -> `this.syncWraps()`. Because `this.geometryToken()` is still `1 !== 0`, `syncWraps` at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:517` immediately executes `l.wrap = null`, silently severing the live wrap link even though the canvas, layers, and surface maps are back in their exact pre-op geometry (leaving the hidden source `D` active on the Transform tool while dragging it no longer updates the wrap).

The lazy-pruning half of the finding also holds — and is even broader than the missing-`normals` case: none of the five geometry functions clears `l.wrap` directly, relying entirely on `syncWraps()`. When `this.maps.normals` is absent (e.g. a `.scumble` opened with a missing normals map at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:376`, or maps cleared via `setMaps`), `syncWraps` returns early at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:507`, so `getValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:60`) persists the pre-crop `l.wrap` and `wrapLink()` (`:20-26`) strips `geo` on reopen. Moreover, even when `maps.normals` IS present, `setValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:234, 383-390`) and `openDocument` / `settleKey` (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:91-107, 296-312`) never call `syncWraps()`, leaving `w.geo === undefined` until the first `notifyChanged()`; if the user's first edit after reopening a `.scumble` is a crop, turn, straighten, or resize, `geometrySeq` increments before `syncWraps()` runs, so line 515 (`if (w.geo === undefined) w.geo = this.geometryToken()`) stamps the post-op token onto the pre-op `w` and line 524 runs `putWrap`, clearing the wrong pre-op `w.box` (`:476-480`) on the already-cropped/turned layer.

Not `known`: `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md:526-528` and `docs/BUGS.md:99` record that the 2026-11-14 release review added `w.geo` to fix 'a wrap link after a turn or crop'; this finding proves two remaining defects in that new 2026-11-14 fix (undoing the geometry op drops the restored link, and lazy `syncWraps` pruning misses geometry ops when `normals` is absent or right after `setValue`). The older 2026-11-07 entry `canvas-b/undo-geometry-no-seq-bump` concerned `computeDepthMap` in-flight token invalidation before Deep paint existed (and bumping `geometrySeq` in `restoreGeometry` would still leave `w.geo !== geometryToken()`). Severity is `should`: wrapping a decal, testing a crop or rotation, and pressing Ctrl+Z (or reopening a `.scumble` and cropping first) is a 100% deterministic normal workflow with a manual workaround (unhide the source and run Wrap onto Surface again).

findings.claim: A Wrap layer loaded from a `.scumble` file or session autosave has `wrap.geo === undefined` until `syncWraps()` first runs, and `setValue()` never calls `notifyChanged()` or `syncWraps()` after loading layers and maps. If the user's first edit on the opened document is a canvas geometry operation (crop, rotate 90°, extend, resize, or straighten), `syncWraps()` stamps `w.geo` with the post-operation `geometryToken()` instead of detaching, clears `out.wrap.box` at the old pre-operation coordinates on the already-transformed Deep paint layer, and re-wraps over it.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a picture, compute surface maps, add a logo/text layer, rotate or place it, run *Layer › Wrap onto Surface*, and save as `test.scumble` (or restart Scumble to restore from autosave).
2. Reopen `test.scumble` (`openDocument` -> `restore` -> `setValue`). All layers and maps are clean, so `flushEditor` neither calls `syncLayers()` nor `storeMaps()`, and for <=16 MP (or empty tiled selections) `getValue()` encodes the selection without calling `notifyChanged()`. `l.wrap.geo` remains `undefined`.
3. Run *Image › Rotate 90° CW*, *Straighten*, or *Crop*.
4. `turnDocumentNow` / `cropCanvasNow` / `straightenDocumentNow` increments `geometrySeq`, transforms `l.px` (moving the wrapped pixels to their new canvas position) and updates `src.x, src.y, src.w, src.h` without updating `l.wrap.box`, then calls `notifyChanged()` -> `syncWraps()`. `syncWraps()` sets `w.geo = this.geometryToken()` (the new token), fails to detach `l.wrap`, sees `src.x !== w.x`, clears `old = out.wrap.box` at the stale pre-turn/pre-crop coordinates (erasing the wrong rectangle of `l.px` and leaving ghost wrapped pixels outside the new box), and re-wraps.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:20-26` (`wrapLink`) returns `{ source: w.source, angle: n(w.angle) || 0, x: w.x, y: w.y, w: w.w, h: w.h, box }` without `geo`. In `setValue` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:133-138`), `setBasePixels`/`setBase` runs while `this.layers` is `[]` and `this.maps` is unset; layers are pushed at `inpaint_ed_persist.js:234` (`wrap: wrapLink(l.wrap)`), maps are loaded at `inpaint_ed_persist.js:361-381`, and lines `382-390` end with `this.draw(); this.drawThumb();` without calling `notifyChanged()` or `syncWraps()`. Then in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:515-524`: `if (w.geo === undefined) w.geo = this.geometryToken(); if (w.geo !== this.geometryToken()) { l.wrap = null; continue; } ... const made = this.wrapPixels(src, w.angle || 0, { useSelection: false }); this.putWrap(l, src, made && !made.error ? made : null);`, and `putWrap` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:478-480`) wipes `const old = out.wrap && out.wrap.box` via `out.px.writeRect(..., old[0], old[1], "copy")` in the new coordinate space.
findings.fix: Stamp `geo: this.geometryToken()` when restoring the layer in `setValue` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:234`, e.g. `const wl = wrapLink(l.wrap); ... wrap: wl ? { ...wl, geo: this.geometryToken() } : null`), so any subsequent geometry operation sees `w.geo !== this.geometryToken()` and detaches `l.wrap = null` as intended.
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:20-26`, `wrapLink(w)` reconstructs a stored wrap link as `{ source, angle, x, y, w, h, box }` without `geo` (`w.geo === undefined`). During `setValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:108-396`), `setBasePixels` / `setBase` (`:133-138`) calls `notifyChanged()` (`inpaint_ed_open.js:154`) while `this.layers` is still `[]` and `this.maps` is unset, so `syncWraps()` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:507`) returns early. Layers are then pushed at `:227-235` (`wrap: wrapLink(l.wrap)`, `dirty: false`, `maskDirty: false`) and `:266-275`, maps are loaded at `:361-381` with `map.ref = j.ref` (`inpaint_maps.js:414`), and `setValue()` ends at `:382-390` (`renderLayers()`, `draw()`, `drawThumb()`) without calling `notifyChanged()` or `syncWraps()`.

Tracing the callers after `setValue()`: although a cold app startup's session restore (`renderer/shell.js:1490-1504`) happens to call `selectRecipe()` afterwards (`applyRecipe` at `host_presets.js:636` -> `settingsChanged` at `inpaint_canvas.js:1017` -> `notifyChanged` -> `syncWraps`), every open/restore path that runs once `host.recipe` is already set—including `host.openDocument` (`host_documents.js:273-313`, covering File > Open, `.scumble` drag-and-drop, MCP `open_document`, and startup CLI `.scumble` files in `openPendingDocuments` at `shell.js:1508`), `host.reopenClosed` (`host_documents.js:356-378`), `openGeneration` (`shell_settings.js`), and offline `host.onConnected` (`host_setup.js:193,203`, where `settingsChanged()` runs before `setValue()`)—runs `applyRecipe` on the empty editor before `setValue()` and only `keepRecipeMode()` (`host_presets.js:624-628`, which does not call `notifyChanged()`) afterwards. In `openDocument`, `settleKey` -> `flushEditor` (`host_documents.js:29-52,91-107`) skips `syncLayers()` because all layers loaded clean, skips `storeMaps()` because `mapsUnstored()` is empty, and calls `getValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:31-41`), which synchronously encodes selections up to `SYNC_ENCODE_PX` (16 MP, `inpaint_consts.js:109`) without calling `notifyChanged()` (and above 16 MP on tiles with an empty selection, `encodeSelectionSoon` at `inpaint_canvas.js:1366-1370` likewise returns synchronously without `notifyChanged()`). Thus `l.wrap.geo` remains `undefined` when the document becomes interactive.

When the user's first edit is a whole-document geometry operation—`turnDocumentNow` (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:678-704,737`), `straightenDocumentNow` (`:1049-1060,1091`), `cropCanvasNow` (`:1391-1394,1405-1406`), `resizeImageNow` (`:1472-1476,1491-1492`), or `extendCanvasNow` when the wrap layer is hidden (`:1642-1657,1674,1681`)—the operation transforms the Deep paint layer's `l.px` into the new canvas space, updates the hidden source layer's `[x, y, w, h]` (and rotates `src.px` on turns/straighten) without touching `l.wrap`, increments `this.geometrySeq++` (`geometryToken()`, `inpaint_ed_depth.js:853-855`), and calls `this.notifyChanged()` -> `this.syncWraps()`. At `inpaint_ed_filters.js:515-517`, `if (w.geo === undefined) w.geo = this.geometryToken();` stamps the post-operation token, so `w.geo !== this.geometryToken()` fails to detach `l.wrap`. Unless `src`'s rectangle happened not to change numerically, `syncWraps()` (`:521-525`) calls `wrapPixels` and `putWrap` (`:475-498`), which clears `old = out.wrap.box` (the stale pre-operation coordinates) on the already-transformed `out.px`—erasing the wrong region and leaving ghost transformed wrap pixels outside the new `made.box`—and writes a re-wrapped decal (using the already-turned `src.px` with the old `w.angle` on turns) while leaving `l.wrap` live.

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including `Deep paint: small points left from the 0.1.56 release review` at `:96-106`), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md:526-528`, all three `verified.json` files, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`. Detaching `l.wrap` via `geo` on turns/crops was added in the 2026-11-14 release review fix (`PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md:526-528`), and `tools/deeppaint_test.py:711-728,836-854` undid the wrap layer before testing turns/crops and `.scumble` reopen; this is a genuine, unrecorded hole in that new fix. Severity is `should`: opening a `.scumble` document and immediately cropping, rotating 90°, or straightening is a normal workflow that visibly corrupts the Wrap layer's pixels (and uploads them via `syncLayers()`), though `Ctrl+Z` recovers the untouched pre-operation `l.px` held in the `canvas` undo snapshot.

findings.claim: `wrapLayer` explicitly invites wrapping paint layers (`kind === "paint"`), which are created at full canvas size (`0, 0, W, H`). `wrapPixels` reads the entire `src.px` via `readRect(0, 0, src.px.width, src.px.height)` and sizes `wrapBox` from `src.w, src.h`, causing a ~3.6 GB synchronous main-thread allocation (and renderer OOM crash / multi-second freeze) on a 15,000 × 10,000 document while unwrapping from the canvas centre `(W/2, H/2)` instead of the painted content's centre.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a 15,000 × 10,000 image on tiles and compute surface maps.
2. Click *Add paint layer* (`addPaintLayer` creates an empty `15000 × 10000` tiled layer with `x = 0, y = 0, w = 15000, h = 10000`), paint a small 300 × 300 logo at `(2000, 3000)`, and run *Layer › Wrap onto Surface* (or MCP `wrap_layer`).
3. `wrapPixels` computes `place = { cx: 7500, cy: 5000, w: 15000, h: 10000 }` and `box = [0, 0, 15000, 10000]` (150 MP), allocates 600 MB in `src.px.readRect(0, 0, 15000, 10000)`, 1.2 GB in `wrapSlopes`/`wrapSlopesPoints` (`gx, gy`), 1.2 GB in `wrapCoords` (`u, v`), and 600 MB in `wrapDecal` (`out`) synchronously on the window thread (~3.6 GB live at once), freezing or OOM-crashing the renderer and integrating surface arc-length from `(7500, 5000)` instead of `(2150, 3150)`.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:424` invites paint layers: `"Select a picture, paint or text layer to wrap (a logo, a pattern, a word)."` `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:559-562` (`addPaintLayer`) sets `px: this.pixels.Layer.empty(this.width, this.height), x: 0, y: 0, w: this.width, h: this.height`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:458-471` (`wrapPixels`): `const place = { cx: src.x + src.w / 2, cy: src.y + src.h / 2, w: src.w, h: src.h, angle }; const box = wrapBox(place, this.width, this.height, ...); ... const decal = src.px.readRect(0, 0, src.px.width, src.px.height);`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_wrap.js:37,110,147,255` allocate four `Float32Array(w * h)` buffers and one `Uint8ClampedArray(w * h * 4)` over `box`.
findings.fix: Trim `wrapPixels` to the non-empty pixel bounds of `src.px` (using `src.px.bounds()` on `TilePixels`, or scanning alpha on smaller canvas layers) mapped into document coordinates for `place` and `src.px.readRect(...)`, and refuse `wrapPixels` with a clear message if the resulting `box` area still exceeds a safe cap (e.g. 36–64 MP).
findings.why:
Every step of the claim and call path holds at commit f45a86cc. All three entry points to `wrapLayer` — *Layer › Wrap onto Surface* (`renderer/shell.js:1398`), the layer panel's Deep paint menu (`renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js:444`, tooltip: "The active picture, paint or text layer laid round the surface it lies on"), and MCP `wrap_layer` (`renderer/commands_edit.js:115-126`) — as well as `wrapLayer`'s own guard at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:424` ("Select a picture, paint or text layer to wrap (a logo, a pattern, a word).") explicitly invite wrapping `paint` layers (`kind === "paint"`). However, `addPaintLayer()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:556-565`) creates every paint layer at full document dimensions (`px: this.pixels.Layer.empty(this.width, this.height), x: 0, y: 0, w: this.width, h: this.height`), and painting strokes onto it (`commitStroke` / `commitStrokeTiles` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:433-510`) keeps `x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = H` and `px` sized `W × H` (sparse tiles in `TileLayerPixels`).

When `wrapLayer` calls `wrapPixels(src, angle)` synchronously on the window thread (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:428, 457-472`), line 458 sets `place = { cx: src.x + src.w / 2, cy: src.y + src.h / 2, w: src.w, h: src.h, angle }` without trimming to `src.px.bounds()`, and line 459 computes `wrapBox(place, this.width, this.height, ...)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_wrap.js:171-176`), where `r = 0.5 * Math.hypot(W, H) * Math.max(1, grow) + 2` always exceeds half of both sides and clamps `box` to the entire `[0, 0, W, H]`. That causes two defects: (1) on any document size, `wrapCoords` (`inpaint_wrap.js:146-161`) and `wrapSlopesPoints` (`inpaint_wrap.js:107-109`) integrate surface arc-length and sample reference depth `z_c` from the canvas centre `(W/2, H/2)` rather than the painted decal's centre, misplacing and distorting off-centre painted decals across curved surfaces or occlusion jumps; and (2) on a 15,000 × 10,000 (150 MP) document, line 470 (`src.px.readRect(0, 0, src.px.width, src.px.height)` -> `TilePixels.readRect` at `inpaint_tiles.js:1397`) allocates a 600 MB `ImageData`, and `wrapDecal` (`inpaint_wrap.js:243-281`) simultaneously holds `gx, gy` (`2 × Float32Array(150e6)` = 1.2 GB at lines 37 / 110), `u, v` (`2 × Float32Array(150e6)` = 1.2 GB at line 147), and `out` (`Uint8ClampedArray(600e6)` = 600 MB at line 255) — 3.6 GB of live typed arrays (plus 750 MB more in lines 464-465 if a selection is active) and ~450M+ synchronous JS pixel iterations on the renderer main thread (~25 s hang or renderer OOM crash; even larger up to 1 GiP on tiles).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including `Deep paint: small points left from the 0.1.56 release review` at lines 96-106 and `Size limits` at lines 162-189), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md` (line 425 only timed 1000×600 and 3000×2000 decals), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (all predating Deep paint on 2026-11-13..14): this defect is not recorded anywhere. Severity `should` fits strictly: users are explicitly invited to wrap paint layers in normal workflows, hitting wrong unwrap geometry at any size and a multi-gigabyte main-thread hang / OOM crash on 15k+ documents, with a workaround of copying the painted region to a bounded layer first.

findings.claim: `packPoints` writes `[0, 0, 0]` into the `rgb16` points map at masked-out texels (`mask < 0.5`), which `wrapSlopesPoints`'s bilinear sampler `P()` decodes as `[lo[0], lo[1], lo[2]]` (the scene's minimum X/Y and nearest Z, with `lo[2] > 0`). This causes severe 3D slope spikes (`gx`/`gy` 10×–400× too large) along the ~0.5-map-texel silhouette rim of every masked object, and defeats the `if (!(c0[2] > 0)) return null` fallback when a decal's centre lies on an unmasked sky/background region.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a 3000 × 2000 outdoor portrait or product photo where MoGe-2 masks out the sky (`mask = 0` in sky, `mask = 255` on the subject at `z = 2.0 m`, scene `lo = [-0.8, -0.6, 1.5]`), and compute surface maps.
2. Case A: Place a decal extending to the subject's silhouette edge against the sky and wrap it. At foreground pixels within half a map texel (~2–10 document px) of the sky texel, nearest-neighbour `masked(px, py)` is still `false` (`alpha = 255`), while `P(px - 0.5, py)` and `P(px + 0.5, py)` bilinearly interpolate between `[X, Y, 2.0]` and the sky texel's decoded `[lo[0], lo[1], lo[2]] = [-0.8, -0.6, 1.5]`. `|b - a| / unit` spikes by orders of magnitude, crushing/tearing the decal along the silhouette.
3. Case B: Centre a wide pattern or text over a sky gap between two foreground surfaces. `P(cx, cy)` decodes `[0, 0, 0]` as `c0[2] = lo[2] = 1.5 > 0`, so `!(c0[2] > 0)` does not return `null`; instead of falling back to `wrapSlopes`, it uses the scene's nearest depth `lo[2]` as the centre depth and shrinks the decal across the foreground.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_surface.js:235-236,255-262` (`packPoints`): only `z > 0` points enter `lo`, so `lo[2] > 0`, and pixels failing `mask[i] >= 0.5` stay `0` in `Uint16Array`. (Compare `disparityFromPoints` at `inpaint_surface.js:271-272`: "a bilinear sample across the mask's border would mix a kept point with the 0 of a dropped one".) In `renderer/editor/inpaint_wrap.js:95-108` (`wrapSlopesPoints`): `out[c] = lo[c] + ((top + (bot - top) * fy) / 65535) * sp[c]; ... const c0 = P(cx, cy, [0, 0, 0]); if (!(c0[2] > 0)) return null;`. At lines `123-129`: `if (masked(px, py)) { gx[i] = 1; gy[i] = 1; continue; } P(px - 0.5, py, a); P(px + 0.5, py, b); gx[i] = Math.max(0.05, Math.hypot(b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1], b[2] - a[2]) / unit);`.
findings.fix: Check the mask (or all-zero point texel) on `(cx, cy)` so `wrapSlopesPoints` returns `null` when the centre tap is unmasked (and `wrapGrow` returns `1`), and in `P()` / the finite-difference step require all four bilinear taps of `P` to be unmasked—falling back to nearest kept neighbour or the orthographic normal slope (`wrapSlopes` formula) at silhouette boundary pixels where any tap is masked out.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc across `renderer/editor/inpaint_surface.js`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_wrap.js`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js`, and `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js`. In `packPoints` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_surface.js:228-265`), the bounds loop (`:233-239`) only includes pixels with `mask[i] >= 0.5`, `z > 0`, and `Number.isFinite(z)`, requiring `kept >= 16` (`:240`), so `meta.lo[2]` is strictly positive (`lo[2] > 0`) on every non-null return, while `lo[0]` and `lo[1]` hold the scene-wide minimum camera-space X and Y. In the u16 packing loop (`:255-263`), pixels failing `mask[i] >= 0.5` or `points[3 * i + 2] > 0` are skipped and remain `[0, 0, 0]` in `new Uint16Array(n * 3)` (an invariant explicitly noted in `disparityFromPoints` at `inpaint_surface.js:271-274`).

When *Layer › Wrap onto Surface*, MCP `wrap_layer`, or live `syncWraps` runs (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:422-472,506-525`), `computeSurfaceMaps` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:449,467-472`) has populated both `maps.normals` and `maps.points` at `surfaceModelSize(W, H)` (long side 768, e.g. ~3.91 doc px/texel at 3000w and ~19.53 doc px/texel at 15000w), so `wrapDecal` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_wrap.js:247`) always enters `wrapSlopesPoints(points, map, box, place.cx, place.cy)` (`inpaint_wrap.js:84-133`). Inside `wrapSlopesPoints`, the bilinear sampler `P(dx, dy, out)` (`:95-106`) decodes raw `Uint16Array` values via `out[c] = lo[c] + ((top + (bot - top) * fy) / 65535) * sp[c]` (`:103`) without checking the mask on any of its four taps `(i00, i10, i01, i11)`. Any `[0, 0, 0]` masked-out texel therefore decodes to `[lo[0], lo[1], lo[2]]` rather than zero.

Both failure modes hold with no mitigating guards: (1) At lines `107-108`, `const c0 = P(cx, cy, [0, 0, 0]); if (!(c0[2] > 0)) return null;` is dead code for every `packPoints` map because `top, bot >= 0`, `sp[2] >= 0`, and `lo[2] > 0` guarantee `c0[2] >= lo[2] > 0` everywhere, even when `(cx, cy)` sits on masked-out sky or background; instead of returning `null` to fall back to `wrapSlopes(map, box)` (`:247`), `wrapSlopesPoints` uses `lo[2]` (the scene's nearest kept depth) as `c0[2]` and scales the entire decal by the wrong perspective depth. (2) In the pixel loop (`:119-131`), `masked(px, py)` (`:114-118`) tests nearest-neighbour `Math.floor(u)` on `nmap`'s alpha (`< 128`), whereas `P(px ± 0.5, py)` and `P(px, py ± 0.5)` (`:126-129`) sample bilinearly around map texel centres (`qu = u * pw - 0.5`). On every unmasked foreground pixel within ~0.5 map texels of a masked-out texel (`qu` between `u0` and `u0 + 0.5`, where `masked(px, py)` is still `false`), `P` linearly blends the foreground 3D point with `[lo[0], lo[1], lo[2]]`; there is only a lower floor `Math.max(0.05, ...)` and no upper clamp on `gx`/`gy`, so `|b - a| / unit` spikes by two orders of magnitude, crushing the decal across the foreground silhouette rim and permanently shifting `wrapCoords`'s integrated `u`/`v` (`:146-160`) along any row or column that grazes a silhouette or crosses an internal `mask < 0.5` patch.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Fixed` at `:18-20` covers only `relightNormalOnMask` sky normals, ViT-S selection, and map upload retry; `## Open` at `:96-106` lists only source layer opacity/mask/blend in `wrapPixels` and older-version autosave compatibility), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md` (§6 `:521-537`), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: this defect is not recorded anywhere. Severity is `should`: it corrupts wrapped decal pixels baked onto the Deep paint layer (and exports) in normal workflows on photos with sky or masked regions, while preserving the hidden source layer and undo step as a workaround.

findings.claim: `syncWraps` checks only `src.x, src.y, src.w, src.h` and `l.px._wrapStamp !== w.stamp`, never whether the source layer's pixels (`src.px` or `src.px.version`) changed. In-place edits to the active wrapped source layer that preserve its bounding box—such as changing a text layer's colour, editing text to the same dimensions, flipping the source layer horizontally/vertically, rotating a square decal 90°, or painting on the source layer—leave the Wrap layer displaying stale pixels.
findings.scenario:
1. Add a text layer (or image/paint decal), select it, and run *Layer › Wrap onto Surface*. `wrapLayer` hides the source layer and keeps it active.
2. In the active text layer's controls in the Layers panel, change the text colour from white to red (or click *Flip Horizontal* on an image decal).
3. `renderTextLayer` (`inpaint_ed_text.js:129,145`) or `flipLayer` (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:411,417`) replaces `src.px` and calls `markLayerChanged(src)` -> `notifyChanged()` -> `syncWraps()`, while `src.x, src.y, src.w, src.h` remain unchanged.
4. `syncWraps` hits `if (!stale && src.x === w.x && src.y === w.y && src.w === w.w && src.h === w.h) continue;` and skips re-wrapping, leaving the canvas and any export showing the old white / unflipped wrap until the user nudges the layer's position.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:493` (`putWrap`): `out.wrap = { source: src.id, angle: ..., x: src.x, y: src.y, w: src.w, h: src.h, box: ..., stamp, geo: this.geometryToken() };`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:520-521` (`syncWraps`): `const stale = l.px && l.px._wrapStamp !== undefined && w.stamp !== undefined && l.px._wrapStamp !== w.stamp; if (!stale && src.x === w.x && src.y === w.y && src.w === w.w && src.h === w.h) continue;`. Neither `src.px` identity nor `src.px.version` (bumped by `touchSource` / `touchSourceRect` in `markLayerChanged`, `inpaint_ed_select.js:1545-1546`) is recorded or checked.
findings.fix: Record `srcPx: src.px` and `srcVer: src.px.version` on `out.wrap` in `putWrap` (in-memory fields alongside `stamp` and `geo`), and in `syncWraps` also re-wrap when `(w.srcPx !== undefined && (src.px !== w.srcPx || src.px.version !== w.srcVer))`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:475-532. When wrapLayer() (lines 422-451) wraps a source picture, paint, or text layer onto a new Deep paint layer, it calls putWrap(out, layer, made) (line 438), hides the source layer (layer.visible = false, line 439), keeps the source layer active (this.activeLayerId = layer.id, line 443), and switches to the Transform tool (this.setTool("transform"), line 444). In putWrap() (lines 491-493), out.px._wrapStamp is set to stamp and out.wrap records { source: src.id, angle, x: src.x, y: src.y, w: src.w, h: src.h, box, stamp, geo: this.geometryToken() } — recording neither src.px object identity nor src.px.version. In syncWraps() (lines 506-532, invoked from notifyChanged() at renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1348), lines 520-521 compute `const stale = l.px && l.px._wrapStamp !== undefined && w.stamp !== undefined && l.px._wrapStamp !== w.stamp;` and immediately skip re-wrapping via `if (!stale && src.x === w.x && src.y === w.y && src.w === w.w && src.h === w.h) continue;`. Because out.px._wrapStamp and w.stamp only diverge when a `layers` undo/redo step restores an older copy of `out` over mutated `out.px`, `stale` stays false across all in-place edits and pixel replacements on `src`.

Tracing every cited caller confirms there are no guards preventing these edits on the active wrapped source layer, and the UI actively exposes them right after wrapping: (1) In renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:803 and :825, renderLayers() mounts buildTextControls(layer) (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:240-328) for the active text layer even when layer.visible is false (and MCP set_text at renderer/commands_edit.js:190-210 calls renderTextLayer as well). Changing text colour (:285), outline colour (:315), multi-line alignment (:292), or same-width text content runs renderTextLayer() (:101-147), which replaces `layer.px = px` (:129) with identical `x, y, w, h` (:132-138) and calls markLayerChanged(layer) (:145) -> touchSource(layer.px) (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1546, bumping px.version via inpaint_ed_display.js:25) -> notifyChanged() (:1551) -> syncWraps(), which hits line 521 and skips; by contrast, typing a character that alters `layer.w` does trigger re-wrapping, making the behaviour visibly inconsistent. (2) Switching to the Transform tool displays the Transform subbar (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_chrome.js:236-239) with Flip Horizontally, Flip Vertically, Rotate 90° CCW, and Rotate 90° CW buttons acting on activeLayer(). flipLayer() (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:401-420) replaces `l.px = l.px.turned(op)` (:411) without changing `l.x, l.y, l.w, l.h` and calls markLayerChanged(l) (:417); rotateLayer90() (:570-591) replaces `l.px = l.px.turned(dir)` (:579) and swaps `[l.w, l.h]` about the centre (:585-587), leaving `x, y, w, h` unchanged for any square decal (`l.w === l.h`). Both report success in the status bar while syncWraps() leaves the Wrap layer unflipped/unrotated. (3) Painting or erasing on the source layer (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:576-601, :1110-1115 -> commitLayerPaint() at renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_tips.js:499-508 -> commitStroke() at renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:433-466 -> markLayerChanged(p.layer, box) -> touchSourceRect()) likewise bumps `src.px.version` without changing `src.x, src.y, src.w, src.h`, so syncWraps() skips it, and undo/redo of `text`, `layerfull`, or `layerrect` steps (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:868-906) also fails to update the wrap whenever `x, y, w, h` match `w`.
