Checked scratch/known_index.md, docs/BUGS.md (including lines 96-106 "Deep paint: small points left from the 0.1.56 release review", which notes only that wrapPixels ignores source opacity, mask, and blend mode, not source pixel edits), docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md, docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, and all three 2026-11-07/12 verified.json files: this defect is not previously recorded. Severity `should` is appropriate because users hit it directly through the controls shown immediately after *Layer › Wrap onto Surface* (resulting in stale pixels on screen and in exports, and even after undo of a flip/colour edit following a move+undo), while a straightforward workaround exists (nudging the source layer or re-wrapping).

findings.claim: `computeSurfaceMaps` captures `fp` (`64×64`) and the model input `inp` (`mw×mh`) before `await host.surfaceAnalysis(...)` (which runs 6–20 s while the editor stays interactive), then samples the work-size `pic` (`gw×gh`) *after* the await and guards commit only with `geometryToken()`. If the user paints, toggles a layer, or opens another image of the same dimensions during inference, `surface_maps` fits the old picture's decomposition onto the new `pic` pixels under the old `fp` (or lands old maps and an undo step onto a newly opened same-size image).
findings.scenario:
1. Open a 2048 × 2048 image and trigger *Image › Surface Maps › Compute Surface Maps*.
2. Case A: While Marigold + MoGe-2 run (~6–20 s), paint a bright stroke on a normal Paint layer (or hide a layer). When `surfaceAnalysis` resolves, line 455 reads `pic` with the new stroke, `surfaceMaps` (`inpaint_surface.js:182-187`) bakes `I_new - A_old * S_old` into `residual`, and line 463 tags the maps with the pre-stroke `fp`. If the user then presses Ctrl+Z to undo the stroke, `cur.meta.fp === fp` matches (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:448`), so subsequent `computeSurfaceMaps()` calls treat the corrupted maps as fresh.
3. Case B: While `surfaceAnalysis` runs, open a different 2048 × 2048 file via Ctrl+O (`loadFile` -> `setBasePixels`). `setBasePixels` (`inpaint_ed_open.js:109-130`) increments `historyGen` and clears undo, but does not change `geometrySeq` (`geometryToken()`), so `setMaps` commits the hybrid maps and pushes a `Surface maps` undo step onto the new image.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:443-460`: `const token = this.geometryToken(); ... const fpInp = await host.pictureInput(this, 64, 64, ...); const fp = fingerprint(fpInp.image, 64, 64); ... const inp = await host.pictureInput(this, mw, mh, ...); ... const res = await host.surfaceAnalysis(this, { image: inp.image, width: mw, height: mh }); const pic = await host.pictureInput(this, gw, gh, { skipFilters: true, background: "#808080" });`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:109-155` (`setBasePixels`) bumps `this.historyGen++` at line 110 without bumping `this.geometrySeq`, so `setMaps`'s `token !== this.geometryToken()` check at `inpaint_ed_depth.js:351,359` still passes on a same-size image replacement.
findings.fix: Capture `const base0 = this.base;` and `pic` (`gw × gh`) *before* `await host.surfaceAnalysis(...)` (deriving `inp` and `fp` from that same snapshot, or re-checking `this.base === base0` and `fp` after `surfaceAnalysis`), and drop the result in `setMaps` / `computeSurfaceMaps` if `this.base !== base0`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc. In `computeSurfaceMaps` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:441-487`), `token = this.geometryToken()` and `W, H` are captured at lines 443-444, the 64x64 fingerprint `fp` is sampled via `host.pictureInput(this, 64, 64, { skipFilters: true, background: "#808080" })` at lines 445-446, and the model input `inp` (`mw x mh`) is sampled at line 452 before `await host.surfaceAnalysis(this, { image: inp.image, width: mw, height: mh })` at line 454. `surfaceAnalysis` (`renderer/editor/host_helpers.js:526-534`) runs Marigold IID Lighting and MoGe-2 sequentially in the helpers utility process (~6-20 s on GPU, longer cold or on CPU) while the editor remains completely interactive (`surfacePending` is checked only inside `computeSurfaceMaps` at lines 431-432, and nowhere in `pointerDownNow`, `loadFile`, `newCanvas`, `setBaseFromCanvas`, `turnBlocked`, or `shell.js:219` `busy()`). After `surfaceAnalysis` resolves, line 455 samples `pic = await host.pictureInput(this, gw, gh, { skipFilters: true, background: "#808080" })` from the current composite and passes both `model: inp.image` (old) and `picture: pic.image` (new) to the worker's `surface_maps` job (`renderer/editor/inpaint_surface.js:150-198`). There, `fitScale` (line 154) fits scales against `inp.image`, `guided` (lines 162-167) upsamples the old `shading`/`residual` using the new `pic` greyscale as guide, and step 3 (lines 180-187) enforces `A = clamp((I_new - rUpV) / s, 0, 1)` and `rv = I_new - A * s`—permanently baking any bright pixels added during inference (where `A` clamps at 1) into `maps.residual` while tagging all maps with the pre-edit `fp` at `inpaint_ed_depth.js:463`.

Two details of the scenario need minor refinement, neither of which weakens the bug, and both actually expose worse consequences:
1. In Case A, if the user commits a brush stroke during `surfaceAnalysis`, `setMaps` (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:368`) pushes its `"Surface maps"` undo step on top of the stroke's undo step, so a single `Ctrl+Z` right afterwards undoes `"Surface maps"` rather than the stroke. However, any non-undo visibility toggle (`setSelectedFlag` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:607-620`), hiding/deleting the painted layer after the maps land, or—most naturally—dropping a bright logo or text layer onto the canvas while waiting 7-15 s for `Compute Surface Maps` and then running *Layer > Wrap onto Surface* (`wrapLayer` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:422-450`, which hides the flat source layer) restores the underlying composite to the exact pre-run `fp` while leaving the un-wrapped flat decal baked into `maps.residual`. Worse still, *Image > Surface Maps > Compute Surface Maps* (`electron/main/main.js:800` -> `renderer/shell.js:1402`) calls `host.editor.computeSurfaceMaps()` with `{ recompute = false }`, and no GUI button passes `recompute: true`; so once `cur.meta.fp === fp` matches at `inpaint_ed_depth.js:448`, even clicking *Compute Surface Maps* again in the menu silently returns early without recomputing.
2. In Case B, `Ctrl+O` in the app shell (`renderer/shell.js:1074-1096`) opens a new tab when `ed.base` is already set, so `Ctrl+O` itself does not replace the active tab's base. However, replacing the base in place via the top bar's **Load** button (`renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js:94-98,107`), **Ctrl+drop** (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:463`), **Generate new** (`setBaseFromCanvas` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:184-207`, even though line 197 clears `this.maps = {}`), MCP `load_image` (`renderer/commands_docs.js:261-280`), or `new_canvas` (`renderer/commands_docs.js:242`, `inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:355-410`) all go through `setBasePixels` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:104-155`). `setBasePixels` increments `this.historyGen++` (line 110) and clears undo (lines 129, 136), but never increments `this.geometrySeq` (`geometryToken()` at `inpaint_ed_depth.js:853-855`)—not even when `sizeChanged` is `true`! Consequently, `setMaps` (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:351,359`) passes `token === this.geometryToken()` regardless of whether the new image has the same or different dimensions, overwriting `this.maps` on the new picture (with the old `[W, 0, 0, H, 0, 0]` `xf`) and pushing a `"Surface maps"` undo step onto the new document.

Checked against all known-issue lists (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md` §6, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-12 `verified.json` files): this is not known. `canvas-b/undo-geometry-no-seq-bump` (2026-11-07) only covers `restoreGeometry` not bumping `geometrySeq` on canvas/turn undo, and `canvas-c/F4` (2026-11-07) only covers `setBasePixels` failing to clear *pre-existing* `this.maps` on load (which `setBaseFromCanvas` and `newCanvas` already clear, yet still suffer from this in-flight overwrite). Neither covers `computeSurfaceMaps` splitting its snapshot across `await host.surfaceAnalysis` or `setBasePixels` leaving `geometryToken()` unchanged.

Severity `should`: preparing a decal/text layer, toggling layers, or loading another image during a 6-20 s background model run is a plausible workflow, corrupts Deep paint / Relight reflections on screen and in exports, and cannot even be refreshed from the *Compute Surface Maps* menu item when `fp` matches, though the user can work around it via Undo History.

findings.claim: Commit d6753999 updated extendCanvasNow to keep hidden layers instead of dropping them, but leaves l.clip = true on kept hidden layers whose visible clipping base was baked into the flat base, silently re-clipping them to an unrelated layer below (or leaving them orphaned). In the same loop, line 1658 sets l.dirty = true unconditionally on every kept layer, forcing untouched reference/image layers to re-encode over their original lossless ref and causing plain hidden filter layers to upload an unresized W x H empty PNG (up to 150 MP at 15k) as layer.ref.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a picture, add a hidden paint/control layer L0, a visible paint layer L1 above it, and a hidden clipped layer L2 (l.clip = true, clipped to L1) above L1; also add a hidden plain Levels filter layer F and an untouched reference layer R.
2. Run Extend canvas (e.g. add 128 px on the left).
3. L1 is visible so it is baked into the new base and omitted from kept, while L0 and L2 are kept with L2.clip still true: when the user unhides L0 and L2, L2 now clips to L0's alpha instead of L1's. Meanwhile F (whose l.px is still an empty W x H LayerPixels) and R both have l.dirty = true, so the next syncLayersOnce encodes F's empty W x H pixels into a PNG ref on a filter layer and re-encodes R, replacing R's original file ref.
findings.evidence:
In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1639-1660`:
`const kept = [], keptSet = new Set();`
`this.layers.forEach((l, i) => {`
`    const cb = l.clip ? this.clipBaseOf(l, i) : null;`
`    if (this.isControl(l) || this.isReference(l) || !this.shown(l) || (cb && keptSet.has(cb))) { kept.push(l); keptSet.add(l); }`
`});`
If `!this.shown(l)` is true and `l.clip` is true while `cb` was visible (`this.shown(cb)` true), `keptSet.has(cb)` is false (`cb` was baked into `flat` at line 1586), yet `l` is pushed to `kept` with `l.clip === true` intact (contrast `loadLayered` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:499`, which clears `L.clip = false` when the clip base becomes the base). Then at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1645-1659`:
`for (const l of kept) {`
`    if (l.kind === "filter") {`
`        l.x = 0; l.y = 0; l.w = nw; l.h = nh;`
`        if (l.maskPx && l.maskPx.width === W && l.maskPx.height === H) { l.maskPx = l.maskPx.resized(nw, nh, { x: left, y: top }); l.maskDirty = true; l._maskedValid = false; }`
`        if (ownPx(l) && l.px && l.px.width === W && l.px.height === H) l.px = l.px.resized(nw, nh, { x: left, y: top });`
`    } else if (l.kind === "paint" && ...) { ... } else { l.x += left; l.y += top; }`
`    l.dirty = true;`
`}`
Every filter layer is constructed with `px: this.pixels.Layer.empty(W, H)` and `syncLayersOnce` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:901`) tests `if (layer.dirty && layer.px)` without checking `kind !== "filter" || hasOwnPixels(layer)` (contrast `cropCanvasNow` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1388-1394`, which sets `l.dirty = true` only when `ownPx(l) && l.px`, clears `l._fcache = null`, and leaves shifted non-filter layers' `dirty` flag untouched).
findings.fix: In `extendCanvasNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1640-1659`), if `l.clip && (!cb || !keptSet.has(cb))` set `l.clip = false`; clear `l._fcache = null` on kept filter layers; and set `l.dirty = true` only when `l.px` was actually replaced (`ownPx(l)` on filter layers, and full-canvas `paint` layers resized at line 1652).
findings.why:
All three defects claimed against commit d6753999 hold in `extendCanvasNow` at `f45a86cc` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1639-1660`). First, at lines 1639-1643, `this.layers.forEach((l, i) => { const cb = l.clip ? this.clipBaseOf(l, i) : null; if (this.isControl(l) || this.isReference(l) || !this.shown(l) || (cb && keptSet.has(cb))) { kept.push(l); keptSet.add(l); } })` retains a hidden layer (`!this.shown(l)`) or control layer (`this.isControl(l)`) with `l.clip === true` unchanged even when its visible clipping base `cb` was baked into `flat` at line 1586 (`!keptSet.has(cb)`). Once `this.layers = kept` runs at line 1660, `clipTargetOf` / `clipBaseOf` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:105-127`) walk downward in `kept` and silently re-bind `l` to whatever unclipped non-filter layer now sits below it in the same group: if a hidden layer `L0` sits below, unhiding `l` alone renders nothing (`drawLayersInto` at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:75`, `glViewComposite` at `inpaint_ed_display.js:325`, and `stackPlan` at `inpaint_ed_stack.js:166` all skip a clipped layer whose base was not drawn) and unhiding both clips `l` to `L0`'s alpha instead of the baked `L1`'s; even worse, if only a reference layer `R` sits below `l` (reference layers are inserted at index 0 by `addLayer` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:541-542`), `clipTargetOf` line 111 (`if (!this.isReference(b) && (b.group || null) !== (layer.group || null)) return null; return b;`) returns `R`, so unhiding `l` clips it to `R`'s 1/3-size preview rectangle on screen while `forRun: true` exports and runs skip `R` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:86`) and drop `l` completely (`!drawn.has(cb)` at line 75). No post-loop normalization clears `l.clip` (`normalizeGroups` at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:189` only normalizes `l.group`, unlike `loadLayered` at `inpaint_ed_open.js:499` which clears `L.clip = false`).

Second and third, the loop at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1645-1659` unconditionally executes `l.dirty = true` at line 1658 on every kept layer (and omits `l._fcache = null` on filter layers, unlike `cropCanvasNow` at `inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1388-1394` and `resizeImageNow` at `1455-1477`). On untouched reference, control, or hidden image/result/text layers that merely shifted `l.x += left; l.y += top` at line 1656, `l.dirty = true` forces `serializeForPrompt` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:452-455`) to bypass the original `l.ref` and Canvas-2D-encode `exportRef`, and causes the next `syncLayersOnce` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:906-911`, slightly shifted from the finding's `:901` citation) to re-encode `layer.px` as an 8-bit sRGB PNG and overwrite `layer.ref` (discarding original JPEG compression, 16-bit depth, or ICC profiles, and incurring Canvas-2D premultiply rounding when tiles are off). On plain hidden filter layers (`!ownPx(l)`), `addFilterLayer` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:324`) and `setValue` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:208`) allocate `px: this.pixels.Layer.empty(W, H)` with `dirty: false`; line 1649 leaves `l.px` at the old `W x H` while line 1658 marks `l.dirty = true`, so `syncLayersOnce` encodes and uploads a full `W x H` empty PNG (up to 150 MP at 15k) into `layer.ref`, which `getValue` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:49`) serializes and `.scumble` archives pack.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: `review_full_2026-11-12` had `canvas-tools/extend-drops-hidden-layers`, and this finding proves new defects introduced by its fix in `d6753999`, so it is not `known`. Severity is calibrated down from `must` to `should`: `extendCanvasNow` does not destroy `l.px` on kept layers, the immediate outpaint run happens while `l` is still hidden, a user who unhides `l` can see the wrong clipping (and `Clipped to ...` badge in `renderLayers` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:758-762`) and unclip it via Alt+click without losing `l`'s pixels, `setValue` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:190`) ignores the spurious `l.ref` on non-`ownPixels` filter layers on reload, and on the default tile backend 8-bit sRGB pixel values in `l.px` survive `encodeTilePixels`.

findings.claim: Commit 650b6327 guarded only the entry of loadFile and newCanvas with `if (this._loading)`, leaving both the reverse race order (`loadFile` started before `setValue`) and the other image/layer loading entry points unguarded. When `setValue` runs concurrently with an in-flight `loadFile` (e.g. an SVG awaiting its size dialog or a multi-second 15k PSD/ORA/TIFF decode), or when `setBaseFromRef`, `setBaseFromCanvas`, file drop (`addImageLayers`), or `pasteClipboard` runs during `setValue`, the two operations interleave across awaits and mix or wipe layers, masks, maps, and undo state.
findings.scenario:
Path A (reverse order): In an empty tab (`cur.base === null`), drop an SVG (opening `svgTarget`'s `ask()` dialog at `inpaint_ed_open.js:546`) or a 15k PSD/TIFF that decodes in a worker for several seconds; while that open is awaiting, open a `.scumble` document via File > Open Document (`openDocument` at `host_documents.js:293` sees `!cur.base && !cur._loading && !cur.docFile`, reuses `cur`, and runs `setValue`). Clicking Import in the SVG dialog (or when the PSD worker finishes) finishes `loadFile` over the `.scumble` tab — or if `loadFile` lands just before `setValue` finishes its layer loop, `setValue` appends the `.scumble` layers/maps onto the newly opened image with `ed.docFile` still pointing at the `.scumble` file.
Path B (`_loading` active): While a multi-layer `.scumble` or session tab is mid-`setValue` after line 133 (`this.width > 0`, `this._loading === true`), drop a PNG onto the canvas without Ctrl (`inpaint_canvas.js:465` -> `addImageLayers`), press Ctrl+V (`pasteClipboard`), or run MCP `load_image` with `filename` (`commands_docs.js:276` -> `setBaseFromRef`): none of them check `this._loading`, mutating `this.layers` / `this.base` mid-restore.
findings.evidence:
1. `loadFile` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:161-206`) checks `if (this._loading)` only at line 161, before `loadLayered` (line 170), `loadTiff` (line 171), `svgTarget` (line 173, which awaits `this.ask(...)` at line 546), `pixelsOffThread`/`up` (lines 190-193), and `loadImageEl` (line 203), and `later()` at line 166 checks only `this._destroyed || this._openToken !== token`. Meanwhile `setValue` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:94-97`) increments `this._loadToken` without incrementing `this._openToken` or closing an open SVG `ask` dialog (contrast `newCanvas` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:386`, which rechecks `if (this._loading)` after its `ask`, though not after `setBaseFromCanvas`'s upload).
2. `setBaseFromRef` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:46`, called by `load_image` at `renderer/commands_docs.js:276`) and `setBaseFromCanvas` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:184`) have no `this._loading` check and do not bump `_loadToken` or `_openToken`.
3. Canvas drop (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:463-465`: `if (!this.width || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) this.loadFile(files[0]); else this.addImageLayers(files, ...)`), `addImageLayers` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:24`), and `pasteClipboard` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1351`) never check `this._loading`, even though `this.width` is already non-zero throughout `setValue`'s async layer/mask/map loops (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:133-348`).
findings.fix: In `setValue` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:94`), also bump `this._openToken = (this._openToken || 0) + 1` (so any in-flight `loadFile`/`loadTiff`/`loadLayered` aborts via `later()`); include `this._loading` in `loadFile`'s `later()` check (`inpaint_ed_open.js:166`, plus rechecking after `svgTarget`); and guard `setBaseFromRef`, `setBaseFromCanvas`, `addImageLayers`, and `pasteClipboard` with `if (this._loading)` (and prevent `openDocument` at `host_documents.js:293` from reusing a tab whose `_openToken` has an open in flight).
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc, with severity calibrated down from `must` to `should`.

**1. Reverse-order race (`loadFile` started before `setValue`) holds.** Commit 650b6327 added `if (this._loading)` only at the entry of `loadFile` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:161`) and `newCanvas` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:357, 386`). Inside `loadFile` (`inpaint_ed_open.js:157-214`), `later()` at line 166 checks only `this._destroyed || this._openToken !== token`—never `this._loading`—before awaiting `loadLayered` (line 170; `484-529`), `loadTiff` (line 171; `221-247`), `svgTarget` (line 173, which awaits `this.ask(...)` at line 546), `pixelsOffThread` / `uploadBlob` (lines 186-193), and `loadImageEl` (line 203). Meanwhile, `setValue` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:108-396`; note that at f45a86cc the token/flag setup is at lines 115-117 rather than the candidate's cited 94-97) increments `this._loadToken` and sets `this._loading = true`, but neither increments `this._openToken` nor calls `this.closeAsk()`. In an empty tab (`cur.base === null`), dropping an SVG (opening the non-modal `.ipc-ask` overlay at `inpaint_ed_open.js:546`) or opening a multi-second 15k PSD/ORA/TIFF leaves `cur.base === null` and `cur._loading` falsy; opening a `.scumble` document via File > Open, a window `.scumble` drop (`renderer/shell.js:1191`, capture phase), Explorer, or MCP `open_document` hits `openDocument` (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:293`), which sees `cur && !cur.base && !cur._loading && !this._rawStates.has(cur) && !cur.docFile === true`, reuses `cur`, sets `cur.docFile` (`renderer/editor/host_setup.js:237`), and runs `cur.setValue(doc.state)` (`host_setup.js:240`). For an SVG, the Import SVG dialog remains mounted right over the `.scumble` document; clicking Import (or when the PSD/TIFF worker decode completes) either finishes `loadFile` after `setValue`—wiping the `.scumble`'s base and layers in memory while `ed.docFile` still points at the `.scumble` path—or lands `setBasePixels` (`inpaint_ed_open.js:104-155`, which does not bump `_loadToken`) mid-`setValue`, causing `setValue` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:185-381`) to push the `.scumble`'s remaining layers, selection, maps, history, and guides onto the newly opened image. (`newCanvas` at `inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:386-407` has a narrower version of the same gap across `await uploadCanvas` at line 395.)

**2. Unguarded entry points during `setValue` (`_loading === true`) hold.** Once `setValue` sets the base at `inpaint_ed_persist.js:133` or `137`, `this.width > 0` and `this.base !== null` hold throughout the multi-second async loops for layers (`185-288`), text (`296-301`), selection (`314-341`), and maps (`362-381`). During this window: (a) a plain or Shift drop on the canvas (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:463-465`, and node widget `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_chrome.js:40-41`) or an image paste (`inpaint_canvas.js:448`) sees `this.width > 0` and dispatches to `addImageLayers` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:24-125`), which has no `this._loading` check (nor does MCP `add_image_layer` at `renderer/commands_docs.js:291`) and mutates `this.layers`, `this.groups` (lines 51-56), and reference labels before `setValue` overwrites `this.refMap` at `inpaint_ed_persist.js:305`; (b) `Ctrl+V` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:228`) and MCP `copy_to_layer` (`renderer/commands_layers.js:256`) call `pasteClipboard` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1351-1364`), which checks only `if (!this.width)` and inserts a layer mid-stack while `setValue` is still pushing upper layers; and (c) MCP `load_image` with `filename` (`renderer/commands_docs.js:276`, dispatched via `renderer/commands.js:119-126` with no `_loading` guard) calls `setBaseFromRef` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:46-71`), which neither checks `this._loading` nor bumps `_loadToken`, reproducing the exact base-replacement + layer-mixing bug that commit 650b6327's message claimed to cover for `load_image`, drop, and paste. (For `setBaseFromCanvas` at `inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:184`, its app caller `runGenerate` at `renderer/editor/host_generate.js:30, 120` checks `generateNewBlocked` -> `editor._loading` up front; the reverse case where `runGenerate` starts on an empty tab before `openDocument` is already recorded under `host/H-1`, though `setBaseFromCanvas` itself also lacks a `_loading` guard or `_loadToken` bump if it lands mid-`setValue`.)

**3. Known-issues check.** `canvas-core/loadfile-during-setvalue-mixes-documents` (`docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:54-68`) was addressed in commit 650b6327 (2026-11-12) by guarding only the top of `loadFile` and `newCanvas` instead of bumping tokens or guarding the sibling entry points. Because this finding proves concrete remaining holes in that 2026-11-12 fix (reverse execution order and missed callers `setBaseFromRef`, `addImageLayers`, and `pasteClipboard`), it is a genuine finding on the fix rather than `known`. `host/H-1` (`docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json:120-131`) covers only `providerPending` / `runGenerate` (`Generate new`) on an empty tab, not `loadFile`, `setBaseFromRef`, `addImageLayers`, or `pasteClipboard`. Nothing in `docs/BUGS.md` or `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` covers these paths.

**4. Severity calibration (`should`, not `must`).** Both directly analogous verified findings—`canvas-core/loadfile-during-setvalue-mixes-documents` (`review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:56, 67`) and `host/H-1` (`review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json:123, 130`)—were calibrated as `should`. Hitting Path A requires opening a `.scumble` while an SVG dialog is visibly up or a heavy image is still opening in the same empty tab, and the `.scumble` file on disk is untouched unless the user subsequently saves after seeing the replaced/mixed picture on screen. Hitting Path B requires dropping, pasting, or running an external MCP command during the multi-second restore window while the tab shows its busy indicator (`shell.js:220`), producing visible mixed/misordered layers rather than silent pixel loss on disk.

findings.claim: Commit 9ec6863d guarded `settleKey` against user edits during `flushEditor` by comparing `mark(ed)` (`[historyGen, undo.length, undo[last], redo.length]`), which misses both (1) every persisted document edit that does not push an undo step and (2) even undo-pushing strokes made on an already-restored tab while `restore()` is still loading later tabs. In both cases `edited` evaluates to `false` and `settleKey` sets `ed.docFile.key = key` to the hash of the post-edit state, hiding the `*` unsaved marker and letting `closeDocument` close the tab without prompting to save.
findings.scenario:
Scenario A (non-undo edit during flush): Open a `.scumble` document that has a large selection (`openDocument` -> `settleKey` awaits `flushEditor` for several seconds while `encodeSelectionSoon` encodes the selection PNG). While it flushes, edit the prompt or negative prompt, toggle a layer's visibility/lock/mask, change generation or recipe settings, drag a guide, or type into a text layer's `<textarea>` without blurring (`_textUndo` stays on the layer until `change`). When `flushEditor` finishes, `mark(ed)` is unchanged, so `ed.docFile.key` is overwritten with the hash that includes the unsaved edit; pressing Ctrl+W then closes the tab with no Save prompt, losing the edit.
Scenario B (stroke during multi-tab restore): Launch Scumble restoring two clean `.scumble` tabs (`restore()` at `host_setup.js:230-248`), where Tab 1 restores quickly and Tab 2 is a heavy multi-layer 15k document. Paint a brush stroke or delete a layer on Tab 1 while Tab 2 is still in `ed.setValue(doc.state)`. Only after Tab 2 finishes does `restore()` call `this.settleKey(ed)` (line 248), which takes `const before = mark(ed)` AFTER the stroke is already on `ed.undo`, sees `edited === false`, and marks Tab 1 clean with the unsaved stroke.
findings.evidence:
In `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:91-106`:
`async settleKey(ed) {`
`    const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));`
`    for (const until = Date.now() + 60000; this._restoring && Date.now() < until;) await sleep(100);`
`    const mark = (e) => [e.historyGen, e.undo && e.undo.length, e.undo && e.undo[e.undo.length - 1], e.redo && e.redo.length];`
`    const before = mark(ed);`
`    await this.flushEditor(ed, () => {}, "saving");`
`    if (!ed.base || !ed.docFile || !this._editors.includes(ed)) return;`
`    const key = hashString(ed.getValue());`
`    ed._stateKey = key;`
`    const edited = mark(ed).some((v, i) => v !== before[i]);`
`    if (!edited && (!ed.docFile.key || ed.docFile.clean)) ed.docFile.key = key;`
`    delete ed.docFile.clean;`
1. `before` is captured at line 98 AFTER the `this._restoring` wait loop at line 93, and `restore()` (`renderer/editor/host_setup.js:240-248`) calls `settleKey` only after ALL tabs finish `setValue`.
2. `mark(ed)` ignores `notifyChanged()` mutations that do not touch `ed.undo` (`setPromptText`, `setNegativeText`, `setSelectedFlag`, `genSettings`, `cropSettings`, `settings`, `guides`, `savedSelections`, unblurred `_textUndo`), yet `ed.getValue()` at line 101 serializes all of them into `key`.
3. Once `ed.docFile.key === ed._stateKey`, `documentDirty(ed)` (`host_documents.js:81`) returns `false`, so `closeDocument` (`renderer/shell.js:315`) skips `askDocument({ kind: "close" })`.
findings.fix: Increment a monotonic `ed._changeSeq = (ed._changeSeq || 0) + 1` inside `notifyChanged()` (or `host.changed(editor)`), capture `ed._changeSeq` immediately when `ed.setValue` finishes for that tab (passing that initial mark into `settleKey(ed, mark0)`), and treat any change to `_changeSeq` (except `encodeSelectionSoon`'s own background PNG completion) or `mark(ed)` as `edited = true`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc. In `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:91-107`, commit 9ec6863d attempted to fix `files-io/settlekey-adopts-user-edit-as-saved` by comparing `mark(ed)` (`[e.historyGen, e.undo && e.undo.length, e.undo && e.undo[e.undo.length - 1], e.redo && e.redo.length]`) at line 97-98 (`const before = mark(ed)`) against `mark(ed)` after `await this.flushEditor(ed, () => {}, "saving")` at line 99-103. When `edited` is `false` and `!ed.docFile.key || ed.docFile.clean`, line 104 writes `ed.docFile.key = key` (where `key = hashString(ed.getValue())` from line 101) and line 102 sets `ed._stateKey = key`. Both holes claimed by the finding hold with no preventing guard:

1. Multi-tab restore window (even for undo-pushing edits like brush strokes or layer deletions): `restore()` (`renderer/editor/host_setup.js:228-248`) increments `this._restoring++` and loops sequentially over `docs`. For the first tab, `createDocument` (`renderer/shell.js:171-185` -> `host.addEditor` at `renderer/editor/host_state.js:223-224` and `editor.open()` at `shell.js:180`) immediately mounts Tab 1 as `host.editor` without `shell-hidden`, and once `await ed.setValue(doc.state)` finishes (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:394` sets `this._loading = false`), Tab 1 is visible, active, and accepts pointer/key input while later tabs are still awaiting `setValue` (e.g. decoding a multi-layer or 15k document). If Tab 1 was clean when saved (`ed.docFile.clean === true`, set via `docMeta` at `host_util.js:197` and `bundle` at `host_queue.js:529`), any stroke or layer deletion on Tab 1 during Tab 2's `setValue` pushes onto `ed1.undo` and bumps `ed1.historyGen` while `saveAll()` defers on `this._restoring` (`host_queue.js:536`). Only after ALL tabs finish `setValue` does `restore()` decrement `this._restoring--` and call `this.settleKey(ed)` (`host_setup.js:248`) — and even if `settleKey` were entered earlier, line 93 waits for `this._restoring` to reach 0 BEFORE line 98 captures `const before = mark(ed)`. Thus `before` already includes the user's stroke, `flushEditor` (`host_documents.js:36`) uploads the dirty layer and clears `layer.dirty`, `edited` evaluates to `false`, and line 104 overwrites `ed1.docFile.key` with the post-stroke hash.

2. Non-undo persisted edits during `flushEditor`: On opening (`openDocument`, `host_documents.js:295-301`, where `ed.docFile.key` starts `null` and the tab is activated before `await this.settleKey(ed)` — in fact `settleKey` runs twice, once unawaited from `restore()` at `host_setup.js:248` and once awaited at line 301) or restoring a clean `.scumble` above `SYNC_ENCODE_PX` (16 MP, e.g. a 24 MP photo) that has a selection, `setValue` clears `selectionEncoded = false` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:339-340`) and `flushEditor` polls in `pending()` (`host_documents.js:43-51`) while `encodeSelectionSoon` (`inpaint_canvas.js:1354-1408`) encodes the selection PNG off-thread. Many persisted edits serialized by `ed.getValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:42-105`) never push to `ed.undo` or increment `ed.historyGen`: editing `promptText` or `negativeText` (`inpaint_modal.js:984,997`), toggling layer `visible` or `locked` (`setSelectedFlag` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:607-620`), toggling `alphaLock` (`795`), changing `opacity` (`812-819`) or `blend` (`856`), toggling group flags (`931-942`), changing `genSettings` / `upsampleSettings` / `cropSettings` (`inpaint_modal.js:1013-1145`) or recipe `settings` (`inpaint_canvas.js:1042`), dragging `guides` (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:392-397`), calling `saveSelection` (`inpaint_ed_select.js:1201-1209`), or typing into a text layer's sidebar `<textarea>` before blur (`inpaint_ed_text.js:246-260`, which holds `_textUndo` unpushed until `change`; note one minor detail in the candidate's list: `setMaskOff` at `inpaint_ed_masks.js:540` *does* push a `layers` undo step, unlike the visibility/lock/alphaLock toggles). Once `settleKey` sets `ed.docFile.key = key` and `ed._stateKey = key`, `documentDirty(ed)` (`host_documents.js:75-84`) returns `false` (and stays `false` after subsequent `saveAll()`/`bundle()` runs because `hashString(ed.getValue())` still equals `ed.docFile.key`), hiding the `*` indicator (`shell.js:249,265`) and causing `closeDocument` (`shell.js:315`) to close the tab without asking to save.

Not `known`: `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` (`files-io/settlekey-adopts-user-edit-as-saved`) reported the unguarded `settleKey`, commit `9ec6863d` added the `mark(ed)` fix in 2026-11-12..16, and this finding proves two remaining holes in that new fix; nothing in `docs/BUGS.md`, the 2026-11-07 `verified.json` files, or `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` covers them.

Severity `should`: Closing a tab with `Ctrl+W` silently skips the Save prompt so edits (including brush strokes in Scenario B and prompt/layer/setting changes in Scenario A) never reach the `.scumble` file on disk, reachable in plausible workflows (multi-tab session restore or editing right after opening a >16 MP `.scumble` with a selection), while `Reopen Closed Tab` (`rememberClosed` in the session autosave) keeps a recoverable copy within the session.

findings.claim: Commit 8c0e0cc1 added `chat.deleted = true` when deleting `this.chat`, but `deleteChat` never aborts an active turn (`this.stop()` ) and cannot mark a detached chat whose slow tool call outlived `reset()`'s 5-second timeout. Deleting the active chat mid-turn leaves the turn running LLM requests, executing MCP tool calls on documents, and streaming events into `this.events`; deleting a detached chat whose tool call is still running lets `done(chat)` resurrect the deleted chat file on disk and overwrite its events with `this.events` from the current chat.
findings.scenario:
Path A: Start an assistant turn in chat C1. While it is streaming or running tools, open the chat list and delete C1 (`deleteChat(C1.id)`). `this.chat` and `this.events` are cleared, but `this.stop()` is never called: C1's `runTurn` keeps calling the LLM and running MCP edits on the user's canvas while `this.emit(...)` appends C1's new events into `this.events` and renders them into the cleared panel.
Path B: Start a turn in C1 that calls a tool taking > 5 s (e.g. `generate` or `upscale`). Click New chat (`reset()`): `reset()` calls `this.stop()`, waits 5 s on `Promise.race([this.turnDone, 5000])`, and sets `this.chat = null; this.events = []` while C1's `runTurn` is still awaiting `callTool`. Now delete C1 from the history list (`deleteChat(C1.id)`): `this.chat` is null, so `C1.deleted` is never set. When `callTool` finishes, `done(C1, "stopped")` calls `saveChat(C1)`, recreating `<C1.id>.json` on disk with `{ events: this.events }` from the new chat.
findings.evidence:
In `electron/main/assistant/index.js:438-451` (`reset`):
`if (this.turnAbort) this.stop();`
`if (this.turnDone) { await Promise.race([this.turnDone.catch(() => {}), new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5000))]); }`
`this.chat = null;`
`this.events = [];`
Then in `electron/main/assistant/index.js:562-583` (`deleteChat` and `saveChat`):
`deleteChat(id) {`
`    if (!this.deps.store) return { ok: false };`
`    if (this.chat && this.chat.id === id) {`
`        this.chat.deleted = true;`
`        this.chat = null;`
`        this.events = [];`
`    }`
`    return this.deps.store.remove(id);`
`}`
`saveChat(chat = this.chat) {`
`    if (!this.deps.store || !chat || chat.deleted) return;`
`    try { this.deps.store.save(chat, { events: this.events }); ... }`
1. `deleteChat` never calls `this.stop()`, so `this.turnAbort` is not aborted and `runTurn` (`lines 690-895`) continues calling `this.emit(...)` (which pushes to `this.events` and sends IPC events to the renderer).
2. `deleteChat` only checks `this.chat && this.chat.id === id`; a chat detached by `reset()` after the 5 s timeout is not in `this.chat`, so `chat.deleted` remains falsy and `saveChat(chat)` writes it back to disk using `this.events` (the new session's event list rather than `chat`'s own events).
findings.fix: Track a `deletedIds = new Set()` (or a map of in-flight `chat` objects by ID) on `Assistant`, have `deleteChat(id)` add `id` to `deletedIds` and call `this.stop()` whenever the in-flight turn belongs to `id`, guard `this.emit` so events from a detached/deleted turn are not pushed to `this.events` or sent to the UI, and store each turn's `events` array on its `chat` object rather than reading `this.events` in `saveChat(chat)`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc` (with two accuracy corrections to the candidate's paraphrased code and Path B trigger). Commit `8c0e0cc1` attempted to fix `assistant-glb/deleted-chat-resaved` from `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:534-548` by marking `this.chat.deleted = true` in `deleteChat` and `resetAll`, tracking `this.saves`, and skipping `chat.deleted` in `saveChat`, so the remaining defects in that fix are genuine new findings rather than `known`.

**Path A holds in full (active turn keeps running, mutates documents, and pollutes `this.events` and the next chat).** Once a chat `C1` finishes its first turn, `done()` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:1045`) writes `<C1.id>.json` to disk. During turn 2+, neither the `Chats` button (`renderer/assistant.js:136,197,686-697`) nor a row's `×` delete button (`renderer/assistant.js:709-716`) is disabled while `busy` is true. Clicking `×` on `C1` invokes `deleteChat(id)` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:562-570`), which sets `this.chat.deleted = true`, awaits `this.savesDone()`, deletes `<C1.id>.json` and its picture folder via `this.deps.store.remove(id)`, and sets `this.chat = null; this.events = []` — without ever calling `this.stop()` (`8c0e0cc1`'s test at `tools/assistant_test.js:1156-1157` manually called `a.stop()` after `a.deleteChat(id)`, masking this omission). Consequently, `runTurn(chat, turn, ...)` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:683-764`) keeps running in the background: making further LLM requests, executing MCP tool calls on the user's open documents (`runCall` -> `this.client.callTool` at `lines 865-869`), and even opening `ask` cards (`lines 832,994-1001`). Every `this.emit(...)` (`lines 308-322`) pushes `C1`'s post-delete events into the newly emptied `this.events` and forwards them to the panel (`renderer/assistant.js:712-716` also only calls `node.remove()` without clearing `ui.list`). Worse, when `C1`'s turn ends and the user sends a new message, `_startTurn` (`index.js:388`: `if (!this.chat) this.chat = await this.newChat();`) creates `C2` without clearing `this.events`, so `C1`'s trailing events are saved into `<C2.id>.json` on disk.

**Path B holds via unabortable waits, though not via `callTool` on `generate`/`upscale`.** Two corrections to the candidate's evidence: (1) the quoted snippets at `index.js:438-451,562-583` were paraphrased (`this.turnAbort` does not exist; `reset()` calls `this.stop()` at lines 439 and 442, and `deleteChat` awaits `this.savesDone()` and returns `boolean`); and (2) `this.client.callTool` for `generate` or `upscale` (`index.js:865-869`) cannot outlive `reset()`'s 5 s `Promise.race` (`index.js:443`), because both `Client.callTool` (`{ signal: turn.signal }`) and `Bridge.run` (`electron/main/bridge.js:131-141`, via `metaFor` at `index.js:144`) listen to `turn.signal` and reject synchronously with `AbortError` as soon as `this.stop()` aborts `this.turn.abort` (`index.js:331`). However, `runTurn` DOES have unabortable waits that ignore `turn.signal` and exceed 5 s: `postStream` (`electron/main/assistant/http.js:126,139,143-145`) awaits an unabortable `setTimeout` `sleep(waitMs)` of 8 s (`BACKOFF[2]`) or up to 60 s (`MAX_RETRY_WAIT`) on HTTP 429/500/502/503/529 `Retry-After`, and `Bridge.run` (`electron/main/bridge.js:112,115,117`) awaits `_waitReady()` (up to 120 s on a window reload) before checking `signal.aborted`. If the user clicks `New chat` (`reset()`) during such a wait, `reset()` times out after 5 s and sets `this.chat = null; this.events = []` (`index.js:443-445`) while `runTurn` still holds `C1`. Deleting `C1` from `Chats` then sees `this.chat === null` (`index.js:565`), leaving `C1.deleted` undefined; when the wait finishes, `done(C1, turn, "stopped")` -> `saveChat(C1)` (`index.js:1045,573-583`) -> `store.save(C1, ...)` (`electron/main/assistant/store.js:40-71`) recreates `<C1.id>.json` and writes every screenshot in `C1.history` back to `<C1.id>/<n>.jpg` on disk (with `[turn:done]` as `events`, since `_start` at `index.js:371` blocks starting a new chat while `this.turn` is still set).

**Severity `should`:** Deleting the active chat from `Chats` during a turn (while streaming, running tools, or waiting on an `ask` card) is a normal UI action, and leaving the deleted chat's turn running LLM/MCP calls while leaking events or resurrecting deleted screenshots after a timed-out `reset()` violates the user's explicit delete/privacy action, with `Stop` before `Delete` as a workaround.

findings.claim: Two 2026-11-12 review fixes (`landUndo` in commit 1b2f05d7 and `dropStaleSelectionEdit` in commit 1f27f6d6, along with `cancelRange`) corrupt `this.undoBytes` by subtracting `snap.bytes` more times than it was added. `releaseSnapshot(snap)` unconditionally subtracts `snap.bytes || 0`, so releasing an unpushed held snapshot subtracts bytes that were never added, and `dropStaleSelectionEdit` / `cancelRange` subtract `popped.bytes` manually and then call `releaseSnapshot(popped)` to subtract it a second time — driving `this.undoBytes` negative so `trimUndo()` fails to enforce `maxUndoBytes`.
findings.scenario: On the canvas backend (or whenever `snapshotSelection` / `snapshotRect` sets `bytes > 0`), make a selection on a 4000 x 4000 image (`snap.bytes = 64 MB`) and Shift-click or Alt-click with the rectangle marquee tool without dragging (`landUndo(p, false)` at `inpaint_ed_pointer.js:1012`), or start a Feather/Grow/Select-range operation and deselect/cancel before the worker finishes (`dropStaleSelectionEdit` / `cancelRange`). Each occurrence subtracts up to 64 MB from `this.undoBytes` without a matching addition, driving `this.undoBytes` to `-64 MB`, `-128 MB`, etc., so subsequent heavy undo steps bypass `this.undoBytes > bytes` in `trimUndo()` by hundreds of megabytes.
findings.evidence:
1. `this.undoBytes` is only incremented in `pushUndoSnapshot` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:492`: `this.undoBytes += snap.bytes || 0;`) and `historyStepNow` (`line 1101`), NOT in `snapshot()` (`line 356`). Yet `releaseSnapshot(snap)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:138-140`) unconditionally runs:
`releaseSnapshot(snap) {`
`    if (!snap) return;`
`    this.undoBytes -= snap.bytes || 0;`
2. `holdUndo` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:19-23`) calls `this.snapshot(step)`, and `landUndo` (`lines 25-30`) runs:
`if (changed) this.pushUndoSnapshot(snap); else this.releaseSnapshot(snap);`
On a no-op marquee click in `add`/`subtract`/`intersect` mode (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:1012`), `changed` is `false` and `snap` (`kind: "selection"`, `bytes: w * h * 4` at `inpaint_ed_history.js:91`) was never pushed.
3. `dropStaleSelectionEdit` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:645-651`) and `cancelRange` (`lines 663-668`) both run:
`if (popped) {`
`    this.undoBytes -= popped.bytes || 0;`
`    this.releaseSnapshot(popped);`
subtracting `popped.bytes` twice.
findings.fix: Mark snapshots when their bytes are added to `this.undoBytes` (`snap._counted = true` in `pushUndoSnapshot` and `historyStepNow`), subtract in `releaseSnapshot` only `if (snap._counted) { this.undoBytes -= snap.bytes || 0; snap._counted = false; }`, and remove the redundant `this.undoBytes -= popped.bytes || 0;` lines in `dropStaleSelectionEdit` and `cancelRange`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc. `this.undoBytes` is only incremented when a snapshot is actually placed onto an undo/redo stack — in `pushUndoSnapshot` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:492`: `this.undoBytes += snap.bytes || 0;`) and `historyStepNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1101`) — and is NOT incremented in `snapshot()` (`lines 356-363`). However, `releaseSnapshot(snap)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:138-140`) unconditionally executes `this.undoBytes -= snap.bytes || 0;` without checking whether `snap.bytes` was ever added or already deducted.

Tracing every call path confirms three live ways `this.undoBytes` is undercounted or driven negative — including on the default `tiles` backend, not just the canvas backend, because `snapshotSelection()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:76-92`, with `selectionExtent()` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_export.js:458-461`) sets `bytes: w * h * 4` on BOTH backends whenever `w * h <= SNAP_CANVAS_PX` (`16 * 1024 * 1024` px = up to 64 MiB per snapshot, e.g. any selection on a 4000x4000 image or any <= 4096x4096 selection on a 15k image):
1. Unpushed held snapshots (`holdUndo` / `landUndo` from commit 1b2f05d7): In `pointerDownNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:419-435`), pressing with the `rect` or `ellipse` tool in `add`, `subtract`, or `intersect` mode (`Shift`, `Alt`, or `Shift+Alt`) calls `this.holdUndo(step)` (`lines 19-23`), which calls `this.snapshot(step)` without adding `snap.bytes` to `this.undoBytes`. Releasing without dragging >3 screen px runs `onPointerUp` (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:1012`): `this.landUndo(p, !(p.startPx && !p.moved && p.mode !== "replace"))` -> `landUndo(p, false)` (`lines 25-30`) -> `this.releaseSnapshot(snap)`, subtracting up to 64 MiB that was never added. (By contrast, `layer._textUndo` releases in `inpaint_ed_text.js:182,235,248`, `inpaint_ed_masks.js:330`, and `inpaint_ed_history.js:131`, as well as unpushed `transform`/`canvas`/`layers`/`turn` releases, happen to subtract `0` today only because `snapshotOf` omits `bytes` on those kinds.)
2. Dropped stale async selection edits (`dropStaleSelectionEdit` from commit 1f27f6d6): `featherSelectionNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1168-1173`), `growSelectionNow` (`lines 1432-1436`), and `invertSelectionNow` (`lines 1481-1494`) push `undoSnap` once (`+B`) and, if the selection changes while the worker/pool runs, call `dropStaleSelectionEdit(undoSnap, ...)` (`lines 645-653`), which manually executes `this.undoBytes -= popped.bytes || 0;` (`line 648`) AND then calls `this.releaseSnapshot(popped)` (`line 649`), subtracting `B` twice (`+B - 2B = -B`).
3. Cancelled or failed range selections (`cancelRange` and `selectRange`): `selectRange` pushes `snap` once (`inpaint_ed_select.js:74-75`, `+B`), and both `cancelRange()` (`lines 663-668`, triggered by Escape at `inpaint_canvas.js:300` / `inpaint_ed_pointer.js:106`) and `selectRange`'s `catch` block (`lines 606-611`) subtract `popped.bytes || 0` manually and then call `this.releaseSnapshot(popped)` (`-2B`); moreover, if `pending.snap` was already trimmed or cleared from `this.undo`, `cancelRange`'s `else if (pending.snap)` branch (`lines 668-671`) calls `this.releaseSnapshot(pending.snap)` a second time.

No guard clamps `this.undoBytes` at `0` or recomputes it from `this.undo`/`this.redo`; only `clearUndo()` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:617`) resets it. Consequently, the accumulated negative offset persists across the editing session and directly weakens `trimUndo()` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:501`: `this.undoBytes > bytes && this.undo.length > 1`), allowing subsequent large `layerrect` or `maps` undo steps to exceed `maxUndoBytes` (default 384 MiB) by hundreds of megabytes up to `maxUndo` steps. Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, all three `verified.json` files, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: this defect is not in any known list (it is a new regression in the 2026-11-12 review fixes `1b2f05d7` and `1f27f6d6`, alongside `cancelRange`). Severity is `should` because users hit it in normal Shift/Alt marquee clicks and Escape-cancelled range selections on the default backend, breaking the configured undo memory cap until history is cleared.

findings.claim: Adding a contact shadow to a clipped layer (`layer.clip === true`) inserts the shadow unclipped underneath the clipping base `target` instead of clipped directly underneath `layer`. Wherever `target` is opaque — the only region where the clipped `layer` itself is visible — `target` paints over and hides the shadow on Apply (contradicting the dialog's live preview overlay), while outside `target` the unclipped shadow leaks onto the backdrop below `target`.
findings.scenario: Place a cut-out object layer `L` above a non-fullscreen card or tabletop layer `B` (`opacity: 1`, `blend: "normal"`), clip `L` to `B` (`L.clip = true`), and open Layer > Add Contact Shadow on `L`. In the dialog preview (`drawShadowOverlay`, drawn over the scene), the contact shadow appears on `B` beneath `L`'s foot; click Apply (or run MCP `contact_shadow` on `L`). `L shadow` (`clip: false`, `blend: "multiply"`) is inserted at index 0 below `B`, so `B` completely covers and hides the shadow under `L` while any part of the shadow extending past `B`'s edge darkens the background behind `B`.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shadow.js:203-207`: `shadowPlace(layer) { const i = this.layers.indexOf(layer); if (!layer.clip) return { at: i, group: layer.group || null, clip: false }; const target = this.clipTargetOf(layer, i); if (target) return { at: this.layers.indexOf(target), group: target.group || null, clip: false }; ... }`, used by `addContactShadow` (`lines 238-241`) to splice `out` at `place.at` (`target`'s index, below `target`) with `clip: false`. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:70-93` (`drawLayersInto`), `out` at index 0 is drawn onto the backdrop before `target` at index 1 draws over it in `source-over`, whereas `clipTargetOf` (`lines 105-115`) skips clipped layers (`if (b.clip) continue;`), so inserting `out` at `i` with `clip: true` would keep `layer` clipped to `target` without making `out` its base.
findings.fix: In `shadowPlace` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shadow.js:206-210`), when `layer.clip` is true, insert the shadow directly below `layer` with `clip: true` (`return { at: i, group: layer.group || null, clip: true };`) so both `out` and `layer` clip to the same `target` above `target`.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `shadowPlace(layer)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shadow.js:203-211`) resolves `const target = this.clipTargetOf(layer, i);` and at line 207 returns `{ at: this.layers.indexOf(target), group: target.group || null, clip: false }`. `addContactShadow` (`lines 238-243`) then creates `out` (`blend: "multiply"`, `clip: place.clip`) and splices it at `place.at` — i.e., underneath the unclipped clipping base `target` with `clip: false`. No guard in `shadowRefusal` (`lines 38-45`), `contactShadowDialogNow` (`lines 272-341`), or `commands_layers.js:127-146` (`contact_shadow`) prevents running Contact Shadow on a clipped pixel layer.

Tracing all three compositing paths (`drawLayersInto` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:70-93`, `glViewComposite` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_display.js:311-359`, and `stackPlan` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:150-207`) confirms the visual failure: when `layer` (`clip: true`) is clipped to an opaque `normal`-blend pixel layer `B` (`clipBaseOf(layer) === B`), `out` at index 0 composites onto the backdrop below `B`, and `B` at index 1 immediately draws over it in `source-over` (`alpha = 1`), completely overwriting and hiding the shadow across the entire region where the clipped `layer` itself can be seen. Simultaneously, any portion of `out` extending outside `B`'s alpha darkens the backdrop behind `B` unclipped (and if `B` is hidden, `layer` is skipped at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:75` while `out` remains visible on its own). By contrast, while the dialog is open (`contactShadowDialogNow`, `lines 282-295`), `drawShadowOverlay` (`lines 186-195`, called from `drawOverlays` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_view.js:691, 697`) paints the preview on top of the composited scene, showing the shadow on `B` right until Apply makes it disappear. Because `clipTargetOf` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:105-115`) skips clipped layers (`if (b.clip) continue;`), inserting `out` at `i` with `clip: true` would keep both `out` and `layer` clipped to `target` without making `out` the clipping base.

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md`, and the three `verified.json` files: item 61 (`inpaint_ed_shadow.js`) was introduced in the 2026-11-15/16 night build (`4fad3634`), and `shadowPlace` was added in review-fix commit `e55907d8` (`PLAN_0_1_57.md:78-79`), whose gate (`tools/editor_test.py:14552-14573`) only tested clipping over a filter layer and clipping at index 0, missing the primary case of clipping to a pixel base layer. Thus this is a genuine remaining defect in the new fix rather than a known issue. Severity is `should`: a user-visible functional bug in a plausible clipped-layer workflow that contradicts the live dialog preview, with a manual workaround (reordering and clipping the created shadow layer in the Layers panel) and no destructive loss of existing pixels.

findings.claim: When a Generate result lands while the user is typing in a text layer's panel `<textarea>` or dragging a Colour Match or filter slider in the layer list, `addResults` snapshots the user's pre-edit state into the `"Result n"` undo record and immediately calls `addLayer` -> `renderLayers()`, wiping `layerList.innerHTML`. Detaching the active control aborts the edit without firing `change` (so its own undo step is never pushed and `filterPreview` stays stuck), and pressing `Ctrl+Z` once to undo `"Result n"` reverts the user's text, match, or filter edit along with the result.
findings.scenario: Start a local or API Generate run, then while waiting for it to finish either (a) click a text layer's `<textarea>` in the Layers panel and type new text without blurring, or (b) drag a layer's Colour Match slider or a filter layer's parameter slider and hold the pointer down. When the result lands, `addResults` switches `activeLayerId` to `Result 1` and rebuilds `layerList`, kicking focus/capture off the control without committing its undo step; press `Ctrl+Z` once to remove `Result 1` and the typed text or slider adjustment is wiped back to the value from before the edit started.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:662-663`: `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Result " + n }); const layer = this.addLayer({ name: "Result " + n, ... });`. During `pushUndo`, `snapshotLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:191-210`) overwrites the record's `c.params` (`committedFilter` via `l._undoPending` while `this.filterPreview === l.id`, `inpaint_ed_depth.js:1107, 1115-1122`), `c.text` (`typing && l._textUndo`, `lines 200-208`), and `c.match` (`l._matchUndo`, `line 210`) with the edit's `"before"` values assuming `"the edit itself goes on"`. On the next line, `addLayer` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:523, 544, 549`) sets `this.activeLayerId = layer.id` and calls `this.renderLayers()`, which executes `list.innerHTML = ""` (`line 695`). As `renderLayersUnlessEditing` (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:1126-1128`) notes, rebuilding the list under a slider ends the drag without `change` so its step is never pushed, and `ta`'s `blur` (`inpaint_ed_text.js:248, 258`) only drops unchanged snapshots (`JSON.stringify(s.text) === JSON.stringify(layer.text)`), never committing modified text.
findings.fix: Before `pushUndo` in `addResults` (or when `layerList` holds an active text/slider edit), either settle and push any active panel edit first (`settleTextUndo`, `_matchUndo`, `_undoPending`, clearing `filterPreview`) so it becomes its own undo step below `"Result n"`, or pass `{ activate: false }` to `addLayer` and defer `renderLayers()` via `renderLayersUnlessEditing()` while a panel control is being edited.
findings.why:
At `f45a86cc`, `addResults` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:662-663`) executes `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Result " + n })` and immediately calls `this.addLayer({ name: "Result " + n, ... })`. During `pushUndo` -> `snapshot({ kind: "layers" })` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:412`), `snapshotLayer(l)` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:191-210`, extended in commit `725478dc`) intentionally replaces any live in-progress edit on `l` with its pre-edit `"before"` state under the assumption that `"the edit itself goes on"`: for a filter control with an active preview (`this.previewShown(l)` true while `l._undoPending` is set and `this.filterPreview === l.id`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:1106-1123`), `c.params` gets `committedFilter(l).params`; for a focused control inside `[data-layer="${l.id}"]` (`typing === true`, lines 200-208), `c.text` and `c.px` get `l._textUndo`'s pre-edit state; and for a held Colour Match drag (`l._matchUndo`, line 210), `c.match` gets `l._matchUndo.match`.

Whereas on-canvas edits (`this.textEdit` mounted in `this.viewEl` and `this.pointer` on `viewCanvas`) survive `addLayer`, panel controls live inside `this.layerList` on the active layer's row (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:803, 824-851`). On the very next line (`663`), `addLayer` (`lines 523, 544, 549`) sets `this.activeLayerId = layer.id` and calls `this.renderLayers()`, which wipes `list.innerHTML = ""` (`line 695`). Detaching a focused `<textarea>` / `<input type="color">` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:246-261, 283-286, 313-316`) or a dragged `<input type="range">` / curves / limit bar (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:836-843`; `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:101-105, 173-187, 198-210, 323-431`) aborts the interaction without firing `change` (as `renderLayersUnlessEditing` at `inpaint_ed_depth.js:1126-1128` explicitly notes, and `ta`'s `blur` handler `drop` at `inpaint_ed_text.js:248` only releases unchanged snapshots). Consequently, no undo step is pushed for the panel edit, `this.filterPreview` and `_undoPending` / `_matchUndo` / `_textUndo` remain stuck on `l`, and pressing `Ctrl+Z` once to undo `"Result n"` reverts the user's text, match, or filter edit back to the pre-edit state along with removing the result. Even worse, for filter and match drags, `historyStepNow` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:1098-1100`) runs `this.cancelPreviews()` (calling `cancelFilterParams(l)`) and `this.snapshot(snap)` (reading the stuck `l._matchUndo` in `snapshotLayer`) before `applySnapshot`, so even `Ctrl+Y` (redo) permanently loses the adjustment.

Checked against all known-issue lists (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the 2026-11-07 / 2026-11-12 `verified.json` files): `canvas-tools/stale-text-undo-snapshot` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` was an older missing-`blur` / missing-`settleTextUndo` bug fixed prior to `f45a86cc`, whereas this defect was newly introduced on 2026-11-16 by `31a1c4ba` + `725478dc` writing pre-edit state into `"Result n"` right before `addLayer` destroys the active panel row. Severity is `should`: editing another layer in the panel while waiting 10-60s for a local or API Generate run is an explicitly supported workflow (`docs/MANUAL.md:98`, `inpaint_canvas.js:1338-1341`), and typing in the panel `<textarea>` keeps focus indefinitely until `addResults` lands and causes silent loss of user edits on `Ctrl+Z`.

findings.claim: On the canvas backend (`!this.tileMode`), `snapshotLayer` during an open text edit sets `c.w, c.h` to the pre-edit dimensions `tb.w, tb.h` and marks `c._textRedraw = true`, but leaves `c.px` pointing at `l.px` from the newly typed text. When that `layers` or `canvas` undo step is restored, `renderTextLayer` computes the user scale factor `k = layer.w / (layer.px.width / oldRes)` from `tb.w` divided by the edited `l.px.width`, shrinking or blowing up the restored text layer.
findings.scenario: Launch or open an editor on the canvas backend (`!tileMode`), create a text layer containing `"a"` (`w = 20`, `px.width = 40`), start a Generate run, double-click the text on canvas (`beginTextEdit`) and type `"hello world"` (after 120 ms `l.px.width` becomes ~400 and `l.w` ~200). Let the Generate result land while `textEdit` is still open, press `Esc` to cancel the inline text edit, and press `Ctrl+Z` to undo `Result 1`: the restored `"a"` text layer renders shrunken to ~10% of its original size (or ~10x oversized if text was shortened during the edit).
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:177, 203-208`: `const c = { ...l }; ... if (tb && l.text) { c.text = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(tb.text)); Object.assign(c, { x: tb.x, y: tb.y, w: tb.w, h: tb.h, dirty: true }); if (tb.px) c.px = tb.px.clone(); else c._textRedraw = true; }`. On the canvas backend `snapshot({ kind: "text" })` (`lines 428, 438, 452`) sets `{ url, cw: layer.px.width, ch: layer.px.height }` with `tb.px === undefined`, so `c.px` stays `l.px` (the edited text's pixels). On undo, `applySnapshot` (`lines 632-633`) calls `releaseDroppedEdits` (`line 135`: `if (l.text) this.renderTextLayer(l);`), and `renderTextLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:111-112, 132-133`) sees `had = layer.px && layer.px.width > 1` (`true`) and computes `let k = keepScale && had ? layer.w / (layer.px.width / oldRes) : 1;`, dividing `tb.w` by `l.px.width / oldRes` instead of `tb.cw / oldRes`.
findings.fix: In `snapshotLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:208`), when `!tb.px`, replace `c.px` with an empty `LayerPixels` of the pre-edit pixel dimensions (`c.px = this.pixels.Layer.empty(tb.cw || 1, tb.ch || 1); c._textRedraw = true;`) so `renderTextLayer` reads `tb.cw` as `layer.px.width` (and does not retain the discarded canvas).
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js and renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js. In snapshotLayer(l) (inpaint_ed_history.js:176-216), line 177 shallow-copies the live layer via `const c = { ...l }`, so `c.px` initially aliases `l.px`. When a text edit is in progress on `l` — either via the inline canvas editor (`this.textEdit && this.textEdit.layer === l`, opened by `beginTextEdit` at inpaint_ed_text.js:20) or via a focused control in the Layers panel (`typing && l._textUndo && l._textUndo.kind === "text"`, taken on focus at inpaint_ed_text.js:246) — lines 203-209 overwrite `c.text`, `c.x`, `c.y`, `c.w`, `c.h`, and `c.dirty` from the pre-edit text snapshot `tb`, and line 208 executes `if (tb.px) c.px = tb.px.clone(); else c._textRedraw = true;`.

On the canvas backend (`!this.tileMode`, which is the default in the ComfyUI node via `editorTileMode` at inpaint_consts.js:11-16 and selectable in Scumble via Settings > Rendering > Tile engine or `--no-tiles`), `snapshotOf` for `step.kind === "text"` (inpaint_ed_history.js:428, 438, 452-453) stores `{ url: this.snapUrl(p.toCanvas()), cw: layer.px.width, ch: layer.px.height, x: layer.x, y: layer.y, w: layer.w, h: layer.h, ... }` with `tb.px === undefined`. Meanwhile, as the user types, `scheduleTextRender` (inpaint_ed_text.js:149-152) re-runs `renderTextLayer` after 120 ms and replaces `l.px` (`layer.px = px`, line 129) with a new canvas sized to the edited text. When a `layers` or `canvas` undo step is then taken while the edit is open — for example when `addResults` (inpaint_ed_layers.js:662) pushes `"Result n"` for a landed Generate run, or an MCP/assistant command pushes a `layers`/`canvas` step — `snapshotLayer` sets `c.w = tb.w, c.h = tb.h` and `c._textRedraw = true`, but leaves `c.px` pointing at the edited `l.px`.

No guard or later step repairs `c.px`: whether the user cancels the inline edit with Escape (`endTextEdit(false)` at inpaint_ed_text.js:60-74, which replaces `te.layer.px` on the live layer without touching `c.px` on the undo record and pushes no `Edit text` step) and presses Ctrl+Z once, or commits the text edit with Enter (`endTextEdit(true)`) and later presses Ctrl+Z twice to undo past `Result n`, `applySnapshot` (inpaint_ed_history.js:632-633 for `layers`, 757-758 for `canvas`) installs the snapshot's layer copy and calls `releaseDroppedEdits` (line 135: `for (const l of this.layers) if (l && l._textRedraw) { delete l._textRedraw; if (l.text) this.renderTextLayer(l); }`). Inside `renderTextLayer` (inpaint_ed_text.js:110-114, 132-133) with default `keepScale = true`, `had = layer.px && layer.px.width > 1` is `true`, and `let k = keepScale && had ? layer.w / (layer.px.width / oldRes) : 1;` divides the pre-edit `tb.w` by the edited `l.px.width / oldRes` instead of `tb.cw / oldRes` (missing the `Math.abs(k - 1) * (layer.px.width / oldRes) < 1` drift guard whenever the width changed by >= 1 px). Lines 132-133 then set `layer.w` and `layer.h` scaled by `tb.cw / l_edited.px.width`, shrinking or blowing up the restored text layer.

Checked known-issue sources (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md`, and all three `verified.json` files): not known. `_textRedraw` and lines 197-214 of `inpaint_ed_history.js` were newly introduced on 2026-11-16 in commit `725478dc` ("Review of the landing step: records hold an edit's before, a run's end keeps a text edit open") after the 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-12 reviews. Severity is `should`: typing on a text layer while a Generate run finishes is the exact workflow `725478dc` targets, it deterministically corrupts the text layer's geometry on undo on the canvas backend (default in the ComfyUI node, user-configurable in Scumble), and while no pixel data is permanently lost (the text remains vector-editable and can be resized or redone), the visual corruption is immediate and severe.

findings.claim: `ScopePart.updateScope` calls `sampleRegionSettled` with `{ display: true }` and leaves `forRun` false, so visible reference layers (`@img1`, ...) and control layers are composited over the sampled picture and counted into the Scope histogram and `Black % · White %` clipping readout. Because reference layers must stay `visible: true` to hold an `@img` label, any active reference card skews the picture's histogram and triggers false clipping warnings even though exports and runs exclude it.
findings.scenario: Open a mid-tone photo with 0% pure black and 0% pure white. Add a product reference layer (`add_image_layer` with `role: 'reference'`, or Shift+drop) that has a `#ffffff` background; it sits visible at a third of the canvas in the top-left as `@img1`. Open Image › Scope to grade the photo with Curves. `updateScope()` samples the composite without `forRun: true`, drawing the `@img1` card over the photo: the histogram shows a pure-white spike and `scopeInfo` warns `White ~8 %` in yellow, although `Export Image` and `Generate` exclude reference and control layers and have `White 0.0 %`.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_scope.js:323 `const src = await this.sampleRegionSettled("image", [0, 0, this.width, this.height], s, { display: true });`. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:46,84-86 `drawLayersInto(ctx, { forRun = false, ... } = {}) { ... const ctrl = this.isControl(layer); ... if (forRun && (ctrl || this.isReference(layer))) continue; }` and renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:812,851 `passStores(..., { forRun = false, ... }) { ... if (forRun && (this.isControl(layer) || this.isReference(layer))) continue; }`. Contrast `renderer/plugins.js:102` (`{ forRun: true }`) and `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:18` (`referenceLayers()` requires `l.visible`).
findings.fix: Pass `{ forRun: true, display: true }` to `this.sampleRegionSettled("image", [0, 0, this.width, this.height], s, { forRun: true, display: true })` in `updateScope()`.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `ScopePart.updateScope()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_scope.js:323`) reads the composite via `await this.sampleRegionSettled("image", [0, 0, this.width, this.height], s, { display: true })`, omitting `forRun: true`. Tracing the call path: `sampleRegionSettled` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:892-903`) forwards `opts` (`{ display: true }`, so `forRun` defaults to `false`) to `primePass` -> `passStores` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:812, 851`, which only skips `this.isControl(layer) || this.isReference(layer)` when `forRun` is truthy) and to `sampleRegion` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:27-83`, `viewPass.forRun = !!opts.forRun`) -> `drawComposite` -> `drawLayersInto` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:46, 86`, `if (forRun && (ctrl || this.isReference(layer))) continue;`). Consequently, every visible reference card (`role === "reference"`) and visible control layer (`role !== "none" && role !== "reference"`) inside `[0, 0, width, height]` is composited over the image and counted into `scopeHistogram(bytes)` (`inpaint_ed_scope.js:23-65, 333`) as well as the `Black % · White %` readout (`inpaint_ed_scope.js:392-394`).

Refutation checks confirm this is an unintended omission rather than consistent design. While `drawViewComposite` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_display.js:382`) and `drawClipWarning` (`inpaint_ed_scope.js:185-211`, operating on `sceneCanvas`) show helper cards on the stage so the user can place/mask them, Scumble explicitly defines reference and control layers as "not part of the image" / "no part of the picture" (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:122, 782, 860, 1134`, `inpaint_ed_composite.js:416`), excludes them from exports (`inpaint_ed_export.js:88-89`), `flattenNow` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:420`), `plugins.js` `flatten` (`renderer/plugins.js:77, 102`), and runs, and defaults every other whole-picture grading/statistics reader to `forRun = true` (`pictureStats`, `pictureHistogram`, and `pictureSample` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1008-1022`, `setRangePreview` at `:1288`, and `handlePickOnce` at `:1410, 1428`). In fact, `inpaint_ed_scope.js:5-6` comments that Scope is "read through sampleRegionSettled as the eyedropper and the filters' statistics read it", overlooking that `pictureStats`/`pictureHistogram` pass `forRun = true` by default. Passing `{ forRun: true, display: true }` is also safe with colour-match layers (`sampledMatchStats` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_match.js:251-259` caches `forRun` separately in `_mstatsSampleRun`).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-12 `verified.json` files: `inpaint_ed_scope.js` was newly added on 2026-11-15 in commit `0395462b` (updated in `105ee0b1`) and is not in any known list. Severity is `should`: exports and paid runs are unaffected (not `must`), but in normal workflows an active reference card defaults to 1/3 canvas width/height (~11% of canvas area, `inpaint_ed_layers.js:97`), has no opacity slider in `renderReferences` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:1065-1144`), and cannot be hidden without disabling it from runs and parking/renumbering `@img` prompt tokens (`inpaint_ed_refs.js:18`, `inpaint_ed_layers.js:1110-1116`), so any white-background product reference or black-ground pose/control layer skews the grading histogram and falsely trips the `>= 0.1%` yellow clipping readout unless dragged off-canvas.

findings.claim: fromPrompt (and detach for Comfy Cloud) preserves every consumer when one Inpaint Canvas setting_<n> output fans out to multiple node inputs, emitting multiple recipe.settings entries with the same 1-based index. However, InpaintEditor stores row values in editor.settings[String(t.index)] keyed solely by slot index rather than target key. When two targets share an index, settingsChanged overwrites the first target with the second on every pass (resetting user-entered values), renderSettings binds both UI controls to the second target's label and entry, and host.rowValues omits all earlier targets so queueGenerate and provider runs never send the Settings value to the other wired node inputs.
findings.scenario: In the ComfyUI window, wire setting_1 of InpaintCanvas to both k1.seed and k2.seed (the fan-out pattern supported by comfyparams.listParams in commit 33b21be9) and click Save as new recipe. fromPrompt writes two entries with index: 1 ({ index: 1, node: "k1", input: "seed" } and { index: 1, node: "k2", input: "seed" }) and replaces both prompt inputs with static literals. In the editor's Settings panel, two controls appear, both labeled with k2's title. Change the seed in the Settings panel to 42 and click Generate (or run set_settings with {"1": 42}): rowValues checks e.target === target against editor.settings["1"], whose target is "<recipe>/k2:seed", so "<recipe>/k1:seed" is dropped from rows and k1.inputs.seed runs with its saved default instead of 42 (and set_settings immediately calls settingsChanged(), which sees cur.target mismatch on k1 then k2 and resets 42 back to k2's widget default).
findings.evidence: electron/main/comfyparams.js:48-49, 88-89 explicitly allows one setting_<n> output to feed multiple inputs, and electron/main/recipes_graph.js:98-111 (`fromPrompt`) pushes `{ index, node: id, input: name, ... }` for every wired input while replacing `node.inputs[name]` with a literal (`node.inputs[name] = value !== undefined ? value : specDefault(spec);` at line 107; `detach` at line 693 copies `index: s.index` to Comfy Cloud `settings`). `renderer/editor/host_presets.js:669-687` (`settingTargets`) emits one target per `r.settings` entry with `index: s.index` and `key: \`${r.id}/${s.node}:${s.input}\``. `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:998-1014` (`settingsChanged`) keys `this.settings` by `const key = String(t.index);` (line 999) and checks `if (!cur || cur.target !== target)` (line 1007), so two targets with `t.index === 1` and distinct `target` strings clobber `this.settings["1"]` on every call (`renderer/commands_gen.js:97-100` `set_settings` writes `ed.settings[String(t.index)]` then calls `ed.settingsChanged()`). `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1033-1042` (`renderSettings`) reads `const entry = this.settings[String(t.index)]` for every target. Finally, `renderer/editor/host_presets.js:89-93` (`rowValues`) runs `const e = editor.settings[String(t.index)]; if (e && e.target === target) out.push([target, e.value]);`, omitting the first target so `renderer/editor/host_queue.js:84, 217-220` (`const value = rows.get(\`${r.id}/${s.node}:${s.input}\`); if (value != null && node && node.inputs) node.inputs[s.input] = value;`) never writes the Settings value into `k1`.
findings.fix: Either treat a fanned-out `setting_<n>` slot as one shared row in `settingTargets` (one UI row for `index: n` that fan-outs its value to all `r.settings` entries sharing `s.index === n` in `queueGenerate` / `runProvider`, matching how `setting_<n>` behaves in ComfyUI), or key `editor.settings` by `t.key || String(t.index)` when `t.key` is present so each target keeps its own state while `fromPrompt` / `listParams` clarifies whether fan-out shares one control or distinct controls.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc`. Fan-out of a single `InpaintCanvas` `setting_<n>` output to multiple node inputs is explicitly supported in `electron/main/comfyparams.js:48-49, 88-89` (and tested in `tools/comfyparams_test.js:115-128`, where `setting_1` feeds both `k1.seed` and `k2.seed`). When such a graph is saved via the ComfyUI window (`fromGraph` -> `fromPrompt` at `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:98-112`) or imported as an API prompt, `fromPrompt` replaces every wired input with a static literal (`node.inputs[name] = ...` at line 107) and pushes one `recipe.settings` entry per consumer sharing the same 1-based `index` (e.g. `{ index: 1, node: "k1", input: "seed" }` and `{ index: 1, node: "k2", input: "seed" }`), which `normalize` (`electron/main/recipes_store.js:515-570`) preserves.

In the renderer, `host.settingTargets` (`renderer/editor/host_presets.js:669-687`) emits one target per `r.settings` entry with the same `index: 1` and distinct `key` strings (`"<r.id>/k1:seed"` and `"<r.id>/k2:seed"`). However, `InpaintEditor.settingsChanged` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:995-1018`) stores entries in `this.settings[String(t.index)]` (line 999) and checks `if (!cur || cur.target !== target)` (line 1007). With two targets sharing `t.index === 1`, every call to `settingsChanged()` ping-pongs `cur.target`: `t1` mismatches `t2`'s target and resets `this.settings["1"]` to `t1`'s widget value, then `t2` mismatches `t1`'s target and overwrites `this.settings["1"]` with `t2`'s widget value and target. Consequently: (1) `renderSettings` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1033-1072`) renders two controls that both show `t2`'s `entry.label` and mutate the same `entry` (only remembering `t2`'s target via `onSettingSet`); (2) `set_settings` (`renderer/commands_gen.js:97-100`) writes `ed.settings["1"].value = v` and immediately calls `ed.settingsChanged()`, which clobbers `v` back to `t2`'s default/remembered value; and (3) on a local/API ComfyUI `Generate`, `queueGenerate` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:84`) builds `rows` from `this.rowValues(editor, this.settingTargets())` (`renderer/editor/host_presets.js:86-95`), which checks `e.target === target` and omits `"<r.id>/k1:seed"`, so `host_queue.js:217-221` never writes the Settings value into `prompt.k1.inputs.seed` and `k1` runs with its baked default.

One minor nuance in the finding's wording: on a detached Comfy Cloud recipe (`recipes_graph.js:693`), `settingTargets` (`host_presets.js:653-665`) does hit the same `settingsChanged` clobbering, duplicate `renderSettings` labels, and `set_settings` reset, whereas `runProvider` (`renderer/editor/host_provider.js:321`) reads `providerParams` (`host_presets.js:710-720`) rather than `rowValues`, and `providerParams` does not check `entry.target` so a UI-set value still reaches both `k1|seed` and `k2|seed` unless `settingsChanged()` ran afterwards.
