Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, both 2026-11-07 `verified.json` files, `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: `host/H-2` (2026-11-07) covered cross-recipe leakage on `restore()` and its fix introduced the `e.target === target` filter in `rowValues`, creating this remaining gap for intra-recipe fan-out. Severity `should`: easily hit on multi-sampler ComfyUI graphs that fan out one `setting_<n>` slot, with a workaround of wiring separate `setting_<n>` outputs.

findings.claim: Opening a ComfyUI recipe in the ComfyUI window replaces every `recipe.settings` input in the prompt sent to the page with `[canvasId, slot]` (`toPrompt`) without seeding the page's widget with the recipe's stored literal value, and unticking that row in Parameters (`exposeScript`) disconnects the link without restoring the recipe's value. When the graph is then saved (`fromPrompt`), `baseValue` is consulted only for inputs still wired to `canvasId`, so any unticked row silently reverts in the saved recipe to ComfyUI's node default (or a stale UI `workflow` widget value) instead of keeping the recipe's own value.
findings.scenario: Take a ComfyUI recipe `R` without a stored UI `workflow` whose prompt sets `KSampler.steps = 8` (while ComfyUI's `KSampler` widget defaults to `20`) or `UNETLoader.unet_name` to the recipe's model file (while ComfyUI's widget defaults to the first model in `models/diffusion_models`), with that input exposed in `R.settings`. Open the ComfyUI window, click `Parameters`, untick `steps` (or `unet_name`) so users can no longer override it from Scumble's Settings panel, and click `Save to recipe`. `toPrompt` stripped `8` before `loadApiJson`, so the page's widget initialized to `20`; `disconnectInput` left `20` on the widget; `fromPrompt` saves `steps: 20` (or the wrong model file) into `R.prompt`, changing every subsequent run of the recipe.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:34-37` (`toPrompt`): `for (const s of recipe.settings || []) { if (!s || !s.index || !prompt[s.node] || !s.input) continue; prompt[s.node].inputs = { ...(prompt[s.node].inputs || {}), [s.input]: [canvasId, FIXED_OUTPUTS + s.index - 1] }; }` overwrites the literal value in `recipe.prompt`. `electron/main/main.js:1150` (`comfyRecipe`) passes `prompt: recipes.toPrompt(r)` and `electron/main/comfyview.js:150-156` (`loadScript`) loads `recipe.workflow` or `recipe.prompt` without writing `r.prompt[s.node].inputs[s.input]` onto the page's widgets. On untick, `electron/main/comfyparams.js:170-175` (`exposeScript` with `on = false`) runs `node.disconnectInput(slot);` and leaves the widget untouched. On save, `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:100-107` (`fromPrompt`) skips any unlinked input at line 101 (`if (!Array.isArray(v) || String(v[0]) !== canvasId || +v[1] < FIXED_OUTPUTS) continue;`), so `baseRow` / `baseValue` (lines 84-93) never run for the unticked input.
findings.fix: Pass a `{ "<node>|<input>": literalValue }` map from `r.prompt` for `r.settings` alongside the held recipe in `comfyRecipe`, and after `loadGraphData` / `loadApiJson` in `loadScript` (or on `disconnectInput` in `exposeScript`), assign each matching widget's `.value` on the page when `r.workflow` did not already set one, so disconnecting a `setting_<n>` link leaves the recipe's own value in the widget.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc across the full call path for both recipes without a stored `workflow` and recipes with one.

1. Call path when `recipe.workflow` is absent (true of ALL shipped ComfyUI recipes, such as `recipes/flux2_klein_local.json`, `recipes/flux3_klein_local.json`, and `recipes/realism_pass.json`, AND all recipes imported via `recipes.importFile` at `electron/main/recipes.js:276-284`, since neither `fromWorkflow` at `electron/main/recipes_workflow.js:279-283` nor `fromPrompt` at `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:117` stores `workflow`): `comfyRecipe(id)` (`electron/main/main.js:1150`) passes `{ prompt: recipes.toPrompt(r), workflow: null }` to `ComfyView`, discarding the literal values in `r.prompt[s.node].inputs[s.input]` for every `s` in `r.settings` because `toPrompt` (`electron/main/recipes_graph.js:34-37`, line 36) overwrites each with `[canvasId, FIXED_OUTPUTS + s.index - 1]`. `loadScript` (`electron/main/comfyview.js:150-156`) calls `window.app.loadApiJson(recipe.prompt, name)`, which initializes linked widgets on the page to ComfyUI's node-spec defaults (e.g., `CFGGuider.cfg = 8` instead of `5` or `1`, `BasicScheduler.steps = 20` instead of `16`, `DLSS5Settings.dlss_model_preset = "Default"` instead of `"L"`, or `options[0]` for `UNETLoader`/`CLIPLoader` model filenames). When the user unticks a row in Parameters, `expose` (`electron/main/comfyview.js:754-763`) runs `exposeScript(node, input, false)` (`electron/main/comfyparams.js:170-175`), which calls `node.disconnectInput(slot)` without restoring any widget value; `readParams()` immediately displays ComfyUI's default, and on `Save to recipe` / `Save as new recipe` (`comfyview.js:688-700` -> `main.js:1182` -> `recipes_graph.js:146-151`), `graphToPrompt()` emits that unlinked widget default in `output[id].inputs[name]`. Inside `fromPrompt` (`electron/main/recipes_graph.js:98-111`), line 101 (`if (!Array.isArray(v) || String(v[0]) !== canvasId || +v[1] < FIXED_OUTPUTS) continue;`) skips unlinked inputs, so `baseRow` / `baseValue` (lines 84-93) are never consulted for unticked rows and the recipe's own value is silently overwritten with ComfyUI's default. Notably, both tests (`tools/comfyparams_test.js:34-35` and `tools/comfyview_test.py:667-671`) masked this bug by manually extracting `r.prompt[s.node].inputs[s.input]` and passing it as `widgets` into `__miniGraph` (`tools/fixtures/comfyview/minigraph.js:46-48`), which production `comfyRecipe` / `loadScript` never do.

2. Call path when `recipe.workflow` IS present (`comfyview.js:152-153` calls `window.app.loadGraphData(recipe.workflow, true, true, name)`, ignoring `recipe.prompt`): a ComfyUI recipe only acquires `workflow` when previously saved through `fromGraph` (`recipes_graph.js:151`). If the graph was originally built from scratch in the ComfyUI page where the widget itself held the intended value and `r.prompt` was never edited externally, `r.workflow`'s `widgets_values` happens to match `r.prompt` and unticking keeps that value. However, if a shipped or `importFile` recipe was opened once via `loadApiJson` and saved back (creating `r.workflow`) while that Settings row stayed ticked—e.g., after moving nodes or editing another parameter—`fromPrompt` preserved `baseValue` in `r.prompt` (`recipes_graph.js:106`) while `graphToPrompt()` recorded ComfyUI's default widget value inside `r.workflow`. On any subsequent open via `loadGraphData(r.workflow)` (or if `r.prompt` was edited outside the page), the widget is seeded with that stale `r.workflow` widget value rather than `r.prompt[s.node].inputs[s.input]`, so unticking and saving still clobbers the recipe's stored value.

3. Known-list & severity check: Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and `docs/PLAN_COMFY_VIEW.md` (item 66 landed 2026-11-15; its review fixed untick-then-retick via `baseRow` fallback at `recipes_graph.js:87`, leaving plain untick unfixed). Severity `should` is well calibrated: unticking an exposed parameter in the new Parameters UI on any shipped or imported ComfyUI recipe silently corrupts the saved recipe's parameters or model filenames on local ComfyUI runs, with a manual workaround of editing the widget in the graph after unticking.

findings.claim: When editing a placed 3D object or mannequin, `place()` checks `ed.isLocked` before mutating state only for control layers being removed (`gone`), not for kept control layers (`was`) whose pixels will be replaced. If the user locked the depth or OpenPose pose control layer, `place()` pushes the undo step and overwrites the main object layer's pixels and placement, then throws inside `replacePixels(was.id, ...)` (`doc.setPixels`), leaving the visible object layer at the new pose while the control layer and `glb` plugin data keep the old pose. Furthermore, `existing.locked` and `doc.setPixels` check `l.locked` rather than `ed.isLocked(l)`, allowing edits to overwrite layers inside a locked group.
findings.scenario: Place a mannequin (`glb.place({ mannequin: true })`), creating `Mannequin`, `Mannequin depth`, and `Mannequin pose`. Lock `Mannequin pose` in the Layers panel (`locked: true`), then open `Edit` in the 3D object panel (or run `glb.edit({ pose: "walking" })`) with the Pose layer checkbox still ticked. `place()` passes lines 168-173 because `Mannequin` is unlocked and `gone` is empty, pushes `"Edit mannequin"` onto `ed.undo`, and replaces `Mannequin`'s pixels and bounds with the walking pose. At line 215, `replacePixels(was.id, ...)` calls `doc.setPixels`, which throws `Mannequin pose is locked` before `remember(doc, layer.id, entry)` runs. The edit reports an error, yet `Mannequin` now shows the walking figure while `Mannequin pose` still holds the standing skeleton and `glb` plugin data still records `pose: "standing"`.
findings.evidence: `plugins/glb/main.js:168`: `if (existing && existing.locked) throw new Error(\`${existing.name} is locked\`);` (`existing` comes from `doc.layer()` -> `layerSummary` at `renderer/commands_util.js:67`, where `locked: !!l.locked` excludes group locks). `plugins/glb/main.js:170-173`: `const gone = CONTROLS.map((c, i) => (!r[c.key] && prevCtl[i] ? prevCtl[i].id : null)).filter(Boolean); const lockedCtl = gone.map((id) => doc.rawLayer(id)).find((l) => l && ed.isLocked(l)); if (lockedCtl) throw new Error(...);` checks `gone` only. `plugins/glb/main.js:190` pushes the `layers` undo step, and lines 202-205 mutate the object layer (`replacePixels(layerId, ...)`, `placeAt(layerId, ...)`, `doc.run("set_layer", ...)`). Then lines 213-216 run `const was = prevCtl[i] && doc.layers().find((l) => l.id === prevCtl[i].id); if (was) { replacePixels(was.id, imageDataOf(frame)); ... }`, which calls `doc.setPixels` (`renderer/plugins.js:143`: `if (l.locked) throw new Error(\`${l.name} is locked\`);`), throwing before `remember(doc, layer.id, entry)` at `plugins/glb/main.js:229`.
findings.fix: Before pushing undo or mutating any layer in `plugins/glb/main.js:168-173`, check `ed.isLocked(doc.rawLayer(layerId))` for `existing` and check `ed.isLocked(doc.rawLayer(prevCtl[i].id))` for every present `prevCtl[i]` (both removed and kept/updated control layers); also update `DocHandle.setPixels` (`renderer/plugins.js:143`) to check `this.editor.isLocked(l)`.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc in plugins/glb/main.js, renderer/plugins.js, and renderer/commands_util.js. Every edit entry point — the 3D object panel's Edit button (plugins/glb/main.js:300 -> placeInteractive at 255-278), the Plugins menu's Edit 3D object action (312 -> placeInteractive), and the glb.edit command (370-386) — calls place(doc, { ..., layerId }) without pre-checking layer locks.

Inside place() (plugins/glb/main.js:141-233), lines 168-173 check locks before pushing undo or mutating layers, but with two gaps:
1. Line 170 computes `gone = CONTROLS.map((c, i) => (!r[c.key] && prevCtl[i] ? prevCtl[i].id : null)).filter(Boolean)` and line 172 checks `ed.isLocked(l)` only over `gone` (control layers being switched off and deleted, which is the only case tools/glb_test.py:374-379 tests). Kept control layers (`r[c.key]` truthy and `prevCtl[i]` present) are not checked.
2. Line 168 checks `if (existing && existing.locked)` where `existing` comes from `doc.layers()` (renderer/plugins.js:65 -> layerSummary at renderer/commands_util.js:64-77), which sets `locked: !!l.locked` (line 67) and puts group locks on `locked_by_group` (line 76). Likewise, Document.prototype.setPixels (renderer/plugins.js:139-155) checks `if (l.locked)` at line 143 rather than `this.editor.isLocked(l)` (inpaint_ed_composite.js:160-166). Consequently, an object and its kept control layers inside a locked group (`g.locked = true`, `l.locked = false`) are overwritten without refusal, whereas unticking a control layer in that same locked group is refused at line 172.

When a kept control layer (`Mannequin depth` or `Mannequin pose`) has `locked: true` while `existing` is unlocked, place() passes lines 168-173, deletes any `gone` layer and/or pushes the `layers` undo step at lines 176-190, and overwrites the main 3D layer's pixels and geometry at lines 202-205 (`replacePixels(layerId, ...)`, `placeAt(layerId, ...)`, `doc.run("set_layer", ...)`). If `depth` is unlocked and `pose` is locked, the `CONTROLS.forEach` loop (lines 210-225) also overwrites `Mannequin depth` on `i = 0`. When the loop reaches the locked control layer, line 215 calls `replacePixels(was.id, imageDataOf(frame))` -> `doc.setPixels` (plugins/glb/main.js:194-195 -> renderer/plugins.js:143), which synchronously throws `${l.name} is locked` before `remember(doc, layer.id, entry)` at line 229 runs. Although the caller reports the lock error, the visible 3D layer (and any earlier control layer) now holds the new pose/render on the canvas while the locked control layer and stored `glb` plugin data (`entry.params`, `depthId`, `poseId`) retain the old pose.

Checked known-issue lists (scratch/known_index.md, docs/BUGS.md, PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, and all three verified.json files). `assistant-glb/glb-place-no-undo` (2026-11-12) was the missing single-step undo in `place()`, and lines 160-196 were newly written after 2026-11-12 to fix that finding and add item 67's mannequin `pose` control layer; `shell/F6` (2026-11-07) concerned `set_layer` geometry, `set_text` angle, and assistant policy, not `glb` or `Document.setPixels`. Thus this is a genuine new bug in the post-2026-11-12 code. Severity is `should`: it deterministically tears layer pixels and plugin state apart in a plausible workflow (with mismatched visible vs. ControlNet pose if the user subsequently generates, and stale dialog parameters on the next Edit), while remaining recoverable via Ctrl+Z.

findings.claim: The new Florence-2 `describe` command (when `to_prompt` is omitted or false, the default) only reads the picture and mutates nothing, but `describe` is omitted from `READS` in `electron/main/assistant/policy.js`. As a result, Read-only mode in the assistant refuses plain `describe` calls as document mutations, and normal assistant turns that only call `describe` take a full-document `turnSnapshot()` (cloning layer/mask/selection tiles) and display a misleading "Undo this turn" button.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a picture with Florence-2 installed, open the Assistant pane, turn Read-only on, and ask "Describe what is in the selection". The assistant calls `describe({ detailed: true })`; `Assistant.callTool` checks `if (this.readOnly && !policy.READS.has(name))` and refuses with "Read-only is on in the assistant pane: describe changes the document".
2. Turn Read-only off and ask the same question. `Assistant.runCommand` computes `const write = !policy.READS.has("describe")` (`true`), sets `meta.turn = turn.id` (triggering `ed.turnSnapshot()` in `renderer/shell.js:1453-1457`), records `turn.docs.add(doc)`, and finishes the turn offering "Undo this turn" even though nothing in the document was modified.
findings.evidence: electron/main/assistant/policy.js:14-20 defines `READS` without `"describe"`, while line 57 sets `describe: AUTO` and line 487 documents `to_prompt: true puts it in the prompt field` (optional, default false in `renderer/commands_depth.js:147`). electron/main/assistant/index.js checks `policy.READS.has(name)` directly at line 135 (`const write = !policy.READS.has(name);` -> `meta.turn = turn.id`), line 779 (`if (this.readOnly && !policy.READS.has(name))`), line 859 (`if (!policy.READS.has(name) && doc != null) turn.docs.add(doc)`), and line 1040 (emits `lastTurn` whenever `turn.docs.size > 0`).
findings.fix: Add a `isRead(name, args)` helper in `electron/main/assistant/policy.js` returning `READS.has(name) || (name === "describe" && !(args && args.to_prompt))` and use it at the `READS.has` call sites in `electron/main/assistant/index.js` and `policy.js`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc on the write-classification / turn-undo path, with adversarial corrections to the candidate's Scenario 1 and line citations.

In commit 1b18b1ad, `describe` was added to `renderer/commands_depth.js:14-27` (not line 147, which is the end of `depth_edit`) with `to_prompt: P.bool("put the text into the prompt field too", { default: false })` at line 19 and `yes = (v) => v === true || v === "true"` at line 23. `host.describeArea` (`renderer/editor/host_vlm.js:183-206`) only mutates document state when `toPrompt` is true (`if (toPrompt && text) editor.setPromptText(text);` at line 203); with `to_prompt` omitted or false, it only reads the composite/selection box into a 768x768 buffer, runs Florence-2 (`vlmJob` sets `editor.vlmUsed = true` at line 60), and writes the status line (`editor.setStatus` at lines 190, 204).

Commit 1b18b1ad added `describe: AUTO` under `// ---- read the app` at `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:57` (note: `policy.js:487` is `TIMEOUT_DEFAULTS`, not a `to_prompt` comment), but left `describe` out of `READS` (`electron/main/assistant/policy.js:14-20`), and every read-vs-write check tests `policy.READS.has(name)` by command name alone without inspecting `args.to_prompt`: `backendFor`'s `metaFor(command)` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:129-148`, line 135), `runCall` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:779, 801, 859, 895`), and `policy.undoStep` (`electron/main/assistant/policy.js:558`).

Tracing the normal assistant turn path (Scenario 2): when a user asks the assistant to describe the picture or selection (or a non-vision model calls `describe({})` / `describe({ detailed: true })` with `to_prompt` false/omitted), `metaFor` sets `wait: true` and `turn: turn.id` (`index.js:138, 140`). In `renderer/shell.js:1442-1457`, the bridge waits on `waitForUser` and calls `snapshotTurn(meta, args && args.doc)` (`beforeCall` in `renderer/assistant_turns.js:42-55`). First, if an earlier assistant turn actually edited the document, `beforeCall` line 47 (`if (record && record.turn !== meta.turn) { release(record); record = null; }`) releases that previous turn's snapshot, permanently disabling the earlier turn's "Undo this turn" card (`renderer/assistant.js:659-662`) — even for non-Ctrl+Z changes like `set_prompt`, `set_generation`, `set_crop`, and `set_settings` where "Undo this turn" was the only undo. Second, `beforeCall` line 51 takes a fresh `ed.turnSnapshot()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:231-264` — CoW clones on the tile backend rather than eager pixel copies, null on the canvas backend). `runCall` also performs two extra `list_layers` reads (`index.js:801-820, 895-907`), adds `doc` to `turn.docs` (`index.js:859`), sets `this.lastTurn` in `done()` (`index.js:1040`), and `onEvent` `"turn:done"` (`renderer/assistant.js:577` -> `undoCard` at `637-654`) displays a misleading "Undo this turn" button on a turn that changed nothing.

Correction to Scenario 1: there is no user-facing "Read-only" toggle in the Assistant pane (`renderer/assistant.js:121-218`, `renderer/index.html:139-146`), no `Assistant.callTool` or `Assistant.runCommand` method, and no `"Read-only is on in the assistant pane: describe changes the document"` string. `this.readOnly` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:61, 434-436, 449, 779-782`) is an internal gate flag set via `assistant:reset { readOnly: true }` that refuses non-`READS` tools in `runCall` with `"refused by Scumble: not enabled in this run"`.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: `describe` was introduced on 2026-11-16 (`1b18b1ad`) and this defect is not in any known list. Severity remains `should` because any plain `describe` call in the assistant pane both shows a bogus "Undo this turn" card and wipes out the real "Undo this turn" snapshot from a preceding editing turn, though no pixels are silently lost (`askThenUndo` warns if the user edited since, and `restoreTurn` pushes an undo step).

findings.claim: `vlmJob` tracks Florence-2 VRAM residency on a per-tab boolean (`editor.vlmUsed = true` after `describeImage` resolves), even though main runs a single shared `helperProcess` across all open tabs and loads Florence-2's three ONNX sessions into VRAM before the first decoder step. If Florence-2 runs in Tab A (or is cancelled mid-decode after loading its sessions) and the user runs a local ComfyUI Generate in Tab B (or in Tab A after a cancelled describe), `this.vlmUsed` is false on the generating editor and `host.freeHelpers()` is never called.
findings.scenario:
1. Download Florence-2 base (automatic layer naming is enabled) and connect local ComfyUI (`genSettings.mode = "local"`).
2. Have Tab A and Tab B open. In Tab A, paste a layer or add a reference image so `autoNameLayer` runs `vlmJob(tabA, ...)`, loading Florence-2 into the shared helpers process on GPU and setting `tabA.vlmUsed = true` (or start `Describe Selection` in Tab A and cancel it after step 1, leaving even `tabA.vlmUsed === false` because `describeImage` rejects before line 60).
3. Switch to Tab B (`tabB.vlmUsed === false`, `tabB.helperUsed === false`) and click Generate in local mode.
4. `tabB.generate()` checks `this.vlmUsed` (`false`), skips `host.freeHelpers()`, and runs local ComfyUI while the helpers process still holds Florence-2's sessions in GPU VRAM.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/host_vlm.js:58-61: `const res = await this.describeImage(image, { detailed, jobId: run.jobId, timeoutMs }); if (editor) editor.vlmUsed = true; return res;`. electron/main/onnx/index.js:48, 294-301 holds one shared `let helperProcess = null;` retired by `freeHelpers()`. renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1318-1324 checks only `this.helperUsed` and `this.vlmUsed` on `this` (the active tab's `InpaintEditor`) before calling `await host.freeHelpers()`.
findings.fix: Track helper-process residency on `host` (e.g. set `this._helpersLoaded = true` in `host.helperCall` before invoking `window.scumble.helpers.run`, and clear `this._helpersLoaded = false` in `host.freeHelpers()`), and check `host._helpersLoaded` alongside `this.helperUsed` in `InpaintEditor.generate()`.
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `HostVlmPart.vlmJob` (`renderer/editor/host_vlm.js:54-65`) awaits `this.describeImage(image, { detailed, jobId: run.jobId, timeoutMs })` at line 59 and only then sets `if (editor) editor.vlmUsed = true;` at line 60 on that single tab's `InpaintEditor` instance (initialized at `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:217`). Meanwhile, the main process owns a single app-wide `const helperProcess = new HelperProcess()` (`electron/main/onnx/index.js:25`) shared across every open tab, and `Florence2.run` (`electron/main/onnx/florence2.js:129-146`) loads all four quantized ONNX sessions (`vision`, `embed`, `encoder`, `decoder`, ~275 MB of weights in `florence2.json:13-24`, not three as the candidate states) into `Runtime.sessions` (`electron/main/onnx/runtime.js:60-63`) and executes the vision and text encoders on the GPU before the greedy decoder loop yields to `check` (`florence2.js:174-175`). When `InpaintEditor.generate()` runs in local ComfyUI mode (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1325-1327` — 7 lines below the candidate's cited 1318-1324), it checks only `this.helperUsed` and `this.vlmUsed` on `this` (the generating tab) before calling `host.freeHelpers()` (`renderer/editor/host_helpers.js:705-711` -> `onnx/index.js:187-189` `helperProcess.retire({ reason: "free" })`).

Tracing all callers and guards confirms three unguarded paths where Florence-2 remains resident in GPU VRAM during a local ComfyUI generation (until the 5-minute `IDLE_MS` timer in `electron/main/onnx/helpers.js:30, 203-214` expires): (1) Cross-tab or closed-tab workflows: with Florence-2 installed, `autoName` is enabled by default (`onnx/index.js:23`, `host_vlm.js:24-26`), so pasting, cutting out, dropping a reference, or landing a result in Tab A runs `autoNameLayer` -> `vlmJob` (`host_vlm.js:142`) and sets `tabA.vlmUsed = true`; switching to Tab B (or closing Tab A, since `host_state.js:228-257` `removeEditor` calls `cancelRuns` at line 236 without `freeHelpers()`) and clicking Generate in local mode finds `tabB.vlmUsed === false` and skips `host.freeHelpers()`. (2) Cancelled or timed-out describe in the same tab: `HelperProcess.cancel` (`helpers.js:255-264`) only posts `{ type: "cancel", jobId }` so `engine.describe` (`electron/main/onnx/engine.js:253`) rejects with `"cancelled"` between decoder steps without retiring `helperProcess` or releasing `rt.sessions`; `describeImage` rejects at `host_vlm.js:59` before line 60 runs, leaving `editor.vlmUsed === false` even on Tab A while all four sessions sit in VRAM. (3) In-flight auto-naming in the same tab: dropping a reference image triggers `autoNameLayer` (3.6-6.3 s cold on DirectML per `docs/HELPERS.md:507`), and clicking local Generate before `describeImage` resolves reads `this.vlmUsed === false` at `inpaint_canvas.js:1327`, so `helperProcess.retire` is not called to drain and exit the process.

Checking git history (`diff_p1_lanes_bce.patch`): `editor.helperUsed` already used the per-tab pattern prior to `ce91ff3a` (originating in the single-editor ComfyUI node for server-side helper prompts at `inpaint_ed_segment.js:87, 256, 374` and `inpaint_ed_masks.js:71`, and copied onto `editor.helperUsed` by in-app helpers in `host_helpers.js:357, 392, 532, 569, 646` and `host_key.js:332, 344, 355`). However, `vlmUsed` is brand-new in commit `ce91ff3a` ("Florence-2 review fixes: VRAM freed before a local run"), added specifically so Florence-2 captions free `helperProcess` VRAM before a local ComfyUI run without sending `/free` to ComfyUI (which the initial Florence-2 commit's `editor.helperUsed = true` in `describeArea` had done, while `autoNameLayer` had set nothing). Implementing that new fix as a post-await per-tab `editor.vlmUsed` flag leaves the fix incomplete for cross-tab, closed-tab, cancelled, and in-flight runs.

This defect is not in `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, or any of the three `verified.json` review files, and because it is a hole in `ce91ff3a`'s new VRAM-free fix, it is not `known`. Severity is `should`: `autoName` runs automatically by default whenever Florence-2 is downloaded, making multi-tab local ComfyUI generation hit this deterministically and leave four DirectML/CUDA ONNX sessions competing with large local diffusion models (Flux.2, Klein, Qwen) for GPU VRAM for up to 5 minutes (risking DirectML/ComfyUI paging or OOM), with the manual `Free VRAM` button (`freeHelperModels`) as a workaround.

findings.claim: `layerVlmInput` computes its tile mip level from `s = Math.max(S / layer.w, S / layer.h)` (`S = 768`) while stretching the entire layer `[0, 0, px.width, px.height]` into a `768 x 768` canvas. On any wide or tall tiled layer whose short side is near or below 768 px (such as a `15000 x 600` horizon/foreground strip pasted or cut out on a 15k image), `Math.max` selects `level = 0` (full resolution), synchronously allocating full-width `cpuCanvas` and `ImageData` buffers on the window thread — and throwing `checkCanvas`'s 65,535 px side-limit error if the long side exceeds 65,535 px.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a `15000 x 10000` tiled document with Florence-2 auto-naming on, select a `15000 x 600` strip, and press Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V (or run Cutout on a `15000 x 600` layer).
2. `pasteClipboard` calls `layerLanded(layer, "paste")` -> `host.autoNameLayer` -> `host.layerVlmInput(editor, layer)`.
3. `s = Math.max(768 / 15000, 768 / 600) = 1.28`, so `level = editor.tileLevel(Math.min(1, 1.28)) = 0` and `vp.sx = Math.min(1, 1.28) = 1`.
4. `editor.drawPixelsInto` -> `px.regionCanvas([0, 0, 15000, 600], 0, false)` synchronously allocates `cpuCanvas(15104, 768)` (~46 MB) plus `new ImageData(15104, 768)` (~46 MB) on the main thread (doubled if masked) just to downsample into `768 x 768`. On a `70000 x 600` tiled layer, `cpuCanvas` throws `above Chromium's canvas limit of 65,535 px a side`.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/host_vlm.js:97-108: `const s = Math.max(S / layer.w, S / layer.h); const fx = layer.w / px.width; const level = editor.tileLevel(Math.min(1, fx * s)); ... const vp = { x: layer.x, y: layer.y, w: layer.w, h: layer.h, sx: Math.min(1 / fx, s), sy: Math.min(1 / fx, s), sample: true }; editor.drawPixelsInto(x, layer, px, vp);`. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_chrome.js:110-114 computes `this.tileLevel(fx * vp.sx)` (`0`) and calls `px.regionCanvas([0, 0, px.width, px.height], 0, false)`. renderer/editor/inpaint_tiles.js:2342, 2391 allocates `cpuCanvas((ax1 - ax0 + 1) * cell, (ay1 - ay0 + 1) * cell)` (guarded by `checkCanvas` `CANVAS_MAX_SIDE = 65535` at line 507) and `new ImageData(cw, ch)`.
findings.fix: Fit the layer into the `768 x 768` `#808080` square using `const s = Math.min(S / layer.w, S / layer.h)` (letterboxed onto the neutral grey already filled at lines 86-87, which also avoids severe aspect distortion for Florence-2 and guarantees `px.width >> level` is bounded near `S`), and guard `if (!(layer.w > 0 && layer.h > 0))`.
findings.why:
At `renderer/editor/host_vlm.js:96-99`, the comment explicitly states `// the layer's box onto the square; the levels at the scale of its longer side`, but line 97 writes `const s = Math.max(S / layer.w, S / layer.h)` (`S = VLM_SIDE = 768` at line 11), which is the scale of the *shorter* side rather than the longer side (`S / Math.max(layer.w, layer.h) = Math.min(S / layer.w, S / layer.h)`). Line 99 then computes `const level = editor.tileLevel(Math.min(1, fx * s))` (`fx = layer.w / px.width`) and line 107 sets `vp.sx = vp.sy = Math.min(1 / fx, s)` before calling `editor.drawPixelsInto(x, layer, px, vp)` (line 108) and, when masked, `editor.drawPixelsInto(x, layer, mask, vp)` (line 111).

Tracing the full call path confirms there are no guards preventing full-resolution main-thread materialisation or the 65,535 px side-limit throw. `editor.layerLanded` (`renderer/editor/host_state.js:307`) invokes `host.autoNameLayer` (`host_vlm.js:128-158`, enabled by default whenever Florence-2 is downloaded via `autoNameOn()` at lines 24-26) on new results (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:678`), dropped/added layers and references (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:110`), cutouts (`inpaint_ed_masks.js:135`), and pastes (`inpaint_ed_select.js:1362`). Inside `layerVlmInput`, `drawPixelsInto` (`inpaint_ed_strokes.js:731-735`) delegates on tiles to `drawTilesInto` (`inpaint_ed_chrome.js:108-122`), which computes `this.tileLevel(fx * vp.sx)` (`inpaint_ed_chrome.js:97-99`, `Math.floor(-Math.log2(scale))`) and calls `px.regionCanvas([0, 0, px.width, px.height], level, false)` (`inpaint_ed_chrome.js:114`). Because `Math.floor(-Math.log2(scale)) === 0` whenever `scale > 0.5`, *any* unscaled (or aspect-preserving) tiled layer whose shorter pixel side is below `1536` px (`768 / shortSide > 0.5`) gets `level = 0` (`primeRegion` at `inpaint_tiles.js:920-921` becomes a no-op). On a `15000 x 10000` tiled document, pasting, generating (e.g. an item-63 outpaint border), dropping, or cutting out a `15000 x 600`..`1500` strip synchronously allocates `cpuCanvas(15104, 768..1536)` (46–93 MB, retained in `px._regions` under `SAMPLE_REGION` at `inpaint_tiles.js:2333-2347`) plus `new ImageData(cw, ch)` (another 46–93 MB at `inpaint_tiles.js:2391`) on the window thread — doubled if the layer has a mask. Furthermore, on any valid tiled panorama layer of width `65,281..65,535` px (permitted by `checkBaseSize`'s `HUGE_MAX_SIDE = 65535` at `inpaint_ed_open.js:88`, or wider TIFF layers added via `addImageLayers` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:70-75` which skips `checkBaseSize`), `lastX = (w - 1) >> 8 = 255`, so `(ax1 - ax0 + 1) * 256 = 65,536 > CANVAS_MAX_SIDE` and `cpuCanvas` (`inpaint_tiles.js:2342` -> `checkCanvas` at line 507) throws `above Chromium's canvas limit of 65,535 px a side`.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the three `verified.json` files: `host_vlm.js` was newly introduced on 2026-11-16 for item 62 (Florence-2) and this defect is not recorded in any known list. Severity is `should`: `autoNameLayer` catches the error (`host_vlm.js:150-155`) so no user pixels or money are lost (ruling out `must`), but users with Florence-2 installed hit synchronous multi-hundred-MB main-thread allocations/retentions on normal wide/tall layers (any short side < 1536 px on a 15k document) and outright auto-naming failure at 65,281..65,535 px.

findings.claim: fal.js, replicate.js, and wavespeed.js send the user's Authorization API key header directly to server-returned polling and result URLs (job.status_url, job.response_url, pred.urls.get, data.urls.get) with no https: or provider-hostname check and no redirect guard. By contrast, askStop in the very same files validates cancel URLs via allowedStopUrl, bfl.js validates polling_url via pollUrlOf, and comfysdk.js guards job links to cloud.comfy.org. Any plain-http link (such as the http:// link regression hit on Comfy Cloud) or off-origin/loopback link in a queue response leaks the live API key in cleartext or to an untrusted host, and wavespeed.js upload() likewise PUTs user image bytes with server-chosen method and headers to an unvalidated up.url.
findings.scenario: A user runs Generate, Generate new, Upscale, Relight, or Split into layers on fal.ai, Replicate, or WaveSpeedAI. A gateway/proxy bug, compromised upstream route, or MITM returns status_url / response_url / urls.get with an http:// scheme or another hostname (for example http://queue.fal.run/... or https://attacker.example/poll). pollJob immediately sends GET requests carrying Authorization: Key <fal-key> or Authorization: Bearer <token> to that URL without checking protocol or hostname.
findings.evidence: electron/main/providers/fal.js:254 `const statusUrl = job.status_url, resultUrl = job.response_url, cancelUrl = job.cancel_url;` -> :260-270 `pollJob(ctx, { ..., url: statusUrl, resultUrl, headers: { Authorization: headers.Authorization } })` (whereas :290,293 guard `cancelUrl` via `askStop(cancelUrl, { host: "queue.fal.run", ... })` -> `util.js:108-117` `allowedStopUrl`). electron/main/providers/replicate.js:221-222 `url: (p) => (p.urls && p.urls.get ? p.urls.get : ...), headers: { Authorization: headers.Authorization }` (whereas :250,253 guard `cancelUrl` against `"api.replicate.com"`). electron/main/providers/wavespeed.js:377,386-387 `const resultUrl = (data.urls && data.urls.get) || ...; ... url: resultUrl, headers: { Authorization: headers.Authorization }`, and :88-89 `ctx.fetch(up.url, { method: up.method || "PUT", headers: up.headers || { "Content-Type": mime }, body: bytes })` with no `https:` or non-loopback check (compare `comfypartner.js:108-110` and `bfl.js:46-52`). `util.js:306,340` calls `callFetch(ctx, pollUrl, { headers, signal })` and `callFetch(ctx, resUrl, { headers })` with no origin check and default `redirect: "follow"`.
findings.fix: Validate status_url / response_url in fal.js (https: on queue.fal.run or *.fal.run / *.fal.ai, else fall back or refuse), pred.urls.get in replicate.js (https: on api.replicate.com, else `${BASE}/predictions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`), and data.urls.get in wavespeed.js (https: on api.wavespeed.ai, else `${BASE}predictions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/result`), and pass `redirect: "error"` when sending Authorization in pollJob. In wavespeed.js upload(), require `up.url` to be `https:` on a non-loopback host and restrict method to PUT.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc, with one partial refutation on the redirect sub-claim and severity calibrated down from `must` to `should`.

**Call path and code verification.** Every quoted line and line number matches f45a86cc:
1. `electron/main/providers/fal.js:249-285` (`queued`, called from `edit` at `:364`, `upscale` at `:379`, and `relight` at `:389`): submits to `https://queue.fal.run/<model>`, reads `const statusUrl = job.status_url, resultUrl = job.response_url, cancelUrl = job.cancel_url;` (`:254`), checks only truthiness (`:255`), and passes `url: statusUrl` (`:268`), `resultUrl` (`:269`), and `headers: { Authorization: headers.Authorization }` (`:270`, `"Key " + ctx.key`) straight into `pollJob`. By contrast, `:290` and `:293` pass `cancelUrl` from the exact same `job` object through `askStop(cancelUrl, { host: "queue.fal.run", method: "PUT", auth: headers.Authorization })`, which enforces `allowedStopUrl` (`electron/main/providers/util.js:108-117`: `u.protocol === "https:" && u.hostname === host && !u.username && !u.password`) and `redirect: "error"` (`:132`).
2. `electron/main/providers/replicate.js:214-228` (`edit`, also serving `generate` at `:191`): passes `url: (p) => (p.urls && p.urls.get ? p.urls.get : \`${BASE}/predictions/${p.id}\`)` (`:221`) with `headers: { Authorization: headers.Authorization }` (`:222`, `"Bearer " + ctx.key`), where `parse` (`:224-228`) merges every poll response `{ ...prev, ...j }` back into state, while `:250` and `:253` guard `cancelUrl` against `host: "api.replicate.com"`.
3. `electron/main/providers/wavespeed.js:369-391` (`submitAndWait`, called from `edit` at `:309` and `layers` at `:348`): sets `const resultUrl = (data.urls && data.urls.get) || \`${BASE}predictions/${data.id}/result\`;` (`:377`) and passes `url: resultUrl` (`:386`) with `headers: { Authorization: headers.Authorization }` (`:387`) to `pollJob`. Separately, `wavespeed.js:81-91` (`upload`) sends user image `bytes` via `ctx.fetch(up.url, { method: up.method || "PUT", headers: up.headers || { "Content-Type": mime }, body: bytes })` (`:89`) with no `https:` check, no loopback check, and server-chosen `method` and `headers` (unlike `comfypartner.js:108-110`, which requires `^https:\/\/` and hardcodes `method: "PUT"`).
4. `electron/main/providers/util.js:306` and `:340` (`pollJob`) call `callFetch(ctx, pollUrl, { headers, signal })` and `callFetch(ctx, resUrl, { headers })`, forwarding to `ctx.fetch` (`providers/index.js:601-604`) -> `globalThis.fetch` (`electron/main/curlfetch.js:342-344`) with no scheme or hostname check.

**Guards checked (and partial refutation on 3xx redirects).** On a cross-origin 3xx redirect from a valid `https://` poll URL, both `curlFetch` (`curlfetch.js:290`, `if (next.origin !== u.origin) headers = headers.filter(([k]) => !KEY_HEADERS.has(k.toLowerCase()))`, where `KEY_HEADERS` at `:39` contains `"authorization"`) and Node's built-in undici `fetch` DO strip `Authorization`, so a 3xx redirect alone does not leak the Bearer/Key header. However, nothing guards **hop 0** when `status_url`, `response_url`, or `urls.get` itself has an `http://` scheme or another host: `curlfetch.js:277` explicitly permits `http:`, and `curlfetch.js:324` (`isLoopback`) routes loopback URLs directly to Node's `fetch`. Compare `bfl.js:46-52` (`pollUrlOf`: "The key goes with every poll, so never to another host", requiring `https:` on `bfl.ai` / `*.bfl.ai`) and `comfysdk.js:106-117` (restricting Comfy Cloud job links to `https://cloud.comfy.org`).

**Not in known lists.** Checked `docs/BUGS.md` (lines 1-698), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` (all 30 entries; `S2` covers `comfy.js` stored ComfyUI secrets and custom-header redirects, `S8` covers `provision.sh` wget `HF_TOKEN`), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json` (all 73 entries; `providers/PRV-1` introduced `pollJob` for retry resilience and `providers/PRV-3` introduced `askStop`/`allowedStopUrl` for `cancel_url` only, creating this exact asymmetry between guarded cancel URLs and unguarded poll/result URLs), and `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` (all 56 entries; `providers/polljob-deadline-before-reread` and `main-net/comfy-custom-auth-header-cross-origin` are distinct). The 2026-11-16 Comfy Cloud fix (`comfysdk.js:102-123`, `CHANGELOG.md:36-39`) fixed Comfy Cloud v2 job links only.

**Severity calibration (`should`, not `must`).** All three adapters send their initial submit POST to hardcoded `https://` origins (`https://queue.fal.run/`, `https://api.replicate.com/v1`, `https://api.wavespeed.ai/api/v3/`) with no user-configurable `baseUrl` override, so neither a crafted local file/recipe nor an unauthenticated network attacker can inject a rogue `status_url` / `urls.get` while TLS holds; the provider's HTTPS endpoint already received the API key on submit. Under the project's calibration (compare `providers/PRV-2` and `providers/polljob-deadline-before-reread` at `should`), `must` is overstated. Conversely, `nice` is too low because a provider reverse-proxy returning `http://` job links instead of `https://` is a proven real-world failure mode that hit Comfy Cloud in production on 2026-11-16 (`comfysdk.js:102-105`). If fal.ai, Replicate, or WaveSpeedAI emits an `http://` poll/result URL during a gateway misconfiguration, Scumble (1) transmits the live `Authorization` API key in cleartext HTTP over port 80 on hop 0, and (2) when that `http://` URL 301-redirects to `https://`, `curlFetch`/undici strips `Authorization` across the scheme change, causing an immediate 401 failure (`util.js:318`) that abandons a submitted, billed job with no `cloudjobs` recovery and no user workaround.

findings.claim: Comfy Cloud's OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 partner node caps its required INT `seed` input at 2147483647 (2^31 - 1), while Scumble generates unsigned 32-bit random seeds up to 4294967295 (0xffffffff). Unlike ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3 and Krea3ImageNode in the same file, SHAPES.OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2 passes `v.seed` (`req.seed >>> 0`) without `% NODE_SEEDS`. Roughly half of all random seeds on all five shipped Comfy Cloud GPT Image variants fail workflow validation after uploading the crop and mask.
findings.scenario: Select a region on a canvas, pick any of GPT Image 2, GPT Image 2.5 Flare/Sunburst, or GPT Image 2.6 Flare/Sunburst on Comfy Cloud with default random seed enabled (`seedRandom: true`), and click Generate. Whenever `randomSeed()` picks a value in `2147483648..4294967295` (~50% of runs), Scumble uploads the crop and mask assets to Comfy Cloud and submits `OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2` with `inputs.seed > 2147483647`, which Comfy Cloud refuses with `422 invalid_workflow`.
findings.evidence: tools/refs/comfy_cloud/nodes/OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2.json:13: `"seed": { "type": "INT", "required": true, "min": 0, "max": 2147483647 }`. renderer/editor/inpaint_backends.js:96: `const randomSeed = () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 0xffffffff);` (sent via `host_provider.js` / `host_generate.js:94`). electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:79-80: `const NODE_SEEDS = 2147483648;` (applied at `:122,130` for `ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3` and `:147` for `Krea3ImageNode`), `:671`: `seed: req.seed != null && !req.params.random_seed ? (req.seed >>> 0) : Math.floor(Math.random() * 2147483647)`, and `:90-91`: `OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2(g, v) { g.set("prompt", v.prompt); g.set("model", v.model); g.set("n", 1); g.set("seed", v.seed);` without `% NODE_SEEDS`. Shipped variants: `recipes/gpt_image_2.json:425`, `recipes/gpt_image_2_5_flare.json:492`, `recipes/gpt_image_2_5_sunburst.json:492`, `recipes/gpt_image_2_6_flare.json:418`, `recipes/gpt_image_2_6_sunburst.json:499`. (`tools/gpt26_test.js:86` only tested `seed: 42`.)
findings.fix: In `electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:91`, change `g.set("seed", v.seed)` to `g.set("seed", v.seed % NODE_SEEDS)` (and check the remaining partner nodes in `SHAPES` for int32 seed caps), plus add a `seed: 3e9` check in `tools/gpt26_test.js` mirroring `tools/seedream55_test.js:184-186`.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, Comfy Cloud's saved partner-node specification in tools/refs/comfy_cloud/nodes/OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2.json:13 defines `seed` as `{ "type": "INT", "required": true, "min": 0, "max": 2147483647 }` (signed 32-bit positive ceiling `2^31 - 1`), matching `ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3` (tools/refs/comfy_cloud/nodes/ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3.json:13) and `Krea3ImageNode` (tools/refs/comfy_cloud/nodes/Krea3ImageNode.json:13). In electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:79-81, `const NODE_SEEDS = 2147483648` is defined specifically to reduce 32-bit unsigned seeds modulo `2^31` for partner nodes with this cap, and is applied in `SHAPES.ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3` (:122, :130) and `SHAPES.Krea3ImageNode` (:147). However, `SHAPES.OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2` at electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:90-91 writes `g.set("prompt", v.prompt); g.set("model", v.model); g.set("n", 1); g.set("seed", v.seed);` without `% NODE_SEEDS`.

Tracing the full call path confirms no guard or clamp prevents seeds above 2147483647 from reaching Comfy Cloud. In the renderer, `GEN_DEFAULTS` sets `seedRandom: true` (renderer/editor/inpaint_backends.js:91) and `randomSeed` generates `Math.floor(Math.random() * 0xffffffff)` up to `4294967295` (renderer/editor/inpaint_backends.js:96), rolled both in the `InpaintEditor` constructor (renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:166) and on every `generate()` call when `seedRandom` is enabled (renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1318; fixed seeds via `set_generation` at renderer/commands_gen.js:36 are likewise unclamped above 0). `runProvider` reads `const seed = editor.genSettings.seed` (renderer/editor/host_provider.js:323, :369) and `providerParams` (renderer/editor/host_presets.js:710-720) copies only the recipe's Settings rows and `fixed` map—none of the five shipped Comfy Cloud `OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2` variants (recipes/gpt_image_2.json:425, recipes/gpt_image_2_5_flare.json:492, recipes/gpt_image_2_5_sunburst.json:492, recipes/gpt_image_2_6_flare.json:418, recipes/gpt_image_2_6_sunburst.json:499) defines `random_seed` or a `seed` override. Over IPC, electron/main/providers/index.js:260-314 forwards `req.seed` untouched into `comfycloud.edit` -> `runV2` (or legacy `run`). Inside `buildGraph` (electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:671), `vals.seed` evaluates `req.seed != null && !req.params.random_seed ? (req.seed >>> 0) : Math.floor(Math.random() * 2147483647)`: because `req.seed` is always non-null and `req.params.random_seed` is undefined, the `< 2147483647` fallback never runs and `(req.seed >>> 0)` preserves values in `2147483648..4294967295` (~50% of random rolls). `AFTER_PARAMS.OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2` (:294-298) only normalizes `model.complexity`. Both `runV2` (:1026, :1036-1058) and legacy `run` (:679-686, :847-855) upload the crop, references, and mask before submitting the workflow, which Comfy Cloud then rejects at prompt validation (`422 invalid_workflow`). The unit test in tools/gpt26_test.js:86, :532 missed this only because `editReq` hardcoded `seed: 42`.

Checked against known_index.md, docs/BUGS.md, docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, CHANGELOG.md, and all three `verified.json` files: this defect is not listed or fixed at f45a86cc (earlier seed-cap fixes covered `ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3` in tools/seedream55_test.js:183-186, `Krea3ImageNode` in comfycloud.js:147, and OpenRouter Seedream in CHANGELOG.md:40-42, leaving `OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2` unfixed). Severity is `should`: Comfy Cloud refuses the workflow before running or billing the partner node so no credits or pixels are lost (`must` does not apply), but ~50% of default Generate runs across all five GPT Image recipes on Comfy Cloud fail after uploading assets until the user retries or sets a manual seed `<= 2147483647`.

findings.claim: For Seedream 5.0 Lite and 5.0 Pro on Comfy Cloud, ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3 uses `fit(v.width, v.height, 1024, pro ? 2496 : 4992, 2)` and `seedream_5_lite.json` sets `limits.max: 4992`, exceeding both the node catalog's 4514 side ceiling and Seedream 5.0's total-pixel limits. At the default Highres fix (Maximum), every `seedream_5_lite` run sends a 4992 px long side (> 4514), and square crops send 4992x4992 (24.9 MP > Lite's 16.78 MP max) on Lite and 2496x2496 (6.23 MP > Pro's 4.62 MP max) on Pro, while small crops with Highres fix Off send 1024x1024 (1.05 MP < Lite's 3.69 MP floor).
findings.scenario: Open a 6000x6000 image, select a 1000x1000 area, choose Seedream 5.0 Lite on Comfy Cloud with default Highres fix = Maximum, and click Generate. `planCrop` emits a 4992x4992 crop and `ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3` submits `model.width: 4992, model.height: 4992` (24,920,064 px), exceeding both Comfy Cloud's `4514` widget bound on `ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3` and Seedream 5.0 Lite's `16,777,216` pixel maximum. With Highres fix = Off on a 1024x1024 crop, it sends `1024x1024` (1,048,576 px), under Lite's `3,686,400` pixel minimum.
findings.evidence: tools/refs/comfy_cloud/nodes/ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3.json:2: `The catalog merges the bounds of every model's width and height (1024 to 4514); the 5.5 bounds are comfy_api_nodes/nodes_bytedance.py of Comfy-Org/ComfyUI#17631 (merged 2026-11-10): min_size 240, max 8594, step 2, and execute()'s checks 921,600 to 4,624,220 pixels, aspect 1:16 to 16:1.` docs/RECIPES.md:2640-2641 (and `tools/refs/comfyrouter/byteplus_seedream-5-0-260128.json:1`, `byteplus_seedream-5-0-pro-260628.json:1`): 5.0 pro total pixels `[921,600 (or 1,048,576), 4,624,220 (or 4,194,304)]`, 5.0 lite `[3,686,400, 16,777,216]`. Yet `electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:131` (unlike `:85,123` which uses `fitPixels(v.width, v.height, SEEDREAM55_SIZE)` for 5.5) runs `const [w, h] = fit(v.width, v.height, 1024, pro ? 2496 : 4992, 2);`, and `recipes/seedream_5_lite.json:232-236` sets `"limits": { "min": 1024, "max": 4992, "step": 2 }` with no `pixels` or `minPixels` (and `recipes/seedream_5_pro.json:207-211` sets `"max": 2496` with no `pixels`).
findings.fix: Use `fitPixels` in `comfycloud.js:131` for 5.0 pro (`{ step: 2, min: 1024, max: 2496, minPixels: 1048576, maxPixels: 4194304, maxRatio: 16 }` or `4624220` matching `nodes_bytedance.py`) and 5.0 lite (`{ step: 2, min: 1024, max: 4514, minPixels: 3686400, maxPixels: 16777216, maxRatio: 16 }`), and add matching `max`, `pixels`, and `minPixels` to the `comfycloud` `limits` in `recipes/seedream_5_lite.json` and `recipes/seedream_5_pro.json`.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `SHAPES.ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3` in `electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:117-135` applies `fitPixels(v.width, v.height, SEEDREAM55_SIZE)` (`:84-85, 118-128`) only when `SEEDREAM55.test(v.model)` matches `"seedream 5.5"`, while falling through at `:129-134` for `"seedream 5.0 lite"` and `"seedream 5.0 pro"` to `const [w, h] = fit(v.width, v.height, 1024, pro ? 2496 : 4992, 2);` (`:131`). `fit` (`comfycloud.js:57-62`) only clamps individual side lengths to `[lo, hi]` on multiples of `2` and enforces no `minPixels`, `maxPixels`, or `maxRatio`. Upstream in the crop planner, `recipes/seedream_5_lite.json:224-237` sets `comfycloud.limits` to `{ "min": 1024, "max": 4992, "step": 2 }` and `recipes/seedream_5_pro.json:199-212` sets `{ "min": 1024, "max": 2496, "step": 2 }`, both omitting `pixels`, `minPixels`, and `ratio` (normalized to `0` by `editLimits` in `electron/main/recipes_store.js:149-167`). Consequently, when `runProvider` (`renderer/editor/host_provider.js:326, 370`) calls `planCrop` (`renderer/editor/stitch.js:395, 458-479`) with `host.cropLimits()` (`renderer/editor/host_state.js:27, 146-150`, default `apiSize = "max"`), neither the pixel ceiling (`stitch.js:462`) nor the pixel floor (`stitch.js:469`) nor aspect clamping (`stitch.js:442`) runs.

Tracing into ComfyUI's upstream `ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3` (`comfy_api_nodes/nodes_bytedance.py:778-1049`, matching `docs/RECIPES.md:2640-2641`), `execute()` explicitly rejects total pixel counts outside `[3,686,400, 16,777,216]` for `"seedream 5.0 lite"` (`seedream-5-0-260128`) and outside `[921,600, 4,624,220]` for `"seedream 5.0 pro"` (`seedream-5-0-pro-260628`), plus input image aspect ratios outside `1:16..16:1`. With the default `Highres fix = Maximum`, `emitTarget` (`stitch.js:369`) targets `limits.max`: on Seedream 5.0 Lite, any selection with aspect ratio closer to square than ~1.485:1 (1:1 -> `4992x4992` = 24,920,064 px, 5:4 -> `4992x3994` = 19.94 MP, 4:3 -> `4992x3744` = 18.69 MP) uploads all crop/reference PNGs (`comfycloud.js:1036-1048`) and then fails in `ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3.execute()` (`Maximum image resolution for the selected model is 16.78MP`); on Seedream 5.0 Pro, any selection closer to square than ~1.347:1 (1:1 -> `2496x2496` = 6,230,016 px, 5:4 -> `2496x1996` = 4.98 MP) likewise fails (`Maximum image resolution for the selected model is 4.62MP`). Conversely, with `Highres fix = Off` (`apiSize = "crop"`) on Seedream 5.0 Lite, any crop under 3,686,400 px (e.g. `1024x1024` = 1,048,576 px or `1920x1080` = 2,073,600 px) passes `fit` unchanged and fails (`Minimum image resolution for the selected model is 3.68MP`). (One minor detail to clarify for the fix: in `nodes_bytedance.py:653-654, 812-852`, the `4514` widget cap noted in `tools/refs/comfy_cloud/nodes/ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3.json:2` comes from `seedream 5.0 pro`/`flash`'s `max_width=4514, max_height=4514`, whereas `seedream 5.0 lite`'s `DynamicCombo.Option` inherits `max_width=6240, max_height=4992`; the real blocker on both models is the missing `fitPixels` / recipe `pixels` + `minPixels` + `ratio` bounds.)

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including `Size limits: gaps found reading the code` at `:162-190`), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: none record Seedream 5.0 Lite/Pro pixel or dimension bounds on Comfy Cloud. Severity is `should`: users hit immediate Comfy Cloud execution failures in completely standard default workflows (any square/4:3/5:4 edit at default `Highres fix = Maximum` on Lite or Pro, and any small crop with `Highres fix = Off` on Lite), with a manual workaround (`Highres fix = Target size`, e.g. `2048 px`), and `ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV3.execute()` raises `ValueError` before invoking `BYTEPLUS_IMAGE_ENDPOINT` so there is no silent pixel loss or partner API double-charge.

findings.claim: Oxen's published request schema for `qwen-image-3` sets both `enable_prompt_expansion` and `enable_thinking` to `default: true`, and states that `enable_thinking` 'Requires prompt expansion.' Scumble's `qwen_image_edit` Oxen variant sends `fixed: { enable_prompt_expansion: false, watermark: false }` while omitting `enable_thinking` from `accepts` and `fixed`, so every Oxen `qwen-image-3` edit and Generate-new call leaves `enable_thinking` at `true` with `enable_prompt_expansion: false`.
findings.scenario: Select Qwen Image Edit with provider Oxen.ai and run either Generate on a selection or Generate new. `oxen.js` posts `{ model: "qwen-image-3", ..., enable_prompt_expansion: false, watermark: false }` without `enable_thinking: false`, triggering the invalid combination `enable_thinking: true` + `enable_prompt_expansion: false` documented by Oxen's schema.
findings.evidence: tools/refs/oxen/qwen-image-3.json:27-40: `"enable_prompt_expansion": { "default": true, ... }, "enable_thinking": { "default": true, "description": "Reason about the prompt before rendering. Improves quality on complex layouts and long prompts at the cost of generation time. Requires prompt expansion.", "title": "Thinking", "type": "boolean" }`. recipes/qwen_image_edit.json:206-213: `"accepts": ["aspect_ratio", "resolution", "negative_prompt", "seed", "enable_prompt_expansion", "watermark"]`, and `:228-231`: `"fixed": { "enable_prompt_expansion: false, "watermark": false }`. electron/main/providers/oxen.js:387-391 only copies keys listed in `accepts`.
findings.fix: Add `"enable_thinking"` to `providers.oxen.options.accepts` and `"enable_thinking": false` to `providers.oxen.fixed` in `recipes/qwen_image_edit.json` (and update the golden body in `tools/oxen_test.js:236-239`).
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, Oxen's saved schema `tools/refs/oxen/qwen-image-3.json:27-40` defines both `enable_prompt_expansion` (`default: true`, `:28`) and `enable_thinking` (`default: true`, `:35`, with `:36` `"description": "Reason about the prompt before rendering. Improves quality on complex layouts and long prompts at the cost of generation time. Requires prompt expansion."`), and defines no `x-lock` coupling between them (unlike `tools/refs/oxen/bytedance-seedream-5-5.json:101-106`, where Oxen explicitly declares `x-lock` when one field auto-locks another). Meanwhile `recipes/qwen_image_edit.json:202-231` configures `providers.oxen` (`model: "qwen-image-3"`) with `options.accepts: ["aspect_ratio", "resolution", "negative_prompt", "seed", "enable_prompt_expansion", "watermark"]` (`:206-213`) and `fixed: { "enable_prompt_expansion": false, "watermark": false }` (`:228-231`), omitting `enable_thinking` from both.

Tracing both call paths confirms there is no guard or normalization that supplies `enable_thinking: false` or allows a caller override. On an edit (`Generate` or MCP `generate`), `HostPresetsPart.providerParams` (`renderer/editor/host_presets.js:710-720`, called from `renderer/editor/host_provider.js:321`) merges the single `resolution` setting row with `r.fixed`, and `oxen.js` `run` (`electron/main/providers/oxen.js:550-571`) builds the payload via `bodyFor` (`:371-436`). `bodyFor` constructs `accepts = new Set(o.accepts)` (`:376`) and copies only `req.params` entries satisfying `accepts.has(k)` (`:387-391`), so `enable_prompt_expansion: false` is sent while `enable_thinking` is absent (and even a manual param override would be stripped because `"enable_thinking"` is not in `accepts`). On `Generate new` (or MCP `generate_new`), `textVariant` (`electron/main/recipes_store.js:238-254`) inherits `fixed: t.fixed || v.fixed` (`:247`) from `recipes/qwen_image_edit.json:255-261`, `HostGeneratePart.runGenerate` (`renderer/editor/host_generate.js:58,70`) passes `genParams` and `textOptions(r, withRefs)` (`renderer/editor/host_util.js:53-58`, returning `r.options`), and `oxen.generate` (`oxen.js:662`) posts the same `enable_prompt_expansion: false` body without `enable_thinking` to `/api/ai/images/generate` (0 refs) or `/api/ai/images/edit` (with refs). The schema validators in `tools/oxen_test.js:62-86` and `tools/oxen_mock.py:189-220` check types, enums, bounds, and unknown properties without applying defaults or prose dependencies, and `tools/oxen_test.js:236-239` pins the golden `qwen-image-3` bodies without `enable_thinking`.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/RECIPES.md:3664-3835`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`): no entry records this defect (`docs/RECIPES.md:3814-3824` only notes generally that Oxen has not been run live with a real key, not this `enable_thinking` / `enable_prompt_expansion` contradiction). Severity is `should`: while the Oxen adapter has not been run against the live API, sending `enable_prompt_expansion: false` while leaving `enable_thinking` at its schema default `true` directly violates Oxen's documented `'Requires prompt expansion.'` requirement on 100% of edit and Generate-new calls for `qwen_image_edit` on Oxen.ai (with no in-variant setting workaround, only switching to another provider or recipe), without causing silent pixel/data loss or double-charging (`must`).

findings.claim: FLUX.1 Fill is a mask-inpainting-only model whose BFL `FluxProFillInputs` schema requires `image` and defines no `width` or `height` fields. While `flux1_fill.json` sets `"text": false` on `comfyrouter` (`bfl/flux-pro-1.0-fill`), its `bfl`, `fal`, `replicate`, and `wavespeed` variants omit `"text": false`, so `normalize()` synthesizes broken Generate-new routes for them: BFL posts `{ prompt, width, height, ... }` without `image` to `/v1/flux-pro-1.0-fill`, Replicate and WaveSpeed post without `image`/`mask` to `black-forest-labs/flux-fill-pro` and `wavespeed-ai/flux-fill-dev`, and fal strips `/fill` to `fal-ai/flux-pro/v1`.
findings.scenario: Open the Generate new dialog (or call MCP `generate_new`), pick FLUX.1 Fill [pro] on its default provider Black Forest Labs (or Replicate / WaveSpeedAI), enter a prompt, and click Generate. `bfl.js` sends `POST https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-pro-1.0-fill` with `{ prompt, output_format: "png", seed, width, height, steps, guidance, safety_tolerance, prompt_upsampling }` and no `image` field, which BFL refuses with 422 because `image` is required.
findings.evidence: tools/refs/comfyrouter/bfl_flux-pro-1.0-fill.json:1: `"required":["image"],"title":"FluxProFillInputs"` (properties: `guidance, image, mask, output_format, prompt, prompt_upsampling, safety_tolerance, seed, steps, webhook_secret, webhook_url`; no `width`/`height`). recipes/flux1_fill.json:315 sets `"text": false` on `comfyrouter`, but `:9-65` (`bfl`, `model: "flux-pro-1.0-fill"`), `:66-100` (`fal`, `model: "fal-ai/flux-pro/v1/fill"`), `:101-164` (`replicate`, `model: "black-forest-labs/flux-fill-pro"`), and `:165-207` (`wavespeed`, `model: "wavespeed-ai/flux-fill-dev"`) do not. electron/main/recipes_store.js:226-254 (`textModelOf`, `textVariant`) therefore synthesizes `text` shapes with `model: "flux-pro-1.0-fill"`, `"fal-ai/flux-pro/v1"`, `"black-forest-labs/flux-fill-pro"`, and `"wavespeed-ai/flux-fill-dev"`, and `electron/main/providers/bfl.js:59-68` sends `body.width = req.width; body.height = req.height` with no `image`.
findings.fix: Set `"text": false` on the `bfl`, `fal`, `replicate`, and `wavespeed` variants in `recipes/flux1_fill.json` (matching `comfyrouter` at `:315` and `docs/RECIPES.md:1381`'s rule that inpaint-only recipes carry `text: false`), and update `TAKES_NONE` in `tools/recipes_test.js:373`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc. In `recipes/flux1_fill.json`, the `comfyrouter` variant (`bfl/flux-pro-1.0-fill`, lines 256-317) explicitly sets `"text": false` at line 315 (and `comfycloud` at lines 208-255 gets `text: null` because `comfycloud` is in `TEXT_NAMED` at `electron/main/recipes_store.js:121,241`), whereas the `bfl` (lines 9-65, `model: "flux-pro-1.0-fill"`), `fal` (lines 66-100, `model: "fal-ai/flux-pro/v1/fill"`), `replicate` (lines 101-164, `model: "black-forest-labs/flux-fill-pro"`), and `wavespeed` (lines 165-207, `model: "wavespeed-ai/flux-fill-dev"`) variants omit `"text": false`. Because all four providers are in `TEXT_PROVIDERS` (`electron/main/recipes_store.js:118`), `normalize()` (`recipes_store.js:603`) calls `textVariant()` (`recipes_store.js:238-254`) and `textModelOf()` (`recipes_store.js:226-230`), synthesizing non-null `v.text` shapes with `model: "flux-pro-1.0-fill"` (BFL), `"fal-ai/flux-pro/v1"` (fal, after stripping `/fill`), `"black-forest-labs/flux-fill-pro"` (Replicate), and `"wavespeed-ai/flux-fill-dev"` (WaveSpeed, since `/\/(edit|inpaint|fill)$/` does not match `-fill-dev`).

Tracing the full UI and MCP call paths shows no guard blocks these routes: `genRecipesFor("api")` and `genProviderIds(r)` (`renderer/shell_generate.js:210-219`) expose FLUX.1 Fill [pro] with all four providers in both the Generate new dialog and the New dialog's model presets (`newCanvasChoices`, `shell_generate.js:92-121`). Worse, if the user already has `flux1_fill` active for mask inpainting, opening Generate new auto-selects `shellState.settings.recipe` (`shell_generate.js:243`), defaulting the dialog to `flux1_fill`. Clicking Generate (`renderer/shell.js:684-693`) or calling MCP `generate_new` (`renderer/commands_runs.js:21-69`) invokes `host.runGenerate()` (`renderer/editor/host_generate.js:23-103`) with `kind: "text", image: null, mask: null` -> `providers/index.js:314` `p.generate(req, ctx)`.

Every one of the four synthesized text routes fails at the upstream API: (1) On `bfl`, `electron/main/providers/bfl.js:54-82,110-121` (whose comments at lines 11 and 96 mistakenly assumed `/v1/flux-pro-1.0-fill` generates from a prompt alone) POSTs `{ prompt, output_format: "png", seed, width, height, steps, guidance, safety_tolerance, prompt_upsampling }` with no `image` to `https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-pro-1.0-fill`; both `tools/refs/comfyrouter/bfl_flux-pro-1.0-fill.json:1` and BFL's live OpenAPI spec define `FluxProFillInputs` with `"required": ["image"]` and no `width`/`height` fields (which `comfyrouter.js:503` already notes: "needs a crop and a mask; it cannot make a picture from the prompt alone"), so BFL rejects with HTTP 422. (2) On `fal`, `electron/main/providers/fal.js:82-159,249-252` POSTs to `https://queue.fal.run/fal-ai/flux-pro/v1`, a non-existent endpoint (HTTP 404; fal's FLUX.1 [pro] text endpoints are `fal-ai/flux-pro` and `fal-ai/flux-pro/v1.1`, while `v1` is only the prefix of `v1/fill`). (3) On `replicate`, `electron/main/providers/replicate.js:72-86,191-207` POSTs `{ prompt, seed, aspect_ratio, output_format: "png", ... }` with no `image` to `black-forest-labs/flux-fill-pro`, whose schema requires `image` and `prompt` (HTTP 422). (4) On `wavespeed`, `electron/main/providers/wavespeed.js:158-173,294-309` POSTs `{ prompt, seed, size, num_inference_steps, guidance_scale, output_format: "png" }` without `image` or `mask_image` to `/api/v3/wavespeed-ai/flux-fill-dev`, whose published schema requires `prompt`, `image`, and `mask_image` (and `tools/wavespeed_text_test.js:38-42` missed it because `!/\/edit$/.test(edit)` exempted non-`/edit` ids).

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`), and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: this defect is not known (`BUGS.md:191-196` only covers WaveSpeed `/edit` field comparisons and Reve's 404, and `:400,414` cover fixed 26a2 reference drops on fill edits; `tools/recipes_test.js:373` `TAKES_NONE` and `docs/RECIPES.md:1379` codified the mistaken assumption that these four `flux1_fill` variants had text shapes). Severity is `should`: users hit an immediate 404/422 refusal in a normal workflow (especially when opening Generate new while `flux1_fill` is selected), with no pixel or billing loss and an easy workaround of selecting a text-capable recipe.

findings.claim: When setValue restores a filter layer whose Deep paint pixel file (l.ref on ownPixels filters) or 3D LUT PNG (l.lut.ref) is missing or unreadable, it catches the error and falls back to empty pixels / null _lutData, but still preserves the dead l.ref and l.lut on the live layer with dirty: false. Subsequent .scumble saves (Ctrl+S and Save As) serialize that dead ref in getValue(), and main's Documents.write refuses to save the entire document because every non-history ref in document.json is required.
findings.scenario: A session or .scumble holds a Deep paint ('surface') layer or a LUT (.cube) filter layer whose PNG in the local mirror was lost, pruned, or corrupted while ComfyUI is offline. On startup or open, setValue logs 'Deep paint pixels missing' (and warns in leftOut) or 'LUT missing', creates the layer with empty pixels / _lutData: null and dirty: false, and keeps layer.ref = l.ref / layer.lut = l.lut. The user edits the document and presses Ctrl+S or File > Save As. flushEditor skips syncLayers because dirty is false, getValue() writes the dead ref, and Documents.write throws '<filename> is not in the local store and ComfyUI could not send it; the document was not saved', blocking all .scumble saves until the user deletes or repaints that filter layer.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:190-208 catches Deep paint's load failure (`pixels = null; missing.push(...)`) and allocates `pixels = this.pixels.Layer.empty(this.width, this.height)`, and lines 215-217 catch `l.lut.ref` load failure (`lutData = null`). Unlike `maskRef: maskPx ? l.mask : null` (line 230) and `plate: plateImg ? l.plate : null` (line 232), line 228 sets `ref: l.ref || null` with `dirty: false` (line 229), and line 231 sets `lut: l.lut || null, _lutData: lutData`. getValue() emits `ref: l.ref` (line 49) and `lut: l.lut || null` (line 57). host_documents.js:33-36 flushEditor only syncs layers where `(l.dirty && l.px) || ...`. electron/main/documents.js:182, 193-194 collects `outside = docfile.collectRefs({ doc: { ...doc, history: undefined }, plug })` and throws `${ref.filename} is not in the local store...; the document was not saved` when any `outside` ref is missing.
findings.fix: Track whether the ownPixels paint file loaded (`let paintLoaded = false;` set true after the size check at line 200), set `ref: !FILTERS[fid] ? (l.ref || null) : (FILTERS[fid].ownPixels && paintLoaded ? l.ref : null)` at line 228, and set `lut: lutData ? l.lut : null` at line 231 (matching `maskRef` and `plate`).
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `PersistPart.setValue` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:186-236`) explicitly catches load failures on filter layers' auxiliary files so the document can still restore, but fails to clear two of those failed refs on the constructed layer object. When a Deep paint (`ownPixels`) filter layer's `l.ref` fails to fetch/decode or fails the size check (`lines 190-206`), the catch logs `'Deep paint pixels missing'`, sets `pixels = null`, pushes to `missing`, and allocates an empty pixel store (`line 208: if (!pixels) pixels = this.pixels.Layer.empty(this.width, this.height)`). Likewise, when a 3D LUT filter layer's `l.lut.ref` fails to load (`lines 215-217`), the catch logs `'LUT missing'` and leaves `lutData = null` (without even adding a `leftOut` warning). Yet unlike `maskRef: maskPx ? l.mask : null` (`line 230`) and `plate: plateImg ? l.plate : null` (`line 232`), `setValue` pushes the live filter layer with `ref: l.ref || null` (`line 228`), `dirty: false` (`line 229`), and `lut: l.lut || null, _lutData: lutData` (`line 231`). (Note also that any non-`ownPixels` filter layer carrying a stale `l.ref`—for instance after a `canvas` or `turn` snapshot restore in `inpaint_ed_history.js:696, 757` marked it `dirty: true` and `syncLayersOnce` uploaded an empty PNG—skips line 190 altogether and also retains `ref: l.ref || null` unchecked.)

Tracing the save path confirms that no guard clears or re-uploads those dead refs before `Documents.write` rejects the save. When the user later presses Ctrl+S or File > Save As (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:197` `saveDocument`), `flushEditor` (`host_documents.js:34-36`) only triggers `syncLayers` when a layer has `(l.dirty && l.px) || (l.maskDirty && l.maskPx) || l._uploading || l._maskUploading`, and `syncLayersOnce` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:905-932`) only uploads `layer.px` for layers with `layer.dirty && layer.px` and never uploads or clears `layer.lut`. `ed.getValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:49, 57`) then emits `ref: l.ref` and `lut: l.lut || null` into the serialized document JSON. In the main process, `Documents.write` (`electron/main/documents.js:181-194`) runs `outside = docfile.collectRefs({ doc: { ...doc, history: undefined }, plug })` (`electron/main/docfile.js:244-254` recursively collects every object with a string `filename`, catching both `layer.ref` and `layer.lut.ref`), stats the mirror path, tries `fetchMissing` if ComfyUI is connected, and throws `${ref.filename} is not in the local store and ComfyUI could not send it; the document was not saved` (`documents.js:194`) whenever any `outside` ref is absent.

One nuance on entry points was checked adversarially: opening a `.scumble` archive directly (`docfile.js:728-785` `openDocument`) already refuses before `setValue` if a required entry is absent from the zip (`line 743`), and if a corrupt/wrong-sized PNG entry is present in the zip with a valid CRC-32 it is copied into the mirror (so `Documents.write` later re-packs the broken file rather than throwing). However, the missing-mirror-file scenario is directly reachable on session restore (`host_setup.js:218` `restore`), including the built-in recovery workflow *Settings > Local files > Clean up* followed by *Earlier states* (`files.prune` deletes unreferenced mirror files older than an hour while `referencedFileKeys` in `host_queue.js:554-579` does not walk `autosave.2..5.json`, leaving the base mirrored if still open/closed while pruning older Deep paint or LUT PNGs), or when `<userData>/files` loses a file while ComfyUI is offline. For a missing LUT, `buildFilterControls` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:62`) even continues displaying `${layer.lut.name} (${layer.lut.size}³)` with no Remove button, and `setFilterType` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:548-594`) does not clear `layer.lut` either.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: `documents/D2+canvas-c/F1` notes that `files.prune` does not scan earlier autosave generations, and `docs/BUGS.md` (line 20) notes the 2026-11-16 fix for unstored `maps` blocking/dropping on save, neither of which covers `setValue` preserving failed `l.ref` / `l.lut` refs on filter layers. Severity is `should`: it defeats `setValue`'s own graceful-degradation path and blocks all `.scumble` saves (`Ctrl+S`, `Save As`, `Save Copy`, and close-with-save) with an opaque hashed filename error until the user deletes the filter layer, repaints the Deep paint layer, or loads another `.cube` LUT.

findings.claim: turnSnapshot shallow-copies this.maps (`{ ...this.maps }`) and copyTurn shallow-copies snap, sharing every feature map object (depth, shading, residual, normals, points) and its `xf` array with the live editor. In-place `map.xf` mutations during document turns/flips/straightens corrupt stored turn snapshots, and applySnapshot('turn') runs restoreGeometry(snap) at line 687 before replacing `this.maps` at line 729, transforming the outgoing maps instead of the restored ones and double-transforming shared maps on undo.
findings.scenario: On a document with a depth map or Deep paint surface maps: (1) Take a named snapshot (or start an assistant turn), then rotate the canvas 90° CW. mapExtras mutates `map.xf` in place on the shared map object. Restoring the snapshot restores the unrotated base/layers and docXf, while `snap.maps` already holds the rotated `map.xf`. (2) Alternatively, toggle Depth edge snap (`setMapMeta` replaces `this.maps.depth` with a new `deriveMap` object) and then rotate 90° CW; restoring the snapshot runs `restoreGeometry(snap)` against the post-turn `this.maps.depth`, then overwrites `this.maps` with `snap.maps` at line 729, and pressing Ctrl+Z (`restoreTurn` pushed `now = this.turnSnapshot()`) applies the inverse transform a second time to that shared map. Depth limits, Haze/Dehaze/Lens blur, Relight, and Deep paint then sample misaligned maps on screen, in exports, and in paid runs.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:254 (`turnSnapshot`): `maps: this.maps ? { ...this.maps } : {}`. Line 274-276 (`restoreTurn`): `const now = this.turnSnapshot(); if (now) this.pushUndoSnapshot(now, { label }); this.applySnapshot(snap);`. Lines 345-353 (`copyTurn`): `{ ...snap, ... }` without cloning `snap.maps`. In `applySnapshot` (`snap.kind === 'turn'`), `this.restoreGeometry(snap)` runs at line 687 while `this.maps = snap.maps ? { ...snap.maps } : {}` runs later at line 729. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:851-855 (`restoreGeometry`) calls `this.mapExtras(A, 'undo')`, and `mapExtras` (lines 784-791) mutates `map.xf = snapXf(xfMul(A, map.xf))` in place on `this.maps`. `setMapMeta` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:932-950) replaces `this.maps[kind] = deriveMap(cur, meta)`.
findings.fix: Clone each map descriptor and its `xf` array (`xf: Array.isArray(m.xf) ? m.xf.slice() : null`, sharing the immutable typed-array `data`/`guide` buffers) in `turnSnapshot`, `copyTurn`, and `applySnapshot` (`kind === 'turn'`), and in `applySnapshot` (`kind === 'turn'`) assign `this.maps` only without calling `mapExtras` on `snap.maps` since `snap.maps` already carries the snapshot's own `xf`.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js and renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js. In turnSnapshot() (inpaint_ed_history.js:231-264), line 254 stores `maps: this.maps ? { ...this.maps } : {}`, shallow-copying the map dictionary while sharing every DocMap descriptor (`depth`, `shading`, `residual`, `normals`, `points`) by reference with the live editor. Likewise, copyTurn(snap) (lines 345-353, called by restoreSnapshot at line 324) spreads `...snap` without cloning `snap.maps` or its DocMap entries, and snapshotOf({ kind: 'turn' }) (line 380, called by historyStepNow at line 1100 on undo/redo of a turn step) calls turnSnapshot() again. Meanwhile, every whole-document geometry operation—turnDocumentNow (inpaint_ed_geometry.js:705), straightenDocumentNow (line 1060), and cropCanvasNow / resizeImageNow / extendCanvasNow via followGeometry (lines 874, 1405, 1491)—calls mapExtras(A, kind) (lines 784-792), which mutates `map.xf = snapXf(xfMul(A, map.xf))` in place on each DocMap in `this.maps`. Then, in applySnapshot(snap) for `snap.kind === 'turn'` (inpaint_ed_history.js:682-742), `this.restoreGeometry(snap)` runs at line 687—computing `D = xfMul(snap.xf, xfInv(this.docXf))` and calling `this.mapExtras(D, 'undo')` (inpaint_ed_geometry.js:852-855) on the *outgoing* `this.maps`—before line 729 overwrites `this.maps = snap.maps ? { ...snap.maps } : {}`.

Tracing the exact object identities shows why both failure modes hold and no guard prevents them (tileMode is on by default, reachable via the Undo history '+ Snapshot' / Restore UI at inpaint_modal.js:511-575, MCP take_snapshot / restore_snapshot at commands_edit.js:238-257, and the assistant's 'Undo this turn' in renderer/assistant_turns.js:51,84). In the coincidental case where `this.maps.depth` stays the exact same DocMap object M0 throughout, mapExtras(A) mutates M0.xf to A*xf0 and line 687's restoreGeometry mutates that same M0.xf by A^-1 back to xf0 right before line 729 reassigns M0. However, whenever `this.maps[k]` changes identity or presence across a geometry operation, the two mechanisms collide: (1) Take snapshot S1 with map M0 (xf0) -> rotate/crop/extend/resize/straighten (mapExtras mutates shared M0.xf in S1 to A*xf0) -> adjust Depth 'Edges' slider (`setMapMeta` at inpaint_ed_depth.js:928-962 replaces `this.maps.depth` via `deriveMap`), edit depth (`editDepth` line 1032), or recompute depth/surface maps (`setMap`/`setMaps` lines 368, 900), putting M1 in `this.maps` -> restore S1 (or click 'Undo this turn'): line 687's restoreGeometry transforms outgoing M1 (corrupting `now.maps` pushed at line 275) while leaving M0 untouched, and line 729 restores M0 with rotated/shifted `A*xf0` onto the unrotated `I` document. (2) Conversely, take S1 -> create or update map to M1 (xf0) -> rotate 90° CW (`M1.xf = A*xf0`, `docXf = A`) -> restore S1: `restoreTurn` (lines 274-276) pushes `now` holding M1, line 687 mutates `M1.xf` (`now.maps.depth.xf`) to `xf0`, and line 729 installs `S1.maps` (M0 at xf0). Pressing Ctrl+Z runs line 687 (`mapExtras(A)`) on `this.maps` (corrupting S1's stored `M0.xf` to `A*xf0`) and line 729 restores M1 with unrotated `xf0` onto the rotated `A` document; pressing Ctrl+Shift+Z (Redo) then applies `A^-1` a second time to `M1.xf` (`A^-1 * xf0`) and restores M0 with `A*xf0` onto the unrotated document.
