On `Escape`, `inpaint_canvas.js:292-298` (and `inpaint_ed_pointer.js:99-105`) handles `if (this._pendingPick)` and returns before reaching `else if (this._rangeTint)` at line 302, resolving `val` to `null`; `pickBtn` falls through lines 192-206 (note: minor line-number/wording drift in the candidate's evidence—`begin()` is line 190, `commit` is lines 201 and 205, and `val == null` falls through both `typeof` branches rather than an explicit early `return`) without calling `stop()`, leaving `_rangeTint` stuck after 'Pick cancelled.' until a second `Escape`. Likewise, clicking a pixel on the canvas (`handlePickOnce`, `inpaint_ed_filters.js:1386-1454`) updates `ed.rangeLimit` and resolves `val`, and `pickBtn` calls `commit(...)` without `stop()`, leaving `begin()`'s stale pre-pick `_rangeTint` stuck on the canvas.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, all three `verified.json` files, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: `BUGS.md:26-29` covered only the swatch-colour overwrite fixed in `2a969cd7`, and `b8a72af7` only synced `rangeInvertInput -> rangeBar`; this reverse desync and stuck `_rangeTint` defect is not in any known list. Severity `should` holds because both `Pick` and `Invert` in the Select Range bar hit this 100% deterministically in normal usage, desynchronizing two visible Invert controls and leaving a wrong/stale selection-tint overlay over the canvas, with a workaround (`Escape` or using the lower Invert checkbox and handle drags).

findings.claim: `selectionFromLayer` (`Selection > Layer`) materialises the layer and three full-document `W x H` buffers synchronously on the window thread regardless of the layer's bounds, and lacks a filter-layer guard. On a 15k document even a small layer spikes 1.8-2.4 GB and blocks the window for seconds (throwing after `pushUndo` above 268 MP), and on a non-surface filter layer it silently wipes the existing selection while claiming success.
findings.scenario: (1) Open a 15000 x 10000 (150 MP) picture, paste or generate a 512 x 512 layer, and click `Layer` in the Selection panel (`ed.selectionFromLayer()`). Despite the layer covering 0.17 % of the canvas, the window thread allocates a 600 MB `tmp` canvas, a 600 MB `getImageData` buffer, and a 600 MB output `ImageData` (plus a 600 MB `layerPixels` canvas if the layer is full-size), loops over 150M pixels synchronously, writes all 150 MP into `this.sel`, and leaves bounds dirty for a full rescan; on a 30000 x 20000 document `makeCanvas` throws after `pushUndo` has already cleared `redo`. (2) Make a selection, select a Levels, Relight, or Colour Fill filter layer, and click `Selection > Layer`: because `addFilterLayer` gives every filter layer an empty transparent `layer.px`, `selectionFromLayer` pushes an undo step, clears the entire selection to empty, and displays `"Selection taken from Levels 1."`.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js:612` wires the Selection panel's `Layer` button to `() => ed.selectionFromLayer()`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1448-1464`: `selectionFromLayer()` checks only `if (!layer) { ... return; }`, then calls `this.pushUndo({ kind: "selection", label: "Selection from layer" }); const tmp = makeCanvas(this.width, this.height); tmp.getContext("2d").drawImage(this.layerPixels(layer), layer.x, layer.y, layer.w, layer.h); const src = tmp.getContext("2d").getImageData(0, 0, this.width, this.height).data; const img = new ImageData(this.width, this.height); ... this.sel.writeRect(img, 0, 0); this.markSelectionChanged();`. Contrast `fillSelection` (`line 1365`) and `deleteSelection` (`line 1400`), which refuse `layer.kind === "filter" && !this.hasOwnPixels(layer)` (`addFilterLayer` at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:324` sets `px: this.pixels.Layer.empty(this.width, this.height)`), and `applyMaskImage` (`inpaint_ed_segment.js:526-573`), which processes in row bands over the clipped layer box `[max(0, floor(layer.x)), max(0, floor(layer.y)), min(W, ceil(layer.x + layer.w)), min(H, ceil(layer.y + layer.h))]` and combines via `bytesSource`.
findings.fix: Refuse non-pixel filter layers (`if (layer.kind === "filter" && !this.hasOwnPixels(layer))`) with a status message (or use `layer.maskPx` when the filter layer has a live mask). Clear `this.sel` first, clamp the layer's box `[layer.x, layer.y, layer.x + layer.w, layer.y + layer.h]` to `[0, 0, W, H]`, and combine alpha > 127 in row bands over that clipped box using `this.sel.combine(bytesSource(...), "add")` (or tile-by-tile when unscaled on tiles), tracking exact `unionBounds` for `markSelectionChanged(unionBounds)`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1448-1464 (`SelectPart.selectionFromLayer`). The method checks only `if (!layer)` at line 1450 and has no filter-layer guard, no size check, and no clipped bounding-box path. At line 1451 it immediately calls `this.pushUndo({ kind: "selection", label: "Selection from layer" })` (inpaint_ed_history.js:469-496), which releases and clears `this.redo` (lines 489-490) and pushes onto `this.undo`. It then allocates `const tmp = makeCanvas(this.width, this.height)` (line 1452, imported at line 15 from inpaint_consts.js:147-152), draws `this.layerPixels(layer)` at `(layer.x, layer.y, layer.w, layer.h)` (line 1453), synchronously reads back `tmp.getContext("2d").getImageData(0, 0, this.width, this.height).data` (line 1454), allocates `new ImageData(this.width, this.height)` and loops over every pixel on the window thread (lines 1455-1459), writes the whole document into `this.sel.writeRect(img, 0, 0)` (line 1460), marks the selection dirty (`this.markSelectionChanged()` with no bounds hint at line 1461 -> line 1478), and reports `Selection taken from ${layer.name}.` (line 1463).

Both entry points reach this unguarded: the Selection panel's `Layer` button (`renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js:612`, `() => ed.selectionFromLayer()`) and the MCP/command bridge `select_from_layer` (`renderer/commands_select.js:29-33`, which sets `ed.activeLayerId = l.id; ed.selectionFromLayer();` without refusing filter layers, unlike `select_color` at commands_select.js:123). Note two minor citation inaccuracies in the candidate finding that do not affect validity: there is no Ctrl+click layer-thumbnail shortcut calling `selectionFromLayer` in `inpaint_ed_layers.js` (row clicks call `clickLayerRow` in `inpaint_ed_view.js:301-332`), and the sibling filter-layer guards in `inpaint_ed_select.js` live in `fillSelection` at line 1264 (not 1365) and `clearSelectedPixels` at line 1400 (not `deleteSelection` at line 1242).

First, on filter and fill layers: `addFilterLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:313-324`) initializes every filter layer (`levels`, `curves`, `relight`, `fill`, `gradient`, `surface`, etc.) with `px: this.pixels.Layer.empty(this.width, this.height)`. Only `surface` (Deep paint, `inpaint_filters.js:1386-1395`, `ownPixels: true`, tested by `this.hasOwnPixels(layer)` at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:544-546`) stores painted alpha in `layer.px`. On every other filter or fill layer — including Colour fill, Gradient fill, Relight, Levels, or a filter layer that has a `maskPx` — `layer.px` is completely transparent, and `this.layerPixels(layer)` (`inpaint_ed_view.js:368-377`, which composites `maskPx` onto `layerWithStroke(layer)` with `destination-in`) still has alpha 0 everywhere. Clicking `Selection > Layer` or running `select_from_layer` on such a layer clears `this.redo`, overwrites `this.sel` with all-zero alpha (silently wiping any active selection), and falsely states `Selection taken from <layer.name>.`.

Second, on large documents: on a 15,000 x 10,000 (150 MP) document, even for a 512 x 512 layer (`0.17%` of the canvas), `selectionFromLayer` allocates a 600 MB 2D canvas (`tmp`), performs a synchronous 600 MB `getImageData` readback, allocates a second 600 MB `ImageData` (plus another 600 MB CPU canvas inside `layer.px.toCanvas()` at `inpaint_tiles.js:2129-2134` via `layerWithStroke` at `inpaint_ed_strokes.js:847` when the layer itself is full-size), runs 150M JS iterations on the window thread, and scans all 2,360 tiles in `this.sel.writeRect` (`inpaint_tiles.js:1548-1555`). Above Chromium's 268 MP canvas limit (e.g. 30,000 x 20,000 = 600 MP on tiles), `makeCanvas` from `inpaint_consts.js:147` has no limit check (unlike `inpaint_pixels.js:74`), so a full-size layer throws `above Chromium's canvas limit of 268 MP` inside `layer.px.toCanvas()` -> `cpuCanvas` (`inpaint_tiles.js:510-512, 522`) and a small layer throws a RangeError / typed-array allocation failure on the 2.4 GB `getImageData` / `ImageData` — in both cases after `pushUndo` at line 1451 has already pushed a step and cleared `this.redo`.

Not in any known list: checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Open`), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` (related entries cover `saveSelection`, `maskToCanvas`, `applyMaskFile`, and `boxes.fromSelection`, never `selectionFromLayer` or `select_from_layer`). Severity is `should`: Ctrl+Z restores the wiped selection via `snapshotSelection` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:76-92`) so there is no permanent pixel or money loss (`must`), but in normal workflows it silently wipes the selection with a misleading success status on filter/fill layers, clears redo, and freezes the window with >=1.8-2.4 GB of synchronous allocations at 15k (or throws uncaught after mutating undo/redo above 268 MP).

findings.claim: Box descriptions are truncated to DESC_MAX (400) after @img tokens (or Text-box prefixes) have expanded into internal {@layer:...} or {@ref:...} markers, allowing the 400-char slice to cut inside a marker. A truncated marker fails both LAYER_MARK in the renderer and MARKER in main, so literal '{@layer:...' or '{@ref...' text is sent in the paid FLUX 3 / Ideogram 4 prompt row instead of the reference name, and a parked layer marker cut mid-tag bypasses the unsent-layer refusal.
findings.scenario: (1) Document has shown reference A (@img1, layer id Lm3k9x2ab12) and a New box whose stored description is 387 characters ending '... wearing the hat from @img1' (valid: <= 400). Run Generate on FLUX 3 Image (API) with Boxes on: boxes_model.js runDesc expands '@img1' (5 chars) into '{@layer:Lm3k9x2ab12}' (20 chars, total 402); pluginBoxes descOf calls foldDesc first, slicing to 400 ('... wearing the hat from {@layer:Lm3k9x2ab1'), so LAYER_MARK neither resolves it nor throws fail('layer') when A is hidden/parked. (2) With no boxes, Boxes on, a selection, and a 440-char prompt with '@img1' at chars 396-400, selectionBox folds named.prompt (already holding '{@ref:0}') to 400, slicing mid-marker ('... {@ref'). (3) On a Text box with text 'SUMMER SALE 2026' (prefix 'text reading "SUMMER SALE 2026", ' = 33 chars) and a 368-char desc ending '@img1' (371 chars with '{@ref:0}', untouched by pluginBoxes), electron/main/providers/boxes.js descOf prepends the 33-char prefix (404 chars) and resolved() calls fold(raw) before resolveMarkers(), slicing '{@ref:0}' to '{@re'.
findings.evidence:
renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:244-249 runDesc: `return (b.desc || "").replace(TOKEN, (m, n) => (labels.has("img" + n) ? `{@layer:${labels.get("img" + n)}}` : m)).replace(PARKED, (m, id) => `{@layer:${id}}`);`
renderer/editor/boxes.js:89-91 foldDesc: `return String(s == null ? "" : s).replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().slice(0, DESC_MAX);`
renderer/editor/boxes.js:159-163 pluginBoxes: `const descOf = (b, who) => foldDesc(b.desc).replace(LAYER_MARK, (_, id) => { const r = refOf(id); if (!r) throw fail("layer", ...); return `{@ref:${r.index}}`; });`
renderer/editor/boxes.js:118 selectionBox: `const desc = foldDesc(prompt);` called from renderer/editor/host_provider.js:361 with `named.prompt` from line 333 (`{@ref:i}` markers).
electron/main/providers/boxes.js:117-127: `const resolved = (s, who) => { const r = resolveMarkers(fold(s), lay.pictures, patternOf(req)); ... };` and `if (b.kind === "text") { const words = fold(b.text); const raw = own ? \`text reading "${words}", ${own}\` : \`text reading "${words}"\`; return resolved(raw, who); }`.
electron/main/providers/index.js:168-174 checks MARKER_ANY on out.prompt/out.negative before `boxes.applyBoxes(req, lay)` runs at line 307.
findings.fix: Never slice expanded marker text blindly at 400 characters: in pluginBoxes, resolve LAYER_MARK before folding and ensure any truncation avoids cutting inside `{@ref:i}` (or fold the user's own text before marker expansion); in selectionBox, truncate without splitting a `{@ref:i}` marker; in electron/main/providers/boxes.js descOf, resolve markers on `own` before folding the combined Text-box clause (or fold `own` to leave room without splitting markers) and add a `MARKER_ANY` guard in `resolved()` after `resolveMarkers`.
findings.why:
All three truncation paths hold against commit f45a86cc. First, in renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:94-95, normaliseBox folds and caps stored box descriptions at DESC_MAX (400). At send time on both API Edit (renderer/editor/host_provider.js:351) and API Generate new (renderer/editor/host_generate.js:81), renderer/plugins.js:479-482 calls plugins/boxes/main.js:221 -> descOf (line 60-62) -> boxes_model.js:244-249 runDesc, which expands each live @imgN (4-6 chars) or parked @img?<layerId> into `{@layer:<layerId>}`. Because layer IDs come from renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:529 (`"L" + Date.now().toString(36) + this.layerCounter`, 10-11 chars in 2026), `{@layer:...}` is 19-20 chars (+14-15 chars per live token, +4 chars per parked token). In renderer/editor/boxes.js:159-163, pluginBoxes's descOf runs `foldDesc(b.desc)` (lines 89-91, `.slice(0, 400)`) BEFORE `.replace(LAYER_MARK, ...)` (line 131, `/\{@layer:([^}\s]+)\}/g`). Any `{@layer:...}` straddling char 400 loses its closing brace, so LAYER_MARK neither converts it to `{@ref:i}` nor throws `fail("layer", ...)` when the layer is hidden/deleted (and if earlier @img expansions push a parked `{@layer:...}` completely past char 400, `foldDesc` slices it off entirely, also bypassing the parked-layer refusal that boxes_model.js:245-248 was written to enforce).

Second, when Boxes is on with a selection and no explicit boxes, renderer/editor/host_provider.js:361 passes `named.prompt` (produced by `refPrompt` at line 333, where @img tokens are already `{@ref:i}` markers and prompts have no 400-char cap, e.g. after Prompt Upsample) into `selectionBox` (renderer/editor/boxes.js:114-125). Line 118 calls `foldDesc(prompt)`, slicing blindly at 400 chars and cutting any `{@ref:i}` straddling index 400 into a broken prefix like `{@ref`. Worse, in electron/main/providers/boxes.js:243 (`captionFlux3`), `isPrompt` compares `row.desc` (still holding `{@ref`) against `req.prompt` (where `{@ref:i}` resolved to `image k`), so `whole.startsWith(a)` fails and FLUX 3 duplicates the 400-char truncated prompt with literal `{@ref` into a second caption clause instead of emitting `placeOnly`.

Third, in electron/main/providers/boxes.js:117-127 (note: the candidate's evidence paraphrased line 126 as `if (b.kind === "text")`, whereas the actual code checks `b.text != null` on a `kind: "new"` box inside `descOf(req, lay, b)` and passes the combined string to `function resolved(req, lay, b, s)`), `descOf` builds `` `text reading "${fold(b.text)}"${own ? ", " + own : ""}` `` (over 400 chars whenever `own` + prefix > 400) and line 118 calls `resolveMarkers(fold(s), lay.pictures, patternOf(req))`. Because `fold(s)` (line 111) slices to 400 before `resolveMarkers` (electron/main/providers/refs.js:99-114, `/\{@ref:(\d+)\}/g`), a `{@ref:i}` near the end of `own` is cut mid-marker (and if `r.left` would have caught an unsent reference at line 119, cutting or dropping the marker bypasses that check too). Meanwhile electron/main/providers/index.js:168-174 runs its `TOKEN` and `MARKER_ANY` safety net on `out.prompt`/`out.negative` at line 299, before `boxes.applyBoxes(req, lay)` modifies `req.prompt` at line 307.

Checked scratch/known_index.md, docs/BUGS.md, all three verified.json files, and docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md: not known (`prompt-refs/box-desc-tokens-not-remapped` in review_full_2026-11-12 was about `refsMutated` not remapping box descriptions, and its fix in `remapBoxDescs`/`runDesc` actually introduced the parked-token refusal path that Scenario 1 bypasses). Severity is `should`: users with upsampled prompts + selection boxes, Text boxes, or detailed box descriptions containing `@imgN` can send literal `{@layer:...` / `{@ref...` garbage in billed FLUX 3 / Ideogram 4 API calls and bypass pre-flight refusals for hidden/unsent reference layers.

findings.claim: remapBoxDescs rewrites box descriptions across every undo and redo entry carrying pluginData, including `turn` snapshots. Unlike `data` or `canvas` steps, a `turn` snapshot carries its own layers and prompt in its own reference numbering and restores via `refsRebuilt({ carry: true })` without remapping boxes, so any reference change after a `turn` step is pushed leaves the `turn` step's boxes mapped to the newer numbering while its layers and prompt restore the old numbering.
findings.scenario: Document has shown references A (hat, @img1) and B (lamp, @img2), plus box lamp_1 with desc 'the lamp of @img2'. Take a named snapshot S and restore it (or run an assistant edit and click 'Undo this turn'): restoreTurn pushes the current state as `turn` step T onto `this.undo` (holding layers A and B visible and T.pluginData.boxes desc 'the lamp of @img2'). Click A's eye in the reference list to hide it: no undo step is pushed, and `refsMutated()` maps live `@img2` -> `@img1` while `remapBoxDescs` also rewrites `T.pluginData.boxes` desc to 'the lamp of @img1' (leaving T.layers and T.doc.prompt untouched). Press Ctrl+Z: `applySnapshot` restores T's layers (A is @img1, B is @img2) and T's prompt, then `restoreGeometry` restores `T.pluginData` with 'the lamp of @img1', and `refsRebuilt({ carry: true })` does not remap boxes. Generating on FLUX 3 now sends picture A (the hat) for lamp_1 instead of B.
findings.evidence:
renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:113-114: `fix(this.pluginData); for (const s of [...(this.undo || []), ...(this.redo || [])]) if (s && s.pluginData) fix(s.pluginData);` (and comment at lines 99-100 explicitly including `turn` steps).
renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:231-263 turnSnapshot: spreads `...this.geometrySnapshot()` at line 255 (`pluginData: this.pluginDataCopy()` in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:865) alongside `doc: { prompt: this.promptText, ... }` at lines 256-262.
renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:271-279 restoreTurn: `const now = this.turnSnapshot(); if (now) this.pushUndoSnapshot(now, { label }); this.applySnapshot(snap);`
renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:682-723 applySnapshot `turn` branch: line 687 `this.restoreGeometry(snap);` (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:859` restores `snap.pluginData`), lines 720-723 restore `doc.prompt` and call `this.refsRebuilt({ carry: true });` (`inpaint_ed_refs.js:122-130`, which never calls `remapBoxDescs`).
Reference visibility changes push no undo step and call `this.refsMutated()`: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:1113-1116, 617-620, renderer/commands_layers.js:38, renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:198-206.
findings.fix: Skip `turn` steps in `remapBoxDescs`: `if (s && s.kind !== "turn" && s.pluginData) fix(s.pluginData);` so `turn` snapshots keep their self-consistent `{ layers, doc.prompt, pluginData }` tuple just like `this.snapshots` and `assistant_turns.js` records.
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `RefsPart.remapBoxDescs` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:103-115` rewrites `pluginData.boxes` on `this.pluginData` and then loops over every undo and redo step at line 114: `for (const s of [...(this.undo || []), ...(this.redo || [])]) if (s && s.pluginData) fix(s.pluginData);` (with the comment at lines 99-101 explicitly naming `(a data, canvas or turn step)` on line 100 while simultaneously noting on line 101 `Not in remapOthers: a turn snapshot that brings the layers back brings these too`). Tracing all three undo step kinds that carry `pluginData` shows why `data` and `canvas` steps want in-place remapping on `this.undo`/`this.redo`, whereas `turn` steps are broken by it:

1. A `data` step (`inpaint_ed_history.js:383`) restores only `this.pluginData` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:660-664`), keeping live `this.layers` and `this.promptText`, so its stored box descriptions must track live reference renumbering. A `canvas` step (`inpaint_ed_history.js:429-434`) carries `layers` and `pluginData` (`geometrySnapshot()` at `inpaint_ed_geometry.js:865`) without `doc.prompt`, and on restore (`inpaint_ed_history.js:743-783`) calls `this.restoreGeometry(snap)` (line 749) followed by `this.refsMutated()` (line 773), which maps both live `promptText` and `this.pluginData` from pre-undo `this.refMap` to the restored `snap.layers` numbering — so `canvas` steps also require `s.pluginData` to have followed `this.refMap` up to that point.

2. By contrast, a `turn` step (`turnSnapshot` in `inpaint_ed_history.js:231-264`, taken on the default tile backend when `this.tileMode && this.sel`) captures a self-consistent tuple of `layers` (with each reference layer's `visible` flag via `snapshotLayer`), `...this.geometrySnapshot()` (`pluginData: this.pluginDataCopy()` at `inpaint_ed_geometry.js:865`), and `doc: { prompt: this.promptText, negative: this.negativeText, ... }` (lines 256-262). Both named snapshot restores (`restoreSnapshot` -> `restoreTurn`, `inpaint_ed_history.js:321-327, 271-279`) and the assistant's 'Undo this turn' (`renderer/assistant_turns.js:84` -> `ed.restoreTurn`) push the pre-restore document onto `this.undo` as a `turn` step (`pushUndoSnapshot(now, { label })` at `inpaint_ed_history.js:275`), and undoing/redoing a `turn` step pushes its counterpart `turn` step onto `this.redo`/`this.undo` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:1100-1101`). When `applySnapshot` restores `snap.kind === "turn"` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:682-742`), it restores `snap.pluginData` via `this.restoreGeometry(snap)` (line 687, `inpaint_ed_geometry.js:859`), restores `snap.layers` (lines 694-703), restores `doc.prompt` and `doc.negative` (lines 720-721), and calls `this.refsRebuilt({ carry: true })` (line 723). `refsRebuilt` (`inpaint_ed_refs.js:122-130`) updates `this.refMap` and calls only `this.remapOthers(...)` — never `remapBoxDescs`.

3. Consequently, no guard prevents corruption when `refsMutated()` runs while a `turn` step sits on `this.undo` or `this.redo`. Reference visibility toggles (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:1112-1116` eye button in References, `inpaint_ed_layers.js:613-618` `setSelectedFlag`, `inpaint_ed_refs.js:198-206` `showReference`, `renderer/commands_layers.js:38` `set_layer`) push no undo step, do not bump `historyGen`, do not clear `this.redo`, and call `this.refsMutated()`. Hiding shown reference A (`@img1`) while B (`@img2`) stays visible rewrites `T.pluginData.boxes` on `this.undo` from `@img2` to `@img1` (and parks `@img1` as `@img?<A.id>`), leaving `T.layers` and `T.doc.prompt` untouched. Pressing Ctrl+Z then pops `T`, restores A as `@img1` and B as `@img2` alongside `T.doc.prompt` (`@img2` = B), and restores `T.pluginData.boxes` with `@img1` (= A), so a subsequent FLUX 3 / Ideogram 4 API run (`runDesc` -> `pluginBoxes`) or local ComfyUI box run sends picture A instead of B for that box. Furthermore, if the restored snapshot `S` had a different reference numbering than the `turn` step `T` pushed by `restoreTurn`, any `refsMutated()` call while viewing `S` applies `S`'s `before -> target` map to `T.pluginData.boxes`, which was numbered against `T.layers`, not `S`.

Checked known-issue sources (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the three `verified.json` files): `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` (`prompt-refs/box-desc-tokens-not-remapped`) reported that box descriptions were not remapped at all; `remapBoxDescs` was introduced afterwards to fix that finding, and this defect is a new bug in that fix. Severity is `should` (matching `prompt-refs/box-desc-tokens-not-remapped`): hit in plausible workflows combining Boxes + `@img` references with named snapshots or 'Undo this turn' + reference visibility/order changes, resulting in the wrong reference image being sent on a paid or local run without silent loss of stored pixel layers.

findings.claim: On the API path, Generate new emits a `resize` geometry event when the new image dimensions differ from what the document's boxes were drawn on (`host_generate.js:127-129`). On the local ComfyUI path (called by both the UI Generate new dialog and MCP `generate_new` for recipes like FLUX 3 Image Klein and MOSS-Image), `ed.newCanvas` replaces the canvas dimensions without emitting a `geometry` event; the queued run scales a temporary copy via `scaleStateBoxes`, leaving `pluginData.boxes` in the old canvas's pixel coordinates on the new picture.
findings.scenario: Open a 1024 x 1024 canvas, select local recipe FLUX 3 Image Klein, turn Boxes on, and draw `cat_1` at `[512, 512, 1024, 1024]` (the bottom-right quarter). Run Generate new (from the Generate new dialog or `generate_new`) at 16:9, `2048 x 1152`. The first run scales `boxGiven` to `[1024, 576, 2048, 1152]` and places the cat bottom-right, but `pluginData.boxes` stays `[512, 512, 1024, 1024]` on the 2048 x 1152 document (`x` 0.25..0.50, `y` 0.44..0.89). Running Generate new again (including via `newTabFrom`, which copies `pluginData`) or running a selection edit measures the unscaled `[512, 512, 1024, 1024]` box against `2048 x 1152`, placing or cropping the box in the wrong location.
findings.evidence:
renderer/commands_runs.js:92-102: `const drawnOn = [ed.width, ed.height]; await ed.newCanvas(\`${w}x${h}\`, { keepRefs: true }); const boxPlan = host.localBoxPlan(ed, r, shownRefs.map((l) => l.id)); if (boxPlan.takes) ed._newBoxes = { from: drawnOn, aspect, plan: boxPlan }; let res; try { res = await COMMANDS.generate.run(ed, { timeout: a.timeout }); } finally { ed._newBoxes = null; } await ed.flatten(); writeTarget(ed, r, aspect, asked); ed.notifyChanged();` (also called from UI dialog at renderer/shell.js:693).
renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:387-412 `newCanvas`: updates `width`/`height`/`base` with no `host.changed(this, { geometry: ... })`.
renderer/editor/host_generate.js:124-129 (API path): `if (drawnOn.width > 0 && drawnOn.height > 0 && (c.width !== drawnOn.width || c.height !== drawnOn.height)) { this.changed(editor, { geometry: { kind: "resize", m: [c.width / drawnOn.width, 0, 0, c.height / drawnOn.height, 0, 0], from: drawnOn, to: { width: c.width, height: c.height } } }); }`.
plugins/boxes/main.js:208-214: updates stored box coordinates only on `scumble.events.on("geometry", ...)`.
findings.fix: After `localBoxPlan` / `COMMANDS.generate.run` consumes `drawnOn` (or right after `ed.newCanvas` while adjusting `_newBoxes` not to double-scale in `host_queue.js:135`), emit `host.changed(ed, { geometry: { kind: "resize", m: [ed.width / drawnOn[0], 0, 0, ed.height / drawnOn[1], 0, 0], from: { width: drawnOn[0], height: drawnOn[1] }, to: { width: ed.width, height: ed.height } } })` whenever `drawnOn[0] > 0 && drawnOn[1] > 0 && (ed.width !== drawnOn[0] || ed.height !== drawnOn[1])`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc. Compare the two branches of `RunCommandsPart.generate_new.run` in `renderer/commands_runs.js`: on the API provider branch (`commands_runs.js:64-69` -> `HostGeneratePart.runGenerate` in `renderer/editor/host_generate.js:23-151`), `drawnOn` is captured at line 35, the new image replaces the base via `editor.setBaseFromCanvas(c, { keepRefs: true })` at line 120, and lines 127-129 explicitly emit `this.changed(editor, { geometry: { kind: "resize", m: [c.width / drawnOn.width, 0, 0, c.height / drawnOn.height, 0, 0], from: drawnOn, to: { width: c.width, height: c.height } } })` whenever `drawnOn.width > 0 && drawnOn.height > 0 && (c.width !== drawnOn.width || c.height !== drawnOn.height)`. That triggers `host.changed` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:507`) -> `scumble.events.on("geometry", ...)` in `plugins/boxes/main.js:208-214`, which rewrites `pluginData.boxes` via `mapBoxes(boxes, ev.m)` (`renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:239`) so stored boxes stay aligned with the generated image.

On the local ComfyUI branch (`renderer/commands_runs.js:70-102`, used for shipped box-capable local recipes `recipes/flux3_klein_local.json` and `recipes/moss_image_local.json` as well as any other local recipe when the document holds boxes), `boxPlan` is built before the canvas swap via `await host.newBoxPlan(ed, r, snap.refIds.slice(0, plan.lay.kept))` at line 87 (`renderer/editor/host_setup.js:153-161, 172-177`; note the candidate's evidence slightly paraphrased line 87 as `localBoxPlan` after `newCanvas`, whereas at `f45a86cc` `newBoxPlan` runs at line 87 and `ed._newBoxes` is set at line 96 and cleared to `undefined` at line 98, which leaves the defect unchanged). Line 92 records `const drawnOn = [ed.width, ed.height]`, and line 93 awaits `ed.newCanvas(\`${w}x${h}\`, { keepRefs: true })` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:355-440`), which calls `this.setBasePixels(ref, px, { keepLayers: false, keep })` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:104-155`). Neither `setBasePixels` (which only calls `this.notifyChanged()` -> `host.changed(this)` without `info.geometry` at `inpaint_canvas.js:1347-1351`), nor `COMMANDS.generate.run` (`host_queue.js:28-29, 133-138`, which clones `boxPlan.boxes` into a temporary `boxGiven` object and runs `comfyprompt.scaleStateBoxes` at `comfyprompt.js:238-250` on that clone alone), nor `ed.flatten()` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:740-799`), nor `generate_new` lines 100-101 ever emits a `geometry` resize event.

Both entry points hit this path without any guard preventing it: MCP/script `generate_new` runs `RunCommandsPart.generate_new.run` directly on `ed`, and the UI Generate new dialog (`renderer/shell.js:660-709`, `shell_generate.js:60-77, 213, 285`) either runs on `ed` in place or, when `host.replaceLoss(ed)` is truthy (always true after adding a box with undo), clones `ed` at its old dimensions along with `ed.pluginData` via `host.newTabFrom(ed)` (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:131-164`, line 154) and runs `commands.run("generate_new", args)` on `fresh` (`shell.js:693`). Whenever `[w, h]` differs from `drawnOn` (for example choosing 16:9 at 1024 px -> `1024 x 576` or at 2048 px -> `2048 x 1152` from a `1024 x 1024` canvas), the first run places the generated subject at the scaled fractional position, while `ed.pluginData.boxes` (and the `Flatten` undo snapshot pushed at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:781`) retains the old pixel coordinates—leaving boxes visually shifted or outside the new canvas and misplacing or dropping them on any subsequent `Generate`, second `Generate new`, `Copy rows`, or follow-up paid API edit.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/PLAN_BOXES.md`, `docs/PLAN_NODE_BOXES.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`); this defect is not recorded in any of them. Severity is `should`: it reliably breaks box coordinates in a normal advertised workflow (local Generate new with boxes at any changed aspect or resolution), while the initial local run is free and the displaced boxes are visible in the Boxes tool/panel as a manual workaround.

findings.claim: Unlike the main prompt (`PromptField` + `reftokens.js` + `namedPrompt` + `providers/index.js:168`), box descriptions do not normalize `@IMG1`/`@img01` on input, match tokens with a divergent regex (`/@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g`), leave unknown `@imgN` numbers untouched in `runDesc`, and are appended into `req.prompt` by `boxes.applyBoxes` after `resolveNames` has already run its `TOKEN` refusal check. As a result, a box description containing an out-of-range `@img2` or uppercase `@IMG1` is neither normalized nor refused before a paid FLUX 3 / Ideogram 4 API call, sending literal `@img2` / `@IMG1` in the billed prompt (while `foo@img1` inside a word/handle is falsely expanded as reference 1).
findings.scenario: Document has one shown reference (`@img1`). In the Boxes panel, canvas inline box editor, or `boxes.add`, enter box description `'wearing the hat from @img2'` (typo for `@img1`) or `'wearing the hat from @IMG1'`. Run Generate on FLUX 3 Image or Ideogram 4 (paid API) with Boxes on. Whereas the main prompt normalizes `@IMG1` to `@img1` and refuses `@img2` before any network call (`'@img2 names no reference image (1 shown).'`), `runDesc` leaves both `@img2` and `@IMG1` unchanged as plain text, `pluginBoxes` checks only `LAYER_MARK`, `providers/index.js:299` checks `TOKEN` on `req.prompt` before `boxes.applyBoxes` runs at line 307, and `providers/boxes.js` `resolved()` checks only `{@ref:d+}`. The paid API request goes out and bills the user with literal `'@img2'` or `'@IMG1'` in the box row.
findings.evidence:
renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:23: `const TOKEN = /@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g;` (case-sensitive, no `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_@])` lookbehind, unlike `renderer/editor/reftokens.js:14` `/(?<![A-Za-z0-9_@])@img0*([1-9][0-9]*)(?![0-9A-Za-z_])/gi`).
renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:244-249 `runDesc`: `return (b.desc || "").replace(TOKEN, (m, n) => (labels.has("img" + n) ? `{@layer:${labels.get("img" + n)}}` : m)).replace(PARKED, (m, id) => `{@layer:${id}}`);` (leaves unmatched `@imgN` and `@IMG1` as `m`).
plugins/boxes/main.js:309, renderer/editor/boxes_tool.js:87,95, renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:97,112: never call `reftokens.normalize` on `desc`.
electron/main/providers/index.js:168-174 `resolveNames` checks `TOKEN = /(@img[1-9][0-9]*)/i` on `out.prompt`/`out.negative` at line 299, before `req = boxes.applyBoxes(req, lay);` at line 307.
electron/main/providers/boxes.js:117-121 `resolved`: calls `resolveMarkers(...)` and checks `r.left`, with no `TOKEN` check.
findings.fix: Normalize box descriptions with `reftokens.normalize` when stored (or parse tokens in `boxes_model.js` using `reftokens.js`'s `TOKEN` grammar), refuse unknown live `@imgN` tokens in `runDesc`/`pluginBoxes` (matching `namedPrompt`'s refusal before any upload or API call), and add the `TOKEN` refusal check in `electron/main/providers/boxes.js` `resolved()` as defense-in-depth.
findings.why:
Verified against commit f45a86cc. One minor inaccuracy in the candidate's regex quote is that `renderer/editor/reftokens.js:22` (`(?<![\w-])@[Ii][Mm][Gg](?:([1-9]\d{0,2})|\?(L[0-9a-z]+))(?![\w-])`, mirrored identically in `electron/main/providers/refs.js:28`) intentionally treats `@img01` as plain text (`reftokens.js:19-20`, `tools/reftokens_test.js:66-80`), not a leading-zero token. Every substantive part of the defect holds across the full call path.

First, `renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:23` defines `export const TOKEN = /@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g;` (and line 25 `PARKED = /@img\?(L[0-9a-z]+)(?![\w-])/g`), which diverges from `reftokens.js:22`: it is case-sensitive on `@img`, omits the `(?<![\w-])` lookbehind, uses `\b` instead of `(?![\w-])`, and accepts 4+ digits. Box descriptions are plain text inputs (`plugins/boxes/main.js:309`, `renderer/editor/boxes_tool.js:95,118`, `boxes.add`/`boxes.set` -> `normaliseBox` at `boxes_model.js:94`) that never call `reftokens.normalize` and never trigger `ed.refsMutated()`. Thus `@IMG1` (or `@IMG?L...`) stays uppercase unless a later reference-list mutation happens to run `remapBoxDescs` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:93,103-115`), while `foo@img1`, `email@img1`, and `@img1-2` falsely match `TOKEN` in `runDesc` even though `reftokens.js` treats them as plain text.

Second, for an out-of-range live token such as `@img2` when only `@img1` (or no reference) is shown, even `reftokens.remap` (`reftokens.js:116`) deliberately keeps unknown `@imgN` tokens intact so send-time validation will refuse them. On both `runProvider` (`renderer/editor/host_provider.js:307,333,351`) and `runGenerate` (`renderer/editor/host_generate.js:45,81`), `refPrompt` validates only `snap.prompt` and `snap.negative`. When `this.plugins.boxes(...)` (`renderer/plugins.js:472-494` `collectBoxes`) invokes `plugins/boxes/main.js:221` -> `descOf` (line 60-62) -> `runDesc` (`boxes_model.js:244-249`), line 247 evaluates `(b.desc || "").replace(TOKEN, (m, n) => (labels.has("img" + n) ? `{@layer:${labels.get("img" + n)}}` : m))`: `labels.has("img2")` is false (and `@IMG1` does not match `TOKEN`), leaving literal `"@img2"` or `"@IMG1"` in `desc`. `pluginBoxes` (`renderer/editor/boxes.js:159-163`) checks only `LAYER_MARK` (`/\{@layer:([^}\s]+)\}/g`), so no `err.code = "layer"` refusal is thrown (note that any fix throwing in `runDesc` or `pluginBoxes` must use `err.code = "layer"` because `collectBoxes` at `renderer/plugins.js:479-486` catches and swallows non-`layer` plugin errors).

Third, main's safety net misses box rows because of ordering: in `electron/main/providers/index.js:299`, `resolveNames` runs `refs.TOKEN.exec(t)` (`index.js:168-174`) on `req.prompt` and `req.negative` before `boxes.applyBoxes(req, lay)` overwrites `req.prompt` at lines 307-308. Inside `electron/main/providers/boxes.js`, `resolved()` (lines 117-121, called by `descOf` line 126 for FLUX 3 and `elementIdeogram4` line 274 for Ideogram 4) calls `resolveMarkers(...)` and checks only `r.left.length` (`{@ref:\d+}`), with no `refs.TOKEN` check before `index.js:314` dispatches the billed API call.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: `review_full_2026-11-12` had `prompt-refs/box-desc-tokens-not-remapped`, which was fixed by adding `remapBoxDescs` and `PARKED` handling in `runDesc`; that fix only converted parked `@img?<id>` tokens and left unknown live `@imgN` tokens, `@IMG1` casing, regex boundary mismatches, and the `applyBoxes`-after-`resolveNames` gap unaddressed. Severity is `should`: box description inputs have no chip UI or `@` picker, so a simple `@img2` typo or `@IMG1` on a paid FLUX 3 / Ideogram 4 run silently reaches and bills the provider instead of refusing like the main prompt.

findings.function: beforeCall (with shell.js commands.onCall and assistant/index.js runCall)
findings.claim: Every non-read assistant tool call carries `meta.turn`, including `app`-scoped commands (`new_document`, `open_document`, `reopen_closed_tab`, `select_recipe`, `set_node_params`, `set_brush`) and `activate_document`. Because `args.doc` is undefined on `app`-scoped calls, `beforeCall(meta, undefined)` falls back to `host.editor` (the currently active tab), cloning an untouched tab's tiles into `record.docs`, wiping out the previous turn's undo snapshot on non-document changes, and making 'Undo this turn' revert a tab the assistant never modified.
findings.scenario: (1) Turn 1 edits Tab 1 (`doc 1`); 'Undo this turn' holds Tab 1's pre-Turn-1 snapshot. In Turn 2 the user asks 'Switch the recipe to FLUX 3 Image' (`select_recipe`, `scope: 'app'`). `beforeCall(meta, undefined)` sees `record.turn !== meta.turn`, releases Turn 1's snapshot (`assistant_turns.js:47`), and snapshots Tab 1's post-Turn-1 state; Turn 1 can no longer be undone as a turn, and 'Undo this turn' is now offered as a no-op on Tab 1. (2) Tab 1 holds the user's open photo. User asks 'Open `other.scumble` and add a levels filter': Call 1 (`open_document`, `scope: 'app'`, `args.doc === undefined`) runs `beforeCall` before opening Tab 2, snapshotting Tab 1 (`host.editor`) into `record.docs` (`turn.docs` in `assistant/index.js:859` also adds `turn.pin = 1`), and Call 2 snapshots Tab 2. If the user flips Tab 1 via `Image > Flip Horizontal` (menu command, no DOM event on `ed.root`, so `edited` stays `false`) and clicks 'Undo this turn (2 documents)' to undo the assistant's work on `other.scumble`, `restoreTurn` silently reverts Tab 1 as well.
findings.evidence:
electron/main/assistant/index.js:135-145 `metaFor`: sets `turn: read ? undefined : (turn && turn.id)` for every tool not in `policy.READS`.
electron/main/assistant/index.js:792-798, 859: `const takesDoc = !!props.doc; ... const doc = args.doc !== undefined ? args.doc : turn.pin;` and `if (!policy.READS.has(name) && doc !== undefined && doc !== null) turn.docs.add(doc);` (adds `turn.pin` even when `!takesDoc` or `name === "activate_document"`).
renderer/shell.js:1453-1457: `if (meta && meta.turn) { snapshotTurn(meta, args && args.doc); ... }`.
renderer/assistant_turns.js:42-55 `beforeCall`: `const ed = editor(docId);` -> `renderer/assistant_wait.js:17-20` `if (docId == null || docId === "") return host.editor || null;`, then line 47 `if (record && record.turn !== meta.turn) { release(record); record = null; }` and lines 51-53 `const snap = ed.turnSnapshot(); ... record.docs.set(id, { snap, edited: false });`.
findings.fix: Only record a turn snapshot (and only add `doc` to `turn.docs`) for document-mutating commands: in `electron/main/assistant/index.js` gate `meta.turn` (for `snapshotTurn`) and `turn.docs.add(doc)` on `takesDoc && name !== "activate_document"`, and in `renderer/shell.js:1453` skip `snapshotTurn` when the command's `scope === "app"` or `name === "activate_document"`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc by tracing the full assistant tool-call path from main to the renderer.

In `electron/main/assistant/index.js:135-145`, `metaFor(command)` checks only `const read = policy.READS.has(name)` (`electron/main/assistant/policy.js:14-20`) and sets `turn: read ? undefined : (turn && turn.id)` on every non-read tool call. In `runCall` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:791-798, 859`), `takesDoc = !!props.doc` is false for `scope: "app"` commands because `describe()` (`renderer/commands_util.js:960`) omits `doc` from their schema (`new_document` at `commands_docs.js:35`, `open_document` at `commands_docs.js:64`, `reopen_closed_tab` at `commands_docs.js:87`, `select_recipe` at `commands_docs.js:141`, and `set_node_params` at `commands_gen.js:81`), so `args.doc` stays `undefined`, `const doc = args.doc !== undefined ? args.doc : turn.pin` falls back to `turn.pin`, and line 859 still adds `turn.pin` to `turn.docs` (`activate_document` at `commands_docs.js:39-43` and `cancel_run` at `commands_runs.js:444-447` likewise carry `meta.turn` and record `doc` without mutating document state). Note three minor citation details in the report that do not affect the bug: the bridge listener in `renderer/shell.js:1435` is `commands.onRequest` (not `commands.onCall`), `editorOf` in `renderer/assistant_wait.js` is at lines 31-36 (not 17-20), and `set_brush` (`renderer/commands_depth.js:207`) is actually `"doc"`-scoped rather than `scope: "app"` (though `turnSnapshot` does not capture brush state or imported tip `spacing` either).

In `renderer/shell.js:1453-1457` (importing `beforeCall as snapshotTurn` at line 10), `if (meta && meta.turn) snapshotTurn(meta, args && args.doc)` runs unconditionally before `commands.call`. Inside `beforeCall(meta, docId)` (`renderer/assistant_turns.js:42-55`), line 44 calls `editor(docId)` -> `editorOf(docId)` (`renderer/assistant_wait.js:31-36`), which returns `host.editor || null` whenever `docId` is `undefined`. Line 47 (`if (record && record.turn !== meta.turn) { release(record); record = null; }`) immediately destroys the previous turn's snapshot record (even if the active tab is empty and `ed.turnSnapshot()` at line 51 returns `null`), and when the active tab holds an image on the tile backend, lines 51-53 clone its tiles into `record.docs`.

Both scenarios hold: (1) After Turn 1 edits Tab 1, a Turn 2 call such as `select_recipe` or `new_document` releases Turn 1's snapshot at `assistant_turns.js:47` (disabling Turn 1's undo card at `renderer/assistant.js:659-662`), snapshots Tab 1's post-Turn-1 state, and renders a misleading `"Undo this turn"` card for `document 1` (`renderer/assistant.js:577, 637-654`) that neither reverts `host.recipe` / `host.nodeParams` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:725`) nor undoes Turn 1. (2) When Tab 1 has a loaded image (`!reuse` at `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:293`) and a turn runs `open_document` (opening Tab 2) followed by `add_filter` on Tab 2, `open_document`'s `beforeCall(meta, undefined)` snapshots untouched Tab 1 alongside Tab 2 (`documents 1, 2`). Switching back to Tab 1 via `#shell-tab-list` (outside `ed.root`) and running a native menu edit like `Image > Flip Horizontal` (`renderer/shell.js:1390-1393`) fires no trusted DOM event inside `ed.root`, so `watchUserEdits` (`renderer/assistant_turns.js:137-149`) leaves `edited: false` and clicking `"Undo this turn"` reverts Tab 1 without warning.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: not known. `assistant-glb/undo-card-wrong-turn` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` concerned `undoCard()` not checking `state.turn === e.turn` on read-only turns and replayed chats (fixed at `renderer/assistant.js:641, 732` and `renderer/assistant_turns.js:77`); this is a distinct defect where non-read non-document commands actively overwrite `record` with `state.turn === e.turn` for an untouched tab. Severity is `should` (not `must`): `ed.restoreTurn` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:274-275`) pushes the current state onto Tab 1's undo stack before applying the snapshot so `Ctrl+Z` can recover reverted pixels, and Turn 1's individual layer/pixel steps remain on `ed.undo`, making this a plausible workflow bug with a workaround rather than permanent data loss.

findings.function: add (with plugins/sample/main.js selectionToLayer and renderer/plugins.js Document.addLayer)
findings.claim: Adding an AI label (`ailabel.add` via the AI label panel, `Layer > Add AI Label`, or MCP) or running `Plugins > Sample plugin > Selection to new layer` (`selectionToLayer`) calls `doc.addLayer(...)`, which delegates to `editor.addLayer(...)` without pushing an undo step (and without clearing redo). Pressing Ctrl+Z right after adding the layer either reports 'Nothing to undo.' or undoes the user's previous unrelated edit while leaving the newly added layer on the canvas.
findings.scenario: Open an image, paint a brush stroke on a paint layer, then click 'Add label' in the AI label panel (or `Layer > Add AI Label`, with no prior AI label on the document). `'AI label'` is added on top of the layer stack. Press Ctrl+Z expecting to remove `'AI label'`: because `doc.addLayer` pushed no undo step, Ctrl+Z undoes the earlier brush stroke instead and leaves `'AI label'` on the image. Similarly, selecting a region and running `Plugins > Sample plugin > Selection to new layer` adds `'Selection copy'` with no undo step, so Ctrl+Z undoes the selection instead of removing `'Selection copy'`. (When `ailabel.add` replaces an existing label, `remove_layer` pushes a `'Delete layer'` step before `doc.addLayer`, mislabelling the replace in Undo history.)
findings.evidence:
plugins/ailabel/main.js:101-105: `const old = find(doc); if (old) await doc.run("remove_layer", { layer: old.id }); const layer = doc.addLayer(canvas, { name: LAYER_NAME, x, y }); if (o.opacity < 100) await doc.run("set_layer", { layer: layer.id, opacity: o.opacity / 100 });`
plugins/sample/main.js:87: `const layer = doc.addLayer(out, { name: "Selection copy", x, y });`
renderer/plugins.js:162-175 `Document.addLayer`: calls `this.editor.addLayer(...)` with no `pushUndo` (unlike `Document.setPixels` at line 146).
renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:539 `addLayer`: `this.historyGen++;   // no undo step here (a caller that lands a layer pushes its own)`.
renderer/commands_layers.js:39 `set_layer` (`opacity`): sets `l.opacity` with no `pushUndo`.
findings.fix: Have `Document.addLayer` (`renderer/plugins.js:162`) push a `'layers'` undo step by default (`{ undo = true }` -> `if (undo) this.editor.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: typeof undo === "string" ? undo : (name ? \`Add ${name}\` : "Add layer") })`), and in `plugins/ailabel/main.js` when `old` is present either replace `old` in one `'layers'` undo step (passing `undo: false` to `addLayer` after `remove_layer`, or updating in place) so adding or replacing an AI label is always a single undo step.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc across plugins/ailabel/main.js, plugins/sample/main.js, renderer/plugins.js, renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js, and plugins/glb/main.js.

In renderer/plugins.js:162-175, Document.addLayer delegates directly to this.editor.addLayer(...) without pushing an undo snapshot (contrary to docs/PLUGINS.md:93 'every write is one undo step' and unlike Document.setPixels at renderer/plugins.js:139-146, which takes { undo = true } and calls this.editor.pushUndo). In renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:523-554, editor.addLayer intentionally bumps only this.historyGen at line 539 ('no undo step here (a caller that lands a layer pushes its own)') and neither pushes onto this.undo nor clears this.redo.

Tracing both callers confirms there is no outer undo wrapper on any entry path:
1. plugins/ailabel/main.js:92-108 (add): when find(doc) returns null (first AI label on the document), line 103 calls doc.addLayer(canvas, { name: LAYER_NAME, x, y }) and line 104 optionally runs set_layer with opacity (renderer/commands_layers.js:39, a soft property write with no pushUndo). This is reached from the AI label panel's 'Add label' button (line 158), the Plugins menu action 'Add AI label' (line 165 -> electron/main/main.js:734-736 -> renderer/shell.js:1422 -> plugins.runAction; note the candidate's prose slightly misnames the menu as 'Layer > Add AI Label' instead of 'Plugins > Add AI label'), and MCP/command core 'ailabel.add' (lines 169-184; ailabel_add is in EXCLUDED in electron/main/assistant/policy.js:11 and absent from undoStep at lines 555-580). With no undo step recorded, pressing Ctrl+Z right after adding the label either says 'Nothing to undo.' or undoes the user's prior edit (e.g. a brush stroke) while leaving 'AI label' on the canvas. When replacing an existing label (old != null at line 101), doc.run('remove_layer', ...) calls ed.removeLayer (inpaint_ed_layers.js:572), which pushes a 'layers' step before doc.addLayer so Ctrl+Z does revert the replacement, but mislabels the history entry as 'Delete layer'.
2. plugins/sample/main.js:76-90 (selectionToLayer, registered at line 94 as Plugins > Selection to new layer): line 87 calls doc.addLayer(out, { name: 'Selection copy', x, y }) with no undo step, so Ctrl+Z undoes the selection (or earlier edit) instead of removing 'Selection copy'.

Important caller interaction for the fix: plugins/glb/main.js:176-190 (place) already pushes its own single 'layers' undo step (carrying plugin data via data: scumble.id) before calling doc.addLayer at line 207 (new 3D object/mannequin) and line 219 (new depth/pose control layers, also reachable during glb.edit). Therefore, if Document.addLayer in renderer/plugins.js:162 is updated to push a 'layers' step by default ({ undo = true }), plugins/glb/main.js:207 and :219 must pass undo: false to avoid double- or triple-pushing undo steps.

Not known: docs/BUGS.md, review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json, review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json, and PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md have no entry for this. review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json had assistant-glb/glb-place-no-undo (plugins/glb/main.js:147), which noted in passing that Document.addLayer pushes no step, but that finding was scoped to glb.place and was fixed solely inside plugins/glb/main.js:162-190, leaving Document.addLayer, ailabel.add, and sample.selection_layer unfixed.

Severity is 'should': users hit this in normal UI/MCP workflows when adding an AI label or running Selection to new layer and pressing Ctrl+Z, unexpectedly reverting an earlier edit; a workaround exists (delete the added layer manually and Ctrl+Y the undone edit).

findings.claim: clipTargetOf skips the group boundary check on reference layers (`role === "reference"`) without continuing past them, so a clipped layer sitting immediately above a hidden-from-list reference layer binds its clip base to the reference layer instead of the visible layer below. On screen this clips the layer to the reference's small preview box (even across group boundaries), while every run/export walk (`forRun: true`) omits reference layers and therefore silently drops the clipped layer from all exports, Flatten, ComfyUI composite uploads, and paid-provider crops.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a picture on the base layer, add a pixel layer B and paint visible strokes across the canvas.
2. Import a reference image (`addReferenceFile`): because no picture layers sit above B, `addLayer` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:541-543`) sees `lowest === -1` and appends Ref at the top (`layers = [B, Ref]`). `renderLayers` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:701`) hides Ref from the Layers list.
3. Add a new pixel layer C (`layers = [B, Ref, C]`), paint on C over B, and clip C (`Ctrl+Alt+G`, layer context menu, or Alt+click between C and B in the Layers panel).
4. In the viewport (`forRun: false`), C disappears everywhere except over Ref's small corner thumbnail box at `(16, 16)`. Export PNG/JPG/WebP/TIFF/ORA, click Flatten, or click Generate on a paid provider (`forRun: true`): C is completely omitted from the exported file, flattened base, and paid run crop, even though B is visible and C appears clipped directly to B in the Layers panel.
findings.evidence:
In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:105-115`:
`clipTargetOf(layer, i = this.layers.indexOf(layer)) { ... for (let j = i - 1; j >= 0; j--) { const b = this.layers[j]; if (b.clip) continue; if (!this.isReference(b) && (b.group || null) !== (layer.group || null)) return null; return b; } }`
When `b` is a reference layer (`this.isReference(b) === true`), `!this.isReference(b)` is false so line 111 does not return null, and line 112 immediately returns `b` (the reference layer), which `clipBaseOf` (`line 125-126`) returns unchanged because `b.kind !== "filter"`. Note that `normalizeGroups` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:211`: `if (this.isReference(l)) { l.group = null; continue; }`) also permits a reference layer to sit inside a group's run of layers while carrying `group: null`.
Then in every `forRun: true` walk:
- `drawLayersInto` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:74-75, 86`): for Ref, `if (forRun && (ctrl || this.isReference(layer))) continue;` skips `drawn.add(Ref)`; for C, `const cb = controlOnly ? null : this.clipBaseOf(layer, i); if (cb && !drawn.has(cb)) continue;` skips C.
- `stackPlan` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:164-166, 183`): for Ref, `if (forRun && (this.isControl(l) || this.isReference(l))) continue;` never adds Ref to `entryOf`; for C, `const cb = this.clipBaseOf(l, i); const clip = cb ? entryOf.get(cb) : null; if (cb && !clip) continue;` drops C from every banded export, `flattenNow`, and `holdRunStack` / `readBoxBytes` crop.
- In PSD export (`inpaint_ed_export.js:89, 132`), Ref is emitted with `hidden: true` and C immediately above it gets `clip: true`, clipping C to the hidden `(reference)` layer in external editors.
findings.fix: In `clipTargetOf` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:109`), skip reference layers before the group check: `if (b.clip || this.isReference(b)) continue;`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:105-115`. `clipTargetOf` walks downward (`for (let j = i - 1; j >= 0; j--)`) and skips clipped layers (`if (b.clip) continue;` at line 109), then checks `if (!this.isReference(b) && (b.group || null) !== (layer.group || null)) return null;` at line 111 before executing `return b;` at line 112. When `b` is a reference layer (`this.isReference(b)` is true), `!this.isReference(b)` evaluates to false, so line 111 neither returns `null` nor `continue`s past `b`; line 112 immediately returns the reference layer `b`, and `clipBaseOf` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:124-127`) returns `b` unchanged because `b.kind !== "filter"`. Meanwhile, `addLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:541-543`) appends the first reference layer to the top of `this.layers` (`lowest === -1`), so adding pixel layer `B`, importing a reference `Ref`, and adding layer `C` (paint, paste, filter, or a landed `Result`) produces `this.layers = [B, Ref, C]`. Because `renderLayers` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:701`) hides reference layers from `this.layerList` (rendering them separately in `renderReferences` at `1051-1147`), `C` sits visually directly above `B` in the Layers panel. Alt+clicking the boundary between `C` and `B` (`clipEdgeLayer` / `clipEdgeClick`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:485-500`) or pressing `Ctrl+Alt+G` (`setLayerClip`, `458-478` — which refuses clipping a reference layer itself at `464-465` as "not part of the picture") binds `C`'s clip base to the hidden-from-list `Ref` instead of `B`.

The bug also breaks group clipping invariants in two ways. Because `normalizeGroups` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:211`) treats reference layers as group-transparent (`if (this.isReference(l)) { if (l.group) { l.group = null; changed = true; } continue; }`), a reference layer can sit inside a group's contiguous run `[A(G1), Ref(null), C(G1)]` or immediately below a group `[B(null), Ref(null), C(G1)]`. In `[A(G1), Ref(null), C(G1)]`, clipping `C` hits `Ref` instead of group-mate `A`. In `[B(null), Ref(null), C(G1)]`, `C` is the bottom layer of `G1` (which `docs/MANUAL.md:336` and `tools/groups_test.py:159-160` require to have `clipBaseOf === null`, drawn unclipped), yet line 111 bypasses the group-boundary `return null` check for `Ref` and clips `C` out of `G1` onto `Ref`. Worse, in PSD export (`psdSections` / `exportLayerStack` / `exportLayerSources`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_export.js:47, 89, 132`), `sec.at(Ref)` emits nothing before `Ref`, `sec.at(C)` emits `G1`'s bounding divider (`section: 3`, `</Layer group>`), and `C` is written with `clip: true` directly above that group divider.

Tracing all composite walks confirms the downstream behaviour. Although an old 0.1.35 build note (`docs/PLAN_0_1_31.md:910` and the comment at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:110, 120-122`) assumed "a reference is not drawn", reference layers ARE drawn on screen (`forRun: false`) at their cascaded 1/3-canvas preview box (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:95-108`) in both `glViewComposite` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_display.js:334-357`) and `drawLayersInto` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:74-93`). Thus on screen, `C` disappears everywhere over `B` except inside `Ref`'s cyan-framed `img1` box (or disappears completely if `Ref` is hidden). Then every `forRun: true` walk — `drawLayersInto` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:74-75, 86`), `stackPlan` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:164-166, 183`), and `passStores` (`838-839, 851`) — skips `Ref` before recording it in `drawn` / `entryOf`, causing `if (cb && !drawn.has(cb)) continue` / `if (cb && !clip) continue` to omit `C` completely from PNG/JPG/WebP/TIFF exports, `flattenNow` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:756, 770, 782`), ComfyUI `uploadComposite`, and paid-provider crops (`holdRunStack` / `readBoxBytes`, `inpaint_ed_stack.js:745-782`), while PSD clips `C` to the hidden `(reference)` layer and ORA exports `C` visible and unclipped in the layer stack while omitting it from `mergedimage.png`.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Open`), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: this defect is not listed in any open bug or prior review. Severity is calibrated from `must` down to `should`: as soon as the user clips `C`, the viewport already looks visibly wrong (strokes on `C` over `B` immediately vanish everywhere outside `Ref`'s cyan-bordered `img1` reference overlay box, or vanish completely when `Ref` is hidden; the status bar at `inpaint_ed_masks.js:475` and clip badge tooltip at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:761` name `Ref`; and `B` lacks the `ipc-clipbase` underline at `720`), so exports and paid runs do not silently diverge from a plausible-looking picture on screen, `flattenNow` keeps a `canvas` undo snapshot, and dragging `C` onto `B` in the Layers panel (`dropInLayers`, `inpaint_ed_composite.js:394-396`) reorders `[B, C, Ref]` as a straightforward workaround.

findings.claim: Dragging a corner of a polygon control point shallow-copies each point object (`{ ...q }`) and mutates `pt.pts[idx]` in place before `doc.setFilterParams(..., { preview: true })` takes its undo snapshot. Because `snapshotLayer` and `snapshotOf("filter")` only shallow-copy `layer.params`, the drag overwrites the corner coordinates directly inside the live layer and inside `_undoPending` (as well as any earlier `filter`, `layers`, `canvas`, or `turn` snapshots sharing `params.points`). Pressing Ctrl+Z after dragging a polygon corner fails to restore the pre-drag corner.
findings.scenario: Create a polygon control point with corners `[[100, 100], [200, 100], [150, 200]]` on a `Control points` (`film.points`) layer using the Control points tool. Drag corner 0 to `[350, 320]` and release. Press Ctrl+Z to undo: `applySnapshot` restores `_undoPending`, whose `params.points[0].pts[0]` was mutated in place to `[350, 320]` before `_undoPending` was captured and on every subsequent pointer move, so the polygon corner stays at `[350, 320]` instead of returning to `[100, 100]`.
findings.evidence: `plugins/film/points.js:337` copies points with `const points = (layer.params.points || []).map((q) => ({ ...q }));`, leaving `q.pts` aliased to `layer.params.points[i].pts`. Lines 381-385 then execute `if (pt.shape === "polygon" && Array.isArray(pt.pts) && pt.pts[idx]) { pt.pts[idx] = [Math.round(ev.x), Math.round(ev.y)]; }` before line 402 calls `doc.setFilterParams(layer.id, { points }, { preview: true })`. In `renderer/plugins.js:223`, `if (!l._undoPending) l._undoPending = ed.snapshot({ kind: "filter", id: l.id });` runs `snapshotOf` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:449`: `params: { ...(layer.params || {}) }`), which captures the already-mutated `pts` array and shares that array across all subsequent `onMove` writes.
findings.fix: Clone `pts` before mutating a corner in `plugins/film/points.js:383-385` (`pt.pts = pt.pts.map((v, i) => i === idx ? [Math.round(ev.x), Math.round(ev.y)] : [v[0], v[1]]);` or clone `pts` inside the `.map((q) => ({ ...q, pts: Array.isArray(q.pts) ? q.pts.map((v) => [v[0], v[1]]) : undefined }))` helper), and deep-clone `params.points` / `params.curves` alongside `params.lights` in `snapshotLayer`, `snapshotOf("filter")`, and `committedFilter`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc across the full pointer-to-history call path. When pressing on a polygon control point's vertex handle, hitTest -> hitShape (plugins/film/shapes.js:635-640) returns 'corner_' + i, and tool.onDown (plugins/film/points.js:256-280) records drag = { mode: 'corner_' + i, orig: { ..., pts: h.pt.pts.map(...) }, changed: false } and returns without calling setFilterParams, so layer._undoPending remains unset.

On the first pointer move, tool.onMove (plugins/film/points.js:337) shallow-copies the point objects via const points = (layer.params.points || []).map((q) => ({ ...q })), which leaves pt.pts aliased to the live layer.params.points[k].pts array (unlike drag.mode === 'move' at lines 344-346, which maps drag.orig.pts into a fresh array). Lines 381-385 then execute pt.pts[idx] = [Math.round(ev.x), Math.round(ev.y)] in place before line 402 calls doc.setFilterParams(layer.id, { points }, { preview: true }). Inside Document.prototype.setFilterParams (renderer/plugins.js:223), l._undoPending = ed.snapshot({ kind: 'filter', id: l.id }) runs after the live pts array has already been overwritten. Moreover, HistoryPart.snapshotOf for kind === 'filter' (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:448-450), snapshotLayer (lines 183-188), applySnapshot (lines 842-845), cancelFilterParams (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:1081), and committedFilter (lines 1120-1121) only deep-clone params.lights, leaving params.points and each point's pts array shared by reference. Every subsequent onMove and the final onUp commit (points.js:419-424) continue mutating that same pts array in place inside _undoPending (as well as inside any earlier filter, layers, canvas, or turn snapshots that held the same point's pts reference, such as slider edits in buildControl at points.js:697). Pressing Ctrl+Z pops the 'Filter settings' step and runs applySnapshot, which restores _undoPending whose pts[idx] already holds the post-drag coordinates, so the corner never moves back.

Checked scratch/known_index.md, docs/BUGS.md, docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, and all three verified.json files (2026-11-07 full/external and 2026-11-12 full); this defect is not recorded in any known list. Severity 'should' holds: 100% reproducible broken undo on a standard interactive tool handle (dragging any polygon control-point corner), with manual repositioning as a workaround and no silent loss of raster layer pixels or paid runs.

findings.claim: When committing a filter option from the hover-preview flyout (`openChoiceList`), `applyChoice` looks up the layer row with `.ipc-layer[data-id="..."]`, but `renderLayers` sets `data-layer`, never `data-id`. For any `select` parameter that is neither `preset` nor referenced in another parameter's `when` guard, `row` is always `null`, so the `<select>` control in the layer panel is never updated to the chosen value and can no longer re-select the stale option it still displays.
findings.scenario: Add a `Glass` (`effects.glass`), `Chromatic shift` (`effects.chromatic_shift`), `Gradient fill` (`gradient`), `Normalise` (`normalise`), `Glow / Orton` (`film.glow`), `Cross processing` (`film.cross_process`), `Light leak` (`film.light_leak`), `Frame` (`film.frame`), or `Black & white film` (`film.bw`) layer. Click the list-preview button next to `Style` (e.g. `Ribbed` on Glass) or `Shape` (`Linear` on Gradient fill) and click `Frosted` (or `Radial`) in the flyout. The picture updates to `Frosted`, but the layer's `Style` `<select>` still displays `Ribbed`; subsequently choosing `Ribbed` from that `<select>` fires no `change` event because `sel.value` is already `"ribbed"`.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:710` stamps layer rows with `row.dataset.layer = layer.id;` (queried elsewhere at line 198 as `.ipc-layer[data-layer="${layer.id}"]`). In `applyChoice` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:1175-1183`), the `else` branch for non-`preset`, non-`when` parameters runs `const row = this.root && this.root.querySelector(\`.ipc-layer[data-id="${layer.id}"]\`);`, which always evaluates to `null`, skipping `sel.value = choice.id`.
findings.fix: Change `.ipc-layer[data-id="${layer.id}"]` to `.ipc-layer[data-layer="${CSS.escape(layer.id)}"]` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:1178`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js and renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js. In renderLayers() (inpaint_ed_layers.js:709-710) and renderReferences() (line 1067-1068), every .ipc-layer DOM row stamps its layer identifier on dataset.layer (`row.dataset.layer = layer.id;`), which other in-place helpers query as `.ipc-layer[data-layer="..."]` (lines 197 and 213). Nowhere in the codebase is `data-id` set on `.ipc-layer` (only the flyout's own `.ipc-choice-item` buttons set `data-id` at line 1297).

findings.claim: `applyFilterLayer` skips every `kind === "filter"` layer whenever a visible layer below it is being painted, moved, or has a pending transform, so stale cached filter outputs do not hide live edits. Because `Colour fill` (`fill`) and `Gradient fill` (`gradient`) are stored as `kind: "filter"` (`def.over === true`) even though they never read the composite below, any brush stroke or transform on a lower layer causes all fill layers above it—including fill layers clipped to the layer being painted or moved—to disappear for the duration of the gesture.
findings.scenario: Create a paint layer, clip a `Colour fill` or `Gradient fill` layer to it (or place a semi-transparent `Gradient fill` vignette/tint above it), and paint a brush stroke on or drag/transform the paint layer below. On the first pointer press/move (`this.pointer.layer` or `this.pending.layer` set to the lower layer), the Colour fill or Gradient fill completely vanishes from the canvas until the stroke ends or the transform is committed/cancelled.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1472-1477`: `const gestureLayer = (p && p.layer) || (this.pending && this.pending.layer) || null; if (gestureLayer && gestureLayer !== layer && this.shown(gestureLayer)) { const gi = this.layers.indexOf(gestureLayer); if (gi >= 0 && gi < index) return chain; }`. `isFillLayer(layer)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:211`, checking `FILTERS[layer.filter].over`) is true for `fill` and `gradient` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:1264, 1277`), whose `apply` functions (`fillApply`, `gradientApply`) never sample `src`, yet line 1474 does not exclude `this.isFillLayer(layer)`.
findings.fix: Guard the early return at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1474` with `!this.isFillLayer(layer)` so fill layers continue rendering over live strokes and pending transforms below them.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc. In `FiltersPart.applyFilterLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1467-1478`), when `!forRun`, lines 1471-1477 compute `const gestureLayer = (p && p.layer) || (this.pending && this.pending.layer) || null;` and execute `if (gestureLayer && gestureLayer !== layer && this.shown(gestureLayer)) { const gi = this.layers.indexOf(gestureLayer); if (gi >= 0 && gi < index) return chain; }`. Both `Colour fill` (`fill`) and `Gradient fill` (`gradient`) are created in `addFilterLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:322-325`) with `kind: "filter"` and defined in `FILTERS` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:1354-1382`) with `over: true`, which `isFillLayer` tests (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:597-599`; note the candidate's evidence cited stale line numbers `inpaint_ed_layers.js:211` and `inpaint_filters.js:1264, 1277`, while the primary `file` and `line` 1474 are exact). Although `applyFilterLayer` already special-cases `this.isFillLayer(layer)` at lines 1487 (`plain = ... && !this.isFillLayer(layer)`), 1492, 1506, and 1584, line 1474 does not exclude `!this.isFillLayer(layer)`.

Tracing the full screen-draw call path confirms no WebGL compositor path or cache guard prevents this. Every screen redraw runs `draw()` (`inpaint_ed_draw.js:125`) -> `drawScene()` (`inpaint_ed_relight.js:611`, invalidated by `sceneSignature()` at lines 593-609 on `p`, `q`, `pixelVersion`, or `l.x/y/w/h`) -> `drawSceneImage()` (`inpaint_ed_relight.js:685`) -> `drawViewComposite()` (`inpaint_ed_display.js:382`). In `drawViewComposite`, `glCompositeUsable(opts)` (`inpaint_ed_display.js:271-285`) returns `false` for three independent reasons here: `if (this.pending) return false;` (line 275), `if (this.pointer && this.pointer.layer) return false;` (line 276), and `if (l.kind === "filter") return false;` for any shown filter/fill layer (line 279). Thus `glViewComposite` is never used; execution always takes the Canvas 2D region pass (`inpaint_ed_display.js:410-419`), calling `drawComposite` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:25-31`) -> `drawLayersInto` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:46, 80-82`) -> `applyFilterLayer` with `forRun = false` (the node thumbnail in `drawThumb` at `inpaint_ed_chrome.js:75` does the same). Whenever the user paints, erases, clones/heals, smudges/tones, liquifies, or single-layer moves/scales a visible lower layer (`this.pointer.layer` set at `inpaint_ed_pointer.js:499, 529, 554, 568, 587, 599, 631, 633, 644`), or enters a pending Rotate/Distort/Warp transform on a lower layer (`this.pending.layer` set at `inpaint_ed_geometry.js:34, 44` even while idle between drags), `gi >= 0 && gi < index` holds and every Colour fill and Gradient fill layer above it returns `chain` (`null` after `flushFilterChain` at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:87`) without drawing.

Unlike backdrop-filtering layers—whose `_fcacheView` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:843-845`, keyed on `this.compositeVersion` which does not advance mid-stroke or mid-drag) holds pre-gesture backdrop pixels that would obscure live edits—`fillApply` (`inpaint_filters.js:618-632`) never samples `src` pixels, `plain` is always `false` for fill layers (line 1487), any depth `limitStage` on a fill layer writes `over = true` (`vec4(c.rgb, c.a * w)` at `inpaint_limit.js:41, 69`), and `clipCoverage` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:466-489` -> `drawLayer` lines 493-539) already renders live strokes, dragged coordinates, and pending transform meshes of a clipping base. Guarding line 1474 with `!this.isFillLayer(layer)` also preserves GPU filter chaining when painting on a `Deep paint` (`surface`) layer below a fill layer, because line 1519 flushes any incoming `chain` before compositing the fill.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (lines 1-698), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`: not previously known or planned (the only fill-layer entry in `BUGS.md:115` concerns PSD/ORA depth-limit edge-snap guide sampling). Severity is `should`: exports, runs, and flatten pass `forRun: true` so saved/exported pixels are unharmed (not `must`), but in normal interactive workflows—painting or moving layers beneath a fill tint/vignette, or painting/moving/rotating/warping a layer that has a Colour fill or Gradient fill clipped to it—all fill layers above vanish for every stroke and for the entire duration of a pending Rotate/Distort/Warp until committed.

findings.claim: In-progress polygon control-point state (`drawing`) is stored in a module-global variable without a `docId`, and `points.tool` sets `drawAlways: true` with no `onDeselect` cleanup. Switching tools mid-polygon leaves the yellow polygon rubber-band drawn over the image with `Escape` unable to cancel it, and switching document tabs draws the first tab's unfinished polygon onto the second tab and commits those vertices onto the second tab's layer if clicked.
findings.scenario: Select the Control points tool (`film.point`) with shape `Polygon` in Tab A and click two vertices on the canvas (`drawing.pts` has 2 points). Press `B` to switch to the Brush tool: the yellow polygon outline and rubber-band stay drawn over the canvas, and pressing `Escape` does not clear them because `pluginKey` only dispatches to the active tool. Or switch to Tab B: Tab A's unfinished polygon is drawn on Tab B, and clicking with the Control points tool in Tab B appends to and closes Tab A's vertices onto Tab B's `Control points` layer.
findings.evidence: `plugins/film/points.js:106` declares module-global `let drawing = null;` with no `docId` field (unlike `drag` on line 105). Line 213 sets `drawAlways: true` on `tool`, and `tool` defines no `onDeselect` method (`renderer/plugins.js:638` calls `prev.onDeselect` when switching tools). `renderer/plugins.js:603-610` (`drawOverlays`) invokes `t.draw` on every tab redraw whenever `t.drawAlways` is true, and `plugins/film/points.js:496-521` renders `if (drawing && drawing.pts.length > 0)` unconditionally. Meanwhile `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:331` routes `Escape` to `host.pluginKey(this, e, "escape")`, which in `renderer/plugins.js:617` checks `const t = toolReg(ed.tool);` and ignores inactive tools.
findings.fix: Store `docId: doc.id` on `drawing`, clear `drawing = null` (and `drag = null`) in an `onDeselect(doc)` handler on `points.tool`, and guard both `onDown`/`onMove`/`onKey` and `draw` on `drawing.docId === doc.id && doc.editor.tool === TOOL_ID` (resetting `drawing` if `doc.id` changed).
findings.why:
At `plugins/film/points.js:106`, `makePoints(scumble)` (instantiated once for the whole plugin at `plugins/film/main.js:23`) stores in-progress polygon control-point state in a single plugin-wide closure variable `let drawing = null;` with shape `{ pts, lastClickTime, lastClickPos, cursor? }` and no `docId` (unlike `drag` on line 105, which carries `docId`). `points.reset` (`plugins/film/points.js:880-883`) is never wired to any `tool`, `activate`, or `removed` event in `plugins/film/main.js`, and `points.tool` (`plugins/film/points.js:206-630`) sets `drawAlways: true` at line 213 without defining `onDeselect`.

Tracing both scenarios confirms no guard prevents either leak:
1. Tool switch in the same tab: clicking inside the canvas with `film.point` (`U`) and `newShape === "polygon"` sets `drawing` at `plugins/film/points.js:284-293` (and appends corners at lines 243-249). Switching to another tool (e.g. `B`, `P`, `H`) calls `PointerPart.setTool` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:37-82`), which clears built-in `this.polyPoints` / `this.shapePoints` (lines 39-40) and emits `host.toolChanged` (line 47) -> `toolChanged` (`renderer/plugins.js:636-643`). Line 638 checks `if (was.reg.def.onDeselect)`, which is undefined on `points.tool`, leaving `drawing` intact. On every subsequent redraw, `ViewPart.drawOverlays` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_view.js:692, 698`) -> `overlay` (`renderer/plugins.js:601-612`) invokes `points.tool.draw` with `view.active === false` because `reg.def.drawAlways` is `true` (line 605). Inside `points.tool.draw` (`plugins/film/points.js:490-520`), the `if (drawing && Array.isArray(drawing.pts) && drawing.pts.length)` block at lines 496-517 runs before the `if (!layer || !layer.visible) return;` and `if (!view.active && activeLayer !== layer) return;` guards at lines 519-520, keeping the yellow/red polygon overlay drawn over the canvas. Pressing `Escape` hits `InpaintEditor._docKey` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:331`) -> `host.pluginKey(this, e, "escape")` -> `key` (`renderer/plugins.js:615-621`), where `const active = toolReg(ed.tool)` (line 617) returns `null` for any non-plugin tool (or another plugin's tool), falling through to `host.onEscape` (`renderer/editor/host_setup.js:100`: `"Nothing to cancel."`).
2. Tab switch / tab close: activating another tab (`HostStatePart.activate`, `renderer/editor/host_state.js:260-267`) or closing the original tab (`removeEditor`, lines 228-257) redraws the second editor through `overlay` -> `points.tool.draw`, rendering the first tab's `drawing.pts` onto the second tab regardless of its active tool or layers. If `film.point` is used in the second tab, `onDown` (`plugins/film/points.js:219-253`) and `onKey` (`Enter`, lines 451-468) enter `if (drawing != null)` and append to or commit the first tab's polygon vertices onto the second tab's `Control points` layer (`pointsLayer(doc, { create: true })` at lines 231 / 455).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`); no entry covers `plugins/film/points.js` or `drawing`. Severity is `should`: overlays do not corrupt exported pixels (so not `must`), and switching tools (e.g. `H` to pan or `B` to select) or tabs mid-polygon is a plausible normal workflow that deterministically leaves an un-cancellable overlay and cross-tab tool state hijack, with the non-obvious workaround of re-selecting `U` and pressing `Escape`.
