findings.claim: Above 27.9 MP, `relightWhole` refuses `detail: true` and instructs the user to turn off detail restoration (`detail: false`), yet the `detail: false` path still decodes the streamed composite back into a full-size `ImageBitmap` and allocates two synchronous full-document `W x H` 2D canvases (`cFull` and `finCanvas`), PNG-encodes all `W x H` pixels on the window, and reads them back into tiles. On a 15000x10000 (150 MP) picture this spikes ~1.8 GB across three full-size buffers and freezes the window for seconds; on an `editor.huge` (> 268 MP) tile document it has no size guard and fails after streaming the whole composite.
findings.scenario: Open a 15000x10000 (150 MP) photo (or a 20000x15000 = 300 MP PNG/TIFF on tiles), add a Relight layer, uncheck Detail from original (`detail: false`, as the > 27.9 MP refusal message instructs), pick Magnific / fal / Comfy Cloud / local ComfyUI, and click Relight whole picture. At 15000x10000, `encodeComposite` streams a 150 MP PNG, which `relightWhole` immediately decodes into a 600 MB `ImageBitmap` and draws into a 600 MB 15000x10000 canvas `cFull` solely to downsample `cSend` (2048x1365), even though `cFull` is never used when `detail === false`. After the provider returns a ~2048x1365 image, `relightWhole` allocates another 600 MB 15000x10000 canvas `finCanvas`, upscales on Canvas 2D, runs main-thread `finCanvas.toBlob` (`canvasBytes`), and copies 150 MP into tiles (`fromCanvas`). At 20000x15000 (> 268 MP), `encodeComposite` streams all 300 MP and `createImageBitmap(enc.blob)` then fails with a raw browser decode error (and `cFull` / `finCanvas` exceed `CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS`).
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/host_relight.js:63-65` guards only `if ((layer.params || {}).detail !== false && W * H > realism.MAX_AREA)` (`"Turn off detail restoration or scale the picture down first."`), with no `editor.huge` check. Lines `82-89`: `const enc = await editor.encodeComposite({ forRun: true, upTo }); if (enc) { picBytes = new Uint8Array(await enc.blob.arrayBuffer()); const bmp = await createImageBitmap(enc.blob); cFull = document.createElement("canvas"); cFull.width = W; cFull.height = H; cFull.getContext("2d").drawImage(bmp, 0, 0); bmp.close(); }`. Lines `108-115` draw `cFull` into `wSend x hSend` (`<= 2048`), and `cFull` is only read again inside `if (useDetail)` (`:258,266`). In the `else` branch (`detail === false`, `:310-320,339`), it creates `finCanvas = document.createElement("canvas"); finCanvas.width = W; finCanvas.height = H; ... fx.drawImage(img, 0, 0, W, H);`, calls `const lbytes = await canvasBytes(finCanvas);`, and calls `const px = editor.pixels.Layer.fromCanvas(finCanvas);` (contrast `realismPass` at `renderer/editor/host_pictures.js:239-249`, which keeps `px` at `ow x oh` and sets layer `w: lw, h: lh`).
findings.fix: When `detail === false`, obtain `cSend` (`wSend x hSend`) via `sampleRegionSettled` (or draw `bmp` directly to `cSend` when `!editor.huge` without allocating `cFull`), and land the `wAns x hAns` provider image directly as `editor.pixels.Layer.fromImage(img, wAns, hAns)` with layer bounds `x: 0, y: 0, w: W, h: H` and upload `out.bytes` directly without a full-size `finCanvas`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in renderer/editor/host_relight.js. Both entry points — the Relight panel's Render button (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:949) and the MCP relight command when route !== 'app' (renderer/commands_runs.js:373) — call host.relightWhole(editor, layer, ...). Prior awaits (ensureDepthMap at host_relight.js:29-31 -> computeDepthMap at inpaint_ed_depth.js:78-80,149 -> host.pictureInput at host_helpers.js:322-326 using sampleRegionSettled on tiles, and relightSettled at host_relight.js:61 on the <= 4096 depth grid) succeed without full-document canvases on both 15k and >268 MP tile documents. At host_relight.js:63-65, the only size check is `if ((layer.params || {}).detail !== false && W * H > realism.MAX_AREA)` (27,878,400 px in renderer/editor/realism.js:32), whose error message explicitly instructs the user: 'Turn off detail restoration or scale the picture down first' (and commands_runs.js:285 likewise documents `detail`: 'above 27.9 MP it has to be off'). There is no `editor.huge` / `canvasFits(W, H)` check.

When the user follows that instruction and sets `detail: false` on a 15,000 x 10,000 (150 MP) tile document, host_relight.js:82-89 still runs `await editor.encodeComposite({ forRun: true, upTo })` to stream a full 150 MP PNG, reads `enc.blob.arrayBuffer()` into `picBytes` (:84, immediately discarded at :115 because `wSend` x `hSend` is 2048 x 1365), decodes `enc.blob` into a 600 MB `ImageBitmap` (:85), and draws it into a 600 MB 15,000 x 10,000 DOM `<canvas>` `cFull` (:86-88). `cFull` is drawn into `cSend` at :108-115 and is never read again when `detail === false` (`cFull` is only touched inside `if (useDetail)` at :258,266), nor is `cFull` resized to 0, so it remains retained across the entire provider wait and landing. After the provider returns a ~2048 x 1365 image (:255), the `else` branch (:310-317) allocates a second 600 MB 15,000 x 10,000 DOM `<canvas>` `finCanvas` and upscales `img` onto it, runs `await canvasBytes(finCanvas)` (:320, `finCanvas.toBlob` PNG-encoding all 150 MP on the window in stitch.js:742 and uploading the 150 MP PNG instead of `out.bytes`), and calls `editor.pixels.Layer.fromCanvas(finCanvas)` (:339). On tiles, `TileLayerPixels.fromCanvas` -> `_readCanvas` (inpaint_tiles.js:825,2619-2633) synchronously runs 160 `ctx.getImageData` strip reads on the GPU-backed `finCanvas` on the main thread (blocking the window and tripping Chromium's GPU-canvas readback latch) while `cFull`, `finCanvas`, and the new 600 MB tile store `px` (~1.8 GB total) are simultaneously live (note: the parenthetical contrast in the candidate's evidence cites host_pictures.js:239-249, which is `passPicture`'s JSDoc; the actual whole-picture landing that keeps `px` at `img`'s native resolution via `Layer.fromImage(img)` with layer bounds `w: nw, h: nh` is `realismWhole` at host_pictures.js:526,560).

On an `editor.huge` (> 268,435,456 px, e.g. 20,000 x 15,000 = 300 MP) tile document — which `checkBaseSize` (inpaint_ed_open.js:84-94) supports up to 65,535 px per side and 1,073 MP — `relightWhole` with `detail: false` streams all 300 MP through `encodeComposite` (:82) and then rejects at `await createImageBitmap(enc.blob)` (:85) with a raw browser decode error because Blink refuses > 268 MP (1 GiB) `ImageBitmap` decodes (and `cFull` / `finCanvas` via raw `document.createElement('canvas')` also exceed `CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS`). Because the failure at :85 (or `flattenToCanvas` at :91 when `enc` is null) occurs before `comfyPictureRun` (:181) / `relightSend` (:250), no paid provider call is lost.

Checked known-issue lists (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` including 'Size limits' and 'What phase E left open on large documents', `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` including P12 on `detailRatio` under 27.9 MP, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`): none record `relightWhole`'s `detail: false` full-canvas allocations or missing `huge` handling. Severity is `should`: there is no silent pixel loss or lost provider charge, but users and agents on > 27.9 MP / 15k / > 268 MP documents are explicitly directed into `detail: false` and hit multi-second window freezes, ~1.8 GB memory spikes, GPU readback latching at 15k, and an unguarded decode failure after full composite streaming above 268 MP.

findings.claim: The 0.1.57 stale-layer fix in `relightWhole` re-looks up `layer` by ID after `encodeComposite` (`:96`) and before landing (`:358`), but still uses the original `layer` reference at `:70-71` after two earlier `await`s (`ensureDepthMap` before `providerPending` is set, and `relightSettled`), and mutates `.visible` on `layer` and `hiddenRelight` without bumping `editor.compositeVersion`. An undo of a `layers` step during those awaits leaves the live relight layer visible (or deleted while a paid run still goes out), and even without undo any filter layer between a hidden `relightOf` / `relight` layer and `upTo` reuses stale `_fcache` pixels on `flattenToCanvas`.
findings.scenario: Case 1 (no undo): On the canvas backend (or a stack with a colour-matched layer where `encodeComposite` returns `null` and `:91` runs `flattenToCanvas`), have Base, a previous `Relight (magnific)` pixel layer (`relightOf: L1`), a Curves filter layer (cached in `_fcache` at current `compositeVersion`), a visible Paint layer above Curves (so `upTo` is above Curves), and Relight filter `L1`. Run Relight whole picture again on `L1`: `:75` sets `Relight (magnific).visible = false` without bumping `compositeVersion`, so Curves' `filteredCanvas` (`c.version === this.compositeVersion`) returns its cached canvas that still contains the old `Relight (magnific)` pixels, sending the already-relit image to the paid provider. Case 2 (undo during `ensureDepthMap` / `relightSettled`): Add or reorder a layer, trigger Relight whole picture while depth or shadow maps are computing, and press Ctrl+Z before `:70`: if `L1` was undone away, `relightWhole` still sends and charges the paid run; if `L1` was rebuilt by a `layers` undo, `:71` sets `visible = false` on the detached object while the live `L1` stays visible.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/host_relight.js:28-31` awaits `editor.ensureDepthMap()` before `editor.providerPending = token` (`:37`), and `:61` awaits `editor.relightSettled(layer)`. Without re-finding `layer` in `editor.layers`, `:70-78` runs `const wasVis = layer.visible; layer.visible = false;` and `l.visible = false` for `l.relightOf === layer.id`, never setting `editor.uploaded.baseHash = null` (nor in `finally` at `:96-99`). In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:845`, `filteredCanvas` returns `c.canvas` whenever `!keepSurface && c && c.version === this.compositeVersion && c.key === key`, and `filterKey` (`:696-720`) does not include `belowSignature`.
findings.fix: Re-resolve `layer = editor.layers.find((x) => x.id === layer.id)` after `ensureDepthMap()` and `relightSettled()` (aborting without sending if `!layer`), and bump `editor.compositeVersion` (`editor.uploaded.baseHash = null`) both when hiding `layer` / `hiddenRelight` at `:71-78` and when restoring `.visible` in `finally` at `:97-99`.
findings.why:
Verified at `f45a86cc` in `renderer/editor/host_relight.js`. Both defects hold with no blocking guard, and neither is already recorded as an open known issue.

1. **Case 1 (`_fcache` / `_mstatsStackRun` coherency across temporary `.visible` mutation without bumping `compositeVersion`):** At `host_relight.js:70-78`, `relightWhole` mutates `layer.visible = false` (`:71`) and `l.visible = false` on every visible `l.relightOf === layer.id` layer (`:74-76`), reads the composite via `editor.encodeComposite({ forRun: true, upTo })` (`:82`) or `editor.flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true, upTo })` (`:91`), and restores `.visible` in `finally` (`:96-99`) — never setting `editor.uploaded.baseHash = null` (the setter in `renderer/editor/inpaint_strokebuf.js:66-75` that increments `editor.compositeVersion++` and clears `flatCache`). Whenever a filter layer `F` sits above a `relightOf` pixel layer (or above `layer`) and below `upTo` (`realism.topFilterRun` at `renderer/editor/realism.js:555-566` sets `upTo > indexOf(F)` whenever `F` is in a group, clipped, or beneath any pixel/text layer), and `encodeComposite` falls back to `flattenToCanvas` (always on the canvas backend at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:583`, and on the tile backend whenever the stack below `upTo` contains a 2x-rendered text layer, a scaled/fractional pixel layer, a colour-matched layer above a filter, or a plugin filter without finite `reach` per `inpaint_ed_stack.js:110,126,174,194,197` and `inpaint_ed_composite.js:594`), `flattenToCanvas` sets `viewPass = null` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:566`) and calls `filteredCanvas` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:840-845,898`). Because `filterKey` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:696-721`) does not include `belowSignature`, if `F._fcache` (`forRun: true`) was populated at the current `compositeVersion` (e.g. by `exportCanvas` at `host_export.js:115`, `splitlayers.js`, or `serializeForPrompt`), `:845` (`c.version === this.compositeVersion && c.key === key`) returns the stale canvas still containing the old `Relight (<route>)` pixels, sending the already-relit image to the paid provider (`:250`) and feeding it into `detailRatio` (`:266`). Conversely, if `F._fcache` was cold on entry, `:91` populates `F._fcache` at the current `compositeVersion` with `hiddenRelight`/`layer` hidden and `:96-99` restores `.visible = true` without bumping `compositeVersion`, so if the run is cancelled or fails, a subsequent `flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true })` export reuses the hidden-layer cache. Even on tiles when `encodeComposite` succeeds (`:82`), `holdStack` -> `stackMatchOf` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:300-314`) keys `_mstatsStackRun` on `this.compositeVersion`, reusing stale colour-match statistics for any matched layer above `hiddenRelight`.

2. **Case 2 (remaining stale/deleted `layer` window in the 0.1.57 fix):** The 0.1.57 fix for `relight-depth-key/relight-whole-stale-layer-object` added by-id lookups in `readSig` (`:51`), `finally` (`:96-99`), and landing (`:358`), but `relightWhole` still awaits `editor.ensureDepthMap()` at `:30` (before `editor.providerPending = token` at `:37`, reachable whenever Depth Anything is still computing after adding the relight layer) and `editor.relightSettled(layer)` at `:61` (worker-pool `heightNormals` and `shadowMarch` jobs) while holding the original `layer` reference. Neither `removeLayer` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:567`) nor `layers`-kind undo/redo (`inpaint_ed_history.js:628-633,984-1020`) is blocked during those awaits: if `layer` is deleted or undone away, `relightWhole` never checks `editor.layers.find((x) => x.id === layer.id)` and still dispatches and charges the paid `relightSend` (`:250`); if a `layers` step is undone/redone, `applySnapshot` replaces `editor.layers` with copies, so `:71` sets `visible = false` on the detached `layer` (leaving the live copy visible during `:82/:91` when `upTo > indexOf(live)`), and after `:30` `relightIdle` (`inpaint_ed_relight.js:53-55`) populates `live._relight` while `:124-125` passes the detached `layer._relight` (`undefined`), causing `registerRelightGL` (`inpaint_relight.js:2141-2166`) to render Magnific's `mode: 1` lightmap with `DUMMY_NORMALS` and `DUMMY_VIS`.

3. **Known-list & severity check:** Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the 2026-11-12 / 2026-11-07 `verified.json` files. `relight-depth-key/relight-whole-stale-layer-object` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` was fixed in 0.1.57, and Case 2 proves an unfixed hole in that fix; Case 1 was only an unproven note in `reviewer_notes` ('I could not prove a cache hit on the stale composite') and never a known finding entry. Severity is `should`: hitting Case 1 requires a multi-layer stack with a filter layer below `upTo` (and either a `flattenToCanvas` fallback or a colour-matched layer on tiles) and Case 2 requires undo/deletion during the pre-read awaits, so it falls short of unconditional silent data loss (`must`), but produces wrong pixels in a paid run or post-cancel export (`should`).

findings.claim: `relightWhole` clamps `wSend` and `hSend` independently to a minimum of 256 px (`Math.max(256, Math.round(W * scaleFactor))`) and then renders the Magnific light map on `wSend x hSend` using a single scalar `scale: wSend / W` and no `full` size. On any banner/strip with a side under 256 px or any panorama steeper than 8:1 (`2048 / 8 = 256`), the picture sent to the paid provider is anisotropically stretched and the light map's lights, normals, and depth coordinates disagree with both the stretched image and the shadow map.
findings.scenario: Open a 6000x600 panorama (10:1) or a 1200x180 banner, add a Relight layer with a point or spot light, and run Relight whole picture on Magnific (or fal / Comfy Cloud). For 6000x600, `scaleFactor = 2048 / 6000 = 0.3413`, `wSend = 2048`, and `hSend = Math.max(256, 205) = 256`. `cSend` stretches the 600 px height vertically by 25% into 256 px, while `relightInfo` passes `scale: 2048 / 6000 = 0.3413` into `applyFilter("relight", mapCanvas, { ...layer.params, mode: 1 }, relightInfo)`. Inside `relight`, depth/normals and light Y positions map `y = 0..256` to document `y = 0..750` (clamping rows 205..256 past the bottom of the 600 px image), while `u_vis` samples shadows across `0..256`, sending a distorted picture and misaligned light map to Magnific. On a vertical 600x6000 image (`wSend = 256, hSend = 2048, scale = 0.4267`), the bottom 20% (`y = 4800..6000`) of the light map is cut off completely.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/host_relight.js:102-105`: `const longSide = Math.max(W, H); const scaleFactor = Math.min(1.0, 2048 / longSide); const wSend = Math.max(256, Math.round(W * scaleFactor)); const hSend = Math.max(256, Math.round(H * scaleFactor));`. Lines `109-115` draw `cFull` stretched into `wSend x hSend`. Lines `121-128` pass `relightInfo = { scale: wSend / W, maps: editor.maps, relight: layer._relight, layer, forRun: true }` (no `full`) to `applyFilter("relight", mapCanvas, { ...layer.params, mode: 1 }, relightInfo)`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:559-564` (`passToMap`) divides both X and Y by the scalar `scale`, and `renderer/editor/inpaint_relight.js:1600,2137-2138` uses that single `scale` for depth/normals/lights while sampling `u_vis` over `mapCanvas` UV `0..1`.
findings.fix: Do not clamp `wSend` and `hSend` independently in a way that alters aspect ratio (either scale uniformly without a per-side 256 clamp when the route allows it, or refuse aspects steeper than the provider's minimum side at 2048 long side before sending, as `splitLayers` / `capExportSide` avoid per-axis clamping).
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `HostRelightPart.relightWhole` (`renderer/editor/host_relight.js:102-105`) computes `longSide = Math.max(W, H)`, `scaleFactor = Math.min(1.0, 2048 / longSide)`, `wSend = Math.max(256, Math.round(W * scaleFactor))`, and `hSend = Math.max(256, Math.round(H * scaleFactor))`. Both entry points — the Relight layer *Render* button (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:946-955`) and the MCP `relight` command (`renderer/commands_runs.js:371-373`) when `route !== "app"` — reach this code with no minimum-side or aspect-ratio guard (`checkBaseSize` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:84-94` only caps maximum dimensions at 65,535 px / 2^30 px, and `host_relight.js:63-65` only checks `W * H > realism.MAX_AREA` when `detail !== false`). Whenever `W !== H` and either `min(W, H) < 256` (including ordinary-aspect banners or small assets like 970x250, 1200x180, or 320x180) or `max(W, H) / min(W, H) > 8` (`2048 / 256`, e.g. 6000x600 or 600x6000), clamping the short axis to 256 makes `wSend / W !== hSend / H`. Lines `108-116` then draw `cFull` into `wSend x hSend` (`sx.drawImage(cFull, 0, 0, wSend, hSend)`), sending an anisotropically stretched `picBytes` to all five generative routes (`comfyui` at `:150`, `fal-iclight` at `:189,193-194`, `fal-bria` at `:205`, `comfycloud` at `:222`, and `magnific` at `:236`), and none of the provider adapters (`electron/main/providers/magnific.js:455-488`, `fal.js:213-243`) rejects or corrects this distortion.

For the Magnific light map (`host_relight.js:118-130`, which also runs unconditionally before route dispatch), `mapCanvas` is sized `wSend x hSend` and passed to `applyFilter("relight", mapCanvas, { ...layer.params, mode: 1 }, relightInfo)` with `relightInfo = { scale: wSend / W, maps: editor.maps, relight: layer._relight, layer, forRun: true }` and no `full`. In `applyPluginGL` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:1140`), omitting `info.full` sets `u_pictureSize = [wSend, hSend]` and `u_pictureOrigin = [0, 0]`, so `pp = pictureUv(uv) * u_pictureSize` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_relight.js:1959`, matching CPU `applyRelight` at `:1649-1651,1708-1715`) ranges over `[0, wSend] x [0, hSend]`. Two minor corrections to the candidate's evidence citations do not affect the bug: `passToMap` is at `renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:433-439` (not `:559-564`), where `xfScale(1 / sc)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_resample.js:113-115`) divides both X and Y by the single scalar `scale = wSend / W`; and `u_vis` is not sampled over `0..1` canvas UV directly, but via `suv_vis = suv_map = mpx / vec2(normSize)` (`inpaint_relight.js:1971-1974`, CPU `:1725`), using the same scalar-scaled `mpx` as depth, normals, surface maps (`:2055-2056`), MoGe-2 normals (`:2020`), and `lightToMap` (`:742-744,2183`). Consequently, every map-space coordinate in `lmCanvas` maps `py` to document `py / (wSend / W)` while `cSend` (`picBytes`, and `c.rgb` read by bilateral edge snap against `u_guide` at `:1962,1997`) maps `py` to document `py * (H / hSend)`. On horizontal banners/panoramas (`wSend / W < hSend / H`, e.g. 6000x600 -> 2048x256 with `scale = 0.3413`, or 320x180 -> 320x256 with `scale = 1`), the entire image height's depth, normals, shadows, and light Y positions are compressed into rows `0..round(H * wSend / W)` (rows `0..205` or `0..180`) and clamped across the remaining bottom rows, shifting the light map by 25%-42% against the stretched `picBytes`. On vertical strips (`wSend / W > hSend / H`, e.g. 600x6000 -> 256x2048 with `scale = 0.4267`), `py = 0..2048` maps to `docY = 0..4800`, cutting off the bottom 20% of the light map completely.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` (which only recorded the stale-layer-object bug in `relightWhole`), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` (`P12` covered `detailRatio`/`fitOriginalLight` allocations), and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`; this defect is not known or planned. Severity is `should`: while normal-aspect photos with `min(W, H) >= 256` and the default in-app relight filter are unaffected (and padding the canvas is a workaround), relighting web banners, small non-square assets (`< 256` px on one side), or `> 8:1` panoramas is a plausible workflow that silently sends a distorted image and a misaligned/truncated light map to paid generative APIs, corrupting the landed result.

findings.claim: readPng allocates `new Uint8Array(left)` directly from the untrusted 32-bit chunk length header whenever `type === "PLTE"` or `type === "tRNS"`, with neither the PNG specification caps (768 bytes for PLTE, 256 bytes for tRNS) nor a check against `blob.size`. A tiny crafted `.png` (declaring > 268 MP in IHDR) or `.ora` (any size on the default tiles backend) triggers multi-gigabyte allocations in the renderer's worker pool before a single payload byte is read, crashing the renderer with OOM.
findings.scenario: A user opens or drops a ~50-byte crafted `.png` whose 33-byte IHDR declares `20000 x 20000` (or any `.ora` whose layer entry starts with a 33-byte 8-bit non-interlaced PNG header) followed by one or more 8-byte `PLTE` or `tRNS` chunk headers with length `0x70000000` (~1.87 GiB). `pngPartsOf` returns `null` and `pixelsFromPngStream` dispatches `png_read` to `readPng`, which immediately calls `new Uint8Array(0x70000000)` per chunk header before reading payload bytes, exhausting renderer memory and crashing all open tabs (losing edits since the last autosave).
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_png.js:307-309: `left = new DataView(header.buffer).getUint32(0); type = String.fromCharCode(header[4], header[5], header[6], header[7]); small = type === "PLTE" || type === "tRNS" || (type === "tEXt" && left < 4 * 1048576) ? new Uint8Array(left) : null;` — `tEXt` is bounded to `< 4 * 1048576`, while `PLTE` and `tRNS` have no bound at all. Reachable from `OpenPart.loadFile` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:187-189) and `LayersPart.addImageLayers` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:51-53) via `hugePngSize` -> `pixelsFromPngStream` -> `editorPool().run("png_read", { blob })` (renderer/editor/inpaint_load.js:291-294, 350; renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:1166), and at any dimensions from `OpenPart.decodeOraLayer` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:330-335) when `this.tileMode` is true.
findings.fix: Bound `PLTE` and `tRNS` chunk allocations to their PNG spec maxima (and remaining file bytes): e.g. refuse or skip `PLTE` when `left > 768 || left % 3 !== 0` and `tRNS` when `left > 256` (and check `left <= blob.size` before allocating `small`, including for `tEXt`).
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `readPng` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_png.js:307-309` reads each PNG chunk's 8-byte header from `blob.slice(8).stream()` and executes `left = new DataView(header.buffer).getUint32(0); type = String.fromCharCode(header[4], header[5], header[6], header[7]); small = type === "PLTE" || type === "tRNS" || (type === "tEXt" && left < 4 * 1048576) ? new Uint8Array(left) : null;` before reading a single byte of chunk payload. While `tEXt` is explicitly capped at `< 4 * 1048576` (and `pngPartsOf` at `inpaint_png.js:457-475` rejects `at + 12 + len > blob.size` as well as `PLTE`/`tRNS`), `readPng` enforces neither the PNG specification maxima (`<= 768` bytes and divisible by 3 for `PLTE`; `<= 256` bytes for `tRNS`) nor `left <= blob.size`.

Tracing every entry path confirms it is directly reachable without guards: (1) Opening or dropping a crafted `.png` via `OpenPart.loadFile` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:181-190`) or `LayersPart.addImageLayers` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:77-85`, or `:40-42` for layered files) on the default tiles backend calls `hugePngSize` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_load.js:291-302`). A 41-byte `.png` whose 33-byte IHDR declares `20000 x 20000` (400 MP, above `CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS = 268,435,456` so `:294` returns immediately, while below `HUGE_MAX_SIDE = 65535` and `HUGE_MAX_PIXELS = 1024 MP` so `checkBaseSize` at `inpaint_ed_open.js:84-94` passes)—or even a `>= 32 MP` PNG (`InpaintEditor.pngStreamFrom = 32 * 1024 * 1024` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:761`) with an empty `IDAT` before the `PLTE`/`tRNS` header so `pngIsPlainSrgb` (`inpaint_load.js:305-315`) returns `true`—proceeds into `pixelsOffThread` (`:410-415`) -> `pixelsFromPngStream` (`:324-357`). `pngPartsOf` returns `null`, and `:350` dispatches `png_read` to `pngRead` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:1142-1150`, `:2009`), running `readPng` in a renderer Web Worker (same OS process as all open tabs). (2) Opening or dropping a tiny `.ora` on tiles calls `OpenPart.readLayered` -> `OpenPart.decodeOraLayer` (`inpaint_ed_open.js:280, 306, 328-344`), which checks only `h && h.bitDepth === 8 && !h.interlace` (`:332`) and passes any size (even `1 x 1`) straight to `pixelsFromPngStream`, bypassing H1 S5's ORA inflate and pixel-budget guards (`renderer/editor/inpaint_layered.js:48-57, 1078-1144`).

One minor nuance in the scenario wording: within a single `readPng` call, a 50-byte PNG cannot trigger multiple allocations from consecutive 8-byte headers because `left` stays `0x70000000` (`inpaint_png.js:303` requires `left === 0` before reading the next chunk header). However, a single 8-byte `PLTE`/`tRNS` header with `0x70000000` (~1.75 GiB, just under PartitionAlloc's 2 GiB direct-map cap) already commits ~1.75 GiB from a 41-byte file, and because `feed` exits cleanly on EOF without checking `left === 0` or `IEND` (`if (end) break;` at `inpaint_png.js:299`), a 63-byte `1 x 1` PNG entry with a valid 1-pixel `IDAT` followed by a truncated `PLTE` header of `0x70000000` decodes *successfully* in `readPng`—allowing a sub-kilobyte `.ora` whose `stack.xml` references that stored entry N times (or dropping multiple 41-byte `.png` files) to trigger repeated 1.75 GiB allocations across the pool workers and OOM-crash the renderer process.

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three prior `verified.json` files: not known (`S5` in `review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` covered only PSD/ORA `inflateAtMost` and rectangle/pixel budgets in `inpaint_layered.js`, fixed in H1 S5 before K20c wired `decodeOraLayer` to `pixelsFromPngStream`). Severity is `should` per the rubric's explicit criterion for a crafted-file renderer crash/OOM (not `must`, as JS typed arrays remain memory-safe and valid PNGs are unaffected).

findings.claim: When opening a PSD or ORA, `loadLayered` promotes `layers[0]` to `basePx` whenever its bounds are `[0, 0, W, H]`, `visible` is true, `opacity >= 0.999`, `blend === "normal"`, and `!maskPx` — without checking whether `layers[0]` belongs to a group (`b.group`) or has transparency under clipped layers (`layers[1]?.clip`). Promoting a transparent bottom layer strips `L.clip = false` from every layer clipped to it so those layers spill across the transparent background, and promoting a grouped bottom layer pulls it out of its group (making a hidden group's layer permanently visible as the base).
findings.scenario: (a) Open a PSD or ORA with no opaque Background: `Layer 0` is a `[0, 0, W, H]` cutout on a transparent background and `Layer 1` is clipped (`clip: true`) to `Layer 0` (e.g. a colour/lighting paint pass over the subject). `loadLayered` promotes `Layer 0` to `basePx` and sets `Layer 1.clip = false`, so `Layer 1` renders unclipped over the entire transparent background on screen, in exports, and in paid runs, while the status bar still reports `1 clipped layer kept clipped`. (b) Open a PSD whose bottom `[0, 0, W, H]` layer is inside a hidden group (`Group 1` eye off in Photoshop, which sets `flags & 2` on the folder record while keeping `b.visible === true` on the child layer): `b` is promoted out of `Group 1` into the always-visible `basePx`.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:496-499: `const b = layers[0]; if (b && b.x === 0 && b.y === 0 && b.w === W && b.h === H && b.visible && b.opacity >= 0.999 && b.blend === "normal" && !b.maskPx) { basePx = b.px; layers.shift(); } // a layer clipped to what became the base would show "clipped without effect": the base covers the picture anyway` followed by `if (basePx) for (const L of layers) { if (!L.clip) break; L.clip = false; }`. In renderer/editor/inpaint_layered.js:909,926,944, group visibility is stored on `groups` (`visible: !(L.flags & 2)` on `L.section === 1 || 2`), `layer.group` holds the enclosing group id, and `notes` already recorded `"1 clipped layer kept clipped"`. In renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:118-126, `clipBaseOf` cannot clip to `this.basePx`.
findings.fix: Do not promote `b` to `basePx` when `b.group` is set, nor when `layers[1] && layers[1].clip` unless `b` is known to be fully opaque (for example a PSD layer with no `-1` transparency channel); `loadLayered` line 502 already falls back to `basePx = this.pixels.Layer.empty(W, H)` and keeps `b` as `layers[0]` with `layers[1]` clipped to it.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:496-499. In OpenPart.loadLayered (reached from OpenPart.loadFile at :169-170 via File > Open, drag-and-drop onto an empty tab in LayersPart.addImageLayers at inpaint_ed_layers.js:30-31, paste, and MCP load_image), lines 496-499 execute: `const b = layers[0]; if (b && b.x === 0 && b.y === 0 && b.w === W && b.h === H && b.visible && b.opacity >= 0.999 && b.blend === "normal" && !b.maskPx) { basePx = b.px; layers.shift(); }` followed immediately by `if (basePx) for (const L of layers) { if (!L.clip) break; L.clip = false; }`. As the comment on :498 (`the base covers the picture anyway`) and the method docstring on :480-482 (`opaque in the normal mode ... otherwise the base is transparent and every layer stays a layer`) show, this promotion assumes `b` is an ungrouped, pixel-opaque backdrop. Neither `!b.group` nor pixel opacity / clipped dependents (`layers[1]?.clip`) is checked.

Both failure modes hold end-to-end on PSD opens (`kind === "psd"`, via both `readPsdOnPool` at :395-477 and window `readPsd` at :279): (1) Transparent clip base: in decodePsd (renderer/editor/inpaint_layered.js:922-930), when `records[0]` is a `[0, 0, W, H]` normal layer at 100% opacity without a layer mask but with an alpha channel (`id === -1`) containing transparent pixels, `baseKept` becomes `true` (:925), and `records[1]` with `clipping === 1` gets `layer.clip = true` (:928) while `notes` records `"1 clipped layer kept clipped"` (:944) with `lossy = false` (:956). `loadLayered` then promotes `layers[0]` to `basePx` (:497) and clears `L.clip = false` on the entire contiguous clipping chain above it (:499) — and even without :499, `clipTargetOf` / `clipBaseOf` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:105-127), `drawLayersInto` (:74-89), and `stackPlan` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:164-166) only clip to entries in `this.layers`, never `this.basePx`. Every clipped layer therefore spills unclipped over the transparent areas on screen, in exports, and in run crops while :528 still displays `1 clipped layer kept clipped`. (2) Grouped bottom layer: in decodePsd (:896-910, :926), PSD group visibility is stored on the folder section record (`groups.push({ ..., visible: !(L.flags & 2) })` at :909, matching both Photoshop and Scumble's own PSD writer at inpaint_ed_export.js:41,89,132), while a child layer inside a hidden group retains `b.visible === true` and `b.group === "g1"`. Because :497 checks only `b.visible` and ignores `b.group`, `b` is pulled out of its group into the permanently visible `basePx` before `this.groups` and the remaining layers are added (:517-522), making a hidden group's bottom `[0, 0, W, H]` layer unconditionally visible with no eye toggle to hide it. (One scope nuance: ORA is unaffected by (1) and (2) because `oraFromEntries` at inpaint_layered.js:1121-1146 emits no `clip` or `group` fields and folds `<stack visibility="hidden">` directly into `layer.visible = false`, though a transparent `[0, 0, W, H]` bottom ORA layer is still promoted into the unhideable base.)

Checked known-issue sources at f45a86cc (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` Open and Fixed sections, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` §4.7 K20a-c): none record this defect. Severity is `should`: any user opening a non-Background PSD with a `[0, 0, W, H]` cutout + clipping pass or a bottom layer inside a (hidden) folder gets wrong composite pixels in the editor, exports, and runs and cannot re-clip to or hide `basePx` in place, though original disk files are untouched and a workaround exists (creating a `W x H` blank canvas first and dropping the PSD onto it via `addImageLayers` at inpaint_ed_layers.js:40-61, which keeps every layer and group without base promotion).

findings.claim: In the desktop app, `ed.pluginData` (including FLUX 3 / Klein Boxes rows and captions, 3D object placements, and any plugin's `scumble.documents.data(doc).set(...)`) and `ed.docExtra` are persisted in `.scumble` files separately from `ed.getValue()`, yet `docFile.key` and `ed._stateKey` hash `ed.getValue()` alone. Once the 1.5 s autosave timer runs `bundle()`, `ed._stateKey` hashes back to `ed.docFile.key`, clearing the tab's `*` dirty marker so closing the tab does not prompt to save and the `.scumble` file on disk silently loses the plugin edits.
findings.scenario: Open a saved `.scumble` document that already has the Boxes switch enabled (`genSettings.boxes === true`) with two boxes. Drag, resize, edit the description of, add, or delete boxes. `plugins.js` updates `ed.pluginData.boxes` and calls `host.changed(ed)`, which sets `ed._stateKey = null` (`*` appears briefly) and schedules the 1.5 s autosave. After 1.5 s, `saveAll() -> bundle()` computes `ed._stateKey = hashString(ed.getValue())`, which equals `ed.docFile.key` because `host.boxesInEditor` is falsy in the app (`getValue()` omits `pluginData.boxes`). The `*` disappears, `list_documents` reports `dirty: false`, and pressing Ctrl+W closes the tab with no save prompt, leaving the `.scumble` file on disk without the box edits.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/host_documents.js:82-83: `if (ed._stateKey == null) return true; return ed._stateKey !== ed.docFile.key;`. renderer/editor/host_documents.js:247,252 (`saveDocument`) writes `plugins: ed.pluginData || {}` to `.scumble` but hashes `key: hashString(state)` where `state = ed.getValue()`; `settleKey` (:101) and `rememberClosed` (:339) likewise hash `ed.getValue()` only. renderer/editor/host_queue.js:504,527-528: `changed` sets `editor._stateKey = null`, then `bundle` sets `state = ed.getValue(); if (ed.base) ed._stateKey = hashString(state);`. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:78-79 includes `boxes` in `getValue()` only when `host.boxesInEditor` is truthy (the ComfyUI node, not the app). renderer/plugins.js:715-716 writes `ed.pluginData[pluginId] = next; host.changed(ed);`, and renderer/shell.js:315 prompts on close only when `host.documentDirty(editor)` is true.
findings.fix: Compute the document state key via a single helper `stateKeyOf(ed, state = ed.getValue())` (for example `hashString(state + "\0" + JSON.stringify(ed.pluginData || {}))`) and use it everywhere `_stateKey` and `docFile.key` are written (`bundle`, `settleKey`, `saveDocument`, and `rememberClosed`).
findings.why:
Verified against commit f45a86cc: all cited lines and the end-to-end call path hold. In `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:240,246-252`, `saveDocument` serialises `const state = ed.getValue()`, writes `plugins: ed.pluginData || {}` and `extra: ed.docExtra || {}` into the `.scumble` archive alongside `document: state`, yet sets `ed.docFile.key = hashString(state)`. Likewise, `settleKey` (`host_documents.js:101-104`), `rememberClosed` (`host_documents.js:338-340`), and `bundle` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:527-529`) compute `_stateKey` and `docFile.key` from `hashString(ed.getValue())` alone. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:78-79`, `PersistPart.getValue()` includes `this.pluginData.boxes` only when `host.boxesInEditor` is truthy, and in the desktop app `host.boxesInEditor` is `false` (`renderer/editor/host_helpers.js:172`), nor does `getValue()` include `ed.undo` (`history` at `:62` is `this.history`, the generation result list) or any other `ed.pluginData` entry.

Tracing the edit-to-close path confirms there is no guard preventing data loss on the `.scumble` file: when a user adds, moves, resizes, edits, deletes, clears, or undoes/redoes boxes (`plugins/boxes/main.js:38,132-158`, `renderer/plugins.js:712-716`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:660-663`), only adding the very first box while `ed.genSettings.boxes` is falsy mutates `ed.genSettings` (`plugins/boxes/main.js:79-83,138`). On any saved `.scumble` document that already has `genSettings.boxes === true` (for example, any document saved with at least one box), box edits mutate `ed.pluginData.boxes` only and call `host.changed(ed)` (`host_queue.js:504-506`), which sets `ed._stateKey = null` and schedules `saveAll()` in 1500 ms. Once that 1.5 s timer fires, `bundle()` (`host_queue.js:527-529`) sets `ed._stateKey = hashString(ed.getValue())`, which equals `ed.docFile.key`. `documentDirty(ed)` (`host_documents.js:75-84`) checks `healing`, `docFile.key`, dirty/uploading layers or masks, `mapsUnstored()`, `selectionEncoded`, and finally `ed._stateKey !== ed.docFile.key` (`:83`), returning `false`. Consequently: (1) `saveAll()` calls `onDocsChanged -> renderTabs` (`renderer/shell.js:262-265,363`), clearing the `*` indicator from the tab and window title after 1.5 s; (2) `bundle()` passes `clean = !this.documentDirty(ed) === true` into `docMeta` (`renderer/editor/host_util.js:195-201`), persisting `file.clean: true` in `autosave.json` so even a restart + `settleKey` (`host_documents.js:104`) keeps the tab marked clean; (3) `docSummary` (`renderer/commands_util.js:47`, `list_documents` at `renderer/commands_docs.js:32`) reports `dirty: false`; and (4) closing the tab via Ctrl+W or the tab `×` (`renderer/shell.js:315`) skips the `Save the changes to <name>?` prompt because `host.documentDirty(editor)` is `false`, leaving the `.scumble` file on disk without the plugin edits. (Two minor scope notes on the claim: `ed.docExtra` is never mutated in-session today, and `plugins/glb` object placement/re-rendering also mutates layer pixels/`ref` except during legacy storage migration at `plugins/glb/main.js:76`, whereas Boxes and any plugin's `scumble.documents.data(doc).set(...)` hit this unconditionally.)

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: not known. `files-io/settlekey-adopts-user-edit-as-saved` (`review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:310`, fixed by `mark(ed)` at `host_documents.js:97-104`) concerned edits made during `settleKey`'s `flushEditor` await, and `shell/F4` (`review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`) concerned `openGeneration` dropping `plugins`. Severity is `should` (not `must`): no pixels are lost, explicit Ctrl+S still writes `ed.pluginData` to the `.scumble` file (`host_documents.js:247`), and `File › Reopen Closed Tab` (`host_documents.js:340,362`) retains up to `CLOSED_MAX` closed tabs with their `plugins` in the session, but in normal Boxes/plugin workflows the dirty marker clears after 1.5 s and closing the tab silently leaves the `.scumble` file on disk without the user's edits.

findings.claim: Both PSD readers (`mergedPlanes` on the window and `mergedChannelDescs` on the pool stream) unconditionally map the 4th channel of an RGB PSD (2nd of grayscale) in the Image Data section to transparency (`"-1"`). In the PSD format, extra channels in a flattened PSD (`lmLen === 0` or `liLen === 0`) or a layered PSD with a positive layer count are user alpha / spot / saved-selection channels rather than transparency (Photoshop signals merged transparency with a negative layer count). Opening such a flattened PSD cuts out the picture wherever `Alpha 1` is dark instead of keeping the image opaque.
findings.scenario: In Photoshop, save a flattened RGB photo (`Background` only, `lmLen === 0`) that carries a saved selection mask channel (`Alpha 1`, so header `channels = 4`), and open the `.psd` in Scumble. Because `doc.layers` is empty, `loadLayered` uses `doc.compositePx` / `doc.composite`, where channel 3 (`Alpha 1`) was placed into RGBA alpha; `putImageData` / canvas round-trip premultiplies RGB against that alpha, turning unselected regions transparent and destroying RGB values where `Alpha 1` is 0.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_layered.js:779: `const count = Math.abs(r.i16());` discards the sign of the layer count. Lines 665,710-712 (`mergedChannelDescs`) and lines 723,751 (`mergedPlanes`) set `const n = Math.min(channels, gray ? 2 : 4);` and map `descs[3]` / `planes[3]` (or `[1]` in gray) to `"-1"`, which `psdBandRgba` (:577) and `interleave` (:403) write into RGBA alpha. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:500-501 then sets `basePx` from `doc.compositePx` / `doc.composite` when `!layers.length`.
findings.fix: Record `const rawCount = r.i16(); const hasMergedAlpha = rawCount < 0;` when reading Layer Info (`false` when `lmLen === 0` or `liLen === 0`), and pass `hasMergedAlpha` to `mergedPlanes` and `mergedChannelDescs` so `n = Math.min(channels, (gray ? 1 : 3) + (hasMergedAlpha ? 1 : 0))`.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_layered.js. Both PSD merged-image readers unconditionally treat the 4th channel of an RGB PSD (2nd of grayscale) as merged transparency ("-1"): `mergedChannelDescs` (:662-713, specifically :665 `const n = Math.min(channels, gray ? 2 : 4);` and :710-712 returning `"-1": descs[3] || null` / `descs[1] || null`) and `mergedPlanes` (:719-752, specifically :723 `const n = Math.min(channels, gray ? 2 : 4);` and :751 returning `"-1": to8(planes[3])` / `to8(planes[1])`). In `decodePsd` (:755-958), Image Resources are skipped wholesale at :770 (`r.skip(r.u32())`), the sign of the layer count is discarded at :779 (`const count = Math.abs(r.i16());`), and Global Additional Layer Information (`Mtrn` / `Mt16` / `Mt32`, `Lr16` / `Lr32`) is skipped at :874-876 (`r.p = lmEnd`).

Per the Adobe Photoshop File Formats Specification (Layer and Mask Information -> Layer info), merged composite transparency is signaled by a negative `layerCount` (whose absolute value is the layer count while the negative sign means the first alpha channel in Image Data holds merged transparency) or by the global tagged blocks `Mtrn` / `Mt16` / `Mt32`. In Photoshop, a flattened document (`Background` only) cannot have transparency and writes `lmLen === 0`; if the document carries a saved selection mask (`Alpha 1`) or spot channel in the Channels panel, Photoshop writes `header.channels = 4` (2 for grayscale), records the user channel in Image Resources `1006` / `1045` (Alpha Channel Names) and `1053` (Alpha Identifiers `> 0`, whereas `0` denotes transparency), writes `lmLen = 0`, and stores `[R, G, B, Alpha 1]` in the Image Data section. The same mismatch occurs when `doc.layers` ends up empty (`!layers.length`) on a PSD with `layerCount > 0` (opaque Background) or a 16-bit Photoshop PSD whose layers live in `Lr16` (`liLen === 0`, which `decodePsd` skips).

Tracing the full open path from `File > Open`, drag-and-drop into an empty tab (`LayersPart.addImageLayers` at renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:31), or MCP `load_image`: `OpenPart.loadFile` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:169-170) dispatches `.psd` files to `loadLayered` (:484) -> `readLayered` (:254). On the default worker-pool route (`readPsdOnPool` at :395-477 -> `psdRead` in renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:962-995 -> `readPsdStream` -> `decodePsd` :932-939), `!layers.length` calls `mergedChannelDescs` and streams bands through `Px.prototype.psdBandRgba` (renderer/editor/px/px.js:1258-1260, `const hasA = !!descs["-1"];`) or JS `psdBandRgba` (inpaint_layered.js:572-577) into `e.px.writeRect` (inpaint_ed_open.js:428); on the window fallback (`readPsd` -> `decodePsd` :880-883 -> `interleave` :401-406), `loadLayered` :500-501 converts `doc.composite` via `Layer.fromImageData`. No guard intervenes. Both `TileLayerPixels._putBlock` / `normalizeBlock` (renderer/editor/inpaint_tiles.js:540-550, 1432-1443) and `CanvasLayerPixels` (`putImageData`) zero RGB wherever `Alpha 1 === 0` and round-trip RGB against `Alpha 1` elsewhere, and `uploadPixels(basePx, ...)` (inpaint_ed_open.js:509) bakes that cutout into the stored base PNG. (Note for fixing: non-Photoshop writers and Scumble's own `tools/layered_test.js:273,1102` `flat.psd` test fixture emit layerless 4-channel PSDs with empty Image Resources to represent flat RGBA; checking `layerCount < 0` / `Mtrn`/`Mt16`/`Mt32` plus checking Image Resources `1006`/`1045`/`1053` when `lmLen === 0`, as `ag-psd` and `psd-tools` do, distinguishes Photoshop user alpha/spot channels from unnamed third-party flat RGBA.)

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` (where `S5` covered only inflate/dimension bounds), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_K20.md` (:129 carried `n = Math.min(channels, gray ? 2 : 4)` forward into `mergedChannelDescs` unchanged); this defect is not previously recorded. Severity `should` is right: the user's `.psd` on disk is not overwritten and the cutout is visible upon open, but opening a flattened Photoshop PSD with a saved selection or spot channel is a plausible real-world workflow that corrupts the imported picture unless the user strips extra channels beforehand.

findings.claim: When a window close is already flushing unsaved layers and autosave state (`quitGuard.flushing`), `reloadWindow` skips its own flush and immediately calls `win.webContents.reload()`. That navigation aborts `flushWaits`, causing `quitGuard.run` to mark the close done and close the window without finishing the save or asking 'Quit now'. Overlapping `reloadWindow` and close calls also clear `mirror.localOnly` mid-quit.
findings.scenario: The user paints strokes or creates a layer on a 15k document and clicks the window's close button (or File > Quit). While the status bar says 'Saving the edited layers before closing...' (`quitGuard.flushing` is active), the user presses Ctrl+R (or clicks View > Reload). `reloadWindow` sees `quitGuard.flushing` truthy, skips `await flushAll("reload")`, and immediately calls `win.webContents.reload()`. `did-start-navigation` resolves the pending `app:flush` with `{ ok: false, error: "the window reloaded" }`, `quitGuard.run` sets `quitGuard.done = true` and calls `win.close()`, and Scumble exits immediately with all un-uploaded strokes and layers from the last 15 seconds lost.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/main.js:401-412` (`win.on("close")`) sets `mirror.localOnly = true` and starts `quitGuard.run(() => flushAll("quit")).then((r) => { ... if (win && !win.isDestroyed()) win.close(); })`. `electron/main/main.js:530-557` (`reloadWindow`, bound to `CmdOrCtrl+R` at line 831) has no guard returning when `quitGuard.flushing || quitGuard.done`; instead lines 551-556 run `if (!quitGuard.flushing) { mirror.localOnly = true; try { await flushAll("reload"); } finally { mirror.localOnly = false; } } if (!win || win.isDestroyed()) return; if (ignoreCache) win.webContents.reloadIgnoringCache(); else win.webContents.reload();`. `win.webContents.reload()` fires `did-start-navigation` (`main.js:417-423`), which runs `for (const resolve of flushWaits.values()) resolve({ ok: false, error: "the window reloaded" });`, settling `quitGuard.run` (`electron/main/quit.js:38-44`) with `this.done = true` so `win.close()` at `main.js:411` passes `quitGuard.onClose() === "allow"`.
findings.fix: Return early from `reloadWindow` whenever `quitGuard.flushing || quitGuard.done` or a `reloading` flag is already set, re-check `if (quitGuard.flushing || quitGuard.done || !win || win.isDestroyed()) return;` after `await flushAll("reload")`, and only reset `mirror.localOnly = false` in `finally` when `!quitGuard.flushing`.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc in electron/main/main.js and electron/main/quit.js. When the user closes the window (`win.on("close")`, electron/main/main.js:392-413) or installs a downloaded update (`update:install`, electron/main/main.js:1552-1558), main sets `mirror.localOnly = true` and starts `quitGuard.run(() => flushAll("quit" | "update"))`, which sets `quitGuard.flushing` (electron/main/quit.js:38) and waits in `flushWindow` (`flushWaits`, electron/main/main.js:508-515) for the renderer's `onFlush` -> `saveBeforeRestart` (renderer/shell.js:985-1043) to upload dirty layers/masks, unstored maps, pending selection PNGs, and write `autosave.json`. Meanwhile, View > Reload (`CmdOrCtrl+R`, electron/main/main.js:831) and View > Force Reload (line 832) invoke `reloadWindow(ignoreCache)` (electron/main/main.js:530-557) directly in the main process.

No guard prevents `reloadWindow` from running while `quitGuard.flushing` or `quitGuard.done` is active. At electron/main/main.js:551-556, `if (!quitGuard.flushing)` skips `await flushAll("reload")` when a quit/update flush is already in flight, and immediately falls through to `win.webContents.reload()` / `reloadIgnoringCache()` on line 556. That navigation fires `did-start-navigation` (electron/main/main.js:417-429), whose line 423 resolves every pending entry in `flushWaits` with `{ ok: false, error: "the window reloaded" }` while tearing down the renderer mid-`saveBeforeRestart` (and before any renderer-side `.scumble` prep in `host.docSavesIdle()` reaches `documents:write`). `flushAll` returns `{ ok: false, error: "the window reloaded" }` (only waiting on `documents.idle()` if a main-side `.scumble` write had already started), `quitGuard.run` sets `this.done = true` and clears `this.flushing` (electron/main/quit.js:38-44), and `win.on("close")`'s `.then` callback immediately calls `win.close()` (electron/main/main.js:411, or `installOrReset()` at line 1557), which passes `quitGuard.onClose() === "allow"` (electron/main/main.js:401-402) without finishing the save or showing `askWhileSaving()`'s "Keep waiting" / "Quit now" prompt. This is also reachable if `askWindow("Reload window?")` (lines 533-550) is open during a provider run, the user clicks the window's Close button (`quitGuard.flushing` starts), and then clicks "Reload" in the still-open prompt. In the reverse overlap (`reloadWindow` enters `flushAll("reload")` first, and the user clicks Close while it runs), `reloadWindow` has no re-entry flag when `providers.runningCount() === 0`, resets `mirror.localOnly = false` in its `finally` (line 553) while `quitGuard.flushing` is still running, and then calls `win.webContents.reload()`, aborting `flushAll("quit")` the same way.

Checked against docs/BUGS.md, scratch/known_index.md, docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, and all three prior review verified.json files (`main/MAIN-2` in 2026-11-07 only added the `askingToReload` provider-run prompt, and `documents/D5` only covered `fileSaves` exports); this defect is not known. Calibrated as `should`: hitting it requires triggering Reload while a close/update flush is in progress (or closing while the Reload prompt or flush is active), which is plausible on 15k documents where `saveBeforeRestart` takes multiple seconds (and up to 10-60 s before any status text during `docSavesIdle` / `_restoring` / `healing` / `_fileCheck`), and the consequence is silent permanent loss of unsaved layer and selection edits.

findings.claim: `autosave.referencedKeys()` scans only `GENERATIONS` (`autosave.1.json`, `autosave.2.json`, `autosave.crash.json`, `autosave.crash.1.json`) and never `FILE` (`autosave.json`). Whenever `autosave.json` was not restored into the window and could not be rotated or set aside due to a transient read error, `files:prune` neither aborts nor keeps the files named in `autosave.json`, deleting the previous session's layer and base PNGs from the mirror. `walkRefs` also fails to normalize `\` or extra `/` in `subfolder`, unlike `docfile.keyOf` and `mirror.prune`.
findings.scenario: The user has a multi-layer project from yesterday (>1 hour old) in `autosave.json`. At startup, `autosave.json` hits a transient `EBUSY` lock: `autosave.rotate()` returns `{ rotated: false, why: "autosave unreadable" }` without updating `autosave.1.json`, and `shell.js` catches `state.load()`'s error and opens an empty `newDocument()` (writing no autosave so `autosave.json` stays intact on disk for `save()`'s `unreadableCurrent` recovery). The user opens Settings > Local files and clicks Clean up (or an MCP agent runs `cleanup`). `a.keep` is `[]`, `autosave.referencedKeys()` skips `autosave.json` completely, and `mirror.prune()` deletes all >1-hour-old base, layer, mask, and map PNGs of that session.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/autosave.js:18-24` defines `FILE = "autosave.json"` separately from `GENERATIONS`. `autosave.js:195-196` (`rotate`) returns early when `nowRes.status === "error"`, and `autosave.js:222-223` (`setAside`) returns `false` when `prevRes.status === "error"` on a safe-mode double crash (`main.js:444-445`). `renderer/shell.js:1488-1494` catches `window.scumble.state.load()` and creates a blank tab without saving. In `main.js:1257-1263` (`files:prune`), `const kept = autosave.referencedKeys(app.getPath("userData"))`, where `autosave.js:254-279` loops `for (const g of GENERATIONS)` only. Also `autosave.js:249` builds `` `${v.type || "input"}/${v.subfolder || ""}/${v.filename}` `` without normalizing `subfolder`, whereas `files.js:28` normalizes `\` to `/` on disk and `files.js:384-387` (`prune`) matches `/`-joined `path.relative` keys (compare `docfile.js:228` `keyOf`).
findings.fix: Include `FILE` (`autosave.json`) alongside `GENERATIONS` in `autosave.referencedKeys(dir)` (so an unreadable `autosave.json` throws to abort `files:prune`, and a readable un-restored `autosave.json` keeps its mirror files), and normalize `subfolder` in `autosave.walkRefs` (and `files.js` `key()`) with `String(v.subfolder || "").replace(/\\/g, "/").split("/").filter(Boolean).join("/")`.
findings.why:
Verified in the code at commit f45a86cc; both parts of the finding hold (with one minor correction to the scenario: there is no MCP `cleanup` command in `renderer/commands*.js`, so `files:prune` is reached via Settings › Local files › Clean up at `renderer/shell.js:878-893`).

First, `electron/main/autosave.js:18-24` defines `FILE = "autosave.json"` separately from `GENERATIONS`, and `referencedKeys(dir)` (`autosave.js:254-279`) iterates `for (const g of GENERATIONS)` (`line 256`) only, throwing on `r.status === "error"` (`line 258`) for generations while never checking `FILE`. At startup (`electron/main/main.js:1578`), `autosave.rotate()` (`autosave.js:193-210`) reads `autosave.json` via `readState(cur)` (`autosave.js:57-95`). If `autosave.json` hits a transient `EPERM`/`EBUSY`/`EACCES` lock across `retrying(..., 4)` (~250 ms), `readState` sets a 2000 ms cooldown (`readFailUntil`, `line 76`), adds `key` to `unreadableCurrent` (`line 79`), and returns `status: "error"`; `rotate()` then returns `{ rotated: false, why: "autosave unreadable" }` (`line 196`) without updating `autosave.1.json`. Moments later in `renderer/shell.js:1488-1494`, `window.scumble.state.load()` (`autosave.js:131-136`) runs inside the cooldown (`tries = 0` at `line 67`) and throws on the lock; `shell.js` catches it and calls `newDocument()` (`shell.js:171-185`), which creates an empty tab without calling `notifyChanged()` or `saveAll()`, deliberately leaving `autosave.json` intact on disk for `autosave.save()`'s `unreadableCurrent` recovery (`autosave.js:138-148`). The same gap occurs on a double renderer crash (`main.js:438-446`): if `autosave.setAside()` (`autosave.js:217-229`) fails because `autosave.json` (`line 218`) or `autosave.crash.json` (`lines 222-223`) hits a transient read error, `startMode = "safe"` skips `state.load()` (`shell.js:1489`) and directs the user to Settings › Local files (`shell.js:1496`). (Likewise, if a tab's base failed to load at startup and is parked in `host._rawStates`, `bundle()` at `host_queue.js:526` writes it to `autosave.json`, whereas `host.referencedFileKeys()` at `host_queue.js:562-570` walks `ed.getValue()` and not `_rawStates`.) If the user clicks Clean up before an edit triggers `save()`, `a.keep` is `[]`, `main.js:1261` calls `autosave.referencedKeys()`, which neither aborts on an unreadable `autosave.json` nor collects its refs once readable, and `mirror.prune()` (`electron/main/files.js:373-399`) unlinks every file older than 1 hour (`line 391`).

Second, `subfolder` normalization is inconsistent between mirror storage/pruning and the keep-set walkers. `mirrorPath` and `mirrorReadPath` (`files.js:28,37`, `docfile.js:221`) split `subfolder` with `String(subfolder || "").replace(/\\/g, "/").split("/").filter((s) => s && s !== "." && s !== "..")`, and `mirror.prune()` (`files.js:384-387`) builds keys from `path.relative(base, p).split(path.sep)` joined with `"/"`. While `docfile.keyOf()` (`electron/main/docfile.js:228`) normalizes `subfolder` the same way, `autosave.walkRefs()` (`autosave.js:249`), `host.referencedFileKeys()` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:559`), and `FileMirror.key()` (`files.js:160-162`) concatenate `${v.subfolder || ""}` verbatim. A ref with `\` or extra `/` in `subfolder`—for example from MCP `load_image` with `filename`/`subfolder` (`renderer/commands_docs.js:275`), a Windows ComfyUI custom output in a nested subfolder, or an opened `.scumble` whose `document.json` held `subfolder: "a\\b"` (`docfile.openDocument` at `docfile.js:728-790` imports to `<root>/type/a/b/name` and `renameRefs` at `lines 256-260` only updates `filename`, leaving `subfolder` untouched)—produces a keep key like `"input/a\\b/pic.png"` that misses `mirror.prune()`'s `"input/a/b/pic.png"`, deleting the file even from an open tab after 1 hour.

Checked against all known-issue lists (`known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`). This is distinct from `documents/D2+canvas-c/F1` (`2026-11-07`), which was about `host.referencedFileKeys()` not walking `ed.undo`, `ed.redo`, and `ed.snapshots` (fixed via `ed.heldFileRefs()` at `host_queue.js:569`), and from `documents/D3+main/MAIN-7` (`2026-11-07`), whose fix introduced `readState`, `unreadableCurrent`, and the `GENERATIONS` error throw in `autosave.js` while leaving `FILE` out of `referencedKeys`. Neither hole nor the `subfolder` normalization mismatch appears in any known list.

Severity is `should` (matching `D3+main/MAIN-7` and `brush-index-read-failure-deletes-tips`): hitting it requires an explicit Clean up on files >1 hour old combined with either a startup/crash read-error window or a non-normalized `subfolder`, but when triggered it permanently deletes layer/base PNGs from the local mirror—including from a live open document in the `subfolder` case—and the fix in `autosave.js` and `host_queue.js` is small.

findings.claim: ComfyView.save passes the held recipe's id (`heldId`) into `saveRecipe` even when `asNew` is true and the page never loaded `held` or the user switched to a different workflow tab. As a result, 'Save as new recipe' silently copies `held`'s non-graph metadata (`task`, `edit`, `refs`, `models`, `promptRequired`, `loras`, `needsVersion`, etc.), stored LoRA rows, and matching `(nodeId, inputName)` widget values/labels onto an unrelated workflow.
findings.scenario: Open a specialized recipe in the ComfyUI window — e.g. `relight_qwen_local` (`task: "relight"`), `upscale_model_local` (`task: "upscale"`), `moss_image_local` (`edit: false`), or `flux3_klein_local` (`promptRequired: true`, `refs: { token: "<Picture {n}>" }`, `models`, LoRA rows) — then switch to another workflow tab in ComfyUI (or have `loadWorkflow` fail so an existing page stays up). Clicking 'Save to recipe' refuses with `wrongTab()` instructing the user to 'save it as a new recipe, or switch back to its tab'. Clicking 'Save as new recipe' succeeds, but the newly saved recipe inherits `held`'s `task`/`edit`/`refs`/`promptRequired`/`models`, copies `held`'s LoRAs, and overwrites any Settings row whose `(nodeId, inputName)` collides with `held` (common on LiteGraph ids `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`) with `held`'s saved value and label — leaving a normal inpaint workflow unusable (no Use button when `task: "relight"`, refused on selection Generate when `edit: false`, or broken prompt tokens).
findings.evidence: `electron/main/comfyview.js:680-682,686,691,700`: `wrongTab()` tells the user `save it as a new recipe, or switch back to its tab`, and lines 686/691 guard only `!asNew`: `if (!asNew && (heldLoaded !== held.id || lostHeld())) return wrongTab();` and `if (!asNew && (lostHeld() || r.tabChanged || curTab !== heldTab)) return wrongTab();`, yet line 700 unconditionally sends `heldId: held ? held.id : null`: `const saved = await this.saveRecipe({ output, workflow, objectInfo, heldId: held ? held.id : null, name: asNew ? name : "", values });`. In `electron/main/main.js:1160,1178,1182,1190`, `saveComfyGraph` resolves `const base = heldId ? recipes.get(heldId) : null;`, passes `base` into `recipes.fromGraph(...)`, and emits `from: base && base.id ? base.id : null` on `comfyview:saved` (which `renderer/editor/host_presets.js` uses to clone LoRA state). In `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:154`, `if (base) for (const k of GRAPH_KEEPS) if (base[k] !== undefined) kept[k] = base[k];` copies all 15 `GRAPH_KEEPS` fields (`electron/main/recipes_graph.js:134`), and `fromPrompt` (`electron/main/recipes_graph.js:84-93,105-109`) matches `baseRow(id, name, index)` by `(node, input)` and substitutes `baseValue(id, name)` and `was.label`/`was.spec` over `pageValue(pageValues, id, name)`.
findings.fix: In `ComfyView.save` (`electron/main/comfyview.js:698-700`), only pass `held.id` when the page is still on the loaded held recipe's tab: `const onHeld = !!(held && heldLoaded === held.id && !lostHeld() && !r.tabChanged && curTab === heldTab);` and pass `heldId: onHeld ? held.id : null`.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc. In electron/main/comfyview.js:671-716 (`ComfyView.save`), `held = this.recipe`, `heldLoaded = this.loaded`, and `heldTab = this.loadedTab` are captured at lines 674-676. Lines 686 (`if (!asNew && (heldLoaded !== held.id || lostHeld())) return wrongTab();`), 691 (`if (!asNew && (lostHeld() || r.tabChanged || curTab !== heldTab)) return wrongTab();`), and 698 (`if (!asNew && lostHeld()) return wrongTab();`) guard only `!asNew`, while `wrongTab()` (lines 679-682) explicitly instructs the user: `The page shows another graph than "...": save it as a new recipe, or switch back to its tab.` Yet line 700 unconditionally passes `heldId: held ? held.id : null` into `this.saveRecipe({ output, workflow, objectInfo, heldId: held ? held.id : null, name: asNew ? name : "", values })` even when `asNew` is true and the active workflow tab is not `held` (or `held` failed to load, or `this.recipe` changed during `objectInfo()`). Moreover, once a user opens any recipe via 'Edit in ComfyUI' (`comfyview.js:360-365`), `this.recipe` remains non-null until the ComfyUI window is closed (`comfyview.js:533`) — neither Reload (`load()`, lines 567-588) nor clicking the plain ComfyUI button (`open({})`, lines 348-374) clears `this.recipe`.

Tracing the full save path confirms there is no downstream guard against an unrelated graph inheriting `held`: in `electron/main/main.js:1160`, `saveComfyGraph` resolves `const base = heldId ? list.find((r) => r.id === heldId) || null : null;` (note: `list.find`, not `recipes.get` as paraphrased in the finding's evidence). On the ComfyUI branch (`withCanvas`, line 1182), `saveComfyGraph` passes `base: base && base.kind !== "provider" ? base : null` into `recipes.fromGraph` even when `name` is non-empty, and emits `from: base ? base.id : null` on `comfyview:saved` at line 1190 (and likewise at line 1178 on the Comfy Cloud `!withCanvas` branch). In `renderer/shell.js:1558-1573`, `onSaved` calls `copySavedLoras({ id, from })`, which copies `host.loraRows(from)` via `host.saveLoras(id, ...)` (`renderer/editor/host_presets.js:137-152`) onto the newly saved recipe.

Inside `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:146-183` (`fromGraph`), line 154 copies all defined fields in `GRAPH_KEEPS` (line 134, 15 fields) from `base`, and lines 157-171 plus `normalize` (`electron/main/recipes_store.js:515-570`) only drop graph-mismatched `presets`, `task === "pass"`, `boxes`, `upsampler`, `newImage`, and `loras.model`. Unrelated workflows saved as new therefore silently retain `base`'s `task: "relight"` (e.g. `relight_qwen_local`, which hides the new recipe from the main recipe picker, blocks `selectRecipe`, and omits its Use button in `renderer/shell_settings.js:50,109-113,277-284`), `task: "upscale"` and `limits` (e.g. `upscale_model_local`), `edit: false` (e.g. `moss_image_local`, causing `host_queue.js:42` to refuse selection `Generate`), `promptRequired: true` and `refs: { name: "<Picture {n}>", slots: 16 }` (on `minimax_h3_image_local`) or `refs: { name: "<ref_image_{n0}>", slots: 4 }` (on `flux3_klein_local`, overriding graph-derived `@img` token formatting and slot counts via `comfyRefs` at `recipes_store.js:326-342`), `loras.family` or `loras: false` (`recipes_store.js:491,501-503`), `models`, and `needsVersion`. In addition, `fromPrompt` (`recipes_graph.js:84-93,105-109`) matches `baseRow(id, name, index)` by `(node, input)` and prefers `baseValue(id, name)`, `was.label`, and `was.spec` over `pageValue(pageValues, id, name)`, clobbering widget values on colliding LiteGraph/template node IDs.

Not a known issue: `main/MAIN-4` in `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json:627-638` covered `!asNew` ('Save to recipe') overwriting `held` from another tab and was fixed (tested in `tools/comfyview_test.py:1105-1199`); this finding proves a remaining hole in that fix on the `asNew` path that `wrongTab()` itself directs users to take. `docs/BUGS.md:152-160` only covers intentionally importing or saving a relight graph under a custom id rather than cross-tab inheritance onto unrelated workflows. Severity is `should`: users hit this in normal multi-tab ComfyUI use (especially after following `wrongTab()`'s prompt) and end up with a broken or misconfigured recipe on disk, with closing/reopening the ComfyUI window or editing the JSON file as a workaround.

findings.claim: When importing a UI-format workflow JSON, `fromWorkflow` resolves links through `Reroute` and bypassed (`mode === 4`) nodes into `prompt`, but looks up `InpaintCanvas` `setting_n` consumers on raw single-hop `links` with `Array.prototype.find`. Any `setting_n` output routed through a `Reroute`/bypassed node or wired to more than one input leaves raw `[canvasId, slot]` links in `prompt`, breaking execution in ComfyUI and Comfy Cloud detachment.
findings.scenario: Export a workflow JSON from ComfyUI where `InpaintCanvas`'s `setting_1` passes through a `Reroute` node (or a bypassed node) into `KSampler.steps`, or fans out to two samplers' `steps` inputs, and import it via Recipes -> Import workflow. In the imported recipe, `settings` omits the rerouted (or second) input and `prompt[samplerId].inputs.steps` remains `[canvasId, 13]`. When the user runs Generate, `host.queueGenerate` sends no `setting_1` value on `InpaintCanvas`, so `InpaintCanvas` outputs `None` on slot 13 and ComfyUI fails validating/running `KSampler.steps`; if the user detaches the recipe for Comfy Cloud, `recipes.detach` throws `reads the Inpaint Canvas node's setting_1, which a Comfy Cloud recipe cannot give`.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/recipes_workflow.js:202,221-225` skips `SKIP_TYPES` (`Reroute`, `PrimitiveNode`, `Note`, ` MarkdownNote`) and `n.mode === 4` from `prompt`, while resolving links through them so `prompt[id].inputs[inp.name] = [src.id, src.slot]` becomes `[canvasId, slot]`. `tailOutputs` (`line 248`) rewrites `setting_n` slots in `prompt` to `FIXED_OUTPUTS + n - 1`. Then lines 251-271 scan `canvasNode.outputs` with `const l = Array.from(links.values()).find((x) => x.origin === canvasId && x.originSlot === i && !instances.has(x.target) && !x.target.endsWith("-20") && prompt[x.target]);`. When `setting_n` goes into a `Reroute` or bypassed node, the link with `x.origin === canvasId` targets a node absent from `prompt` (`prompt[x.target]` is `undefined`), while the link into the real consumer has `x.origin !== canvasId`, so `l` is `undefined`. When `setting_n` fans out to multiple consumers, `.find(...)` visits only the first consumer and leaves `node.inputs[tin.name] = [canvasId, 13 + n - 1]` untouched on all other consumers (unlike `fromPrompt` at `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:98-111`, which walks every `[id, node]` in `prompt`).
findings.fix: In `fromWorkflow` (`electron/main/recipes_workflow.js:250-271`), walk `Object.entries(prompt)` and inspect resolved `[canvasId, slot]` inputs with `+v[1] >= FIXED_OUTPUTS` (matching `fromPrompt` in `recipes_graph.js:98-111`), looking up each target `(id, inputName)`'s input index on `nodes.get(id)` to pull its default from `overrides`, `widgetValues`, or `specDefault(spec)`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc` in `electron/main/recipes_workflow.js:250-271` (`fromWorkflow`), reachable from *Settings › Recipes › Import* (`electron/main/main.js:1065-1083` `importRecipe` -> `electron/main/recipes.js:276-284` `importFile` -> `fromWorkflow`). During prompt construction (`recipes_workflow.js:200-227`), `SKIP_TYPES` (`Note`, `MarkdownNote`, `PrimitiveNode`, `Reroute` at `electron/main/recipes_store.js:71`), subgraph instances, muted (`mode === 2`), and bypassed (`mode === 4`) nodes are excluded from `prompt` at line 202, while `resolve(n, inp.link)` (`lines 172-195`) traces links back through `Reroute` (`lines 180-183`), bypassed nodes (`lines 185-191`), and subgraph `-20` outputs (`lines 176-178`) so the downstream consumer's `prompt[id].inputs[inp.name]` is written as `[canvasId, slot]` at line 224. Because `prompt[canvasId]` exists, the dangling-link cleanup at lines 229-231 preserves `[canvasId, slot]`, and `tailOutputs` (`line 248`, `recipes_store.js:50-68`) walks `prompt` and normalizes any `setting_1..8` link to `[canvasId, FIXED_OUTPUTS + n - 1]` (`13..20`).

However, when extracting `settings` and substituting literal widget/default values back into `prompt` (`recipes_workflow.js:251-271`), `fromWorkflow` does not walk `prompt` (unlike `fromPrompt` in `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:98-112`). Instead, line 255 searches the raw single-hop `links` map with `.find((x) => x.origin === canvasId && x.originSlot === i && !instances.has(x.target) && !x.target.endsWith("-20") && prompt[x.target])`. When `setting_n` passes through a `Reroute` or bypassed (`mode === 4`) node (or exits a subgraph via `-20`), the link with `x.origin === canvasId` targets a node absent from `prompt` (`prompt[x.target]` is `undefined`), whereas the link targeting the real consumer in `prompt` has `x.origin !== canvasId`. `l` is therefore `undefined` (`line 256` returns early), omitting the row from `recipe.settings` and leaving `prompt[consumerId].inputs[inputName] = [canvasId, 13 + n - 1]` in the saved recipe (`normalize` in `recipes_store.js:515-570` does not strip or validate residual `canvas` setting links). Similarly, when `setting_n` fans out to multiple consumers, `.find(...)` visits only the first link, leaving `[canvasId, 13 + n - 1]` on every subsequent consumer and omitting them from `settings`.

Tracing downstream outcomes: (1) In the reroute/bypassed case, `r.settings` has no row for slot `n`, so `editor.settings[String(n)]` is never populated (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:995-1018` `settingsChanged`) and `host.queueGenerate` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:146,199-221`) neither overwrites `prompt[consumerId].inputs[inputName]` nor sends `settings[String(n)]` in `canvas_state` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:490`); `InpaintCanvas.run` (`nodes.py:455-470,810-811`) then outputs `None` on slot `13 + n - 1`, failing ComfyUI execution on the consumer input. (Note on fanout: during local `queueGenerate`, the first consumer's `r.settings` row does populate `editor.settings[String(n)]` in `canvas_state`, so `InpaintCanvas` emits that value on slot `13 + n - 1` unless recipes are switched mid-upload, though the second consumer is still missing from `r.settings` / presets / `toPrompt`.) (2) In both reroute/bypassed and fanout cases, clicking *Cloud copy* (`main.js:1089-1097` -> `recipes_graph.js:630-687` `detach`) hits the leftover `[canvasId, 13 + n - 1]` link in `r.prompt` and throws `The node <id> (<class>) reads the Inpaint Canvas node's setting_<n>, which a Comfy Cloud recipe cannot give.` at line 684.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`): only `recipes/rec-import-overwrite`, `main-net/save-as-new-overwrites-user-file`, and `S9a` touch recipe import/save IDs; this `fromWorkflow` link-resolution mismatch is unreported. Severity `should` holds: routing `InpaintCanvas` `setting_n` wires through `Reroute` nodes in ComfyUI UI exports is a normal workflow and breaks both local runs and Cloud detachment on import, with workarounds (exporting in API format or rewiring without `Reroute`) and no silent pixel/data loss or double-charging.

findings.claim: `askCompatible` strips inline `<think>...</think>` blocks using a regex that requires a closing `</think>` tag. When a reasoning model on a local/OpenAI-compatible server or custom Chat provider hits `max_tokens` (`finish_reason: "length"`) before closing `</think>`, the unclosed `<think>...` chain-of-thought is not stripped and is returned verbatim as the rewritten image prompt instead of failing with an empty-answer error.
findings.scenario: Configure a local Ollama, LM Studio, or vLLM model that emits `<think>` tags in `message.content` (such as `qwen3-vl`, `qwen3`, or `deepseek-r1`) under *Settings › Local / OpenAI-compatible endpoint* (or a custom Chat provider), and click Prompt rewrite or run Generate with auto-upsampling (`host_vlm.js:98-137`). On a complex image/reference turn where internal reasoning reaches the 4096-token `max_tokens` cap before emitting `</think>`, the server returns `finish_reason: "length"` with `msg.content = "<think>Okay, let's inspect Picture 1 and the mask..."`. `askCompatible` leaves the entire `<think>...` monologue intact, bypasses the `if (!text)` error guard (`finish_reason` would otherwise report `"length"`), overwrites the user's prompt box with raw reasoning text, and — when triggered inside `Generate` — immediately submits that `<think>...` monologue to the image generator.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/llm.js:362-366`: `text = String(text || "").replace(/<think>[\s\S]*?<\/think>/gi, "").trim();` followed by `if (!text) { const why = (out.choices && out.choices[0] && out.choices[0].finish_reason) || (out.error && out.error.message) || "no text in the answer"; throw new Error(`${model} at ${compatHost(url)}: ${why}`); }`. If `msg.content` contains an opening `<think>` without a matching `</think>`, `/<think>[\s\S]*?<\/think>/gi` does not match, `text` remains non-empty (`"<think>..."`), line 363 does not throw, and `ask()` returns `{ text }` to `renderer/editor/host_vlm.js:126-135`.
findings.fix: Match an unclosed `<think>` to end-of-string as well in `electron/main/llm.js:362`: `text = String(text || "").replace(/<think>[\s\S]*?(?:<\/think>|$)/gi, "").trim();` so truncated reasoning becomes `""` and triggers the existing `finish_reason` (`"length"`) error on lines 363-365.
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `askCompatible` in `electron/main/llm.js:360-366` extracts `msg.content` and strips inline reasoning tags with `text = String(text || "").replace(/<think>[\s\S]*?<\/think>/gi, "").trim();` (line 362), immediately followed by the empty-answer guard `if (!text) { const why = (out.choices && out.choices[0] && out.choices[0].finish_reason) || ...; throw new Error(...); }` (lines 363-366). Unlike `askOpenAI` (`llm.js:207,214-222`), `askGemini` (`llm.js:232,240-245`), and `askAnthropic` (`llm.js:259,269-271`) — which both request low reasoning effort and filter structured reasoning blocks so token exhaustion yields `text === ""` and throws — `askCompatible` sends `max_tokens: maxTokens` (default `4096` at `llm.js:423`) with no reasoning-effort cap on `compat:` (`llm.js:305,443`), `askToAPIs` (`llm.js:371-373`), `askOxen` (`llm.js:394-398`), `askChat` (`llm.js:406-410`), or user-added custom `openrouter:` rows (`llm.js:385`). When a model that emits `<think>...</think>` inside `message.content` (e.g. Qwen3, Qwen3-VL-Thinking, or DeepSeek-R1 on LM Studio, llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM without a reasoning parser, or a proxy, especially when crop + reference images consume much of a local server's default 2k-4k context window) hits `max_tokens` (`finish_reason: "length"`) before emitting `</think>`, the regex on line 362 fails to match, `text` stays non-empty (`"<think>..."`), the `if (!text)` error path on lines 363-366 is bypassed, and `llm.ask` (`llm.js:477-481`, which only strips outer code fences and quotes) returns the raw `<think>...` monologue as `{ text }`.
