Tracing all callers from `ipcMain.handle("llm:ask", ...)` (`electron/main/main.js:1368`) and `window.scumble.llm.ask` (`electron/preload.js:183`) through `HostHelpersPart.askLLM` (`renderer/editor/host_helpers.js:56-68`) confirms four reachable paths, while correcting two inaccuracies in the raw finding's renderer citations (`renderer/editor/host_vlm.js` is Florence-2 `helpers.describe`, not `llm.ask`, and clicking `Generate` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:1291-1343` / `host_queue.js:234-238` uses ComfyUI's in-graph `wireUpsampler` in `comfyprompt.js:346-400`, not `llm.js`): (1) the editor's Upsample button (`SegmentPart.upsamplePrompt` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_segment.js:225-248` -> `host.upsampleInApp` at `renderer/editor/host_helpers.js:76-86` -> `applyTextResult` at `inpaint_ed_segment.js:308-333`) overwrites `this.promptText` via `setPromptText(text)` (line 330) with the raw `<think>...` monologue; (2) the Generate new dialog's Upsample button (`renderer/shell.js:604-658`) overwrites `genField` at `shell.js:636`; (3) Select by text with an empty object field (`SegmentPart.segmentByText` with `fromPrompt` at `inpaint_ed_segment.js:54-57,75-88`) immediately queues a ComfyUI segmentation run passing the `<think>...` monologue (minus `[."']`) as the segmentation target; and (4) the MCP / Assistant `upsample_prompt` tool (`renderer/commands_gen.js:145-159`) resolves `{ prompt: "<think>..." }` instead of throwing, so an agent chaining `upsample_prompt` into `generate` submits the raw chain-of-thought straight to image generation.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (lines 1-698), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `docs/research/*/verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`): the only prior `llm.js` entries are two closed 2026-09-29 items (`vision: false` and `4xx` step-down), so this defect is not known. Severity is `should`: local/compatible vision and text reasoning models hitting the 4096-token or context limit during prompt rewriting is a plausible real-world workflow that silently corrupts the prompt field (with `Revert` as a workaround in the UI) and silently poisons `segmentByText` (`fromPrompt`) and automated `upsample_prompt` -> `generate` tool chains instead of surfacing the `finish_reason` (`"length"`) error that `llm.js:363-366` already intends to throw.

findings.claim: `askOpenAI` unconditionally sends `reasoning: { effort: "low" }` to OpenAI's `/v1/responses` endpoint for every `openai` model, unlike `askGemini` and `askAnthropic` which gate reasoning parameters by model family. Any user-added custom OpenAI non-reasoning model (such as `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, or `gpt-4.1`) is rejected by OpenAI with HTTP 400.
findings.scenario: In *Settings › Language models*, add a custom model row (`llm_custom.js`) under provider `OpenAI` with model ID `gpt-4o` or `gpt-4.1`, tick it for prompt writing (`upsample: true`), select it in the editor's prompt-rewrite picker, and click Rewrite. `askOpenAI` sends `{"model":"gpt-4.1",...,"reasoning":{"effort":"low"}}` to `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses`, and OpenAI refuses the request with HTTP 400 (`Unsupported parameter: 'reasoning.effort' is not supported with this model`).
findings.evidence: `electron/main/llm.js:207`: `const body = { model, input: [{ role: "user", content }], max_output_tokens: maxTokens, reasoning: { effort: "low" } };` sends `reasoning` unconditionally, whereas `askGemini` (`electron/main/llm.js:232`: `if (/^gemini-[34]/.test(model)) generationConfig.thinkingConfig = { thinkingLevel: "low" };`), `askAnthropic` (`electron/main/llm.js:259`: `if (/opus|sonnet-5/.test(model)) body.output_config = { effort: "low" };`), and `electron/main/assistant/responses.js:135` (`if (chat.effort) body.reasoning = { effort: chat.effort };`) all gate reasoning fields. `customModel(id)` (`electron/main/llm.js:485-493`) routes any user-added `openai:<model>` row from `llm_custom.forUpsample` straight to `ADAPTERS.openai` (`askOpenAI`).
findings.fix: Gate `reasoning: { effort: "low" }` in `askOpenAI` (`electron/main/llm.js:207`) to OpenAI reasoning model IDs (e.g. `if (/^(gpt-5|o[1-9])/i.test(model)) body.reasoning = { effort: "low" };`).
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `askOpenAI` (`electron/main/llm.js:201-224`) builds the `/v1/responses` payload at line 207 with `const body = { model, input: [{ role: "user", content }], max_output_tokens: maxTokens, reasoning: { effort: "low" } };` unconditionally and throws immediately on non-2xx at line 211 (`if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`OpenAI ${model}: ${await readError(r, key)}`);`) with no retry or parameter fallback. By contrast, every other reasoning-capable adapter in `electron/main/llm.js` gates reasoning parameters on model capability: `askGemini` checks `if (/^gemini-[34]/.test(model))` (`llm.js:232`), `askAnthropic` checks `if (/opus|sonnet-5/.test(model))` (`llm.js:259`), and `askOpenRouter` checks `if (a.row && a.row.reasoning)` (`llm.js:385`, which is unset on custom rows). (Note: `electron/main/assistant/responses.js:135` gates on `if (chat.effort)`, which defaults to `"medium"` in `assistant/index.js:36` and `"low"` in `assistant/help.js:18` unless overridden in settings, whereas `llm.js:207` offers neither a model gate nor a setting override.)

Tracing the full call path confirms no guard blocks non-reasoning OpenAI models from reaching `askOpenAI`: *Settings › Language models* (`renderer/shell.js:547-575` -> `lmSave` at `renderer/shell_settings.js:479-485`) populates its provider select from `llm_custom.options()` (`electron/main/llm_custom.js:18-30` -> `PROVIDERS.openai` in `electron/main/assistant/providers.js:57-68`), explicitly advertised in `docs/ASSISTANT.md:40-46` and `docs/PROMPTS.md:97-99` for adding cheaper or uncurated models of any supported provider for prompt upsampling (`upsample: true` by default at `llm_custom.js:56`). `llm.list()` (`llm.js:105-110`) exposes `openai:<model>` to `host.upsampleBackends()` (`renderer/editor/host_helpers.js:48-50`), and clicking Upsample in the editor (`host_helpers.js:76-86`) or in *Generate new* (`renderer/shell.js:604-625`) invokes `window.scumble.llm.ask` -> `main.js:1368` -> `llm.ask` (`llm.js:451,460`) -> `customModel(id)` (`llm.js:485-493`) -> `ADAPTERS.openai` (`askOpenAI`). When the user configures any non-reasoning OpenAI model such as `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4.1`, or `gpt-4.1-mini`, OpenAI's `/v1/responses` endpoint rejects `reasoning.effort` with HTTP 400 (`Unsupported parameter: 'reasoning.effort' is not supported with this model.`).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (open and fixed sections; line 443 covers only `vision: false` in `llm.ask`), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: this defect is not previously recorded or planned. Severity is `should`: there is no silent pixel/data loss or wasted charge (the 400 fails visibly before modifying the prompt), and workarounds exist (using a built-in `gpt-5.6-*` model, OpenRouter, or the OpenAI-compatible endpoint), but a documented user workflow (*Settings › Language models* with standard non-reasoning OpenAI models) fails 100% of the time.

findings.claim: providers.edit runs resolveNames() (the TOKEN / MARKER_ANY safety net, the empty-reference shift guard, and res.refs tracking) only on req.prompt and req.negative before boxes.applyBoxes() rewrites req.prompt and builds the box rows. Inside providers/boxes.js, resolved() only runs numeric resolveMarkers() and never checks TOKEN or MARKER_ANY (and elementIdeogram4 never resolves b.text at all). Unresolved @img tokens or literal {@ref: strings inside a box's desc or text therefore bypass the main-process safety net and are sent verbatim in a paid FLUX 3 or Ideogram 4 run, and an empty buffer in request.references without a prompt marker silently shifts b.ref / box {@ref:i} to the wrong reference picture.
findings.scenario: Select FLUX 3 Image or Ideogram 4 with one visible reference layer (@img1) and an empty or plain prompt. In the Boxes panel (or via MCP boxes.add / boxes.set), set a New box's description to "a hat like @img2" (or "@IMG1", which boxes_model.js's case-sensitive /@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g skips, or "@img1" when no reference layer exists) and click Generate. runDesc (boxes_model.js:247) leaves @img2 / @IMG1 unchanged; resolveNames (index.js:299) sees no marker or token in req.prompt; boxes.applyBoxes (index.js:307-308) then injects "a hat like @img2" into req.prompt and the JSON box rows, and the paid API run goes out and is billed instead of refusing before send as the main prompt does. Likewise, if request.references carries [emptyBuffer, refA, refB] and req.prompt has no {@ref: marker, resolveNames skips the given !== req.references.length guard (index.js:156-158), so a From box with b.ref = 1 resolves against the compacted list and sends refB instead of refusing.
findings.evidence: electron/main/providers/index.js:268 compacts `references: (request.references || []).map(toBuffer).filter(Boolean)`. At :154-175 `resolveNames` checks `if (given !== req.references.length)` (:158) only when `MARKER_ANY.test(t)` is true on `req.prompt`/`req.negative`, and runs `TOKEN.exec(t)` / `MARKER_ANY.test(t)` (:171-173) only on `out.prompt` and `out.negative`. At :299-308 `named = resolveNames(p, req, lay, stripped ? 0 : given); req.prompt = named.prompt;` runs before `const a = boxes.applyBoxes(req, lay); req.prompt = a.prompt;`, with no post-check on `req.prompt` or `a.rows`, and `:417` returns `refs: named.refs` without box references. In electron/main/providers/boxes.js:117-121 `resolved` runs only `const r = resolveMarkers(fold(s), lay.pictures, patternOf(req)); if (r.left.length) throw ...`, which matches numeric `/\{@ref:(\d+)\}/g` only, and `:273-277` `elementIdeogram4` passes `text: fold(b.text)` without `resolved()`. In renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:23,247 `TOKEN = /@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g` and `runDesc` leave unknown `@imgN` and uppercase `@IMG1` as literal text.
findings.fix: Move the `if (!stripped && given !== req.references.length)` guard before both `resolveNames` and `boxes.applyBoxes` whenever any prompt, negative, `b.ref != null`, or box `desc`/`text` carries a marker. In `boxes.js` `resolved()` (and on `b.text` in `elementIdeogram4`), enforce the same `TOKEN` and `MARKER_ANY` refusal checks after `resolveMarkers` and collect resolved `{ ref, name }` entries into `res.refs` (or re-run the `TOKEN` / `MARKER_ANY` safety net on the final `req.prompt` and serialized box rows in `index.js`).
findings.why:
Confirmed on the main-process prompt/box ordering, safety-net bypass, and `res.refs` omission, with two sub-claims narrowed/refuted after tracing all callers at `f45a86cc`.

1. **Confirmed core bug (`electron/main/providers/index.js:299-308, 417` and `electron/main/providers/boxes.js:117-121`):** `resolveNames()` (`index.js:151-176`) enforces Scumble's main-process safety net (`TOKEN.exec(t)` at `:171` for unresolved `@img1..@img999` / `@img?L...` case-insensitively, and `MARKER_ANY.test(t)` at `:173` for any leftover `{@ref:`) only on `req.prompt` and `req.negative` at `:299`, *before* `boxes.applyBoxes(req, lay)` runs at `:307-308` and overwrites `req.prompt = a.prompt`. Inside `boxes.js:117-121`, `resolved()` only runs `resolveMarkers(fold(s), lay.pictures, patternOf(req))` (`refs.js:99-114`, matching complete numeric `/\{@ref:(\d+)\}/g` only) and checks `r.left.length` — it never checks `TOKEN` or `MARKER_ANY`, and it discards `r.refs`. At `f45a86cc`, this is directly reachable end-to-end from UI and MCP (`plugins/boxes/main.js:60-62, 221, 309, 383-394`, `boxes_tool.js:95`): (a) unknown `@img2` or uppercase `@IMG1` in a box `desc` (left literal by `boxes_model.js:23, 247` `runDesc`, also noted in sibling candidate `prompt-refs/box-desc-unknown-or-cased-token-sent-to-api`) bypasses `index.js:171` and goes out verbatim in a billed FLUX 3 or Ideogram 4 API request when the main prompt has no bad token; (b) even independent of `runDesc`, a literal `{@ref:` string in `b.desc` (typed/pasted in the Boxes panel or `boxes.add`, or produced by `DESC_MAX` slicing mid-marker in `prompt-refs/box-desc-marker-cut-at-400`) and any unresolved token from a `scumble.generate` plugin (`renderer/plugins.js:472-494` -> `renderer/editor/boxes.js:150-200` `pluginBoxes`, which only checks `LAYER_MARK`) bypass `host_provider.js:40` and `index.js:171-173` and are sent in the paid prompt; and (c) because `boxes.js:118` drops `r.refs` and `index.js:417` returns `refs: named.refs`, naming `@img1` only in a New box's `desc` (the exact pattern `boxes.js:139` instructs users to use on FLUX 3 Generate new) leaves `res.refs` empty so `host_generate.js:145-148` (`commands_runs.js:68` `generate_new`) reports `references[i].sentAs: null` and `host_provider.js:414` returns `refs: []`.

2. **Narrowed/refuted sub-claim — empty-reference shift (`index.js:158, 268`):** While `index.js:158` (`if (given !== req.references.length)`) indeed only runs when `req.prompt` or `req.negative` matches `MARKER_ANY` (`:156`) and would fail to guard `b.ref` or box `{@ref:i}` if `req.references` shrank at `:268`, two caveats hold: first, `[emptyBuffer, refA, refB]` (`Buffer.alloc(0)` or `new Uint8Array(0)`) does **not** shrink `req.references`, because `toBuffer(v)` (`index.js:96-102`) checks `if (!v) return null;` and a 0-byte `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` is a truthy object kept by `.filter(Boolean)` — only falsy entries (`null`, `undefined`, `""`) are compacted out; second, every first-party UI and MCP caller (`host_provider.js:326` -> `stitch.js:874, 888, 969` `prepareCropAsync` and `host_generate.js:64` -> `stitch.js:753-758` `referenceBytes`) builds `request.references` via `canvasBytes()` (`stitch.js:741-744`), which always returns a `Uint8Array` (or throws `TypeError` on `null.arrayBuffer()` before IPC). Thus `given !== req.references.length` is unreachable from normal renderer/MCP workflows and is strictly a defense-in-depth IPC check against direct `window.scumble.providers.edit` / `providers.edit` calls carrying `null`/`undefined` in `references`.

3. **Refuted sub-claim — `elementIdeogram4` `b.text` (`boxes.js:276`):** `b.text` is plain literal signage words to render as pixels in the image by design (`boxes_model.js:12, 302`, `plugins/boxes/main.js:57-59`), never prompt prose referencing a layer. Neither `plugins/boxes/main.js:221`, `renderer/editor/boxes.js:197` (`pluginBoxes`), nor `inpaint_ed_refs.js:102-115` (`remapBoxDescs`) ever converts `@img` or `{@layer:}` in `b.text` into `{@ref:i}`, and `recipes/ideogram_4.json` on `fal` (`fal.js:176-177`) drops all reference images anyway. `b.text` should not run `resolveMarkers` or `TOKEN` refusal (a user may legitimately want a sign reading `"@img1"` rendered in the picture).

4. **Known-issues check & severity:** Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Open`), `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` (`prompt-refs/box-desc-tokens-not-remapped` was the already-fixed `refsMutated` remap bug), `review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` — not known. Severity is `should`: in normal FLUX 3 / Ideogram 4 box workflows at `f45a86cc`, an unresolved `@img` token or literal `{@ref:` in `b.desc` bypasses main's pre-flight refusal and sends a billed API request with broken prompt text (note: if `boxes_model.js` `runDesc` and `DESC_MAX` slicing are fixed via the sibling `prompt-refs` findings, the remaining main-process-only gaps — literal `{@ref:`, `res.refs` omission on `generate_new`, plugin safety net, and IPC `null`-ref compaction — still warrant fixing in `index.js`/`boxes.js` as defense-in-depth plus `res.refs` correctness).

findings.claim: While util.js pollJob (fal, Replicate, WaveSpeed) was fixed in 0.1.57 to always read status once after waking from sleep past waitMs and to ride out a 120 s outage window, the hand-rolled poll loops in bfl.js, toapis.js, and magnific.js still enforce `Date.now() - t0 > waitMs` at the top of the loop before reading status and give up after 5-6 consecutive misses (~15 s on BFL/Magnific). In addition, toapis.js calls `await r.json()` on HTTP 200 status polls with no try/catch, so a single truncated or HTML 200 proxy response throws SyntaxError and abandons a billed ToAPIs task; and none of the three adapters sets ctx.jobDone = true before downloading the finished result, misreporting a Cancel during download.
findings.scenario: A user submits a paid FLUX 3 Pro edit on BFL, a Precision 16x upscale on Magnific, or a GPT Image edit on ToAPIs, and closes the laptop lid for 20 minutes (past the 15-minute poll deadline, or 30 minutes on Magnific upscale). The job finishes and is billed upstream within a minute. On wake, the pending sleep resolves and the first status GET runs while Wi-Fi is still reconnecting, throwing ENOTFOUND/ECONNRESET; `continue` jumps to the top of the loop, where `Date.now() - t0 > 15 * 60 * 1000` immediately throws timeout without ever reading the finished job (and on BFL without naming `job.id`). Even without sleep, on ToAPIs a single truncated or HTML 200 response from a gateway/captive proxy during status polling throws an uncaught SyntaxError at `toapis.js:447` and loses the paid task; or a ~16 s Wi-Fi drop exhausts BFL's `++misses > 5` / Magnific's `POLL_FAILURES_MAX = 5` (5 x 3 s = 15 s).
findings.evidence: electron/main/providers/bfl.js:126-142 checks `if (Date.now() - t0 > 15 * 60 * 1000) throw new Error("BFL: timed out after 15 minutes");` at the top of `for (;;)`, retries thrown fetches only up to `if (++misses > 5)` (1+2+3+4+5 = 15 s), and at :154-160 downloads `s.result.sample` without setting `ctx.jobDone = true`. electron/main/providers/toapis.js:423-447 checks `if (Date.now() - t0 > TIMEOUT_MS)` at the loop top and executes `const j = (await r.json()) || {};` at :447 with no try/catch (nor `ctx.jobDone = true` before `download` at :498). electron/main/providers/magnific.js:576-587 checks `if (ctx.now() - t0 > waitMs)` at the loop top, gives up at `POLL_FAILURES_MAX` (5 * 3 s = 15 s), and never sets `ctx.jobDone = true` before `fetchResult` (:711). Contrast `electron/main/providers/util.js:250-306` (`pollJob`: `rem <= 0 && answered`, `gapMs: 120000`, `readSignal()`).
findings.fix: Migrate `bfl.js`, `toapis.js`, and `magnific.js` onto `util.pollJob` (or apply its `answered` / 120 s `gapWatch` + per-read timeout rules), wrap `toapis.js:447` `r.json()` in a `try/catch` that counts a malformed 200 body as a transient lost query, include `job.id` in BFL's timeout/poll errors, and set `ctx.jobDone = true` once status reaches `Ready` / `completed` / `COMPLETED` before downloading the image.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc across `electron/main/providers/bfl.js`, `toapis.js`, `magnific.js`, `util.js`, `index.js`, and `electron/main/curlfetch.js`. While `util.js:252-330` (`pollJob`, used by `fal.js`, `replicate.js`, and `wavespeed.js`) was fixed in 0.1.56 (`CHANGELOG.md:91`; note the candidate claim says 0.1.57, a harmless version-number slip) to enforce `if (rem <= 0 && answered)` (`util.js:290`), bound unanswered reads by a 120 s `gapWatch()` window (`TIMES.gapMs = 120000` at `util.js:79-94`), attach a 30 s per-read `readSignal()` (`util.js:96-98, 305`), and parse bodies defensively via `readBody()` (`util.js:188-201`), the three hand-rolled pollers in `bfl.js`, `toapis.js`, and `magnific.js` were left on the pre-fix pattern. None of the three providers receives a pre-completion `cloudjobs` store (`providers/index.js:597` only attaches `ctx.jobs` when `id === "comfycloud"`), so an abandoned poll permanently loses the billed result from Scumble.

Tracing each call path from `providers.edit` (`electron/main/providers/index.js:314`): (1) In `bfl.js:120-152` (`edit` and `generate`), after the paid job is accepted at `:120-122`, the `for (;;)` loop checks `if (Date.now() - t0 > 15 * 60 * 1000) throw new Error("BFL: timed out after 15 minutes");` at `:127` before polling. If the machine sleeps past 15 minutes during `await (ctx.sleep || sleep)(1000)` (`:128`), the first status `ctx.fetch` on wake (`:137`) runs while Wi-Fi is still reconnecting, throws `ENOTFOUND`/`ECONNRESET` (or curl exit 6), enters `retry` (`:131-134`, `misses = 1`, sleeping 1 s), and hits `continue` (`:141`), where `:127` immediately throws timeout without ever reading the finished job (and without naming `job.id` at `:127` or `:132`, even though BFL `result.sample` URLs are short-lived). Without sleep, 6 consecutive failed reads exhaust `++misses > 5` (`:132`) after 5 `retry` sleeps (`1+2+3+4+5 = 15 s`) plus 5 loop-top 1 s sleeps (`20 s` total), and `:137` has no per-read timeout signal so a half-open post-sleep socket waits up to `STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (300 s in `curlfetch.js:106` / undici). (2) In `magnific.js:572-600` (`edit`, `generate`, `relight` with `EDIT_WAIT_MS = 15 min`, and `upscale` with `UPSCALE_WAIT_MS = 30 min`), `:578` checks `if (ctx.now() - t0 > waitMs) throw ...` at the top of `while (task.status !== "COMPLETED")`, giving the identical wake-from-sleep failure when the first `send()` (`:582`) fails before Wi-Fi is back, and `:585` (`if (++failures >= POLL_FAILURES_MAX) throw tooMany()`) aborts on the 5th failed read after only 4 sleeps of `POLL_MS = 3000 ms` (`12 s` between first and fifth failure, `15 s` including the initial 3 s wait). (3) In `toapis.js:419-457`, `:424` checks `if (Date.now() - t0 > TIMEOUT_MS)` at the top of `for (;;)` (same post-sleep drop, and `++lost > LOST_QUERIES` at `:432` gives up after 5 waits of 5-6 s, ~25-30 s). Worse, at `toapis.js:447`, after `if (!r.ok)` (`:446`), it executes `const j = (await r.json()) || {};` with no `try/catch`: a single HTTP 200 HTML gateway/captive-proxy page, empty 200 body, or mid-body stream reset (`TypeError: terminated` in `curlfetch.js:187` after 200 headers) throws uncaught `SyntaxError`/`TypeError`, abandoning the billed task on the first glitch without even naming `task ${id}`.

The `ctx.jobDone` sub-claim also holds across all three adapters, with a subtle spread detail in two of them: `providers/index.js:326` checks `ctx.jobDone === true` on the original `ctx` object created by `contextFor` (`:282`) to distinguish `'the job had already finished ... and is charged; its picture was not kept'` from `'Scumble stopped waiting ..., which may still finish the job and charge it'` (`:329`). `bfl.js:154-160` never sets `ctx.jobDone = true` once `status === "Ready"` before its download loop, and both `toapis.js:481` and `magnific.js:656` reassign `ctx = { ...ctx, ... }` at the start of `run()` without keeping a reference to the caller's `ctx` (unlike `oxen.js:618` `const caller = ctx` and `comfyrouter.js:973` `const flags = ctx`) and never set `jobDone = true` before `download` (`toapis.js:500`) or `fetchResult` (`magnific.js:710`).

Checked against all known-issue sources (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the three `verified.json` files): not `known`. `providers/PRV-1` (2026-11-07) and `providers/polljob-deadline-before-reread` + `providers/wavespeed-cancel-words-after-completion` (2026-11-12 `verified.json:438, 731`) were scoped specifically to `util.js` `pollJob` (`fal`, `Replicate`, `WaveSpeed`) and `wavespeed.js`, and both were fixed in 0.1.56 (`wavespeed.js:310`, `util.js:274-327`). The 2026-11-12 `reviewer_notes.providers` (`verified.json:821`) mentioned in passing that `bfl.js` had a deadline-at-top loop outside PRV-1, without filing a finding or covering `toapis.js` (`r.json()` / poll) or `magnific.js`. Severity is `should`, matching the 2026-11-12 calibration on `providers/polljob-deadline-before-reread`: a ~12-20 s Wi-Fi drop on Magnific/BFL, a laptop sleep past `waitMs`, or a single non-JSON/truncated 200 status response on ToAPIs loses a paid generation in plausible real-world use, though it requires a network/gateway disruption rather than failing on every run.

findings.claim: When `openCloudResults` recovers a non-`layers` paid picture (a finished Comfy Cloud job or a paid provider result kept in `<userData>/results/`), it calls `cloudJobs.api.ack(p.jobId)` immediately after `ed.loadFile(...)` without flushing and saving `autosave.json` first. `ed.loadFile` only schedules a 1.5 s debounced `host.saveAll()`, whereas `ack` synchronously deletes the job from `cloudjobs.json` and unlinks the kept result file, so a crash in that window or a failed `state.save` permanently loses the paid image. In addition, if `ed.loadFile` fails (`!ed.base`), `openCloudResults` leaves the newly created empty background tab open and writes the error onto that hidden tab instead of `host.editor`.
findings.scenario: A paid fal/OpenAI/BFL/Comfy Cloud run finishes while Scumble's window was closed or reloaded, so `<userData>/results/<job>.png` and its `cloudjobs.json` entry are brought back on the next start via `openCloudResults`. `ed.loadFile` loads the image into a background tab and triggers `host.changed(ed)` (1500 ms timer, `host_queue.js:505`), and `openCloudResults` immediately awaits `cloudJobs.api.ack(p.jobId)`, unlinking `<userData>/results/<job>.png` and removing the job record. Before the 1.5 s timer fires (for example during a startup restore crash that trips `CrashGuard`, or when `state:save` hits `ENOSPC`/`EPERM`), the renderer exits: the paid result is gone from `results/`, `cloudjobs.json`, and `autosave.json`. Conversely, if `loadFile` fails because the mirror write fails (`!ed.base`), the hidden empty `Untitled` tab stays in the tab bar (accumulating in `autosave.json` on each start) and the user never sees the error set on the hidden tab.
findings.evidence: `renderer/shell.js:1651-1668` (the `p.kind === "layers"` branch right above) explicitly enforces durability before `ack`: `await host.flushEditor(ed); durable = got.layers.every((l) => l.ref); if (durable) await window.scumble.state.save(JSON.stringify(host.bundle())); ... if (durable) { try { await cloudJobs.api.ack(p.jobId); } ... }`, and on failure (`1647-1648`) runs `await closeDocument(ed, { force: true, remember: false }); if (host.editor) host.editor.setStatus(said, "error");`. By contrast, `renderer/shell.js:1674-1686` runs `await ed.loadFile(new File([p.bytes], name, { type: p.mime || "image/png" }), { ask: false }); if (!ed.base) { ed.setStatus(..., "error"); continue; } ... try { await cloudJobs.api.ack(p.jobId); } catch (_) {}`. `ed.loadFile` only calls `this.notifyChanged()` -> `host.changed(this)` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:503-505`: `this._saveTimer = setTimeout(() => this.saveAll(), 1500)`), while `ackCloudJob` (`electron/main/providers/index.js:769-779`) immediately removes `jobId` from `cloudjobs.json` and unlinks `entry.resultFile`.
findings.fix: In `openCloudResults` (`renderer/shell.js:1674-1686`), mirror the `p.kind === "layers"` branch: when `!ed.base`, capture `ed.status`, await `closeDocument(ed, { force: true, remember: false })`, and report the error on `host.editor`; when `ed.base` is set (and `ed.base.ref` is stored), await `window.scumble.state.save(JSON.stringify(host.bundle()))` and call `cloudJobs.api.ack(p.jobId)` only after that save succeeds.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc` in `renderer/shell.js:1674-1686`. In `openCloudResults` (`renderer/shell.js:1626-1700`), each recovered item creates a background tab via `const ed = newDocument()` (`1631`). Because startup (`shell.js:1494-1495`) and `closeDocument` (`shell.js:328-329`) guarantee `host.editor` is already non-null, `newDocument()` -> `host.addEditor(editor)` (`renderer/editor/host_state.js:216-226`) keeps the existing `host.editor` active and hides `ed.root` with `shell-hidden`. Right above, the `p.kind === "layers"` branch added on 2026-11-16 (`renderer/shell.js:1639-1673`) explicitly flushes `ed`, awaits `window.scumble.state.save(JSON.stringify(host.bundle()))` (`1654-1656`), and calls `cloudJobs.api.ack(p.jobId)` only when `durable` is true (`1668`); on failure (`!got`, `1643-1650`) it closes `ed` with `closeDocument(ed, { force: true, remember: false })` and reports the error on `host.editor`. By contrast, the non-`layers` branch (`renderer/shell.js:1674-1690`) awaits `ed.loadFile(...)` (`1674`) and, when `ed.base` is truthy, immediately awaits `cloudJobs.api.ack(p.jobId)` (`1686`) without saving `autosave.json` first.

Tracing `ed.loadFile` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:157-214`): for a PNG/JPEG/WebP, `loadFile` uploads the image into `<userData>/files/input/` via `uploadBlob` (`186, 193`, `electron/main/files.js:113-151`) and calls `setBasePixels` / `setBase` (`200, 205`), which ends with `this.notifyChanged()` (`154`). `host.changed` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:503-506`) only schedules `this._saveTimer = setTimeout(() => this.saveAll(), 1500)` (which `saveAll` at `534-538` defers again while `this._restoring` is truthy and invokes with `.catch(() => {})`, ignoring write errors from `electron/main/autosave.js:138-151`). Meanwhile, `cloudJobs.api.ack(p.jobId)` -> `ipcMain.handle("provider:ackCloudJob")` (`electron/main/main.js:1360`) -> `ackCloudJob` (`electron/main/providers/index.js:769-779`) synchronously removes `jobId` from `<userData>/cloudjobs.json` (`cloudjobs.js:166-173`) and unlinks `<userData>/results/<entry.file>` (`cloudjobs.js:60-64`). If the renderer crashes or is killed before the 1.5 s timer fires, or if `state:save` fails (`ENOSPC`, persistent `EPERM`/`EBUSY`, or an unreadable `autosave.json` whose rename fails at `autosave.js:145`), the tab is absent from `autosave.json` while both the `cloudjobs.json` note and `<userData>/results/` file are already gone (leaving only an unreferenced mirror copy in `<userData>/files/input/` that Scumble never reopens and `files:prune` at `main.js:1257-1263` deletes).

The second half of the claim (`!ed.base` at `renderer/shell.js:1675-1680`) also holds: when `ed.loadFile` fails (for instance on a corrupt download, `checkBaseSize` refusal, or failed mirror upload), `openCloudResults` leaves the empty `Untitled` background tab in `host._editors` (where `bundle()` at `host_queue.js:522-529` serializes it as `state: "{}"` into `autosave.json`, accumulating another empty tab on each retry) and calls `ed.setStatus(..., "error")` on that hidden tab instead of `host.editor`. When no other picture opened and `r.kept === 0`, both `openCloudResults` (`1691`) and `cloudCountWords` (`1607-1619`) return `""`, so `recoverCloudResults` (`1594-1596`) writes nothing at all to `host.editor`'s status bar.

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: `main/MAIN-2` (2026-11-07) and `providers/split-pagegone-keeps-base-only` / the 2026-11-16 `BUGS.md:107` split-recovery fix are adjacent, but no entry records `openCloudResults` acking non-`layers` results before a durable `state.save` or leaking empty hidden tabs on `!ed.base`.

Severity is calibrated to `should` rather than `must`: a normal window close, reload, or update install inside the 1.5 s debounce window is protected by `QuitGuard` -> `flushAll` -> `saveBeforeRestart` (`electron/main/main.js:407, 553, 1555`; `renderer/shell.js:985-991, 1042`), which flushes `autosave.json`. Losing the recovered tab therefore requires a compound failure—first a reload/close/crash during a paid run, and then either a second renderer crash/kill inside the 1.5 s debounce window right after recovery or a `state:save` disk error—while the `!ed.base` branch preserves the unacked job and only leaks empty tabs and hides the error message.

findings.claim: Clicking `Restart now` in `Settings › Rendering` (`ui.setTilesRestart`) calls `saveBeforeRestart` and `window.scumble.relaunch()` without awaiting `host.docSavesIdle()`. In main, `app:relaunch` calls `quitGuard.release()` and `app.quit()`, bypassing `flushAll` (`documents.idle()`) and triggering `will-quit` -> `documents.abortAll()`, which silently aborts any in-flight `.scumble` save. The same handler also filters `host.editors().filter(busy)` without `localRendering(ed)`, skipping the confirmation prompt when a local ComfyUI render is running.
findings.scenario: On a 15000 x 10000 multi-layer `.scumble` document, the user presses `Ctrl+S` (which flushes dirty layers and streams the `.scumble` archive over several seconds), then opens `Settings › Rendering`, toggles `Tile engine`, and clicks `Restart now`. `setTilesRestart` shows no warning, does not await `host.docSavesIdle()`, finishes `saveBeforeRestart`, and invokes `app:relaunch`. Main releases `quitGuard` and quits immediately; `will-quit` aborts the unfinished `.scumble` write and deletes its temp file, leaving the `.scumble` file on disk un-updated with no error. Likewise, if a local ComfyUI generation is running (`localRendering(ed)` true, `busy(ed)` false), `Restart now` quits without asking and drops the incoming result.
findings.evidence: `renderer/shell.js:971-978`: `ui.setTilesRestart.addEventListener("click", async () => { const working = host.editors().filter(busy); if (working.length && !(await dialogs.confirm(...))) return; ... await saveBeforeRestart((text) => { ui.setTilesNote.textContent = text; }); await window.scumble.relaunch(); });` — compare `renderer/shell.js:985-991` (`window.scumble.state.onFlush`), which runs `await host.docSavesIdle(); await saveBeforeRestart(say, when);`, and `renderer/shell_updates.js:207` / `renderer/shell.js:300`, which check `busy(ed) || localRendering(ed)`. In `electron/main/main.js:1540-1544`, `ipcMain.handle("app:relaunch", ...)` runs `quitGuard.release(); ... app.relaunch(...); setImmediate(() => app.quit());`, skipping `flushAll` (`main.js:523: await documents.idle()`) and hitting `main.js:1582-1586`: `app.on("will-quit", () => { if (!documents.busy && !fileSaves.busy) return; documents.abortAll(); ... });`.
findings.fix: In `ui.setTilesRestart`'s click handler (`renderer/shell.js:972-977`), check `host.editors().filter((ed) => busy(ed) || localRendering(ed))` and `await host.docSavesIdle()` before `saveBeforeRestart` (and in `main.js` `app:relaunch`, await `documents.idle()` before `quitGuard.release()`).
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in renderer/shell.js:971-982 and electron/main/main.js:1535-1545, 1582-1587. Both code gaps exist, with one important nuance on the Ctrl+S scenario that keeps severity at should rather than must.

First, the missing local ComfyUI render check holds unconditionally. In renderer/shell.js:219-229, busy(editor) checks pending, segmentPending, cutoutPending, upsamplePending, objectsPending, _loading, providerPending, and _docSaving, while intentionally leaving out _localRuns (tracked separately by localRendering(editor) at lines 227-229, populated by queueGenerate in renderer/editor/host_queue.js:298). Whereas closeDocument (shell.js:300, 311), ui.genGo (shell.js:702), and installUpdate (renderer/shell_updates.js:207) all check localRendering(ed) / _localRuns alongside busy(ed), ui.setTilesRestart's click handler at shell.js:972 runs `const working = host.editors().filter(busy);`. Consequently, if a user starts a local ComfyUI generation and then toggles Settings > Rendering > Tile engine and clicks Restart now, working is empty, no confirmation dialog is shown, and the app restarts immediately, losing the in-flight local render result.

Second, the missing .scumble save wait in setTilesRestart and app:relaunch also holds, though the reviewer's scenario misses that busy(editor) at shell.js:220 already includes editor._docSaving (set throughout host.saveDocument in renderer/editor/host_documents.js:201-264). Thus, if Ctrl+S is already in flight before Restart now is clicked, setTilesRestart does show the generic "A document is still working. Restart anyway?" prompt rather than no warning at all. Even so, the defect remains real: (1) per docs/PLAN_DOCUMENTS.md §4.5, app-level restarts/closes/updates are meant to wait for .scumble writes rather than abort them — window.scumble.state.onFlush (shell.js:985-991) awaits host.docSavesIdle() before saveBeforeRestart, and main's flushAll (main.js:521-525, used by window close, reloadWindow, and update:install at main.js:1555) awaits documents.idle(), so even confirming installUpdate's busy prompt still lets an in-flight .scumble save finish; by contrast, confirming Restart in setTilesRestart (or clicking Restart now when an update is downloaded, where shell_settings.js:974 says "Restart now also installs <version>" and main.js:1541 calls installOrReset() directly) skips both host.docSavesIdle() and documents.idle(), calls quitGuard.release() (main.js:1540), and hits app.on("will-quit") -> documents.abortAll() (main.js:1582-1586), silently deleting the temp file and leaving the .scumble file on disk un-updated; and (2) while saveBeforeRestart is running (up to 60 s for layer uploads or selection encoding, shell.js:1004-1042), ui.settings can still be closed with Escape (shell.js:1067), so a Ctrl+S started during saveBeforeRestart bypasses the already-passed line 972 check and is aborted without any prompt.

Checked docs/BUGS.md, scratch/known_index.md, all three verified.json files, and docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md: this is not known. documents/D5 (2026-11-07) covers image exports (fileSaves) not awaited by onFlush/flushAll, and shell/gen-new-closes-tab-of-running-local-render (2026-11-12) covered ui.genGo before localRendering() was introduced (making setTilesRestart a missed caller). Severity is should (not must): paid provider runs set providerPending so they do get the confirmation prompt, and saveBeforeRestart (shell.js:976) still flushes dirty layers/masks/maps to autosave.json before relaunch while documents.abortAll() leaves the prior .scumble target untouched, so no session pixels or money are permanently lost, but local ComfyUI renders are silently dropped on restart and .scumble disk writes are silently aborted instead of awaited.

findings.claim: For in-app assistant tool calls, `onRequest` captures `snapshotTurn` and calls `ed.pushUndo(...)` for `meta.undo` before `commands.call(name, args)` validates arguments or document/layer preconditions. Because `pushUndoSnapshot` immediately releases and empties `ed.redo` and trims `ed.undo`, a tool call that throws validation in `commands.call` permanently destroys the user's redo history, leaves a no-op `Assistant: ...` step on the undo stack, and enables `Undo this turn` even when no write succeeded.
findings.scenario: The user paints several strokes, presses `Ctrl+Z` three times (`ed.redo.length === 3`), and asks the assistant to add a filter or adjust a layer. The model calls `add_filter` with an unknown parameter/type (or `set_layer` with `match: 50` on a filter layer, `add_text` with `line_height: 0`, or `add_image_layer` with a bad path). `shell.js:1457-1465` runs `snapshotTurn` and `ed.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Assistant: add filter" })`, which releases and clears all 3 redo steps (`inpaint_ed_history.js:489-490`), and then `commands.call` throws an error without changing the document. The user's redo stack is gone, `Ctrl+Z` now steps onto a no-op `Assistant: add filter` entry, and if the turn ends, `Undo this turn` is offered for a turn that changed nothing.
findings.evidence: `renderer/shell.js:1453-1468`: `if (meta && meta.turn) { snapshotTurn(meta, args && args.doc); if (meta.undo && meta.undo.kind) { const ed = editorOf(args && args.doc); if (ed && typeof ed.pushUndo === "function") { const label = \`Assistant: ${String(name).replace(/_/g, " ")}\`; try { ed.pushUndo(...); } ... } } } reply(await commands.call(name, args || {}));`. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:489-493`, `pushUndoSnapshot` runs `for (const s of this.redo) this.releaseSnapshot(s); this.redo = []; this.undo.push(snap); ... this.trimUndo();`. Meanwhile validation in `commands_edit.js:61-65` (`add_filter`), `commands_edit.js:165` (`add_text`, whose comment notes `// refused before the layer is added: a call that fails adds nothing`), `commands_layers.js:42,53` (`set_layer`), and `commands.js:84` (`def.needsImage`) runs inside `commands.call` after `pushUndo` has already wiped `ed.redo`.
findings.fix: Take the undo snapshot before `commands.call` via `ed.snapshot(...)` without pushing it yet, run `const res = await commands.call(name, args || {})`, and if `!res.ok`, release the snapshot with `ed.releaseSnapshot(snap)` instead of calling `ed.pushUndoSnapshot`; if `res.ok` (or if the document mutated before failing), push the captured snapshot onto `ed.undo`. Likewise commit the turn snapshot only once a call succeeds.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `window.scumble.commands.onRequest` in `renderer/shell.js:1453-1468` runs both `snapshotTurn(meta, args && args.doc)` (line 1457) and `ed.pushUndo(...)` (line 1463) synchronously before `reply(await commands.call(name, args || {}))` (line 1468). Tracing from the main-process assistant loop (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:129-145, 855-875`), every tool call not in `policy.READS` carries `meta.turn = turn.id` and `meta.undo` from `policy.undoStep` (`electron/main/assistant/policy.js:555-580`), which returns `"layers"` for `add_paint_layer`, `add_filter`, `add_text`, `add_image_layer`, `film_apply_look` (when adding a layer), and `relight` (without `layer`), `"text"` or `"layers"` for `set_text`, and `"match"` or `"layers"` for `set_layer` with soft fields. The in-memory MCP server (`electron/main/mcp/server.js:114-122`) uses low-level `Server.setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, ...)` with no JSON-Schema rejection, and many invalid calls are schema-valid anyway (e.g. `add_filter`'s `type` string and untyped `params` object).

When a document has a loaded image (`ed.sel != null`) and a tool call fails validation inside `commands.call` (`renderer/commands.js:119-131`) before mutating the document — such as `add_filter` (`POLICY.add_filter = AUTO`, `renderer/commands_edit.js:60-63`: unknown filter type, `ownPixels`, `checkParams` failure, or non-depth limit on a fill layer), `set_layer` (`renderer/commands_layers.js:42,49,53,57`: invalid `blend`/`role`/`match_source`, or `match` on a filter layer), `add_image_layer` (`renderer/commands_docs.js:291` -> `renderer/commands_util.js:341-350`: unknown `filename` under `AUTO`, or video/missing `path`), or `set_text` (`renderer/commands_edit.js:194-195`: target is a paint/image layer where `l.kind !== "text"`, or non-numeric `line_height`/`letter_spacing`) — two side effects have already occurred:
1. `ed.pushUndo` -> `pushUndoSnapshot` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:469-496`) has already released and emptied `this.redo` (`lines 489-490`), pushed a no-op `Assistant: <cmd>` step onto `this.undo` (`line 491`), and run `this.trimUndo()` (`line 493`). Worse, for `set_layer` with `match` on a filter layer or `set_text` on a paint layer, `snapshotOf` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:446, 452`) still produces a snapshot, and later undoing it writes `layer.match` onto the filter layer (`line 837`) or `layer.text` onto the paint layer (`line 876`).
2. `snapshotTurn` (`beforeCall` in `renderer/assistant_turns.js:42-55`) has already released any previous turn's kept snapshot (`line 47`, disabling that earlier turn's `"Undo this turn"` card at `renderer/assistant.js:659-662`) and recorded a new `turnSnapshot()` for `meta.turn` (`lines 48-54`). At `turn:done`, `undoCard(e.turn)` (`renderer/assistant.js:577, 637-654`) sees `turnState().turn === turn` and renders an `"Undo this turn"` card even when every write call in the turn failed validation (contradicting the fix comment at `assistant.js:639`).

Two minor details in the candidate's examples do not hold, without affecting the bug: `c.needsImage` is at `renderer/commands.js:123` (not 84) and on an empty tab `ed.sel` is `null`, so `pushUndo` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:470`) and `turnSnapshot` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:232`) already no-op there; and `add_text` with `line_height: 0` is clamped to `0.5` by `textSpacing` (`renderer/commands_util.js:611-620`), which only throws on `""`, booleans, or non-finite values. All other cited paths reproduce on any loaded document.

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: `canvas-tools/noop-click-pushes-undo-clears-redo` covers pointer gestures in `inpaint_ed_pointer.js`, and `assistant-glb/undo-card-wrong-turn` was fixed in `renderer/assistant.js:638-641` under the assumption that a failed turn leaves no `assistant_turns.js` record, making this an unrecorded defect. Severity is `should` (matching `noop-click-pushes-undo-clears-redo` and `undo-card-wrong-turn`): plausible LLM parameter/precondition mistakes permanently wipe the user's redo stack and pollute undo/turn-undo state, without corrupting live pixels or losing money.

findings.claim: `Document.prototype.refresh(layerKey)` treats every layer with `l.kind === "filter"` as purely parametric (`ed.markFilterChanged(l)` only), skipping `ed.markMaskChanged(l)` for filter layer masks and skipping `l.ref = null; ed.markLayerChanged(l)` for Deep paint layers (`l.filter === "surface"`, `ed.hasOwnPixels(l)`). Since `Document.prototype.setPixels` also refuses all `l.kind === "filter"` layers, a plugin editing a filter layer's mask or a Deep paint layer's pixels through `rawLayer(key)` + `refresh(key)` leaves `maskDirty`/`dirty` false and `maskRef`/`ref` pointing at the old file, losing the edits on `.scumble` save and autosave.
findings.scenario: A plugin writes into a Deep paint layer's `rawLayer(id).px` (the only way to write Deep paint pixels from a plugin, because `doc.setPixels` throws `<name> is a filter layer`) or writes/clears `rawLayer(id).maskPx` on any filter layer (such as Curves or Relight), then calls `doc.refresh(id)` as documented. `refresh(id)` runs only `ed.markFilterChanged(l)`: on a Deep paint layer `l.dirty` stays `false`, `l.ref` is not cleared, and `touchSource(l.px)` is not called (leaving tile display mips stale); on any filter layer `l.maskDirty` stays `false` and `l.maskRef` keeps the previous mask file. Saving the `.scumble` document or restarting via autosave silently discards the Deep paint pixel edits and filter mask edits.
findings.evidence: `renderer/plugins.js:142`: `if (l.kind === "filter") throw new Error(\`${l.name} is a filter layer\`);` and `renderer/plugins.js:250-263`: `refresh(layerKey) { if (layerKey != null && layerKey !== "") { const ed = this.editor; const l = findLayer(ed, layerKey); if (l.kind === "filter") ed.markFilterChanged(l); else { l.ref = null; l._fcache = null; ed.markLayerChanged(l); if (!l.maskPx) l.maskEdit = false; ed.markMaskChanged(l); } } ... }`. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:544-546`, `hasOwnPixels(layer)` defines filter layers whose `px` holds paint (`l.kind === "filter" && l.px && FILTERS[layer.filter] && FILTERS[layer.filter].ownPixels`), and `markFilterChanged` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:627-640`) touches neither `l.dirty`/`l.ref` nor `l.maskDirty`/`l.maskRef` (`markMaskChanged` in `inpaint_ed_masks.js:12-33`).
findings.fix: In `Document.prototype.refresh(layerKey)` (`renderer/plugins.js:254-262`), always run `if (!l.maskPx) l.maskEdit = false; ed.markMaskChanged(l);` for filter layers as well, and when `ed.hasOwnPixels && ed.hasOwnPixels(l)` is true, also clear `l.ref = null` and call `ed.markLayerChanged(l)`. Allow `Document.prototype.setPixels` (`plugins.js:142`) on layers where `this.editor.hasOwnPixels(l)` is true.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `Document.prototype.refresh(layerKey)` (`renderer/plugins.js:250-267`) branches on `if (l.kind === "filter") ed.markFilterChanged(l);` (line 254) and skips the `else` block (`l.ref = null; l._fcache = null; ed.markLayerChanged(l); if (!l.maskPx) l.maskEdit = false; ed.markMaskChanged(l);`, lines 255-262) for every filter layer. At the same time, both `Document.prototype.getPixels` (`renderer/plugins.js:129`) and `Document.prototype.setPixels` (`renderer/plugins.js:142`) unconditionally throw on `l.kind === "filter"`, even when `ed.hasOwnPixels(l)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:544-546`, true for Deep paint `filter === "surface"` layers where `FILTERS.surface.ownPixels` is true) holds. Because `Document` provides no dedicated mask-pixel setter either, mutating `doc.rawLayer(key).maskPx` or `doc.rawLayer(key).px` and calling `doc.refresh(key)` is the sole documented plugin path (`renderer/plugins.js:69-74, 246-249`, `docs/PLUGINS.md:113, 189-210`).

Tracing the persistence and invalidation path confirms silent data loss in both cases while the live canvas appears to succeed. On screen, `applyFilterLayer` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:1522-1573`) reads `layer.maskPx` directly and `ownPixelsFor` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:775-808`) reads `layer.px` directly, while `ed.markFilterChanged(l)` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:627-640`) clears `l._fcache*` and redraws, so the plugin's edits show immediately. However, `markFilterChanged(l)` and `touch(ed)` (`renderer/commands_util.js:177-185`) touch neither `l.dirty`/`l.ref` (`markLayerChanged`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1531-1553`) nor `l.maskDirty`/`l.maskRef` (`markMaskChanged`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:12-33`). Consequently, `ed.syncLayersOnce()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:904-937`) and `host.flushEditor(ed)` (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:34-36`) see `l.dirty === false` and `l.maskDirty === false` and upload nothing; `ed.getValue()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:49-50`) serializes the stale `l.ref` / `l.maskRef` (or `null` for a newly added Deep paint stroke or filter mask, or the old mask ref even after `l.maskPx = null`); and on an already clean `.scumble` tab `host.documentDirty(ed)` (`host_documents.js:75-84`) stays `false` so closing does not even prompt to save. (Note on the secondary cache detail: on tiles `writeRect`/`drawInto` do bump per-tile `t.version` in `inpaint_tiles.js:1036`, so tile mips themselves rebuild, but skipping `touchSource` leaves `px.version` / `_dispVer` unchanged at `inpaint_tiles.js:865-868`, which leaves `belowSignature` -> `belowStats` stale at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:917, 966` for any `wholeStats` filter above `l`, and skipping `markLayerChanged` on a wrapped Deep paint layer also fails to clear `l.wrap` at `inpaint_ed_select.js:1535`.)

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including the 0.1.56 Deep paint review notes at lines 18-21 and 96-106), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files; this defect is not previously recorded. For severity, none of the five shipped plugins (`sample`, `glb`, `film`, `effects`, `boxes`) hit this path (`sample` skips filter layers and `glb` refreshes only its own `paint` layers), and a third-party plugin has a workaround via `doc.editor.markMaskChanged(l)` / `doc.editor.markLayerChanged(l)`, so it is not `must`. However, because following the documented `rawLayer` + `refresh(key)` contract in API v4 silently loses saved pixels/masks while rendering them on screen (and `getPixels`/`setPixels` reject Deep paint layers outright), it is a genuine data-loss trap on the public plugin API rather than a cosmetic or narrow race issue, warranting `should`.

findings.claim: Unlike `set_filter` and the editor's own text controls, `set_text` mutates `l.text` in place, calls `ed.renderTextLayer(l)` without settling `l._textUndo` or pushing a `text`/`layers` undo step, and passes `{ step: false }` to `ed.setTextAngle`. When invoked by an external MCP client (`Scumble --mcp`, where `assistant/policy.js`'s `meta.undo` does not run), `set_text` records zero undo steps — even when `angle` resamples the layer's mask — so `Ctrl+Z` cannot undo the text change and instead undoes an earlier edit.
findings.scenario: A user paints on a layer, adds a text layer with a mask, and asks an external MCP agent (Claude Desktop / Claude Code via `Scumble --mcp`) to change the heading and rotate it by 15° (`set_text({ layer: "Text 1", text: "New title", size: 72, angle: 15 })`). `set_text` rewrites `l.text`, renders the new text pixels, and calls `ed.setTextAngle(l, 15, { step: false })`, which rotates and resamples `l.maskPx` without pushing an undo step. When the user presses `Ctrl+Z` to revert the agent's text edit, the text layer and its resampled mask stay at `"New title"` / `15°` while the user's earlier paint stroke is undone.
findings.evidence: `renderer/commands_edit.js:192-210`: `async run(ed, a) { const l = findLayer(ed, a.layer); if (l.kind !== "text") throw new Error(...); const spacing = textSpacing(a); const t = l.text; Object.assign(t, spacing); ... await ed.renderTextLayer(l, { keepScale: true }); if (a.angle != null && l.locked) throw new Error(...); if (a.angle != null) await ed.setTextAngle(l, +a.angle || 0, { step: false }); touch(ed); return layerSummary(ed, l); }`. `renderTextLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:101-147`) pushes no undo step, and `setTextAngle` (`inpaint_ed_text.js:172`: `if (step) this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label });`) is explicitly called with `step: false`. External MCP calls go through `electron/main/mcp/server.js:121` -> `backend.run(name, args)` without `meta.undo` (unlike `set_filter` at `commands_edit.js:151-152`, which pushes its own undo step, and `policy.js:569` which then returns `null` for `set_filter` so the assistant does not double-push).
findings.fix: Validate `a.angle != null && l.locked` before mutating `l.text`, settle any pending panel edit via `if (ed.settleTextUndo) ed.settleTextUndo(l)`, push `ed.pushUndo(a.angle != null ? { kind: "layers", label: "Edit text" } : { kind: "text", id: l.id, label: "Edit text" })` inside `set_text` before mutating `l.text`, and return `null` for `set_text` in `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:571` (`undoStep`) just as `set_filter` does on line 569.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `EditCommandsPart.set_text.run(ed, a)` (`renderer/commands_edit.js:192-210`) looks up the target text layer (`193-194`), validates spacing via `textSpacing(a)` (`195`), mutates `l.text` in place (`196-203`), awaits `ed.renderTextLayer(l, { keepScale: true })` (`204`), checks `if (a.angle != null && l.locked)` (`206`), and when `a.angle != null` awaits `ed.setTextAngle(l, +a.angle || 0, { step: false })` (`207`) before `touch(ed)` (`208`). Neither `renderTextLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:101-147`) nor `setTextAngle` with `step: false` (`inpaint_ed_text.js:161-201`, where line 172 guards `if (step) this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label })`) records an undo step. When `l.maskPx` is present and `delta` is non-zero, `setTextAngle`'s `adopt` callback (`inpaint_ed_text.js:186-196`) also rotates and resamples `l.maskPx` in place (`mask.transformed(...)`) and line 182-183 releases and nulls any held `layer._textUndo` without settling it (while the `a.angle == null` path never calls `ed.settleTextUndo(l)` or `ed.endTextEdit(true)` either).

Tracing every caller confirms there is no undo wrapper on the external MCP, CLI, or plugin paths. External MCP tool calls enter `electron/main/mcp/server.js:114-122` (`await backend.run(name, args)`), which runs either directly on `Bridge.run(name, args)` (`electron/main/bridge.js:102-145`) or over the named pipe in `LocalServer` (`electron/main/local.js:122`: `this.bridge.run(String(msg.name), msg.args || {})`), in both cases without `meta`. In `renderer/shell.js:1453-1468`, `onRequest` only runs `snapshotTurn` and `ed.pushUndo(meta.undo...)` inside `if (meta && meta.turn)` — a path populated exclusively by the in-app assistant (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:140-144, 855-856` via `policy.undoStep` at `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:571`, which returns `args.angle !== undefined ? "layers" : "text"` for `set_text`). All non-assistant callers fall straight through to `commands.call(name, args || {})` (`shell.js:1468` -> `renderer/commands.js:119-131`). By contrast, every UI edit to an existing text layer pushes an undo step (`buildTextControls` in `inpaint_ed_text.js:246-325`, `endTextEdit` at `68-70`, and `setTextAngle`'s default `step = true` at `172`), `transform_layer` on a text layer calls `ed.setTextAngle(l, now + deg, { label: "Rotate" })` with default `step = true` (`renderer/commands_layers.js:196-199`), and `set_filter` was updated in 0.1.42 F2b to push its own `filter` step (`renderer/commands_edit.js:151-152`) with `policy.js:569` returning `null` so the assistant does not double-push. `docs/MCP.md:255-256` likewise promises that non-read-only, non-destructive tools change the document additively or in one undo step.

Checked against all known-issue lists: `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Open`), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`. None records `set_text` missing its undo step: `shell/F6` in `review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json:874-885` is about lock checks (`set_layer` geometry ignoring locks and `set_text` mutating/rendering a locked layer before throwing on `angle`), while `canvas-tools/stale-text-undo-snapshot` (`review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:102-116`, fixed in 0.1.56) is about panel focus/blur snapshots. (A passing note in `docs/PLAN_MCP_COMMANDS.md:276` under `set_filter_preset_fix` observed that external `set_text` had the same missing-undo gap and was 'worth its own item', which was never filed in `BUGS.md` or built.)

Severity is `should`: this is a deterministic bug hit on every external MCP `set_text` call in a normal workflow — pressing `Ctrl+Z` (or calling MCP `undo`) fails to revert the text edit (including a destructively resampled `l.maskPx` when `angle` was changed) and instead silently undoes the user's previous unrelated edit on the stack — matching the `should` calibration of `assistant-glb/glb-place-no-undo` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:502-516`.

findings.claim: `Store` walks every string leaf in `chat.history` and `events` and treats any string of 256+ chars matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9+/\r\n]+={0,2}$/` as a base64 JPEG, decoding it with `Buffer.from(body, "base64")` and re-encoding with `buffer.toString("base64")` on load, which strips all `\r`/`\n` and mutates or truncates non-canonical strings (such as unpadded `encrypted_content`/signatures or newline-separated identifiers/paths). In addition, when a stored screenshot file is missing on disk, `put()` substitutes plain English text directly into `source.data` / `inlineData.data` / `image_url`, causing all four API families to reject every subsequent turn in that chat with HTTP 400.
findings.scenario: Case A: A chat contains an OpenAI Responses `reasoning` item with unpadded base64 `encrypted_content` >= 256 chars whose length mod 4 != 0, or a user/tool string >= 256 chars of newline-separated words/paths (`foo/bar1\n...`) containing only `[A-Za-z0-9+/\r\n]`. `Store.save` writes it to `<n>.jpg` via `Buffer.from(img.body, "base64")`; `Store.load` restores `buffer.toString("base64")`, stripping all newlines, dropping trailing char when `len % 4 === 1`, or zeroing low bits and appending `=`/`==` when `len % 4` is 2 or 3 — breaking byte-for-byte replay (`HTTP 400` invalid signature/encrypted_content) or corrupting message text. Case B: A `.jpg` file in `<userData>/assistant/chats/<id>/` is deleted or missing on reopen. `Store.load` puts `"[screenshot no longer attached; call screenshot again]"` into `source.data` (Anthropic), `inlineData.data` (Gemini), `image_url.url` (Chat Completions), or `input_image.image_url` (OpenAI Responses). When the user sends the next turn, `adapter.prune` leaves the last `keepImages` (3) image blocks intact, and the provider returns HTTP 400 because the base64/URL field contains plain text.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/assistant/store.js:22-24`: `const MIN_BYTES = 256; const DATA_URL = /^data:(image\/[A-Za-z0-9.+-]+);base64,/; const BASE64 = /^[A-Za-z0-9+/\r\n]+={0,2}$/;`. Lines 148-154: `function imageString(value) { if (typeof value !== "string" || value.length < MIN_BYTES) return null; const m = DATA_URL.exec(value); if (m) ...; if (BASE64.test(value)) return { prefix: "", body: value, mime: "image/jpeg" }; return null; }`. Lines 159-173 (`strip`) recurse into every object key and array item in `chat.history` and `events`, decoding `Buffer.from(img.body, "base64")` (line 164), and `put` (lines 185-190) returns `prefix + buffer.toString("base64")` or on `catch (_)` returns `"[screenshot no longer attached; call screenshot again]"` directly into the leaf string. `anthropic.js:179`, `chat.js:295`, `responses.js:209`, and `gemini.js:194` (`prune`) only convert excess image blocks beyond `keepImages` to text blocks.
findings.fix: In `strip()`, match raw base64 only inside known image containers (`node.type === "image" && node.source?.type === "base64"` -> `node.source.data`, and `node.inlineData?.data`), and use `DATA_URL` only for `data:image/...;base64,` strings, leaving signatures, `encrypted_content`, and text untouched. In `put()`, when `readFile` fails inside an image block (`type: "image"`, `type: "image_url"`, `type: "input_image"`, or `inlineData`), replace the enclosing image part with the family's text part (`{ type: "text", text: ... }`, `{ type: "input_text", text: ... }`, or `{ text: ... }`) rather than putting plain text into `data`/`url`.
findings.why:
Both halves of the finding hold against f45a86cc in electron/main/assistant/store.js.

1. Blind base64 classification and non-idempotent round-trip (Case A): At store.js:21-24 and 148-154, imageString(value) treats any string leaf of length >= 256 (MIN_BYTES) matching DATA_URL or BASE64 (/^[A-Za-z0-9+/\r\n]+={0,2}$/) as image bytes. strip() (store.js:159-174), called on both extra.events and chat.history in Store.save (store.js:54-55), walks every array item and object property value regardless of enclosing schema, decodes img.body with Buffer.from(img.body, "base64") (line 164), and writes <n>.jpg. On Store.load (store.js:104-110), put() (lines 177-203) restores prefix + buffer.toString("base64") (line 186). Because BASE64 neither restricts where it matches nor enforces canonical 4-char blocks without whitespace, Node's base64 decoder/encoder is not byte-for-byte lossless on all matched inputs: it strips every \r and \n (e.g. a user message pasting >= 256 chars of 76-column base64 or newline-separated alphanumeric/slash tokens without spaces or punctuation), drops the trailing character when stripped length % 4 === 1, and zeroes unused low bits while appending == or = when length % 4 is 2 or 3 (or when pad bits before =/== are non-zero). Even on canonical base64, strip() currently extracts Anthropic thinking.signature (anthropic.js:217) and Gemini thoughtSignature (gemini.js:264) >= 256 chars into invalid .jpg files in <userData>/assistant/chats/<id>/, and any unpadded, line-wrapped, or non-canonical base64 signature/encrypted_content is mutated on reopen, breaking replay.

2. Missing-file fallback produces invalid image blocks on all four API families (Case B): When fsp.readFile fails in put() (store.js:187-190), the catch returns the plain English string "[screenshot no longer attached; call screenshot again]" directly into the leaf field instead of replacing the enclosing image part. That puts plain English text into source.data on Anthropic (anthropic.js:41), image_url.url on Chat Completions (chat.js:81, 95), input_image.image_url on OpenAI Responses (responses.js:70), and inlineData.data on Gemini (gemini.js:83) — and into signature/thoughtSignature if one of the signature .jpg files was removed. (Even tools/assistant_test.js:4357-4364 asserts this broken leaf state on source.data without running a turn.) When the chat is reopened via openChat (index.js:508-546) and the user sends a turn, index.js:708 only calls adapter.prune when countImages > 2 * s.keepImages (> 6 by default, index.js:34), and prune() in anthropic.js:71-99, chat.js:120-126, responses.js:99-117, and gemini.js:117-137 (note: the finding's evidence mis-cited stream line numbers 179/295/209/194 for prune) always leaves the last keepImages (3) image parts intact. Every family therefore sends an image block containing invalid base64 or a non-URL string, failing with HTTP 400 (only compat local servers have chat.js:257 imageFallback, and refusesImage only matches unsupported-image errors), and done() -> saveChat() (index.js:1045) then overwrites <id>.json with that literal string permanently replacing the $image: marker.

Checked known lists: Neither docs/BUGS.md, docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, nor the findings arrays of review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json, review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json, or review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json record this defect (the 2026-11-12 reviewer_notes only noted the signature .jpg extraction as 'suspected but not proven' and missed both the non-canonical/newline mutation and the broken missing-image fallback). Severity is 'should': users can plausibly paste multi-line base64 in chat or delete screenshot/corrupt-signature .jpg files in assistant/chats/<id>/ (documented in docs/ASSISTANT.md:145-146), permanently bricking the reopened chat with HTTP 400 until they start a new chat.

findings.claim: `add_surface_layer` runs automatically (`POLICY.add_surface_layer = AUTO`), but neither `commands_edit.js` (`ed.addSurfaceLayer()`) nor `policy.undoStep()` pushes a `"layers"` undo step for the newly added Deep paint layer. Pressing Ctrl+Z after `add_surface_layer` therefore undoes an earlier user edit (or only the colour fill / surface maps) while leaving the Deep paint layer in the stack.
findings.scenario: On a document that already has surface maps and a prior brush stroke by the user, the assistant calls `add_surface_layer` (with no `color`). `ed.addSurfaceLayer()` adds `'Deep paint 1'` without pushing an undo step, and `policy.undoStep` returns `null`. The user presses Ctrl+Z expecting to remove `'Deep paint 1'`; instead, Scumble undoes the user's earlier brush stroke while `'Deep paint 1'` stays in the document. If `add_surface_layer` was called with `color: "#ff0000"`, `fillSelection()` pushes only `{ kind: "layer", id: l.id }`, so Ctrl+Z clears the fill and still leaves `'Deep paint 1'`; if called with `compute: true`, `computeSurfaceMaps()` pushes only `{ kind: "maps" }`, so Ctrl+Z drops the surface maps and leaves `'Deep paint 1'` orphaned without maps.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:72` sets `add_surface_layer: AUTO`. `policy.js:563` has `if (["add_paint_layer", "add_filter", "add_text", "add_image_layer"].includes(name)) return "layers";`, omitting `"add_surface_layer"` (returning `null` at line 579). In `renderer/commands_edit.js:98-108`, `add_surface_layer.run` calls `const l = ed.addSurfaceLayer();` and optionally `ed.fillSelection()`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:358-367` (`addSurfaceLayer`) calls `this.addFilterLayer("surface")` -> `this.addLayer(...)` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:539`), neither of which calls `pushUndo` (contrast the UI button `newDeepPaintLayer` in `inpaint_ed_depth.js:630-633`, which calls `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Deep paint layer" })` before `this.addSurfaceLayer()`).
findings.fix: Have `add_surface_layer.run` in `renderer/commands_edit.js:98` call `ed.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Deep paint layer" })` right before `ed.addSurfaceLayer()` (after any `computeSurfaceMaps()` and before any `hex` write into `l.px` without pushing a second step on `fillSelection`), or add `"add_surface_layer"` to `policy.undoStep` when `commands_edit.js` does not push its own step.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc. In Scumble's editor, adding a layer pushes no undo step of its own (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:539`, `inpaint_ed_filters.js:313-367`); instead, per `docs/PLAN_ASSISTANT.md` §2 row 19, every in-app assistant write must be undoable one step at a time with Ctrl+Z by having `electron/main/assistant/policy.js` `undoStep()` name the step kind for `renderer/shell.js:1458-1466` to push right before `commands.call`. At `policy.js:72`, `POLICY.add_surface_layer` is `AUTO`, and at `policy.js:563`, `undoStep()` checks `if (["add_paint_layer", "add_filter", "add_text", "add_image_layer"].includes(name)) return "layers";`, omitting `"add_surface_layer"` and returning `null` at line 579.

Tracing the full call path: `Assistant.runCall` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:855-869`) sets `turn.undo = null`, `backendFor()` (`index.js:143`) forwards `meta.undo = null` through `Bridge.run` (`electron/main/bridge.js:110, 144`) to `renderer/shell.js:1458`, which skips `ed.pushUndo`, and `EditCommandsPart.add_surface_layer.run` (`renderer/commands_edit.js:89-111`) calls `ed.addSurfaceLayer()` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:358-367` -> `addFilterLayer("surface")` -> `addLayer`) without pushing a `"layers"` step. (Note: the raw finding's parenthetical contrast mislocated `newDeepPaintLayer` to `inpaint_ed_depth.js:630-633`; `newDeepPaintLayer` is actually at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:374-387` and intentionally pushes no undo step in the UI, which makes `policy.js:563` even more clearly the omitted site — and `commands_edit.js:81` even documents `color` as `"an undo step of its own after the layer's"`, assuming `undoStep` had pushed the layer's step first.)

Consequently, when the assistant runs `add_surface_layer` on a document with existing surface maps: (1) without `color`, no undo step is pushed at all, so pressing Ctrl+Z silently undoes an earlier step (such as the user's prior brush stroke) while leaving `'Deep paint N'` in the stack; (2) with `color` (the assistant's primary Deep paint workflow, `PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md:369`), `ed.fillSelection()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1265`) pushes only `{ kind: "layer", id: l.id, label: "Fill selection" }`, so Ctrl+Z clears the fill and a second Ctrl+Z undoes the prior selection/user edit while `'Deep paint N'` remains; (3) with `compute: true` when maps were absent, `ed.computeSurfaceMaps()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:368`) pushes only `{ kind: "maps" }`, so Ctrl+Z removes the surface maps and leaves `'Deep paint N'` orphaned. Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including `Deep paint: small points left from the 0.1.56 release review` at lines 96-106), all three `verified.json` files, `PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md`, `PLAN_0_1_57.md`, and `PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: this defect is not known. Severity is `should` because any user asking the assistant to add or paint on a Deep paint layer hits broken Ctrl+Z behaviour in normal use, with workarounds available (Redo + manual layer deletion, or `Undo this turn` on the tile backend).

findings.claim: `SET_LAYER_SOFT` in `policy.js` omits `clip` while including `role`, causing two defects in `set_layer`: (1) `set_layer({ clip })` on a user-made layer bypasses the ownership check and runs `AUTO()`, and (2) `set_layer({ role })` makes `shell.js` push a `"layers"` undo step before `ed.setLayerRole()` pushes its own `"layers"` undo step, recording two undo steps (one of them a no-op duplicate) for a single command.
findings.scenario: 1. User has a painted layer `'Sketch'`. Assistant calls `set_layer({ layer: "Sketch", clip: true })`: `setLayer()` filters `SET_LAYER_SOFT`, finds `soft.length === 0`, and returns `AUTO()`, clipping the user's layer without asking. 2. Assistant calls `set_layer({ layer: "Result 1", role: "reference" })`: `policy.undoStep` sees `"role"` in `SET_LAYER_SOFT` and returns `"layers"`, so `shell.js:1463` calls `ed.pushUndo({ kind: "layers" })`, and then `commands_layers.js:50` calls `ed.setLayerRole(l, "reference")`, which calls `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Layer role" })` again. Pressing Ctrl+Z once restores `setLayerRole`'s snapshot, and the extra `"layers"` step underneath is an identical no-op step that wastes a second Ctrl+Z press.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:41`: `const SET_LAYER_SOFT = ["name", "visible", "opacity", "blend", "role", "match", "match_source", "alpha_lock"];`. `policy.js:470-475` (`setLayer`): `const soft = SET_LAYER_SOFT.filter((k) => args[k] !== undefined); ... if (soft.length && !owns(call, facts)) return ASK("changes a layer you made", card(call, facts, soft)); return AUTO();`. `policy.js:572-578` (`undoStep`): returns `"layers"` whenever `soft` has any key other than `match`/`match_source`. `renderer/shell.js:1463`: `if (ed && meta.undo && meta.undo.kind) ed.pushUndo(meta.undo);`. `renderer/commands_layers.js:47-51`: `ed.setLayerClip(l, !!a.clip, { only: true })` (pushes its own `"layers"` step) and `ed.setLayerRole(l, a.role)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:280`: `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Layer role" });`).
findings.fix: Add `"clip"` to the ownership check in `setLayer()` (so `clip` on `!owns(call, facts)` asks), and in `policy.undoStep()` exclude `"role"` and `"clip"` when deciding whether the shell must push a `"layers"` step (pushing `"layers"` from the shell only when another soft field like `name`, `visible`, `opacity`, `blend`, or `alpha_lock` is also set — or pass `{ undo: false }` in `commands_layers.js` when the shell already pushed one).
findings.why:
Both halves of the finding hold at commit f45a86cc because `SET_LAYER_SOFT` at `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:41` (`["name", "visible", "opacity", "blend", "role", "match", "match_source", "alpha_lock"]`) conflates two distinct rules: (a) which `set_layer` fields require user approval when modifying a non-owned layer (`setLayer` at `policy.js:467-476`), and (b) which `set_layer` fields need the shell to pre-push an undo step because the editor records none (`undoStep` at `policy.js:572-578`).

First, for `clip`: `renderer/commands_layers.js:34, 47` exposes `clip` on `set_layer` and delegates to `ed.setLayerClip(l, !!a.clip, { only: true })` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:458-478`), which pushes its own `{ kind: "layers", label: want ? "Clip to layer below" : "Release clipping" }` step at line 471 (and checks no lock). When the assistant calls `set_layer({ layer: "Sketch", clip: true })` (or `clip: false`) on a layer not in `facts.owned`, `Assistant.runCall` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:804-825`) resolves `layer` to its id and calls `policy.decide(canonical, facts)` (`policy.js:525-546`). Neither the geometry lock check at `policy.js:538` (`SET_LAYER_GEOMETRY`) nor `setLayer()` at `policy.js:467-476` matches `clip`, because `SET_LAYER_SOFT.filter((k) => args[k] !== undefined)` is empty (`soft.length === 0`). `setLayer()` therefore returns `AUTO()`. Unlike `move_layer`, clipping directly alters what of a user's layer is visible—matching `set_mask` (`policy.js:102-105`, whose comment explicitly notes `every operation is one undo step of the editor's own; on a layer the user made it changes what of it shows`), `visible`, `opacity`, and `role` (`docs/PLAN_ASSISTANT.md:2646`). In fact, adding an empty paint layer (`AUTO`) and calling `set_layer({ clip: true })` on the user's layer above it hides the user's layer completely without asking.

Second, for `role`: when `policy.js` was written in 0.1.21, `setLayerRole` recorded no undo step (`docs/PLAN_ASSISTANT.md:363-365`), so `"role"` was put in `SET_LAYER_SOFT`. In 0.1.34 (`CHANGELOG.md:899-900`), `setLayerRole` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:277-294`) was updated to push `{ kind: "layers", label: "Layer role" }` at line 280, but `policy.undoStep` was never updated (contrast `duplicate_layer`, `glb_place`, `generate`, `realism_pass`, and `set_filter` at `policy.js:559-569`, each of which removed the shell step because `a second one would be an empty step`). Today, when the assistant calls `set_layer({ layer, role: "reference" })`, `policy.undoStep` (`policy.js:572-578`) sees `"role"` in `SET_LAYER_SOFT` and returns `"layers"`. `index.js:855-856` and `142` attach `meta.undo = { kind: "layers", id }`, causing `renderer/shell.js:1463` to call `ed.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", id, label: "Assistant: set layer" })` immediately before `commands.call` invokes `ed.setLayerRole(l, a.role)` (`commands_layers.js:50`), which calls `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Layer role" })` at `inpaint_ed_refs.js:280`. `pushUndoSnapshot` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:480-496`) performs no deduplication, so two identical `"layers"` snapshots are pushed onto `ed.undo` for one command (or, if `l.role` already equals `a.role`, `setLayerRole` returns early at `inpaint_ed_refs.js:279` while `shell.js:1463` still pushes a no-op undo step and clears `ed.redo` at `inpaint_ed_history.js:490`).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`): `shell/F1`, `shell/F2`, and `shell/F6` covered `merge_down` ordering, `resolveLayer`, and `SET_LAYER_GEOMETRY` locks, not `SET_LAYER_SOFT`, `clip` ownership, or `role` double-undo. Severity is `should`: there is no permanent data/pixel loss or billing defect (`must`), as Ctrl+Z still restores the layer state, but both defects trigger deterministically in standard assistant layer/reference workflows.

findings.claim: holdStackNow clones a filter layer's mask so later edits cannot reach an in-flight stack program, but keeps a live reference to `s.filter` without cloning `s.filter.px` (or `s.filter.params`) when `FILTERS[s.filter.filter]?.ownPixels` is true. During multi-band async reads without a `compositeVersion` guard (`readBoxBytes`, used by `prepareCropAsync` for paid provider runs and by `frequencySeparation`), edits to the Deep paint layer mid-read tear across bands of the output.
findings.scenario:
1. On a large tiled image with surface maps and a Deep paint layer, select a region and click Generate on an API provider (calling `holdRunStack` -> `holdStackNow` and then `prepareCropAsync` -> `readBoxBytes` across multiple 256-row bands).
2. While the async pool bands are still reading, paint a brush stroke, Fill, Delete, undo, or drag a live Wrap source on the Deep paint layer.
3. Ordinary pixel layers and the Deep paint layer's `maskPx` stay frozen at their pre-click clones, but `bandFilter` -> `ownPixelsFor` reads the mutated `layer.px` for the remaining bands, sending a half-old, half-new torn crop to the paid provider run.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:254-260 in `holdStackNow`: `if (s.filter) { flush(); const mask = s.mask ? s.mask.clone() : null; if (mask) clones.push(mask); steps.push({ filter: s.filter, plain: !!s.plain, mask, alpha: s.alpha, op: s.op, clip: s.clip }); continue; }` — `s.filter.px` is never cloned into `clones`. When `programFinish` (:468) calls `this.bandFilter(st.filter, ...)` (:357-368) -> `this.filterInfo(layer, ...)` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:758) -> `this.ownPixelsFor(layer, pass, w, h)` (:775-808), it reads live `layer.px`. Unlike `encodeComposite` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:648-661), `readBoxBytes` (inpaint_ed_stack.js:757-782) loops `for (let y = y0; y < y1; y = next)` awaiting `reader.read(...)` with no `compositeVersion` check.
findings.fix: In `holdStackNow` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:254-260), when `FILTERS[s.filter.filter]?.ownPixels && s.filter.px`, clone `px = s.filter.px.clone()`, push `px` onto `clones`, and pass a shallow layer snapshot `{ ...s.filter, px, params: s.filter.params ? structuredClone(s.filter.params) : s.filter.params }` as `step.filter`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:236-271` (`holdStackNow`).
