While ordinary layer steps clone both `s.px` and `s.mask` (`hold` at `:241-246`), the filter branch at `:254-262` (`if (s && s.filter)`) clones only `s.mask` (`:255-256`) and pushes the live layer reference `filter: s.filter` into `steps` (`:259`) without cloning `s.filter.px` (or `s.filter.params`) when `FILTERS[s.filter.filter]?.ownPixels` is true (`FILTERS.surface` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:1386-1395`). (Minor correction to the candidate's quote: `:254-262` uses `run = null; return;` inside `plan.forEach` rather than `flush()` / `continue`, and `readBoxBytes` delegates the band loop to `fillBoxFromStack` rather than looping directly.) When `programFinish` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:468`) calls `this.bandFilter(st.filter, input, [px0, py0], prog.forRun, st.plain)` (`:357-376`), `filterInfo` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:758`) wires `info.own = (w, h) => this.ownPixelsFor(layer, pass, w, h)`, and both the WebGL2 path (`registerSurfaceGL` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_surfacefx.js:207`) and CPU twin (`applySurface` at `:124`) call `ownPixelsFor` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:775-808`), which reads live `layer.px` via `this.drawTilesInto(ctx, layer.px, 0, 0, W, H, vp)` (`:797`).

Guards and callers were traced end to end. Export and flatten paths (`encodeComposite` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:656,662`, `exportLayeredBands` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_export.js:178`, and `encodeTiff` at `:227`) check `this.compositeVersion !== version` per band and abort/retry when `layer.px` changes (`markLayerChanged` -> `bumpComposite` at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:275-278`), so file exports cannot tear. However, four callers read a held program across async awaits without a `compositeVersion` guard: (1) `prepareCropAsync` (`renderer/editor/stitch.js:858-866`, called by `runProvider` at `renderer/editor/host_provider.js:326` and selection `runUpscale` at `renderer/editor/host_upscale.js:143`), which calls `holdRunStack` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:745-748`) synchronously before `await stitchCall("plan", ...)`, `await holding` (`stackMatches`), and `readBoxBytes` (`await this.relightIdle()` at `:760`, then `await this.fillBoxFromStack(...)` at `:768`); (2) `finishResultAsync` (`stitch.js:909`) when `finishNeedsRegion(info)` is true; (3) `frequencySeparation` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:185-191`), whose post-await guard checks only `geometrySeq`, `width`, `height`, and `base`; and (4) `selectRange` for luma/colour on tiles (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:274-354`) and `floodOverTiles` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:675-698`). Nothing blocks mutating `layer.px` during those awaits: `providerPending` leaves the editor interactive by design, `historyStepNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1083`) blocks only `"canvas"` / `"turn"` steps under `turnBlocked()` while allowing `"layer"`, `"layerrect"`, and `"layers"` undo/redo to `blit` into `layer.px` synchronously (`:815, :888`), and `fillSelection` (`inpaint_ed_select.js:1258`), `clearSelectedPixels`, committed brush strokes (`commitStroke` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:433`), and live Wrap source drags (`syncWrapsSoon` -> `putWrap` writing `out.px.writeRect` every 40 ms at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:475-486, 535-541`) all mutate `layer.px` in place.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including `Deep paint: small points left from the 0.1.56 release review` at `:96-105`), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md` (`:521-537`), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`. Deep paint (`ownPixels: true` on `surface` filter layers) was introduced after the 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-12 reviews, and no open entry covers `holdStackNow` leaving `s.filter.px` uncloned (`filters/freqsep-stale-box-after-await` covered geometry/base changes during `frequencySeparation` and was fixed at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:185-191`).

Severity is calibrated to `nice` rather than `should`. First, in `prepareCropAsync` the held stack is read only during initial crop preparation (`stitch.js:858-866`), before `providerEdit` sends the network request (`host_provider.js:380`) — measured at ~259 ms total `prep` even at 15,000 x 10,000 (`docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md:106`), unless a relight shadow march is concurrently settling in `relightIdle()`. Second, when `forRun` is true (`prepareCropAsync`, `frequencySeparation`, `selectRange`), `ownPixelsFor` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:786`) ignores live uncommitted brush strokes (`!pass.forRun`), so a user must complete and commit an edit (stroke release, Fill, Delete, Ctrl+Z, or a live Wrap drag) inside that sub-second window. Third, `programRows` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:343-348`) sizes bands up to 2,048 rows (1,536 rows at width 15,000), not 256-row bands as claimed in the candidate's scenario: crops <= 1,536-2,048 px tall run in a single band and cannot tear horizontally across bands (at worst reading post-click `layer.px` whole), while multi-band tearing requires both a crop/box taller than 1,536-2,048 rows (or the ~2.3 s 256-row `selectRange` luma/colour scan) and a committed edit landing mid-read. This is a narrow async race/edge case matching `nice`.

findings.claim: Alpha lock on a Deep paint layer is honoured by brushstrokes, live stroke previews, eraser blocking, bucket fill, MCP `set_layer`, and `getValue()`, but `setValue()`'s `l.kind === "filter"` branch omits `alphaLock: !!l.alphaLock`. Saving and reopening a `.scumble` document (or restoring from autosave) silently drops `alphaLock` on every Deep paint layer, and the layer panel renders no alpha-lock button on Deep paint rows to inspect or re-enable it.
findings.scenario:
1. Create a Deep paint layer, paint a shape on it, and enable alpha lock via MCP `set_layer({ layer, alpha_lock: true })`.
2. Verify that brush strokes and bucket fills stay inside existing painted alpha (`source-atop`) and the eraser is refused.
3. Save to `.scumble` and reopen (or reload from autosave): `getValue()` wrote `"alphaLock": true` into `document.json`, but `setValue()` reconstructs the filter layer without `alphaLock`, so subsequent strokes spill outside the painted shape and the eraser erases freely.
findings.evidence: renderer/commands_layers.js:46 (`set_layer`) sets `if (a.alpha_lock != null) l.alphaLock = !!a.alpha_lock;` with no filter guard; `getValue` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:54) writes `...(l.alphaLock ? { alphaLock: true } : {})`; and `ownPixelsFor` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:787), `onPointerDown` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:583), `commitStroke` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:446), and `bucketFillNow` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shape.js:349) all check `layer.alphaLock`. In `setValue` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:228-235), the `l.kind === "filter"` object includes `locked: !!l.locked, clip: !!l.clip` (:229) but omits `alphaLock: !!l.alphaLock` (unlike the text branch at :179 and pixel branch at :269). Additionally, `renderLayers` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:466) only renders the alpha-lock toggle when `l.kind !== "filter"`.
findings.fix: Add `alphaLock: !!l.alphaLock` to the `l.kind === "filter"` layer object in `setValue` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:229), and show the alpha-lock toggle in `renderLayers` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:466) when `this.hasOwnPixels(l)` (and honour `layer.alphaLock` in `fillSelection` at renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1283 if desired).
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, Deep paint layers (`kind: "filter"`, `filter: "surface"`, `FILTERS.surface.ownPixels === true`) deliberately honour `layer.alphaLock` across the interactive painting paths, serialize it in `getValue()`, and accept it via MCP `set_layer`, but drop it during `setValue()` reconstruction. Specifically, `set_layer` (`renderer/commands_layers.js:46`) sets `if (a.alpha_lock != null) l.alphaLock = !!a.alpha_lock;` without a filter-layer guard (unlike `match` at `:53` and geometry at `:62`), `layerSummary` (`renderer/commands_util.js:67`) reports `alpha_lock: !!l.alphaLock` for all layers, and the Assistant policy (`electron/main/assistant/policy.js:41, 96`) allows `set_layer` with `alpha_lock`. Once set on a Deep paint layer, `onPointerDown` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:583`, before the `hasOwnPixels` check at `:593`) blocks the eraser with `"<name> has its alpha locked: nothing to erase. Unlock alpha first."`, live stroke previews use `source-atop` on both tiles (`ownPixelsFor` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:787, 798`) and canvas (`ownPixelsFor` `:800` -> `layerWithStroke` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:845, 858`), `commitStroke` / `commitStrokeTiles` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:446, 508`) commit brush strokes with `source-atop`, and `bucketFillNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shape.js:323-324, 349`) fills with `source-atop`.

On persistence, `getValue()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:54`) writes `...(l.alphaLock ? { alphaLock: true } : {})` unconditionally for every layer in `this.layers`, so `.scumble` `document.json`, `autosave.json`, and closed-tab snapshots all record `"alphaLock": true`. However, in `setValue()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:186-242`), the `if (l.kind === "filter")` branch reconstructs the layer object at `:227-235` with `locked: !!l.locked, clip: !!l.clip` on line 229, omitting `alphaLock: !!l.alphaLock` (whereas `textLayer` at `:179` and the pixel-layer branch at `:269` both copy `alphaLock: !!l.alphaLock`). Reopening a saved `.scumble`, restoring from autosave, or reopening a closed tab therefore resets `alphaLock` to `undefined` (falsy), and the next `getValue()` drops it from storage as well. Note one citation correction to the candidate's evidence: `renderLayers` is in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:686` (not `inpaint_ed_panels.js:466`), where `:774` sets `const isFx = layer.kind === "filter";` and `:793-798` renders the `alphaLock` `miniButton` only when `if (!isFx)`, with no keyboard shortcut (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:91-315`) or menu item (`inpaint_ed_masks.js:415-451`, `electron/main/main.js:731-886`) to inspect or toggle it in the GUI.

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including `Deep paint: small points left from the 0.1.56 release review` at `:96-106`), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md` (`:332, :521-537`), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` review files: this defect is not previously recorded (note `canvas-c/F5` only covers `match.source` at strength 0 on pixel layers). Severity is calibrated down from `should` to `nice`: no existing pixel data is lost (`l.px` / `l.ref` loads intact), a pure-GUI user cannot enable `alphaLock` on a Deep paint layer in the first place because `inpaint_ed_layers.js:793` hides the button on all filter rows, and autonomous MCP commands (`fill_selection`, `add_surface_layer`, `wrap_layer`) do not consult `alphaLock`. Hitting this bug requires a cross-surface workflow where MCP or the in-app Assistant calls `set_layer({ alpha_lock: true })` on a Deep paint layer, the document is reopened/restored via `setValue()`, and the user then paints or erases manually in the GUI (conversely, before a reload, an MCP-set `alphaLock` blocks GUI erasing with no UI button to unlock it).

findings.claim: `newLightBrushLayer` adds a `relight` filter layer without a layer-creation undo step and then calls `fillLayerMask(layer, false)`, which pushes a `"Mask hides all"` undo step whose prior state is `maskPx: null`. Pressing Ctrl+Z right after *Layer › New Light Brush Layer* removes the black mask instead of removing the layer, leaving the 120% warm sun active across the entire picture.
findings.scenario:
1. Open a picture that already has a depth map (or compute one), then click *Layer › New Light Brush Layer*.
2. Decide against it and press Ctrl+Z.
3. Instead of `Light brush 1` disappearing, `undo()` applies the `"mask"` snapshot from `fillLayerMask`, setting `layer.maskPx = null` and `layer.maskEdit = false`; the 120%-intensity 4500 K sun immediately lights 100% of the canvas.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:398-405`: `const layer = this.addFilterLayer("relight"); ... this.fillLayerMask(layer, false); layer.maskEdit = true;`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:223-233` (`fillLayerMask`): `this.pushUndo({ kind: "mask", id: layer.id, label: reveal ? "Mask reveals all" : "Mask hides all" });` before creating `m = this.pixels.Mask.empty(...)` on a layer whose `maskPx` was `null`.
findings.fix: Either push `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Light brush layer" })` before `addFilterLayer("relight")` and initialize `layer.maskPx = this.pixels.Mask.empty(layer.px.width, layer.px.height); layer.maskOff = false; layer.maskEdit = true; this.markMaskChanged(layer);` without `fillLayerMask`'s separate undo step, or initialize the empty mask directly if layer creation is meant to have no undo step.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, both UI entry points for New Light Brush Layer (`electron/main/main.js:817` -> `renderer/shell.js:1399` and the Layers panel Deep paint menu at `renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js:443`) call `newLightBrushLayer()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:396-412`). Line 398 calls `this.addFilterLayer("relight")` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:313-352`), which creates the layer via `this.addLayer(...)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:523-554`) with `layer.maskPx = null`, `layer.maskEdit = false` (`:535-536`), and no undo step (`:539` only bumps `this.historyGen++`). Lines 402-403 configure a 4500 K, 120% intensity `sun` light, and line 404 calls `this.fillLayerMask(layer, false)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:223-240`) before line 405 sets `layer.maskEdit = true` and line 407 selects the `paint` tool. Inside `fillLayerMask`, line 226 calls `this.pushUndo({ kind: "mask", id: layer.id, label: "Mask hides all" })` while `layer.maskPx` is still `null`. `snapshotOf` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:442-445`) therefore records `{ kind: "mask", id: layer.id, url: null, mw: 0, mh: 0, maskOff: false }` (clearing any redo stack in `pushUndoSnapshot` at `:489-490`), and lines 228-230 attach the empty black mask.

Although the JSDoc at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:393-394` (and `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md:394`) notes "One undo step for the mask (adding a layer is none)", undoing that step does not return the document to any prior user state: when the user presses Ctrl+Z right after adding the layer (or presses Ctrl+Z one step past their painted mask strokes) on a picture that has a depth map, `historyStepNow` -> `applySnapshot` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:861-867`) sets `layer.maskPx = null` and `if (!layer.maskPx) layer.maskEdit = false`. The visible `Light brush` relight layer stays on the stack unmasked, immediately lighting 100% of the canvas with the 120% warm sun. Worse, because `snapshotOf` (`:442-445`) does not store `maskEdit`, pressing Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z to redo restores the black `maskPx` while leaving `layer.maskEdit === false` with `tool === "paint"`, so subsequent brush strokes on the layer are refused until the user manually re-enables mask editing.

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including the open `Deep paint: small points left from the 0.1.56 release review` section at lines 96-106 and `Fixed, waiting for its release` at lines 18-21), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md`, `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (which predate SP6 on 2026-11-13); this defect is not recorded in any known list. Severity is `nice` because it is a non-destructive undo UX papercut with no data or pixel loss and an immediate workaround (deleting the layer or re-hiding/editing its mask).

findings.claim: `packPoints` guards `Number.isFinite(z)` in its bounds loop, but neither checks `Number.isFinite` on `X` and `Y` in that loop nor checks `Number.isFinite` in the u16 packing loop (`+Infinity > 0` is true). Any kept pixel with non-finite `X` or `Y` makes `hi`/`lo` `±Infinity`, zeroing that channel across all finite pixels and serializing `null` into `meta.lo`/`meta.hi` via `mapToJSON`.
findings.scenario:
1. MoGe-2 returns a `points` tensor where an edge pixel with `mask >= 0.5` has `+Infinity` in `Z` (or `±Infinity`/`NaN` in `X`/`Y` while `Z` is finite).
2. If `X` is `+Infinity` and `Z` is finite, line 238 sets `hi[0] = Infinity`, line 259 sets `span = Infinity`, line 260 writes `0` for every finite pixel's X coordinate, and `mapToJSON` (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(map.meta))`) turns `meta.hi[0]` into `null`. If `Z` is `+Infinity`, line 236 skips it in bounds, but line 257 (`!(points[3 * i + 2] > 0)`) lets it through and writes `65535` instead of leaving the dropped texel at `0`.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_surface.js:234-239`: `if (!(mask[i] >= 0.5)) continue; const z = points[3 * i + 2]; if (!(z > 0) || !Number.isFinite(z)) continue; kept++; for (let c = 0; c < 3; c++) { const v = points[3 * i + c]; if (v < lo[c]) lo[c] = v; if (v > hi[c]) hi[c] = v; }`. Lines `256-262`: `if (!(mask[i] >= 0.5) || !(points[3 * i + 2] > 0)) continue;`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:358`: `meta: map.meta ? JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(map.meta)) : {}`.
findings.fix: Use a single helper `const ok = (i) => mask[i] >= 0.5 && points[3 * i + 2] > 0 && Number.isFinite(points[3 * i]) && Number.isFinite(points[3 * i + 1]) && Number.isFinite(points[3 * i + 2]);` in all three loops (bounds, focal-length median, and u16 packing) of `packPoints`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in `renderer/editor/inpaint_surface.js:228-265`. In `packPoints(points, mask, w, h)`, the bounds pass (`inpaint_surface.js:233-239`) checks `if (!(mask[i] >= 0.5)) continue; const z = points[3 * i + 2]; if (!(z > 0) || !Number.isFinite(z)) continue;` on lines 234-236, then updates `lo[c]` and `hi[c]` across all three channels on line 238 (`for (let c = 0; c < 3; c++) { const v = points[3 * i + c]; if (v < lo[c]) lo[c] = v; if (v > hi[c]) hi[c] = v; }`) without checking `Number.isFinite` on `X` (`c = 0`) or `Y` (`c = 1`). In the third loop (`inpaint_surface.js:256-263`), line 257 guards only `if (!(mask[i] >= 0.5) || !(points[3 * i + 2] > 0)) continue;`, omitting `!Number.isFinite` altogether even though `+Infinity > 0` evaluates to `true`. Both defects hold as claimed: (1) if a pixel with `mask[i] >= 0.5` has `Z = +Infinity` (for instance from FP16 overflow on DirectML at a sky/silhouette boundary), line 236 skips it when computing `lo`/`hi`, lines 249-250 skip it via `Number.isFinite(f)` when computing the median focal length `f`, and line 257 lets it into the packing loop where `c = 2` clamps `+Infinity` to `65535` (`hi[2]`) instead of leaving the dropped texel at `[0, 0, 0]` (and any `NaN` in `X`/`Y` at that texel rounds to `NaN` and coerces to `0` in `Uint16Array`); (2) if a pixel with `mask[i] >= 0.5` has finite `Z > 0` and `±Infinity` in `X` or `Y` (or if all kept pixels have `NaN` in `X` while `Y` supplies `>= 8` focal-length samples), `lo[c]`/`hi[c]` becomes `±Infinity`, `span = hi[c] - lo[c]` on line 259 becomes `+Infinity`, every finite pixel's coordinate in channel `c` encodes as `0` (either `finite / Infinity === 0` or `Infinity / Infinity === NaN -> 0`), in-session `wrapSlopesPoints` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_wrap.js:89,103,127`) computes `0 * Infinity = NaN` in `P()` and `NaN` slopes, and `mapToJSON` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:358`, `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(map.meta))`) serializes `Infinity` in `meta.lo`/`meta.hi` as `null`.

Traced the full call path from ONNX inference to persistence to check for upstream sanitization: `Normals.run` (`electron/main/onnx/normals.js:42-50`) copies `out.points.data` straight into a `Float32Array` with no `Number.isFinite` check (`normals.js:35` only validates the `tokens` input scalar); `engine.js:230-239`, `helpers_process.js:31-32`, `helpers.js:139`, `onnx/index.js:324-328`, `main.js:1418`, and `preload.js:223` pass `points` across utility-process `postMessage` and Electron IPC structured clone bit-for-bit; `host_helpers.js:531` returns `normals` untouched to `computeSurfaceMaps` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:454,470`), which calls `packPoints(res.normals.points, res.normals.mask, mw, mh)` directly. The presence of `!Number.isFinite(z)` at `inpaint_surface.js:236` and `Number.isFinite(f)` at `inpaint_surface.js:249-250` confirms that `packPoints` itself is the intended boundary against non-finite MoGe-2 outputs.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including the open 0.1.56 Deep paint review notes at lines 96-106 and fixed 2026-11-16 notes at lines 18-20), `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md` (§6 lines 521-537), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`2026-11-12`, `2026-11-07`, `external_2026-11-07`): `packPoints` post-dates the earlier reviews and this defect is not recorded anywhere. Severity is `nice` because MoGe-2 normally sets `mask < 0.5` on sky/infinite-depth regions and when an unmasked border pixel overflows FP16, `Z` typically overflows alongside `X`/`Y` (triggering only the single-texel `65535` glitch rather than whole-channel `±Infinity` bounds corruption), making it a narrow edge case.

findings.claim: Commit 9a1172a7 made `maskOp(layer, "apply")` convert a text layer to `paint` and `delete layer.text`, but neither ends an open inline canvas text editor (`this.textEdit`) on that layer nor flushes a pending debounced text render (`layer._textTimer`). Applying a mask while inline text editing is open leaves the floating `<textarea>` live over `layer.text === undefined` so the next keystroke or blur throws an uncaught `TypeError`, while applying within 120 ms of typing in the sidebar `<textarea>` cancels the render and bakes the mask into stale pre-edit pixels.
findings.scenario:
1. Add a text layer, add a mask to it, and double-click the text on the canvas to open inline `beginTextEdit(layer)` (`this.textEdit` is now open on `layer`).
2. Click the mask row's `...` button in the Layers panel and choose Apply mask (or invoke MCP `set_mask` with `op: "apply"`).
3. `maskOp` deletes `layer.text` while the inline `<textarea>` stays mounted. Typing a character throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'size')` in `syncBox`, and clicking away or pressing Escape/Enter throws `TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'content')` in `endTextEdit` before `renderLayers()`/`draw()` can run. Alternatively, type in the sidebar text box and run `set_mask` `op: "apply"` (or click Apply mask) before the 120 ms `_textTimer` fires: `clearTimeout(layer._textTimer)` discards the render and rasterizes the old text.
findings.evidence:
In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:322-336`:
`if (layer.kind === "text") {`
`    this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Apply mask" });`
`    layer.kind = "paint";`
`    delete layer.text;`
`    layer._textToken = (layer._textToken || 0) + 1;`
`    clearTimeout(layer._textTimer); layer._textTimer = null; layer._textRendering = 0;`
`    if (layer._textUndo) this.releaseSnapshot(layer._textUndo);`
`    layer._textUndo = null;`
`    this.applyMask(layer, { silent: true, undo: false });`
Compare `setTextAngle` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:165-171`, which flushes `layer._textTimer` via `await this.renderTextLayer(layer)` and calls `if (this.textEdit && this.textEdit.layer === layer) this.endTextEdit(true);` before mutating the layer. Without that call, `endTextEdit` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:68`) executes `te.layer.text.content = val;` when `te.layer.text` is `undefined`, and `syncBox` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:90`) reads `t.size` when `const t = layer.text` is `undefined`.
findings.fix: At the start of the `layer.kind === "text"` branch in `maskOp` (`inpaint_ed_masks.js:322`), call `if (this.textEdit && this.textEdit.layer === layer) this.endTextEdit(true);` and `this.settleTextUndo(layer);` (and if `layer._textTimer` is set, flush `renderTextLayer` first or make the `text` branch await it like `maskFromLayer`).
findings.why:
In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:322-336` (added in commit `9a1172a7` to fix `canvas-select/apply-mask-on-text-layer-undone-by-next-edit`), `maskOp(layer, "apply")` converts a text layer into a paint layer (`layer.kind = "paint"; delete layer.text;`) without ending an active inline canvas text edit (`this.textEdit`), without flushing an unrendered text edit (`layer._textTimer` / `layer._textRendering`), and by calling `this.releaseSnapshot(layer._textUndo)` instead of `this.settleTextUndo(layer)`. Compare `setTextAngle` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:165-171`), which awaits `this.renderTextLayer(layer)` when `_textTimer || _textRendering` is set and calls `if (this.textEdit && this.textEdit.layer === layer) this.endTextEdit(true)`.

However, the UI half of the candidate's scenario does not hold at `f45a86cc` for two reasons: (1) `openMaskMenu` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:345-409`, the mask row's `...` menu) has no "Apply mask" entry at all, while the mask row's checkmark button (`buildMaskRow` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:1041`) calls `this.applyMask(layer)` directly rather than `this.maskOp(layer, "apply")`; and (2) `miniButton` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_dom.js:214-221`) and `bindEvents` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:419-420`) do not `preventDefault()` on `mousedown`/`pointerdown`, so clicking any button in the Layers panel blurs `this.textEdit.ta` on `mousedown` and runs its `blur` listener (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:28` -> `this.endTextEdit(true)`) before `click` fires. (Also note a minor naming discrepancy in the candidate's evidence: `inpaint_ed_text.js` has no `syncBox` at line 90; the overlay positioner is `positionTextEdit` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:36-58`, and `endTextEdit` at lines 68-69 reads/writes `te.layer.text.content` against `te.before.text.content`.)

The defect IS reachable through `set_mask` (`op: "apply"`) in `renderer/commands_layers.js:355`, which — unlike sibling commands `match_edges` (`line 117`), `contact_shadow` (`line 141`), and `transform_layer` (`line 189`) — does not call `if (ed.textEdit) ed.endTextEdit(true)` before `ed.maskOp(l, "apply")`. While the in-app assistant waits on `ed.textEdit` via `waitForUser` (`renderer/shell.js:1442-1445`, `renderer/assistant_wait.js:43`), external MCP calls, `--cmd`, and plugins (`renderer/plugins.js:63`) carry no `meta` (`assistant_wait.js:12-13`). When `set_mask` `op: "apply"` runs while `this.textEdit` is open on `layer`, `maskOp` mutates the layer (`pushUndo`, `layer.kind = "paint"`, `delete layer.text`, `applyMask`) and then calls `this.draw()` at `inpaint_ed_masks.js:333` -> `drawOverlays()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_view.js:719`) -> `positionTextEdit()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:43`: `const res = t.res || 2;`), which synchronously throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'res')`. `set_mask` therefore reports an error after already converting the layer, leaves `<textarea class="ipc-textedit">` mounted, and causes subsequent draws (`inpaint_ed_text.js:43`), typing (`line 27`), or blur/Enter/Escape (`endTextEdit` at `lines 68-69`, before `releaseSnapshot(te.before)`) to throw `TypeError`. Likewise, `userBusy` (`assistant_wait.js:39-48`) does not check sidebar `<textarea>` edits (`buildTextControls` at `inpaint_ed_text.js:251-261`), so an external MCP or mid-turn assistant `set_mask` `op: "apply"` within the 120 ms `_textTimer` window cancels the pending render and bakes stale pixels, and while the sidebar `<textarea>` remains unblurred drops `layer._textUndo` instead of settling it.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, all three `verified.json` files, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: `review_full_2026-11-12` recorded `canvas-select/apply-mask-on-text-layer-undone-by-next-edit`, and this finding exposes new holes introduced by its `9a1172a7` fix, so it is not `known`. Severity is downgraded from `should` to `nice` because the UI cannot call `maskOp(layer, "apply")` (and clicking UI buttons blurs `textEdit` first), so triggering either symptom requires an external MCP / plugin `set_mask` call (or an in-flight assistant turn racing a 120 ms sidebar keystroke) concurrent with an active text edit on the same layer.

findings.claim: Commit f7f6e0e0 cleared `layer.dirty = false` before `await uploadPixels(...)` in `syncLayersOnce`, and commit 46ff8b0f updated `flushEditor`, `saveBeforeRestart`, `documentDirty`, `snapshotLayer`, and `syncLayers` to check `layer._uploading` — but missed `serializeForPrompt` line 452. If a reference layer is painted during `serializeForPrompt`'s composite/mask uploads and `syncLayersOnce` begins uploading it, `!l.dirty` is already true while `l.ref` still names the previous PNG, so the local ComfyUI run receives the stale reference image.
findings.scenario:
1. On a large document with a reference layer `l` (no layer mask, `l.ref` pointing to its initial PNG) and a local ComfyUI multi-reference recipe, paint on `l` within 15 s of an earlier edit and click Generate.
2. `serializeForPrompt` awaits `uploadComposite` (line 419) and `uploadCanvas` for the mask (line 433); if the user strokes `l` during that multi-second encode/upload window and the 15 s autosave timer fires `syncLayersOnce`, `l.dirty` becomes `false` and `l._uploading` becomes `true` while `l.ref` is still the old file.
3. Line 452 sees `!l.maskPx && l.ref && !l.dirty` as true and sends the old `l.ref` to ComfyUI instead of encoding `l.exportRef` from `this.layerPixels(l)`.
findings.evidence:
In `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:901-903` (`syncLayersOnce`):
`if (layer.dirty && layer.px) {`
`    layer.dirty = false;`
`    layer._uploading = true;`
while `layer.ref = ref` is assigned only after `await uploadPixels(...)` resolves (`line 907`). In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:450-458` (`serializeForPrompt`):
`const refLayers = this.refLayersFor(opts.refIds);`
`for (const l of refLayers) {`
`    if (!l.maskPx && l.ref && !l.dirty) { references.push(l.ref); continue; }`
`    if (!l.exportRef) {`
`        const up = await uploadCanvas(this.layerPixels(l), ...);`
Unlike `host_documents.js:40,80`, `shell.js:1011`, `inpaint_canvas.js:886`, and `inpaint_ed_history.js:180`, line 452 does not check `!l._uploading`.
findings.fix: Change `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:452` to `if (!l.maskPx && l.ref && !l.dirty && !l._uploading) { references.push(l.ref); continue; }`.
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `serializeForPrompt` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:407-460`) serializes reference layers at lines 451-458 with `if (!l.maskPx && l.ref && !l.dirty) { references.push(l.ref); continue; }` (line 452), falling back to `uploadCanvas(this.layerPixels(l), ...)` into `l.exportRef` only when that condition is false. Meanwhile, `syncLayersOnce` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:904-937`, shifted from the candidate's cited lines 898-908) clears `layer.dirty = false` and sets `layer._uploading = true` at lines 907-908 BEFORE `const { ref } = await uploadPixels(...)` at line 910, only updating `layer.ref = ref` at line 911 and deleting `layer._uploading` in `finally` at line 916. (Historically, clearing `layer.dirty = false` before the await pre-dated `f7f6e0e0`; commits `f7f6e0e0` and `46ff8b0f` added `_uploading` / `_maskUploading` and guarded `duplicateLayer` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:307`, `snapshotLayer` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:180`, `flushEditor` at `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:34`, `documentDirty` at `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:79`, and `saveBeforeRestart` at `renderer/shell.js:1011`, leaving `inpaint_ed_persist.js:452` as the remaining `dirty` check that ignores `l._uploading`.)

Tracing the full call path (`generate` at `inpaint_canvas.js:1291` -> `queueGenerate` at `renderer/editor/host_queue.js:22` -> `editor.serializeForPrompt(sopts)` at `host_queue.js:143,146`) shows strong partial guards that block any ordinary pre-click edit, plus one flaw in the candidate's autosave timing detail, without making line 452 unreachable. First, `serializeForPrompt` begins with `await this.syncLayers()` at `inpaint_ed_persist.js:411`, and `syncLayers()` (`inpaint_canvas.js:898-902`) chains onto `this._syncing`, so any reference-layer edit that was already `dirty` or already `_uploading` when `serializeForPrompt` started is completely uploaded into `l.ref` before execution reaches line 412. Second, painting a stroke calls `markLayerChanged` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_select.js:1552`) -> `scheduleAutosave` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:297-304`), which calls `clearTimeout(this._autosave)` and resets the 15 s timer, so an earlier edit's 15 s autosave does not fire right after a new stroke.

Nevertheless, between line 411 (`await this.syncLayers()`) and line 452, `serializeForPrompt` awaits `this.uploadComposite()` (line 419), `uploadCanvas` for the mask (lines 431/433), `uploadCanvas` for control layers (line 441), and `uploadCanvas` for any preceding masked reference layers (line 454). During those awaits, an unmasked reference layer `l` with an existing `l.ref` can become `dirty = true` with `l.exportRef = null` — for example via a debounced/async `renderTextLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_text.js:71,101-145,259`) from text typed immediately before clicking Generate, a stroke during the composite/mask upload, or a `canvas`/`turn` undo in `applySnapshot` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:696,757`, which sets `dirty: true, exportRef: null` without calling `scheduleAutosave()`, leaving an earlier 15 s `_autosave` timer armed). If `syncLayers()` is then kicked off before line 452 runs — by `Ctrl+S` (`saveDocument` -> `flushEditor` at `host_documents.js:36`), a second queued local `Ctrl+Enter` (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:131` -> `generate` -> `serializeForPrompt` line 411), closing the modal (`inpaint_canvas.js:413`), an un-reset `_autosave` timer after undo, or a >15 s composite upload — `syncLayersOnce` sets `l.dirty = false` and `l._uploading = true` while `l.ref` still points to the previous PNG, and line 452 pushes that stale `l.ref` instead of encoding `this.layerPixels(l)` via `l.exportRef`.

This defect is not in `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, or any of the three `verified.json` files; it is a genuine missed call site in the 2026-11-12/16 `_uploading` fixes (`f7f6e0e0` and `46ff8b0f`), fixed by checking `!l.dirty && !l._uploading` at `inpaint_ed_persist.js:452`. Because `await this.syncLayers()` at line 411 flushes all normal pre-click edits and reaching `!l.dirty && l._uploading` at line 452 requires a narrow overlapping edit + concurrent `syncLayers()` trigger during composite/mask upload on the local ComfyUI path (not paid API providers, which capture reference canvases synchronously in `prepareCropAsync` / `runGenerate`), `nice` is the appropriate severity.

findings.claim: Applying a canvas extension with *Generate the new border* (`extendGenerate`) enabled asks for cost confirmation only when `s.provider && s.charged` is truthy, which `resultInputState` sets only on `r.kind === "provider"` recipes. ComfyUI workflows that call paid ComfyUI API Partner Nodes (`kind: "comfy", mode: "api"`, wired to `result` instead of `result_local`) return neither `provider` nor `charged`, so extending the canvas silently queues a paid ComfyUI API run without asking.
findings.scenario: Enable *Generate the new border* in the Canvas tool (saved in `localStorage` as `ipc.extendGenerate` across tabs and restarts), select an imported ComfyUI workflow recipe that uses paid ComfyUI API Partner Nodes (`mode: "api"`), drag a Canvas frame outward, and press Enter or Apply. No cost confirmation dialog appears and `generateAfterExtend()` immediately queues the paid ComfyUI API Partner Node workflow.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/host_presets.js:698-701`: `if (r.kind === "provider") return { name: "result", wired: true, fallback: editor.genSettings.mode === "local", provider: true, charged: r.provider !== "inapp", label: r.providerLabel || r.provider || "", recipeName: r.name || r.id || "" }; const want = editor.genSettings.mode === "local" ? "result_local" : "result"; const has = r.mode === "api" ? "result" : "result_local"; return { name: has, wired: !!r.result, fallback: want !== has };` (and `resultInputStateFromGraph` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1081-1088` likewise omits `charged`). `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1245-1246`: `const s = this.resultInputState(); if (s.provider && s.charged) { ... }`. By contrast, `renderer/editor/eacharea.js:182-185` explicitly treats `r.mode === "api" || !!(state && state.name === "result")` as `charged` (`"ComfyUI API"`).
findings.fix: Set `charged: r.mode === "api", label: "ComfyUI API", recipeName: r.name || r.id || ""` on `kind: "comfy"` recipes in `host_presets.js:701` (and `charged: name === "result", label: "ComfyUI API"` when wired in `resultInputStateFromGraph`), and check `if (s && s.charged)` in `applyFrame` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1246`).
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, the quoted code in `renderer/editor/host_presets.js:698-701`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1081-1088`, and `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1244-1257` holds as described. In `host_presets.js:698`, `resultInputState(editor)` sets `{ provider: true, charged: r.provider !== "inapp", label: ..., recipeName: ... }` only when `r.kind === "provider"`, whereas for `r.kind === "comfy"` (`lines 699-701`) it returns `{ name: has, wired: !!r.result, fallback: want !== has }` (`has = r.mode === "api" ? "result" : "result_local"`) with neither `provider` nor `charged`. Likewise, `resultInputStateFromGraph()` (`inpaint_canvas.js:1081-1088`, used by the ComfyUI custom node's `js/host.js:91-93`, which shares `inpaint_ed_geometry.js` via `tools/build_node.py:48`) returns `{ name, wired, fallback }` without `charged`. In `applyFrame()` (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1244-1257`), when `grows && this.extendGenerate` is true, line 1246 checks `if (s.provider && s.charged)` before opening `this.ask(...)`. When a ComfyUI workflow wired to `result` (`kind: "comfy", mode: "api"`) is active, `s.provider && s.charged` is falsy, so `applyFrame()` skips the confirmation dialog, runs `extendCanvas(pos)` (`line 1283`), and immediately calls `this.generateAfterExtend()` (`line 1292` -> `this.generate()` at `line 1308` -> `host.queueGenerate` at `inpaint_canvas.js:1329` / `host_queue.js:216` `result_source = r.result`), queueing the workflow without asking. (Note: `provider: true` on `resultInputState` must stay restricted to `r.kind === "provider"` because `inpaint_canvas.js:1309` uses `this.resultInputState().provider` for the `providerPending` concurrency guard, so `applyFrame` should check `s && s.charged` once `charged` is populated.)

One piece of the candidate's evidence is false at f45a86cc: `renderer/editor/eacharea.js:182-185` is `areaCount` and contains no `r.mode === "api"` or `"ComfyUI API"` logic; `runEachArea` (`eacharea.js:448, 466-468`) and `eachAreaRow` (`electron/main/assistant/policy.js:300-306`) actually use the same `r.kind === "provider" && r.provider !== "inapp"` rule as `host_presets.js:698`. Even so, the gap in `applyFrame` is real: Scumble's `modeOf` (`renderer/shell_settings.js:23, 194` and `docs/RECIPES.md:641-643`) groups `kind: "comfy", mode: "api"` recipes under `"api"` (`"API models"`), `extendGenerateInput()`'s tooltip (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1339`) promises that `"an API recipe is charged as for Generate"`, and in the shared ComfyUI node (`inpaint_modal.js:208` and `ComfyUI-InpaintCanvas/examples/inpaint_canvas_flux2_api.json` / `inpaint_canvas_flux3_boxes.json`) the `result` input specifically exists to isolate paid ComfyUI API Partner Node chains (`Flux2ImageNode`, `Flux 3 Image`) that spend ComfyUI API credits.

Severity is downgraded from `should` to `nice`. Zero shipped recipes in Scumble's `recipes/` have `kind: "comfy", mode: "api"`: all 13 shipped `kind: "comfy"` recipes have `mode: "local"`, while every shipped paid API, Comfy Cloud (`cloud_*` in `tools/cloud_recipes.js:104-108`), Comfy Router (`comfyrouter`), and Comfy Partner (`comfypartner`) recipe has `kind: "provider"` and does prompt on `applyFrame`. In Scumble, `kind: "comfy", mode: "api"` only exists when a user imports or saves a workflow wired to `InpaintCanvas`'s `result` input (`electron/main/recipes_workflow.js:244, 273, 280`; `electron/main/recipes_graph.js:76-77, 113, 117`). Moreover, `extendGenerate` (`localStorage` `ipc.extendGenerate`, `inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1316-1324`) is off by default and visibly shown in both the Canvas tool bar (`inpaint_ed_chrome.js:521`) and Canvas side panel (`inpaint_modal.js:874`), and `recipes_workflow.js` / `resultInputStateFromGraph` infer `mode: "api"` purely from the `result` pin without knowing whether the upstream nodes actually bill credits. Hitting an unintended charge requires leaving `extendGenerate` sticky across tabs/sessions and extending the canvas on a user-imported `mode: "api"` Partner Node workflow (or in the ComfyUI node on a `result`-wired Partner Node graph).

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Open` and `## Fixed`), `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md` (item 63 was introduced on 2026-11-15/16 in `33e5cedc` / `ad1d30e8`), `scratch/leads_p1-outpaint-shadow.json`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the 2026-11-07 / 2026-11-12 `verified.json` files: not previously recorded.

findings.claim: `idsNamedBy` does not extract the created layer ID from either `contact_shadow` (`result.id`) or `extend_canvas` with `generate: true` (`result.generated.layer.id`), while `runCall` immediately records every layer in `after` into `chat.seen`. As a result, the assistant never owns the shadow or outpainted border layer it just created, and any follow-up `set_layer`, `set_mask`, `transform_layer`, or `remove_layer` on that layer interrupts the turn with a false `"changes/removes a layer you made"` ask card.
findings.scenario: Ask the built-in assistant to add a contact shadow under the cut-out layer and lower its opacity or mask part of it (or to `extend_canvas` with `generate: true` and set `match: 50` on the generated border layer). After `contact_shadow` (auto) or `extend_canvas` (approved once) creates the new layer, the assistant's very next `set_layer` or `set_mask` call on that new layer pauses on an approval card claiming it modifies `"a layer you made"`.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/assistant/index.js:899-902`: `const named = idsNamedBy(name, parsed); const fresh = after.map((l) => l.id).filter((id) => !before.includes(id) && !this.setOf(chat.seen, doc).has(id)); for (const id of named) if (fresh.includes(id)) this.setOf(chat.owned, doc).add(id); for (const l of after) this.setOf(chat.seen, doc).add(l.id);`. In `idsNamedBy` (`lines 1077-1089`), line 1081 lists `["add_paint_layer", "add_filter", "add_text", "add_image_layer", "duplicate_layer", "film_apply_look", "copy_to_layer"]` (missing `"contact_shadow"`, which returns `{ ...layerSummary(ed, out), ... }` at `renderer/commands_layers.js:145`), and line 1082 checks `result.layer && result.layer.id` for `generate` etc. (missing `extend_canvas`, which nests it at `result.generated && result.generated.layer && result.generated.layer.id` at `renderer/commands_edit.js:311`). `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:98-105, 116-118, 474` then gates `set_layer`, `set_mask`, `transform_layer`, and `remove_layer` on `owns(call, facts)`.
findings.fix: In `idsNamedBy` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:1081-1088`), include `"contact_shadow"` in the `add(result.id)` list (along with other layer-creating tools like `dodge_burn_layer` / `add_surface_layer` / `wrap_layer` if applicable) and for `name === "extend_canvas"` call `add(result.generated && result.generated.layer && result.generated.layer.id)`.
findings.why:
At `f45a86cc`, `Assistant.runCall` (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:895-906`) grants layer ownership to `chat.owned` for non-read document commands only when a layer ID is both fresh (`!before.includes(id) && !this.setOf(chat.seen, doc).has(id)`, line 900) and returned by `idsNamedBy(name, parsed)` (lines 899, 901), and then unconditionally adds every layer in `after` to `chat.seen` on line 902 (`for (const l of after) this.setOf(chat.seen, doc).add(l.id)`). Once a call finishes without `idsNamedBy` naming its newly created layer, that layer ID is permanently in `chat.seen` and excluded from `chat.owned` for the rest of the chat.

Tracing the layer-creating commands confirms the gap at `electron/main/assistant/index.js:1077-1089`. First, `contact_shadow` (`renderer/commands_layers.js:127-146`, policy `AUTO` at `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:73`) creates a new paint layer via `ed.addContactShadow` -> `this.addLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shadow.js:239`) and returns `{ ...layerSummary(ed, out), under: l.id, ms: ed._shadowMs, status: ed.status }` (line 145), putting the new ID at `result.id` (`renderer/commands_util.js:64-66`), yet `"contact_shadow"` is absent from the `result.id` allowlist on `index.js:1081` (`["add_paint_layer", "add_filter", "add_text", "add_image_layer", "duplicate_layer", "film_apply_look", "copy_to_layer"]`). Second, `extend_canvas` with `generate: true` (`renderer/commands_edit.js:269-315`, policy `ASK` at `policy.js:141-145`) runs `RunCommandsPart.generate.run` at line 305 (`renderer/commands_runs.js:441`, which returns `{ layer: layerSummary(ed, layer), ... }`) and nests that object at `result.generated` on line 311 (`return { width, height, status: ed.status, generated }`), whereas `idsNamedBy` line 1082 only inspects `result.layer && result.layer.id` for `generate`, `upscale`, `realism_pass`, `glb_place`, and `relight` and has no branch for `extend_canvas` (`result.generated.layer.id`). The same omission in `idsNamedBy` line 1081 also affects `add_surface_layer` (`renderer/commands_edit.js:79-112`, returning `layerSummary(ed, l)` via `ed.addSurfaceLayer` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:358-367`), `wrap_layer` (`renderer/commands_edit.js:113-127`, returning `{ ...layerSummary(ed, out), hidden: l.id, ... }` via `ed.wrapLayer` at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:422-451`), and `dodge_burn_layer` (`renderer/commands_layers.js:86-90`, returning `layerSummary(ed, l)`), as well as `frequency_separation` (`commands_layers.js:81-85`, returning `{ low, high }` at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:216`).

No guard prevents the follow-up ask card: in subsequent steps of the same turn or later turns, `factsFor` passes `owned: this.setOf(chat.owned, doc)` (`index.js:919`), `owns(call, facts)` (`policy.js:241-244`) returns `false` for the disowned layer, and `policy.decide` gates `set_layer` soft fields (`opacity`, `blend`, `visible`, `name`, `role`, `match`, `match_source`, `alpha_lock` at `policy.js:41, 474`), `remove_layer` (`lines 98-100`), `set_mask` (`lines 103-105`), `merge_down` (`lines 107-113`), `transform_layer` (`lines 116-118`), and `copy_to_layer` with `cut: true` (`line 122`) behind `ASK("... a layer you made", ...)`. Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: not previously recorded (`contact_shadow` and `extend_canvas` `generate` were added in 0.1.57 items 61 and 63). Severity `nice` holds because no pixels, state, or money are lost — the defect only triggers an extra confirmation prompt with misleading `"a layer you made"` text, and clicking Allow lets the call proceed normally.

findings.claim: `localRunEnded` and the `status` (`queue_remaining === 0`) listener clear `ed._localRuns` as soon as ComfyUI finishes executing, while `addResults` is still asynchronously fetching and decoding the result image over HTTP. During that decode window `turnBlocked()` returns `""`, so a single `Ctrl+Z` (undoing `"Extend canvas"`), crop, or turn can change the document's geometry before `addResults` pushes `"Result n"` (clearing redo) and places the result at the old extended coordinates.
findings.scenario: On a local ComfyUI recipe, extend a 1024x1024 canvas by 512 px on the left with *Generate the new border* ticked. As soon as ComfyUI finishes (`execution_success` / `queue_remaining: 0`), press `Ctrl+Z` while `addResults` is awaiting `loadImageEl(viewUrl(ref))`: because Lane A removed the pre-Generate undo step, that single `Ctrl+Z` immediately undoes `"Extend canvas"` back to 1024x1024, and milliseconds later `addResults` pushes `"Result 1"` (wiping the redo stack) and places the outpainted border layer at the extended geometry's coordinates.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/host.js:206-210`: `executed` calls `ed.addResults(detail.output.inpaint_canvas_results)` without awaiting it or holding a landing counter. `renderer/editor/host.js:229-245`: `execution_success` calls `localRunEnded(detail)` (`ed._localRuns.delete(id)`) and `status` with `queue_remaining === 0` calls `ed._localRuns.clear()`. Meanwhile `addResults` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:652-663`) awaits `loadImageEl(viewUrl(ref))` before calling `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Result " + n })` and `this.addLayer(...)` with `r.x, r.y, r.width, r.height`, with no geometry-token check around the await, while `turnBlocked()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:627-636`) sees `_localRuns.size === 0` and allows geometry undo/edits.
findings.fix: Increment a counter (e.g. `ed._landingResults`) around `ed.addResults(...)` in `host.js:208` (or inside `addResults` around `loadImageEl`) and include `this._landingResults > 0` in `turnBlocked()` (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:627`).
findings.why: Verified at `f45a86cc`. For a ComfyUI recipe (`r.kind !== "provider"`), `queueGenerate` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:298`) records `prompt_id` in `editor._localRuns`. When the output node finishes on ComfyUI, the `executed` listener in `renderer/editor/host.js:189-207` (note: the property is `out.inpaint_result` at lines 189 and 197, not `inpaint_canvas_results` as written in the candidate's evidence note) invokes `ed.addResults(...)` at line 197 without holding any pending-landing guard on `ed`. Immediately after `executed`, ComfyUI emits `execution_success` (`host.js:240` -> `localRunEnded(detail)` at `host.js:229-233`, deleting `id` from `ed._localRuns`) and `status` with `queue_remaining === 0` (`host.js:242-245`, calling `ed._localRuns.clear()` and idling `ed.runProgress`). Meanwhile, `addResults` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:644-684`) is suspended at `const img = await loadImageEl(viewUrl(ref))` (line 652). Because a fresh ComfyUI output is not yet in Scumble's local mirror, `handleView` (`electron/main/files.js:279-309`) misses locally (line 295), fetches `/view` over HTTP from the local or remote (e.g. RunPod) ComfyUI server (line 297), writes the file atomically to the mirror (line 304), and returns the PNG to the renderer for `` decode. `eacharea.js:393, 416-421` (`waitLocal`) explicitly documents this exact gap ("a result may land a little after its prompt's end") and waits up to 10 s for `_landedPrompts` after `_localRuns` clears, whereas `turnBlocked()` does not. Tracing all guards on geometry changes and undo during that fetch/decode window: unlike API runs in `runProvider` (`renderer/editor/host_provider.js:315, 390, 401, 415-417` and `host_generate.js:426-433`), which intentionally hold `editor.providerPending` across `await editor.addResults(...)` until `finally`, local runs leave `providerPending` null, `addResults` is not wrapped in `trackEdit` (`_pendingEdits`), and `turnBlocked()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:627-636`) and `generateNewBlocked()` (`renderer/editor/host_generate.js:439-447`) check only `_localRuns.size` (line 633 / line 442). Once `localRunEnded` / `status` clears `_localRuns` (and hides the progress bar), `turnBlocked()` returns `""`, allowing `historyStepNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1083`) to undo a `canvas` or `turn` step (such as Item 63's `"Extend canvas"`, which sits directly at the top of `this.undo` now that Lane A removed the pre-Generate undo step) or allowing `turnDocumentNow`, `cropCanvasNow`, `resizeImageNow`, or `extendCanvasNow` to change document geometry. When `loadImageEl` resolves moments later, `addResults` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:653-663`) checks no geometry or history token, calls `this.pushUndo({ kind: "layers", label: "Result " + n })` (which clears `this.redo` in `pushUndoSnapshot` at `inpaint_ed_history.js:489-490`, wiping the undone `"Extend canvas"` redo entry), and places the layer at the pre-undo/pre-turn `r.x, r.y, r.width, r.height`. Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including Lane A's fixed entry at lines 53-64), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` (`shell/gen-new-closes-tab-of-running-local-render` is a separate `shell.js` `busy()` omission on timeout), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json` (`host/H-1` and `host/H-4` cover empty-tab `Generate new` and dropped `executed` events on socket reconnect), `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: this defect is not previously recorded. Severity `nice` holds because hitting it requires acting inside the brief post-`execution_success` `/view` fetch and PNG decode window (tens of milliseconds on localhost, up to ~1-2 s on a remote ComfyUI server), matching the project's `nice` calibration for narrow async edit/undo races.

findings.claim: When large `distance`, `softness`, or `skew` values push the shadow grid past `SHADOW_MAX_CELLS` (4M) or `SHADOW_MAX_CELLS_PREVIEW` (1M), `shadowGrid` repeatedly box-averages coverage with `coarserCoverage` and re-runs `shadowExtent` / `contactShadow` against the hard `SOLID = 0.5` threshold. Narrow opaque features (such as a thin pole or thin chair/table legs) average below `0.5` in the coarse cells, either falsely refusing with `"has no opaque part in the picture"` or losing the legs so `foot` jumps up to the wider body.
findings.scenario: On a 2048 px tall layer containing a fully opaque 3 px wide vertical pole (or a chair standing on 2 px legs), run `contact_shadow` with `distance: 300, softness: 100` (or drag Softness/Distance high in the Contact Shadow dialog, where the preview cap is 1M cells). `shadowSource` builds coverage with `th = 2048, tw = 16`, `shadowGrid` coarsens by `f = 8` (`coarserCoverage`), peak cell alpha drops to at most `2/8 = 0.25 < 0.5`, and `addContactShadow` refuses with `"<layer> has no opaque part in the picture: it casts no shadow."` (or for the chair, places the shadow's contact line up at the seat instead of the floor).
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shadow.js:110-121`: `for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { const e = shadowExtent(src.alpha, src.w, src.h, params); if (!e) return { grid: null, src }; if (e.cells <= maxCells || (src.w <= 8 && src.h <= 8)) break; src = coarserCoverage(src, Math.max(2, Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(e.cells / maxCells)))); } ... return { grid: contactShadow({ alpha: src.alpha, w: src.w, h: src.h, params, depthAt }), src };`. `coarserCoverage` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_shadow.js:115-128`) computes arithmetic mean `sum[i] / n[i]`, while `alphaBox` (`lines 42-50`, called by both `shadowExtent` at `line 103` and `contactShadow` at `line 137`) requires `alpha[row + x] >= SOLID` (`SOLID = 0.5`, `line 26`). When `grid` comes back `null`, `addContactShadow` (`inpaint_ed_shadow.js:228`) reports `"has no opaque part in the picture"` even though `src0` had opaque pixels.
findings.fix: Compute `box0 = alphaBox(src0.alpha, src0.w, src0.h)` before coarsening, scale `box0` down alongside `src` (passing `box` into `contactShadow` and using max-pooling or preserving peak column contact in `prof` / `coarserCoverage`), so coarsening for wide blur/reach never erases thin opaque features or shifts `foot`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit `f45a86cc` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_shadow.js:110-122` (`shadowGrid`) and `renderer/editor/inpaint_shadow.js:31, 58-73, 89-128, 136-201`. (Minor line-offset note on the candidate's `inpaint_shadow.js` citations: `SOLID = 0.5` is at line 31, `alphaBox` at lines 58-73, `shadowExtent`'s `alphaBox` call at line 109, `coarserCoverage` at lines 119-128, and `contactShadow`'s `alphaBox` call at line 137; `inpaint_ed_shadow.js:113` and `228` match exactly.)

Tracing the full call path confirms no guard prevents coarsening from erasing narrow opaque features or shifting `foot` upward. Both entry points — `contactShadowDialogNow` (`inpaint_ed_shadow.js:276, 285`, `SHADOW_WORK_PREVIEW = 768`, `SHADOW_MAX_CELLS_PREVIEW = 1e6`) and `addContactShadow` (`inpaint_ed_shadow.js:226-228`, also reached from MCP `contact_shadow` at `renderer/commands_layers.js:142-143`, `SHADOW_WORK = 2048`, `SHADOW_MAX_CELLS = 4e6`) — build `src0` via `shadowSource` (`lines 87-103`), where the `FIND_WORK = 512` pass uses a low `0.02` alpha threshold (`line 93`). On a 2048x2048 layer with a 3 px wide opaque vertical pole, `coarse` (`512x512`, `sx = sy = 0.25`) sees alpha `0.75 >= 0.02` and produces `ob` of `16x2048`, so `src0` has `w = 16, h = 2048` with 3 columns at `alpha = 1.0`. Inside `shadowGrid` (`lines 111-116`), iteration `i = 0` calls `shadowExtent` (`inpaint_shadow.js:108-113`): with `distance: 300, softness: 100`, `extentOf` (`lines 89-102`) computes `H = 2048, R = 6144, sigma = 2048, pad = 6146, up = 861`, yielding `gw = 12295, gh = 19298` (`e.cells = 237,268,910 > 4e6`). The loop guard `(src.w <= 8 && src.h <= 8)` (`line 114`) uses `&&`, so `src.h = 2048` prevents breaking, and `coarserCoverage(src, 8)` (`inpaint_shadow.js:119-128`) box-averages 8x8 blocks to `w = 2, h = 256`, dropping peak alpha to at most `3/8 = 0.375` (`0.25` when split across the block boundary), strictly below `SOLID = 0.5`. On iteration `i = 1`, `shadowExtent` -> `alphaBox` returns `null`, `shadowGrid` returns `{ grid: null, src }` at line 113, and `addContactShadow` (`line 228`) falsely refuses with `"<layer> has no opaque part in the picture: it casts no shadow."` (which MCP `contact_shadow` throws as an error). Even at moderate settings (e.g. default `distance: 30` with `softness: 25` in the dialog preview gives ~1.71M > 1M cells, `f = 2`; `softness: 50` on Apply gives ~44.4M > 4M cells, `f = 4`), thin poles vanish, and on objects with thin legs beneath a wider body, `alphaBox` loses the legs (`< 0.5`) while keeping the upper body (`>= 0.5`), jumping `box.foot` (and `footDepth` sampling at `inpaint_shadow.js:174`) up from the floor to the body's underside (`contactShadow` at line 136 accepts an optional `box`, but `shadowGrid` at line 121 never scales or passes the pre-coarsening box).

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, all three `verified.json` review files, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md`: item 61 (`4fad3634` / `e55907d8`) is new in 0.1.57 and this defect was introduced by `e55907d8`'s cell-cap coarsening loop, so it is not known. Severity is `nice` because triggering it requires both high softness/distance/skew (pushing `e.cells` past 1M/4M) and features narrower than ~0.2-0.4% of the object's height, causing no data loss or corruption of existing layers.

findings.claim: Closing a tab while File › Open is still streaming its granted file into a Blob (`Reading <name> ...`) does not cancel the open. When `grantedFile(g)` finishes, `onOpened` treats `ed._destroyed` the same as `ed.base` and calls `openInto(file)`, opening a new tab (or overwriting the empty tab now in front) with the file from the tab the user just closed.
findings.scenario: Have a picture open in Tab 1. Press Ctrl+O and choose a large file (e.g. a 1.5–2.6 GB PSD or a file on a slow/network drive, where `grantedFile` streams for several seconds). `onOpened` creates and activates Tab 2 showing `Reading big.psd ...`. Close Tab 2 (`Ctrl+W` or the tab's `×`) while it is still reading. `closeDocument` destroys Tab 2 (`ed._destroyed = true`) and returns focus to Tab 1; seconds later `grantedFile` resolves with no abort, hits `if (ed._destroyed || ed.base) await openInto(file);`, and opens a brand-new Tab 3 loading `big.psd` anyway (unlike `loadFile`, which stops when `this._destroyed` is true).
findings.evidence: renderer/shell.js:1079-1083 `if (!ed || ed.base) { ed = newDocument(); activate(ed); made = true; } ed.setStatus(\`Reading ${g.name} ...\`); let file; try { file = await grantedFile(g, { type: pictureType(g.name, { svg: false }) }); }` (no AbortSignal passed to `grantedFile`). renderer/shell.js:1094-1095 `if (ed._destroyed || ed.base) await openInto(file); else await ed.loadFile(file);`. Contrast renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:165-166 `// a closed tab's open is over too: its read stops at its next band and nothing reaches the local store` / `const later = () => this._destroyed || this._openToken !== token;`.
findings.fix: Abort the `fetch` in `grantedFile` when `ed` is closed (or check `if (ed._destroyed) return;` after `await grantedFile(...)`), and route to `openInto(file)` only when `!ed._destroyed && ed.base` (another picture landed in the reused empty tab during the read).
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc. When the user picks an image or layered file in File › Open, `openImage` -> `openChosen` -> `filePayload` (`electron/main/main.js:927-960`) grants a token and sends `file:opened` (`main.js:952`). In `renderer/shell.js:1074-1096`, the `window.scumble.file.onOpened` listener picks or creates the target tab before reading: if `!ed || ed.base`, it creates and activates a new empty tab (`ed = newDocument(); activate(ed); made = true;` at `shell.js:1079`), sets `ed.setStatus("Reading " + g.name + " ...")` (`shell.js:1080`), and awaits `grantedFile(g, ...)` (`shell.js:1083`). Inside `renderer/grantfile.js:29-48`, `grantedFile` runs `fetch(g.url, { cache: "no-store" })` (`grantfile.js:34`) and `await res.blob()` (`grantfile.js:42`) without taking an `AbortSignal`.

No guard prevents closing `ed` during that read or cancels the read when `ed` closes. In `closeDocument` (`renderer/shell.js:296-335`), `ed.base` is still `null`, `runs.length` is 0, and `busy(ed)` (`shell.js:219-221`) is `false`, so both the busy confirmation (`shell.js:311`) and the dirty prompt (`shell.js:315`) are skipped; `closeDocument` removes `ed` (`shell.js:326`), creates a replacement empty tab if none remain (`shell.js:328`), activates the remaining tab (`shell.js:329`), and calls `editor.destroy()` (`shell.js:333`), which sets `this._destroyed = true` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1600`). Meanwhile `grantedFile` keeps streaming the entire file into a `Blob`. When `grantedFile` resolves, `onOpened` reaches `renderer/shell.js:1094-1095`: `if (ed._destroyed || ed.base) await openInto(file); else await ed.loadFile(file);`. Because `ed._destroyed` is `true`, it enters the first branch and calls `openInto(file)` (`shell.js:356-360`), which either opens and activates a brand-new tab (when the active tab has `ed.base`) or loads `file` into the active empty tab (such as the fresh empty tab created at `shell.js:328` when the sole tab was closed). By contrast, the error catch just above (`shell.js:1088-1092`) does nothing when `ed._destroyed` is `true`, and `loadFile` itself (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:165-166`) explicitly treats `this._destroyed` as cancellation (`const later = () => this._destroyed || this._openToken !== token;`).

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: not known. This defect was newly introduced on 2026-11-16 in commit `454dcc3f` (lane D of `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md`, fixing `docs/BUGS.md:38-52` "Ctrl+O sends the whole file to the window in one message").

Severity calibrated from `should` down to `nice`: no user pixels, edits, or undo history are lost (`openInto` never overwrites a tab with `ed.base`), and a single `Ctrl+W` closes the resurrected tab. Moreover, on local NVMe the `grantedFile` window before `loadFile` starts (after which `this._destroyed` does stop the open) is narrow for ordinary files — 329–358 ms at ~250 MB and 1,429 ms for a 970 MB 15k PSD (`docs/measurements/ctrlo_2026-11-16/summary.txt:36-44`), only stretching to several seconds on multi-GB files (2.8–3.3 s at 2.0–2.6 GB, `:62-63`) or slow/network/cloud-placeholder drives.

findings.claim: `openFiles` uses `GrantedFiles`'s default cap of `max = 8` active tokens, while incoming bridge/MCP commands (`add_image_layer`, `load_image`) run concurrently without serialization. Issuing 9 or more concurrent `add_image_layer` or `load_image` calls by `path` evicts the earliest tokens in `grant()` before their renderer `fetch` reaches `serve()`, failing valid readable files with `404: no such file`.
findings.scenario: An MCP agent (e.g. an LLM turn emitting 9 parallel `add_image_layer` tool calls to populate layers or `@img` references) or a plugin calls `commands.run('add_image_layer', { path })` 9 times concurrently. `window.scumble.commands.onRequest` runs all 9 concurrently (`shell.js:1435-1469`), so all 9 enter `fileFrom` -> `grantPath` -> IPC `file:grant` -> `openFiles.grantReadable`. The 9th `grant()` sees `this.grants.size > 8` and deletes the 1st token before the renderer receives its `file:grant` reply and starts `fetch('scumble://app/file/<token>')`. The 1st call then gets HTTP 404 (`no such file`) and fails with `could not read <name> (404: no such file)`.
findings.evidence: electron/main/main.js:170 `const openFiles = new GrantedFiles({ types: { ... } });` (omits `max`). electron/main/grantedfiles.js:59 `constructor({ max = 8, types = {}, words = {} } = {})`, :67-71 `grant(file) { const token = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString("hex"); this.grants.set(token, path.resolve(String(file))); while (this.grants.size > this.max) this.grants.delete(this.grants.keys().next().value); return token; }`. renderer/commands_util.js:347-348 `const g = await grantPath(String(a.path)); return grantedFile(g, ...);`. renderer/shell.js:1435,1468 `window.scumble.commands.onRequest(async ({ id, name, args, meta }) => { ... reply(await commands.call(name, args || {})); });`.
findings.fix: Raise `max` on `openFiles` (e.g. `max: 256` in `main.js:170` or as `GrantedFiles`'s default while keeping `MAX = 8` in `videofiles.js`), since `grantedFile` always releases its token in `finally` (`renderer/grantfile.js:46`).
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `electron/main/main.js:170` instantiates `openFiles = new GrantedFiles({ types: { ... } })` without passing `max`, so it inherits `max = 8` from `GrantedFiles`'s constructor (`electron/main/grantedfiles.js:59`, carried over from `VideoFiles`'s `MAX = 8` in `electron/main/videofiles.js:16`). Whenever `grant(file)` (`grantedfiles.js:67-72`) inserts a token, it immediately evicts oldest entries via `while (this.grants.size > this.max) this.grants.delete(this.grants.keys().next().value);`. Both `load_image` (`renderer/commands_docs.js:271`) and `add_image_layer` (`renderer/commands_docs.js:291`) resolve a `path` argument through `fileFrom` (`renderer/commands_util.js:347-348`) -> `grantPath` (`renderer/grantfile.js:17-23`, `ipcRenderer.invoke("file:grant", ...)` -> `main.js:1306` -> `filePayload` at `main.js:957-960` -> `openFiles.grantReadable` at `grantedfiles.js:79-92`) followed by `grantedFile` (`renderer/grantfile.js:29-48`, which calls `fetch("scumble://app/file/<token>")` -> `main.js:245` -> `openFiles.serve` at `grantedfiles.js:103-126`).

Tracing every command entry point confirms there is no serialization along the external MCP, local-socket, bridge, or plugin paths: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`'s `Protocol._onrequest` invokes `CallToolRequestSchema` (`electron/main/mcp/server.js:114-129`) without awaiting prior requests; `LocalClient.run` and `LocalServer._accept` (`electron/main/local.js:56-64, 118-130, 183-192`) dispatch each JSON line concurrently into `bridge.run`; `Bridge.run` (`electron/main/bridge.js:102-148`, once `ready` is true and `_timeouts` is cached by `list_commands`) immediately sends `commands:request` over IPC; `window.scumble.commands.onRequest` (`renderer/shell.js:1435-1469`) runs `commands.call(name, args)` concurrently for each message; and plugins (`renderer/plugins.js:63, 680-681`) can likewise call `Promise.all` over `doc.run` / `commands.run`. If 9 or more `add_image_layer` or `load_image` calls with `path` are dispatched in a concurrent burst and main completes 9 `grantReadable()` (`open` + `stat` + `close`) calls before the earliest call's `file:grant` IPC reply + renderer `fetch()` reaches `openFiles.serve()` (`grantedfiles.js:104`), the earliest token is already deleted from `this.grants`; `serve()` answers HTTP 404 `"no such file"`, and `grantedFile()` (`renderer/grantfile.js:36-40`) throws `could not read <name> (404: no such file)` for a valid readable file.

This defect is not in `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Open`), the three `verified.json` files, or `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: `grantedfiles.js` and `openFiles` were newly introduced on 2026-11-16 in lane D (`docs/BUGS.md:38-52`). Severity is calibrated to `nice` rather than `should`: normal GUI workflows cannot hit it (`File > Open` at `main.js:929` uses single-selection `openFile`, and Explorer drag-and-drop passes native `File` objects without `openFiles`), the in-app Assistant is unaffected because `runTurn` awaits tool calls strictly sequentially (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:755-759`), `--run` and `--cmd` are sequential, and even for an external MCP client or plugin firing >=9 parallel calls in one turn it requires the 9th `grantReadable` in main to finish before the 1st call's `fetch` reaches `openFiles.serve()` (once `serve()` passes line 104 and opens its `FileHandle`, token eviction no longer affects that stream), failing cleanly with an error rather than losing data.

findings.claim: `openVideo` captures `const ed = host.editor` before `await loadVideo(url, name)` (which can take seconds during `findDuration` or slow loads) to decide `canLayer`, whereas it applies the chosen action to `host.editor` after `showPicker` resolves, and overlapping `openVideo` calls have no generation check. Switching tabs during `loadVideo` mis-sets `Add as layer`'s enabled state, and an earlier slow `loadVideo` finishing after a second video's picker opened cancels and replaces the newer picker.
findings.scenario: Drop a durationless WebM (`findDuration` seeks to `1e101` and back, up to ~11 s) and immediately drop a short MP4 (loads in <100 ms), or switch from an empty tab to a tab with a picture while the video loads. In the two-drop case, the MP4 picker opens first, then when the earlier WebM's `loadVideo` finishes it calls `showPicker` (`if (current) current.cancel()`), closing the MP4 picker the user is scrubbing; in the tab-switch case, `Add as layer` is disabled (`canLayer` read from the old empty tab) even though `host.editor` now has a picture.
findings.evidence: renderer/shell.js:1106-1125 `async function openVideo({ url, name, focus = "new", note = "", onClose = null }) { const ed = host.editor; ... v = await loadVideo(url, name); ... const r = await showPicker(v, { name, canLayer: !!(ed && ed.base), focus, onClose }); ... const target = host.editor; if (r.action === "new" || !target) await openInto(r.file); else if (r.action === "layer" && target.base) ...` and renderer/videoframe.js:82-93 (`findDuration` awaits up to 5000 + 1000 + 5000 ms), :160 `if (current) current.cancel();`.
findings.fix: Guard `openVideo` with a monotonic sequence counter (if a newer `openVideo` started while `loadVideo` was awaiting, clean up `v`, call `onClose()` and return `null`) and read `const ed = host.editor` after `await loadVideo(url, name)` for `canLayer`.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `openVideo` in `renderer/shell.js:1106-1127` captures `const ed = host.editor;` at line 1107 before `v = await loadVideo(url, name);` at line 1112, then passes `canLayer: !!(ed && ed.base)` to `showPicker` at line 1119, whereas after `showPicker` resolves it reads `const target = host.editor;` at line 1121 (and `say` at line 1108 also writes to the live `host.editor`). `loadVideo` (`renderer/videoframe.js:40-65`) waits up to `LOAD_MS = 20000` ms (`videoframe.js:23,57`) for `loadeddata` and then awaits `findDuration(v)` (`videoframe.js:53,82-93`), which on durationless recordings (`!Number.isFinite(v.duration)`) seeks to `1e101` and back with timeouts of up to 5000 + 1000 + 5000 ms while no modal dialog is open yet. Neither `openVideo` nor its two entry points (`window.scumble.file.onOpenedVideo` at `shell.js:1130-1132` and the window capture `drop` listener at `shell.js:1137-1152`) has a busy guard, AbortSignal, or generation counter, and `videoframe.js` only tracks an already-open dialog via `current` (`videoframe.js:152,160,391`), not an in-flight `loadVideo`.

Both claimed failure modes hold with no intervening guard: (1) If the user switches from an empty tab (`!ed.base`) to a tab with a picture (`host.editor.base`) while `loadVideo` is awaiting, `showPicker` opens over the picture tab with `canLayer: false`, disabling `btn.layer` (`videoframe.js:214`) even though `target = host.editor` has a base; conversely, switching from a picture tab (`ed.base`) to an empty tab leaves `canLayer: true` (and on a drop, `focus: "layer"` from `shell.js:1147-1148` remains the `primary` default at `videoframe.js:221`), so choosing `Add as layer` misses `r.action === "layer" && target.base` (`shell.js:1123`) and falls through to `openInto(r.file)` (`shell.js:1125`). (2) If a slow first `openVideo` (e.g. a durationless WebM or slow network video) is still in `await loadVideo` when a fast second video is dropped or opened via File > Open, the second video opens `showPicker` first (`current = handle`); when the first video's `loadVideo` later resolves, it calls `showPicker`, executing `if (current) current.cancel()` (`videoframe.js:160`), which closes the newer picker, revokes its URL (`onClose`), resolves the second `openVideo` with `null` (writing `No frame taken from <second>.` at `shell.js:1120`), and replaces it with the stale first video's picker (or pops up the stale picker after the user already finished with the second video).

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (all open and recently fixed sections), `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md` (item 68 added in `8ef6a3b1` / `9214a769`), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the 2026-11-07 / 2026-11-12 `verified.json` files: item 68 is newly built in 0.1.57 and this defect is not recorded in any known list. Severity `nice` applies because hitting either issue requires switching tabs or starting a second video open during `loadVideo`'s async window, and neither path loses user data or pixels.

findings.claim: The video frame picker captures a frame without checking whether the seek to `v.currentTime` succeeded: `settled()` resolves identically after its 10 s timeout, `frameFile()` never inspects `v.error`, `v.seeking` or `v.readyState`, and nothing listens for media `error` events once `loadVideo` has resolved. On a truncated or mid-stream damaged video, seeking into the unreadable region and clicking an action waits 10 s and silently imports the previously decoded frame (or blank) mislabelled with the target timestamp.
findings.scenario: Open an MP4 with `moov` at the front declaring 60 s whose file was truncated at 20 s. `loadVideo` decodes the first frame and opens `showPicker`. Drag the range slider to 40 s (`range` input sets `v.currentTime = 40`, line 198); the seek fails past EOF (`error` fires with no listener). Click `Open as new picture`: `settled(v)` times out after 10 s and resolves normally, `v.videoWidth` / `v.videoHeight` are still > 0, `drawImage(v, ...)` draws the stale pre-seek frame, and a PNG named `<stem> 40.000s.png` opens with no error.
findings.evidence: renderer/videoframe.js:113-123 `function settled(v) { return new Promise((resolve) => { if (!v.seeking && v.readyState >= 2) { resolve(); return; } const t = setTimeout(done, 10000); function done() { clearTimeout(t); ... resolve(); } ... }); }`. :126-139 `export async function frameFile(v, name) { await settled(v); const w = v.videoWidth, h = v.videoHeight; if (!(w > 0 && h > 0)) throw new Error("the video shows no frame"); ... return new File([blob], \`${stem} ${v.currentTime.toFixed(3)}s.png\`, ...); }`. :62 `{ once: true }` `error` listener in `loadVideo` only; :263-266 `showPicker` listens only to `timeupdate`, `seeked`, `pause`, `play`.
findings.fix: Have `settled(v)` resolve `false` on timeout or `error`, check `!ok || v.error || v.seeking || v.readyState < 2` in `frameFile(v)` and throw a readable error (which `take()` already catches and displays), and attach an `error` listener in `showPicker` to surface `MEDIA_ERRORS` in `info`.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `renderer/videoframe.js` only attaches a `{ once: true }` `error` listener inside `loadVideo` (line 62, whose `end()` callback also returns early via `if (done) return;` at line 50 once `loadeddata` has fired at line 58). Once `showPicker` opens (line 159), it attaches listeners only for `timeupdate`, `seeked`, `pause`, and `play` (lines 263-266), never `error`, and `update()` (lines 235-246) never inspects `v.error`.

When the user scrubs or jumps into an unreadable region after frame 0 has decoded — for instance a front-`moov` MP4 truncated mid-file (where `GrantedFiles.serve` in `electron/main/grantedfiles.js:114` answers HTTP 416 or `BlobDataSource` hits unexpected EOF), a mid-stream packet decode failure (`MEDIA_ERR_DECODE`), a file removed/unmounted while served via `scumble://app/video/<token>` (`grantedfiles.js:108` answering 404), or a seek over a stalled mount exceeding 10 s — clicking an action calls `take()` (line 343) -> `frameFile(v, name)` (line 126) -> `settled(v)` (line 113). In `settled(v)` (lines 113-123), if `v.seeking` remains true or `v.readyState < 2`, no `error` listener is registered, so it waits out the full `setTimeout(done, 10000)` (line 116) and resolves `undefined` identically to a successful seek; if Chromium already cleared `v.seeking` while setting `v.error` with `readyState >= 2`, line 115 (`if (!v.seeking && v.readyState >= 2)`) resolves immediately despite `v.error`.

`frameFile` (lines 126-139) then checks only `!(w > 0 && h > 0)` (line 129), which still passes because metadata (`videoWidth`/`videoHeight`) was populated at `loadeddata` and is retained across post-metadata media errors and pending seeks. It never checks `v.error`, `v.seeking`, or `v.readyState < 2`. `c.getContext("2d").drawImage(v, 0, 0, w, h)` (line 133) either draws the stale pre-seek frame held by Chromium's compositor or, when `v.readyState === 1` (`HAVE_METADATA`), acts as a spec-mandated Canvas 2D no-op leaving `c` transparent black. `c.toBlob` encodes a valid PNG `File` mislabelled `${stem} ${v.currentTime.toFixed(3)}s.png` (line 138), bypassing `take()`'s `catch` handler (lines 353-358) and handing the wrong or blank image to `openVideo` (`renderer/shell.js:1120-1125`).

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, both 2026-11-07 `verified.json` files, `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md`: `renderer/videoframe.js` was newly introduced in 0.1.57 (`8ef6a3b1` / `9214a769`) and this defect is not recorded in any known list. Severity is `nice` because triggering it requires a truncated/corrupt/vanishing video or >10 s stalled seek, the `<video>` preview in the dialog already visibly fails to advance, and no existing document data is lost.
