findings.claim: While `take()` is awaiting `settled(v)` and PNG encoding (`c.toBlob`), the picker still accepts seeks via the range slider, `Shift+Arrow` (`seconds`), and `Home`/`End` (`jump`), and reads `v.currentTime` only after `toBlob` finishes. Seeking during encode labels the resulting `File` and returned `time` with the new timestamp while the pixels come from the earlier frame (and seeking during `settled` captures a different frame than confirmed).
findings.scenario: Pause a 4K video at `3.200 s`, press `Enter` (`take(def)`), and while `c.toBlob` is encoding the 3840×2160 PNG press `End` or `Shift+Right` or drag the slider. `take()` set `busy = true` and disabled the buttons (line 348), but `range` is not disabled and neither the `range` `input` handler (line 198), `seconds()` (line 327), `jump()` (line 333), nor the `keydown` listener (lines 375-389) checks `busy`. `drawImage` already captured the `3.200 s` pixels, but line 138 names the file `<stem> 58.000s.png` and line 352 returns `time: 58`.
findings.evidence: renderer/videoframe.js:133-138 `c.getContext("2d").drawImage(v, 0, 0, w, h); const blob = await new Promise((resolve) => c.toBlob(resolve, "image/png")); ... return new File([blob], \`${stem} ${v.currentTime.toFixed(3)}s.png\`, { type: "image/png" });`. :198 `range.addEventListener("input", () => { v.pause(); v.currentTime = +range.value; update(); });`. :327-338 `seconds(n)` and `jump(toEnd)` have no `if (busy) return;` (whereas `step` at :286 and `toggle` at :340 check `busy`). :348 `for (const b of [...Object.values(btn), cancel, back, play, fwd]) b.disabled = true;` (omits `range`). :352 `finish({ action, file, time: v.currentTime, ... })`.
findings.fix: Capture `const at = v.currentTime` immediately before `drawImage` in `frameFile` (using `at` for the filename and returning it for `take()`), include `range` in the disabled controls during `busy`, and return early from `seconds()`, `jump()`, and `range`'s `input` listener when `busy` is true.
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc in `renderer/videoframe.js`. When the user confirms an action in `showPicker`, `take(action)` (`renderer/videoframe.js:343-359`) sets `busy = true` (line 346) and disables `[...Object.values(btn), cancel, back, play, fwd]` (line 348), then awaits `frameFile(v, name)` (line 351). However, `range` (`<input type="range">`) is omitted from the disabled controls list at line 348, its `input` handler at line 198 (`() => { v.pause(); v.currentTime = +range.value; update(); }`) does not check `busy`, and neither `seconds(n)` (lines 327-331) nor `jump(toEnd)` (lines 333-338) nor the dialog's capture-phase `keydown` listener (lines 375-389) checks `busy` (unlike `step(n)` at line 286 and `toggle()` at line 340, which both guard on `busy`). In particular, dragging or clicking `range` is always live during `take()`, and if the user scrubbed with `range` and pressed `Enter` (handled at line 388 when `!onButton`), focus remains on the enabled `range` inside the dialog so `Shift+ArrowLeft`/`Shift+ArrowRight` (`seconds`) and `Home`/`End` (`jump`) also fire during `take()` (additionally, an already in-flight `stepping` promise from `step()` is not awaited by `take()`).

Inside `frameFile(v, name)` (`renderer/videoframe.js:126-139`), line 127 awaits `settled(v)`, line 133 draws the current video frame into canvas `c`, and line 134 awaits `new Promise((resolve) => c.toBlob(resolve, "image/png"))` (which takes tens to hundreds of milliseconds on 1080p/4K frames). Only after `toBlob` resolves does line 138 read `v.currentTime` to construct `${stem} ${v.currentTime.toFixed(3)}s.png`, and `take()` likewise reads `time: v.currentTime` at line 352. Consequently, seeking during `toBlob` mutates `v.currentTime` (and `update()` overwrites `info.textContent = "Taking the frame ..."`), causing the resulting `File` name — which `openVideo` in `renderer/shell.js:1122-1125` uses as the new document or layer name — and returned `time` to reflect the new timestamp while the encoded PNG pixels come from the earlier frame drawn at line 133 (and seeking while `settled(v)` is still pending captures a different frame than was on screen when `take()` started).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md` (item 68, introduced 2026-11-16 in `8ef6a3b1`/`9214a769`), and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: this defect is not in any known list. Severity `nice` fits: it is a narrow user-input race window during `settled`/`toBlob` that mislabels the imported frame's layer/document name (or grabs the newly scrubbed frame) without corrupting existing document pixels or billing.

findings.claim: When the Scope section is open and Compare (A/B) is active, every scene redraw (pan, zoom, or dragging the compare divider) invalidates `this.uploaded.baseHash` three times, bumping `compositeVersion`, while `scopeHeld()` ignores `pan` and `split` pointers. As a result, `updateScope()` re-runs `sampleRegionSettled` over the whole picture (up to 1 MP with filter layers on the window thread) roughly every 300 ms throughout the pan, zoom, or divider drag even though no pixels changed.
findings.scenario: On a 15k document with two result layers and filter layers, open Image › Scope and turn on Compare (A/B). Pan with Space+drag (`pointer.kind = 'pan'`), zoom with the wheel, or drag the compare split (`pointer.kind = 'split'`). Every frame's `drawScene` misses `sceneSig` (view `x`/`y`/`scale` or `compare.split` changed) and calls `drawSceneImage`, whose compare loop sets `this.uploaded.baseHash = null` three times (`compositeVersion += 3`). `draw()` calls `scopeSoon()`, `scopeKey()` differs, `scopeHeld()` is false (`gestureHeld()` excludes `pan`, `split`, `guide`), and `updateScope()` composites up to 1024 px on the main thread every ~300 ms until the gesture stops.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_relight.js:664-684 `if (this.compare && this.compare.a && this.compare.b) { ... for (const side of ["a", "b"]) { ... this.compareShow = this.compare[side]; this.uploaded.baseHash = null; this.drawViewComposite(ctx); ... } this.compareShow = null; this.uploaded.baseHash = null;`. renderer/editor/inpaint_strokebuf.js:66-70 `set baseHash(v) { if (v == null) { const ed = this._editor; ed.compositeVersion++;`. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_scope.js:277-279 `scopeKey() { return \`${this.compositeVersion}|${this.historyGen || 0}|${this.width}x${this.height}|${this.base ? 1 : 0}\`; }`, :304-306 `scopeHeld() { return !!(this.gestureHeld() || this.pending); }`, :341-342 `else if (this._scope && this._scope.key !== this.scopeKey()) this.scopeSoon();`. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1029-1032 `gestureHeld() { const p = this.pointer; return !!p && !["pan", "split", "guide"].includes(p.kind); }`. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_draw.js:125-130 `draw()` calls `this.scopeSoon()`.
findings.fix: Treat any active pointer as held in `scopeHeld()` (`!!(this.pointer || this.pending)`), and avoid bumping `compositeVersion` for transient `compareShow` toggles inside `drawSceneImage` (invalidate view caches without `this.uploaded.baseHash = null`, or restore/separate the scope's content counter).
findings.why:
Verified against commit f45a86cc across the full call path. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_relight.js:664-684`, whenever Compare (A/B) is active (`this.compare && this.compare.a && this.compare.b`, with `!this.peekBase`), `drawSceneImage` renders the left and right halves by toggling `this.compareShow` and executing `this.uploaded.baseHash = null` three times per scene redraw (lines 676, 676 on the second iteration, and 681). In `renderer/editor/inpaint_strokebuf.js:66-75`, `UploadCache.set baseHash(null)` unconditionally increments `this._editor.compositeVersion++` (and clears `ed.flatCache`), so every `drawSceneImage` call under Compare bumps `compositeVersion` by 3 even though no document pixels or layer parameters changed.

When the user pans (`pointer.kind = "pan"`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:369,791-795`), zooms (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_view.js:184-192` or wheel zoom), or drags the compare divider (`pointer.kind = "split"`, `inpaint_ed_pointer.js:385-387,922-924`), `drawScene` (`inpaint_ed_relight.js:623-637`) misses `this.sceneSig !== this.sceneSignature()` because `v.x`, `v.y`, `v.scale`, or `compare.split` changed (`:597-598`), invoking `drawSceneImage` and bumping `compositeVersion += 3` before recording the new `sceneSig` at line 637. Next, `draw()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_draw.js:125-130`) calls `this.scopeSoon()`. When the Image pane is active with the Scope `<details>` open (`scopeShown()` true at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_scope.js:263-267` — Compare stays active across `showPane("image")` after being toggled in Generate › History via `toggleCompare`/`setCompare` at `inpaint_ed_view.js:765-792`), `scopeKey()` (`inpaint_ed_scope.js:277-279`) embeds `${this.compositeVersion}|...`, so `this._scope.key === this.scopeKey()` (`:293`) is false. Because `scopeSoon` intentionally does not reset an active 300 ms `_scopeTimer` (`:284-292`), the timer fires mid-gesture.

Guards checked: at timer expiry (`inpaint_ed_scope.js:298`) and inside `updateScope()` (`:313`), `scopeHeld()` (`:304-306`) checks `!!(this.gestureHeld() || this.pending)`. However, `gestureHeld()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1029-1032`) explicitly excludes `["pan", "split", "guide"]` (and during wheel zoom `this.pointer` is null), so `scopeHeld()` returns false. Consequently, `updateScope()` (`inpaint_ed_scope.js:322-334`) runs `sampleRegionSettled("image", [0, 0, this.width, this.height], s, { display: true })` at up to `1024` px on the long side (~1 MP), and because `compositeVersion` was bumped, sampled filter/match caches (`_fcacheSample` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:843-845` and `_mcacheSample` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_match.js:41,140`) also miss `c.version === this.compositeVersion`, forcing full 1 MP filter evaluation, a CPU scratch `getImageData` readback, and `scopeHistogram` every ~300 ms throughout the gesture (re-queued via `inpaint_ed_scope.js:342` or the next frame's `draw()`).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, the three prior `verified.json` files, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: `inpaint_ed_scope.js` is new in item 65 (`docs/PLAN_0_1_57.md`) and this defect is not recorded in any known list. Severity `nice` is appropriate because it only triggers when both Compare (A/B) and the Image › Scope section are simultaneously active, causes only wasted ~300 ms periodic main-thread work during view/split navigation, and alters no document pixels, exports, or runs.

findings.claim: Two async races exist in `host_vlm.js`: (1) `describeArea` and `autoNameLayer` await `pictureInput` / `pictureInputBox` / `layerVlmInput` before `vlmJob` adds the run to `this._vlmRuns`, and neither checks `_vlmGen` / `_destroyed` afterwards, so a `cancelDescribes` (Cancel, `cancel_run`, or closing the tab) during the input read fails to stop `vlmJob` from launching — and `describeArea({ toPrompt: true })` still overwrites the prompt when it finishes; (2) `renameQuietly` unconditionally calls `editor.renderLayers()`, destroying any open inline `<input>` in `renameLayerInline` (`blur` -> `finish(true)`) and cutting off the user's typing.
findings.scenario:
Race A: Trigger `describe` with `to_prompt: true` while `pictureInput` waits on `sampleRegionSettled` / `relightSettled`, then immediately call `cancel_run` (or press Cancel). `cancelDescribes(ed)` bumps `ed._vlmGen` while `_vlmRuns` is still empty; once `pictureInput` resolves, `describeArea` still runs the multi-second `vlmJob` and writes `editor.setPromptText(text)`.
Race B: Paste a layer (`Paste 1`) with Florence-2 auto-naming enabled, immediately double-click a layer name to rename it inline (`renameLayerInline`), and begin typing. When `autoNameLayer` finishes 2 s later, `renameQuietly` calls `editor.renderLayers()`, wiping `layerList.innerHTML`, firing `blur` on the detached `<input>`, and committing the half-typed string prematurely.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/host_vlm.js:71-75 `cancelDescribes` bumps `editor._vlmGen` / `this._vlmGenAll` and cancels `this._vlmRuns`. In `autoNameLayer` (lines 140-142), `stopped()` is checked before `await this.layerVlmInput(editor, live)` but not before `await this.vlmJob(...)`. In `describeArea` (lines 183-205), `_vlmGen` is never read at all before or after `pictureInput` / `vlmJob` / `editor.setPromptText(text)`. In `renameQuietly` (line 170), `editor.renderLayers()` sets `list.innerHTML = ""` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:659, 1055`), triggering `input.addEventListener("blur", () => finish(true))` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:240`).
findings.fix: Capture `gen = editor._vlmGen || 0` and `genAll = this._vlmGenAll || 0` on entry to `describeArea`, check them (and `editor._destroyed`) after `pictureInput`/`pictureInputBox` and after `vlmJob` (throwing `new Error("cancelled")`), and re-check `stopped()` after `layerVlmInput` in `autoNameLayer`. In `renameQuietly`, if `editor.layerList` or `editor.refList` has an open inline rename `<input>`, update the target row's `.ipc-name` span in place (or skip if that row itself is being edited) instead of calling `editor.renderLayers()`.
findings.why:
Both async races in `renderer/editor/host_vlm.js` hold at commit `f45a86cc`. First, `cancelDescribes(editor)` (`host_vlm.js:71-75`, called by `host.cancelRuns` at `renderer/editor/host_generate.js:334` from the `cancel_run` command at `renderer/commands_runs.js:457`, tab close `removeEditor` at `renderer/editor/host_state.js:236`, and title-row `cancelProviderRuns` at `host_generate.js:319-321`) only increments `editor._vlmGen` / `this._vlmGenAll` and cancels active entries in `this._vlmRuns`. However, a run is only added to `this._vlmRuns` upon entering `vlmJob` (`host_vlm.js:55-57`). In `describeArea` (`host_vlm.js:183-206`), lines 193-195 first await `this.pictureInputBox(...)` (`renderer/editor/host_helpers.js:583-609`, awaiting `sampleRegionSettled` at line 600 or `relightSettled` at line 603) or `this.pictureInput(...)` (`host_helpers.js:314-333`, awaiting `sampleRegionSettled` at line 324 or `relightSettled` at line 327), and `describeArea` never reads `_vlmGen`, `_vlmGenAll`, or `editor._destroyed` at all—neither before `vlmJob` (line 196, even when `describe` in `renderer/commands_depth.js:24-25` pre-creates a `jobId`) nor before `editor.setPromptText(text)` (line 203). Consequently, a `cancel_run` (or tab close whose input read still resolves) during the `pictureInput`/`pictureInputBox` await fails to prevent `vlmJob` from launching Florence-2 inference and, for `toPrompt: true`, still overwrites the prompt when inference completes. Likewise, in `autoNameLayer` (`host_vlm.js:128-158`), `stopped()` (line 135) is checked via `find()` at line 139 before `await this.layerVlmInput(editor, live)` (line 141, which awaits `primeRegion` on tiles at line 100), and is not checked again until line 144 after `await this.vlmJob(...)` (line 142), so a cancel or tab close during `layerVlmInput` still launches an unnecessary Florence-2 decode in the helpers process.

Second, when `autoNameLayer` finishes, `renameQuietly` (`host_vlm.js:161-173`) sets `layer.name = name` (line 162) and unconditionally calls `editor.renderLayers()` (line 170). `renderLayers()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:686-883`) wipes `this.layerList.innerHTML = ""` at line 695 (note: the candidate's evidence cited line 659 instead of 695) and calls `this.renderReferences()` (line 882), which wipes `this.refList.innerHTML = ""` at line 1055. If the user has an inline rename `<input>` open via `renameLayerInline` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:219-245`, or `renameGroupInline` at lines 949-972)—whether on another row or even on the newly landed layer itself, since `layer.name` remains `before` until `finish(true)` runs at line 229, allowing `now.name !== before` at `host_vlm.js:145` to pass—detaching the focused `<input>` triggers its `blur` listener (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:240` / `967`), committing the half-typed text (or clobbering the VLM name back to `before` with an undo step if nothing was typed yet) and moving focus to `this.root` (line 232). Notably, `redrawThumbsOf` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:189-193`) explicitly avoids `renderLayers()` for this exact reason ('a rebuild took an open rename').

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the 2026-11-07/2026-11-12 `verified.json` files: `host_vlm.js` (Florence-2, item 62) is new in this slice and has no prior known entry. Severity `nice` is appropriate because both defects are narrow async timing windows without data or pixel loss: Race A requires cancellation during the pre-job composite/mip read (and `#shell-cancel` in `renderer/shell.js:851` is hidden unless a provider/picture run is also active, making `cancel_run` or tab close the main triggers), and Race B requires actively editing a layer/group name inline at the moment background auto-naming finishes.

findings.claim: Commit `0aebd028` hooks map upload retries (`storeMaps`) into `syncLayersOnce()`, `flushEditor()`, and `saveBeforeRestart()`, but neither `setMap` nor `setMaps` schedules `this.scheduleAutosave()` when a map's initial upload fails, and `storeMaps()` itself does not call `this.notifyChanged()` after populating `map.ref` / `map.guideRef`. Consequently, if no pixel layer is dirtied (e.g. the user only adjusts Relight/filter sliders) or if a manual save fails/cancels after `flushEditor` uploaded the maps, `autosave.json` keeps `ref: null` and loses the maps on an unexpected crash.
findings.scenario:
1. Compute Surface Maps or a Depth Map while the local mirror upload transiently fails (`setMaps` / `setMap` catches the error and leaves `map.ref = null`).
2. Add a Relight or Depth of Field filter layer and adjust lights/sliders without painting on any pixel layer: `scheduleAutosave()` is never called, `syncLayersOnce()` never runs, and `autosave.json` retains `ref: null` (`setValue` skips `!j.ref` at `inpaint_ed_persist.js:364`).
3. Alternatively, press Ctrl+S and cancel during save or hit a disk write error (`documents.write` throws): `flushEditor` already ran `storeMaps()` and set `map.ref`, but because `storeMaps()` did not call `this.notifyChanged()`, `host.saveAll()` never rewrites `autosave.json` with the new `ref`.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:355-357 (`setMaps`) and lines 876-890 (`setMap`) catch `uploadCanvas` failures leaving `map.ref = null` / `map.guideRef = null` and call only `this.notifyChanged()` (lines 382, 917), never `this.scheduleAutosave()`. Lines 402-419 (`storeMaps`) assign `map.ref = ...` and `map.guideRef = ...` (lines 410-411) and return without calling `this.notifyChanged()`. renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:364 drops any map with `!j.ref` on restore.
findings.fix: In `setMap` and `setMaps`, call `if (this.mapsUnstored().length) this.scheduleAutosave();` so the 15 s background pass runs `syncLayersOnce()` even without dirty pixel layers; in `storeMaps()`, track whether any `ref` or `guideRef` was set and call `this.notifyChanged()` before returning or throwing.
findings.why:
Both gaps in the new map-retry plumbing exist as claimed at f45a86cc. First, Scumble separates metadata autosave (`InpaintEditor.notifyChanged` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1347-1351` -> `host.changed` -> 1.5 s `host.saveAll` at `renderer/editor/host_queue.js:503-539`, which synchronously serializes `ed.getValue()` without uploading anything) from the 15 s background upload pass (`scheduleAutosave` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:297-304` -> `syncLayers` -> `syncLayersOnce` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:898-937`). In `setMaps` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:350-384`, lines 354-358) and `setMap` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:869-919`, lines 874-890), failed `uploadCanvas` calls are caught and leave `map.ref = null` / `map.guideRef = null`, ending with `this.notifyChanged()` (lines 382, 917) and never `this.scheduleAutosave()`. Because `scheduleAutosave()` is only invoked from `markLayerChanged` and `markMaskChanged` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:13`) — never from `addFilterLayer` or `markFilterChanged` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:313-352, 627-640`) — a workflow that computes Depth or Surface Maps and then only adjusts Relight lights, Depth of Field / Haze sliders, or prompts never triggers `syncLayersOnce()`. Every 1.5 s `saveAll()` writes `mapToJSON(m)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:349-364`) with `ref: null` (or `guide: null`) into `autosave.json`, and on crash recovery `setValue` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:364`) skips `!j.ref` (or `mapFromJSON` at `inpaint_maps.js:394` drops the missing guide). Note also that if `syncLayersOnce()` does run once and `storeMaps({ quiet: true })` still returns failed kinds, nothing reschedules `scheduleAutosave()` either.

Second, `storeMaps` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:402-419`) mutates `map.ref` and `map.guideRef` in place (lines 410-411) and returns (or throws on a later map in the loop at line 415) without calling `this.notifyChanged()`. In `host.flushEditor` (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:29-52`), `ed.syncLayers()` (which calls `this.notifyChanged()` at `inpaint_canvas.js:936`) runs at line 36 only when a pixel layer or mask is dirty; otherwise line 41 calls `await ed.storeMaps()` directly. If `saveDocument` (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:197-265`) is then cancelled via `cancelDocumentJob` (`ed._docCancel` at lines 239, 243), fails in `documents.write` (line 246), throws part-way through `storeMaps` after uploading an earlier surface map, or runs with `copy: true` (line 251 skips `this.saveAll()` for Save a Copy), `map.ref` is populated in memory so `mapsUnstored()` is now empty, yet `notifyChanged()` / `saveAll()` never runs to rewrite `autosave.json`.

Checked guards and known-issue lists: clean shutdowns and restarts are protected because `saveBeforeRestart` (`renderer/shell.js:1023-1028, 1042`) explicitly runs `ed.storeMaps({ quiet: true })` and writes `host.bundle()`, and normal `.scumble` saves run `flushEditor` then `saveAll()`. `docs/BUGS.md:18-21` records the 2026-11-16 lane C fix (`storeMaps`), while `docs/BUGS.md` `## Open`, the three `verified.json` files, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` do not record this remaining gap in that fix, making it `confirmed` rather than `known`. Severity is `nice` because hitting actual loss requires a compound sequence: a transient local-mirror upload failure during map creation (past `writeAtomic`'s 2 s `renameRetry` in `electron/main/files.js:89-111`, or a transient server failure in the ComfyUI node), followed by no pixel-layer edits (or an aborted / copy-only save without further edits), followed by an unclean renderer/app crash before close.

findings.claim: When Settings > Network > Use curl for API calls is switched off (or no curl binary is found on Linux), curlfetch.js delegates globalThis.fetch directly to Node's built-in undici fetch. As curlfetch.js:37-39 itself notes, native fetch drops only Authorization across cross-origin 3xx redirects and forwards custom API-key headers (x-key, x-magnific-api-key, x-goog-api-key, x-api-key, X-API-Key) verbatim to any cross-origin Location. Eight main-process call sites send these custom key headers without redirect: "error" or redirect: "manual", so any cross-origin 3xx redirect leaks the raw provider key.
findings.scenario: The user unticks 'Use curl for API calls' in Settings > Network (or runs on a minimal Linux install without curl) and runs an edit, prompt upsample, or assistant turn on BFL, Magnific, Google Gemini, Anthropic, Comfy Partner API, Comfy Router (Krea 3 asset upload), or Comfy Cloud (legacy API). If an upstream proxy, CDN, or endpoint responds with a 301/302/307/308 redirect to another origin, undici automatically follows the redirect and sends x-key / x-magnific-api-key / x-goog-api-key / x-api-key / X-API-Key to the foreign host.
findings.evidence: electron/main/curlfetch.js:37-39: `// headers that may carry a key: dropped when a redirect leaves the origin (fetch drops Authorization alone; the providers' own key headers would go along with it there, so they are dropped here too)` `const KEY_HEADERS = new Set(["authorization", ..., "x-api-key", "x-key", "api-key", "x-goog-api-key", "x-comfy-api-key", ..., "x-magnific-api-key"]);`. Yet at :324,343: `if (!state.enabled() || ...) return "node";` and `return route(urlOf(input)) === "curl" ? curlFetch(input, init) : native(input, init);`. Unguarded custom-header callers: `bfl.js:120,137` (`"x-key": ctx.key`), `magnific.js:560,582` (`"x-magnific-api-key": ctx.key`), `gemini.js:96` (`"x-goog-api-key": ctx.key`), `comfycloud.js:310,746,854,865` (`"X-API-Key": ctx.key`, whereas `:336` `keyedGet` only wraps `/api/object_info` and `/api/assets`), `comfyrouter.js:349` (`"X-API-Key": ctx.key`), `comfypartner.js:96-98` (`"X-API-Key": ctx.key`), `llm.js:235,261` (`"x-goog-api-key"`, `"x-api-key"`), and `assistant/http.js:120` (`postStream` with Anthropic `x-api-key` from `assistant/anthropic.js:206` and Gemini `x-goog-api-key` from `assistant/gemini.js:228`).
findings.fix: In curlfetch.js install(), wrap the `native` branch as well whenever request headers contain any entry in KEY_HEADERS (other than authorization/cookie/proxy-authorization) and redirect is "follow": perform hop-by-hop redirects with `redirect: "manual"` and strip KEY_HEADERS on `next.origin !== u.origin`, matching curlFetch (:279-294); also set `redirect: "error"` on POST/PUT API calls that carry keys.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc. In `electron/main/curlfetch.js:37-39`, `KEY_HEADERS` lists custom API-key headers (`x-api-key`, `x-key`, `api-key`, `x-goog-api-key`, `x-comfy-api-key`, `x-auth-token`, `x-token`, `x-magnific-api-key`) alongside `authorization`, `cookie`, and `proxy-authorization`, with the explicit comment that native `fetch` drops `Authorization` alone across cross-origin redirects so `curlFetch` drops the provider key headers too (`curlfetch.js:290`: `if (next.origin !== u.origin) headers = headers.filter(([k]) => !KEY_HEADERS.has(k.toLowerCase()));`). However, `install()` (`curlfetch.js:336-345`, wired at `electron/main/main.js:44-47`) patches `globalThis.fetch` at line 343 with `return route(urlOf(input)) === "curl" ? curlFetch(input, init) : native(input, init);`. Whenever `route()` (`curlfetch.js:322-330`) returns `"node"` — either because the user unticked *Send requests through curl* (`#set-net-curl` in `renderer/index.html:181`, setting `network.curl: false`) or because `probe()` (`curlfetch.js:73-84`) found no `curl` binary on a minimal Linux install — requests bypass `curlFetch` and go directly to Node's built-in undici `fetch`, which follows 3xx redirects by default (`redirect: "follow"`) and strips only `authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `cookie`, and `host` when the `Location` origin changes.

Tracing all eight cited main-process call-site groups confirms there is no `redirect: "error"` or `redirect: "manual"` guard on any of them (`providers/index.js:601-604` `contextFor` only merges `signal` into `init`): (1) `electron/main/providers/bfl.js:117,120` (submit) and `:137` (poll to `pollUrlOf` on `*.bfl.ai`) send `"x-key": ctx.key`; (2) `electron/main/providers/magnific.js:554-557` (`submit` -> `send` at `:539,545`; the finding cites `:560`, which is the `catch` line) and `:582` (`poll` -> `send`) send `"x-magnific-api-key": ctx.key`; (3) `electron/main/providers/gemini.js:95-97` sends `"x-goog-api-key": ctx.key`; (4) `electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:310,746,854,865` send `"X-API-Key": ctx.key` on the non-default `legacy` Comfy Cloud path (`settings.comfycloud.api === "legacy"`), whereas `keyedGet` in the same file (`comfycloud.js:333-347`) explicitly notes that `fetch` carries `X-API-Key` across cross-origin redirects and guards only `/api/object_info` (`:353`) and `/api/assets` (`:568`) with `redirect: "manual"` (the default `v2` path in `comfysdk.js:119-126` uses `Authorization: Bearer` and sets `redirect = "error"` on non-GET/HEAD); (5) `electron/main/providers/comfyrouter.js:349` (`kreaAsset`) sends `"X-API-Key": ctx.key`; (6) `electron/main/providers/comfypartner.js:96-98` (`post`) sends `"X-API-Key": ctx.key`; (7) `electron/main/llm.js:235` (`askGemini`) and `:261` (`askAnthropic`) send `"x-goog-api-key"` and `"x-api-key"`; and (8) `electron/main/assistant/http.js:120` (`postStream`) sends `"x-api-key": chat.key` from `assistant/anthropic.js:171-177` (cited as `:206` in the raw finding) and `"x-goog-api-key": chat.key` from `assistant/gemini.js:223-228`.

Checked against all known-issue lists (`known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`): this is a distinct defect, not `known`. Finding `S2` Part 2 (`review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json:36-45`) and its repeat `main-net/comfy-custom-auth-header-cross-origin` (`review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:886-900`) strictly concern `electron/main/comfy.js` (`ComfyClient.fetch`/`proxy`/`probe`) forwarding a user-named `settings.comfy.auth.type === "header"` token (such as `X-Pod-Token`, which is not even in `KEY_HEADERS`) when talking to the user's ComfyUI server. By contrast, `curlfetch.js` was introduced later in 0.1.55 (2026-11-11/12) specifically to strip `KEY_HEADERS` for cloud providers on the `curl` path while leaving its `route() === "node"` fallback unprotected across the eight cloud provider, upsampler, and assistant adapters.

Severity is calibrated down from `must` to `nice` (matching the `low`/`nice` calibration of `S2` and `main-net/comfy-custom-auth-header-cross-origin`). First, on the default `network.curl: true` path (`settings.js:39`), `curlFetch` is active on Windows, macOS, and standard Linux installs and already strips every header in `KEY_HEADERS` on cross-origin redirects. Second, all eight non-loopback call sites connect over `https://` to hardcoded official provider hosts (`api.bfl.ai`, `api.freepik.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `api.anthropic.com`, `cloud.comfy.org`, `api.comfy.org`); untrusted files, prompts, or MCP callers cannot control those URLs, an external network party cannot inject a 3xx over TLS, and none of these JSON/upload API endpoints redirects cross-origin in normal operation. Exposure requires both disabling curl (or lacking a `curl` binary on Linux) and an official provider or its CDN unexpectedly issuing a cross-origin 3xx redirect on an authenticated API route, making this a defense-in-depth parity gap rather than an exploitable vulnerability.

findings.claim: On Comfy Cloud's legacy API path (`settings.comfycloud.api === "legacy"`), `download()` handles a 3xx redirect from `/api/view` by passing the raw `Location` header string directly to `ctx.fetch(loc)`. Unlike `keyedGet` in the same file, it neither resolves a relative `Location` against the request URL nor checks that the redirect target uses `https:` and is not a loopback/private address.
findings.scenario: With `"comfycloud": { "api": "legacy" }` in `settings.json`, a finished Comfy Cloud job downloads its output via `/api/view`. If `/api/view` returns a relative redirect (for example `/api/assets/...`), `ctx.fetch(loc)` throws `TypeError: Failed to parse URL` and loses the paid job's output; if it returns an `http://` or loopback `Location`, `ctx.fetch` fetches it.
findings.evidence: electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:732-737: `const r = await ctx.fetch(`${BASE}/api/view?${q}`, { headers: { "X-API-Key": ctx.key }, redirect: "manual" }); if (r.status >= 300 && r.status < 400) { const loc = r.headers.get("location"); if (!loc) throw new Error("Comfy Cloud view: redirect without location"); const s = await ctx.fetch(loc);` — compare `:342` `const next = new URL(loc, target);` and `magnific.js:610` `const ok = /^https:\/\//i.test(s) ...`.
findings.fix: Resolve `const next = new URL(loc, `${BASE}/api/view`);`, require `next.protocol === "https:"` and `!isLoopback(next.href)`, and fetch `next.href` with `downloadImage` retries.
findings.why:
At `f45a86cc`, `download(ctx, file)` in `electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:730-742` fetches `${BASE}/api/view?${q}` with `redirect: "manual"` (`:732`), reads `const loc = r.headers.get("location")` on any `3xx` response (`:733-735`), and passes `loc` straight into `const s = await ctx.fetch(loc)` (`:736`) without resolving it against the request URL or validating its scheme or host. By contrast, `keyedGet` in the same file (`comfycloud.js:342-343`) resolves `const next = new URL(loc, target)` before following a redirect, and peer adapters such as `magnific.js:610-611` and `comfypartner.js:108-109` require `https://` before fetching provider-returned storage URLs.

Tracing the full call path confirms the code is still reachable and unguarded: `providers/index.js:594` sets `ctx.cloudApi = ((settings.get().comfycloud || {}).api === "legacy") ? "legacy" : "v2"`, `comfycloud.js:789-803,819-821` dispatches `edit`/`relight`/`generate`/`upscale` to `run()` whenever `ctx.cloudApi !== "v2"`, and `run()` calls `download(ctx, file)` at `comfycloud.js:888` after the job completes. `ctx.fetch` (`providers/index.js:601-604`) delegates to `globalThis.fetch` (`electron/main/curlfetch.js:342-344`). If `/api/view` returns a valid RFC 9110 relative `Location` header (for example `/api/...` or a path-relative signed URL), both `curlFetch` (`curlfetch.js:266`, `new Request(...)`) and Node's native undici `fetch` in Electron's main process have no base URL and throw `TypeError: Failed to parse URL`, losing the finished job's image (and legacy `run()` does not write a `cloudjobs.json` recovery note). Conversely, if `loc` uses `http://` or points to a loopback address (`http://127.0.0.1:...` / `localhost`), `curlfetch.js:277` allows `http:` and `curlfetch.js:324` (`isLoopback`) routes loopback URLs directly to Node's native `fetch`, which performs the GET unchallenged.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/PLAN_COMFY_SDK.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`); `PLAN_COMFY_SDK.md:455` added `keyedGet` for `/api/object_info` while leaving legacy `download()` untouched, and no open bug or prior finding covers `comfycloud.js` `download()`. Severity `nice` holds strictly: v2 (`runV2` -> `out.toBytes()`) is the default path for all users unless `"comfycloud": { "api": "legacy" }` is hand-edited into `settings.json`, `BASE` is hardcoded to `https://cloud.comfy.org` (`comfycloud.js:47`), and `ctx.fetch(loc)` sends no API key (`:736`), making this a narrow edge-case / defense-in-depth defect on a deprecated fallback path.

findings.claim: Dropping `.psd`, `.ora`, or OS-untyped `.tif`/`.tiff` files onto the Layers list (`ed.layerList`) or References list (`ed.refList`) silently does nothing because both drop handlers pre-filter `dataTransfer.files` with `f.type.startsWith('image/')` and stop propagation before calling `ed.addImageLayers`, even though `addImageLayers` and the canvas drop handler explicitly accept `LAYERED_EXT` and `TIFF_EXT`.
findings.scenario: On Windows (where Explorer gives `.psd` and `.ora` `file.type === ''` or `application/octet-stream`), drag a `.psd` or `.ora` file onto the Layers panel list or References panel list—whose header button tooltips promise 'Dropping files on this list does the same'. The green drop highlight appears on dragover, and on drop nothing happens and no status message is shown (the top-bar Load and panel file pickers also hide `.psd` and `.ora` because their `accept` attributes omit `.psd,.ora`).
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js:453-458 (`ed.layerList` drop) and lines 481-486 (`ed.refList` drop) call `e.stopPropagation()` and filter `Array.from((e.dataTransfer && e.dataTransfer.files) || []).filter((f) => f.type.startsWith('image/'))` before calling `ed.addImageLayers(...)`. By contrast, `viewEl` drop (renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:459) and `addImageLayers` itself (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:25) check `((f.type && f.type.startsWith('image/')) || LAYERED_EXT.test(f.name || '') || TIFF_EXT.test(f.name || ''))`. Also `ed.fileInput.accept` (inpaint_modal.js:92) and `fileInput` in `buildLayers` (line 427) set `'image/*,.tif,.tiff'` without `.psd,.ora`, and `nodeRoot` drop (inpaint_ed_chrome.js:37) checks `TIFF_EXT` without `LAYERED_EXT`.
findings.fix: Pass `e.dataTransfer && e.dataTransfer.files` directly to `ed.addImageLayers(...)` in `inpaint_modal.js:456-457` and `484-485` (letting `addImageLayers` run its own `image/ || LAYERED_EXT || TIFF_EXT` filter), add `LAYERED_EXT` in `inpaint_ed_chrome.js:37`, and include `.psd,.ora` in `accept` at `inpaint_modal.js:92, 427`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js: both the Layers panel drop handler on ed.layerList (lines 453-458, specifically line 456) and the References panel drop handler on ed.refList (lines 481-486, specifically line 484) call e.preventDefault() and e.stopPropagation() and pre-filter dropped files with Array.from((e.dataTransfer && e.dataTransfer.files) || []).filter((f) => f.type.startsWith("image/")) before calling ed.addImageLayers(...), even though their dragover handlers (lines 451 and 479) unconditionally add the ipc-dropping highlight and their header button tooltips (lines 436 and 474) state that dropping files on the list behaves like importing layers / Shift+dropping on the canvas.

Tracing the full drop path confirms no other handler rescues or intercepts these files: the window-level capture drop listeners in renderer/shell.js only claim video files (lines 1137-1152, isVideoFile) and .scumble archives (lines 1191-1203, /\.scumble$/i), so .psd, .ora, and OS-untyped .tif/.tiff drops reach ed.layerList or ed.refList and are swallowed by e.stopPropagation(). Meanwhile, ed.addImageLayers itself (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:25) already filters with ((f.type && f.type.startsWith("image/")) || LAYERED_EXT.test(f.name || "") || TIFF_EXT.test(f.name || "")) and explicitly implements PSD/ORA import for both "none" and "reference" roles (lines 39-61) as well as TIFF decoding (lines 70-75), matching the main canvas viewport drop handler on this.viewEl (renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:459). On Windows and Linux setups where Chromium/OS MIME sniffs leave File.type empty (or non-image/*, e.g. application/octet-stream) for .ora, .psd, or untyped .tif/.tiff, files.length is 0 and the panel drop silently does nothing with no status feedback. Relatedly, the hidden <input type="file"> elements in inpaint_modal.js:92 and :427 (and prompt_field.js:1517) set accept = "image/*,.tif,.tiff" without .psd,.ora, and inpaint_ed_chrome.js:37 checks TIFF_EXT without LAYERED_EXT (as does prompt_field.js:1811).

Checked scratch/known_index.md, docs/BUGS.md, docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, and all three verified.json review archives (2026-11-07 full, 2026-11-07 external, 2026-11-12 full); this inconsistency is not previously recorded. Severity is calibrated as 'nice' because there is no data or pixel loss and dropping onto the main canvas viewport (or File > Open for base documents) works as expected, making this a minor UI consistency papercut on secondary panel drop zones.

findings.claim: syncLayersOnce awaits `uploadPixels(layer.maskPx, ...)` and then assigns `layer.maskRef = ref` without checking that `layer.maskPx` is still that mask (or still present). If the user removes, applies, or merges away the mask while its 15 s autosave upload is in flight, `layer.maskRef` is written back onto the maskless layer, serialized by `getValue()`, and revived as a live mask when the document is reopened.
findings.scenario: Paint on a layer mask of a 15,000 x 10,000 layer, wait 15 s for `scheduleAutosave` -> `syncLayers` to start encoding/uploading `layer.maskPx`, and click Remove mask (or Apply mask, or Merge down into that layer) before the upload finishes. `markMaskChanged` / `mergeInto` sets `layer.maskPx = null` and `layer.maskRef = null`. When `uploadPixels` resolves, line 924 sets `layer.maskRef = ref` on the maskless layer. Saving and reopening the `.scumble` (or restarting from autosave, or duplicating the layer) brings the deleted mask back.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:919-931 (`syncLayersOnce`): `const { ref } = await uploadPixels(layer.maskPx, ...); layer.maskRef = ref;` at line 924 with no check on `layer.maskPx`. `markMaskChanged` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:16-17) clears `if (!layer.maskPx) layer.maskRef = null`, and `mergeInto` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:494) sets `below.maskPx = null; ... below.maskRef = null`. `getValue` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:50) writes `mask: l.maskRef || null` regardless of `l.maskPx`, and `setValue` (lines 210-212, 262-265, 270) decodes `l.mask` back into `maskPx`.
findings.fix: Capture `const mpx = layer.maskPx;` before `await uploadPixels(mpx, ...)` in `syncLayersOnce` (`inpaint_canvas.js:922-924`) and assign `if (layer.maskPx === mpx) layer.maskRef = ref;`; also emit `mask: l.maskPx ? (l.maskRef || null) : null` in `getValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:50`).
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc. In `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:919-931` (`syncLayersOnce`), when `layer.maskDirty && layer.maskPx` is true, the code sets `layer.maskDirty = false` (line 920) and `layer._maskUploading = true` (line 921), awaits `uploadPixels(layer.maskPx, ...)` (line 923), and unconditionally writes `layer.maskRef = ref` on line 924 before deleting `layer._maskUploading` on line 929. On a large (e.g. 15,000 x 10,000) mask, worker PNG encoding plus upload in `uploadPixels` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_upload.js:48-57`) takes roughly 1-3 seconds, triggered either by the 15 s `scheduleAutosave()` timer (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:297-304`) or by `flushEditor` (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:34-36`).

No guard blocks mask removal, baking, or merging while `layer._maskUploading` is set: `maskBlocked` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:196-200`) checks only `this.pending && this.pending.layer === layer`. If during the `uploadPixels` await the user runs `removeMask` (`inpaint_ed_masks.js:550-561`, calling `markMaskChanged` at lines 15-19), `applyMask` (`inpaint_ed_masks.js:514-532`), `mergeInto` into `below` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:439-500`, line 494), or undoes mask creation via `applySnapshot` (`snap.kind === "mask"`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:861-867`), the live `layer` object sets `maskPx = null`, `maskRef = null`, and `maskDirty = false`. When `uploadPixels` subsequently resolves, line 924 overwrites `layer.maskRef = ref` onto that same maskless `layer` object. Because `layer.maskDirty` is `false` and `layer.maskPx` is `null`, no later `syncLayersOnce` pass clears or updates `layer.maskRef`.

On serialization, `getValue()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:50`) emits `mask: l.maskRef || null` without checking `l.maskPx` (unlike line 51's `l.maskOff && l.maskPx`), and main's `Documents.write` packs the just-uploaded mask PNG into `.scumble` because it exists in the local mirror. When the document is reopened or restored from autosave, `setValue()` (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:210-213, 230` for filter layers; `262-265, 270` for pixel/text layers) decodes `l.mask` back into a live `maskPx` — reviving a removed mask, applying a baked mask a second time over `applyMask`'s alpha, or stretching `below`'s old mask across `mergeInto`'s merged union bounds. (Minor precision note on the scenario text: `duplicateLayer` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:307-318` copies the stale `maskRef` onto `copy` once `_maskUploading` has cleared while leaving `copy.maskPx` null, so duplicating propagates the latent revival to the copy on save/reopen rather than showing it immediately in the live session.)

Checked against `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: `canvas-core/sync-clean-before-upload-lands` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` covered copies/snapshots taken while `_uploading`/`_maskUploading` was in flight and was fixed in 0.1.57 via those flags, leaving this post-await stale write onto a cleared `maskPx` unaddressed. Severity `nice` holds: hitting the bug requires removing, applying, or merging away a mask during the brief async upload window, and `layer.px` itself is preserved intact in `l.ref` (removing the revived non-destructive mask restores the intended layer).

findings.claim: `onKey` does not check `this.gestureHeld()` before layer-mutating shortcuts such as `Delete`/`Backspace` (line 310) or `Ctrl+E`/`Ctrl+G`/`Ctrl+J` (lines 210-212). Pressing `Delete` while holding a paint stroke removes the active layer (whose `'Delete layer'` undo snapshot retains `l.px` by reference), and releasing the pointer then runs `commitLayerPaint` onto the detached layer — pushing a dead `layerrect` step for a missing layer ID and mutating the pixels stored inside the `'Delete layer'` undo snapshot.
findings.scenario: Select a paint layer, press and hold the left mouse button to paint a stroke across it (`this.pointer.kind === "layerpaint"`), press `Delete` before releasing the mouse button (`removeLayer` deletes the layer and pushes `'Delete layer'`), then release the mouse button. Undo History now has `'Paint'` on top of `'Delete layer'`; pressing `Ctrl+Z` once does nothing (layer ID not in `this.layers`), and pressing `Ctrl+Z` a second time restores the deleted layer with the unfinished stroke baked into its pixels.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:289-311`: `if (e.key === "Delete" || e.key === "Backspace") { ... if (this.activeLayerId) { this.removeLayer(this.activeLayerId); return; } }` has no `this.gestureHeld()` guard (unlike `undoStep` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1050`). `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:169-177` (`layers` snapshot) keeps `l.px` by reference. On pointer release, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:1115` calls `commitLayerPaint(p)` -> `commitStroke(p)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:434-458`), which pushes `layerrect` for `p.layer.id` and writes the stroke into `p.layer.px` without checking `this.layers.includes(p.layer)`.
findings.fix: Refuse destructive/layer-structure shortcuts in `onKey` while `this.gestureHeld()` is true (with the same status message `historyStepNow` uses), and guard `commitLayerPaint` / `smudge` / `maskpaint` release on `this.layers.includes(p.layer)`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc. When a brush/erase/clone/gradient stroke is held down (`pointerDownNow` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:598-600` sets `this.pointer = { kind: "layerpaint", layer, stroke, ... }`), dabs accumulate in `p.stroke` (`StrokeBuffer`) while `layer.px` still holds the pre-stroke pixels. Pressing `Delete` or `Backspace` before releasing the pointer reaches the window capture listener `_docKey` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:278-346`), which only blocks shortcuts when `this.pointer && this.pointer.healing` (`340-344`) and otherwise dispatches to `this.onKey(e)` (`345`). Inside `onKey` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:91-330`), neither `case "delete": case "backspace":` (`289-311`, calling `this.removeLayer(l.id)` at line `310` and `this.removeLayers(...)` at line `309` when `this.getBounds()` is null) nor `Ctrl+E` (`mergeDown` at line `212`) checks `this.gestureHeld()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1029-1032`).

`removeLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:567-584`) pushes `{ kind: "layers", label: "Delete layer" }` (`572`) and removes the layer from `this.layers` (`573`) without clearing or cancelling `this.pointer` (likewise synchronous `mergeDownNow` -> `mergeInto` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:399-400,497`; only the async merge-into-base branch checks `this.gestureHeld()` at line `375`). Because `snapshot` for `kind === "layers"` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:410-415`) calls `snapshotLayer` (`176-216`), which shallow-copies `{ ...l }` and retains `l.px` by reference under the assumption that layer-list operations replace rather than mutate `px`, the `'Delete layer'` undo record shares the exact `TileLayerPixels`/`CanvasLayerPixels` object `p.layer.px`. When the user then releases the pointer, `onPointerUp` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:1110-1115`) calls `commitLayerPaint(p)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_tips.js:499-508`) -> `commitStroke(p)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:433-466`), which only guards `if (!target) return;` (`435`), pushes a `layerrect` undo step for the detached `p.layer.id` (`442`), and writes the stroke into `p.layer.px` (`448` on tiles via `commitStrokeTiles`, `453-457` on canvas via `target.drawInto`). Pressing `Ctrl+Z` once pops that `layerrect` step (`inpaint_ed_history.js:1088`), `snapshotOf` returns `null` (`367-368`, pushing nothing to `this.redo`), `applySnapshot` returns early because `snap.id` is not in `this.layers` (`804-805`), and `releaseSnapshot` frees the pre-stroke pixel copy (`1109`). Pressing `Ctrl+Z` a second time restores `'Delete layer'` (`632`) with the unfinished stroke permanently baked into `l.px` (and if `l` was previously clean with a stored `ref`, `snap.layers`'s pre-commit copy still has `dirty: false` while `markLayerChanged` marked only the detached `p.layer.dirty = true`, leaving `l.px` and `l.ref` out of sync).

Checked against `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three prior `verified.json` files (`2026-11-12`, `2026-11-07` full, `2026-11-07` external): `second-pointer-replaces-stroke` and `undoStep`'s `gestureHeld()` guard are distinct, and no entry covers keyboard layer mutations during a held pointer gesture. Severity `nice` is well-calibrated because triggering it requires pressing `Delete`/`Backspace` or `Ctrl+E` while physically holding a mouse/pen stroke down.

findings.claim: `layerStroke` and `onPointerMove` expand `strokeBounds` and `strokeDirty` by `this.brushSize / 2 + 2`, whereas a rotated square/rectangular custom or ABR brush tip (`this.tipRotate`) reaches up to `Math.SQRT2 * (this.brushSize / 2)` from the stroke centre (and on an anisotropically scaled layer `full = brushSize * (sx + sy) / 4` also exceeds `(brushSize / 2) * min(sx, sy)`). At pointer release, `strokeBands` and `commitStrokeTiles` clip the written stroke to `strokeRect(p, target)`, slicing the outer corners of rotated stamps flat.
findings.scenario: Import or pick a square/chisel custom brush tip, set Brush Size to 120 px and Tip Angle (`tipRotate`) to 45°, and click once on a paint layer. While the button is held the live preview shows all four corners (`R = rMax * 1.5 + 2`), then on mouse release all four corners are clipped ~23 px inward along an axis-aligned 124 × 124 box.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:104-105`: `strokeBounds: [ix - this.brushSize / 2 - 2, iy - this.brushSize / 2 - 2, ix + this.brushSize / 2 + 2, iy + this.brushSize / 2 + 2], strokeDirty: [ix - this.brushSize / 2 - 2, iy - this.brushSize / 2 - 2, ix + this.brushSize / 2 + 2, iy + this.brushSize / 2 + 2],` and `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:906`: `const r = this.brushSize / 2 + 2;`. By contrast, line `114` of `inpaint_ed_strokes.js` pads the stroke buffer by `const R = rMax * 1.5 + 2;` because `layerStamp` (`248`) rotates rectangular tips by `(this.tipRotate || 0) * Math.PI / 180`. On release, `strokeBands` (`404-406`) and `commitStrokeTiles` (`482-484`) clip to `this.strokeRect(p, target)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:103-110`).
findings.fix: Compute the image-space reach of a stamp using the same conservative factor (`this.brushSize * Math.SQRT1_2 + 2`, and accounting for anisotropic `sx`/`sy` when `layer.w / target.width !== layer.h / target.height`) in both `layerStroke` and `onPointerMove`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:104-105` (with minor corrections to the candidate's paraphrased code quotes). Both `pointerDownNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:588,600` -> `layerDab` at `inpaint_ed_strokes.js:80-82`) and `onPointerMove` (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:807-810`, which calls `this.layerStroke` directly rather than having a separate `strokeBounds` at line 906) funnel `layerpaint` and `maskpaint` brush segments into `layerStroke` (`inpaint_ed_strokes.js:94-171`). At lines `104-105`, `layerStroke` records image-space bounds via `this.strokeBounds(p, ix, iy, x, y, this.brushSize / 2 + 2)` and `this.strokeDirty(p, ix, iy, x, y, this.brushSize / 2 + 2)`. Immediately below at lines `113-114` and `125`, `layerStroke` explicitly pads the `StrokeBuffer` draw box by `const R = rMax * 1.5 + 2` (`// the buffer holds the path plus the dab (a tip may be wider than round, and turned)`), so the full stamp lands inside `p.stroke` (`sb.px` on tiles or `sb.canvas` on the canvas backend).

Two reachable paths make the stamp in `p.stroke` exceed `strokeRect(p, target)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:103-110`), which maps `p.bounds` into target layer/mask pixels by `[(x0 - layer.x) * sx, (y0 - layer.y) * sy, ...]`: (1) `this.tipRotate` is the boolean 'Follow stroke' checkbox (`renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js:185-191`), not a numeric degree input, and `layerStroke` (`inpaint_ed_strokes.js:121-124`) sets `this._tipAngle = Math.atan2(dy, dx)` whenever a move exceeds `0.5` layer px while keeping the last `_tipAngle` on stationary clicks. Both `stampDab` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_tips.js:203-219`, for `flow === 1`) and `flowStamps` (`inpaint_ed_strokes.js:240,248`, for `flow < 1`) rotate the `tipStamp` canvas (scaled so its long side is `2 * radius`, `inpaint_ed_tips.js:179-195`) by `this._tipAngle`. For a square custom or `.abr` tip at `brushSize = 120` (`sx = sy = 1`) after or at the ends/turns of a 45° stroke (`_tipAngle = Math.PI / 4`), the rotated corners reach `60 * Math.SQRT2 ≈ 84.85` px along X and Y from the dab centre, ~23 px past `brushSize / 2 + 2 = 62`. (2) Even with the built-in round brush and `tipRotate === false`, on an anisotropically scaled layer (`sx !== sy`, e.g. a `1000 × 1000` layer stretched to `layer.w = 2000, layer.h = 1000` so `sx = 0.5, sy = 1`), `full = this.brushSize * (sx + sy) / 4 = 0.375 * brushSize` (`inpaint_ed_strokes.js:99`) draws a round dab of radius `75` target px at `brushSize = 200`, whereas `strokeRect` scales the `102` image-px pad by `sx = 0.5` to `51` target px in X (`cloneStroke` at `inpaint_ed_tips.js:448-450` has the same anisotropic mismatch, unlike `smudgeDab` at `inpaint_ed_tips.js:268`, which divides by `Math.min(sx, sy)`).

On the first frame of a press (`layerRegionView`, `inpaint_ed_strokes.js:644-648`), `full === true` redraws `strokeView` unclipped (`box = null` in `refreshStrokeView`, `659-684` -> `sb.drawOver`), showing all four corners while held (whereas incremental `pointermove` frames clip `strokeView` updates to `dirtyView`). On `onPointerUp` (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:1115,1135-1137` -> `commitLayerPaint` at `inpaint_ed_tips.js:500-504`), `commitStroke` (`inpaint_ed_strokes.js:442,448-458`) clamps both the tile-backend coverage mask (`commitStrokeTiles`, `482-508`) and the canvas-backend bands (`strokeBands`, `404-412`), as well as `strokeUndo` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:118-120`) and `markLayerChanged`/`markMaskChanged`, to `strokeRect(p, target)`, slicing the protruding stamp corners or sides flat.

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: this defect is not previously recorded. Severity `nice` is appropriate because hitting it requires either an imported non-round tip with 'Follow stroke' at diagonal endpoints/clicks or painting onto a non-uniformly scaled layer, and the clipped edge is immediately visible on release with no silent document corruption.

findings.claim: `this.lastStrokeEnd` (used for `Shift+click` straight-line strokes on layers and masks) and `this.cloneSource` / `this.cloneOffset` (used by Clone and Heal) store raw image coordinates, and neither `followGeometry` (`cropCanvasNow`, `resizeImageNow`, `extendCanvasNow`, `turnDocumentNow`, `straightenDocumentNow`) nor per-layer transforms update or clear `lastStrokeEnd`, while `cropCanvasNow`, `resizeImageNow`, and `extendCanvasNow` also leave `cloneSource` and `cloneOffset` untransformed.
findings.scenario: 1. Paint a dab at `(200, 200)` on a paint layer, crop 150 px off the left and top (`cropCanvasNow`), then `Shift+click` at `(200, 200)`: instead of drawing from `(50, 50)` (where the previous dab moved), the line shoots from `(200, 200)` (150 px down-right of the previous dab). 2. Or `Alt+click` a clone source on a feature at `(400, 400)`, extend the canvas by 256 px on the left, and paint with Clone: it samples `(400, 400)` in the extended coordinates (256 px left of the feature).
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_tips.js:507`: `if (!p.grad && !p.patch && !p.move) this.lastStrokeEnd = { layerId: p.layer.id, x: p.last[0], y: p.last[1], mask: false };` and `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:1139` (`mask: true`), consumed at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:581-582,588,600`. `cloneSource` / `cloneOffset` are set at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:505-506,520`. `turnDocumentNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:731`) and `straightenDocumentNow` (`1086`) only do `this.cloneSource = null;` (leaving `cloneOffset` and `lastStrokeEnd`), while `followGeometry` (`1251-1259`), `cropCanvasNow` (`1405`), `resizeImageNow` (`1491`), and `extendCanvasNow` (`1674`) touch neither `lastStrokeEnd` nor `cloneSource`/`cloneOffset`.
findings.fix: In `followGeometry(kind, A, oldSize, newSize)`, transform `this.lastStrokeEnd` and `this.cloneSource` through `xfApply(A, x, y)` (clearing `cloneSource` if outside `[0, newSize.width] × [0, newSize.height]` and clearing `cloneOffset` on `turn`/`straighten`/`resize`); also clear or transform `lastStrokeEnd` when its layer is moved/transformed.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc. `commitLayerPaint` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_tips.js:507` records `this.lastStrokeEnd = { layerId: p.layer.id, x: p.last[0], y: p.last[1], mask: false }`, and `onPointerUp` for `maskpaint` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_pointer.js:1139` records `{ layerId: p.layer.id, x: p.last[0], y: p.last[1], mask: true }`, where `p.last` is in raw document image coordinates. When the user `Shift+click`s with `paint` or `erase` (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:581-582, 588, 600`), `[prev.x, prev.y]` is passed directly to `layerDab` -> `layerStroke` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_strokes.js:80-82, 101`), which converts image coordinates to layer pixel coordinates via `lx = (x0 - layer.x) * sx, ly = (y0 - layer.y) * sy`. Likewise, Clone/Heal stores raw image coordinates in `this.cloneSource = { x: ix, y: iy }` and image-space displacement in `this.cloneOffset = { x: this.cloneSource.x - ix, y: this.cloneSource.y - iy }` (`inpaint_ed_pointer.js:505-506, 520, 530`), consumed in `cloneStroke` (`inpaint_ed_tips.js:440-441`), `healSource` (`inpaint_ed_heal.js:150, 157`), and the crosshair/ghost overlay in `drawScene` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_relight.js:1038-1054`).

Tracing all whole-document geometry operations and layer transforms in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js` confirms there are no guards or coordinate updates for these fields (note one minor line-number correction in the candidate's evidence: `followGeometry` is at `inpaint_ed_geometry.js:872-878`, not `1251-1259`; all other cited line numbers are exact). Specifically, `turnDocumentNow` (`731`) and `straightenDocumentNow` (`1086`) set `this.cloneSource = null` (which also makes any leftover `this.cloneOffset` unreachable until `Alt+click` resets it at `inpaint_ed_pointer.js:506`), but neither clears or maps `this.lastStrokeEnd`. Meanwhile, `followGeometry` (`872-878`) -> `mapExtras` (`762-822`), `cropCanvasNow` (`1393, 1405`), `resizeImageNow` (`1474-1475, 1491`), and `extendCanvasNow` (`1650-1657, 1674`) touch neither `this.lastStrokeEnd` nor `this.cloneSource` / `this.cloneOffset` (nor do `restoreGeometry` at `851-860`, `setBasePixels` at `inpaint_ed_open.js:104-155`, or per-layer moves/scales/rotates/flips at `inpaint_ed_geometry.js:218, 237, 332, 394, 411, 586` and `inpaint_ed_pointer.js:148, 894-919`). Thus cropping 150 px off top/left shifts `layer.x, layer.y` by `-150` while `lastStrokeEnd` stays at `(200, 200)` (so `Shift+click` draws from 150 px down-right of the previous dab), and cropping, extending, or resizing after `Alt+click` leaves `cloneSource` (and `cloneOffset` under resize) sampling the wrong location.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`): `canvas-a/F6` only covered Gradient fill layer parameters in `mapExtras`, and no open bug or prior finding covers `lastStrokeEnd`, `cloneSource`, or `cloneOffset`. Severity is `nice`: hitting this requires carrying a transient tool anchor (`Shift+click` line origin or `Alt+click` clone point) across a tool switch into a canvas geometry or layer-transform operation and back without clicking anew, the clone crosshair/ghost overlay visibly shows the unshifted source before painting, and `Ctrl+Z` / `Alt+click` immediately recovers.

findings.claim: When a reference layer is hidden or deleted, `remapBoxDescs` parks any box token naming it as `@img?<layerId>`. The API route refuses parked box tokens via `runDesc` -> `pluginBoxes`, and the main prompt refuses parked tokens on both API and local routes via `refPrompt`, but local ComfyUI box runs (`FLUX 3 Image Klein`, `MOSS-Image`) build `st.boxes` via `promptPayload` and `nameBoxTokens` (`/@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g`), sending literal `'@img?Lm3k9x2ab12'` into the model's prompt rows with no refusal or note.
findings.scenario: Select local recipe FLUX 3 Image Klein, turn Boxes on, add shown references A (`@img1`) and B (`@img2`), and create a New box with desc `'the hat from @img1'` (main prompt has no `@img1`). Click A's eye in the reference list to hide it: `remapBoxDescs` rewrites the stored box desc to `'the hat from @img?<A.id>'`. Click Generate: `queueGenerate` -> `localBoxPlan` -> `promptPayload` copies `o.desc = foldDesc(b.desc)` verbatim, and `nameBoxTokens` only matches `/@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g`. The queued `canvas_state.boxes` sends `'the hat from @img?Lm3k9x2ab12'` to the ComfyUI node and into FLUX 3's row text instead of refusing as the API route does.
findings.evidence:
renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:107-111 `remapBoxDescs`: writes `@img?<layerId>` into `pluginData.boxes`.
renderer/editor/host_setup.js:153-160 `localBoxPlan`: `const p = promptPayload(list, editor.refLayersFor(refIds));`
renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:286 `promptPayload`: `o.desc = foldDesc(b.desc);` (unlike `runDesc` at lines 244-249, `PARKED` is not expanded).
renderer/editor/comfyprompt.js:211-226: `const BOX_TOKEN = /@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g; ... return { ...b, desc: b.desc.replace(BOX_TOKEN, (m, n) => nameOf(+n) || m) };`
renderer/editor/host_queue.js:152, 168-177: `refPrompt` checks only `prompt` and `negative`, while `st.boxes` only passes through `nameBoxTokens`.
findings.fix: In `localBoxPlan` (or before `queueGenerate` serializes `boxGiven`), scan kept box descriptions for `PARKED` (and out-of-range live `@imgN` tokens) and throw a refusal naming the hidden/removed layer ('show it or take the token out'), matching the API route's `pluginBoxes` refusal and `refPrompt`.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc. When a shown reference layer is hidden, deleted, or has its role changed away from 'reference' in the app (`host.refTokens === true`, `renderer/editor/host_state.js` / `host.js:109`), `RefsPart.refsMutated` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_refs.js:78-95`) builds `r = (t) => (t ? remap(t, before, target) : t)` (`reftokens.js:111-121`) and calls `this.remapBoxDescs(r)` at line 93. `remapBoxDescs` (`inpaint_ed_refs.js:103-115`) rewrites every box's `desc` in `this.pluginData.boxes.boxes` in place, turning a live `@img1` for hidden/deleted layer `Lm3k9x2ab12` into the parked form `@img?Lm3k9x2ab12` (`reftokens.js:118`).

On the API route (`host_provider.js:350-351` and `host_generate.js:81`), `plugins/boxes/main.js:60-62, 221` passes each box through `runDesc` (`renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:244-249`), which explicitly maps `PARKED = /@img\?(L[0-9a-z]+)(?![\w-])/g` (line 25) to `{@layer:${id}}` so `pluginBoxes` (`renderer/editor/boxes.js:159-163`) throws `fail('layer', ...)` before any request is sent (unless the box lies outside the crop and is dropped first at `boxes.js:187-188`). Likewise, `HostProviderPart.refPrompt` (`renderer/editor/host_provider.js:68-73` -> `reftokens.js:142`) refuses parked tokens on both API and local routes, but only inspects `prompt` and `negative` (`host_queue.js:75, 152` and `commands_runs.js:77`).

On the local ComfyUI box route — reachable via `Generate` on `recipes/flux3_klein_local.json` (`host_queue.js:110-119`) and `Generate new` on `flux3_klein_local` or `recipes/moss_image_local.json` (`commands_runs.js:87` -> `host_setup.js:172-177` `newBoxPlan`) when the Boxes switch is on and the main/negative prompts do not themselves hold the parked token — `HostSetupPart.localBoxPlan` (`renderer/editor/host_setup.js:153-161`) calls `promptPayload(list, editor.refLayersFor(refIds))` (`renderer/editor/boxes_model.js:270-291`). `promptPayload` drops unsent `from` boxes at lines 278-279, but for kept boxes (e.g. a `new` or Text box, or a `from` box of another shown reference) line 286 copies `o.desc = foldDesc(b.desc)` with `@img?<layerId>` intact. `serializeForPrompt` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:467-474`) preserves `opts.boxes` verbatim, and `queueGenerate` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:168-177`) runs `comfyprompt.nameBoxTokens` (`renderer/editor/comfyprompt.js:212, 221-226`), whose `BOX_TOKEN = /@img([1-9][0-9]*)\b/g` requires a digit after `@img` and leaves `@img?<layerId>` untouched. Downstream in `ComfyUI-InpaintCanvas` (`docs/PLAN_NODE_BOXES.md:519-521`), `nodes.py` only matches `@imgN` against `referenceLabels` (the node's own editor has `host.refTokens = false` and never produces parked tokens), so literal `@img?Lm3k9x2ab12` goes into `box_prompt` or `elements` (`MOSSImageLayoutPrompt`) with no refusal and no warning note.

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including lines 371-430), both 2026-11-07 `verified.json` files, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`: `prompt-refs/box-desc-tokens-not-remapped` (`verified.json:198-212`) reported that box descriptions were not remapped at all; `remapBoxDescs` and `runDesc`'s `PARKED` handling were introduced after 2026-11-12 to fix that finding, and this finding proves a missed route (`localBoxPlan` / `promptPayload` / `nameBoxTokens`) in that new fix, so it is a genuine new finding rather than `known`.

Severity is `nice`: paid API runs are already guarded by `runDesc` + `pluginBoxes`, no document pixels or money are lost, and hitting it requires a local ComfyUI box recipe (`flux3_klein_local` or `moss_image_local`) where `@imgN` appears in a kept non-dropped box's `desc` without also appearing in the main/negative prompt (which `refPrompt` would refuse at `host_queue.js:75`), resulting in a wasted local render with garbled `@img?L...` text instead of an upfront refusal.

findings.function: closeEditor / forget (with plugins/boxes/main.js and inpaint_canvas.js close)
findings.claim: Double-clicking a box mounts `<dialog class="boxes-inline">` on `document.body` outside `editor.root`, but neither `forget(docId)`, tab switching (`activate`), nor `InpaintEditor.close()` closes `editing` (or clears `drag`). Moreover, when a closed tab's inline editor later blurs or presses Enter, `closeEditor` evaluates `env.docById(e.docId) || e.doc` — since `scumble.documents.byId` returns `null` rather than throwing, it falls back to the closed `e.doc` and mutates/emits `changed` on a destroyed editor.
findings.scenario: Open two tabs, select the Boxes tool (`X`) on a clean Tab 1, double-click a box so `<dialog class="boxes-inline">` opens on `document.body` with focus in its `<textarea>`, type a new description, and press `Ctrl+W` (or `Ctrl+Tab` to switch to Tab 2, or close Tab 1 via `close_document`). `activate` hides Tab 1's `root` without moving focus, and `forget(doc.id)` only deletes from `selected`, so the floating `<dialog>` remains visible at `z-index: 10050` over Tab 2. Clicking Tab 2's canvas then blurs the textarea and runs `closeEditor(true)`: `env.docById(e.docId)` returns `null`, `d` becomes `null || e.doc` (the destroyed Tab 1 `Document`), and `api.set(d, ...)` pushes undo and calls `host.changed(ed)` on the closed editor.
findings.evidence:
renderer/editor/boxes_tool.js:90-98 `closeEditor`: `let d = e.doc; try { d = env.docById(e.docId) || e.doc; } catch (_) { /* the tab was closed: nothing to write */ return; } ... const n = api.set(d, b.id, { [e.field]: value });`
renderer/editor/boxes_tool.js:131-134 `openEditor`: `document.body.appendChild(dlg); dlg.show(); editing = { docId: doc.id, doc, id: b.id, field, dlg, area }; area.focus();`
renderer/editor/boxes_tool.js:420: `forget: (docId) => selected.delete(docId)` (does not close `editing` or clear `drag` when `docId` matches).
renderer/plugins.js:699: `byId: (id) => docOf(host.editorById(id))` (returns `null`, never throws).
plugins/boxes/main.js:205-206: `activate` only calls `renderPanel(ev.doc)`; `renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:366-414` `close()` never calls `if (this.boxes) this.boxes.deselect()`.
findings.fix: In `boxes_tool.js`, drop the `|| e.doc` fallback in `closeEditor` (`const d = env.docById(e.docId); if (!d) return;`), make `forget(docId)` call `if (editing && editing.docId === docId) closeEditor(false)` and clear matching `drag`/`hover`, close/commit any open inline editor on tab `activate` in `plugins/boxes/main.js`, and call `if (this.boxes) this.boxes.deselect()` in `InpaintEditor.close()`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc. In `renderer/editor/boxes_tool.js:100-137`, double-clicking a box with the Boxes tool calls `openEditor(doc, b, ev)`, which appends `<dialog class="boxes-inline">` (styled `position:fixed; ... z-index:10050`) directly to `document.body` (`boxes_tool.js:115-117, 131-134`) rather than inside `editor.root`, sets `editing = { docId: doc.id, doc, id: b.id, field, dlg, area }`, and focuses `area`. Nothing closes `editing` when switching tabs or closing a tab without a prior blur: `plugins/boxes/main.js` registers no `activate` listener at all (only `removed` at line 205 and `geometry` at line 208), `boxTool.forget(docId)` at `boxes_tool.js:420` only runs `selected.delete(docId)` (leaving `editing`, `drag`, and `lastClick` intact), `onDeselect` (`boxes_tool.js:200`) only fires when changing tools (`renderer/plugins.js:636-638`), and `InpaintEditor.close()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:366-414`) cleans up `textEdit`, `flyout`, `ask`, `tipPicker`, and `promptField.closePopups()` but never calls `if (this.boxes) this.boxes.deselect()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_boxes.js:258-260`).

Tracing the user/MCP entry points and guards: clicking another tab or the tab `×` button with the mouse blurs `area` on `mousedown` before switching/closing, and closing a dirty tab opens `askDocument`'s modal dialog (`showModal()`), which also blurs `area` while the tab is still open. However, Electron menu accelerators `CmdOrCtrl+Tab` / `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+Tab` and `CmdOrCtrl+W` (`electron/main/main.js:760, 764-765` -> `renderer/shell.js:1408-1410`), as well as MCP `activate_document` and `close_document`, do not move DOM focus. On `Ctrl+Tab`, `host.activate` (`renderer/editor/host_state.js:260-267`) toggles `shell-hidden` on `editor.root` without touching `document.body`, leaving Tab 1's `<dialog class="boxes-inline">` visible and focused on top of Tab 2. On `Ctrl+W` of a clean `.scumble` tab (typing in `area` has not yet mutated `pluginData`, so `host.documentDirty` at `renderer/editor/host_documents.js:75-84` is still `false`) or `close_document` (`force: true`), `closeDocument` (`renderer/shell.js:296-335`) calls `host.removeEditor(editor)` (`host_state.js:228-257`) and `editor.destroy()` (`inpaint_canvas.js:1599-1616`) while `dlg` stays mounted and focused on `document.body`.

When `area` subsequently blurs (`boxes_tool.js:129`) or receives `Enter` (`boxes_tool.js:127`), `closeEditor(true)` (`boxes_tool.js:83-99`) executes `try { d = env.docById(e.docId) || e.doc; } catch (_) { return; }` at line 91. Although the JSDoc at `boxes_tool.js:65-66` states that `env.docById` 'throws or answers null once the tab is closed', `plugins/boxes/main.js:188` wires `scumble.documents.byId(id)` (`renderer/plugins.js:668, 699` -> `host.editorById(id)` at `renderer/editor/host_setup.js:71-73`), which returns `null` rather than throwing. The `|| e.doc` fallback therefore selects the closed `Document` wrapper, and `api.set(d, b.id, ...)` (`boxes_tool.js:95` -> `plugins.js:712-717`) pushes an undo step, mutates `pluginData`, and calls `host.changed(ed)` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:503-513`, scheduling `areasSoon` and emitting `changed`) on the destroyed editor.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, all three prior `verified.json` files, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: none mention `boxes-inline`, `closeEditor`/`openEditor`, or `boxes_tool.js` `forget`. Severity is `nice`: mouse tab clicks and dirty-close prompts naturally blur and commit first, so this requires keyboard/menu/MCP tab switching or closing a clean/forced tab while editing a box inline, and does not corrupt open documents' pixels or incur provider charges.

findings.claim: The MCP/script command `sample.mean_color` (marked `readOnly: true`, so agents can invoke it freely) calls `doc.getPixels().data.data` when there is no selection, synchronously flattening the entire document to a single canvas and allocating full-size `ImageData` (~1.2 GB on a 15000 x 10000 picture, and throwing above Chromium's 268 MP canvas limit), while `selectionBox` allocates ~1.95 GB synchronously when the full 15k canvas is selected.
findings.scenario: Open a 15000 x 10000 document (150 MP) with no selection (or after `Select All`) and run `sample.mean_color` via MCP or the assistant. Without a selection, `doc.getPixels()` calls `ed.flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true })` (600 MB canvas) plus `ctx.getImageData(0, 0, 15000, 10000)` (600 MB `ImageData`) synchronously on the renderer main thread; with `Select All`, `doc.selection({ box: true })` (600 MB `readRect` + 150 MB mask) plus `doc.flatten({ box, exact: true }).getContext('2d').getImageData(...)` (600 MB + 600 MB) spikes ~1.95 GB synchronously. On a 20000 x 15000 (300 MP) document, `mean_color` throws `'larger than any canvas'`.
findings.evidence:
plugins/sample/main.js:68-74 `selectionBox`: `const sel = doc.selection({ box: true }); ... const flat = doc.flatten({ box: [x, y, x + w, y + h], exact: true }).getContext("2d").getImageData(0, 0, w, h).data;`
plugins/sample/main.js:138-146 `mean_color`: `const got = selectionBox(doc); const sel = got && got.sel; const flat = got ? got.flat : doc.getPixels().data.data;`
renderer/plugins.js:107, 124-127: `getPixels()` calls `this.flatten()` -> `ed.flattenToCanvas(o())` and `c.getContext("2d").getImageData(0, 0, c.width, c.height)`.
Contrast `plugins/sample/main.js:108-109`, where `probe` reads `256 x 256` boxes via `doc.flatten({ box, exact: true })`.
findings.fix: Accumulate `r, g, b, n` in horizontal strips (e.g. 256 rows high across `sel ? sel.bounds : { x: 0, y: 0, w: doc.width, h: doc.height }`) using `doc.flatten({ box: [x0, y, x1, y1], exact: true })` (and reading the selection strip-by-strip or reusing `doc.selection({ box: true })` per strip), keeping peak scratch memory to a few megabytes at 15k and avoiding full-document canvas limits.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc. `plugins/sample` is shipped in packaged builds (`package.json:61,105,152` includes `"plugins/**/*"`) and enabled by default (`plugins/sample/plugin.json:8` sets `"enabledByDefault": true`, which `electron/main/plugins.js:74,82` loads unless explicitly added to `settings.plugins.disabled`, and `electron/main/settings.js:10-67` leaves it enabled). Moreover, `sample.mean_color` (`plugins/sample/main.js:132-151`) is marked `readOnly: true` for external MCP clients and is explicitly listed in `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:16,57` under both `READS` and `POLICY` as `AUTO`, so the in-app assistant and MCP agents can invoke `sample_mean_color` without confirmation.

Tracing both execution paths confirms the synchronous full-size allocations and >268 MP failure:
1. **No selection (`plugins/sample/main.js:139-141`)**: `selectionBox(doc)` calls `doc.selection({ box: true })` (`renderer/plugins.js:182-185`), which returns `null` when `bounds(this.editor)` is `null`. `mean_color` then evaluates `doc.getPixels().data.data` at line 141. `Document.getPixels()` with no `layerKey` (`renderer/plugins.js:122-127`) calls `this.flatten()` -> `ed.flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true })` (`renderer/plugins.js:97-107`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:561-574`) and then `c.getContext("2d").getImageData(0, 0, c.width, c.height)`. On a 15000 x 10000 (150 MP) document, this synchronously allocates a 600 MB `<canvas>` (plus another 600 MB `flatCanvas` at `inpaint_ed_composite.js:33` if any filter or colour-matched layer is visible, and a full-size display mirror for `this.basePx` at line 59) and a 600 MB `ImageData` (~1.2 GB minimum) on the renderer main thread. On a 20000 x 15000 (300 MP) document (`ed.huge === true` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:97`, since `w * h > CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS` = 268,435,456 in `inpaint_sizelimit.js:6`), `flattenToCanvas` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:564`) throws `"this 20000 × 15000 document is larger than any canvas (268 MP)..."`.
2. **Full/large selection (`plugins/sample/main.js:68-74`)**: `selectionBox(doc)` (used by both `mean_color` at line 139 and `selectionToLayer` at line 77) calls `doc.selection({ box: true })` (`renderer/plugins.js:186-190`), which runs `this.editor.sel.readRect(b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h).data` (`inpaint_tiles.js:1387-1410`, allocating a 600 MB `ImageData` at 15k) and builds a 150 MB `Uint8Array` `mask`, then calls `doc.flatten({ box: [x, y, x + w, y + h], exact: true }).getContext("2d").getImageData(0, 0, w, h).data` (`renderer/plugins.js:111` -> `ed.readBox` at `inpaint_ed_stack.js:930-940`, allocating a 600 MB canvas and a 600 MB `ImageData`, or two 600 MB canvases when `boxReach` is `Infinity`), totaling ~1.95 GB of synchronous main-thread allocations in a single turn. Above 268 MP with `Select All`, `sampleRegion` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:46`) creates an oversized `<canvas>` above Chromium's 268 MP limit, which draws nothing and reads back all-zero pixels (`{ pixels: 300000000, rgb: [0, 0, 0], hex: "#000000" }`).

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files: earlier reviews covered `plugins/sample` `probe` (`prompt-refs/probe-cache-unbounded`, now capped at 16 tiles at lines 98-111) and `plugins/boxes` `fromSelection` (`prompt-refs/from-selection-reads-whole-selection`), not `sample.mean_color` or `plugins/sample/main.js` `selectionBox`.
