Severity is `nice`: `sample.mean_color` is a template/sample plugin command not invoked by core interactive editing UI, and the impact is a main-thread memory/latency spike on very large (15k) images or a >268 MP edge case with no document data or billing loss.

findings.claim: flattenNow captures `before = this.snapshot({ kind: "canvas" })` and `gen = this.historyGen` at the start, awaits `encodeComposite` (which first awaits `relightSettled()` and retries once if a band saw `compositeVersion` move), and then overwrites `ver = this.compositeVersion` at lines 764 and 769 before uploading and checking `this.compositeVersion !== ver` at line 774. Consequently, any composite-only edit during `relightSettled()` or the first band retry (hiding/showing or soloing a layer, hiding a group, or changing opacity/blend) is baked into the flattened base without aborting Flatten or matching the `before` undo snapshot, while a pending relight debounce flushed by `relightSettled()` spuriously aborts Flatten.
findings.scenario:
Path A (mismatched flatten & dangling solo state): On a large document with layers A and B (plus a Relight filter computing full shadow maps, or during `encodeComposite` band encoding), click Flatten (`flattenNow` snapshots `before` with both A and B visible, `gen = historyGen`, `ids = "1,2"`), then immediately click Solo (or toggle visibility / opacity / blend) on layer A. `soloLayers` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:264-278`) sets `this._solo = new Set([A.id])` and bumps `compositeVersion` without changing `historyGen` or `ids`. `encodeComposite` restarts its band loop once on `/the picture changed/` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:666-667`, resetting `px` at `y0 === 0` on line 759) or falls through to `flattenToCanvas` on line 770, baking ONLY layer A into `px`. Line 764/769 overwrites `ver = this.compositeVersion`, so line 774 passes, line 782 deletes both A and B (leaving `this._solo` pointing at deleted layer ID), and `before` restores pre-solo state on Undo.
Path B (spurious refusal): Nudge a Relight light with an arrow key or mouse wheel (`pushRelightUndoDebounced`, 300 ms timer) and trigger Flatten within 300 ms. `flattenNow` records `gen = this.historyGen` at line 752, then `encodeComposite` calls `await this.relightSettled()` (`636`), which calls `this.flushPendingDebounces()` (`inpaint_ed_relight.js:38`), incrementing `this.historyGen` for the user's prior nudge; after encoding and uploading the entire image, line 774 sees `this.historyGen !== gen` and aborts Flatten.
findings.evidence: In `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:749-779`: `before = this.snapshot({ kind: "canvas" }); const gen = this.historyGen, ids = this.layers.map((l) => l.id).join(","); let ver = this.compositeVersion; const banded = await this.encodeComposite({ forRun: true }, { ... }); if (banded) { ver = this.compositeVersion; hash = banded.hash; ref = await uploadBlob(...); } else { if (px) px.release(); ver = this.compositeVersion; const flat = this.flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true }); ... } if (this.historyGen !== gen || this.compositeVersion !== ver || this.layers.map((l) => l.id).join(",") !== ids || this.gestureHeld()) { ... return; }`. Inside `encodeComposite` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:636, 665-668`), `await this.relightSettled();` runs before `encodeBands`, and `for (let round = 0; round < 2; round++)` catches `/the picture changed/` on `round === 0` and re-encodes the mutated composite. Actions that mutate the composite without bumping `historyGen` or `ids`: `soloLayers` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:264-278`), `setSelectedFlag` for `"visible"` (`607-620`, debounced undo), `setGroupFlag` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:340`, debounced undo), opacity slider `"input"` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:816`), and blend select `"input"` (`856`). Compare `mergeDownNow` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:362, 375`), which keeps `const ver = this.compositeVersion` immutable from before the async work.
findings.fix: In `flattenNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:748`), await `this.relightSettled()` (and re-check `if (!this.base || !this.layers.length) return;`) BEFORE taking `before = this.snapshot({ kind: "canvas" })` and capturing `const gen = this.historyGen, ver = this.compositeVersion, ids = ...`, and delete `ver = this.compositeVersion;` on lines 764 and 769 (also clearing `this._solo = null` when non-kept layers are flattened on line 782).
findings.why:
Confirmed at commit f45a86cc in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:742-799`. This is a genuine hole in the post-2026-11-12 fix for `tiles/flatten-commits-stale-composite` (which added `gen`, `ver`, `ids`, and `gestureHeld()` to `flattenNow` and `mergeDownNow`), so under the review rules it is not `known`; no open entry in `docs/BUGS.md`, `scratch/known_index.md`, the three `verified.json` files, or `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` records this defect.

In `flattenNow` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:749-756`), `before = this.snapshot({ kind: "canvas" })` (749) and `const gen = this.historyGen, ids = this.layers.map((l) => l.id).join(","); let ver = this.compositeVersion;` (752-753) are captured before `await this.encodeComposite({ forRun: true }, { hash: true, each: ... })` (756-762). Inside `encodeComposite` (`635-672`), line 636 runs `if (opts && opts.forRun) await this.relightSettled();` (`inpaint_ed_relight.js:37-40`), which calls `this.flushPendingDebounces()` (line 38) and `await this.relightIdle(also)` (line 39). When pending relight normal/shadow jobs land during `relightIdle`, `ensureRelightMaps` calls `this.markFilterChanged(layer, { soon: true })` (`inpaint_ed_relight.js:344, 535`) -> `this.uploaded.baseHash = null` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:631`) -> `ed.compositeVersion++` (`inpaint_strokebuf.js:69`). Apparently to avoid tripping over that `compositeVersion` bump, `flattenNow` overwrites `ver = this.compositeVersion;` after `encodeComposite` returns — both on the banded path at line 764 (before `await uploadBlob(...)` at 766) and on the fallback path at line 769 (before `this.flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true })` at 770 and `await uploadCanvas(...)` at 772) — whereas `mergeDownNow` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:362, 375`) keeps `const ver = this.compositeVersion` immutable and `extendCanvasNow` (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1578-1581`) awaits `this.relightSettled()` before taking `before`.

Both failure paths hold:
- Path A (composite-only mutation during `relightSettled` or `encodeComposite`): Because `flattenNow` passes `each`, `encodeComposite` skips `stackSource` (`638`) and runs `bandSource` + `encodeBands` (`647-671`), retrying once (`round === 0` -> `round === 1` at `666-667`, resetting `px` on `y0 === 0` at `759`) if `compositeVersion` changes mid-read, or returning `null` to `flattenToCanvas` (`770`) when `!bandPlan` or `NO_PROGRAM`. Several UI and command actions change the rendered composite and bump `compositeVersion` (`uploaded.baseHash = null`) without pushing an undo step or changing `historyGen` or layer IDs: `soloLayers` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:264-279`), `soloResult` (`inpaint_ed_histpanel.js:162-177`), `setSelectedFlag` for `"visible"` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:607-620` — note: no undo step at all, not debounced), `setGroupFlag` for `"visible"` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:338-350` — also no undo step), layer opacity `"input"`/`"change"` (`inpaint_ed_layers.js:812-820`), blend `<select>` `"change"` (`856`), MCP `set_layer` (`commands_layers.js:38-44`), and any unreleased `"input"` drag on a filter or colour-match slider (`inpaint_ed_panels.js:198-205`, `inpaint_ed_layers.js:836-842`, since `gestureHeld()` at `inpaint_ed_history.js:1029-1032` only inspects canvas `this.pointer`). Because lines 764/769 overwrite `ver = this.compositeVersion`, the recheck at line 774 passes, baking the mutated composite into `this.base`, deleting all pixel/filter layers (`782`), leaving `before` out of sync with the baked state, and leaving `this._solo` (`{ visible, known, groups, key }`) non-null so a later `soloLayers` + `unsolo` on newly added layers fails to restore their visibility (`known.has(l.id)` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:285`).
- Path B (spurious abort after Relight light nudge/wheel): Arrow-key nudging (`flushNudge` / `l._flushNudge` at `inpaint_ed_pointer.js:186-200`, 300 ms timer) and mouse-wheel light adjustment (`flushWheel` / `l._flushWheel` at `inpaint_ed_view.js:237-252`, 300 ms timer) defer `this.pushUndoSnapshot(snap, { ..., fromDebounce: true })`. Neither the Flatten toolbar button (`inpaint_modal.js:325`) nor `commands.run("flatten")` (`commands_layers.js:313`) flushes debounces before `flattenNow` records `gen = this.historyGen` at line 752. When `encodeComposite` calls `relightSettled()` -> `flushPendingDebounces()` (`inpaint_ed_relight.js:38`, `inpaint_ed_history.js:993-1003`), `pushUndoSnapshot` runs `if (!tracked) this.historyGen++;` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:483`), so after running the full shadow march, band encode, and PNG upload, line 774 sees `this.historyGen !== gen` and aborts Flatten.

Severity is calibrated down from `should` to `nice` (matching `feather-grow-write-back-over-newer-selection` and `freqsep-stale-box-after-await` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`): unlike the earlier `flatten-commits-stale-composite` bug where strokes or landed paid results were permanently lost, `historyGen` and `ids` now guard pixel edits and landed layers, `before` preserves all layers and pixels for `Ctrl+Z`, Path A requires touching composite controls mid-flatten while `"Flattening ..."` is active, and Path B requires clicking Flatten within 300 ms of a Relight arrow/wheel step and fails closed with a retry prompt.

findings.claim: When `GLCompositor.composite` prepares a stack mixing tile-backed layers (`l.pixels`, e.g. the base layer) and canvas-backed layers (`l.source`, e.g. a colour-matched layer off tiles or a layer with a non-grid mask) and `this._source(...)` returns `null` at line 1080, `composite` returns `null` immediately without calling `this._evictAtlas()` or `this._evict()`. Atlas slots and source textures allocated by earlier layers in the same `composite()` call remain unevicted past `atlasBudget` / `sourceBudget` while the viewport falls back to Canvas 2D.
findings.scenario: On a tiled document whose base (`this.basePx`) uploads visible tiles into `GLCompositor`'s atlas (`inpaint_compositor.js:1070`), have an upper layer take the `l.source` path (`glViewComposite` at `inpaint_ed_display.js:353, 377-379`, e.g. a colour-matched layer while `matchFromTiles` is false or a layer with an unaligned mask) under a viewport/window or GPU texture state where `this._source(l.source, l.version, need)` returns `null` (`w > this.maxTexture || h > this.maxTexture` or texture allocation failure at `inpaint_compositor.js:686, 697`). As the user pans across the document, each `composite()` call uploads newly visible base tiles into the atlas at line 1070 and then aborts at line 1080 without running `_evictAtlas()`, growing `this.atlasPages` above `this.atlasBudget` without eviction.
findings.evidence: In `renderer/editor/inpaint_compositor.js:1066-1083`: for `l.pixels`, `if (!tiles) { this._evictAtlas(); return null; }` (line 1071, fixed in 0.1.57 for `tiles/T1`), whereas for `l.source`, `const s = this._source(l.source, l.version, need); if (!s) return null;` (line 1080 — omits both `this._evict()` and `this._evictAtlas()`, which normally run only at the end of `composite()` on lines 1134-1135).
findings.fix: Change `renderer/editor/inpaint_compositor.js:1080` from `if (!s) return null;` to `if (!s) { this._evict(); this._evictAtlas(); return null; }`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_compositor.js:1053-1083` (with minor corrections to auxiliary line numbers and atlas-growth details in the raw report). In `GLCompositor.composite`, `this.frame++` runs at line 1056 before the preparation loop (`lines 1066-1083`). For tile-backed layers (`l.pixels`), line 1070 calls `this._tileInstances(l, region)` and line 1071 handles failure with `if (!tiles) { this._evictAtlas(); return null; }`. Nine lines below, for canvas-backed layers (`l.source`), lines 1079-1080 run `const s = this._source(l.source, l.version, need); if (!s) return null;`, returning before `this._evict()` and `this._evictAtlas()` at the end of `composite()` (`lines 1235-1236`, not 1134-1135 as stated in the raw evidence). Neither `_evict()` (`lines 537-554`) nor `_evictAtlas()` (`lines 1010-1036`) has any other caller on the normal frame path (`releaseDetachedDisplays` in `inpaint_ed_history.js:580-604` only drops detached records via `retainPixels`, and `releaseCaches` in `inpaint_canvas.js:1187-1191` only runs on background tabs or manual Free VRAM).

Tracing reachability from `drawViewComposite` -> `glCompositeUsable` -> `glViewComposite` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_display.js:271-285, 297-364, 397-409`): `glCompositeUsable` admits any visible stack without filter layers, mask editing, live strokes, pending transforms, compare/peek, or emulated (`dissolve`) blends. When line 1080 returns `null` on each frame: (1) for `this.atlas`, `_slot` (`lines 663-685`) does bound unbounded page creation once `this.atlasBytes >= this.atlasBudget` via `_evictOther(entry)` and slot reuse, so atlas memory does not grow without bound, but the last `_newPage` allocated just under budget (up to ~60 MB at level 0) stays above `atlasBudget` because `_evictOther` skips `entry` (`line 994`), and unused pages across zoom levels never age out via `ATLAS_STALE` (`300` frames, `lines 1016-1020`) even though WebGL output is discarded every frame; (2) for `this.textures`, neither `_texture` nor `_source` has any allocation-time eviction, so if an earlier layer in the stack uses `l.source` and creates new canvases across edits (`matchCanvas` in `inpaint_ed_match.js:43` or rebuilt pyramid levels in `inpaint_ed_display.js:165`), `this.textures` grows without bound past `TEXTURE_STALE`, `TEXTURE_CACHE` (64), and `TEXTURE_BUDGET` (1 GB), strongly retaining both the WebGL textures and their `HTMLCanvasElement` keys.

findings.claim: `lutToCanvas` packs a 3D LUT of size `N` into a single horizontal strip of dimensions `N * N` by `N`, and `lutFromCube` imposes no upper (or positive) bound on `LUT_3D_SIZE`. For a spec-valid `256`³ Adobe `.cube` file (`LUT_3D_SIZE 256`), `N * N` is `65,536`, exceeding Chromium's `65,535` px maximum canvas dimension: either `uploadCanvas` fails with a null-blob TypeError or uploads a blank backing store that `lutFromImage` reads back as all-zero black on reopen, while a negative `LUT_3D_SIZE` bypasses the length check and throws `RangeError`.
findings.scenario: Load a standard 256³ `.cube` file (`LUT_3D_SIZE 256`, allowed by Adobe Cube LUT Spec 1.0) onto a Colour LUT filter layer. `lutFromCube` parses the `256³` floats and `lutToCanvas` calls `makeCanvas(65536, 256)`. Because a `65,536` px wide HTMLCanvasElement has no usable backing store in Chromium (`putImageData` draws nothing and `toBlob` produces `null` or zeroed pixels), either loading fails with an unhelpful TypeError (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'arrayBuffer')`) or, if encoded empty while `layer._lutData` stays valid in RAM during the session, saving and reopening the `.scumble` document calls `lutFromImage(img, 256)` (`makeCanvas(65536, 256)`) and replaces the LUT with all zeros, turning the layer solid black.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:389` parses `size = parseInt(line.split(/\s+/)[1], 10)` and line 398 checks only `if (!size || values.length < size * size * size * 3)` (which passes for `size = 256`, `size > 256`, or negative `size = -2` where `size * size * size * 3` is `-24 <= values.length`). Line 455 (`lutToCanvas`) allocates `const c = makeCanvas(N * N, N);` and line 474 (`lutFromImage`) allocates `const c = makeCanvas(N * N, N);`. Per `CLAUDE.md:1260`, a canvas `65,536` px on a side draws and reads nothing in Chromium (`65536 = 256 * 256`).
findings.fix: Validate `size >= 2 && size <= 256` in `lutFromCube` (resampling lattices above e.g. `65` or `128` via `lutOnUnitDomain`, or tiling the `N` blue slices into a 2D grid `cols * N` by `rows * N` in `lutToCanvas` / `lutFromImage` so neither dimension ever approaches `65,535`, while keeping backwards compatibility in `lutFromImage` when `img.width === N * N`).
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, `lutFromCube` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:380-412`) parses `size = parseInt(line.split(/\s+/)[1], 10)` at line 389 and checks only `if (!size || values.length < size * size * size * 3)` at line 398, with no lower or upper bound on `size`. Both `lutToCanvas` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:453-469`, line 455 `const c = makeCanvas(N * N, N);`) and `lutFromImage` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:472-485`, line 474 `const c = makeCanvas(N * N, N);`) pack all `N` blue slices horizontally into an `N * N` by `N` 2D canvas using the module-local `makeCanvas` (`inpaint_filters.js:26-31`), which performs no dimension check. Entry from the UI is `PanelsPart.buildFilterControls` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:52-64`, line 56) -> `FiltersPart.loadLutFile` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:642-659`), and document restore enters `lutFromImage` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:215-217`. No callers normalize, clamp, or resample `lut.size`.

Adobe Cube LUT Specification 1.0 defines `LUT_3D_SIZE` `N` as an integer in `[2, 256]`. For `N = 256`, `N * N` is `65,536`, which exceeds Chromium's `65,535` px maximum canvas side (`CLAUDE.md:1260`), even though the total pixel count is only `16.78 MP` and WebGL2's 3D texture path (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:866-867`) supports `N = 256`. On a 6-decimal `256`³ `.cube` file (~432 MiB, under V8's ~512 MiB max string length), `lutFromCube` parses all `16,777,216` entries, `lutToCanvas` creates an unbacked `65,536 × 256` canvas where `putImageData` draws nothing, and `uploadCanvas` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_upload.js:42-45`) -> `encodeCanvas` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_encode.js:23-38`) fails in both the worker (`createImageBitmap` / `OffscreenCanvas(65536, 256).convertToBlob()` at `inpaint_worker.js:1307-1323`) and the main-thread fallback (`canvas.toBlob` resolves `null`), causing `hashBlob(null)` (`inpaint_encode.js:37, 44-48`) to throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'arrayBuffer')`. In addition, a negative `LUT_3D_SIZE` (e.g. `-2`, where `size * size * size * 3` is `-24 <= values.length`) bypasses line 398 and throws `RangeError: Invalid typed array length` at line 406/420 instead of `"not a valid 3D .cube file"`, and `LUT_3D_SIZE 1` (invalid per spec) is accepted and forces CPU fallback at `inpaint_filters_gl.js:867`.

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (including `Size limits: gaps found reading the code` at lines 162-190), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: `filters/cube-domain-applied-to-outputs` in the 2026-11-07 review was a separate `DOMAIN_MIN`/`DOMAIN_MAX` scaling bug already fixed at `inpaint_filters.js:399-450`, and no known item covers `.cube` size bounds or `lutToCanvas` exceeding `65,535` px.

Severity is calibrated to `nice` rather than `should` (and not `must`): because `canvas.toBlob` resolves `null` on a `65,536`-px-wide canvas and `hashBlob(null)` throws before `loadLutFile` reaches `pushUndo` or writes `layer.lut` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:647-650`), the silent save/reopen data-loss branch does not occur in Electron/Chromium; instead, `loadLutFile`'s `try/catch` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:655-658`) catches the failure and leaves the existing layer intact. Every standard LUT grid size (`17`, `32`, `33`, `64`, `65`, `128`, `144`, up to `255` where `255² = 65,025 <= 65,535`) works, so this only affects the rare ~450 MB `256`³ boundary case and malformed `<= 1` headers, producing wasted parsing and a misleading error message.

findings.claim: When replacing the stock on an active `Film look` (`film.look`) layer, `applyLook` overwrites `l.name` on the raw layer before calling `doc.setFilterParams(active.id, params)`. Whenever no hover-preview `_undoPending` snapshot is already held on the layer—such as any `film.apply_look` MCP/assistant call or clicking a stock tile in the Film looks panel within the 120 ms hover debounce—`setFilterParams` snapshots the layer after `l.name` was already changed, so Ctrl+Z reverts the look's pixels while leaving the undone stock's name on the layer.
findings.scenario: Have an active `Film look` layer set to `Kodak Portra 400` (layer name `Kodak Portra 400`). Run `film.apply_look` with `preset: "velvia50"` (or click `Fujifilm Velvia 50` in the Film looks panel within 120 ms of entering the tile). Press Ctrl+Z: `params.preset` returns to `"portra400"`, but the layer row remains named `Fujifilm Velvia 50`. Also, `cancelLookHover` (lines 79-82) cancels `doc.activeLayer()` rather than the layer id that entered preview at line 108, leaving `_undoPending` and the previewed preset stuck if selection changes before `pointerleave`.
findings.evidence: `plugins/film/main.js:39-43`: `if (active && active.kind === "filter" && active.filter === LOOK_ID) { const l = doc.rawLayer(active.id); l.name = stock ? stock.label.replace(/ \(.*\)$/, "") : l.name; const out = doc.setFilterParams(active.id, params); ... }`. In `renderer/plugins.js:223-228`, `setFilterParams` captures `const prev = l._undoPending || ed.snapshot({ kind: "filter", id: l.id });` at call time; when `l._undoPending` is null (the 120 ms `setTimeout` at `plugins/film/main.js:104-110` was cleared by `click` at line 114 before firing, or `applyLook` was called from `film.apply_look` at line 206), `ed.snapshot` records the already-overwritten `l.name`.
findings.fix: Move `l.name = stock ? stock.label.replace(/ \(.*\)$/, "") : l.name;` in `plugins/film/main.js` to run after `doc.setFilterParams(active.id, params)` (when `l._undoPending` has already been snapshotted and pushed with the previous name), and remember `previewLayerId` in `looks` panel hover state so `cancelLookHover` cancels that exact layer id.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in `plugins/film/main.js:34-48`. When the active layer is a `film.look` filter layer (`active && active.kind === "filter" && active.filter === LOOK_ID`), `applyLook` fetches the raw layer object at line 40 (`const l = doc.rawLayer(active.id);`), mutates `l.name = stock ? stock.label.replace(/ \(.*\)$/, "") : l.name;` in place at line 41, and only then calls `const out = doc.setFilterParams(active.id, params);` at line 42. In `renderer/plugins.js:219-231`, `Document.setFilterParams` checks `if (!l._undoPending) l._undoPending = ed.snapshot({ kind: "filter", id: l.id });` at line 223 before patching `l.params` (line 224) and pushing `l._undoPending` via `ed.pushUndoSnapshot` (line 227). Because `HistoryPart.snapshotOf` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:447-451`) records `name: layer.name` at snapshot time, any call to `applyLook` when `l._undoPending` is null snapshots the already-overwritten `l.name` alongside the old `l.params`. On `Ctrl+Z`, `applySnapshot` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:840-861`) restores `layer.params` to the previous stock while `layer.name = snap.name || layer.name` (line 858) keeps the undone stock's name. (Note for the fix: because `doc.setFilterParams` returns `layerSummary(ed, l)` at `renderer/plugins.js:230`, moving `l.name = ...` after `setFilterParams` should also update `out.name = l.name` so `film.apply_look` returns the updated summary name.)

Traced both callers of `applyLook` (`plugins/film/main.js:115` and `plugins/film/main.js:203`, mis-cited as 206 in the candidate's evidence). First, the MCP/assistant command `film.apply_look` (`plugins/film/main.js:196-205`) invokes `applyLook` directly with `l._undoPending` unset, so 100% of `film.apply_look` stock replacements on an active `film.look` layer fail to restore the previous layer name on undo. Second, in the `Film looks` panel (`plugins/film/main.js:93-119`), `pointerenter` schedules `doc.setFilterParams(active.id, { preset: s.id }, { preview: true })` behind a 120 ms `setTimeout` (`cellHoverTimer`, lines 104-110), while `click` clears `cellHoverTimer` at line 114 and calls `applyLook(doc, s.id)` at line 115. If the user hovers inside the grid for >= 120 ms before clicking, `l._undoPending` is already populated with the original `l.name` and undo restores the name; however, clicking or tapping a tile within 120 ms of entering the grid clears the timer before `l._undoPending` is created, reproducing the stale name on undo. The secondary observation in `cancelLookHover` (`plugins/film/main.js:75-83`) also holds: `pointerenter` previews on whatever `active.id` was active when the 120 ms timer fired (line 108), whereas `pointerleave` cancels `doc.activeLayer()` (lines 79-81) instead of the previewed layer id, leaving `l.params.preset`, `l._undoPending`, and `ed.filterPreview` stuck if `activeLayerId` changes while the pointer stays inside `.film-grid` (e.g. a result layer landing via `addResults` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:544, 663`).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (all open and fixed sections), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: neither `applyLook` nor `cancelLookHover` in `plugins/film/main.js` is previously recorded.

Severity is downgraded from `should` to `nice`. Standard mouse browsing in the `Film looks` panel hovers for >= 120 ms before clicking, which primes `l._undoPending` prior to `applyLook` and avoids the bug; hitting it requires either `film.apply_look` followed by undo or a sub-120 ms click/tap on grid entry followed by undo. Even when hit, `params.preset`, rendered/exported pixels, and the layer's `Preset` `<select>` all revert cleanly—only the layer row's display `name` string remains stale, and `cancelLookHover` missing its target requires `activeLayerId` to change mid-hover inside `.film-grid`.

findings.claim: When a plugin or ad-hoc shader passes `null` for an optional `sampler2D` uniform (such as `u_blur` in `film.bw` when `structure === 0`, `u_blur` in `film.points`, or `u_map`/`u_guide` in `LIMIT_SHADER`), `applyPluginGL` skips both `uploadSampler` and `gl.uniform1i`. Once that program has previously set its sampler uniform to `s.unit` (e.g. `TEXTURE5`), `s.unit` can still hold a `GLSurface` texture bound by an earlier pass (such as `LIMIT_SHADER`'s `u_in` on `TEXTURE5`) that has since been returned to `POOL`; when `renderToSurface` pops that same `GLSurface` as its draw FBO, WebGL2 raises `GL_INVALID_OPERATION` (feedback loop), forcing a fallback to main-thread tiled 2D canvas readbacks.
findings.scenario: On a 15k document, add a `Black & white film` (`film.bw`) layer with a `Luminosity` limit, adjust `Structure` to a non-zero value once (setting `BW`'s `u_blur` uniform to unit `5`), then return `Structure` to `0` (`u_blur: null`). `limitStage` binds the input `GLSurface` texture to `TEXTURE5` (`u_in` is sampler 0 -> unit `5`) and releases it back to `POOL` at `endScope`. On subsequent redraws or `programBand` export bands, `BW` pops that `GLSurface` from `POOL` as its destination FBO while `TEXTURE5` still binds its texture and `BW`'s active uniform `u_blur` still points to unit `5`: `gl.drawArrays` fails with `GL error 1282` (`GL_INVALID_OPERATION`), `renderToSurface` returns `null`, and `renderOut` falls back to `renderTiled` CPU `getImageData`/`putImageData` tiles.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:1025-1030` assigns plugin samplers sequential units starting at `PLUGIN_TEX_UNIT` (`5`). Line 1044 (`uploadSampler`) binds `GLSurface` inputs directly to `gl.TEXTURE0 + s.unit` (`if (isGLSurface(v)) { gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D, v.tex); return; }`), which `LIMIT_SHADER` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:15, 82`) does for `u_in: src` on unit `5`, without unbinding after draw. In `applyPluginGL` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:1133-1138`), `if (v == null || pg.u[s.name] == null) continue;` leaves both `gl.TEXTURE0 + s.unit` and `pg.u[s.name]` untouched when `plugins/film/filters.js:678` (`BW`) or `plugins/film/points.js:131` (`POINTS`) passes `u_blur: null`. `renderToSurface` (`inpaint_filters_gl.js:555-568`) then acquires a pooled surface from `POOL`, attaches `s.fbo`, draws, hits `gl.getError() === 1282`, logs a warning, and returns `null`.
findings.fix: In `applyPluginGL` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:1134-1138`), when `v == null` and `pg.u[s.name] != null`, either point the unused sampler uniform at unit `0` (`gl.uniform1i(pg.u[s.name], 0)`, which `bindSource` binds right below at line 1143 to the active `src`, never the newly acquired output FBO) or bind a shared `1x1` dummy `TEXTURE_2D` to `gl.TEXTURE0 + s.unit`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:1133-1138`. `pluginProgram` (`inpaint_filters_gl.js:1025-1031`) assigns `sampler2D` uniforms sequential texture units starting at `PLUGIN_TEX_UNIT = 5` (`:960`). When a sampler value is a `GLSurface`, `uploadSampler` (`:1041-1044`) binds `v.tex` directly to `gl.TEXTURE0 + s.unit` and never unbinds it after the draw. In `applyPluginGL` (`:1133-1138`), `if (v == null || pg.u[s.name] == null) continue;` skips both `uploadSampler` and `gl.uniform1i` whenever a pass supplies `null` for an optional sampler. Because uniform values are per-program WebGL state and WebGL2 validates render-texture feedback loops across all statically active sampler uniforms of the linked program regardless of dynamic `if (u_useBlur)` branches (the same reason `inpaint_depthfx.js:469-474`, `inpaint_lensblur.js:439-440`, `inpaint_relight.js:2273`, and `inpaint_surfacefx.js:209` bind `DUMMY_*` textures), any program whose sampler uniform was previously set to `s.unit` keeps pointing at `gl.TEXTURE0 + s.unit` when `v` later becomes `null`.

Tracing the exact LIFO `POOL` (`free.push` at `:404`, `free.pop` at `:373`) confirms the collision is reachable in normal workflows—and is even easier to arm than the finding states because `film.bw` (`plugins/film/filters.js:662`, registered with `chain: true` at `plugins/film/main.js:22`) defaults `structure` to `20`, so its very first render runs `BW` (`filters.js:72, 676-678`) with a blur canvas and sets `BW`'s active `u_blur` uniform to unit `5`; dragging `Structure` to `0` then passes `u_blur: null`. Concrete trace 1 (`programFinish` -> `bandFilter`, `inpaint_ed_stack.js:357-376, 465-492`, single `film.bw` layer at `structure = 0` with a Luminosity limit): in Band 1, `surfaceFromBytes` (`:465`) acquires `S1`; `BW` acquires `S2` and draws cleanly; `limitStage` (`inpaint_limit.js:18, 82, 97`) runs `LIMIT_SHADER`, whose first sampler `u_in` is unit `5`, binding `S1.tex` to `gl.TEXTURE5` and drawing into `S3`; `endScope(S3)` (`:373`) pushes `S2` (`POOL = [S2]`); `free(input)` (`:470`) pushes `S1` (`POOL = [S2, S1]`); `finally` (`:492`) pushes `S3` (`POOL = [S2, S1, S3]`). In Band 2 (same `pw x ph`), `surfaceFromBytes` pops `S3` (`POOL = [S2, S1]`), and `BW` (`u_blur: null`) calls `renderToSurface` (`:554-568`), which pops `S1` from the top of `POOL`, attaches `S1.fbo` (`S1.tex`), and calls `gl.drawArrays` while `BW`'s `u_blur` uniform is `5` and `gl.TEXTURE5` still binds `S1.tex`—raising `GL_INVALID_OPERATION` (`1282`) on Band 2 and every subsequent band. Concrete trace 2 (interactive viewport redraws in `applyFilterLayer`, `inpaint_ed_filters.js:1507-1518`): while a single `film.bw` layer on screen gets `ctx.canvas` (not a `GLSurface`) as `u_in`, any stack where a plain filter layer (`S1`) feeds a limited plain filter layer (`Curves` -> `S2`, `limitStage(S1, S2)` binds `S1.tex` to `TEXTURE5` -> `S3`, `endScope` -> `POOL = [S2]`, `releaseSurface(chain.surface)` at `:1516` -> `POOL = [S2, S1]`) followed by `film.bw` (`structure = 0`) pops `S1` in `BW` and hits `GL_INVALID_OPERATION` on every single viewport frame.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`2026-11-12`, `2026-11-07` full & external): only `filters/depth-map-texture-reuploaded-every-pass` touches `uploadSampler`, for a different reason (`rg8View` identity), so this is not `known`. Severity is calibrated from `should` down to `nice`: when `renderToSurface` sees `err !== gl.NO_ERROR` (`:565-568`), it unbinds the FBO, returns `s` to `POOL`, and returns `null`, whereupon `renderOut` (`:573-579`) falls back to `renderTiled` (`:159-203`). Note a slight inaccuracy in the finding's impact wording: `renderTiled` still runs the fragment shader on WebGL2 (into the default drawing buffer or a fresh unpooled `renderToTexture` FBO) and copies into a 2D canvas via `drawImage`, rather than running CPU per-pixel loops (a main-thread `getImageData` only occurs in `programFinish:440-443` if `BW` itself has no post-stage returning a `GLSurface`). Thus output pixels are 100% unaffected and no workflow fails; the actual user impact is console error spam plus wasted GPU-to-2D-canvas round trips when chaining.

findings.claim: `loadLutFile` and `loadPlateFile` perform async file reads, PNG encoding/uploads, and image decoding without `trackEdit`, and after awaiting they push an undo step and write `layer.lut` / `layer.plate` onto the captured `layer` reference without checking that it is still in `this.layers`. Pressing Ctrl+Z during the upload undoes the previous edit onto `this.redo`, which `pushUndo` then wipes out, and if a `layers` undo or deletion replaced or removed `layer` meanwhile, the loaded LUT or grain plate is written onto a detached object while the status bar reports success.
findings.scenario: Paint a stroke (or rename a layer), then load a large `.cube` LUT or high-resolution grain plate file onto a `Colour LUT` or `Film grain` layer and press Ctrl+Z while `"Uploading ..."` is still in flight. `historyStepNow` is not held back because neither loader uses `trackEdit`, so the earlier stroke/rename is undone onto `this.redo`. When the upload finishes, `this.pushUndo({ kind: "filter", id: layer.id, ... })` clears `this.redo` (losing the undone edit's redo), and if the undone step was a `layers` step (which clones `this.layers`) or `layer` was deleted, `layer.lut` / `layer.plate` lands on the detached `layer` object so nothing changes on screen despite `"loaded"` in the status bar.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:642-655` (`loadLutFile`) awaits `file.text()` and `uploadCanvas(...)` (lines 646-647), then calls `this.pushUndo({ kind: "filter", id: layer.id, label: "Load LUT" })` (line 648, clearing `this.redo` in `inpaint_ed_history.js:431-432`) and assigns `layer.lut = ...; layer._lutData = lut;` (lines 649-650) with no `trackEdit` and no `this.layers.includes(layer)` check. `loadPlateFile` (lines 661-676) likewise awaits `uploadBlob` and `loadImageEl` (lines 667-668) before `this.pushUndo` (line 670) and `layer.plate = ...` (line 671).
findings.fix: Wrap `loadLutFile` and `loadPlateFile` in `this.trackEdit(...)` (passing `tracked: true` to `pushUndoSnapshot`), and after the awaits verify `if (this._destroyed || !this.layers.includes(layer)) return;` before pushing undo and mutating `layer`.
findings.why:
The defect holds in the code at `f45a86cc`, with one stale line citation in the candidate's evidence (`inpaint_ed_history.js:489-490`, not `:431-432`) and severity calibrated down from `should` to `nice`.

**Call path and missing guards.** Both loaders are invoked solely from hidden `<input type="file">` `change` listeners built in `PanelsPart.buildFilterControls` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:56` calling `this.loadLutFile(layer, f)` and `:70` calling `this.loadPlateFile(layer, f)`), capturing the active `layer` object reference at render time (there are no MCP commands for loading LUTs or grain plates). In `FiltersPart.loadLutFile` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:642-659`), execution awaits `file.text()` (`:646`) and `uploadCanvas(lutToCanvas(lut), ...)` (`:647`, which awaits worker PNG encoding + SHA-256 hashing and `uploadBlob` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_upload.js:42-45`). In `FiltersPart.loadPlateFile` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:661-680`), execution awaits `uploadBlob` (`:667`) and `loadImageEl(viewUrl(ref))` (`:668`). Neither caller nor method wraps the promise in `this.trackEdit(...)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1020-1026`), `this.pointer` is null (`gestureHeld()` at `:1029-1032` is false), and neither method checks `this._destroyed`, `this.layers.includes(layer)`, `this.historyGen`, or `layer.filter` after its `await`s.

**Outcomes under concurrent undo or layer mutation.** Because `_pendingEdits` does not hold the load promise, pressing `Ctrl+Z` while `"Reading ..."` / `"Uploading ..."` is in flight runs `undoStep` -> `historyStepNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_history.js:1006, 1047-1113`) immediately, popping the previous undo step and pushing the present state onto `this.redo` (`:1100-1101`). When the upload/decode finishes:
1. If `layer` is still the live object in `this.layers` (e.g. a prior `layerrect` stroke was undone), `this.pushUndo({ kind: "filter", id: layer.id, ... })` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:648` / `:670`) calls `pushUndoSnapshot` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:480-496`), which releases and clears `this.redo` at `:489-490`, permanently discarding the undone edit's redo.
2. If the undone (or redone) step was a `"layers"`, `"turn"`, or `"canvas"` step, `applySnapshot` (`inpaint_ed_history.js:632, 694, 757`) replaces `this.layers` with fresh shallow-cloned layer objects that keep the same `id`s. `pushUndo` then looks up by `step.id` in `snapshotOf` (`:435`), snapshots the *live* layer in `this.layers`, pushes a no-op undo step, and wipes `this.redo`, while `layer.lut` / `layer._lutData` (`:649-650`) or `layer.plate` / `layer._plateImg` (`:671-672`) is written onto the detached `layer` reference. Nothing changes on screen, yet `this.setStatus` (`:654, :675`) reports `"loaded"`.
3. If `layer` was removed meanwhile, `snapshotOf` returns `null` (`:436`), the LUT/plate is written onto the detached object, and `markFilterChanged`, `renderLayers`, and `setStatus` still announce success; if `setFilterType` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:548`) retyped `layer` in place during the wait, `loadLutFile` / `loadPlateFile` still pushes the undo step and mutates `layer.lut` / `layer.plate` on the new filter type.

**Known-issues check.** Not a known entry: absent from `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `scratch/known_index.md`, and the `findings` arrays of all three `verified.json` files (`documents/D1` only mentions plates regarding mirror filename collisions; `bucket-fill-untracked-undo-race` and `inapp-cutout-lands-on-stale-layer` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` were on `bucketFill` and `cutoutLayer`, both since fixed at `inpaint_ed_shape.js:309-334` and `inpaint_ed_masks.js:109-114`; `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:502` had only a one-sentence passing note under `notes.filters` "Suspected but not proven or too small to list" about deleted/retyped layers, never recorded as a finding and missing the `trackEdit`/`redo`-wipe and `layers`-clone split).

**Severity calibration (`nice`, not `should`).** Unlike `bucketFill` (canvas click followed by up to 2 s of 15k flood) or `cutoutLayer` (5-10 s in-app model inference), `loadLutFile` and `loadPlateFile` can only start after the user picks a file in the OS modal file dialog. Locally, a typical 33³ `.cube` LUT completes in tens of milliseconds and a grain plate in a few hundred milliseconds; the window only stretches to seconds for multi-tens-of-MB grain scans or 64³/128³ LUTs when `FileMirror.handleUpload` (`electron/main/files.js:196-202`) forwards to a slow/remote ComfyUI server. Hitting `Ctrl+Z` or deleting/retyping the layer immediately after dismissing the file picker inside that upload window is a narrow async edge case that never corrupts existing canvas pixels or saved documents (matching `canvas-select/mask-from-layer-writes-detached-target` and `filters/freqsep-stale-box-after-await`, both `nice` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`).

findings.claim: `limitStage` and `limitAlphaRows` short-circuit with `if (limit.lo <= 0 && limit.hi >= 1 && !limit.invert) return out;` before checking whether `limit.source === "depth"` is missing its depth map or whether `info.limitView` is active. Widening a depth limit's handles to `0..1` when no depth map exists abruptly flips `limitMissing` off and applies the filter or fill at 100% everywhere instead of 0%, and widening any limit to `0..1` while viewing the limit mask flashes the canvas from the greyscale mask back to the colour image.
findings.scenario: Without a depth map computed, add a `Levels` or `Colour fill` layer and set `Limit` to `Depth`: at the default `0..0.5` range (and up to `0..0.99`), `limitMissing` is `true`, the UI warns `needs a depth map: compute it first`, and the layer draws nothing. Drag the upper range handle from `0.99` to `1.00`: `limitStage` returns `out` at line 59 before reaching line 60, clearing `limitMissing` and applying the full effect across the picture (and in exports). Similarly, with `limitView` active on any limit, dragging the handles to `0..1` shows the colour filtered output instead of a solid white (`1.0`) mask.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:59-63`: `if (limit.lo <= 0 && limit.hi >= 1 && !limit.invert) return out;` runs before `if (limit.source === "depth" && (!info || !info.maps || !info.maps.depth)) { if (info) info.limitMissing = true; return src; }` (which also checks `!info.maps.depth` rather than `!info.maps.depth || !info.maps.depth.data`), and before `info.limitView` is handled at line 95 / 178. `limitAlphaRows` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:215-221`) has the same order: `if (lim.lo <= 0 && lim.hi >= 1 && !lim.invert) return;` before `if (lim.source === "depth" && (!map || !map.data))`.
findings.fix: Move the missing-depth check (`!info?.maps?.depth?.data`) above the full-range shortcut in both `limitStage` and `limitAlphaRows`, and guard `limitStage`'s full-range shortcut with `!(info && info.limitView)`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js. In limitStage (lines 55-63), line 59 executes `if (limit.lo <= 0 && limit.hi >= 1 && !limit.invert) return out;` before line 60's missing-depth guard (`if (limit.source === "depth" && (!info || !info.maps || !info.maps.depth)) { if (info) info.limitMissing = true; return src; }`) and without checking `!(info && info.limitView)`. Likewise, in limitAlphaRows (lines 209-221), line 215 returns early on `if (lim.lo <= 0 && lim.hi >= 1 && !lim.invert) return;` before line 218's missing-depth zeroing loop (`if (lim.source === "depth" && (!map || !map.data)) { for (let i = 3; i < rgba.length; i += 4) rgba[i] = 0; return; }`). Both LIMIT_SHADER (lines 39-40) and limitStageCPU (lines 170-180) explicitly define missing-depth weight as `w = 0` and `limitView` (`u_view == 1` / `isView`) as opaque greyscale `vec4(vec3(w), 1.0)`.

Both scenarios are reachable with no upstream guard preventing `lo = 0, hi = 1, invert = false`: normalizeLimit / normalizeStoredLimit (inpaint_weights.js:256-306) return a valid Limit object for `0..1` (only `null`/`false`/`undefined` become `null`), and dragging the upper handle in buildRangeBar (inpaint_rangebar.js:85-88, mounted by buildLimitBlock in inpaint_ed_panels.js:471) to `x01 >= 1` produces `{ lo: 0, hi: 1, invert: false }`.

1. 'Show the effect' (`limitView`) path: Selecting 'Show the effect' in a filter/fill layer's mask menu (inpaint_ed_masks.js:397-401) sets `this.maskView = { id: layer.id, mode: "effect" }`. On screen passes, effectViewOf (inpaint_ed_depth.js:621-625) returns true; applyFilterLayer (inpaint_ed_filters.js:1486-1488) sets `limitView = true` and `plain = false`, and filteredCanvas / filterInfo (inpaint_ed_filters.js:749-751, 884) set `info.limitView = true` and `info.limitOver = true` (which also keeps line 72's `if (out === src && !over)` from short-circuiting identity filters). For any range up to `0..0.99`, limitStage returns greyscale `[v, v, v, 255]` and applyFilterLayer (lines 1574-1594) composites it over `#000000`. At `0..1` (`!invert`), line 59 returns `out`—the colour filtered output (or colour fill)—so applyFilterLayer draws the colour image over black instead of a solid white `[255, 255, 255, 255]` weight mask. This occurs for all three limit sources (`depth`, `luma`, `color`) even when a depth map exists, because R1-S10 (PLAN_NIK9_BUILD.md:2048-2050) added `info.limitView` to the shader/CPU loop without guarding R1-S7a's earlier line-59 shortcut.

2. Missing depth map path: Without `this.maps.depth`, a depth-limited filter or fill layer at `0..0.5` through `0..0.99` hits lines 60-63, sets `info.limitMissing = true` (`layer.limitMissing = true` at inpaint_ed_filters.js:890), and draws nothing on screen, in flattenToCanvas, in bandFilter (inpaint_ed_stack.js:374), or in PSD/ORA fill exports (inpaint_ed_filters.js:607, 622 -> limitAlphaRows:218). Dragging the upper handle from `0.99` to `1.00` hits line 59 (and line 215 in limitAlphaRows), leaving `info.limitMissing` unset (`layer.limitMissing` flips to `false` while the static panel note from buildLimitBlock's `mount()` still warns 'needs a depth map: compute it first') and jumping from 0% to 100% effect across screen and exports. Note that tools/limit_test.js:519-524 has a unit test asserting the current shortcut order (`limitAlphaRows(..., { source: "depth", lo: 0, hi: 1, ... }, null)` keeping alpha 255), so swapping lines 215 and 218 requires updating that test.

Checked scratch/known_index.md, docs/BUGS.md, docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, and all three verified.json files (2026-11-07 full/external and 2026-11-12 full); this defect is not listed in any of them. Severity is `nice`: `limitView` at `0..1` is a screen-only cosmetic preview glitch, and hitting exact `0..1` non-inverted on a depth limit without a depth map is a boundary handle edge case where the panel already warns that a depth map is needed and screen and export remain consistent.

findings.claim: The MCP `sample_depth` command maps document coordinates `(x, y)` into depth-map grid coordinates via `(x / ed.width) * dw` and `(y / ed.height) * dh`, ignoring `depthObj.xf`. After any crop, canvas extension, rotation, flip, or straighten — all of which update `map.xf` without resampling `map.data` — `sample_depth` samples the wrong pixel of the depth map while the shaders, range selection, and `ed.depthAt` sample the transformed map accurately.
findings.scenario: Compute a depth map on a 2000x1000 image where a foreground subject sits at `(200, 500)` (`depth` ~ 0.1) and the right side `(1800, 500)` is far background (`depth` ~ 0.95). Flip the canvas horizontally (Image > Transform > Flip Horizontal, or crop to `[1000, 0, 2000, 1000]`). `mapExtras` updates `maps.depth.xf` instead of resampling `maps.depth.data`. Calling MCP `sample_depth` at the subject's new position `(1800, 500)` indexes `(1800 / 2000) * dw` in the unflipped buffer and returns ~0.95 (`far`) instead of ~0.1 (`near`).
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:784-792` (`mapExtras`, called on turn/crop/extend/straighten at `:705`, `:854`, `:874`, `:1060`) transforms `map.xf` (`deriveMap(m, { xf: xfMul(op, mXf) })`) without modifying `map.data`. `renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:448-454` (`sampleMap`) and `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1128-1135` (`depthAt`) apply `xfInv(map.xf)` / `passToMap(map, 1)`, whereas `renderer/commands_depth.js:97-107` computes `const gx = Math.max(0, Math.min(dw - 1, Math.floor((x / ed.width) * dw))); const gy = Math.max(0, Math.min(dh - 1, Math.floor((y / ed.height) * dh)));` (and `:103-106` does the same for `meta.raw`) without consulting `depthObj.xf`.
findings.fix: Use `sampleMap(depthObj, x + 0.5, y + 0.5)` (or `ed.depthAt(x, y)`, and transform `(x + 0.5, y + 0.5)` through `xfInv(depthObj.xf)` before indexing `meta.raw` and checking out-of-map bounds after `extendCanvas`).
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, `DepthCommandsPart.sample_depth.run` in `renderer/commands_depth.js:90-122` validates `0 <= x < ed.width` and `0 <= y < ed.height` (`:93`), reads `depthObj = (ed.maps && ed.maps.depth) || ed.depth` (`:94`), and then maps `(x, y)` directly into the map grid via `gx = Math.max(0, Math.min(dw - 1, Math.floor((x / ed.width) * dw)))` and `gy = Math.max(0, Math.min(dh - 1, Math.floor((y / ed.height) * dh)))` (`:98-99`), repeating the same un-transformed `(x / ed.width) * meta.rw` and `(y / ed.height) * meta.rh` indexing for `meta.raw` (`:103-107`). Neither lookup reads `depthObj.xf`.

Tracing the document-map lifecycle confirms the scenario is reachable with no intervening guard. Depth maps are created in `computeDepthMap` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:181`), `depthFromPoints` (`:253`), and `depthFromLayer` (`:575`) via `makeMap` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:80-121`) with initial `xf = [W, 0, 0, H, 0, 0]`. As stated in `inpaint_maps.js:2`, document maps are never resampled on whole-document geometry operations: `turnDocumentNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:705`), `restoreGeometry` (`:854`), `followGeometry` (`:874`, called by `cropCanvasNow` at `:1405`, `resizeImageNow` at `:1491`, and `extendCanvasNow` at `:1674`), and `straightenDocumentNow` (`:1060`) all call `mapExtras` (`:784-792`), which updates `map.xf = snapXf(xfMul(A, map.xf))` in place while leaving `map.data` and `map.meta.raw` untouched. Other map consumers (`sampleMap` at `inpaint_maps.js:448-454` and `ed.depthAt` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1123-1139`) invert `map.xf` via `xfInv` / `passToMap(map, 1)`, whereas `commands.run("sample_depth", args)` (`renderer/commands.js:119-126`) forwards `args` straight to `sample_depth.run`. Consequently, after any flip, rotation, crop, canvas extension, or straighten, `sample_depth` indexes the un-transformed buffer and returns the wrong pixel's `depth`, `u16`, and `raw_disparity`.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, all three `verified.json` review ledgers (`2026-11-12`, `full_2026-11-07`, `external_2026-11-07`), and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: no open bug or prior finding covers `sample_depth` ignoring `map.xf`. Severity `nice` holds because `sample_depth` is a `readOnly: true` MCP/assistant query command (`commands_depth.js:84`) — all rendering, filter shaders, range selections, exports, and relight runs sample through `map.xf`, so no pixels, saves, or paid runs are affected.

findings.claim: `mapStale` states in its JSDoc that it renders `pictureInput` through `map.xf` into 64x64 to compare against `meta.fp`, but the implementation calls `host.pictureInput(this, 64, 64, ...)` on the whole current document without reading `map.xf`. Any crop, extend, quarter-turn, flip, or straighten that transforms `map.xf` therefore makes `mapStale` / `isDepthStale` falsely report the valid map as stale in the UI and MCP commands and prevents `computeSurfaceMaps` from reusing fresh surface maps.
findings.scenario: Load an asymmetric photo, compute a depth map (or surface maps), and add a Haze or Relight layer. Rotate the canvas 90 degrees clockwise or crop to half the frame. `mapExtras` updates `map.xf` so the depth and surface maps remain aligned with the picture, but `checkDepthStale` -> `isDepthStale` -> `mapStale("depth")` hashes the rotated/cropped 64x64 whole document against the pre-turn `meta.fp`, setting `_depthStale = true`: the filter panel shows `Depth: ... (stale)`, MCP `depth_map` and `sample_depth` return `stale: true`, and calling `computeSurfaceMaps()` without `recompute` re-runs the models instead of reusing the valid maps.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:1136-1155`: line `1137` comments `* Renders pictureInput through the map's xf into 64 x 64 and compares fingerprint against meta.fp.`, but lines `1146-1150` execute `const { image } = await host.pictureInput(this, 64, 64, { skipFilters: true, background: "#808080" }); const currentFp = depthFingerprint(image, 64, 64); return !fingerprintClose(map.meta.fp, currentFp);` without reading `map.xf`. Called by `isDepthStale` (`:636`) -> `checkDepthStale` (`:650`), `computeSurfaceMaps` (`:452`), and `commands_depth.js:75,120`.
findings.fix: Sample the 64x64 image grid through `map.xf` (mapping each `(u + 0.5) / 64, (v + 0.5) / 64` in map normalized coordinates into document space via `map.xf`, filling `#808080` outside `[0, width) x [0, height)`) before computing `depthFingerprint`.
findings.why:
At f45a86cc, both the architecture plan (`docs/PLAN_NIK9_BUILD.md:946-950, 993`) and the JSDoc on `mapStale(kind)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:1136-1137`) explicitly specify that map freshness must render `pictureInput` *through `map.xf`* into 64x64 so turned/flipped/cropped maps are not misreported as stale. However, `mapStale(kind)` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:1141-1155` calls `host.pictureInput(this, 64, 64, { skipFilters: true, background: "#808080" })` (`:1146`) and compares `fingerprint(inp.image, 64, 64)` against `map.meta.fp` via `fingerprintDiff(map.meta.fp, fp) >= thresh` (`:1147-1150`, `STALE_DIFF = 6` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_depth.js:8`), ignoring `map.xf` completely (`host.pictureInput` at `renderer/editor/host_helpers.js:314-333` always squashes the upright `[0, 0, W, H]` document into 64x64). The same omission exists in the inline reuse checks in `computeDepthMap` (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:79-87`), `depthFromPoints` (`:223-226`), and `computeSurfaceMaps` (`:445-448`), which compare `meta.fp === fp` against an upright 64x64 `pictureInput` without `map.xf` (note: the candidate slightly misquoted helper names as `depthFingerprint`/`fingerprintClose` instead of `fingerprint`/`fingerprintDiff` from `inpaint_maps.js:493,534`, and attributed `computeSurfaceMaps` to calling `mapStale` when it actually performs the equivalent `cur.meta.fp === fp` check inline).

Tracing the full call path confirms the defect is reachable without guards preventing it: when a depth or surface map is computed on an upright `W x H` document (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:168-181, 249-253, 462-472`), `map.xf` is `[W, 0, 0, H, 0, 0]` and `map.meta.fp` stores the pre-transform 64x64 luma fingerprint. Subsequent document geometry ops — `turnDocumentNow` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:705`), `straightenDocumentNow` (`:1060`), `cropCanvasNow` (`:1405` -> `followGeometry` `:874`), and `extendCanvasNow` (`:1674` -> `followGeometry` `:874`) — call `mapExtras(A, kind)` (`:784-792`), updating `map.xf = snapXf(xfMul(A, map.xf))` while leaving `map.data` and `map.meta.fp` intact so consumers keep sampling aligned pixels through `map.xf`. Turns/flips/straightens also call `dropCompositeCaches()` (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:701, 1054` -> `this.uploaded.baseHash = null`, bumping `this.compositeVersion` in `UploadCache` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_strokebuf.js:66-75`), invalidating `_depthStaleAt`. Consequently: (1) MCP `depth_map` with `force: false` (`renderer/commands_depth.js:59-64, 75`) awaits `ed.checkDepthStale()` (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:649-653` -> `mapStale("depth")`) and falsely reports `stale: true` on any non-symmetric rotated/flipped/cropped image; (2) MCP `sample_depth` (`commands_depth.js:120`) and the Selection › Depth UI row (`renderDepthRow` at `inpaint_ed_depth.js:632-645, 739-747`, also invoked on `.scumble`/autosave restore via `inpaint_ed_persist.js:386`; note the badge is in Selection › Depth rather than the filter layer row) falsely display `(stale)` and highlight `Recompute`; and (3) `computeDepthMap`/`computeSurfaceMaps` with `recompute: false` fail their `meta.fp === fp` fast path after a turn/flip/crop and needlessly re-run ONNX inference.

Cross-checking `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md` (`:258` assumes `mapStale` works, and `tools/maps_test.py:342-360` only tests unrotated maps) confirms this defect has not been previously recorded. Severity is `nice`: `map.xf` keeps actual depth/relight/surface rendering and sampling pixel-accurate, so the impact is limited to a false `(stale)` UI/MCP warning and redundant model recomputation after geometry transforms.

findings.claim: When Depth Anything is not downloaded and `depthFromPoints` builds a depth map from MoGe-2's `this.maps.points`, it stamps the new depth map's `meta.fp` with the current picture's fingerprint instead of `points.meta.fp` (or checking `mapStale("points")`). If the picture was edited or replaced after *Compute Surface Maps* ran, the depth map derived from the old scene's 3D points is marked fresh for the new picture, suppressing `(stale)` warnings and causing `depthFromPoints({ recompute: false })` to reuse it.
findings.scenario: With MoGe-2 + Marigold downloaded in Settings > Helpers and Depth Anything not downloaded, open photo A and run Image > Surface Maps > Compute Surface Maps (`maps.points` is stored with photo A's `fp`). Paint or paste a completely new full-canvas image layer over photo A, then add a Haze, Dehaze, or Relight layer (triggering `ensureDepthMap` -> `depthFromPoints`). `depthFromPoints` computes `fp` from the new composite, builds `depth` from photo A's stale `maps.points` (`guidedFar` snaps old points to the new guide), writes the new composite's `fp` into `depth.meta.fp`, and sets `_depthStale = false`: the UI shows no `(stale)` badge and `sample_depth` / `depth_map` report `stale: false` even though the geometry came from photo A.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:219-262`: lines `223-224` compute `const { image: fpImg } = await host.depthInput(this, 64, 64); const fp = depthFingerprint(fpImg, 64, 64);`; line `236` reads `const pm = this.maps.points;` without checking `this.mapStale("points")` or `pm.meta.fp`; line `249` writes `const meta = { fp, source: "points", model: (pm.meta && pm.meta.model) || "moge2", ... }`; and line `260` sets `this._depthStale = false;` (`pm.meta.fp` was recorded at `:463,472` when `computeSurfaceMaps` ran).
findings.fix: Stamp `meta.fp` in `depthFromPoints` from `pm.meta && pm.meta.fp` (not the current picture's `fp`), and set `this._depthStale = !!(pm.meta && pm.meta.fp && !fingerprintClose(pm.meta.fp, fp))` so a depth map built from stale `points` reports `(stale)` accurately.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:212-275. When Depth Anything V2 Small is not downloaded (`host.depthModel()` returns null at host_helpers.js:537-540) and surface maps with MoGe-2 points exist (`this.maps.points.data`), `ensureDepthMap` (:51-53) -> `computeDepthMap` (:66) delegates to `depthFromPoints({ recompute, edges })` (:212). At lines 223-224, `depthFromPoints` renders a 64x64 composite of the current picture via `host.pictureInput(this, 64, 64, { skipFilters: true, background: "#808080" })` and hashes it with `fingerprint(fpInp.image, 64, 64)` (note: the raw finding's evidence slightly paraphrases these helper names as `depthInput`/`depthFingerprint`, which are equivalent since `depthInput` at host_helpers.js:545-547 calls `pictureInput` with the exact same options, and the line numbers 223-224, 249, 260, and 463/472 match verbatim). At lines 234-236, `depthFromPoints` derives raw disparity via `disparityFromPoints` from `this.maps.points` (`pm`) and `this.maps.normals` (`nm`), without checking `pm.meta.fp` (recorded when `computeSurfaceMaps` ran at :445-446, :463, :472) or `mapStale("points")`. After running the `depth_guide` worker job against the current picture's guide (:239-243), line 249 stamps the new depth map's metadata with the current picture's `fp` (`const meta = { fp, source: "points", ... }`), and line 260 sets `this._depthStale = false`.

Tracing callers and staleness checks confirms no guard prevents this: if a user computes surface maps on picture A and then pastes/drops an opaque layer or paints over picture A (or even loads a new base picture, since `setBasePixels` at inpaint_ed_open.js:104-155 does not clear `this.maps`), adding a Relight or Light brush layer (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:346-349, 398`), clicking Compute depth map in Selection > Depth (`inpaint_ed_depth.js:711`) or Limit > Depth (`inpaint_ed_panels.js:294-301`), or calling MCP `depth_map` (`commands_depth.js:65`) builds `maps.depth` from picture A's 3D points while stamping `depth.meta.fp` with picture B's fingerprint. Consequently, `isDepthStale()` / `checkDepthStale()` (:632-653) -> `mapStale("depth")` (:1141-1155) compares `depth.meta.fp` against picture B's 64x64 fingerprint, computes `diff === 0 < STALE_DIFF`, and keeps `_depthStale = false`: `renderDepthRow()` (:739-747) omits the `(stale)` warning, MCP `depth_map` (:75) and `sample_depth` (:120) return `stale: false`, and if the user subsequently refreshes `maps.points` for picture B via `computeSurfaceMaps()`, a non-forced `ensureDepthMap()` / `depthFromPoints({ recompute: false })` hits the early return at line 226 (`existing.meta.fp === fp`) and reuses the depth map derived from picture A's points.
