findings.claim: `oraFromEntries` parses `<stack>` and `<layer>` elements with `/<(\/?)(stack|layer)\b([^>]*?)(\/?)>/g` and extracts each attribute independently with `new RegExp(`\\s${name}\\s*=\\s*("([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')`).exec(tag)`. Because Scumble's ORA writers emit `name="..."` first without escaping `'`, single-quoted `x='...'` / `src='...'` substrings inside a layer name shadow the real attributes after it; and in valid external ORA files (Krita/GIMP) a literal `>` inside `name="A > B"` truncates the tag match before `src="..."`, dropping the layer.
findings.scenario: (a) Name a layer `ref x='800'` (or `note src='none.png'`), export to `.ora`, and reopen it: `attr(tag, "x")` matches `x='800'` inside `name="ref x='800'"` instead of the real `x="0"`, shifting the layer (or dropping it as missing when `src='...'` matches). (b) Open an `.ora` from Krita or GIMP with a layer named `Fg > Bg` (`<layer name="Fg > Bg" src="data/layer0.png" .../>`, valid XML 1.0): `([^>]*?)` stops at the `>` inside `name`, `attr(tag, "src")` returns `null`, and the layer is omitted as `without a picture left out`.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_layered.js:1018-1022: `const attr = (tag, name) => { const m = new RegExp(`\\s${name}\\s*=\\s*("([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')`).exec(tag); ... };`, line 1101 `/<image\b[^>]*>/`, line 1113 `const re = /<(\/?)(stack|layer)\b([^>]*?)(\/?)>/g;`, and lines 1128-1133 reading `src`, `name`, `visibility`, `opacity`, `x`, `y`, `composite-op` via `attr`. Both ORA writers (renderer/editor/inpaint_export.js:294,313 and renderer/editor/inpaint_bands.js:404,435) escape `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` (not `'`) and write `name="..."` first on `<layer>`.
findings.fix: Match tag bodies quote-aware (`/<(\/?)(stack|layer)\b((?:[^>"']|"[^"]*"|'[^']*')*?)(\/?)>/g`, and the same for `<image>`) and tokenize all attributes of a tag in one left-to-right pass (`/([a-zA-Z_:][\w:.-]*)\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')/g`) into a dictionary.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc in `renderer/editor/inpaint_layered.js`. `oraFromEntries` (lines 1077-1151, shared by `readOra` at :1030 and `readOraBlob` at :1047) parses `<image>` with `/<image\b[^>]*>/` (:1101) and `<stack>` / `<layer>` tags with `const re = /<(\/?)(stack|layer)\b([^>]*?)(\/?)>/g;` (:1113), then extracts each attribute independently via `attr(tag, name)` (:1018-1022), which runs `new RegExp(`\\s${name}\\s*=\\s*("([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')`).exec(tag)`. There is no `DOMParser` or tokenizer pass, and no upstream caller restricts layer or group names (`renameLayerInline` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_layers.js:219-245`, `addImageLayers` at `:108`, and `set_layer` / `add_paint_layer` in `renderer/commands_layers.js:37,78` accept arbitrary strings).

Both failure modes hold end-to-end with no guard preventing them:
1. Both Scumble ORA writers — `OraWriter.layer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_export.js:294,313`, used via `exportLayerStack` / `buildLayered` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_export.js:322-326`) and `OraBandWriter.layer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_bands.js:404,435`, used on the tile/pool path via `exportLayeredBands` at `inpaint_ed_export.js:147-193`) — escape `&`, `<`, `>`, and `"` in `xmlEsc`, leaving `'` unescaped (valid XML 1.0 inside double-quoted attributes), and emit `name="..."` first on `<layer ... />`. When a layer name contains a single-quoted attribute-like substring such as `ref x='800'` or `note src='none.png'`, reopening or dropping the `.ora` (`OpenPart.readLayered` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:280` or `LayersPart.addImageLayers` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:42`) runs `attr(tag, "x")` / `attr(tag, "src")` from the start of `tag` and matches inside `name="..."` ahead of the real `x="..."` / `src="..."`, shifting the layer or dropping it at `:1136-1137` (`missing.push(name)`).
2. In XML 1.0 (`AttValue` production [10]), a literal `>` is legal inside quoted attribute values. In any external `.ora` whose `stack.xml` has an unescaped `>` inside an attribute before `src` (e.g. `<layer name="Fg > Bg" src="data/layer0.png" .../>`), `([^>]*?)` in `re` (:1113) terminates the match at the `>` inside `name`, so `attr(tag, "src")` and `attr(tag, "name")` both return `null` and `:1136-1137` skips the layer with a warning (`1 layer without a picture left out (Layer)`). On a `<stack>` tag, an unescaped `>` similarly loses attributes after `>` (or `selfClose` `/` on an empty stack, desynchronizing `groups` and `level`).

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (open and fixed sections), `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` (including `S5` on `inpaint_layered.js`), and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` (§4.7 and K20c): none record `attr` or `oraFromEntries`'s XML tag/attribute regexes. Severity is `nice`: the Scumble round-trip requires a layer name containing whitespace plus an ORA attribute assignment in single quotes (`x='...'`, `src='...'`, etc.), and in external files most ORA producers (Krita's Qt XML writer, GIMP's GMarkup, MyPaint's ElementTree) escape `>` as `>` even though XML 1.0 allows literal `>`, with any dropped layer surfaced as a `warn` status note rather than silent pixel loss.

findings.claim: When a Rust TIFF strip encode (`p.tiffStrip`) hits `PxOutOfMemory` or traps in `tiffPartJob` or `kernels.js`'s `tiffStrip`, `recovered` renews the thread's `Px` instance and the JS fallback immediately calls `pz.zlib(bytes, level)` on that fresh instance without `try / catch (recovered)`. Because `pz.zlib` requires the same wasm arena footprint (`rawLen + storedCap(rawLen) + 6` bytes) that just failed `p.tiffStrip`, it throws an unhandled `PxOutOfMemory` instead of falling back to JS `deflate(bytes)` (`CompressionStream`), aborting the TIFF export.
findings.scenario: Export a large document as TIFF (`encodeTiff` -> `tiff_part` worker jobs, or `tiffStrip` on the window when unpooled) under memory pressure where `memory.grow` for a strip's `PxArena` throws `PxOutOfMemory`. `p.tiffStrip` catches and recovers via `recovered(p, err, "tiff_part")`, which synchronously (or after `await pxSettled()` at `inpaint_worker.js:885`) installs a fresh 256 KB `Px` instance. `const pz = rustPx()` then returns that new instance and `tiffPart` invokes `pz.zlib(bytes, level)` unguarded, which immediately throws `PxOutOfMemory` again; `encodeTiff` (`inpaint_ed_export.js:241-244`) only retries `NO_PROGRAM`, so the user's save fails with `Save failed: px: out of wasm memory...` and leaves `pz.trapped` set without calling `recovered`.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:866-889`: `try { r = p.tiffStrip({ rgba, w: msg.w, rows: msg.rows, predictor: msg.predictor }, level, laps); } catch (err) { delete laps.predict; delete laps.deflate; if (!recovered(p, err, "tiff_part")) throw err; } finally { releaseIfLarge(); } ... await pxSettled(); } const pz = rustPx(); const r = await tiffPart({ rgba, w: msg.w, rows: msg.rows, predictor: msg.predictor }, (bytes) => (pz ? pz.zlib(bytes, level) : deflate(bytes)), laps);`. The identical unguarded pattern appears in `renderer/editor/px/kernels.js:1208-1223` (`tiffStrip`): `try { return p.tiffStrip(...); } catch (err) { if (!recovered(p, err, "tiff_part")) throw err; } finally { releaseIfLarge(); } ... const pz = rustPx(); return J.tiffPart(args, (bytes) => (pz ? pz.zlib(bytes, lvl) : J.deflate(bytes)), lp);` (which also omits `releaseIfLarge()` after `pz.zlib` when `setRoute("tiffStripWasm", "js")` or `setRoute("tiffPredict", "js")` routes directly to line 1221). In `renderer/editor/px/px.js:1988-2002` and `1390-1402`, both `tiffStrip` and `zlib` allocate `rawLen` plus `storedCap(rawLen)` in `this.job`, and `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_export.js:241-244` rethrows any error other than `NO_PROGRAM`.
findings.fix: Wrap the `pz.zlib(bytes, level)` compressor callback in both `inpaint_worker.js:888` (`tiffPartJob`) and `px/kernels.js:1222` (`tiffStrip`) in `try { return pz.zlib(bytes, level); } catch (err) { if (!recovered(pz, err, "zlib")) throw err; } finally { releaseIfLarge(); }` before falling back to `deflate(bytes)` / `J.deflate(bytes)`, and skip `pz` altogether when `tiffPart` was reached via OOM/trap recovery of `p.tiffStrip`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc in both `renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:887-888` (`tiffPartJob`) and `renderer/editor/px/kernels.js:1221-1222` (`tiffStrip`). In `tiffPartJob` (`inpaint_worker.js:864-889`), when `p.tiffStrip({ rgba, w: msg.w, rows: msg.rows, predictor: msg.predictor }, level, laps)` throws `PxOutOfMemory` (`px.js:245`) or traps (`WebAssembly.RuntimeError` / `RangeError` via `trapMark` at `px.js:152-155`), line 871 calls `recovered(p, err, "tiff_part")` (`kernels.js:342-352`), which logs that the JS kernel ran and calls `renew(why, p)` (`kernels.js:237-265`). `renew` synchronously instantiates a fresh `Px` (`PX = new Px(new WebAssembly.Instance(module, {}), module)` at `kernels.js:243`, or asynchronously into `PENDING`, which `await pxSettled()` at `inpaint_worker.js:885` resolves). Immediately afterward, `const pz = rustPx()` at line 887 returns that newly renewed `Px` instance rather than `null`, and line 888 passes `(bytes) => (pz ? pz.zlib(bytes, level) : deflate(bytes))` into `tiffPart` (`inpaint_tiff.js:1407-1424`) with no `try / catch (recovered)` fallback to `deflate(bytes)` (`CompressionStream("deflate")` at `kernels_js.js:1111-1114`). Because `Px.prototype.zlib` (`px.js:1382-1403`) allocates the same `rawLen` + `storedCap(rawLen)` arena blocks and calls the same `adler32` and `deflate_part` exports as `Px.prototype.tiffStrip` (`px.js:1988-2047`), any persistent OOM or input-triggered trap in `p.tiffStrip` immediately throws unhandled from `pz.zlib`. (One minor detail in the candidate's scenario: `PxOutOfMemory` from `alloc` only leaves `pz.trapped` set if `_reset(a)` at `px.js:313-319` also hits `PxOutOfMemory` while coalescing `a.chunks.length > 1`; a wasm trap always sets `pz.trapped`.) The error is serialized as `{ ok: false, error }` (`inpaint_worker.js:2081-2085`), `encodeTiff` (`inpaint_ed_export.js:241-244`) only retries `NO_PROGRAM`, and `exportImage` (`inpaint_ed_export.js:340-344`) fails the user's save instead of using `deflate(bytes)`. The identical unguarded pattern exists in `kernels.js:1208-1223` (`tiffStrip`), which additionally omits `releaseIfLarge()` after `pz.zlib` when `setRoute("tiffStripWasm", "js")` or `setRoute("tiffPredict", "js")` bypasses `p` at line 1209. Existing test `tools/px_test.js:12857-12863` missed this because it monkey-patched `p0.tiffStrip` only on the pre-renewal instance.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` (`P2`, `S9b`), and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` (§4.6, K15, K17-K19): this defect is not recorded in any known or open list.

Severity is downgraded from `should` to `nice` because the failure path is a narrow edge case rather than reachable in normal or plausible user workflows. Every production TIFF export (`encodeTiff` -> `writeTiff` at `inpaint_bands.js:184-187`) sizes strips via `tiffStripRows(source.width)` (`inpaint_tiff.js:1376-1383`), capping `rawLen = w * rows * 4` at `TIFF_STRIP_BYTES = 8 MiB` (e.g. 7.32 MiB at 15,000 px wide, 256 KiB at 65,535 px wide), while `kernels.js`'s `tiffStrip` has zero production callers (`inpaint_ed_export.js:238` calls `tiffPart(args, deflate)` directly when unpooled). Each worker has its own 4 GiB wasm32 address space trimmed by `releaseMB = 256` MB and `keepMB = 16` MB, and even if `partPtrOf` / `tiffStripFromPtr` (`inpaint_worker.js:835-837`) OOMs on a deep layer stack, `recovered` replaces `p` with a fresh ~1 MB instance before `p.tiffStrip` runs (and `recovered` after `p.tiffStrip` likewise frees any prior instance growth before `pz.zlib` runs). Thus `pz.zlib` can only fail in production if the OS/renderer process has under ~17 MiB (`8 MiB` + `storedCap(8 MiB)` + ~320 KiB `CompressorOxide`) of committable memory left across the process, or under developer-only `setRoute` overrides.

findings.claim: `Px.prototype.limitAlphaRows` and `Px.prototype.rangeTilesRgba` explicitly accept raw `ArrayBuffer` and `SharedArrayBuffer` inputs, but `kernels.js` mid-call OOM/trap recovery (`done > 0`) and the JS twins in `kernels_js.js` do not, causing `TypeError` or spurious `'short rgba'` rejections on fallback.
findings.scenario: 1) Call `limitAlphaRows` (`px/kernels.js:1249`) with `h > 256` and `rgba` (or `col`) passed as a raw `ArrayBuffer` or `SharedArrayBuffer`. Chunk `cy = 0` succeeds in `p.limitAlphaRows` (mutating rows `0..255` in place) and chunk `cy = 256` throws `PxOutOfMemory` with `err.doneRows = 256` (`px.js:2162`). `kernels.js:1262` executes `new Uint8Array(rgba.buffer, rgba.byteOffset + off, ...)`, where `rgba.buffer` and `rgba.byteOffset` are `undefined`, throwing `TypeError` with `rgba` left half-mutated. 2) Under `setKernels("js")`, `setRoute(..., "js")`, or wasm load failure, passing a raw `SharedArrayBuffer` to `limitAlphaRows` (`rgba`, `col`, or `guide`) throws `Error("limitAlphaRows: short rgba/col/guide")`, and passing a raw `ArrayBuffer` or `SharedArrayBuffer` to `rangeTilesRgba` throws `TypeError` in `bytesOf(rgba)`.
findings.evidence: `renderer/editor/px/px.js:2060-2066` (and `2072-2078` for `col`, `2105-2111` for `gRaw`) accepts `(rgba instanceof ArrayBuffer || (SAB && rgba instanceof SAB)) ? new Uint8Array(rgba)` and sets `if (cy > 0 && err && typeof err === "object") err.doneRows = cy;` at `px.js:2162`. In `renderer/editor/px/kernels.js:1260-1265`: `if (done > 0 && done < h) { const off = done * w * 4; const subRgba = new Uint8Array(rgba.buffer, rgba.byteOffset + off, (h - done) * w * 4); const subCol = col ? new Uint8Array(col.buffer, col.byteOffset + off, (h - done) * w * 4) : null; ... }`. In `renderer/editor/px/kernels_js.js:3023-3025` (and `3031-3033`, `3061-3063`): `const u8 = ArrayBuffer.isView(rgba) ? bytesOf(rgba) : (rgba instanceof ArrayBuffer ? new Uint8Array(rgba) : null);` omits `SharedArrayBuffer`. In `renderer/editor/px/kernels_js.js:2901` (`rangeTilesRgba`): `const u8 = bytesOf(rgba);` (`new Uint8Array(a.buffer, a.byteOffset, a.byteLength)` at line `45`), whereas `px.js:1757-1763` accepts both `ArrayBuffer` and `SharedArrayBuffer`.
findings.fix: Normalize raw `ArrayBuffer` and `SharedArrayBuffer` inputs with a shared helper (e.g. `toBytesView`) in `kernels.js:1261-1263`, `kernels_js.js:2901` (`rangeTilesRgba`), and `kernels_js.js:3023-3063` (`limitAlphaRows`) so Rust, mid-call recovery, and JS twins accept the exact same buffer types.
findings.why:
The contract drift across `px.js`, `kernels.js`, and `kernels_js.js` holds in the code at `f45a86cc`, with one minor ECMAScript correction on the thrown error type and with no current production caller passing raw buffers.

In `renderer/editor/px/px.js`, `Px.prototype.limitAlphaRows` explicitly normalizes raw `ArrayBuffer` and `SharedArrayBuffer` inputs for `rgba` (`px.js:2060-2066`), `col` (`px.js:2072-2078`), and `gRaw` (`px.js:2105-2111`) via `(x instanceof ArrayBuffer || (SAB && x instanceof SAB)) ? new Uint8Array(x) : null` (`SAB` at `px.js:73`), and `Px.prototype.rangeTilesRgba` does the same for `rgba` (`px.js:1757-1763`). `Px.prototype.limitAlphaRows` runs in chunks of `ROW_CHUNK = 256` (`px.js:2114`), writing rows into `u8` in place (`px.js:2158`), and sets `err.doneRows = cy` if a chunk `cy > 0` (`h > 256`) fails (`px.js:2162`). In `renderer/editor/px/kernels.js:1260-1265`, when `recovered(p, err, "limit_alpha_rows")` catches an OOM or wasm trap with `done > 0 && done < h`, lines 1262-1263 construct `new Uint8Array(rgba.buffer, rgba.byteOffset + off, (h - done) * w * 4)` (and similarly for `col`). For a raw `ArrayBuffer` or `SharedArrayBuffer`, `rgba.buffer` and `rgba.byteOffset` are `undefined`. Per ECMA-262 §23.2.5.1, `new Uint8Array(undefined, NaN, len)` does not throw `TypeError` — because the first argument is not an Object, it coerces `ToIndex(undefined) === 0` and ignores the remaining arguments, returning a zero-length `Uint8Array(0)`. That `Uint8Array(0)` then trips `J.limitAlphaRows`'s length check at `renderer/editor/px/kernels_js.js:3027` (`u8.length < needBytes`) and throws `Error("limitAlphaRows: short rgba")` (or `"short col"` at `3035`), aborting recovery with rows `0..done-1` already mutated in place. Likewise, in `kernels_js.js:3023-3025`, `3031-3033`, and `3061-3063`, `limitAlphaRows` accepts `ArrayBuffer.isView(...)` and `instanceof ArrayBuffer` but omits `SharedArrayBuffer` (throwing `"short rgba"` / `"short col"` / `"short guide"`), and in `kernels_js.js:2901`, `rangeTilesRgba` calls `bytesOf(rgba)` (`kernels_js.js:45`), which turns a raw `ArrayBuffer` or `SharedArrayBuffer` into `Uint8Array(0)` and throws `Error("rangeTilesRgba: short rgba")` at line 2902.

Tracing every caller in Scumble shows this is latent in production workflows today. `limitAlphaRows` from `px/kernels.js` is imported in production only by `renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:13` (`limitAlphaRowsKernel`, called at line 259). Before reaching the kernel, `inpaint_limit.js:239-241` checks `rgba.length >= w * h * 4 && (!col || col.length >= w * h * 4) && (!gRaw || (gw === map.w && gh === map.h && gRaw.length >= map.w * map.h * 4))`, which is `false` for raw `ArrayBuffer`/`SharedArrayBuffer` (`.length` is `undefined`). Its only callers, `fillLayerCanvas` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:607`) and `fillLayerRows` (`inpaint_ed_filters.js:622`), pass `rows = fillPixels(...)` (`Uint8ClampedArray`, `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:571`), `col = null`, and `depthMap.guide` (`Uint8Array` over `ArrayBuffer` or `SharedArrayBuffer` from `makeMap`/`deriveMap` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_maps.js:88-100, 269-275`). `rangeTilesRgba` is imported in production only by `renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:69`, where `rangeSelectJob` (`inpaint_worker.js:1780-1786`) wraps `msg.sab || msg.buffer` in `new Uint8Array(...)` at line 1780 before calling `rangeTilesRgba`.

Not a known entry: checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` (K23/K25). Severity is `nice`: `px.js` and `kernels_js.js` explicitly coded raw-buffer normalization for these K23/K25 kernels and drifted against `kernels.js`'s twin/recovery contract (`kernels.js:1-4, 23-25`), but no current editor, worker, or export path passes raw buffers.

findings.claim: Unlike `queueGenerate` (which snapshots `rows` via `entry.target` and runs `missingFilesRefusal` before its first await), `runComfyUpscale` renders, PNG-encodes, and uploads the full base image before checking `missingFilesRefusal`, and then passes live `editor.settings` to `comfyprompt.wholePicturePrompt`, which writes `settings[String(s.index)].value` by numeric index without checking `entry.target`. Switching recipes during the base upload (or running on a `.scumble` document restored with another recipe's `editor.settings`) bypasses or misfires `missingSettingFiles` and injects another recipe's setting 1 value into the upscale graph.
findings.scenario: 1) Start a whole-picture ComfyUI upscale (`upscale_model_local` or `rtx_vsr_local`) on a large image (or over a slow remote RunPod upload) and switch to another tab's recipe (e.g. `flux2_klein_local`) before `uploadInput` finishes: `r !== this.recipe` causes `missingSettingFiles(editor, r)` to return `[]`, `setRecipe` has already rewritten `editor.settings['1']` to `flux-2-klein-base-9b.safetensors`, and `wholePicturePrompt` writes that UNet filename into `UpscaleModelLoader.inputs.model_name` (or `RTXVideoSuperResolution.inputs.quality`), failing `/prompt` after the full image was already encoded and uploaded. 2) Open a `.scumble` file saved under `flux2_klein_local` while `rtx_vsr_local` is selected (`keepRecipeMode` does not re-run `settingsChanged`) and run whole-picture upscale: `editor.settings['1']` still has `target: 'flux2_klein_local/unet:unet_name'`, which `wholePicturePrompt` and `missingSettingFiles` read blindly for `rtx_vsr_local`'s setting 1.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/host_upscale.js:274 captures `const r = this.recipe;`, awaits `canvasBytes(c)` (line 316) and `this.uploadInput(...)` (lines 320-331), and only then runs `const lacks = this.missingFilesRefusal(editor, r);` (line 333) and `const prompt = comfyprompt.wholePicturePrompt(r, ref, factor, editor.settings);` (line 336). In renderer/editor/host_presets.js:524-538, `missingSettingFiles(editor, r = this.recipe)` starts with `if (!r || r !== this.recipe || !r.prompt || !editor || !editor.settings) return [];` and loops `const entry = editor.settings[String(t.index)];` without checking `entry.target === t.key`. In renderer/editor/comfyprompt.js:96-101, `wholePicturePrompt` writes `const entry = settings ? settings[String(s.index)] : undefined; ... if (entry && entry.value != null && node && node.inputs) node.inputs[s.input] = entry.value;` with no `entry.target === `${r.id}/${s.node}:${s.input}`` check (compare renderer/editor/host_queue.js:84-88 `rowValues` and `missingFilesRefusal` before the first await).
findings.fix: In `runComfyUpscale`, run `this.missingFilesRefusal(editor, r)` and snapshot `editor.settings` (filtering entries where `!entry.target || entry.target === `${r.id}/${s.node}:${s.input}``) synchronously before `canvasBytes(c)` / `uploadInput`. Also check `!entry.target || entry.target === `${r.id}/${s.node}:${s.input}`` in `wholePicturePrompt` and `!entry.target || entry.target === t.key` in `missingSettingFiles`.
findings.why:
The code defects hold at commit f45a86cc, though Scenario 2 is blocked in the UI Upscale dialog and the practical impact calibrates to `nice` rather than `should`.

findings.claim: While `runComfyUpscale`, `realismWhole`, and `runSplitLayers` track tab removal via `gone()` and abort landing if the tab was closed, `runUpscale` (both `scope: 'document'` and `scope: 'selection'`), `runProvider`, and `runGenerate` perform no closed-tab check before landing results. Closing a tab right as `providerEdit` resolves (or while `finishResultAsync` / `bytesToImage` / `uploadResult` runs) causes the run to execute `resizeImage` / `addResults` / `setBaseFromCanvas` on an already-destroyed editor, leaking WASM tile arena stores for the rest of the session, writing unreferenced PNGs into the local mirror, and firing `host.changed` / `saveAll` for a dead tab.
findings.scenario: Start a whole-picture API upscale (`runUpscale` with `scope: 'document'`), an API edit (`runProvider`), or `Generate new` (`runGenerate`), and close the tab (confirming 'close anyway') just as the provider HTTP response arrives or while `bytesToImage` / `finishResultAsync` / `wholeLandingRefusal`'s busy-wait is running. `closeDocument` calls `host.removeEditor(ed)` and `ed.destroy()`, releasing the editor's tile stores; `runUpscale` line 187 then calls `landWholePicture` without `gone` (so `gone` defaults to `() => false`), running `resizeImageNow` on the destroyed editor, allocating new `TilePixels`, `TileMask`, and undo snapshot stores that are never freed, uploading an orphaned base PNG to `%APPDATA%/Scumble/files/`, and emitting `geometry` and `changed` events.
findings.evidence: renderer/editor/host_upscale.js:187 calls `const land = await this.landWholePicture(editor, res.bytes, res.mime, { label, seconds: res.seconds, W, H, note: texts.note });` without passing `gone` (contrast `runComfyUpscale` at host_upscale.js:300-301, 346-347 `const gone = () => closed || !this._editors.includes(editor); if (gone()) return ...; await this.landWholePicture(..., { ..., gone });`). In `landWholePicture` (host_upscale.js:205, 219) and `wholeLandingRefusal` (host_upscale.js:242-246), `gone` defaults to `() => false`, so `await editor.resizeImage(nw, nh, { base: nb })` (renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:1419-1495) runs after `editor.destroy()`, allocating `this.pixels.Layer.fromCanvas(nb)`, `this.pixels.Mask.fromCanvas(sel)`, and `this.snapshot({ kind: 'canvas' })`, uploading via `uploadCanvas`, and calling `this.notifyChanged()`. Likewise renderer/editor/host_upscale.js:174-179, renderer/editor/host_provider.js:395-401, and renderer/editor/host_generate.js:114-120 call `uploadResult` + `editor.addResults` / `editor.setBaseFromCanvas` with no `!this._editors.includes(editor)` or `editor._destroyed` guard.
findings.fix: Define `const gone = () => editor._destroyed || !this._editors.includes(editor);` in `runUpscale`, `runProvider`, and `runGenerate`; pass `gone` into `landWholePicture` in `runUpscale`, and check `if (gone()) return ...;` before `uploadResult`, `addResults`, and `setBaseFromCanvas` (and after `finishResultAsync` / `bytesToImage`).
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, the missing closed-tab guard on the post-answer landing path of API runs is real across all three methods cited. In `renderer/editor/host_upscale.js:187`, `runUpscale` (`scope: 'document'`) calls `this.landWholePicture(editor, res.bytes, res.mime, { label, seconds: res.seconds, W, H, note: texts.note })` without passing `gone`, so `landWholePicture` (`host_upscale.js:205, 219`) and `wholeLandingRefusal` (`host_upscale.js:242-246`) fall back to the default `gone = () => false` instead of returning `'the document was closed; nothing was changed.'` — in direct contrast to `runComfyUpscale` (`host_upscale.js:300-301, 346-347`), `realismWhole` (`renderer/editor/host_pictures.js:487, 519, 530-531, 550`), and `runSplitLayers` (`renderer/editor/splitlayers.js:414, 442-443`), which all check `!this._editors.includes(editor)` via `gone()` and abort landing. Likewise, `runUpscale` with `scope: 'selection'` (`host_upscale.js:174-179`), `runProvider` (`renderer/editor/host_provider.js:395-401`), and `runGenerate` (`renderer/editor/host_generate.js:114-128`) run `finishResultAsync` / `bytesToImage`, `uploadResult`, and `editor.addResults` / `editor.setBaseFromCanvas` / `this.changed(editor, { geometry })` with no check on `editor._destroyed` or `this._editors.includes(editor)`.

Checking `closeDocument` (`renderer/shell.js:296-335`) and `removeEditor` (`renderer/editor/host_state.js:228-257`) shows that closing a tab *while* `providerEdit` is still awaiting IPC does stop the run cleanly: `host.removeEditor(editor)` (`host_state.js:236`) calls `this.cancelRuns(editor)` (`host_generate.js:328-336`), which invokes `window.scumble.providers.cancel(t.runId)` and aborts the `AbortController` in `electron/main/providers/index.js:191-200, 315, 320-332`, causing `providerEdit` (`renderer/editor/host_util.js:378-389`) to throw into the `catch` block before any landing code executes. However, as soon as `providerEdit` resolves, the `finally` block (`host_upscale.js:163`, `host_provider.js:388`, `host_generate.js:109`) calls `this.endRunRow(token)`, deleting `token` from `this._providerRuns` while keeping `editor.providerPending = token` during landing. If `closeDocument` runs (or resumes past its confirmation dialog at `shell.js:312, 316`, or via `close_document` with `force: true` at `renderer/commands_docs.js:84`) during `finishResultAsync` / `bytesToImage` / `wholeLandingRefusal` / `uploadResult`, `cancelRuns(editor)` finds nothing in `_providerRuns`, `rememberClosed(editor)` (`renderer/editor/host_documents.js:334-352`) either finishes quickly (immediately for an empty tab in `runGenerate` or when `remember: false`) so `editor.destroy()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:1599-1616`) runs before `resizeImageNow` / `addResults` / `setBaseFromCanvas`, or if `rememberClosed` is still awaiting `flushEditor` on dirty layers, its second `capture()` (`host_documents.js:349-351`) records the landed result/resized/replaced base into `Reopen Closed Tab` despite the close dialog and `close_document` promising that closing stops the run and nothing lands.

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`): related entries (`shell/gen-new-closes-tab-of-running-local-render`, `shell/close-document-reentry-after-busy-question`, `shell/F5`, `host/H-1`, `main/MAIN-2`) cover distinct defects, so this is not `known`.

Severity is calibrated to `nice` rather than `should`. First, the window is a narrow post-`providerEdit` race (~0.1–2 s during decode/stitch/upload, versus 5–120 s in `providerEdit` where `cancelRuns` already aborts cleanly; UI `closeDocument` also cancels `_docSaving` at `shell.js:323`, so `wholeLandingRefusal` does not spin on a save there). Second, the candidate's main memory-leak claim — 'leaking WASM tile arena stores for the rest of the session' — does not hold on the default tile backend: tile bytes live in JS `SharedArrayBuffer` chunks in `renderer/editor/inpaint_arena.js:9-13, 110-133` (not WASM linear memory) and are reclaimed automatically via `FinalizationRegistry` once the async function finishes and the detached `editor` becomes unreachable (`editor.destroy()` never frees `layers`/`base`/`sel` tiles manually anyway, `autoNameLayer` guards `editor._destroyed` at `host_vlm.js:135`, and `areasSoon` guards `!host.editors().includes(editor)` at `eacharea.js:325`). The actual effects are transient wasted CPU/arena work, an unreferenced PNG uploaded to the local mirror (cleanable via Settings > Local files > Clean up), a redundant `saveAll()` / `geometry` / `changed` emission for a removed editor, a leaked selection `blob:` URL only on the non-default canvas backend (`tileMode === false`, where `snapUrl` runs after `destroy()`'s `clearUndo()`), and the narrow `rememberClosed` capture race.

findings.claim: 0.1.57 fixed `brushes.readIndex()` to rethrow non-`ENOENT` errors on `brushes.json`, but `brushes.list()` still catches and ignores every error when reading each `<id>.png` tip file. A transient `EBUSY`/`EPERM`/`EACCES` on a tip PNG at startup silently omits that tip without rejecting `list()`, so `brushTipsUnread` stays unset and the next `brushes.save()` permanently unlinks the tip's PNG and removes it from `brushes.json`.
findings.scenario: The user has imported `.abr` brush tips under `<userData>/brushes/`. At startup, an antivirus scan, backup tool, or sync client briefly holds `<id>.png` open while `host.loadBrushTips()` calls `window.scumble.brushes.list()`. `readIndex()` succeeds, `fsp.readFile(path.join(dir(), t.id + ".png"))` throws `EBUSY`, and `list()` swallows it and returns the remaining tips. Because `list()` resolved, `host.brushTipsUnread` is not set. When the user later imports, renames, or deletes any brush tip, `brushes.save()` unlinks every `<id>.png` not in `keep` and rewrites `brushes.json` without the locked tip, deleting it permanently.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/brushes.js:51-57`: `for (const t of await readIndex()) { if (!t || !SAFE_ID.test(String(t.id))) continue; try { const data = await fsp.readFile(path.join(dir(), t.id + ".png")); out.push(...); } catch (_) { /* the file is gone: drop the entry */ } }`. Unlike `readIndex()` (`brushes.js:29-31`: `if (err && err.code === "ENOENT") return fromFiles(d); throw err;`), line 56 catches all error codes. In `renderer/editor/host_generate.js:167,215`, `this.brushTipsUnread = true` is only set when `brushes.list()` rejects. `electron/main/brushes.js:76-79` then runs `if (m && !keep.has(m[1])) await fsp.unlink(path.join(d, f)).catch(() => {});` and rewrites `brushes.json` (lines 81-84).
findings.fix: In `brushes.js` `list()` (line 56), ignore only `err && err.code === "ENOENT"` and rethrow any other read error (optionally after short `EBUSY`/`EPERM`/`EACCES` retries, and use `renameRetry` on line 84), so `list()` rejects and `host.brushTipsUnread` blocks `saveBrushTips` for the session.
findings.why:
The code path and line numbers hold at f45a86cc. In `electron/main/brushes.js:49-59`, `list()` iterates `await readIndex()` and reads each tip file with `await fsp.readFile(path.join(dir(), t.id + ".png"))` (line 54), catching every error at line 56 with `} catch (_) { /* the file is gone: drop the entry */ }`. Unlike `readIndex()` (`brushes.js:29-31`) and `fromFiles()` (`brushes.js:44`), which check `err && err.code === "ENOENT"` and rethrow any other filesystem error, `list()` swallows `EBUSY`, `EPERM`, `EACCES`, and I/O errors on individual `<id>.png` files and resolves normally with the remaining tips. At startup, `renderer/shell.js:1487` calls `host.loadBrushTips()` (`renderer/editor/host_generate.js:164-185`) via `preload.js:196` -> `electron/main/main.js:1385`. Because `window.scumble.brushes.list()` resolves without throwing, `this.brushTipsUnread = true` (`host_generate.js:167`) is not set, so `_saveBrushTipsNow()`'s guard at `host_generate.js:215` does not block persistence.

When the user later triggers `brushTipsChanged()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_tips.js:70-72`)—by importing tips (`inpaint_ed_tips.js:125`), removing a tip (`inpaint_ed_tips.js:64`), or changing a tip's spacing (`renderer/editor/inpaint_modal.js:181`; note there is no tip-rename action as casually mentioned in the scenario)—`saveBrushTips()` calls `brushes.save(tips)` (`brushes.js:65-86`). `save()` builds `keep` solely from the renderer's `brushLibrary`, unlinks every `/^([a-z0-9]+)\.png$/i` not in `keep` (`brushes.js:76-79`), and atomically replaces `brushes.json` (`brushes.js:81-84`). Even if `<id>.png` is still locked during `save()` so `fsp.unlink` fails, rewriting `brushes.json` without `t.id` permanently drops its metadata and orphans the PNG for deletion on a subsequent save.

Checked against known-issue lists: `docs/BUGS.md` and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md` have no brush-tip entries. `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:358-372` (`main-docs/brush-index-read-failure-deletes-tips`) covered `readIndex()` swallowing errors and non-atomic writes of `brushes.json`, and its verifier note (`:371`) mentioned in passing that `list()` also drops entries on any PNG read failure. However, that 2026-11-12 finding was closed as fixed in 0.1.56 (`CHANGELOG.md:95`, not 0.1.57 as the claim states), and the 0.1.56 fix updated `readIndex()`, `fromFiles()`, and `save()` while leaving `list()` line 56 unfixed. Per the verification rules, a remaining hole in a 2026-11-12..16 fix is confirmed rather than `known`.

Severity is calibrated down from `should` to `nice`. Unlike `brushes.json` before 0.1.56 (which was rewritten non-atomically and wiped the entire library on a damaged or locked index), `<userData>/brushes/<id>.png` files are immutable once written on import, and `fsp.readFile` opens them read-only (`GENERIC_READ` with `FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE` on Windows), which normal antivirus/indexer scans do not block. Hitting this requires an exclusive read-denying lock or `EACCES` on `<id>.png` during startup right after `brushes.json` in the same folder read cleanly, followed by a brush-library edit in the same session, and at worst loses a single re-importable brush tip rather than user document pixels (matching `host-gen/brush-tip-saves-race` at `nice` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json:680`).

findings.claim: When `ensureOnServer` uploads a file without a `~<sha256>` suffix (`overwrite: false`) because a different-sized file with the same name already exists on ComfyUI, ComfyUI saves it under a new collision name (`serverName !== ref.filename`), and `ensureOnServer` records that mapping only in the per-call `report.renamed` object and not on `FileMirror`. Because `rewriteStateRefs` only updates that single run's `canvas_state` JSON, every subsequent local run misses `known`, fails the `HEAD /view` size check on the original name again, re-uploads the full PNG, and writes another numbered duplicate onto ComfyUI.
findings.scenario: A user opens a `.scumble` document saved before 0.1.57 (whose 15k `base` is `image.png`), or a `.scumble` whose `photo~1a2b3c4d.png` collided on open and was renamed to `photo~1a2b3c4d (1).png` by `docfile.freeName`, or has any layer/mask uploaded as `n1_layer_<hash>.png` (`_` rather than `~`), while ComfyUI's `input/inpaint_canvas/` already holds a different-sized file under that name. On the first local Generate, `ensureOnServer` uploads the 150 MB PNG with `overwrite: false`; ComfyUI stores `image (1).png` and the run succeeds. On the second, third, and every later Generate click in that session, `ensureOnServer` still checks `HEAD /view` for `image.png`, sees the size mismatch, reads and uploads the entire 150 MB PNG again, and creates `image (2).png`, `image (3).png`, ... on ComfyUI.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/files.js:14,65-72`: `HASH_NAME = /~([0-9a-f]{8,64})(?:\.[a-z0-9]+)?$/i` returns `false` for pre-0.1.57 plain names, `docfile.js:686` collision imports (`${stem} (${n})${ext}`), and `renderer/editor/inpaint_upload.js:44,50` (`${prefix}_${hash}.png`). In `electron/main/files.js:337-359`: `HEAD /view` compares `Number(len) === st.size` (`onServer = false`), `pushToServer(..., { overwrite: proven })` sends `overwrite: false`, and lines 353-358 do `if (serverName && serverName !== ref.filename) { report.renamed[k] = serverName; ref.filename = serverName; } else { known.add(k); }`. `ref` is a deserialized IPC copy (`main.js:1243`), and `renderer/editor/host_queue.js:197-198,348-360` only rewrites the transient `state` string for that one prompt.
findings.fix: Keep a per-server `renamed` `Map` (`serverUrl -> Map<mirrorKey, { serverName, size }>`) alongside `this.known` in `FileMirror` (cleared on `prune`), and on later `ensureOnServer` calls verify/reuse the mapped `serverName` (via `known` or `HEAD /view` on `serverName` against `st.size`) and populate `report.renamed[k] = serverName` without re-uploading.
findings.why:
Confirmed in the code at `f45a86cc`, downgraded from `should` to `nice`.

**Call path and exact lines.** `FileMirror` (`electron/main/files.js:153-168`) caches server presence only in `this.known` (`Map<serverUrl, Set<mirrorKey>>`, cleared on `prune` at line 397). In `FileMirror.ensureOnServer(refs)` (`electron/main/files.js:317-362`), line 325 checks `if (report.renamed[k]) { ref.filename = report.renamed[k]; continue; }` against the per-call `report` object only, and line 326 checks `if (known.has(k)) continue;`. When `k` is not in `known`, lines 334-346 send `HEAD /view` for `ref.filename` and require `Number(len) === st.size` (line 343). If ComfyUI already holds a different-sized file under `ref.filename`, `onServer` is `false`; lines 350-352 read the mirror file `buf = await fsp.readFile(local)`, compute `const proven = hasContentHash(ref.filename, buf)` (`HASH_NAME = /~([0-9a-f]{8,64})(?:\.[a-z0-9]+)?$/i` at line 14; `hasContentHash` at lines 65-72), and call `this.pushToServer(type, subfolder, ref.filename, buf, undefined, { overwrite: proven })`. When `proven` is `false`, `pushToServer` / `pushLargeToServer` (`files.js:241,259`) upload with `overwrite=false`, ComfyUI saves the collision under a new name (`serverName !== ref.filename`, e.g. `image (1).png`), neither `pushToServer` (line 254) nor `ensureOnServer` (lines 353-358) adds `k` to `known`, and `report.renamed[k] = serverName` is returned without storing any `k -> serverName` mapping on `FileMirror`.

**Renderer callers and guards checked.** `ipcMain.handle("comfy:ensure", (_e, refs) => mirror.ensureOnServer(refs))` (`electron/main/main.js:1243`, via `electron/preload.js:71` and `renderer/editor/host_generate.js:552-554`) operates on a structured-cloned IPC copy, so `ref.filename = serverName` at `files.js:355` only deduplicates repeated entries within that single `refs` array. In `HostQueuePart.ensureOnServer` (`renderer/editor/host_queue.js:368-379`), `stateRefs` (`lines 336-344`) builds fresh `{ filename, subfolder, type }` objects from `stateJson`, and `rewriteStateRefs` (`lines 348-362`) only rewrites the transient `state` string used by `queueGenerate` (`lines 197-198`) for that one prompt; `SegmentPart.segmentSource` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_segment.js:132-144`) similarly updates only its local `sent` object. Neither `editor.base.ref`, `editor.uploaded.baseRef`, nor `layer.ref` can be overwritten with `serverName` because the local mirror file still lives at the original `ref.filename`.

**Narrowing of the reviewer's sub-cases and severity calibration.** Every run still succeeds and crops the right pixels, so there is no data or pixel loss (`must` ruled out). Moreover, two of the reviewer's three trigger examples are near-unreachable in practice: (1) all new `overwrite: false` uploads in 0.1.57 go through `storeMirrorFile` (`files.js:129-151`) and receive a `~<sha256>` suffix (`contentName`, lines 75-85), so `docfile.freeName` (`electron/main/docfile.js:686`, `${stem} (${n})${ext}`) only strips `HASH_NAME` on a 32-bit SHA-256 stem collision in the local mirror combined with a second name+size mismatch on ComfyUI; (2) `uploadCanvas` / `uploadPixels` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_upload.js:44,50`) name files `${prefix}_${hash}.png` with a 48-bit SHA-1 of the PNG (`renderer/editor/inpaint_encode.js:47`) and upload with `overwrite = true` (`inpaint_upload.js:16`), which `handleUpload` / `handleRawUpload` (`files.js:198,227`) already push with `overwrite: true` and add to `known` when connected, and even if uploaded offline will not collide with a different-sized file on ComfyUI absent a truncated server write or 48-bit SHA-1 collision. Even on a pre-0.1.57 `.scumble` or `autosave.json` with a plain `base` like `image.png`, once the first `Generate` lands a visible result layer, `serializeForPrompt` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_persist.js:415-420`) switches to `uploadComposite` (`n<id>_base_<sha1>.png`) instead of `this.base.ref`, so repeated re-uploads happen only for an untouched pre-0.1.57 `reference` layer (`inpaint_ed_persist.js:452`) or repeated bare-base runs (`Each area`, undo/hide result + retry, or `segmentSource` + `Generate`). Because the impact is strictly redundant uploads and duplicate numbered files in ComfyUI's `input/inpaint_canvas/` on legacy plain-named refs colliding with an existing server file, `nice` fits the rubric.

**Known-issues check.** `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json` (`documents/D1`) reported unhashed `overwrite: false` uploads overwriting server files and `ensureOnServer` not checking `Content-Length`. The `hasContentHash`, `Content-Length`, `overwrite: proven`, and `report.renamed` / `rewriteStateRefs` logic was introduced to fix `documents/D1`; this finding identifies a missing server-side cache in that new fix and is absent from `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Open`), all three `verified.json` files, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`.

findings.claim: In `--run` mode, `agentMain` registers `app.once("will-quit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); app.exit(code); })` before `startApp()` registers its own `will-quit` cleanup and never removes that listener when the headless instance is handed over to a visible window or another connected agent. When the app later quits or restarts, this first listener terminates the process immediately via `app.exit(code)`, skipping `startApp`'s temp-file abort/sweep and `electron-updater`'s `autoInstallOnAppQuit` handler, and exiting an interactive session with the earlier batch's exit code.
findings.scenario: A user runs `Scumble --run batch.json` when Scumble is not yet open, so `AgentBackend` starts Scumble in-process (`backend.own = true`), and one step in `batch.json` fails (`code = 1`). While the batch runs (or if an MCP client connects), the user launches Scumble from the desktop (`onSecondInstance` calls `showWindow()`), so when `batch.json` finishes, `maybeQuit()` sees `windowVisible() === true` and hands the running app over to the user. Later, an update finishes downloading (or a save/export is aborted at quit) and the user closes Scumble expecting the update to install on quit: `will-quit` runs line 1699's listener first, calling `e.preventDefault(); app.exit(1)`, which bypasses `electron-updater`'s `will-quit` installer hook and `main.js:1582`'s temp-file cleanup and exits with code 1.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/main.js:1698-1710`: `let code = 1; app.once("will-quit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); app.exit(code); }); ... try { code = await require("./cli_run").main(...); } finally { agentMode = null; } if (!backend.own) { ... } showAgents(); maybeQuit(); return;`. `startApp()` is called inside `cli_run` -> `backend.ensure()` (`main.js:1660`), so `startApp()`'s `app.on("will-quit", ...)` (`main.js:1582-1587`: `documents.abortAll(); fileSaves.abortAll()...; documents.sweep();`) and `electron-updater`'s `addQuitHandler()` (`electron/main/updater.js:241`) are registered after line 1699 and never reached once `app.exit(code)` runs. `onSecondInstance` (`main.js:495-501`) calls `showWindow()` for any normal launch during `--run`, and `maybeQuit()` (`main.js:1615-1617`) leaves the app alive when `windowVisible() || local.clients.size > 0` without removing the `will-quit` listener.
findings.fix: Keep a named reference `onWillQuit` to the listener: remove it in `agentMain` whenever `!agentsLeft` after `maybeQuit()` (and in `win.on("close")` line 410 if `maybeQuit`'s close is cancelled by a newly arrived window or agent), and before calling `app.exit(code)` inside `onWillQuit`, run the `documents` / `fileSaves` abort-and-sweep cleanup first.
findings.why:
At `electron/main/main.js:1698-1710` (`agentMain`), `--run` mode initializes `let code = 1;` and immediately registers `app.once("will-quit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); app.exit(code); });` at line 1699 before `cli_run.main` calls `backend.ensure()` -> `startApp()` (`main.js:1660`). Consequently, line 1699's listener is registered ahead of `startApp()`'s `app.on("will-quit", ...)` cleanup at `main.js:1582-1587` (`documents.abortAll(); fileSaves.abortAll().catch(() => {}); documents.sweep();`). Furthermore, if no Scumble was running initially (`backend.own === true`) and the user opens Scumble (`onSecondInstance` -> `showWindow()` at `main.js:495-501`) or another agent attaches while `--run` executes (or during `win.on("close")`'s flush at `main.js:410`), `maybeQuit()` (`main.js:1615-1617, 1709`) leaves the app running without removing the `will-quit` listener from line 1699.

Tracing the exact Electron and `electron-updater` mechanics refines two parts of the candidate's claim while confirming the underlying defect. First, in Electron, `app.exit(code)` (`Browser::Exit` -> `Browser::Shutdown`) sets the process exit code, synchronously emits `"quit"` with `exitCode = code`, and quits Chromium's main `RunLoop` before returning to JS `EventEmitter.emit("will-quit")`: so `"quit"` fires prematurely before `main.js:1582-1587` runs, and any async work in `fileSaves.abortAll()` (`electron/main/filesaves.js:175-182, 200-208`) gets no event-loop turns after `will-quit` returns. Second, `electron-updater` 6.8.9 (`electron/main/updater.js:241` `addQuitHandler()` -> `node_modules/electron-updater/out/BaseUpdater.js:69-90` -> `ElectronAppAdapter.js:37-39`) actually listens on `app.once("quit", (_, exitCode) => ...)`, not `"will-quit"`. Thus when `code === 0`, `autoInstallOnAppQuit` is not bypassed; however, when a batch step failed (`code === 1`), `app.exit(1)` passes `exitCode = 1` to `BaseUpdater`'s `"quit"` listener, which hits `if (exitCode !== 0) { ... return; }` (`BaseUpdater.js:83-86`) and silently skips installing a downloaded update on quit, while also exiting the handed-over interactive session with stale exit code `1`.

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: `--run` (`cli_run.js`, item 69) is new since those reviews and this issue is not in any known list. Severity is calibrated down from `should` to `nice`: there is no data or pixel loss (`win.on("close")` at `main.js:407` already awaits `flushAll("quit")` -> `documents.idle()`, `render-process-gone` at `main.js:435-436` and `askWhileSaving` at `main.js:599` already abort saves, and `startApp()` at `main.js:1581` sweeps `document-temps.json` on the next launch); `docs/MCP.md:162-163` intentionally keeps the `--run` Electron process as the waiting CLI call until the last window/agent closes (`mcp/launch.js:90` forwards its exit code); and hitting the skipped-update-on-quit symptom requires all of: starting `--run` headless with a failing step (`code = 1`), handing that instance over to a window, manually triggering an update check (since `main.js:1609` skips automatic startup checks when `headless || agentMode` is truthy), and closing the window instead of clicking *Install and restart* (`quitAndInstall` spawns the installer before `app.quit()`).

findings.claim: `mcp/launch.js` attaches error handlers to `stdin` and `child.stdin` but not to `process.stdout` before forwarding child output with `process.stdout.write(buf)`. If the caller's stdout pipe closes early during a `--run` or `--cmd` invocation (`!SERVES`), `launch.js` crashes with an unhandled `EPIPE` error and its `exit` listener immediately kills the child Scumble process, even when that child owns a headless app instance.
findings.scenario: A user or script runs a batch via the Node-mode launcher piped into a tool that stops reading early, e.g. `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 Scumble.exe resources\app.asar\electron\main\mcp\launch.js --run steps.json | head -n 1`, when no other Scumble instance is running (`backend.own = true`). After `head` closes the pipe, the second JSON line written by `child` hits `process.stdout.write(buf)` in `launch.js`, throwing an uncaught `Error: write EPIPE`. `launch.js` exits and runs `process.on("exit", () => child.kill())`, abruptly terminating the Electron process (`TerminateProcess` on Windows) mid-command or mid-save instead of letting it finish or flush cleanly.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/mcp/launch.js:50,54` sets `const SERVES = CHILD_ARGS.includes("--mcp");` and spawns `child`. Lines 63-73 forward `child.stdout` via `process.stdout.write(buf);` with no `process.stdout.on("error", ...)` handler anywhere in `launch.js` (contrast `electron/main/cli_run.js:253`: `stdout.on("error", () => { /* the reader went away (a closed pipe) */ });`, and `launch.js:76,88` for `stdin`). Line 92 registers `if (!SERVES) process.on("exit", () => { try { child.kill(); } catch { /* gone */ } });`.
findings.fix: Add `process.stdout.on("error", () => {});` in `electron/main/mcp/launch.js` so a closed downstream stdout pipe does not crash the launcher and force-kill the child Scumble process.
findings.why:
Confirmed at `f45a86cc`. `electron/main/mcp/launch.js` (93 lines total) is documented as a clean-stdout wrapper not only for `--mcp` but also for `--run` and `--cmd` (`launch.js:12` and `docs/MCP.md:129`). At `launch.js:50`, `const SERVES = CHILD_ARGS.includes("--mcp");` is `false` for `--run` and `--cmd`, so `spawn` at `launch.js:54` starts the Electron child with `detached: false`, and `launch.js:92` registers `if (!SERVES) process.on("exit", () => { try { child.kill(); } catch { /* gone */ } });`. In the `child.stdout.on("data", ...)` listener (`launch.js:63-73`), line 72 calls `process.stdout.write(buf);` directly. While `launch.js` attaches error listeners to `child.stdin` (`launch.js:76`) and `stdin` (`launch.js:88`), there is no `process.stdout.on("error", ...)` listener anywhere in the file, nor any `uncaughtException` handler.

Tracing the full execution path: in Node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` or plain `node`), `SIGPIPE` is ignored by libuv and writing to a pipe whose reader has closed causes `process.stdout` to emit an asynchronous `'error'` event (`EPIPE` / `EOF`). Even a single-step `--run` batch writes at least two lines to stdout in the child (`cli_run.js:222` for the step and `cli_run.js:231` for the `{"done":true,...}` summary). When a downstream pipe consumer closes early after reading the first line (for example `... launch.js --run steps.json | head -n 1`), the next chunk from `child.stdout` hits `process.stdout.write(buf)` at `launch.js:72`, emitting an unhandled `'error'` event on `process.stdout`. Node terminates `launch.js` with an uncaught exception and runs `process.on("exit", ...)` (`launch.js:92`), which calls `child.kill()` (`TerminateProcess` on Windows). That abruptly kills the child Scumble process mid-batch or mid-shutdown instead of letting `cli_run.js` finish its remaining steps (including closing temporary batch tabs on an attached instance) or letting a headless `backend.own` instance complete `maybeQuit()` -> `app.quit()` -> `flushAll("quit")` (`electron/main/main.js:1708-1709`). By contrast, `electron/main/cli_run.js:253` explicitly attaches `stdout.on("error", () => { /* the reader went away (a closed pipe) */ });` for direct `Scumble --run` invocations, proving the intended behavior when the stdout reader closes early.

Checked all known-issue lists (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`). The only prior finding on `launch.js` is `main/MAIN-1` (`review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json:94-105`), which concerned `clientGone()` killing `--mcp` children 5 seconds after `stdin` EOF; in fact, the fix for `MAIN-1` introduced `SERVES` and the `!SERVES` `process.on("exit", () => child.kill())` hook at `launch.js:92`, leaving this unguarded `process.stdout` `EPIPE` interaction intact. Severity is `nice`: hitting it requires invoking `--run` (or `--cmd`) specifically via the Node-mode `launch.js` wrapper rather than `Scumble --run` directly and piping stdout into a reader that closes early.

findings.claim: 0.1.57's `overStored` and `windowSawDefaults` merge plain-object settings shallowly (`{ ...had, ...v }` / `{ ...base[k], ...v }`), treating structured setting objects (`plugins`, `llm`, `assistant`) the same as per-id maps (`recipeValues`, `recipeLoras`). When `settings.json` has a transient read error at startup, toggling a plugin or editing a `llm` sub-field from default-seeded state overwrites stored array/nested properties such as `plugins.disabled`/`enabled` or `llm.models`.
findings.scenario: The user has custom language models in `settings.llm.models` and disabled plugins in `settings.plugins.disabled`. At startup `settings.json` hits a transient `EBUSY` lock (`loaded = false`, `windowSawDefaults = true`). During the 2-second read cooldown, `plugins.setEnabled("film", true)` runs (or the user opens Settings during the cooldown so `shellState.settings.llm.models` is `[]` and edits the local compat URL). Once `settings.json` becomes readable, `overStored` / `set()` shallow-merges `{ ...had.plugins, ...v }` and `{ ...base.llm, ...v }`, replacing the user's `disabled` plugin list and `llm.models` array with the default-derived arrays.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/settings.js:174,182-191,235-238`: `const isMap = (v) => !!v && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v);`, in `overStored`: `else if (isMap(had) && isMap(v)) out[k] = { ...had, ...v };`, and in `set()`: `if (loaded && windowSawDefaults) { ... for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(p)) if (isMap(v) && isMap(base[k])) p[k] = { ...base[k], ...v }; }`. `electron/main/plugins.js:89-93` (`setEnabled`) reads `const prefs = settings.get().plugins || {};` and writes `{ plugins: { ...prefs, disabled: Array.from(disabled), enabled: Array.from(enabled) } }`, where both properties are arrays that replace `had.disabled` and `had.enabled`. `DEFAULTS.llm` (`settings.js:50`) has `models: []`, which likewise overwrites `base.llm.models` under `{ ...base.llm, ...v }`.
findings.fix: Restrict the per-entry `{ ...had, ...v }` / `windowSawDefaults` map merge to true dictionary maps (`recipeValues`, `recipeLoras`, `recipePresets`, `recipeProviders`, `recipeByMode`, `pluginData`), and keep stored values (or merge per leaf) for structured objects like `plugins`, `llm`, and `assistant`.
findings.why:
Verified against f45a86cc in electron/main/settings.js, electron/main/plugins.js, electron/main/main.js, renderer/shell.js, and renderer/shell_settings.js. In settings.js:174, `isMap` is defined as `(v) => !!v && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v)`, which matches every plain-object setting rather than only per-id dictionary maps (`recipeValues`, `recipeLoras`, `recipePresets`, `recipeProviders`, `recipeByMode`, `pluginData`). Both recovery paths rely on `isMap`: `overStored(stored, patch)` at settings.js:182-191 merges pending writes taken while `loaded === false` via `else if (isMap(had) && isMap(v)) out[k] = { ...had, ...v };` (line 187), and `set(patch)` at settings.js:235-238 merges later writes after `windowSawDefaults` was set at line 218 via `if (isMap(v) && isMap(base[k])) p[k] = { ...base[k], ...v };` (line 237).

Tracing the concrete call paths confirms the defect with one minor nuance on the `llm` timing. First, in electron/main/plugins.js:89-93, `setEnabled(id, on)` reads `const prefs = settings.get().plugins || {};`, builds `disabled` and `enabled` Sets from `prefs`, and calls `settings.set({ plugins: { ...prefs, disabled: Array.from(disabled), enabled: Array.from(enabled) } })`. If `settings.json` fails its 4 retries at startup (~250 ms backoff in `retrying`, settings.js:80-87, 113) and `setEnabled` runs while `loaded` is still `false` (e.g. during the 2 s `READ_FAIL_COOLDOWN_MS` at settings.js:69, 110-124), `prefs` is `{}` and `pending.plugins` stores `{ disabled: [...], enabled: [...] }` built from empty sets. When `settings.json` becomes readable on a subsequent `get()`, `overStored` evaluates `{ ...had, ...v }` (line 187), and `v`'s `disabled` and `enabled` arrays completely replace `had.disabled` and `had.enabled` before `writeJson` persists `cache` at line 223.

Second, for `llm`, `saveCompat()` (renderer/shell_settings.js:455-460) does not read `shellState.settings.llm.models` directly — it calls `await window.scumble.settings.get()` first. However, if `saveCompat()` (or `promptRefPics`'s change handler at renderer/shell.js:755-760) runs while `settings.json` is still unreadable, `settings.get()` returns `DEFAULTS.llm` (`{ compat: { url: "", model: "" }, models: [] }` at settings.js:50), so `pending.llm` carries `models: []` and `overStored`'s `{ ...had, ...v }` overwrites `stored.llm.models` with `[]` on recovery (conversely, `lmSave` at shell_settings.js:479-485 during the outage carries `DEFAULTS.llm.compat` and wipes `stored.llm.compat`). Moreover, even after `settings.json` recovers (`loaded === true`), structured objects cached from the initial `settings:get` at renderer/shell.js:126-141 without re-reading — such as `assistant` in `ui.setAsKeep` / `ui.setAsSteps` (shell.js:909-918, spreading `DEFAULTS.assistant` from settings.js:63 including `model`, `effort`, and `noticed: {}`), `memory` (shell.js:943-958), `realism` (shell.js:137, 713-716), `nodeParams` (shell.js:137), and `key` (shell.js:140-141) — send full objects populated with default sibling fields, so `set()`'s `{ ...base[k], ...v }` at settings.js:237 overwrites the user's stored sibling fields and nested `assistant.noticed` map with defaults.

Checked known lists (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`). `main-docs/settings-pending-clobbers-stored-maps` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` was the pre-0.1.56 defect where `pending` replaced top-level keys unconditionally; `overStored` and `windowSawDefaults` were introduced in 0.1.56 to fix that finding (CHANGELOG.md:95), and this candidate proves a remaining flaw in that new fix, so it is `confirmed` rather than `known`. Severity is `nice`: hitting it requires `settings.json` to stay locked past all five synchronous read retries (>250 ms) at startup and then editing one of the affected structured settings groups, and it affects only those non-secret preference fields rather than documents, pixels, or keys.

findings.claim: The ONNX helper utility process dispatches incoming IPC jobs concurrently without a queue, while `Matting.run` releases the shared cached `InferenceSession` immediately after `session.run` when running on GPU (`provider !== "cpu"`). Because `onnxruntime-node` defers `binding.run` via `setImmediate` but executes `session.release()` synchronously, two overlapping GPU cutout jobs share one session and the first to finish disposes it before or during the second job's native run.
findings.scenario: Set *Settings › Helper models › Device* to GPU (`gpu`) and trigger Cutout (`matting.js`) on two open document tabs in quick succession (or via two concurrent plugin/MCP actions) while DirectML takes 8-14 s on cold session creation (`runtime.js:41-48` shares the in-flight `this.loading` promise for `this.file`). Both `Matting.run` calls receive the same `{ session, provider: "dml" }` and call `session.run(...)`, scheduling two `setImmediate` callbacks in `onnxruntime-node`. As soon as the first `setImmediate` finishes, Job 1 resumes its `async run()` continuation and calls `await this.runtime.release(this.file)` (`matting.js:44`), which synchronously calls `session.release()` -> `binding.dispose()` before Job 2's `setImmediate` executes `binding.run()`, failing Job 2 with a disposed-session error.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/onnx/helpers_process.js:38`: `if (port) port.on("message", (e) => { handle(e.data); });` invokes `async function handle(msg)` concurrently for every message without awaiting the previous job. `electron/main/onnx/runtime.js:41-48`: `session(file, opts)` deduplicates concurrent loads via `this.loading.get(file)` and returns the same cached `{ session, provider }` entry from `this.sessions`. `electron/main/onnx/matting.js:26,29,44`: `const { session, provider } = await this.runtime.session(this.file, { auto: ["cpu"] }); ... const out = await session.run({ [session.inputNames[0]]: input }); ... if (provider !== "cpu") await this.runtime.release(this.file);`. In `node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/backend.js:102-118`, `run()` wraps `this.#inferenceSession.run(...)` inside `setImmediate(() => { try { resolve(...); } ... })`, whereas `dispose()` synchronously calls `this.#inferenceSession.dispose()`.
findings.fix: Serialize job execution in `electron/main/onnx/helpers_process.js` on a promise queue (`let queue = Promise.resolve();` for `JOBS`, while keeping `msg.type === "cancel"` immediate so `Florence2` decoder cancellation still fires mid-run), and track an active-run refcount per file in `Runtime` (`electron/main/onnx/runtime.js`) so `release()`/`free()`/`setDevice()` defer `session.release()` until in-flight runs complete (which also protects main-thread fallback mode `this.local`).
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc. Every quoted line and the async/event-loop interleaving hold in the code.

Code & call-path trace: On main's side, `onnx/index.js:253-257` (`cutout`) calls `job("cutout", ...)` (`index.js:222-229`, where `busy` is only a status `Set` and does not serialize calls) -> `helperProcess.call("cutout", ...)` (`electron/main/onnx/helpers.js:237-248`), which posts `{ ...job, id, type }` straight to `this.proc` (or runs `this._runLocal` in main-thread fallback). Inside the utility process, `electron/main/onnx/helpers_process.js:38` (`port.on("message", (e) => { handle(e.data); })`, and `:40` `process.on("message", handle)`) dispatches `async function handle(msg)` (`:24-36`) concurrently without awaiting prior jobs — an intentional design so SAM2 point clicks can interleave between automask batches (`docs/PLAN_HELPERS_PROCESS.md:226-235`). `engine.js:187-193` reuses one `Matting` instance per `(model.id, file)` (`mattingOf`, `:97-101`) and calls `Matting.run` (`electron/main/onnx/matting.js:22-46`). At `matting.js:26`, `this.runtime.session(this.file, { auto: ["cpu"] })` deduplicates concurrent loads via `this.loading.get(file)` (`electron/main/onnx/runtime.js:41-48`) and caches `{ session, provider, file }` in `this.sessions` (`:61-62`). When `this.device === "gpu"`, `providerCandidates("gpu", ["cpu"])` (`runtime.js:19-24`) picks `"dml"` (Windows) or `"coreml"` (macOS) first, so `provider !== "cpu"`.

Why the race is deterministic across both cold-start sub-cases: In `node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/backend.js`, both `createInferenceSessionHandler` (`:132-144`) and `run` (`:113-125`) defer their synchronous native calls via `setImmediate(...)`, whereas `dispose()` (`:102-104`, called by `InferenceSession.release()` in `onnxruntime-common/dist/cjs/inference-session-impl.js:114-116` <- `Runtime.release` at `runtime.js:74-80`) has no `setImmediate` and calls `this.#inferenceSession.dispose()` synchronously before yielding. (1) If two `cutout` IPC messages arrive before `createInferenceSessionHandler`'s `setImmediate` runs (e.g. during the ~50 ms utility-process startup or two parallel `cutout_layer` calls across two `doc` IDs), both await `this.loading.get(file)`, resume on the same microtask checkpoint when `loadModel` finishes, and enqueue two `setImmediate` `run` callbacks `[Immediate_Job1, Immediate_Job2]`. (2) Even more broadly, if Job 1 starts a cold DirectML load (measured at ~2.6 s for BiRefNet lite and ~6-10 s for full BiRefNet in `PLAN_HELPERS_PROCESS.md:78,80`) and Job 2's IPC message arrives at any point during that multi-second synchronous `loadModel` block: when `loadModel`'s `setImmediate` finishes, Node's `processImmediate` drains microtasks (`_create` populates `this.sessions` and Job 1 queues `Immediate_Job1` for the next check turn), then yields to I/O / the Mojo `parentPort` pump before the next check phase; `handle(msg2)` runs, hits `this.sessions.get(file)` (`runtime.js:42-43`), and appends `Immediate_Job2` right behind `Immediate_Job1`. In both cases, during the next `processImmediate` turn, `Immediate_Job1` finishes `binding.run` and Node flushes microtasks before advancing to `Immediate_Job2`: Job 1 runs lines 30-42 of `matting.js`, reaches line 44 (`if (provider !== "cpu") await this.runtime.release(this.file)`), deletes the `this.sessions` entry, and synchronously disposes the native `InferenceSession` right before `Immediate_Job2` invokes `this.#inferenceSession.run(...)`, rejecting Job 2 with a disposed-session error. Note on fix: adding per-file active-run reference counting / deferred release in `Runtime` (or serializing inside `Matting.run`) fixes both utility-process and `this.local` fallback modes without breaking `PLAN_HELPERS_PROCESS.md` §3.5's intentional SAM2 `objects`/`segment` interleaving.

Guards checked & severity calibration (`nice` rather than `should`): (1) Under the default setting `helpers.device: "auto"` (`onnx/index.js:23`), `Matting.run` passes `{ auto: ["cpu"] }` (`matting.js:26`), so `provider === "cpu"` and line 44 never runs; a user must explicitly switch *Settings › Helpers › Device* to `GPU`. (2) Within a single tab, `MasksPart.cutoutLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:58`) and MCP `cutout_layer` (`renderer/commands_layers.js:319`) already block concurrent cutouts via `ed.cutoutPending`, and the in-app assistant awaits tool calls sequentially (`electron/main/assistant/index.js:755-757`). Hitting this requires `device === "gpu"` plus either switching across two open tabs and clicking Cutout during Tab 1's 2.6-10 s session load, or an external MCP client / plugin firing concurrent cutout calls on two documents. (3) When hit, Tab 1 succeeds, no pixels or undo history are lost on Tab 2, `cutoutLayer`'s `catch` (`inpaint_ed_masks.js:79-85`) resets `cutoutPending = null` and shows the error in the status line, and clicking Remove background again succeeds.

Known-issues check: Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (B5 at `:227-250` covers the 24.7 GB DirectML retention that motivated line 44, not concurrent disposal), `docs/PLAN_HELPERS_PROCESS.md` (§3.5 `:226-235` and §7 `:414-419` U1 review, which covered `free()`/`retire()` during cross-tab cutouts, not two concurrent GPU cutouts), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`P14` in external `verified.json` covers moving ONNX off main). Not previously recorded.

findings.claim: Unlike `onnx/helpers.js`, `onnx/lama.js` calls `UtilityProcess.kill()` directly without guarding for the pre-`spawn` window where Electron's `UtilityProcess.kill()` is a no-op. Calling `lama.kill()` right after `warm()`/`run()` starts the process leaves an orphaned `Scumble LaMa` utility process that loads the 208 MB ONNX graph on CPU, holds `lama_fp32.onnx` open on Windows, and leaks its memory.
findings.scenario: Select the Remove tool (which triggers `warmInpaint` -> `lama.warm()`, forking `Scumble LaMa` and posting `{ type: "warm", file }`) and immediately delete the LaMa model in *Settings › Helper models* (`remove("lama")`), change the models folder (`clearInstances()`), or quit the app before `UtilityProcess` emits `"spawn"`. `lama.kill()` calls `p.kill()` (which returns `false` and does nothing before `"spawn"`) and sets `this.proc = null`. The orphaned utility process finishes spawning anyway, spends ~9 s of CPU loading `lama_fp32.onnx` into ONNX Runtime's CPU arena, holds the `.onnx` file handle open on Windows (which can cause `models.remove`'s `fsp.unlink` to fail with `EBUSY`/`EPERM`), and stays alive until app termination.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/onnx/helpers.js:61-66` explicitly documents and works around this Electron quirk: `let spawned = false; p.once("spawn", () => { spawned = true; }); ... kill: () => { if (!spawned) p.once("spawn", () => p.kill()); p.kill(); }`. In contrast, `electron/main/onnx/lama.js:80-81` writes `const p = electron.utilityProcess.fork(script, [], { serviceName: "Scumble LaMa" }); return { post: (m) => p.postMessage(m), kill: () => p.kill(), on: (ev, fn) => p.on(ev, fn), kind: "utility" };`, and `Lama.kill()` (`electron/main/onnx/lama.js:167-176`) clears `this.proc = null` immediately after calling `p.kill()`.
findings.fix: Apply the same `spawned` guard from `onnx/helpers.js:61-66` to `spawn()` in `electron/main/onnx/lama.js:80-81`: track `let spawned = false; p.once("spawn", () => { spawned = true; });` and in `kill` run `if (!spawned) p.once("spawn", () => p.kill()); p.kill();`.
findings.why:
At `f45a86cc`, `spawn()` in `electron/main/onnx/lama.js:80-81` forks the Electron utility process with `const p = electron.utilityProcess.fork(script, [], { serviceName: "Scumble LaMa" });` and returns `kill: () => p.kill()` directly, whereas `electron/main/onnx/helpers.js:58-67` (which copied `lama.js`'s pattern in U1 and was patched in U1's 2026-11-07 review, `docs/PLAN_HELPERS_PROCESS.md:417-418`) tracks `let spawned = false; p.once("spawn", () => { spawned = true; });` and registers `if (!spawned) p.once("spawn", () => { try { p.kill(); } catch (_) { /* gone already */ } });` because Electron's `UtilityProcess.kill()` is a no-op returning `false` while the OS launch is still pending (before `"spawn"` assigns a PID).

Tracing the full call path: `helpers:warmInpaint` (`electron/main/main.js:1415` -> `electron/main/onnx/index.js:286-295` -> `lama.warm()`) and `helpers:inpaint` (`main.js:1414` -> `onnx/index.js:264-279` -> `lama.run()`) invoke `Lama._call()` (`lama.js:140-148`), which calls `this._start()` (`lama.js:102-125`) to fork the utility process and immediately posts `{ id, type, file: this.file, ...payload }` onto the Mojo `MessagePort` (`lama.js:146`). If `Lama.kill()` (`lama.js:169-175`) is called before `p` emits `"spawn"` (~12 ms window per `PLAN_HELPERS_PROCESS.md:123`, e.g. via `clearInstances()` at `onnx/index.js:116-120` from `configure({ dir })` at `:91` or `scan()` at `:108`, or via `remove("lama")` at `onnx/index.js:174-176`), `Lama.kill()` sets `this.proc = null`, rejects `this.pending`, and calls `p.kill()`, which silently does nothing. Because `electron/main/onnx/lama_process.js:26` (`if (port) port.on("message", (e) => handle(e.data));`) has no parent-disconnect exit path on `utilityProcess`, the child finishes spawning anyway, reads the queued `warm`/`run` message from `process.parentPort`, spends ~9 s of CPU loading `lama_fp32.onnx` (`lama_process.js:17-18`, `lama.js:41`), holds the `.onnx` file handle open on Windows while `models.remove` (`onnx/models.js:657-673`) attempts `fsp.unlink`, and remains orphaned in memory until app exit (note that on `will-quit` at `onnx/index.js:124-127`, Electron's own browser shutdown tears down utility processes when main exits, so the persistent leak applies to the in-session `configure`/`scan`/`remove` paths).

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, the three `verified.json` review files, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and `docs/PLAN_HELPERS_PROCESS.md`: while `PLAN_HELPERS_PROCESS.md:417-418` records fixing this exact `UtilityProcess.kill()` race in `helpers.js`, the unfixed mirror in `lama.js` is not recorded in any open bug, verified finding, or plan step. Severity is `nice` because hitting `lama.kill()` within the ~12 ms pre-`"spawn"` window requires a narrow race (e.g. scripted calls or overlapping IPCs under heavy load) and causes wasted CPU/RAM (and a transient `fsp.unlink` failure if racing `remove("lama")`) rather than silent data or pixel loss.

findings.claim: `prompts.readDir` exposes user `.md` templates in `<userData>/prompts/` using their verbatim filename stem as `id`, whereas `prompts.remove` strips characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` instead of validating the filename. A template added via 'Open folder' whose filename contains spaces or Unicode cannot be deleted from Settings (failing with `ENOENT`), or deletes a different template whose name matches the stripped stem.
findings.scenario: Click 'Open folder' in *Settings › Prompt writing* (`prompts.openFolder()`), place `My Style.md` (and optionally `MyStyle.md`) into `<userData>/prompts/`, and reload templates. `prompts.list()` lists `id: "My Style"`. Clicking Remove on `My Style` calls `prompts.remove("My Style")`, which computes `safe = "MyStyle"` and unlinks `MyStyle.md` — either deleting the wrong user template (`MyStyle.md`) while leaving `My Style.md` intact, or throwing `ENOENT: no such file or directory, unlink '...\MyStyle.md'`.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/prompts.js:58`: `out.push(parse(text, name.replace(/\.md$/i, ""), source));` preserves spaces and non-ASCII characters in `id` for files placed in `userDir()` (opened by `openFolder()` at lines 93-97). `electron/main/prompts.js:86-90`: `async function remove(id) { const safe = String(id || "").replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, ""); if (!safe) throw new Error("bad template id"); await fsp.unlink(path.join(userDir(), safe + ".md")); return true; }`. (Compare `electron/main/recipes_store.js:659-666`, where `remove` validates `path.basename(raw) !== raw` and resolves inside `userDir` rather than stripping characters.)
findings.fix: Validate `id` as a single path segment without stripping valid filename characters (matching `recipes_store.js:659-666`): reject empty strings, `"."`, `".."`, path separators, and verify `path.dirname(target) === path.resolve(userDir())` before calling `fsp.unlink(target)`.
findings.why:
Confirmed at f45a86cc by reading electron/main/prompts.js, electron/main/main.js, electron/preload.js, renderer/shell_settings.js, renderer/shell.js, and renderer/index.html.

In electron/main/prompts.js:50-64, readDir(dir, source) enumerates every /.md$/i file in userDir() (<userData>/prompts/) and sets each entry's id verbatim to name.replace(/\.md$/i, "") on both the normal path (line 58) and the read-error path (line 60), preserving spaces, parentheses, Unicode characters, and punctuation. Settings › Prompt templates (renderer/index.html:101-105; called 'Prompt writing' in the candidate's scenario text) exposes an 'Open folder' button (ui.promptFolder at renderer/shell.js:774-778 -> window.scumble.prompts.open() -> main.js:1389 -> prompts.openFolder() at prompts.js:93-97) specifically so users can manage .md files in <userData>/prompts/. When renderPrompts() (renderer/shell_settings.js:572-619) renders a row with t.source === 'user' (line 606), its Remove button calls window.scumble.prompts.remove(t.id) (line 610 -> preload.js:203 -> main.js:1390 -> prompts.remove(id) at prompts.js:86-91) with no confirmation and no try/catch.

In electron/main/prompts.js:86-90, remove(id) computes const safe = String(id || "").replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, ""), throws 'bad template id' if !safe (line 88), and calls fsp.unlink(path.join(userDir(), safe + ".md")) (line 89). No upstream caller normalizes or filters id beforehand (importFile at prompts.js:75-84 replaces /[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g with '_' when copying a file via 'Import .md ...', so UI-imported files are unaffected, and an imported 'My Style.md' becomes 'My_Style.md' rather than 'MyStyle.md'). For a file placed via Open folder such as 'My Style.md' (id: 'My Style'), safe becomes 'MyStyle': if 'MyStyle.md' does not exist, fsp.unlink rejects with ENOENT (and for an all-non-ASCII stem such as '日本語.md', safe is '' and line 88 throws), which goes uncaught in renderer/shell_settings.js:609-613 so the click silently fails as an unhandled rejection and leaves the template in place; if a separate 'MyStyle.md' also exists in <userData>/prompts/, clicking Remove on 'My Style' unlinks 'MyStyle.md' instead while leaving 'My Style.md' intact (on case-sensitive Linux, a '.MD' suffix also fails because line 89 hardcodes lowercase '.md'). Note one minor inaccuracy in the candidate's parenthetical comparison: at f45a86cc, electron/main/recipes_store.js:659-666 does not check path.basename(raw) !== raw — instead it checks safeId(want) (matching readId at recipes_store.js:85-91), looks up the entry from readDir(userDir(), 'user'), and unlinks path.join(userDir(), r.file), which deletes the exact directory entry that produced the listed item.

Checked known lists (scratch/known_index.md, docs/BUGS.md, docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md, and all three verified.json files): S9a in docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json noted the analogous recipes.remove sanitization bug on electron/main/recipes.js (since fixed in recipes_store.js:659-666), but electron/main/prompts.js was never reported or tracked anywhere, so this is a distinct unfixed bug.

Severity 'nice' holds: templates imported via 'Import .md ...' already get '[A-Za-z0-9._-]' filenames and remove cleanly; the bug only affects hand-placed files in <userData>/prompts/ with characters outside '[A-Za-z0-9._-]' (where 'Open folder' sits right beside it as a trivial workaround), and unlinking the wrong template requires a separate colliding '<stripped>.md' file in the same folder, with no impact on canvas pixels, documents, or paid runs.

findings.claim: The 0.1.57 `.split` recovery path in providers.edit writes `results/<savedId>.split.tmp` asynchronously across multiple awaits (`fs.promises.open`, `cloudjobs.writeSplit`, `fh.sync`, `fh.close`) after `finally` has already removed `runSlot` from `running` and before renaming to `.split` or adding the note in `cloudjobs.json`.
