If `recoverCloudJobs()` runs its first-call `cloudjobs.sweepResults(dir)` during those awaits, `sweepResults` unlinks every `*.tmp` file in `results/`, causing the subsequent `fs.renameSync(tmp, target)` to throw `ENOENT` and lose all paid split layers. Because `runningCount()` is already 0 during the async write, closing or reloading the window during the `.split` write also neither warns nor waits.
findings.scenario: Scumble starts hidden for an MCP session (`--mcp`, where `askCloudJobs` in `main.js:337` skips `recoverCloudJobs` while `!windowVisible()`, leaving `sweptDirs` empty) or reloads before `sweptDirs` has recorded `dir`. A paid 16-layer Seedream 5.5 `Split into layers` run completes while its originating frame is gone (`hooks.pageGone()` is true), and `index.js:367-371` begins writing and fsyncing ~50-100 MB of 2K layer PNGs to `results/<uuid>.split.tmp`. While that async write is in flight, the window becomes visible or finishes reloading and invokes `provider:cloudJobs` -> `recoverCloudJobs()` (`index.js:653`), which calls `cloudjobs.sweepResults(dir)` (`cloudjobs.js:86-90`) and unlinks `<uuid>.split.tmp` (permitted on open handles on both Windows via libuv `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` and POSIX). `fs.renameSync(tmp, target)` at `index.js:376` then fails with `ENOENT`, caught at `:398`, and `:412` returns `layers: []` and `layersToken: null`, permanently dropping all 16 billed layers.
findings.evidence: electron/main/providers/index.js:335-338 `finally { running.delete(runSlot); ... }` runs before `:344 if (out && out.bytes && hooks && typeof hooks.pageGone === "function" && hooks.pageGone())`. At `:362-376`: `tmp = target + ".tmp"; if (split) { const fh = await fs.promises.open(tmp, "w"); try { await cloudjobs.writeSplit(fh, out, ...); await fh.sync(); } finally { await fh.close(); } } ... cloudjobs.retrying(() => fs.renameSync(tmp, target));`. At `:652-655`: `if (!sweptDirs.has(dir)) { if (cloudjobs.sweepResults(dir) !== null) sweptDirs.add(dir); }`. In electron/main/providers/cloudjobs.js:86-90: `for (const name of names) { if (!name.endsWith(".tmp") && referenced.has(name)) continue; try { retrying(() => fs.unlinkSync(path.join(resDir, name))); } ... }`. In electron/main/main.js:337 `if (!win || win.isDestroyed() || !windowVisible()) return;` defers the first `recoverCloudJobs()` until a window is shown.
findings.fix: Track in-flight result `.tmp` paths in a module `Set` (or pass `activeTmps` into `cloudjobs.sweepResults(dir)`) so `sweepResults` skips any `.tmp` currently being written by this process, and keep `runSlot` in `running` (moving `finally { running.delete(runSlot); }` below the `pageGone` persistence block) so `runningCount()` covers the async `.split` write and `fsync`.
findings.why:
Confirmed as a genuine race defect introduced in the 2026-11-16 `.split` recovery fix, calibrated down from `should` to `nice` because the `sweptDirs` once-per-process guard makes the race window very narrow in practice, and part of the secondary `runningCount()` claim overstates how window close works.

At `electron/main/providers/index.js:344-378`, when a `Split into layers` (`request.kind === "layers"`) run finishes after its originating frame navigated or crashed (`hooks.pageGone()` is true, `electron/main/main.js:1349`), lines `362-371` write `<userData>/results/<savedId>.split.tmp` asynchronously across multiple event-loop turns (`await fs.promises.open(tmp, "w")` at `:367`, `await cloudjobs.writeSplit(...)` looping `await fh.write(...)` at `electron/main/providers/cloudjobs.js:232-238`, `await fh.sync()` at `:370`, and `await fh.close()` at `:371`) before `fs.renameSync(tmp, target)` (`:376`) and `cloudjobs.store(dir, ...).add(...)` (`:378`). Unlike the pre-existing single-picture branch (`index.js:372-375`), which uses synchronous `openSync`/`writeFileSync`/`fsyncSync`/`closeSync` with no `await`s, the async `.split` write yields the main thread while `*.split.tmp` sits on disk unreferenced. If `recoverCloudJobs()` (`index.js:649-653`) runs its first-call `if (!sweptDirs.has(dir) && cloudjobs.sweepResults(dir) !== null) sweptDirs.add(dir)` during those awaits, `cloudjobs.sweepResults(dir)` (`cloudjobs.js:86-91`) unconditionally calls `fs.unlinkSync` on every `*.tmp` entry in `results/`. Because libuv opens files on Windows with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` (and POSIX allows unlinking open files), `unlinkSync` succeeds (removing the entry immediately under Windows 10+/POSIX semantics or marking it delete-on-close so `fh.close()` removes it), causing `fs.renameSync(tmp, target)` at `index.js:376` to fail with `ENOENT`. That error is caught at `:398-401`, no `cloudjobs.json` entry is written, and `:412` returns `{ layersToken: null, layers: [] }` without `keepLayerParts`, permanently losing the billed layers.

Checking guards and reachability refutes normal-GUI reload scenarios and narrows severity to `nice`: (1) In a normal visible GUI start, `renderer/shell.js:1536` calls `recoverCloudResults()` -> `provider:recoverCloudJobs` (`main.js:1359`) -> `askCloudJobs()` (`main.js:335-350`) right at startup (before `commands.ready()` at `shell.js:1538`, or immediately on `ready-to-show` via `cloudWindowShown()` at `main.js:388-391`), and `sweepResults(dir)` returns `[] !== null` even when `<userData>/results` does not exist yet (`cloudjobs.js:75`), populating `sweptDirs` before a user can start a split and reload. Once `sweptDirs.has(dir)` is true, reloads never run `sweepResults` again unless startup's `sweepResults` returned `null` due to `cloudjobs.json` failing 5 `retrying()` reads with `EBUSY`/`EPERM`. (2) In a headless `--mcp`/`--run` start, `askCloudJobs()` at `main.js:337` (`if (!windowVisible())`) indeed skips `recoverCloudJobs()` and leaves `sweptDirs` empty, and `split_layers` is exposed as an MCP/CLI command (`renderer/splitdialog.js:98`). However, hitting the sweep race still requires the hidden renderer to crash/reload mid-split (so `hooks.pageGone()` is true while `headless` keeps `sweptDirs` empty) and the window to become visible (`showWindow()` -> `cloudWindowShown()`) during the exact sub-second/few-second `writeSplit` + `fh.sync()` window. (3) On the secondary `running.delete(runSlot)` point (`index.js:336`): `providers.runningCount()` (`index.js:185`) is only consulted by `reloadWindow()` (`main.js:532`), and a second reload in the renderer does not abort main's in-progress `writeSplit`; meanwhile `win.on("close")` (`main.js:392-413`) and `flushAll()` (`main.js:521-525`) never check `providers.runningCount()` at all (though quitting during those ~100-500 ms after a prior crash/reload also does not wait on `writeSplit`).

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md:107`, and `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json` (`providers/split-pagegone-keeps-base-only`): the prior entry was the missing `.split` recovery itself, which was fixed on 2026-11-16 (`PLAN_0_1_57.md` Lane B), whereas this finding identifies a new race introduced by that async `.split.tmp` implementation, so it is `confirmed`, not `known`.

findings.claim: util.readError(r, key) scrubs the provider API key from error bodies only when callers pass `key` as the second argument, but 11 call sites across bfl.js, openai.js, gemini.js, and comfycloud.js call `readError(r)` with one argument (`key === undefined`), and bfl.js slices raw poll body text into Error without scrub(). If an upstream error or an intermediary proxy/gateway error page echoes the submitted API key or auth header, the unredacted key is written to Scumble's log file and returned over IPC/MCP to the renderer, assistant, and external MCP clients.
findings.scenario: A user configures an OpenAI, Gemini, BFL, or Comfy Cloud API key (or connects through an enterprise/reverse proxy that echoes request headers or rejected tokens in 401/403/502 error bodies) and triggers `generate` from the UI, assistant, or MCP. The request fails with a non-2xx status whose JSON `error.message` or HTML body contains `ctx.key`. Because `openai.js:114` (`await readError(r)`), `gemini.js:98`, `bfl.js:121`, and `comfycloud.js:311` omit `ctx.key`, `scrub(text, undefined)` in `util.js:25-29` is a no-op; `index.js:333` records the raw key in `log.record` on disk and rethrows it to the caller.
findings.evidence: electron/main/providers/util.js:25-29 `function scrub(text, key) { let s = String(text == null ? "" : text); if (key && key.length >= 6) s = s.split(key).join("[key]"); return s; }` and `:39 async function readError(r, key)`. Single-argument calls without `ctx.key`: `electron/main/providers/bfl.js:121` (`readError(submit)`), plus `:148-149` (`text.slice(0, 300)` unscrubbed); `electron/main/providers/openai.js:114` and `:186` (`readError(r)`); `electron/main/providers/gemini.js:98` (`readError(r)`); `electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:311` (`readError(r)`), `:354` (`readError(r)`), `:569` (`readError(h)`), `:740` (`readError(r)`), `:855` (`readError(submit)`), `:866` (`readError(r)`), `:876` (`readError(h)`). `electron/main/providers/index.js:333` logs `err.message` and `err.stack` and rethrows `err`.
findings.fix: Pass `ctx.key` to every `readError(..., ctx.key)` call in `bfl.js`, `openai.js`, `gemini.js`, and `comfycloud.js` (and `scrub(text, ctx.key)` at `bfl.js:148-149`), and as a belt-and-braces net scrub `key` from `err.message` in `providers/index.js`'s `catch` block before logging and rethrowing.
findings.why:
Every quoted function and line number holds at commit f45a86cc. In electron/main/providers/util.js:25-29, scrub(text, key) replaces occurrences of key with "[key]" only when `key && key.length >= 6`, and readError(r, key) (:39-47) forwards `key` to jsonError(JSON.parse(text), key) (:31-37) and scrub(text, key) (:46). While newer or updated adapters (e.g., fal.js:252, replicate.js:207, wavespeed.js:372, openrouter.js:491, magnific.js:562, comfypartner.js:105) pass `ctx.key` and wrap errors in `scrub(..., ctx.key)`, 11 call sites omit the second argument so `key` is `undefined` and `scrub` is a no-op: electron/main/providers/bfl.js:121 (`readError(submit)`), electron/main/providers/openai.js:114 and :186 (`readError(r)`), electron/main/providers/gemini.js:98 (`readError(r)`), and electron/main/providers/comfycloud.js:311, :354, :569, :740, :855, :866, and :876. In addition, bfl.js:148-149 embeds `text.slice(0, 300)` from non-JSON poll responses directly into `new Error(...)` without `scrub`.

Tracing the full call paths from IPC (`main.js:1345` `provider:edit`), UI Generate, assistant tool calls, and MCP `generate` through `electron/main/providers/index.js:314-335` confirms that on the active default paths for BFL (`bfl.js:121,148-149`), OpenAI (`openai.js:114,186`), and Gemini (`gemini.js:98`), thrown errors reach `providers/index.js:333` with no intermediate catch or key redaction. There, `log.record` writes `err.message` and `err.stack` to the ring buffer and `<userData>/logs/scumble.log` (`electron/main/log.js:64-78`, whose contract at :62 states "never a key, never image bytes: the callers see to that") and rethrows `err` back across IPC/MCP (and to the assistant LLM's tool error text). Checking guards in `comfycloud.js` narrows its impact slightly but does not refute it: on the default v2 SDK path (`ctx.cloudApi === "v2"`, `providers/index.js:594`), `:569` (`assetNames`) is always caught inside `loraList` (`comfycloud.js:590-596`), which scrubs via `sdk.scrub(..., ctx.key)`, and `runV2` catches `cloudInfo` (`:354` via `:999-1002`) with `sdk.errorText(err, ctx.key)`. However, `comfycloud.js:354` still leaks unscrubbed into `scumble.log` via `main.js:1080` (`importRecipe` -> `comfycloud.objectInfo` -> `console.warn`, patched by `log.js:128-139`), and all six remaining sites (`:311, :354, :740, :855, :866, :876`) propagate unscrubbed to `providers/index.js:333` when `settings.comfycloud.api === "legacy"`.

Checked against `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`: not previously recorded. `providers/PRV-5` in `review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json` (`util.js:31`) concerned only uncapped `JSON.stringify` length / FastAPI `input` base64 echoes (since fixed at `util.js:35-36`), not missing `ctx.key` arguments to `readError`.

Severity is `nice` (not `must` or `should`): no untrusted remote party can trigger this on their own, and standard upstream responses from BFL, Gemini, OpenAI (which masks middle characters of normal-length `sk-...` keys on 401), and Comfy Cloud do not normally echo full valid keys verbatim. Exposure requires a short/malformed key echo, an unusual upstream error reflection, or an intermediary proxy/gateway error page echoing request headers, making this a clean defense-in-depth consistency fix.

findings.claim: In magnific.js fetchResult(), only the header fetch `ctx.fetch(s, {})` is inside the `DOWNLOAD_TRIES` retry `try/catch`, while `await r.arrayBuffer()` at line 621 runs outside it, and the `catch` block also sleeps through user aborts without checking `isAbort(err, ctx)`. If the CDN connection resets mid-stream while downloading a large upscaled PNG after returning `200 OK` headers, `r.arrayBuffer()` throws uncaught on attempt 1 without using the remaining retries and without naming the paid `task ${id}` in the error.
findings.scenario: A user runs a paid Magnific Precision 16x upscale (producing a 50-100 MB PNG on Magnific's CDN). Polling reaches `COMPLETED` and the task is billed. `fetchResult` receives `200 OK` headers on attempt `n = 1`, enters `if (r.ok) return { bytes: Buffer.from(await r.arrayBuffer()), ... }`, and the CDN stream drops partway through reading the body. Because `await r.arrayBuffer()` is outside the `try/catch`, `fetchResult` does not retry `n = 2..3` and throws raw `TypeError: terminated` (without `task ${id}`), losing the paid result.
findings.evidence: electron/main/providers/magnific.js:613-624: `for (let n = 1; ; n++) { let r; try { r = await ctx.fetch(s, {}); } catch (err) { if (n < DOWNLOAD_TRIES) { ctx.log(...); await ctx.sleep(POLL_MS); continue; } throw new Error(\`Magnific ${route}: the result could not be downloaded ... task ${id}.\`); } if (r.ok) return { bytes: Buffer.from(await r.arrayBuffer()), mime: ... }; ... }`. Compare `electron/main/providers/util.js:207-225` (`downloadImage`), which awaits `fetchImage` (including `await r.arrayBuffer()`) inside the `try` block and rethrows immediately when `isAbort(e, ctx)` is true (note `toapis.js:468` also lacks `if (isAbort(err, ctx)) throw err;`, though `ctx.sleep` there rejects on abort).
findings.fix: Move `if (r.ok) return { bytes: Buffer.from(await r.arrayBuffer()), ... }` inside the `try` block in `magnific.js:fetchResult` (or delegate to `util.downloadImage`), and add `if (isAbort(err, ctx)) throw err;` at the start of the `catch` in both `magnific.js:617` and `toapis.js:468`.
findings.why:
At commit f45a86cc, electron/main/providers/magnific.js:613-624 implements fetchResult(task, ctx, test, route, id), which is called from run() at magnific.js:710 after submit() (:706) and poll() (:707) reach task.status === "COMPLETED" across all four Magnific entry points (edit, relight, generate, upscale at :755-760, invoked via providers.edit in electron/main/providers/index.js:314). Inside the DOWNLOAD_TRIES (= 3, magnific.js:53) loop, lines 615-620 wrap only `r = await ctx.fetch(s, {});` in try/catch, while line 621 executes `if (r.ok) return { bytes: Buffer.from(await r.arrayBuffer()), mime: ... };` outside the try/catch. Both HTTP transports used by ctx.fetch resolve once the response headers arrive and stream the body lazily: in electron/main/curlfetch.js:191-210, 223-237, and 299, hop() resolves as soon as `\r\n\r\n` is parsed and errors the ReadableStream controller with `new TypeError("terminated", { cause })` (:187) if curl exits non-zero or stalls mid-transfer; Node's native undici fetch (used when Settings > Network curl is off or on loopback) behaves the same way. Consequently, if Magnific's CDN returns 200 OK headers on attempt n = 1 and the connection resets mid-body (most plausible on a large Precision/Creative 16x upscale PNG), `await r.arrayBuffer()` rejects uncaught: attempts n = 2..3 are bypassed, and the raw `TypeError: terminated` propagates to providers/index.js:316-334 without the formatted message at magnific.js:619 that names the paid `task ${id}`. By contrast, util.js:223-225 (`downloadImage` -> `fetchImage` at util.js:20-22), toapis.js:466-468 (`download` -> `fetchImage`), and bfl.js:158-160 all await `fetchImage` (including `await r.arrayBuffer()`) inside their retry try blocks.

One nuance in the reviewer's secondary abort sub-claim was checked against the callers and partially refuted: when called through providers.edit (index.js:279-282), contextFor(id, p, key, ac.signal) always sets `ctx.sleep` to an abort-aware timer (index.js:605-610) that checks `if (signal.aborted) { reject(aborted()); return; }` immediately, and magnific.js:656 (`sleep: ctx.sleep || realSleep`) preserves it. Thus, if a user cancels during `ctx.fetch(s, {})` at magnific.js:616 (or in toapis.js:467), the catch block at magnific.js:618 does not actually wait POLL_MS (3 s) in production — it logs a spurious `result download failed (cancelled), trying again` line and then `await ctx.sleep(POLL_MS)` rejects immediately with AbortError (and on n === DOWNLOAD_TRIES, index.js:320 catches the thrown Error because `ac.signal.aborted` is true). A real 3 s sleep on abort only occurs if magnific's methods are called directly with an AbortSignal in ctx.fetch but without contextFor's `ctx.sleep` (falling back to `realSleep` at magnific.js:656). Adding `if (isAbort(err, ctx)) throw err;` (or delegating to `util.downloadImage`) is still the right cleanup.

Checked against all known-issue lists (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` under `## Open`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json`, and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`): not known. In fact, `providers/PRV-1` in `review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json` (line 35) assumed Magnific's `DOWNLOAD_TRIES` already retried downloads properly, and the 0.1.56 `util.downloadImage` fix (`providers/polljob-deadline-before-reread`) only migrated fal, Replicate, WaveSpeed, Comfy Router, and Comfy Partner, leaving `magnific.js:fetchResult` untouched.

Severity is `nice`: pre-header network errors and 5xx responses on Magnific's CDN are already retried (:615-620, :622), so losing the download requires a TCP reset or stall specifically after 200 OK headers have already arrived and while streaming the body — a narrow network edge case.

findings.claim: `loadPlugins`, `reloadPlugins`, and `setEnabled` have no serialisation guard, and `unload` fires `onChanged()` -> `renderPlugins()` after each unloaded plugin, rebuilding the Settings rows with enabled checkboxes while a reload or toggle is still awaiting `import()` / `getData()` / `activate()`. If `unload` runs while `load(p)` is suspended at an `await`, `unload` removes the unfinished entry from `plugins`, and the first `load(p)` later resumes on the orphaned entry, colliding with or leaking global filter, command, tool, and panel registrations.
findings.scenario: In `Settings › Plugins`, the user toggles a plugin checkbox on (`setEnabled` starts `load(p)`, inserting `entry1` into `plugins` and awaiting `import()` / `getData()`) and immediately clicks `Reload` (which is not disabled while a checkbox toggle runs), or clicks a checkbox that `renderPlugins()` re-enabled mid-`reloadPlugins()`. `reloadPlugins()` calls `unload(entry1)` while `entry1.loaded` is still `false`, deleting `p.id` from `plugins`, and then starts a second `load(p)` (`entry2`). Both `entry1` and `entry2` run `activate()`: whichever finishes second throws `already registered` on filters/commands/panels (marking `entry2` failed in `plugins` while `entry1`'s registrations remain live in `FILTERS`/`COMMANDS` and mounted in editor side panels with no entry in `plugins` able to unload them).
findings.evidence: `renderer/plugins.js:826-846`: `load(p)` calls `plugins.set(p.id, entry)` on line 828, then awaits `import(...)` (831), `window.scumble.plugins.getData(p.id)` (833), and `fn(entry.api)` (837) without checking whether `plugins.get(p.id) === entry`. `unload(entry)` (`860-869`) skips `deactivate` when `!entry.loaded`, runs `removeRegs(entry)` (which is empty before `activate`), calls `plugins.delete(entry.id)`, and invokes `onChanged()` (868). In `renderer/shell.js:818`, `onChanged` runs `renderPlugins()` (`renderer/shell_settings.js:778-792`), creating fresh checkboxes with `cb.disabled = false`, while `loadPlugins` / `reloadPlugins` / `setEnabled` (`plugins.js:877-897`) run without a queue.
findings.fix: Serialise `loadPlugins`, `reloadPlugins`, and `setEnabled` through a single promise chain in `renderer/plugins.js`, and in `load(p)` check `plugins.get(p.id) === entry` after each `await`, calling `removeRegs(entry)` and bailing out if the entry was superseded.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in `renderer/plugins.js:826-897`, `renderer/shell.js:818-827,1412,1477`, and `renderer/shell_settings.js:778-823`. None of `loadPlugins()` (`renderer/plugins.js:877-886`), `reloadPlugins()` (`889-892`), or `setEnabled(id, on)` (`894-897`) has a serialisation queue or generation token. In `load(p)` (`826-847`), `plugins.set(p.id, entry)` runs synchronously at line 828 with `entry.loaded = false` before three `await` points: `await import(...)` (line 831), `await window.scumble.plugins.getData(p.id)` (line 833), and `await fn(entry.api)` (line 837), with no post-await check that `plugins.get(p.id) === entry`. Meanwhile `unload(entry)` (`860-869`) skips `deactivate` when `!entry.loaded` (line 861), runs `removeRegs(entry)` on the still-empty `entry.regs` (line 864), deletes `entry.id` from `plugins` (line 866), and fires `onChanged()` (line 868).

All entry points and UI guards were checked and leave this race reachable: (1) In `Settings › Plugins`, toggling a checkbox (`renderer/shell_settings.js:788-792`) disables only that `cb` (`cb.disabled = true`), leaving `ui.pluginsReload` (`renderer/shell.js:819-825`) and other checkboxes enabled; (2) clicking `Reload plugins` in Settings disables `ui.pluginsReload`, but each `unload(entry)` and `load(p)` invokes `onChanged()` (`renderer/shell.js:818`) -> `renderPlugins()` (`renderer/shell_settings.js:778-823`), which wipes `ui.plugins.innerHTML` and creates fresh `<input type="checkbox">` nodes with `cb.disabled = false` mid-reload (and mid-`setEnabled` whenever more than one plugin unloads/loads); and (3) `Plugins › Reload plugins` in the native application menu (`electron/main/main.js:738` -> `renderer/shell.js:1412`) calls `plugins.reloadPlugins()` with no UI lock at all, so it can overlap itself, startup `plugins.loadPlugins()` (`shell.js:1477`), or a Settings toggle.

When `unload(entry1)` deletes `p.id` from `plugins` while `entry1` is suspended at line 831 or 833, `entry1` later resumes as an orphaned entry outside `plugins` and runs `activate(entry1.api)`. If the plugin was disabled (`setEnabled(id, false)`), `entry1` still registers its filters (`FILTERS` / `FILTER_IDS`, `plugins.js:325-326`), commands (`COMMANDS`, `plugins.js:690` / `commands.js:135`), `host.on` listeners (`plugins.js:771`), editor side panels (`mountPanel`, `390-405`), and toolbar buttons (`mountTool`, `528-544`) with no entry in `plugins` left to unload them. If `reloadPlugins()` started a replacement `entry2` (`plugins.js:884`), both `entry1` and `entry2` run `activate()`: for filter-registering plugins (`film`, `sample`, `effects`), the second finisher hits the global `if (FILTERS[id]) throw new Error(...)` check at `renderer/plugins.js:282`, marking `entry2` failed in `plugins` (`840-842`) while `entry1`'s registrations remain leaked and unloadable (and if `entry2` registered commands before failing on a filter, `removeRegs(entry2)` at line 855 even deletes `entry1`'s commands from `COMMANDS` because `commands.js:134-138` keys ownership by `p.id` string rather than entry identity); for non-filter plugins (`boxes`, `glb`), per-entry checks in `registerPanel` (`357`) and `registerTool` (`515`) allow both to succeed, leaking duplicate side panels, duplicate tool buttons, and duplicate `host.on("geometry")` listeners.

Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_full_2026-11-07/verified.json`, `docs/research/review_external_2026-11-07/verified.json` (`P16` and `S7` touch `plugins.js` only on `fs` caching and `toolButtonHtml`), and `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`: this defect is not previously recorded. Severity is `nice` because shipped plugins load from local `scumble://app/plugins/...` files with fast IPC `getData` and synchronous `activate()` bodies, making the race window only a few tens of milliseconds unless a user plugin has an async `activate()`.

findings.claim: `done()` fires `this.saveChat(chat)` without awaiting it and `send()` immediately clears `this.turn = null`, while `this.saves` is an unserialized `Set` rather than a sequential queue. Two overlapping `Store.save` calls for the same chat contend on the identical `<id>.json.tmp` path and renumber/delete `<n>.jpg` files concurrently after `adapter.prune` mutates `chat.history` in place, causing failed renames, stale JSON overwrites, or mismatched screenshot files.
findings.scenario: Turn 1 has accumulated > `2 * keepImages` (e.g. 7) screenshots and finishes; `done()` starts `saveChat(chat)` in the background, writing `1.jpg..7.jpg` and `<id>.json.tmp`. Before that disk write finishes, the user immediately sends Turn 2 (or hits Stop on Turn 2). `runTurn` runs `adapter.prune(chat.history, 3)` in place — dropping screenshots 1..4 — and `done()` launches a second concurrent `Store.save(chat)`. Save 2 strips the remaining 3 screenshots as `1.jpg..3.jpg`, unlinks `4.jpg..7.jpg`, and writes the exact same `<id>.json.tmp` while Save 1 is still writing `1.jpg..7.jpg` and renaming `<id>.json.tmp`. One `fsp.rename(tmp, file)` fails with `ENOENT`/`EPERM`, or Save 1's rename lands second and overwrites `<id>.json` with markers pointing to `4.jpg..7.jpg` that Save 2 deleted (or `1.jpg` holding Save 2's pruned screenshot instead of Save 1's).
findings.evidence: `electron/main/assistant/index.js:1045`: `this.saveChat(chat).catch((err) => this.record(...));` (not awaited); `index.js:420-425`: `send()` returns `await this.turnDone` whose `finally` sets `this.turn = null; this.turnDone = null;`. `index.js:573-583`: `saveChat` creates an immediate IIFE `const job = (async () => { const saved = await this.deps.store.save(chat, { events: this.events }); ... })(); this.saves.add(job);` with no chaining on prior saves. `index.js:708` mutates `chat.history` in place via `adapter.prune(chat.history, s.keepImages)`. `electron/main/assistant/store.js:56-70`: `strip` numbers images `1..images.length` (`${images.length + 1}.${ext}`), writes every `<n>.jpg`, writes `const tmp = this.file(chat.id) + ".tmp"; await fsp.writeFile(tmp, ...); await fsp.rename(tmp, this.file(chat.id));`, and deletes any folder file not in `keep`.
findings.fix: Serialize `saveChat` through a single promise chain (`this.saveChain = (this.saveChain || Promise.resolve()).then(run, run)`) and track that promise in `this.saves`, or use a unique temp filename per write while still serializing per-chat saves so `Store.save` cannot overlap itself.
findings.why:
Verified at commit f45a86cc in `electron/main/assistant/index.js` and `electron/main/assistant/store.js`. In `done()` (`index.js:1039-1047`), `this.emit("turn:done", ...)` runs at line 1042 and `this.saveChat(chat).catch(...)` is fired without `await` at line 1045. Immediately after `done()` returns synchronously, `_startTurn`'s `finally` block (`index.js:421-425`) clears `this.turn = null; this.turnDone = null;` (and resolves `send()`'s `started.done` at `index.js:348-351`). Neither `_start` (`index.js:370-377`) nor `_startTurn` (`index.js:379-429`) checks or awaits `this.saves`, and `saveChat` (`index.js:573-583`) launches an unchained async IIFE tracked only in `this.saves = new Set()` (`index.js:65`), which is awaited solely by `deleteChat` (`index.js:566`) and `resetAll` (`index.js:600`).

Inside `Store.save` (`store.js:40-71`), `strip()` runs synchronously before the first `await` (`store.js:54-57`), numbering images `1..images.length` (`store.js:163`). It then sequentially awaits `fsp.writeFile` for each `<n>.jpg` (`store.js:60`), writes to the fixed path `const tmp = this.file(chat.id) + ".tmp"` (`store.js:62-63`), renames `tmp` over `<id>.json` (`store.js:64`), and deletes any file in `<id>/` not in `keep` (`store.js:66-69`). When a second turn on the same chat both starts and finishes while Save 1 is still in `Store.save` — notably when Turn 1 had `> 2 * keepImages` (e.g. 7) screenshots and Turn 2's `runTurn` prunes `chat.history` in place to `keepImages` (3) at `index.js:708` before exiting quickly (`turn.stopped` at `718`, `bytes > cap` `"full"` at `720`, or an immediate stream failure at `731-734`) — Save 2 has only 3 sequential image writes against Save 1's 7. Save 2 therefore overtakes Save 1: it overwrites `1.jpg..3.jpg` with screenshots 5..7, writes and renames `<id>.json.tmp`, and unlinks `4.jpg..7.jpg`, after which Save 1 finishes `7.jpg` and either fails `fsp.rename(tmp, ...)` with `ENOENT`/`EPERM` (if their `tmp` writes overlapped) or overwrites `<id>.json` with Turn 1's stale record whose `$image:1.jpg..3.jpg` markers now point to the wrong screenshots and whose `$image:4.jpg..7.jpg` files were just deleted.

Checked known lists (`scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files): not known. In `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`, `assistant-glb/deleted-chat-resaved` (`index.js:551`) and `assistant-glb/events-unbounded` (`index.js:308`) were different defects; in fact, the 0.1.57 fixes for those two items introduced `this.saves = new Set()` (without serialization) and added the `keep` / `fsp.rm` loop in `store.js:66-69` plus `event.image: null` in `emit()`, which is what makes `images.length` drop across `adapter.prune` and trigger the image renumbering/unlink race.

Calibrated severity from `should` down to `nice`: because `strip()` in `Store.save` (`store.js:54-55`) snapshots `events` and `history` synchronously before its first `await`, merely starting Turn 2 (and running `adapter.prune` at `index.js:708`) while Save 1 writes to disk is harmless on its own. For two `Store.save` calls to overlap, Turn 2 must both start after `turn:done` (`renderer/assistant.js:780` ignores `send()` while `busy`) AND reach `done()` before Save 1 finishes its ~5–50 ms of local file writes. A normal network LLM turn takes far longer than that, so outside programmatic `await assistant.send()` callers (`tools/assistant_test.js`) a user can only hit this in a narrow timing window where Turn 2 immediately aborts/errors (`"full"`, local `ECONNREFUSED`, or Enter+Escape within tens of ms while disk I/O is stalled by AV/slow storage), and no document pixels or money are lost (matching `host-gen/brush-tip-saves-race` at `nice` in `review_full_2026-11-12/verified.json`).

findings.claim: Several layer/group policy rules fail to ask before mutating user-made or group-locked content: `glb_edit` runs `AUTO()` on user-placed 3D objects unless `depth_layer === false` (overwriting the user's 3D layer pixels/pose and even deleting a user-placed mannequin's `pose_layer` unasked), `wrap_layer` hides a user-made source layer unasked, and `decide()` / `ungroup_layers` ignore group locks (`locked_by_group` and locked groups).
findings.scenario: 1. The user places a 3D mannequin with `pose_layer: true` (or hand-paints over a 3D object layer). On a later turn the assistant calls `glb_edit` with new pose/rotation parameters and `pose_layer: false`: `POLICY.glb_edit` sees `depth_layer !== false`, returns `AUTO()`, deletes the user's pose layer, and overwrites the 3D layer's pixels without asking. 2. The user puts a layer into a group and locks the group (`locked: true` on the group, so `list_layers` reports `locked: false, locked_by_group: true`). The assistant calls `set_layer` with `x: 500, y: 500` (or `ungroup_layers` on the locked group): `decide()` checks only `target.locked`, returns `AUTO()`, and `commands_layers.js:60-69` (`set_layer`) moves the layer inside the locked group (or `ungroup_layers` dissolves the lock) without asking.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/assistant/policy.js:147-149`: `glb_edit: (call, facts) => (call.args && call.args.depth_layer === false && !owns(call, facts) ? ASK("removes the depth layer of a 3D object you placed") : AUTO())` — neither `!owns(call, facts)` in general nor `call.args.pose_layer === false` asks. `policy.js:72, 74-75`: `wrap_layer: AUTO` (hides `layer.visible = false` at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:439`), `ungroup_layers: AUTO` (`commands_layers.js:300`), while `set_group` asks on `locked === false`. `policy.js:538`: `if (target && target.locked && (name === "set_text" || (name === "set_layer" && SET_LAYER_GEOMETRY.some(...))))` ignores `target.locked_by_group` (`commands_util.js:76`), and `renderer/commands_layers.js:60-69` (`set_layer` `if (geo)`) and `renderer/commands_edit.js:206` (`set_text`) check neither `refuseLayer(ed, l)` nor `ed.isLocked(l)`.
findings.fix: In `policy.js`, make `glb_edit` `ASK` whenever `!owns(call, facts)` (matching `set_text` / `transform_layer`), make `wrap_layer` `ASK` when `!owns(call, facts)` (since it hides the user's layer), check `target && (target.locked || target.locked_by_group)` at `policy.js:538` (and enforce `refuseLayer(ed, l)` in `commands_layers.js` `set_layer` geometry and `commands_edit.js` `set_text`), and ask on `ungroup_layers` when the target group is locked.
findings.why:
This bundled finding mixes five distinct claims; auditing each at f45a86cc shows one genuinely new policy gap (`wrap_layer: AUTO`), one new gap overlapping `p1-params-mannequin/assistant-policy-glb-edit-pose-layer` (`glb_edit` with `pose_layer === false`), one already-known issue (`shell/F6`), one intentional design choice (`glb_edit` on `!owns` in general), and one factually false claim (`ungroup_layers` dissolving locks). Overall verdict is `confirmed` at `nice` (downgraded from `should`).

1. **`wrap_layer` hiding user-made layers unasked (`electron/main/assistant/policy.js:72`) — CONFIRMED (`nice`):** `POLICY.wrap_layer` is `AUTO` (set during SP7 in `docs/PLAN_SURFACE_PAINT.md:424`), and `renderer/commands_edit.js:120-126` calls `ed.wrapLayer(l, ...)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:422-451`), which sets `layer.visible = false` at line 439 on any non-filter pixel/text layer without checking `!owns(call, facts)`, `ed.isLocked(layer)`, or `ed.isReference(layer)`. That bypasses the ownership gate enforced by `set_layer({ visible: false })` (`policy.js:41, 474`) and `set_mask({ op: 'hide' })` (`policy.js:103-105`), which `docs/PLAN_ASSISTANT.md:2646` specifically requires so the model cannot hide a user's layer via another `AUTO` tool after `remove_layer` is declined (and on a reference layer, `inpaint_ed_filters.js:439` also hides the reference without calling `refsMutated()`, tripping `_refDrift` at `inpaint_ed_layers.js:1060-1062`). However, `wrapLayer` pushes `{ kind: 'layers', label: 'Wrap onto surface' }` at `inpaint_ed_filters.js:430` before mutating state, so no pixels are lost and one Ctrl+Z (or 'Undo this turn') restores visibility.

2. **`glb_edit` on `!owns(call, facts)` (`electron/main/assistant/policy.js:147-149`) — `pose_layer === false` CONFIRMED (overlaps `p1-params-mannequin/assistant-policy-glb-edit-pose-layer`), general `!owns` REFUTED as intentional design:** `policy.js:147-149` asks only when `call.args.depth_layer === false && !owns(call, facts)`. Item 67 added `pose_layer` (`plugins/glb/main.js:160, 170, 179, 348, 384`), which deletes `Mannequin pose` via `ed.removeLayers(gone)` when `pose_layer === false`, so omitting `call.args.pose_layer === false` at `policy.js:147` is a real gap (already covered in `p1-params-mannequin/assistant-policy-glb-edit-pose-layer`). findings.claim: `models.costOf` computes ToAPIs usage in ToAPIs credits (`currency: "credits"`, where 200 credits = $1), but `Assistant.addUsage`, `Assistant.recordTurn`, and `renderer/assistant.js` ignore `cost.currency` and format `amount` directly with a `$` prefix. On ToAPIs, both the assistant panel footer and `scumble.log` display credits as US dollars, overstating the dollar cost by 200x.
findings.scenario: Select `toapis:claude-sonnet-5` in the assistant and run a turn using 100k input tokens and 10k output tokens (`0.09 + 0.045 = 0.135` ToAPIs credits, i.e. `$0.000675`). The panel footer displays `this chat $0.1350 · last turn $0.1350` and `scumble.log` logs `$0.1350 for the chat` instead of `0.1350 credits` or `$0.0007`.
findings.evidence: `electron/main/assistant/models.js:37-41, 131`: `toapis: { "claude-sonnet-5": [0.90, 4.50, null, null], ... } // in ToAPIs credits, 200 credits = $1` and `if (provider === "toapis") return { amount, currency: "credits", note: notes.concat("200 credits = $1").join("; ") };`. `electron/main/assistant/index.js:1012-1013`: `const cost = this.costOf(chat, usage); if (cost && cost.amount != null) chat.usage.cost += cost.amount;` and line 1029: `const cost = u.cost ? \`, $${u.cost.toFixed(4)} for the chat\` : "";`. `renderer/assistant.js:563, 613-614`: `if (e.cost && e.cost.amount) lastTurnCost += e.cost.amount;` and `parts.push(\`this chat $${u.cost.toFixed(4)}\`); parts.push(\`last turn $${lastTurnCost.toFixed(4)}\`);`.
findings.fix: Either convert ToAPIs credits to USD in `models.costOf` (`amount / 200`, `currency: "USD"`, keeping the credit count in `note`), or store `chat.usage.currency = cost.currency` and format `currency === "credits"` as `${v.toFixed(2)} credits` instead of `$${v.toFixed(4)}` in `index.js` and `renderer/assistant.js`.
findings.why:
Verified at f45a86cc across `electron/main/assistant/models.js`, `electron/main/assistant/providers.js`, `electron/main/assistant/chat.js`, `electron/main/assistant/index.js`, and `renderer/assistant.js`. Every quoted line and line number in the finding matches the code as committed.

In `electron/main/assistant/models.js:37-41`, `PRICES.toapis` lists the three curated ToAPIs models (`claude-sonnet-5`: `[0.90, 4.50, null, null]`, `claude-opus-5`: `[1.50, 7.50, null, null]`, `gemini-3.8-flash`: `[0.30, 1.50, null, null]`) in ToAPIs credits per million tokens (`200 credits = $1`, matching `electron/main/providers/toapis.js:12, 525`), and `costOf()` at `models.js:131` explicitly returns `{ amount, currency: "credits", note: notes.concat("200 credits = $1").join("; ") }` (documented at `models.js:96`). However, no caller inspects `cost.currency` or `cost.note`: in `electron/main/assistant/index.js:1010-1014`, `addUsage()` accumulates `chat.usage.cost += cost.amount` (line 1013) onto `chat.usage` (`index.js:248, 533`, which carries no `currency` field); `runTurn()` at `index.js:739` emits `usage` with `cost: this.costOf(chat, res.usage)`; and `recordTurn()` at `index.js:1029` formats `u.cost` unconditionally as `, $${u.cost.toFixed(4)} for the chat` into `scumble.log`. On the renderer side, `renderer/assistant.js:563` adds `e.cost.amount` into `lastTurnCost` without checking `e.cost.currency`, and `showCost()` at `renderer/assistant.js:613-614` formats both `u.cost` and `lastTurnCost` unconditionally with a `$` prefix (`this chat $${u.cost.toFixed(4)}` and `last turn $${lastTurnCost.toFixed(4)}`), including after chat save/reopen via `store.js:52` and `index.js:473, 525`.

The full path is reachable in normal use with no guard preventing it: `toapis` is in `ORDER` (`providers.js:155-167, 216`) on the `chat` family with `streamOptions: true`, `index.js:649-654` enables its picker group whenever the `toapis` key is set, `baseFor` (`index.js:108-110`) points at `<toapisBase>/v1`, and `chat.js:287, 373` normalizes streamed `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` into `res.usage` without `u.cost` (and even if a server sent `usage.cost`, `models.costOf` only reads `u.cost` when `provider === "openrouter"` at `models.js:100`). Thus 100k input + 10k output tokens on `toapis:claude-sonnet-5` yields `amount = 0.135` credits ($0.000675) and displays `$0.1350`, overstating the USD figure 200x (`docs/PLAN_ASSISTANT.md:1914` had planned to show ToAPIs credits beside dollars, which was never wired into `assistant.js` or `index.js`).

Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` (`## Open`), `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and all three `verified.json` files (`review_full_2026-11-12`, `review_full_2026-11-07`, `review_external_2026-11-07`): prior cost findings covered `responses.js`/`gemini.js` cached-token double counting (`assistant-glb/usage-cache-double-count`, fixed) and `lastTurnCost` not resetting on `turn:start` (`assistant-glb/last-turn-cost-cumulative`, fixed at `assistant.js:530`), never `toapis` credit currency formatting. Severity is `nice` because this is purely misleading status/log text on one reseller provider—no pixels, chat data, or actual billing are affected.

refuted.claim: Commit 46ff8b0f (`limit-dropped-when-filter-returns-input`) added `const over = ownPx(layer)` to `limitStage`'s early return (`if (out === src && !over) return src;`), but forgot to check `info.limitView`. Whenever a plain filter layer (`over === false`) returns `src` unchanged, enabling the Limit mask preview (`limitView`) returns the colour image `src` instead of rendering the black-and-white limit mask.
refuted.scenario:
1. Add a Relight filter layer (before adding any light or with strength at 0, so `relightSkip` is true) or stack a new Levels/Curves/HSL filter layer at neutral settings directly above another filter layer while WebGL filter chaining is active (`src` is a `GLSurface`).
2. Enable a Limit (e.g. Hue, Luminance, or Depth) on that filter layer and toggle the Limit preview eye/view (`limitView = true`).
3. Instead of showing the black-and-white coverage mask of the Limit, the canvas keeps showing the unmodified colour picture until the user nudges a filter slider away from neutral.
refuted.evidence:
In `renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:70-76`:
`export function limitStage(layer, src, out, info, gl = null) {`
`    const over = ownPx(layer);`
`    if (out === src && !over) return src;`
`    const lim = !info.forDepth && layer.params && layer.params.limit;`
`    if (!lim && !over) return out;`
When `out === src` (which occurs in `applyFilterGL` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:1079` for `relightSkip`, and at lines `1166`, `1185`, `1199` when an identity `levels`/`curves`/`hsl`/`vibrance` filter receives a `GLSurface` `src` from a filter below), line 72 returns `src` before reading `info.limitView` (used at lines 107 and 113 to render `vec4(vec3(w), 1.0)` / greyscale `w`).
refuted.why:
First, the candidate finding misquotes `limitStage` in `renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js`. At `f45a86cc`, `limitStage` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:55-105`) has signature `export function limitStage(src, out, limitIn, info = {}, def = null)` — not `limitStage(layer, src, out, info, gl = null)` — and does not call `ownPx(layer)` (which lives in `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_geometry.js:16` for Deep paint geometry transforms) or read `layer.params.limit`. Instead, commit `46ff8b0f` wrote `const over = !!(def && def.over) || !!info.limitOver;` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:69` followed by `if (out === src && !over) return src;` at line `72`. (The `inpaint_filters_gl.js` citations in the finding are also off: `applyPluginGL`'s skip return `return isGLSurface(src) ? src : copyCanvas(src)` is at `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:1115`, `applyFilterGL`'s `if (ok === false)` return is at line `1192`, and `SETUP.levels` at lines `777-782` never returns `false`.)

Second, tracing the full call path from UI entry point to `limitStage` proves that `over` is unconditionally `true` whenever `info.limitView` is `true`, making the `out === src && !over` early return at `renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:72` unreachable during Limit preview. In the UI, the Limit coverage view ("Show the effect", set via `openMaskMenu` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_masks.js:397-401` as `this.maskView = { id, mode: "effect" }`; there is no separate eye toggle in `buildLimitBlock` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_panels.js:235-487` or MCP command for it) only activates `info.limitView = true` inside `filterInfo` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:749-751`), which checks `this.effectViewOf(layer, pass.forRun)`. `effectViewOf` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_depth.js:621-625`) returns `true` exclusively during a screen pass (`!forRun && !!vp && !!vp.screen && !vp.sample && !!this.maskView && this.maskView.mode === "effect" && this.maskView.id === layer.id`). Of the only two callers of `filterInfo` in the codebase, `bandFilter` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:357-376`) runs on full-resolution bands without `viewPass.screen` (so `effectViewOf` is always `false`), and `filteredCanvas` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:840-900`) is called solely from `applyFilterLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1486-1511`).

In `applyFilterLayer` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1486-1487`), the editor computes:
`const limitView = this.effectViewOf(layer, forRun);`
`const plain = !limitView && !this.liveMask(layer) && Math.round(layer.opacity * 255) === 255 && (!layer.blend || layer.blend === "normal") && !preview && !clip && !this.isFillLayer(layer);`
Because `plain` starts with `!limitView`, enabling "Show the effect" forces `plain = false` (and `keepSurface = false` at line `1507`) even on an otherwise plain filter layer. `applyFilterLayer` passes `plain = false` to `filteredCanvas` (`line 1511`), which includes both `isEffectView` and `!!plain` in `filterKey` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:717-719`) and sets `info.limitOver = !plain;` (`true`) at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:882` before calling `applyFilter` (`line 884` -> `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters.js:1482`). Inside `limitStage` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:69-72`), `over` evaluates to `true` via `!!info.limitOver`, so `if (out === src && !over) return src;` does not return `src`. Both `LIMIT_SHADER` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:40`, `if (u_view == 1) return vec4(vec3(w), 1.0);` before line `41`'s `u_over == 1`) and `limitStageCPU` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_limit.js:174-185`, `if (isView)` before `else if (over)`) check `limitView` before `over`, outputting opaque greyscale `(w, w, w, 1.0)`, which `applyFilterLayer` then composites over `#000000` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_filters.js:1574-1579, 1591-1594`). (Moreover, for a standalone Relight layer with no filter layer below it, `chain` is `null` so `src` is `ctx.canvas` rather than a `GLSurface`, and `applyPluginGL` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:1115` returns `copyCanvas(src)` with `out !== src` anyway; and `info.limitView` is an internal editor flag not exposed in the plugin API at `renderer/plugins.js:726` / `docs/PLUGINS.md:74`).

Checked against `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the three `verified.json` files: the earlier `2026-11-12` finding `filters/limit-dropped-when-filter-returns-input` was fixed in commit `46ff8b0f`, and this candidate's claimed regression in that fix does not exist.

refuted.claim: Unlike `ark.js` and `oxen.js`, `openrouter.js` `layers()` does not check `if (!req.image)`, does not refuse `req.references`, and omits ModelArk's 15 px / 36 MP layer-split bounds in `picturesFor`. Calling `providers.edit` with `kind: "layers"` on OpenRouter with a missing/empty `image` throws a raw `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` on `Buffer.from(null)`, and passing `references` silently drops them (`references: []`) because `providers/index.js` `layoutFor` falls through to the edit layout instead of a single-picture split layout.
refuted.scenario: Invoke `providers.edit({ provider: "openrouter", model: "bytedance-seed/seedream-5.5", kind: "layers", options: { layers: { max: 32, count: true, text: true } } })` via IPC without `image` (or with an empty `Uint8Array(0)`), or with `references: [pngBytes]`. Without `image`, `toBuffer` produces `null` (`providers/index.js:262`) and `openrouter.js:247` throws `TypeError: The first argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer... Received null`. With `references`, `layoutFor` (`providers/index.js:142`) validates against `openrouter.layout` (up to 16 images) and `openrouter.js:546` silently discards `references: []` instead of refusing like `ark.js:539`.
refuted.evidence: electron/main/providers/openrouter.js:545-546: `const ask = split.askOf(req, who, spec); const pics = await picturesFor({ ...req, kind: "layers", references: [] }, { max_images: 1, max_ratio: 16 }, ctx, model);`, and line 247: `bytes: Buffer.from(req.image)`. Compare electron/main/providers/ark.js:538-545 (`if (!req.image) throw ...; if ((req.references || []).length) throw ...; layerSizeRefusal(...)`) and electron/main/providers/index.js:126-144 (`layoutFor` has branches for `text`, `upscale`, `relight`, but none for `layers`).
refuted.fix: In `electron/main/providers/openrouter.js` `layers()`, add `if (!req.image) throw new Error(`${who}: no picture to split.`);` and `if ((req.references || []).length) throw new Error(`${who} splits exactly one picture; this run has ${req.references.length + 1}.`);`, pass `min_side: 15, max_pixels: 36_000_000` into `picturesFor`, and add a `req.kind === "layers"` branch in `electron/main/providers/index.js` `layoutFor`.
refuted.why:
Every sub-claim of this finding is refuted by `split.askOf(req, who, spec)` (`electron/main/providers/layersplit.js:40-47`), which `openrouter.js` `layers()` calls at line 545 (`const ask = split.askOf(req, who, spec);`) immediately before `picturesFor` at line 546 — the exact same shared helper that `oxen.js:627` and `wavespeed.js:333` rely on instead of duplicating `ark.js:538-545`.

1. Missing/null `image` does not reach `picturesFor` or throw `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]`: in `providers.edit` (`electron/main/providers/index.js:262`), `toBuffer(undefined)` returns `null` (`index.js:97`), `layoutFor` (`index.js:142` -> `openrouter.js:321-326`) does not inspect `req.image`, and `p.layers(req, ctx)` (`index.js:314`) enters `openrouter.js:534`. At `openrouter.js:545`, `split.askOf` executes `if (!req.image) throw new Error(\`${who}: no picture to split.\`);` (`layersplit.js:41`), throwing a clean refusal before `picturesFor` (`openrouter.js:546` / `:247`) is ever called. Nor does passing `new Uint8Array(0)` throw a `TypeError`: `toBuffer(new Uint8Array(0))` (`index.js:99`) returns a 0-length `Buffer` (truthy, as in `ark.js:538` and `oxen.js:627`), `Buffer.from(emptyBuf)` returns an empty `Buffer` rather than throwing on `null`, and `pngSize` (`util.js:459`) returns `null` (`b.length < 24`). (Through UI and MCP, `renderer/editor/splitlayers.js:181,425-432` and `renderer/commands_runs.js:233-261` require `editor.base`, encode non-empty PNG bytes via `sourceBytes`, and hard-code `references: []`.)

2. Non-empty `references` are refused, never silently dropped: when `providers.edit` is called via IPC with `kind: "layers"` and `references: [pngBytes]`, `layoutFor` (`index.js:142`) calls `openrouter.layout(req)` (`openrouter.js:321-326`), which returns `drops: null` and `max: 16` (or `10` when `options.max_images` is set). `checkPictures` (`electron/main/providers/refs.js:219-237`) only strips `references` when `lay.drops` is truthy (`refs.js:224-227`); with `drops: null`, it either refuses runs exceeding `max` (`refs.js:234`) or returns `req` with `req.references` intact (`refs.js:236`). `openrouter.layers` then passes the unmodified `req` to `split.askOf` at `openrouter.js:545`, where `layersplit.js:42` throws `Error(\`${who} splits exactly one picture; this run has ${req.references.length + 1}.\`)` before line 546 (`references: []`, which only normalizes `undefined` to `[]` for `openrouter.js:249`, just as `ark.js:546` and `oxen.js:628` do) and before any HTTP call.

refuted.claim: `liquifyJob` inlines its `RESAMPLE_RT` lookup instead of calling `residentRt(msg.rt)` and overwrites `RESAMPLE_RT = null` whenever `msg.rt` is `null` (such as baking Liquify on a layer mask or selection). The next colour `liquify`, `resample`, or `png_part_read` job on that worker then allocates a duplicate permanent 64 KB block in wasm linear memory (`Px._resident`) and retains the new JS `Uint8Array` in `Px._kept`.
refuted.scenario: Bake a Liquify mesh on a layer that has a layer mask (or on a selection mask), where `liquifyStore` sends `rt: null` for the mask store, followed by a colour `liquify`, `resample`, or `png_part_read` job on the same pool worker. In `liquifyJob`, `msg.rt` is `null`, so `else RESAMPLE_RT = rt;` clears the cached `Uint8Array(65536)` reference. On the next colour job, `msg.rt` is a newly structured-cloned `Uint8Array(65536)`; `Px.prototype._resident` (`px.js:868-877`) keys `this._kept` (`Map`) by object identity, misses, calls `this.alloc(65536)` (never freed for the lifetime of the `Px` instance), and retains the JS `Uint8Array` in `this._kept`. Repeating mask + colour Liquify bakes leaks 64 KB of wasm heap and 64 KB of JS heap per cycle on each worker until the `Px` instance is replaced.
refuted.evidence: `renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:1551-1556`: `function residentRt(rt) { if (!rt) return null; if (RESAMPLE_RT && RESAMPLE_RT.length === rt.length && RESAMPLE_RT.every((v, i) => v === rt[i])) return RESAMPLE_RT; RESAMPLE_RT = rt; return rt; }`, used by `pngPartRead` (`1232`), `pngPartFinishJob` (`1256`), and `resampleJob` (`1561`). By contrast, `liquifyJob` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:1597-1599` writes: `let rt = msg.rt; if (rt && RESAMPLE_RT && RESAMPLE_RT.length === rt.length && RESAMPLE_RT.every((v, i) => v === rt[i])) rt = RESAMPLE_RT; else RESAMPLE_RT = rt;`. In `renderer/editor/px/px.js:868-877`: `_resident(data) { const kept = this._kept || (this._kept = new Map()); let ptr = kept.get(data); if (!ptr) { ptr = this.alloc(data.byteLength); this.put(ptr, data); kept.set(data, ptr); } return ptr; }`.
refuted.fix: Replace lines 1597-1599 of `renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js` with `const rt = residentRt(msg.rt);`.
refuted.why:
While the quoted lines at `renderer/editor/inpaint_worker.js:1597-1599` do inline the `RESAMPLE_RT` lookup (`let rt = msg.rt; if (rt && RESAMPLE_RT && RESAMPLE_RT.length === rt.length && RESAMPLE_RT.every((v, i) => v === rt[i])) rt = RESAMPLE_RT; else RESAMPLE_RT = rt;`) instead of calling `residentRt(msg.rt)` (`inpaint_worker.js:1551-1556`), and `Px.prototype._resident` (`renderer/editor/px/px.js:868-877`) does key `this._kept` by `Uint8Array` object identity over permanent `this.alloc(data.byteLength)` blocks, the claimed `msg.rt === null` path is completely unreachable in the application and in the ComfyUI node.

First, Liquify never bakes layer masks or selection masks. `LiquifyPart.liquifyRefusal` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_liquify.js:34-39`) delegates to `HealPart.patchRefusal(layer, "Liquify")` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_heal.js:209-218`), which explicitly refuses both Quick Mask (`this.quickMask`) and layer mask editing (`layer && layer.maskEdit`). Even when a layer has an active `maskPx` (with `maskEdit` off) or a selection is present, `liquifySession(layer)` (`inpaint_ed_liquify.js:48-65`) clones only `const px = layer.px` (`orig: px.clone()`), `liquifyLand` (`inpaint_ed_liquify.js:286-320`) bakes only `liq.orig.liquified(...)` / `liq.orig.liquifiedAsync(liq.s, nodes, opts)`, and `liquifyCommit` (`inpaint_ed_liquify.js:340-385`) writes only `px.putTiles(results, liq.orig)` (selections and freeze masks only scale node weights via `liquifyThaw` at `inpaint_ed_liquify.js:98-142`). Other transforms/resamples (`straightenDocument`, `resizeImage`, `maskFromLayer`) use `transformedAsync` (`op: "resample"`), which goes through `resampleJob` -> `residentRt(msg.rt)` (`inpaint_worker.js:1561`), and `applyPending` (`inpaint_ed_geometry.js:150-226`) uses Canvas 2D `drawMesh`.

Second, tracing every caller of `liquifyJob` (`inpaint_worker.js:1594`, non-exported and dispatched solely on `msg.op === "liquify"` at `inpaint_worker.js:1995`) shows `msg.rt` can never be falsy even in principle. The finding's scenario misattributes worker messages to `liquifyStore` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_liquify.js:643`), which runs synchronously inside a thread and posts no messages. The sole sender of `op: "liquify"` in the codebase is `liquifyTransport` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_jobs.js:223-227`), registered via `setLiquifyTransport` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_tiles.js:450-452`) and invoked exclusively by `tiled(Base).prototype.liquifiedAsync` (`inpaint_tiles.js:2022-2098`). At `inpaint_tiles.js:2026` and `2083`, `liquifiedAsync` accepts no `rt` option and does not branch on `MaskPixels`: it unconditionally sets `rt = roundTripTable()` (`roundTripTable = canvasRoundTrip` at `inpaint_tiles.js:537`), and `canvasRoundTrip()` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_resample.js:165-184`) always builds, caches in `ROUND_TRIP`, and returns a non-null `Uint8Array(65536)`. Every `op: "liquify"` message therefore carries the same 65,536-byte table, `RESAMPLE_RT` is populated on the worker's first job and reused on every subsequent job, and no wasm or JS memory is leaked. Checked `scratch/known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the three `verified.json` files (not listed there); replacing the three lines with `residentRt(msg.rt)` would be a pure code-style cleanup rather than a bug or leak fix.

refuted.claim: stitch.js defines its own unchecked makeCanvas(w, h) without canvasFits(w, h), while editor.readBoxBytes composites tiled regions up to 536.8 MP (w * h * 4 <= 0x7fffffff). When a planned crop box [x0, y0, cw, ch] on a tiled document exceeds Chromium's 268,435,456-pixel Canvas 2D limit, stitch_worker.js creates an unbacked OffscreenCanvas(cw, ch), silently resizes that blank surface down to a valid [ew, eh] PNG with an all-zero mask, bills the paid API provider on empty inputs, and then crashes in finishResultAsync when encoding the >268 MP stitched patch.
refuted.scenario: Open or extend a tiled document to 20000 x 15000 (300 MP, within Scumble's 1 GiP tiled limit) and select either All (Ctrl+A) or a 15000 x 10000 box whose auto context padding (pad = 2925) expands the planned crop box to 20000 x 15000, then click Generate (or Upscale selection) on any paid API recipe. prepareCropAsync reads the selection window and composites all 300 MP via readBoxBytes into a 1.2 GB SharedArrayBuffer, then stitchJob('crop') puts those pixels into an unbacked 20000 x 15000 OffscreenCanvas and scales it to 2048 x 1536, sending a completely transparent/black PNG and all-zero mask to the paid API; when the billed answer returns, finishPixels creates a 20000 x 15000 patch whose toBlob resolves null on the window fallback, throwing a TypeError in uploadResult and losing the result.
refuted.evidence: renderer/editor/stitch.js:24-30 `function makeCanvas(w, h) { w = Math.max(1, w | 0); h = Math.max(1, h | 0); if (typeof document === "undefined") return new OffscreenCanvas(w, h); const c = document.createElement("canvas"); c.width = w; c.height = h; return c; }` has no `canvasFits` guard (unlike renderer/editor/inpaint_pixels.js:23 and renderer/editor/inpaint_sizelimit.js:6 `CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS = 268435456`). renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:761-768 `if (this.tileMode && !this.huge && w * h * 4 <= 0x7fffffff ...)` succeeds up to 536.8 MP. In renderer/editor/stitch.js:866-868, 944-955, 537-555, `canvasFrom(msg.region)` calls `makeCanvas(20000, 15000)` where `ctx.putImageData` silently no-ops, and `drawResized(crop, ew, eh)` / `resizeMask(denoise_mask, ew, eh)` (lines 249-254, 552-553) draw from unbacked 300 MP canvases onto valid `ew x eh` canvases, so `convertToBlob` succeeds with blank PNG bytes sent to `providerEdit` (renderer/editor/host_provider.js:380, renderer/editor/host_upscale.js:158). On return, `finishPixels` (stitch.js:632, 700) builds `20000 x 15000` canvases; worker `convertToBlob` rejects into the window fallback (stitch.js:933-936 `fin.patch.toBlob(resolve, "image/png")`), resolving `blob = null` and crashing in `uploadResult`.
refuted.fix: Refuse crops above `canvasFits(p.cw, p.ch)` before `providerEdit` (or sample the composited region directly to `[ew, eh]` from tile levels / band-downsample the `SharedArrayBuffer` without a `cw x ch` Canvas 2D surface, and stream/tile-stitch >268 MP patches instead of `makeCanvas(w, h)` in `finishPixels`). At minimum, check `canvasFits(w, h)` inside `stitch.js`'s `makeCanvas` so an oversized box fails before any paid API call leaves.
refuted.why:
The claimed blank-crop upload, wasted paid API call, and post-payment crash in `finishResultAsync` are unreachable at `f45a86cc` because the finding misreads the `!this.huge` guard in `editor.readBoxBytes` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_stack.js:761`) and overlooks the `checkCanvas` guard in `TileLayerPixels.prototype.regionCanvas` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_tiles.js:506-513, 2342`).

First, a planned crop box `[x0, y0, cw, ch]` from `planCrop` (`renderer/editor/stitch.js:395-491`) is always clamped within `[0, editor.width] × [0, editor.height]` via `selectionBbox` (`stitch.js:274, 281-282`), `ensureMinSpan` (`stitch.js:79-89`), and `fitSpanToMultiple` (`stitch.js:91-101`), so `cw <= editor.width` and `ch <= editor.height`. Every document in Scumble has sides `<= 65,535` px (`checkBaseSize` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_open.js:88-90` with `HUGE_MAX_SIDE = 65535` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_load.js:278` on tiles, and `makeCanvas` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_pixels.js:74` on the canvas backend). Consequently, `!canvasFits(cw, ch)` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_sizelimit.js:13-15`, `CANVAS_MAX_SIDE = 65535`, `CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS = 268435456`) can only occur when `cw * ch > 268,435,456`, which since `cw * ch <= editor.width * editor.height` strictly requires `editor.width * editor.height > 268,435,456` — i.e., `editor.tileMode === true` and `editor.huge === true` (`inpaint_ed_open.js:97`: `get huge() { return this.width * this.height > CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS; }`).

Second, when `editor.huge` is `false`, `w * h <= editor.width * editor.height <= 268,435,456`, so `readBoxBytes`'s `SharedArrayBuffer` path (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:761`: `if (this.tileMode && !this.huge && w * h * 4 <= 0x7fffffff && InpaintEditor.boxOverTiles !== false)`) never composites more than 268.4 MP. Conversely, when `editor.huge` is `true` (such as the scenario's `20000 × 15000 = 300 MP` tiled document), both `holdRunStack` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:746`) and `readBoxBytes`'s `SharedArrayBuffer` branch (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:761`) are skipped by `!this.huge`. Execution falls through to `inpaint_ed_stack.js:779` (`ctx.drawImage(this.readBox(box, { forRun }), 0, 0)`).

Third, `readBox` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:930-940`) either calls `this.sampleRegion("image", box, 1, { ...o, pad: reach })` at line 935 (when `reach` is finite) or `this.compositeCanvas(o)` -> `this.flattenToCanvas(o)` at line 936 (which immediately throws `if (this.huge)` at `renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_composite.js:564`). In `sampleRegion` (`inpaint_ed_stack.js:27-83`), `this.viewPass` is set with `sx = 1, sy = 1` (line 76) and `drawComposite` -> `drawLayersInto` (`inpaint_ed_composite.js:46-60`) unconditionally draws `bs = this.basePx` via `this.drawTilesInto(ctx, bs, 0, 0, this.width, this.height, vp)` at line 58. `drawTilesInto` (`renderer/editor/inpaint_ed_chrome.js:108-114`) computes `level = 0` and calls `bs.regionCanvas([vp.x, vp.y, vp.x + vp.w, vp.y + vp.h], 0, false)` (`inpaint_tiles.js:2316-2342`). Because `(ax1 - ax0 + 1) * 256 >= cw` and `(ay1 - ay0 + 1) * 256 >= ch`, their product exceeds `CANVAS_MAX_PIXELS`, and `cpuCanvas` (`inpaint_tiles.js:520-522, 2342`) calls `checkCanvas` (`inpaint_tiles.js:506-513`), synchronously throwing `Error: Inpaint Canvas: a region canvas of ... is above Chromium's canvas limit of 268 MP`.

Fourth, in `prepareCropAsync` (`stitch.js:844-891`), `regionBytes` at line 866 rejects before `stitchCall("crop", ...)` at line 868 is ever invoked, so `stitch_worker.js` never runs `"crop"` or creates an `OffscreenCanvas(cw, ch)`. After catching at line 876, `prepareCropAsync` falls back to synchronous `prepareCrop` (`stitch.js:886` -> `571` -> `regionOf` at `114` -> `editor.readBox`), which throws the exact same `checkCanvas` error uncaught before `cropPixels` is entered. Both `runProvider` (`renderer/editor/host_provider.js:326, 384-386`) and `runUpscale` (`renderer/editor/host_upscale.js:143, 159-161`) catch that rejection, call `this.endRun(editor, token)`, and abort before `providerEdit` (`host_provider.js:380`, `host_upscale.js:158`) is ever reached. Checked `known_index.md`, `docs/BUGS.md`, `docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md`, and the 2026-11-07/12 `verified.json` files (not listed as a known open bug). Severity is calibrated to `nice` on the refuted finding (at worst, an oversized crop on a >268 MP document wastes the selection read and worker `plan` before failing pre-flight with `checkCanvas`'s technical error message).
